declarations.name: simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl
declarations.informal: Let G be an r-regular simple graph on N vertices. For every vertex v, td_{Ḡ}(v) = C(N − r − 1, 2) − N r / 2 + r² − td_G(v), where Ḡ is the complement of G.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (r N : ℕ) (hN : Fintype.card V = N)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree r) (v : V) :
    (simple_graph_triangle_degree Gᶜ v : ℚ) =
      ((N - r - 1).choose 2 : ℚ) - (N * r : ℚ) / 2 + (r : ℚ) ^ 2 -
        simple_graph_triangle_degree G v
declarations.source:
theorem triangle_compl_two_mul_card_clique_pairs {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (S : Finset V)
    (R : V → V → Prop) [DecidableRel R] :
    2 * ((S.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → R x y)).card =
      (S.offDiag.filter (fun p => R p.1 p.2 ∧ R p.2 p.1)).card := by
  rw [Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := fun p : V × V => ({p.1, p.2} : Finset V))
    (t := (S.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → R x y))]
  · rw [mul_comm, ← smul_eq_mul, ← Finset.sum_const]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun t ht => ?_
    obtain ⟨hts, hcl⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.1 ht
    obtain ⟨hsub, hcard⟩ := Finset.mem_powersetCard.1 hts
    obtain ⟨a, b, hab, rfl⟩ := Finset.card_eq_two.1 hcard
    have hfib : ((S.offDiag.filter fun p => R p.1 p.2 ∧ R p.2 p.1).filter
        fun p => ({p.1, p.2} : Finset V) = {a, b}) = {(a, b), (b, a)} := by
      ext ⟨x, y⟩
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_offDiag, Finset.mem_insert,
        Finset.mem_singleton, Prod.mk.injEq]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨⟨⟨hx, hy, hxy⟩, hr⟩, heq⟩
        have hx' : x ∈ ({a, b} : Finset V) := heq ▸ (by simp)
        have hy' : y ∈ ({a, b} : Finset V) := heq ▸ (by simp)
        simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx' hy'
        rcases hx' with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy' with rfl | rfl <;> simp_all
      · rintro (⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
        · exact ⟨⟨⟨hsub (by simp), hsub (by simp), hab⟩,
            hcl _ (by simp) _ (by simp) hab, hcl _ (by simp) _ (by simp) hab.symm⟩, rfl⟩
        · exact ⟨⟨⟨hsub (by simp), hsub (by simp), hab.symm⟩,
            hcl _ (by simp) _ (by simp) hab.symm, hcl _ (by simp) _ (by simp) hab⟩,
            Finset.pair_comm _ _⟩
    rw [hfib, Finset.card_pair (by simp [hab])]
  · rintro ⟨x, y⟩ hp
    simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_offDiag] at hp
    obtain ⟨⟨hx, hy, hxy⟩, hr1, hr2⟩ := hp
    simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powersetCard]
    refine ⟨⟨?_, Finset.card_pair hxy⟩, ?_⟩
    · intro z hz; simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hz
      rcases hz with rfl | rfl <;> assumption
    · intro z hz w hw hzw
      simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hz hw
      rcases hz with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hw with rfl | rfl <;> simp_all

def triangle_compl_adj_count {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S T : Finset V) : ℕ := ∑ x ∈ S, ∑ y ∈ T, if G.Adj x y then 1 else 0

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_union_left {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S S' T : Finset V) (h : Disjoint S S') :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G (S ∪ S') T = triangle_compl_adj_count G S T + triangle_compl_adj_count G S' T := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count; rw [Finset.sum_union h]

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S T T' : Finset V) (h : Disjoint T T') :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G S (T ∪ T') = triangle_compl_adj_count G S T + triangle_compl_adj_count G S T' := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count; rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => Finset.sum_union h

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_comm {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S T : Finset V) : triangle_compl_adj_count G S T = triangle_compl_adj_count G T S := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count; rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => ?_
  simp [G.adj_comm]

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_univ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S : Finset V) : triangle_compl_adj_count G S Finset.univ = ∑ x ∈ S, G.degree x := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
  rw [Finset.sum_boole, ← G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, G.neighborFinset_eq_filter]
  simp

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_self {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S : Finset V) :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G S S = 2 * ((S.powersetCard 2).filter
      (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → G.Adj x y)).card := by
  have h2 := triangle_compl_two_mul_card_clique_pairs S G.Adj
  have h : S.offDiag.filter (fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2 ∧ G.Adj p.2 p.1) =
      (S ×ˢ S).filter (fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2) := by
    ext ⟨x, y⟩
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_offDiag, Finset.mem_product]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨hx, hy, -⟩, h, -⟩; exact ⟨⟨hx, hy⟩, h⟩
    · rintro ⟨⟨hx, hy⟩, h⟩; exact ⟨⟨hx, hy, h.ne⟩, h, h.symm⟩
  have h3 : triangle_compl_adj_count G S S =
      (S.offDiag.filter (fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2 ∧ G.Adj p.2 p.1)).card := by
    rw [h, Finset.card_filter, Finset.sum_product]
    rfl
  rw [h3]
  convert h2.symm

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_singleton_nbr {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G (G.neighborFinset v) {v} = G.degree v := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count
  simp only [Finset.sum_singleton]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (g := fun _ => 1), Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul, mul_one,
    G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
  intro x hx
  rw [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset] at hx
  simp [hx.symm]

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_singleton_self {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : triangle_compl_adj_count G {v} {v} = 0 := by
  simp [triangle_compl_adj_count]

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_nonnbr_singleton {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) (B : Finset V) (hB : ∀ x ∈ B, ¬ G.Adj x v) :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G B {v} = 0 := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count
  simp only [Finset.sum_singleton]
  exact Finset.sum_eq_zero fun x hx => by simp [hB x hx]

theorem triangle_compl_pair_clique_iff {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (R : V → V → Prop) {a b : V}
    (hab : a ≠ b) :
    (∀ x ∈ ({a, b} : Finset V), ∀ y ∈ ({a, b} : Finset V), x ≠ y → R x y) ↔ R a b ∧ R b a := by
  simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨h a (Or.inl rfl) b (Or.inr rfl) hab, h b (Or.inr rfl) a (Or.inl rfl) hab.symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ x hx y hy hxy
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy with rfl | rfl
    · exact absurd rfl hxy
    · exact h1
    · exact h2
    · exact absurd rfl hxy

theorem simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (r N : ℕ) (hN : Fintype.card V = N)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree r) (v : V) :
    (simple_graph_triangle_degree Gᶜ v : ℚ) =
      ((N - r - 1).choose 2 : ℚ) - (N * r : ℚ) / 2 + (r : ℚ) ^ 2 -
        simple_graph_triangle_degree G v := by
  set A := G.neighborFinset v with hA
  set B := Gᶜ.neighborFinset v with hB
  have hBeq : B = Finset.univ \ insert v A := by
    ext x
    simp only [hB, hA, SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, SimpleGraph.compl_adj, Finset.mem_sdiff,
      Finset.mem_univ, Finset.mem_insert, true_and]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hne, hna⟩; rintro (rfl | h)
      · exact hne rfl
      · exact hna h
    · intro h; exact ⟨fun e => h (Or.inl e.symm), fun e => h (Or.inr e)⟩
  have hvA : v ∉ A := by simp [hA]
  have hcardA : A.card = r := by rw [hA, G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, hreg v]
  have hcardB : B.card = N - r - 1 := by
    rw [hBeq, Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset (Finset.subset_univ _), Finset.card_univ, hN,
      Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hvA, hcardA]
    omega
  have hdisjAB : Disjoint A B := by
    rw [hBeq]; exact Finset.disjoint_sdiff.mono_left (Finset.subset_insert _ _)
  have hdisjv : Disjoint {v} (A ∪ B) := by
    rw [Finset.disjoint_singleton_left, Finset.mem_union, not_or]
    exact ⟨hvA, by rw [hBeq]; simp⟩
  have huniv : (Finset.univ : Finset V) = {v} ∪ (A ∪ B) := by
    ext x; simp only [Finset.mem_univ, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_singleton, true_iff]
    by_cases h1 : x = v
    · exact Or.inl h1
    · by_cases h2 : x ∈ A
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inl h2)
      · right; right; rw [hBeq]; simp [h1, h2]
  have hBnv : ∀ x ∈ B, ¬ G.Adj x v := by
    intro x hx h; rw [hBeq] at hx; simp at hx
    exact hx.2 (by rw [hA, SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset]; exact h.symm)
  -- the counts
  set eA := ((A.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → G.Adj x y)).card
  set eB := ((B.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → G.Adj x y)).card
  have htdG : simple_graph_triangle_degree G v = eA := rfl
  have hfilt : (B.powersetCard 2).filter
        (fun s => ¬ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → Gᶜ.Adj x y) =
      (B.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → G.Adj x y) := by
    apply Finset.filter_congr
    intro s hs
    obtain ⟨-, hc⟩ := Finset.mem_powersetCard.1 hs
    obtain ⟨a, b, hab, rfl⟩ := Finset.card_eq_two.1 hc
    rw [triangle_compl_pair_clique_iff _ hab, triangle_compl_pair_clique_iff _ hab]
    simp only [SimpleGraph.compl_adj]
    constructor
    · intro h
      by_contra hn
      apply h
      refine ⟨⟨hab, fun h1 => hn ⟨h1, h1.symm⟩⟩, ⟨hab.symm, fun h2 => hn ⟨h2.symm, h2⟩⟩⟩
    · rintro ⟨h1, -⟩ ⟨⟨-, h2⟩, -⟩
      exact h2 h1
  have htdC : simple_graph_triangle_degree Gᶜ v + eB = (N - r - 1).choose 2 := by
    calc simple_graph_triangle_degree Gᶜ v + eB
        = ((B.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → Gᶜ.Adj x y)).card +
          ((B.powersetCard 2).filter
            (fun s => ¬ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → Gᶜ.Adj x y)).card := by
          rw [hfilt]; rfl
      _ = (B.powersetCard 2).card := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _
      _ = _ := by rw [Finset.card_powersetCard, hcardB]
  have e1 : triangle_compl_adj_count G Finset.univ Finset.univ = N * r := by
    rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_univ, Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun x _ => hreg x), Finset.sum_const,
      Finset.card_univ, hN, smul_eq_mul]
  have e2 : triangle_compl_adj_count G A Finset.univ = r * r := by
    rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_univ, Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun x _ => hreg x), Finset.sum_const, hcardA,
      smul_eq_mul]
  have e3 : triangle_compl_adj_count G A Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G A {v} + (triangle_compl_adj_count G A A + triangle_compl_adj_count G A B) := by
    calc triangle_compl_adj_count G A Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G A ({v} ∪ (A ∪ B)) := by rw [← huniv]
      _ = _ := by rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right _ _ _ _ hdisjv, triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right _ _ _ _ hdisjAB]
  have e4 : triangle_compl_adj_count G Finset.univ Finset.univ =
      triangle_compl_adj_count G {v} Finset.univ + (triangle_compl_adj_count G A Finset.univ + triangle_compl_adj_count G B Finset.univ) := by
    calc triangle_compl_adj_count G Finset.univ Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G ({v} ∪ (A ∪ B)) Finset.univ := by rw [← huniv]
      _ = _ := by rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_union_left _ _ _ _ hdisjv, triangle_compl_adj_count_union_left _ _ _ _ hdisjAB]
  have e5 : triangle_compl_adj_count G B Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G B {v} + (triangle_compl_adj_count G B A + triangle_compl_adj_count G B B) := by
    calc triangle_compl_adj_count G B Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G B ({v} ∪ (A ∪ B)) := by rw [← huniv]
      _ = _ := by rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right _ _ _ _ hdisjv, triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right _ _ _ _ hdisjAB]
  have e6 : triangle_compl_adj_count G {v} Finset.univ = r := by
    rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_univ, Finset.sum_singleton, hreg v]
  have e7 : triangle_compl_adj_count G A {v} = r := by
    rw [hA, triangle_compl_adj_count_singleton_nbr, hreg v]
  have e8 : triangle_compl_adj_count G B {v} = 0 := triangle_compl_adj_count_nonnbr_singleton G v B hBnv
  have e9 : triangle_compl_adj_count G B A = triangle_compl_adj_count G A B := triangle_compl_adj_count_comm G B A
  have eAA : triangle_compl_adj_count G A A = 2 * eA := triangle_compl_adj_count_self G A
  have eBB : triangle_compl_adj_count G B B = 2 * eB := triangle_compl_adj_count_self G B
  have key1 : N * r = r + r * r + triangle_compl_adj_count G A B + 2 * eB := by
    rw [← e1, e4, e6, e2, e5, e8, e9, eBB]; ring
  have key2 : r * r = r + 2 * eA + triangle_compl_adj_count G A B := by
    rw [← e2, e3, e7, eAA]; ring
  have q1 : (N : ℚ) * r = r + r * r + (triangle_compl_adj_count G A B : ℚ) + 2 * eB := by exact_mod_cast key1
  have q2 : (r : ℚ) * r = r + 2 * eA + (triangle_compl_adj_count G A B : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast key2
  have q3 : (simple_graph_triangle_degree Gᶜ v : ℚ) + eB = ((N - r - 1).choose 2 : ℕ) := by
    exact_mod_cast htdC
  rw [htdG]
  linarith
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.08478 (Regular K_3-Irregular Graphs of Every Regularity at Least Nine), Lemma 2.1 (first part); stated over ℚ so that N r / 2 and the subtraction are exact.

explanation.summary: To compute the triangle degree of a vertex v in the complement graph Ḡ, the vertex set V is partitioned into {v}, its neighborhood A = N_G(v) of size r, and its non-neighborhood B = N_{Ḡ}(v) of size N - r - 1. The triangle degrees td_G(v) and td_{Ḡ}(v) correspond to the number of induced edges e_A in A and e_B in B respectively, with td_{Ḡ}(v) + e_B = C(N - r - 1, 2). Double counting the edges out of A and out of the whole graph produces two linear relations involving the cross-edge count e(A, B), e_A, and e_B. Eliminating e(A, B) and e_B from this linear system over ℚ directly yields the formula for td_{Ḡ}(v).

steps.claim: Twice the number of 2-element cliques for a relation R on a finite set S equals the number of distinct ordered pairs in S mutually related by R.
steps.explanation: We count ordered pairs fiberwise via `Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise`, mapping each off-diagonal symmetric pair (x, y) to the unordered pair {x, y}. For every 2-clique {a, b}, the fiber consists of exactly two ordered pairs, (a, b) and (b, a) (lines 12–29), each of cardinality 2 by `Finset.card_pair`. We also check that every such ordered pair maps to a valid 2-element clique (lines 30–39), giving the factor of 2.
steps.code:
theorem triangle_compl_two_mul_card_clique_pairs {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (S : Finset V)
    (R : V → V → Prop) [DecidableRel R] :
    2 * ((S.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → R x y)).card =
      (S.offDiag.filter (fun p => R p.1 p.2 ∧ R p.2 p.1)).card := by
  rw [Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := fun p : V × V => ({p.1, p.2} : Finset V))
    (t := (S.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → R x y))]
  · rw [mul_comm, ← smul_eq_mul, ← Finset.sum_const]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun t ht => ?_
    obtain ⟨hts, hcl⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.1 ht
    obtain ⟨hsub, hcard⟩ := Finset.mem_powersetCard.1 hts
    obtain ⟨a, b, hab, rfl⟩ := Finset.card_eq_two.1 hcard
    have hfib : ((S.offDiag.filter fun p => R p.1 p.2 ∧ R p.2 p.1).filter
        fun p => ({p.1, p.2} : Finset V) = {a, b}) = {(a, b), (b, a)} := by
      ext ⟨x, y⟩
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_offDiag, Finset.mem_insert,
        Finset.mem_singleton, Prod.mk.injEq]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨⟨⟨hx, hy, hxy⟩, hr⟩, heq⟩
        have hx' : x ∈ ({a, b} : Finset V) := heq ▸ (by simp)
        have hy' : y ∈ ({a, b} : Finset V) := heq ▸ (by simp)
        simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx' hy'
        rcases hx' with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy' with rfl | rfl <;> simp_all
      · rintro (⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
        · exact ⟨⟨⟨hsub (by simp), hsub (by simp), hab⟩,
            hcl _ (by simp) _ (by simp) hab, hcl _ (by simp) _ (by simp) hab.symm⟩, rfl⟩
        · exact ⟨⟨⟨hsub (by simp), hsub (by simp), hab.symm⟩,
            hcl _ (by simp) _ (by simp) hab.symm, hcl _ (by simp) _ (by simp) hab⟩,
            Finset.pair_comm _ _⟩
    rw [hfib, Finset.card_pair (by simp [hab])]
  · rintro ⟨x, y⟩ hp
    simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_offDiag] at hp
    obtain ⟨⟨hx, hy, hxy⟩, hr1, hr2⟩ := hp
    simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powersetCard]
    refine ⟨⟨?_, Finset.card_pair hxy⟩, ?_⟩
    · intro z hz; simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hz
      rcases hz with rfl | rfl <;> assumption
    · intro z hz w hw hzw
      simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hz hw
      rcases hz with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hw with rfl | rfl <;> simp_all

steps.claim: The cross-set adjacency count e(S, T) is additive in both arguments over disjoint unions, symmetric, and sums to the vertex degrees when T is the full vertex set.
steps.explanation: Left additivity `triangle_compl_adj_count_union_left` follows from splitting the outer sum with `Finset.sum_union` (lines 43–46). Right additivity `triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right` follows after distributing the inner sum (lines 47–51). Symmetry `triangle_compl_adj_count_comm` holds by interchanging the sums using `Finset.sum_comm` and applying the symmetry of graph adjacency (lines 52–56). Finally, summing over all y ∈ V evaluates each inner sum to the degree of x via `Finset.sum_boole`, so e(S, V) is the sum of degrees in S (lines 57–62).
steps.code:
theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_union_left {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S S' T : Finset V) (h : Disjoint S S') :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G (S ∪ S') T = triangle_compl_adj_count G S T + triangle_compl_adj_count G S' T := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count; rw [Finset.sum_union h]

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S T T' : Finset V) (h : Disjoint T T') :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G S (T ∪ T') = triangle_compl_adj_count G S T + triangle_compl_adj_count G S T' := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count; rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => Finset.sum_union h

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_comm {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S T : Finset V) : triangle_compl_adj_count G S T = triangle_compl_adj_count G T S := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count; rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => ?_
  simp [G.adj_comm]

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_univ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S : Finset V) : triangle_compl_adj_count G S Finset.univ = ∑ x ∈ S, G.degree x := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
  rw [Finset.sum_boole, ← G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, G.neighborFinset_eq_filter]
  simp

steps.claim: The self-adjacency count e(S, S) equals twice the number of induced edges on S.
steps.explanation: Because simple graphs are loopless, the pairs in S × S that are adjacent in G coincide with the off-diagonal mutually adjacent pairs (lines 67–73). Rewriting the sum with `Finset.card_filter` and `Finset.sum_product` (line 76), the previous lemma `triangle_compl_two_mul_card_clique_pairs` shows this count is exactly twice the number of 2-cliques on S, which are the induced edges.
steps.code:
theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_self {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (S : Finset V) :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G S S = 2 * ((S.powersetCard 2).filter
      (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → G.Adj x y)).card := by
  have h2 := triangle_compl_two_mul_card_clique_pairs S G.Adj
  have h : S.offDiag.filter (fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2 ∧ G.Adj p.2 p.1) =
      (S ×ˢ S).filter (fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2) := by
    ext ⟨x, y⟩
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_offDiag, Finset.mem_product]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨⟨hx, hy, -⟩, h, -⟩; exact ⟨⟨hx, hy⟩, h⟩
    · rintro ⟨⟨hx, hy⟩, h⟩; exact ⟨⟨hx, hy, h.ne⟩, h, h.symm⟩
  have h3 : triangle_compl_adj_count G S S =
      (S.offDiag.filter (fun p => G.Adj p.1 p.2 ∧ G.Adj p.2 p.1)).card := by
    rw [h, Finset.card_filter, Finset.sum_product]
    rfl
  rw [h3]
  convert h2.symm

steps.claim: Singleton adjacency counts satisfy e(N(v), {v}) = deg(v), e({v}, {v}) = 0, and e(B, {v}) = 0 for any set B of non-neighbors of v.
steps.explanation: Specialising the second set to {v} collapses the inner sum with `Finset.sum_singleton`. For the neighborhood N(v), each term is 1 because all members are adjacent to v, so the sum equals deg(v) (lines 81–90). For {v}, irreflexivity gives 0 (lines 91–93). For a set B of non-neighbors, every term is 0, so the sum vanishes by `Finset.sum_eq_zero` (lines 94–99).
steps.code:
theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_singleton_nbr {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G (G.neighborFinset v) {v} = G.degree v := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count
  simp only [Finset.sum_singleton]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (g := fun _ => 1), Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul, mul_one,
    G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
  intro x hx
  rw [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset] at hx
  simp [hx.symm]

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_singleton_self {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) : triangle_compl_adj_count G {v} {v} = 0 := by
  simp [triangle_compl_adj_count]

theorem triangle_compl_adj_count_nonnbr_singleton {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : V) (B : Finset V) (hB : ∀ x ∈ B, ¬ G.Adj x v) :
    triangle_compl_adj_count G B {v} = 0 := by
  unfold triangle_compl_adj_count
  simp only [Finset.sum_singleton]
  exact Finset.sum_eq_zero fun x hx => by simp [hB x hx]

steps.claim: Two distinct vertices a ≠ b form a 2-clique for relation R if and only if R a b and R b a both hold.
steps.explanation: A 2-element set {a, b} is an R-clique when every pair of distinct elements is related. Since a ≠ b, the only ordered pairs of distinct elements are (a, b) and (b, a), so the condition reduces to R a b ∧ R b a by unpacking set membership and case splitting.
steps.code:
theorem triangle_compl_pair_clique_iff {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (R : V → V → Prop) {a b : V}
    (hab : a ≠ b) :
    (∀ x ∈ ({a, b} : Finset V), ∀ y ∈ ({a, b} : Finset V), x ≠ y → R x y) ↔ R a b ∧ R b a := by
  simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨h a (Or.inl rfl) b (Or.inr rfl) hab, h b (Or.inr rfl) a (Or.inl rfl) hab.symm⟩
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ x hx y hy hxy
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy with rfl | rfl
    · exact absurd rfl hxy
    · exact h1
    · exact h2
    · exact absurd rfl hxy

steps.claim: The vertex set V partitions into the disjoint union of {v}, the neighbors A = N_G(v) of size r, and the non-neighbors B = N_{Ḡ}(v) of size N - r - 1.
steps.explanation: We set A = N_G(v) and B = N_{Ḡ}(v) = V \ ({v} ∪ A) (lines 120–130). By r-regularity, |A| = r and v ∉ A (lines 131–132). Using `Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset` and `Finset.card_univ`, |B| = N - (r + 1) = N - r - 1 (lines 133–136). The sets {v}, A, and B are pairwise disjoint with union V (lines 137–148), and no vertex in B is adjacent to v in G (lines 149–151).
steps.code:
theorem simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (r N : ℕ) (hN : Fintype.card V = N)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree r) (v : V) :
    (simple_graph_triangle_degree Gᶜ v : ℚ) =
      ((N - r - 1).choose 2 : ℚ) - (N * r : ℚ) / 2 + (r : ℚ) ^ 2 -
        simple_graph_triangle_degree G v := by
  set A := G.neighborFinset v with hA
  set B := Gᶜ.neighborFinset v with hB
  have hBeq : B = Finset.univ \ insert v A := by
    ext x
    simp only [hB, hA, SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, SimpleGraph.compl_adj, Finset.mem_sdiff,
      Finset.mem_univ, Finset.mem_insert, true_and]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hne, hna⟩; rintro (rfl | h)
      · exact hne rfl
      · exact hna h
    · intro h; exact ⟨fun e => h (Or.inl e.symm), fun e => h (Or.inr e)⟩
  have hvA : v ∉ A := by simp [hA]
  have hcardA : A.card = r := by rw [hA, G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, hreg v]
  have hcardB : B.card = N - r - 1 := by
    rw [hBeq, Finset.card_sdiff_of_subset (Finset.subset_univ _), Finset.card_univ, hN,
      Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hvA, hcardA]
    omega
  have hdisjAB : Disjoint A B := by
    rw [hBeq]; exact Finset.disjoint_sdiff.mono_left (Finset.subset_insert _ _)
  have hdisjv : Disjoint {v} (A ∪ B) := by
    rw [Finset.disjoint_singleton_left, Finset.mem_union, not_or]
    exact ⟨hvA, by rw [hBeq]; simp⟩
  have huniv : (Finset.univ : Finset V) = {v} ∪ (A ∪ B) := by
    ext x; simp only [Finset.mem_univ, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_singleton, true_iff]
    by_cases h1 : x = v
    · exact Or.inl h1
    · by_cases h2 : x ∈ A
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inl h2)
      · right; right; rw [hBeq]; simp [h1, h2]
  have hBnv : ∀ x ∈ B, ¬ G.Adj x v := by
    intro x hx h; rw [hBeq] at hx; simp at hx
    exact hx.2 (by rw [hA, SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset]; exact h.symm)
  -- the counts

steps.claim: The triangle degree td_G(v) equals e_A (the induced edges on A), while td_{Ḡ}(v) + e_B = C(N - r - 1, 2), where e_B is the number of edges of G induced on B.
steps.explanation: The triangle degree td_G(v) is defined as the number of edges induced by G on N_G(v) = A, which is e_A (line 155). In the complement graph Ḡ, two distinct vertices in B are adjacent if and only if they are not adjacent in G (lines 156–171). Hence the 2-subsets of B partition into edges of Ḡ (counted by td_{Ḡ}(v)) and edges of G (counted by e_B). By `Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not` and `Finset.card_powersetCard`, their sum is |B choose 2| = C(N - r - 1, 2) (lines 172–179).
steps.code:
set eA := ((A.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → G.Adj x y)).card
  set eB := ((B.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → G.Adj x y)).card
  have htdG : simple_graph_triangle_degree G v = eA := rfl
  have hfilt : (B.powersetCard 2).filter
        (fun s => ¬ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → Gᶜ.Adj x y) =
      (B.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → G.Adj x y) := by
    apply Finset.filter_congr
    intro s hs
    obtain ⟨-, hc⟩ := Finset.mem_powersetCard.1 hs
    obtain ⟨a, b, hab, rfl⟩ := Finset.card_eq_two.1 hc
    rw [triangle_compl_pair_clique_iff _ hab, triangle_compl_pair_clique_iff _ hab]
    simp only [SimpleGraph.compl_adj]
    constructor
    · intro h
      by_contra hn
      apply h
      refine ⟨⟨hab, fun h1 => hn ⟨h1, h1.symm⟩⟩, ⟨hab.symm, fun h2 => hn ⟨h2.symm, h2⟩⟩⟩
    · rintro ⟨h1, -⟩ ⟨⟨-, h2⟩, -⟩
      exact h2 h1
  have htdC : simple_graph_triangle_degree Gᶜ v + eB = (N - r - 1).choose 2 := by
    calc simple_graph_triangle_degree Gᶜ v + eB
        = ((B.powersetCard 2).filter (fun s => ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → Gᶜ.Adj x y)).card +
          ((B.powersetCard 2).filter
            (fun s => ¬ ∀ x ∈ s, ∀ y ∈ s, x ≠ y → Gᶜ.Adj x y)).card := by
          rw [hfilt]; rfl
      _ = (B.powersetCard 2).card := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not _
      _ = _ := by rw [Finset.card_powersetCard, hcardB]

steps.claim: Double counting cross-set edges yields two linear equations: N r = r + r² + e(A, B) + 2 e_B and r² = r + 2 e_A + e(A, B).
steps.explanation: By r-regularity, e(V, V) = N r (`e1`) and e(A, V) = r² (`e2`) using `triangle_compl_adj_count_univ`. Decomposing V = {v} ∪ A ∪ B with the union lemmas expresses e(A, V) as e(A, {v}) + e(A, A) + e(A, B) = r + 2 e_A + e(A, B), yielding `key2` (lines 186, 206–207). Decomposing e(V, V) = e({v}, V) + e(A, V) + e(B, V) and expanding e(B, V) = 0 + e(A, B) + 2 e_B yields `key1`: N r = r + r² + e(A, B) + 2 e_B (lines 189–205).
steps.code:
have e1 : triangle_compl_adj_count G Finset.univ Finset.univ = N * r := by
    rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_univ, Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun x _ => hreg x), Finset.sum_const,
      Finset.card_univ, hN, smul_eq_mul]
  have e2 : triangle_compl_adj_count G A Finset.univ = r * r := by
    rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_univ, Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun x _ => hreg x), Finset.sum_const, hcardA,
      smul_eq_mul]
  have e3 : triangle_compl_adj_count G A Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G A {v} + (triangle_compl_adj_count G A A + triangle_compl_adj_count G A B) := by
    calc triangle_compl_adj_count G A Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G A ({v} ∪ (A ∪ B)) := by rw [← huniv]
      _ = _ := by rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right _ _ _ _ hdisjv, triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right _ _ _ _ hdisjAB]
  have e4 : triangle_compl_adj_count G Finset.univ Finset.univ =
      triangle_compl_adj_count G {v} Finset.univ + (triangle_compl_adj_count G A Finset.univ + triangle_compl_adj_count G B Finset.univ) := by
    calc triangle_compl_adj_count G Finset.univ Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G ({v} ∪ (A ∪ B)) Finset.univ := by rw [← huniv]
      _ = _ := by rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_union_left _ _ _ _ hdisjv, triangle_compl_adj_count_union_left _ _ _ _ hdisjAB]
  have e5 : triangle_compl_adj_count G B Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G B {v} + (triangle_compl_adj_count G B A + triangle_compl_adj_count G B B) := by
    calc triangle_compl_adj_count G B Finset.univ = triangle_compl_adj_count G B ({v} ∪ (A ∪ B)) := by rw [← huniv]
      _ = _ := by rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right _ _ _ _ hdisjv, triangle_compl_adj_count_union_right _ _ _ _ hdisjAB]
  have e6 : triangle_compl_adj_count G {v} Finset.univ = r := by
    rw [triangle_compl_adj_count_univ, Finset.sum_singleton, hreg v]
  have e7 : triangle_compl_adj_count G A {v} = r := by
    rw [hA, triangle_compl_adj_count_singleton_nbr, hreg v]
  have e8 : triangle_compl_adj_count G B {v} = 0 := triangle_compl_adj_count_nonnbr_singleton G v B hBnv
  have e9 : triangle_compl_adj_count G B A = triangle_compl_adj_count G A B := triangle_compl_adj_count_comm G B A
  have eAA : triangle_compl_adj_count G A A = 2 * eA := triangle_compl_adj_count_self G A
  have eBB : triangle_compl_adj_count G B B = 2 * eB := triangle_compl_adj_count_self G B
  have key1 : N * r = r + r * r + triangle_compl_adj_count G A B + 2 * eB := by
    rw [← e1, e4, e6, e2, e5, e8, e9, eBB]; ring
  have key2 : r * r = r + 2 * eA + triangle_compl_adj_count G A B := by
    rw [← e2, e3, e7, eAA]; ring

steps.claim: Eliminating e(A, B) and e_B from the linear system establishes td_{Ḡ}(v) = C(N - r - 1, 2) - N r / 2 + r² - td_G(v) over ℚ.
steps.explanation: The equations `key1`, `key2`, and `htdC` are cast from ℕ to ℚ as `q1`, `q2`, `q3` (lines 208–211). Rewriting td_G(v) to e_A via `htdG` (line 212), `linarith` solves the linear system over ℚ by eliminating e(A, B) and e_B, completing the proof (line 213).
steps.code:
have q1 : (N : ℚ) * r = r + r * r + (triangle_compl_adj_count G A B : ℚ) + 2 * eB := by exact_mod_cast key1
  have q2 : (r : ℚ) * r = r + 2 * eA + (triangle_compl_adj_count G A B : ℚ) := by exact_mod_cast key2
  have q3 : (simple_graph_triangle_degree Gᶜ v : ℚ) + eB = ((N - r - 1).choose 2 : ℕ) := by
    exact_mod_cast htdC
  rw [htdG]
  linarith

glossary.Finset.sum_boole: The sum of a Boolean indicator over a finite set equals the cardinality of the subset satisfying the predicate.
glossary.triangle_compl_two_mul_card_clique_pairs: Twice the number of 2-element cliques for a relation R on S equals the number of distinct ordered pairs in S mutually related by R.
glossary.Finset.card_filter: The cardinality of a filtered subset equals the sum over the parent set of the indicator of the condition.
glossary.Finset.sum_product: The sum over a Cartesian product of two finite sets equals the iterated double sum over each set.

glossary.Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not: The number of elements in a finite set satisfying a predicate plus the number not satisfying it equals the cardinality of the set.

declarations.name: simple_graph_compl_regular_triangle_distinct
declarations.informal: If G is an r-regular triangle-distinct graph on N vertices, its complement is an (N − r − 1)-regular triangle-distinct graph.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_compl_regular_triangle_distinct {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (r N : ℕ) (hN : Fintype.card V = N)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree r) (htd : simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct G) :
    Gᶜ.IsRegularOfDegree (N - r - 1) ∧ simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct Gᶜ
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_compl_regular_triangle_distinct {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (r N : ℕ) (hN : Fintype.card V = N)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree r) (htd : simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct G) :
    Gᶜ.IsRegularOfDegree (N - r - 1) ∧ simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct Gᶜ := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · have h := hreg.compl
    rw [hN] at h
    have e : N - 1 - r = N - r - 1 := by omega
    rwa [e] at h
  · intro x y hxy
    apply htd
    have h1 := simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl G r N hN hreg x
    have h2 := simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl G r N hN hreg y
    have : (simple_graph_triangle_degree G x : ℚ) = simple_graph_triangle_degree G y := by
      rw [hxy] at h1; linarith
    exact_mod_cast this
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.08478 (Regular K_3-Irregular Graphs of Every Regularity at Least Nine), Lemma 2.1 (consequence); follows from the complement formula simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl.

explanation.summary: The proof splits into two parts: regularity and triangle-distinctness of the complement graph Gᶜ. Regularity of Gᶜ follows from the general theorem for regular graph complements, which gives degree |V| - 1 - r = N - r - 1. For triangle-distinctness, the triangle degree of any vertex in Gᶜ is shown to be an affine function of its triangle degree in G with slope -1; hence any two vertices with equal triangle degree in Gᶜ must have equal triangle degree in G, which implies they are the same vertex since G is triangle-distinct.

steps.claim: Gᶜ is regular of degree N - r - 1.
steps.explanation: The theorem requires proving two conjuncts: regularity and triangle-distinctness of Gᶜ. For regularity, `hreg.compl` states that the complement of an r-regular graph on vertex set V is regular of degree |V| - 1 - r. Rewriting |V| as N using the hypothesis hN and simplifying the arithmetic identity N - 1 - r = N - r - 1 establishes that Gᶜ is regular of degree N - r - 1.
steps.code:
refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · have h := hreg.compl
    rw [hN] at h
    have e : N - 1 - r = N - r - 1 := by omega
    rwa [e] at h

steps.claim: To show Gᶜ is triangle-distinct, it suffices to show that any two vertices x and y with equal triangle degree in Gᶜ also have equal triangle degree in G.
steps.explanation: By definition, a graph is triangle-distinct if its triangle-degree function is injective. Assuming x and y have the same triangle degree in Gᶜ, injectivity of the triangle degree in G (the hypothesis htd) reduces proving x = y to proving that x and y have the same triangle degree in G.
steps.code:
· intro x y hxy
    apply htd

steps.claim: The triangle degrees of x and y in G are equal, which proves x = y and completes the proof.
steps.explanation: By `simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl`, the triangle degree of any vertex v in Gᶜ is given in ℚ by a constant depending only on N and r minus its triangle degree in G. Since x and y have equal triangle degrees in Gᶜ, linear arithmetic over ℚ implies that their triangle degrees in G are equal. Casting this equality back from ℚ to ℕ closes the goal.
steps.code:
have h1 := simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl G r N hN hreg x
    have h2 := simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl G r N hN hreg y
    have : (simple_graph_triangle_degree G x : ℚ) = simple_graph_triangle_degree G y := by
      rw [hxy] at h1; linarith
    exact_mod_cast this

glossary.hreg.compl: If a graph G on a finite vertex set V is r-regular, then its complement Gᶜ is regular of degree |V| - 1 - r.
glossary.simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl: For an r-regular graph G on N vertices, the triangle degree of any vertex v in Gᶜ equals ((N - r - 1).choose 2) - N * r / 2 + r^2 - (triangle degree of v in G), evaluated in ℚ.

caveats: The formula relating triangle degrees in the complement graph and the original graph (`simple_graph_triangle_degree_compl`) is stated over the rational numbers ℚ to handle division by 2, requiring the equality of triangle degrees in G to be derived in ℚ before being cast back to ℕ via `exact_mod_cast`.

declarations.name: simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist
declarations.informal: In the clique blow-up H of G, two vertices x ∈ Q_i and y ∈ Q_j with i ≠ j are at the same distance in H as v_i and v_j in G (including distance ∞ when disconnected).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (a : V → ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) (p q : Σ i, Fin (a i)) (hpq : p.1 ≠ q.1) :
    (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).edist p q = G.edist p.1 q.1
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_proj {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (a : V → ℕ)
    {p q : Σ i, Fin (a i)} (w : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).Walk p q) :
    ∃ w' : G.Walk p.1 q.1, w'.length ≤ w.length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => exact ⟨SimpleGraph.Walk.nil, le_rfl⟩
  | @cons x y z h w ih =>
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := ih
    rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons]
    have h' : (x.1 = y.1 ∧ x ≠ y) ∨ G.Adj x.1 y.1 := h
    rcases h' with ⟨hxy, -⟩ | h'
    · exact ⟨w'.copy hxy.symm rfl, by rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_copy]; omega⟩
    · exact ⟨SimpleGraph.Walk.cons h' w', by rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons]; omega⟩

theorem simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_lift {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (a : V → ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) {i j : V} (w : G.Walk i j) :
    ∀ p q : Σ i, Fin (a i), p.1 = i → q.1 = j → 1 ≤ w.length →
      ∃ w' : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).Walk p q, w'.length ≤ w.length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => intro p q _ _ h; simp at h
  | @cons x y z h w ih =>
    intro p q hp hq _
    by_cases hw : w.length = 0
    · have hyz : y = z := SimpleGraph.Walk.eq_of_length_eq_zero hw
      have hadj : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).Adj p q :=
        Or.inr (by rw [hp, hq, ← hyz]; exact h)
      refine ⟨SimpleGraph.Walk.cons hadj SimpleGraph.Walk.nil, ?_⟩
      simp
    · obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := ih ⟨y, ⟨0, ha y⟩⟩ q rfl hq (Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 hw)
      have hadj : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).Adj p ⟨y, ⟨0, ha y⟩⟩ :=
        Or.inr (by rw [hp]; exact h)
      refine ⟨SimpleGraph.Walk.cons hadj w', ?_⟩
      simp only [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons]; omega

theorem simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (a : V → ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) (p q : Σ i, Fin (a i)) (hpq : p.1 ≠ q.1) :
    (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).edist p q = G.edist p.1 q.1 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · by_cases htop : G.edist p.1 q.1 = ⊤
    · rw [htop]; exact le_top
    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_edist_ne_top htop
    have h1 : 1 ≤ w.length := by
      by_contra h0
      exact hpq (SimpleGraph.Walk.eq_of_length_eq_zero (p := w) (by omega))
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_lift G a ha w p q rfl rfl h1
    calc (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).edist p q ≤ w'.length := SimpleGraph.edist_le w'
      _ ≤ w.length := by exact_mod_cast hw'
      _ = G.edist p.1 q.1 := hw
  · by_cases htop : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).edist p q = ⊤
    · rw [htop]; exact le_top
    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_edist_ne_top htop
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_proj G a w
    calc G.edist p.1 q.1 ≤ w'.length := SimpleGraph.edist_le w'
      _ ≤ w.length := by exact_mod_cast hw'
      _ = _ := hw
declarations.citation: Claim 1 in the proof of arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Theorem 1.6; serves forall_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup.

explanation.summary: To show that two vertices in different fibers have the same distance in the clique blow-up as their base vertices in G, the proof establishes mutual inequalities via antisymmetry. For the forward inequality, any shortest walk in G has length at least 1 (since the base vertices are distinct) and lifts edge-by-edge to a walk of the same length in the blow-up, using the assumption that all fibers are nonempty. For the reverse inequality, any walk in the blow-up projects to a walk in G of length at most that of the original walk, contracting internal clique edges to length zero and preserving edges between different fibers. Both inequalities extend naturally to the disconnected case where distances are infinite.

steps.claim: The empty walk in the clique blow-up projects to the empty walk in G.
steps.explanation: By induction on the walk w in the blow-up, the base case of an empty walk (nil) between vertices in the same fiber projects to the empty walk in G (SimpleGraph.Walk.nil), which trivially has length 0 ≤ 0.
steps.code:
induction w with
  | nil => exact ⟨SimpleGraph.Walk.nil, le_rfl⟩

steps.claim: Any walk in the clique blow-up projects to a walk in G of length at most that of the original walk.
steps.explanation: In the inductive step for an edge (x, y) followed by a walk w from y to z, the induction hypothesis provides a projected walk w' in G from y.1 to z.1 with |w'| ≤ |w|. By definition of the blow-up, the edge (x, y) is either internal to a fiber (x.1 = y.1) or connects adjacent fibers (G.Adj x.1 y.1). If internal, w' already connects x.1 to z.1 (via w'.copy), giving a walk of length |w'| ≤ |w| + 1. If between adjacent fibers, prepending this edge to w' via SimpleGraph.Walk.cons yields a walk of length |w'| + 1 ≤ |w| + 1.
steps.code:
| @cons x y z h w ih =>
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := ih
    rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons]
    have h' : (x.1 = y.1 ∧ x ≠ y) ∨ G.Adj x.1 y.1 := h
    rcases h' with ⟨hxy, -⟩ | h'
    · exact ⟨w'.copy hxy.symm rfl, by rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_copy]; omega⟩
    · exact ⟨SimpleGraph.Walk.cons h' w', by rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons]; omega⟩

steps.claim: A walk of length at least 1 cannot be empty.
steps.explanation: To show that any walk of length at least 1 in G lifts to the blow-up, we induct on the walk w. The base case of an empty walk is impossible since its length is 0, which contradicts the hypothesis 1 ≤ |w|.
steps.code:
induction w with
  | nil => intro p q _ _ h; simp at h

steps.claim: A single-edge walk in G lifts to an edge between corresponding fibers in the blow-up.
steps.explanation: In the inductive step for a walk starting with edge x ~ y, if the remaining walk w has length 0, then y = z. Since x is adjacent to y in G, any vertex p over x is adjacent in the blow-up to any vertex q over z. The single-edge walk from p to q in the blow-up has length 1, which is at most the length of the original walk.
steps.code:
| @cons x y z h w ih =>
    intro p q hp hq _
    by_cases hw : w.length = 0
    · have hyz : y = z := SimpleGraph.Walk.eq_of_length_eq_zero hw
      have hadj : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).Adj p q :=
        Or.inr (by rw [hp, hq, ← hyz]; exact h)
      refine ⟨SimpleGraph.Walk.cons hadj SimpleGraph.Walk.nil, ?_⟩
      simp

steps.claim: A walk of length at least 2 in G lifts inductively through a chosen vertex in the intermediate fiber.
steps.explanation: If the remaining walk w has nonzero length, then |w| ≥ 1. Since the fiber over y is nonempty (0 < a(y)), we choose a canonical representative vertex ⟨y, 0⟩ in that fiber. Applying the induction hypothesis to this vertex and q yields a lifted walk w' of length |w'| ≤ |w|. Prepending the blow-up edge between p and ⟨y, 0⟩ produces a walk from p to q of length |w'| + 1 ≤ |w| + 1.
steps.code:
· obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := ih ⟨y, ⟨0, ha y⟩⟩ q rfl hq (Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.2 hw)
      have hadj : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).Adj p ⟨y, ⟨0, ha y⟩⟩ :=
        Or.inr (by rw [hp]; exact h)
      refine ⟨SimpleGraph.Walk.cons hadj w', ?_⟩
      simp only [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons]; omega

steps.claim: Equality of extended distances reduces to mutual inequalities.
steps.explanation: We apply the antisymmetry of the partial order on extended natural numbers (le_antisymm), reducing the equality of distances to proving that the blow-up distance is bounded by the graph distance, and conversely.
steps.code: apply le_antisymm

steps.claim: The blow-up distance is bounded by the graph distance when the base vertices are disconnected.
steps.explanation: We case split on whether G.edist p.1 q.1 = ⊤. If the distance in G is ⊤ (disconnected), the inequality edist_H(p, q) ≤ ⊤ holds trivially by le_top.
steps.code:
· by_cases htop : G.edist p.1 q.1 = ⊤
    · rw [htop]; exact le_top

steps.claim: When the base vertices are connected, the blow-up distance is bounded above by the graph distance.
steps.explanation: When G.edist p.1 q.1 ≠ ⊤, there exists a shortest walk w in G between p.1 and q.1 whose length equals the distance (SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_edist_ne_top). Because p.1 ≠ q.1, this walk has length at least 1. By simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_lift, w lifts to a walk w' from p to q in the blow-up with |w'| ≤ |w|. Since the blow-up distance is bounded by the length of any walk (SimpleGraph.edist_le), we obtain edist_H(p, q) ≤ |w'| ≤ |w| = edist_G(p.1, q.1).
steps.code:
obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_edist_ne_top htop
    have h1 : 1 ≤ w.length := by
      by_contra h0
      exact hpq (SimpleGraph.Walk.eq_of_length_eq_zero (p := w) (by omega))
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_lift G a ha w p q rfl rfl h1
    calc (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).edist p q ≤ w'.length := SimpleGraph.edist_le w'
      _ ≤ w.length := by exact_mod_cast hw'
      _ = G.edist p.1 q.1 := hw

steps.claim: The graph distance is bounded by the blow-up distance when the fiber vertices are disconnected.
steps.explanation: Similarly, we case split on whether the distance between p and q in the blow-up is ⊤. If so, the inequality edist_G(p.1, q.1) ≤ ⊤ holds trivially by le_top.
steps.code:
· by_cases htop : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).edist p q = ⊤
    · rw [htop]; exact le_top

steps.claim: When the fiber vertices are connected, the graph distance is bounded above by the blow-up distance.
steps.explanation: When the blow-up distance is finite, there exists a walk w between p and q realizing that distance. By simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_proj, w projects to a walk w' in G between p.1 and q.1 of length |w'| ≤ |w|. By SimpleGraph.edist_le, edist_G(p.1, q.1) ≤ |w'| ≤ |w| = edist_H(p, q), completing the proof.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_edist_ne_top htop
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_proj G a w
    calc G.edist p.1 q.1 ≤ w'.length := SimpleGraph.edist_le w'
      _ ≤ w.length := by exact_mod_cast hw'
      _ = _ := hw

glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.nil: The empty walk from a vertex to itself, having length 0.
glossary.le_rfl: Reflexivity of a preorder: every element is less than or equal to itself (a ≤ a).
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons: Prepending an edge to a walk increases its length by 1: |h :: p| = |p| + 1.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.length_copy: Transporting the endpoints of a walk along propositional equalities preserves its length: |p.copy hu hv| = |p|.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.cons: Extends a walk from v to w by prepending an edge u ~ v, producing a walk from u to w.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.eq_of_length_eq_zero: A walk of length 0 starts and ends at the same vertex: if |p| = 0, then u = v.
glossary.le_antisymm: Antisymmetry of a partial order: if a ≤ b and b ≤ a, then a = b.
glossary.le_top: Every element in an order with a greatest element is bounded above by ⊤ (a ≤ ⊤).
glossary.SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_edist_ne_top: If the extended distance between two vertices is finite, there exists a walk between them whose length equals that distance.
glossary.simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_lift: When all fibers are nonempty, every walk of length at least 1 in G lifts to a walk between specified fiber vertices in the clique blow-up with length at most that of the original walk.
glossary.SimpleGraph.edist_le: The extended distance between two vertices is at most the length of any walk connecting them: edist u v ≤ |p|.
glossary.simple_graph_clique_blowup_walk_proj: Every walk in the clique blow-up projects to a walk between the corresponding base vertices in G with length at most that of the original walk.

caveats: The requirement p.1 ≠ q.1 in simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist is essential: two distinct vertices in the same fiber have distance 1 in the blow-up (since each fiber is turned into a clique), whereas their base projection in G is a single vertex with self-distance 0.

The projection of walks uses SimpleGraph.Walk.copy to adjust walk endpoints along propositional equalities without adding edges, contracting edges internal to a clique into stationary transitions in the base graph.

declarations.name: simple_graph_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup
declarations.informal: For every d ≥ 1 and positive integers a_i, G^d is well-covered iff H^d is well-covered, where H = G[K_{a_1}, …, K_{a_n}].
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (a : V → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d) ↔
      simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a) d)
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_clique_blowup_power_adj_iff {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (a : V → ℕ)
    (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) (p q : Σ i, Fin (a i)) :
    (simple_graph_power (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a) d).Adj p q ↔
      p ≠ q ∧ (p.1 = q.1 ∨ (simple_graph_power G d).Adj p.1 q.1) := by
  simp only [simple_graph_power]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hne, hle⟩
    refine ⟨hne, ?_⟩
    by_cases h : p.1 = q.1
    · exact Or.inl h
    · right; exact ⟨h, by rwa [← simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist G a ha p q h]⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, h | ⟨h1, h2⟩⟩
    · refine ⟨hne, ?_⟩
      have hadj : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).Adj p q := Or.inl ⟨h, hne⟩
      rw [SimpleGraph.edist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 hadj]; exact_mod_cast hd
    · exact ⟨hne, by rwa [simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist G a ha p q h1]⟩

theorem simple_graph_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (a : V → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d) :
    simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d) ↔
      simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a) d) := by
  set Gd := simple_graph_power G d
  set Hd := simple_graph_power (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a) d
  have hA := simple_graph_clique_blowup_power_adj_iff G a ha d hd
  -- independence in Hd
  have indep_iff : ∀ I : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i)), Hd.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i))) ↔
      (Set.InjOn (Sigma.fst : (Σ i, Fin (a i)) → V) (I : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i))) ∧ Gd.IsIndepSet ((I.image Sigma.fst : Finset V) : Set V)) := by
    intro I
    constructor
    · intro hI
      refine ⟨fun x hx y hy hxy => ?_, ?_⟩
      · by_contra hne
        exact hI hx hy hne ((hA x y).2 ⟨hne, Or.inl hxy⟩)
      · intro i hi j hj hij hadj
        simp only [Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe] at hi hj
        obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := hi
        obtain ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ := hj
        have hne : x ≠ y := fun e => hij (e ▸ rfl)
        exact hI hx hy hne ((hA x y).2 ⟨hne, Or.inr hadj⟩)
    · rintro ⟨hinj, hJ⟩ x hx y hy hne hadj
      obtain ⟨-, h | h⟩ := (hA x y).1 hadj
      · exact hne (hinj hx hy h)
      · refine hJ ?_ ?_ (Gd.ne_of_adj h) h
        · simp only [Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe]; exact ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
        · simp only [Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe]; exact ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
  -- lift of a set of parts
  let L : Finset V → Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i)) := fun J => J.image (fun i => ⟨i, ⟨0, ha i⟩⟩)
  have L_inj : Function.Injective (fun i : V => (⟨i, ⟨0, ha i⟩⟩ : Σ i, Fin (a i))) := by
    intro i j h; exact congrArg Sigma.fst h
  have L_card : ∀ J, (L J).card = J.card := fun J => Finset.card_image_of_injective _ L_inj
  have L_fst : ∀ J, (L J).image Sigma.fst = J := by
    intro J; ext x; simp [L]
  -- maximal independent sets correspond
  have max_proj : ∀ I, Maximal (fun u : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i)) => Hd.IsIndepSet (u : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i)))) I →
      Maximal (fun u : Finset V => Gd.IsIndepSet (u : Set V)) (I.image Sigma.fst) ∧
        (I.image Sigma.fst).card = I.card := by
    intro I hI
    obtain ⟨hinj, hJ⟩ := (indep_iff I).1 hI.1
    refine ⟨⟨hJ, fun t ht hsub => ?_⟩, Finset.card_image_of_injOn hinj⟩
    intro k hk
    by_contra hkn
    set z : Σ i, Fin (a i) := ⟨k, ⟨0, ha k⟩⟩
    have hzI : z ∉ I := fun hz => hkn (Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨z, hz, rfl⟩)
    have hind : Hd.IsIndepSet ((insert z I : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i))) : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i))) := by
      intro x hx y hy hne hadj
      simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Set.mem_insert_iff, Finset.mem_coe] at hx hy
      have hnz : ∀ x ∈ I, ¬ Hd.Adj z x := by
        intro x hx h
        obtain ⟨-, h | h⟩ := (hA z x).1 h
        · exact hkn (Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨x, hx, h.symm⟩)
        · exact ht hk (hsub (Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)) (Gd.ne_of_adj h) h
      rcases hx with rfl | hx <;> rcases hy with rfl | hy
      · exact hne rfl
      · exact hnz y hy hadj
      · exact hnz x hx hadj.symm
      · exact hI.1 hx hy hne hadj
    have := hI.2 hind (Finset.subset_insert _ _)
    exact hzI (this (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _))
  have max_lift : ∀ J, Maximal (fun u : Finset V => Gd.IsIndepSet (u : Set V)) J →
      Maximal (fun u : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i)) => Hd.IsIndepSet (u : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i)))) (L J) := by
    intro J hJ
    have hindL : Hd.IsIndepSet ((L J : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i))) : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i))) := by
      refine (indep_iff _).2 ⟨?_, by rw [L_fst]; exact hJ.1⟩
      intro x hx y hy hxy
      simp only [L, Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe] at hx hy
      obtain ⟨i, -, rfl⟩ := hx
      obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := hy
      simp only at hxy; subst hxy; rfl
    refine ⟨hindL, fun t ht hsub => ?_⟩
    intro y hy
    by_contra hyn
    by_cases hyJ : y.1 ∈ J
    · -- y is in the same part as a member of L J
      have hmem : (⟨y.1, ⟨0, ha y.1⟩⟩ : Σ i, Fin (a i)) ∈ L J :=
        Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨y.1, hyJ, rfl⟩
      have hne : y ≠ ⟨y.1, ⟨0, ha y.1⟩⟩ := fun e => hyn (e ▸ hmem)
      exact ht hy (hsub hmem) hne ((hA _ _).2 ⟨hne, Or.inl rfl⟩)
    · have hind : Gd.IsIndepSet ((insert y.1 J : Finset V) : Set V) := by
        intro i hi j hj hij hadj
        simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Set.mem_insert_iff, Finset.mem_coe] at hi hj
        have hny : ∀ j ∈ J, ¬ Gd.Adj y.1 j := by
          intro j hj h
          have hmem : (⟨j, ⟨0, ha j⟩⟩ : Σ i, Fin (a i)) ∈ L J := Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨j, hj, rfl⟩
          have hne : y ≠ ⟨j, ⟨0, ha j⟩⟩ := fun e => hyn (e ▸ hmem)
          exact ht hy (hsub hmem) hne ((hA _ _).2 ⟨hne, Or.inr h⟩)
        rcases hi with rfl | hi <;> rcases hj with rfl | hj
        · exact hij rfl
        · exact hny j hj hadj
        · exact hny i hi hadj.symm
        · exact hJ.1 hi hj hij hadj
      exact hyJ (hJ.2 hind (Finset.subset_insert _ _) (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _))
  constructor
  · intro hG I I' hI hI'
    obtain ⟨h1, c1⟩ := max_proj I hI
    obtain ⟨h2, c2⟩ := max_proj I' hI'
    rw [← c1, ← c2]; exact hG _ _ h1 h2
  · intro hH J J' hJ hJ'
    rw [← L_card J, ← L_card J']
    exact hH _ _ (max_lift J hJ) (max_lift J' hJ')
declarations.citation: The per-d form of the argument proving arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Theorem 1.6 (Claim 2 there: maximal independent sets of H^d are exactly one vertex from Q_i for each v_i in a maximal independent set of G^d).

explanation.summary: For any graph G, positive weights a_i, and d ≥ 1, the d-th graph power G^d is well-covered if and only if the d-th power of the clique blowup H = G[K_{a_1}, …, K_{a_n}] is well-covered. The argument hinges on the fact that two vertices in H are adjacent in H^d if and only if they are distinct and either belong to the same clique fiber or project to adjacent vertices in G^d. As a result, independent sets in H^d correspond to independent sets in G^d via projection, which induces a size-preserving bijection between maximal independent sets in H^d and maximal independent sets in G^d. Well-coveredness (every maximal independent set having the same cardinality) therefore transfers directly between G^d and H^d.

steps.claim: Two vertices p and q in the clique blowup H are adjacent in the graph power H^d if and only if p ≠ q and either they share the same base vertex (p.1 = q.1) or their projections are adjacent in G^d.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of the graph power, adjacency means p ≠ q and the distance d_H(p, q) ≤ d. If p.1 = q.1 with p ≠ q, then p and q are adjacent in the clique fiber, giving d_H(p, q) = 1 ≤ d. If p.1 ≠ q.1, simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist equates d_H(p, q) with d_G(p.1, q.1), so d_H(p, q) ≤ d is equivalent to adjacency in G^d.
steps.code:
simp only [simple_graph_power]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hne, hle⟩
    refine ⟨hne, ?_⟩
    by_cases h : p.1 = q.1
    · exact Or.inl h
    · right; exact ⟨h, by rwa [← simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist G a ha p q h]⟩
  · rintro ⟨hne, h | ⟨h1, h2⟩⟩
    · refine ⟨hne, ?_⟩
      have hadj : (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a).Adj p q := Or.inl ⟨h, hne⟩
      rw [SimpleGraph.edist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 hadj]; exact_mod_cast hd
    · exact ⟨hne, by rwa [simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist G a ha p q h1]⟩

steps.claim: A subset I of vertices of H is independent in H^d if and only if the projection π : (i, x) ↦ i is injective on I and the projected set π(I) is independent in G^d.
steps.explanation: Using the adjacency criterion hA for H^d: if I is independent, any two distinct vertices in I cannot share the same base vertex (which would make them adjacent in H^d), proving injectivity of π on I; nor can their projections be adjacent in G^d (which would also make them adjacent in H^d), showing π(I) is independent in G^d. Conversely, if π is injective on I and π(I) is independent in G^d, no two distinct vertices of I can be adjacent in H^d.
steps.code:
set Gd := simple_graph_power G d
  set Hd := simple_graph_power (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a) d
  have hA := simple_graph_clique_blowup_power_adj_iff G a ha d hd
  -- independence in Hd
  have indep_iff : ∀ I : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i)), Hd.IsIndepSet (I : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i))) ↔
      (Set.InjOn (Sigma.fst : (Σ i, Fin (a i)) → V) (I : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i))) ∧ Gd.IsIndepSet ((I.image Sigma.fst : Finset V) : Set V)) := by
    intro I
    constructor
    · intro hI
      refine ⟨fun x hx y hy hxy => ?_, ?_⟩
      · by_contra hne
        exact hI hx hy hne ((hA x y).2 ⟨hne, Or.inl hxy⟩)
      · intro i hi j hj hij hadj
        simp only [Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe] at hi hj
        obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := hi
        obtain ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩ := hj
        have hne : x ≠ y := fun e => hij (e ▸ rfl)
        exact hI hx hy hne ((hA x y).2 ⟨hne, Or.inr hadj⟩)
    · rintro ⟨hinj, hJ⟩ x hx y hy hne hadj
      obtain ⟨-, h | h⟩ := (hA x y).1 hadj
      · exact hne (hinj hx hy h)
      · refine hJ ?_ ?_ (Gd.ne_of_adj h) h
        · simp only [Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe]; exact ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
        · simp only [Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe]; exact ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩

steps.claim: The canonical section L(J) = {(j, 0) : j ∈ J} embeds subsets of V(G) into subsets of V(H) with |L(J)| = |J| and π(L(J)) = J.
steps.explanation: Because each a(i) > 0, the element 0 is available in every fiber Fin(a(i)). The assignment i ↦ (i, 0) is injective by projecting to the first component using congrArg, so L preserves cardinality by Finset.card_image_of_injective. Projecting L(J) back to the first component recovers J.
steps.code:
let L : Finset V → Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i)) := fun J => J.image (fun i => ⟨i, ⟨0, ha i⟩⟩)
  have L_inj : Function.Injective (fun i : V => (⟨i, ⟨0, ha i⟩⟩ : Σ i, Fin (a i))) := by
    intro i j h; exact congrArg Sigma.fst h
  have L_card : ∀ J, (L J).card = J.card := fun J => Finset.card_image_of_injective _ L_inj
  have L_fst : ∀ J, (L J).image Sigma.fst = J := by
    intro J; ext x; simp [L]

steps.claim: If I is a maximal independent set in H^d, then its projection π(I) is a maximal independent set in G^d and |π(I)| = |I|.
steps.explanation: By injectivity of the projection on I, |π(I)| = |I| via Finset.card_image_of_injOn. If π(I) were not maximal in G^d, there would be some k ∉ π(I) independent from π(I) in G^d. Then adding z = (k, 0) to I would form a strictly larger independent set in H^d (using Finset.subset_insert and Finset.mem_insert_self), contradicting the maximality of I in H^d.
steps.code:
have max_proj : ∀ I, Maximal (fun u : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i)) => Hd.IsIndepSet (u : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i)))) I →
      Maximal (fun u : Finset V => Gd.IsIndepSet (u : Set V)) (I.image Sigma.fst) ∧
        (I.image Sigma.fst).card = I.card := by
    intro I hI
    obtain ⟨hinj, hJ⟩ := (indep_iff I).1 hI.1
    refine ⟨⟨hJ, fun t ht hsub => ?_⟩, Finset.card_image_of_injOn hinj⟩
    intro k hk
    by_contra hkn
    set z : Σ i, Fin (a i) := ⟨k, ⟨0, ha k⟩⟩
    have hzI : z ∉ I := fun hz => hkn (Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨z, hz, rfl⟩)
    have hind : Hd.IsIndepSet ((insert z I : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i))) : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i))) := by
      intro x hx y hy hne hadj
      simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Set.mem_insert_iff, Finset.mem_coe] at hx hy
      have hnz : ∀ x ∈ I, ¬ Hd.Adj z x := by
        intro x hx h
        obtain ⟨-, h | h⟩ := (hA z x).1 h
        · exact hkn (Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨x, hx, h.symm⟩)
        · exact ht hk (hsub (Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)) (Gd.ne_of_adj h) h
      rcases hx with rfl | hx <;> rcases hy with rfl | hy
      · exact hne rfl
      · exact hnz y hy hadj
      · exact hnz x hx hadj.symm
      · exact hI.1 hx hy hne hadj
    have := hI.2 hind (Finset.subset_insert _ _)
    exact hzI (this (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _))

steps.claim: If J is a maximal independent set in G^d, then its canonical lift L(J) is a maximal independent set in H^d.
steps.explanation: The lift L(J) is independent in H^d because π is injective on L(J) and π(L(J)) = J is independent in G^d. If L(J) were not maximal, some y ∉ L(J) could be added to it. If y.1 ∈ J, y is adjacent in H^d to (y.1, 0) ∈ L(J). If y.1 ∉ J, then J ∪ {y.1} would be an independent set in G^d strictly containing J (via Finset.subset_insert and Finset.mem_insert_self), contradicting maximality of J in G^d.
steps.code:
have max_lift : ∀ J, Maximal (fun u : Finset V => Gd.IsIndepSet (u : Set V)) J →
      Maximal (fun u : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i)) => Hd.IsIndepSet (u : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i)))) (L J) := by
    intro J hJ
    have hindL : Hd.IsIndepSet ((L J : Finset (Σ i, Fin (a i))) : Set (Σ i, Fin (a i))) := by
      refine (indep_iff _).2 ⟨?_, by rw [L_fst]; exact hJ.1⟩
      intro x hx y hy hxy
      simp only [L, Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe] at hx hy
      obtain ⟨i, -, rfl⟩ := hx
      obtain ⟨j, -, rfl⟩ := hy
      simp only at hxy; subst hxy; rfl
    refine ⟨hindL, fun t ht hsub => ?_⟩
    intro y hy
    by_contra hyn
    by_cases hyJ : y.1 ∈ J
    · -- y is in the same part as a member of L J
      have hmem : (⟨y.1, ⟨0, ha y.1⟩⟩ : Σ i, Fin (a i)) ∈ L J :=
        Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨y.1, hyJ, rfl⟩
      have hne : y ≠ ⟨y.1, ⟨0, ha y.1⟩⟩ := fun e => hyn (e ▸ hmem)
      exact ht hy (hsub hmem) hne ((hA _ _).2 ⟨hne, Or.inl rfl⟩)
    · have hind : Gd.IsIndepSet ((insert y.1 J : Finset V) : Set V) := by
        intro i hi j hj hij hadj
        simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Set.mem_insert_iff, Finset.mem_coe] at hi hj
        have hny : ∀ j ∈ J, ¬ Gd.Adj y.1 j := by
          intro j hj h
          have hmem : (⟨j, ⟨0, ha j⟩⟩ : Σ i, Fin (a i)) ∈ L J := Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨j, hj, rfl⟩
          have hne : y ≠ ⟨j, ⟨0, ha j⟩⟩ := fun e => hyn (e ▸ hmem)
          exact ht hy (hsub hmem) hne ((hA _ _).2 ⟨hne, Or.inr h⟩)
        rcases hi with rfl | hi <;> rcases hj with rfl | hj
        · exact hij rfl
        · exact hny j hj hadj
        · exact hny i hi hadj.symm
        · exact hJ.1 hi hj hij hadj
      exact hyJ (hJ.2 hind (Finset.subset_insert _ _) (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _))

steps.claim: G^d is well-covered if and only if H^d is well-covered.
steps.explanation: A graph is well-covered when all maximal independent sets have identical sizes. If G^d is well-covered, any two maximal independent sets I, I' in H^d project to maximal independent sets in G^d with the same sizes |I| and |I'|, so |I| = |I'|. Conversely, if H^d is well-covered, any two maximal independent sets J, J' in G^d lift to maximal independent sets in H^d of sizes |J| and |J'|, so |J| = |J'|.
steps.code:
constructor
  · intro hG I I' hI hI'
    obtain ⟨h1, c1⟩ := max_proj I hI
    obtain ⟨h2, c2⟩ := max_proj I' hI'
    rw [← c1, ← c2]; exact hG _ _ h1 h2
  · intro hH J J' hJ hJ'
    rw [← L_card J, ← L_card J']
    exact hH _ _ (max_lift J hJ) (max_lift J' hJ')

glossary.simple_graph_clique_blowup_edist: For two vertices in the clique blowup whose projections to the base graph are distinct, their distance in the clique blowup equals the distance between their projections in the base graph.
glossary.simple_graph_clique_blowup_power_adj_iff: Two vertices in the clique blowup are adjacent in its d-th graph power if and only if they are distinct and either have the same projection or their projections are adjacent in the d-th power of the base graph.
glossary.congrArg: Equal inputs produce equal outputs under any function.
glossary.Finset.card_image_of_injective: An injective map between finite sets preserves the cardinality of the set under its image.
glossary.Finset.card_image_of_injOn: A map injective on a finite set preserves the set's cardinality under its image.
glossary.Finset.subset_insert: A set is a subset of the result of inserting an element into it.
glossary.Finset.mem_insert_self: An element belongs to the set obtained by inserting that element into any set.

declarations.name: forall_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup
declarations.informal: Let G be a finite simple graph and a_1, …, a_n positive integers, H = G[K_{a_1}, …, K_{a_n}] its clique blow-up. Then G^d is well-covered for all d ≥ 1 iff H^d is well-covered for all d ≥ 1.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (a : V → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) :
    (∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)) ↔
      (∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d →
        simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a) d))
declarations.source:
theorem forall_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (a : V → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, 0 < a i) :
    (∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)) ↔
      (∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d →
        simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power (simple_graph_clique_blowup G a) d)) :=
  forall_congr' fun d => imp_congr_right fun hd =>
    simple_graph_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup G a ha d hd
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Theorem 1.6.

explanation.summary: The universal statement across all powers d ≥ 1 is reduced by logical congruence to the claim for an individual exponent d. For any fixed d ≥ 1, the theorem simple_graph_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup already establishes that G^d is well-covered if and only if the d-th power of the clique blow-up is well-covered. Applying universal and conditional congruence yields the equivalence for all d ≥ 1 simultaneously.

steps.claim: For all d ≥ 1, G^d is well-covered if and only if for all d ≥ 1, the d-th power of the clique blow-up is well-covered.
steps.explanation: Universal quantifier congruence (forall_congr') and implication congruence (imp_congr_right) reduce the equivalence of the universally quantified assertions over d ≥ 1 to the pointwise equivalence for each fixed exponent d ≥ 1. That pointwise equivalence is supplied directly by simple_graph_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup applied to G, the weight function a, its positivity hypothesis ha, and the assumption hd that d ≥ 1.
steps.code:
forall_congr' fun d => imp_congr_right fun hd =>
    simple_graph_power_well_covered_iff_clique_blowup G a ha d hd

glossary.forall_congr': Universally quantified statements are logically equivalent if their underlying predicates are pointwise equivalent for every argument.
glossary.imp_congr_right: Two implications with the same antecedent are equivalent if the antecedent implies that their consequents are equivalent.
glossary.simple_graph_power_well_covered_iff_cliq: For a finite graph G and positive weights a, and any fixed power exponent d ≥ 1, the d-th power G^d is well-covered if and only if the d-th power of the clique blow-up G[K_a]^d is well-covered.

declarations.name: finset_one_inclusion_graph
declarations.informal: The one-inclusion graph G_1(F) of a set system F: its vertices are the members of F, two members adjacent when their symmetric difference has exactly one element.
declarations.statement:
def finset_one_inclusion_graph {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (𝓕 : Finset (Finset α)) :
    SimpleGraph 𝓕
declarations.source:
/-- The one-inclusion graph of a set system: its members are the vertices, and two members are adjacent when their symmetric difference has exactly one element. -/
def finset_one_inclusion_graph {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (𝓕 : Finset (Finset α)) :
    SimpleGraph 𝓕 where
  Adj A B := (symmDiff (A : Finset α) B).card = 1
  symm := ⟨fun A B (h : (symmDiff (A : Finset α) B).card = 1) => by rwa [symmDiff_comm]⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun A (h : (symmDiff (A : Finset α) A).card = 1) => by simp at h⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.08151 (Polynomial-in-r bounds for forbidden traces of uniform hypergraphs), Sec. 2.2 (one-inclusion graph G_1(F), before Lemma 2). Vertices are the members of 𝓕 (a subtype).

declarations.name: finset_one_inclusion_graph_adj_empty_singleton
declarations.informal: In the one-inclusion graph of {∅, {a}}, ∅ and {a} are adjacent.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_one_inclusion_graph_adj_empty_singleton {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (a : α) :
    (finset_one_inclusion_graph ({∅, {a}} : Finset (Finset α))).Adj
      ⟨∅, by simp⟩ ⟨{a}, by simp⟩
declarations.source:
theorem finset_one_inclusion_graph_adj_empty_singleton {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (a : α) :
    (finset_one_inclusion_graph ({∅, {a}} : Finset (Finset α))).Adj
      ⟨∅, by simp⟩ ⟨{a}, by simp⟩ := by
  show (symmDiff (∅ : Finset α) {a}).card = 1
  have h : symmDiff (∅ : Finset α) {a} = {a} := by
    ext x; simp [Finset.mem_symmDiff]
  rw [h, Finset.card_singleton]
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for finset_one_inclusion_graph (arXiv:2610.08151 (Polynomial-in-r bounds for forbidden traces of uniform hypergraphs)).

explanation.summary: Two vertices in the one-inclusion graph are adjacent if and only if their symmetric difference has cardinality 1. The proof shows that the symmetric difference of the empty set and {a} equals {a}, and then evaluates its cardinality to 1 using Finset.card_singleton.

steps.claim: ∅ and {a} are members of the family {∅, {a}}
steps.explanation: The vertices of the one-inclusion graph are terms of the subtype of elements belonging to {∅, {a}}. The membership conditions ∅ ∈ {∅, {a}} and {a} ∈ {∅, {a}} are verified by simplification.
steps.code: ⟨∅, by simp⟩ ⟨{a}, by simp⟩ := by

steps.claim: Adjacency of ∅ and {a} reduces to showing |∅ △ {a}| = 1
steps.explanation: By definition of the one-inclusion graph, two vertices are adjacent if and only if the cardinality of their symmetric difference is 1.
steps.code: show (symmDiff (∅ : Finset α) {a}).card = 1

steps.explanation: By extensionality, two finite sets are equal if they contain the same elements. By Finset.mem_symmDiff, x ∈ ∅ △ {a} means (x ∈ ∅ ∧ x ∉ {a}) ∨ (x ∈ {a} ∧ x ∉ ∅); since ∅ has no elements, simplification reduces this to x ∈ {a}.
steps.code:
have h : symmDiff (∅ : Finset α) {a} = {a} := by
    ext x; simp [Finset.mem_symmDiff]

steps.claim: The symmetric difference has cardinality 1, completing the proof
steps.explanation: Rewriting the symmetric difference with {a} using the identity just established, the goal becomes |{a}| = 1, which holds by Finset.card_singleton.
steps.code: rw [h, Finset.card_singleton]

glossary.Finset.mem_symmDiff: An element belongs to the symmetric difference of two finite sets if and only if it belongs to the first and not the second, or to the second and not the first.
glossary.Finset.card_singleton: The cardinality of any singleton finite set {a} is 1.

declarations.name: finset_one_inclusion_graph_not_adj_empty_pair
declarations.informal: In the one-inclusion graph of {∅, {a, b}} with a ≠ b, ∅ and {a, b} are not adjacent.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_one_inclusion_graph_not_adj_empty_pair {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (a b : α)
    (hab : a ≠ b) :
    ¬ (finset_one_inclusion_graph ({∅, {a, b}} : Finset (Finset α))).Adj
      ⟨∅, by simp⟩ ⟨{a, b}, by simp⟩
declarations.source:
theorem finset_one_inclusion_graph_not_adj_empty_pair {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (a b : α)
    (hab : a ≠ b) :
    ¬ (finset_one_inclusion_graph ({∅, {a, b}} : Finset (Finset α))).Adj
      ⟨∅, by simp⟩ ⟨{a, b}, by simp⟩ := by
  show ¬ (symmDiff (∅ : Finset α) {a, b}).card = 1
  have h : symmDiff (∅ : Finset α) {a, b} = {a, b} := by
    ext x; simp [Finset.mem_symmDiff]
  rw [h, Finset.card_pair hab]
  decide
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for finset_one_inclusion_graph (arXiv:2610.08151 (Polynomial-in-r bounds for forbidden traces of uniform hypergraphs)).

explanation.summary: In the one-inclusion graph of a family of finite sets, two vertices are adjacent if and only if their symmetric difference has cardinality 1. For the vertices ∅ and {a, b}, their symmetric difference is simply {a, b}. Since a ≠ b, this pair has cardinality 2 rather than 1, which rules out adjacency.

steps.claim: Non-adjacency of ∅ and {a, b} reduces to showing |∅ △ {a, b}| ≠ 1.
steps.explanation: The sets ∅ and {a, b} are verified to be members of {∅, {a, b}} inline by `simp`. By definition of `finset_one_inclusion_graph`, two vertices are adjacent if and only if the cardinality of their symmetric difference is 1. The `show` statement unfolds this definition, so the negated adjacency goal becomes ¬ (|∅ △ {a, b}| = 1).
steps.code:
⟨∅, by simp⟩ ⟨{a, b}, by simp⟩ := by
  show ¬ (symmDiff (∅ : Finset α) {a, b}).card = 1

steps.explanation: By extensionality (`ext x`), it suffices to show that an arbitrary element x is in ∅ △ {a, b} if and only if x ∈ {a, b}. Using `Finset.mem_symmDiff`, x belongs to the symmetric difference if and only if it is in exactly one of the sets. Since ∅ is empty, this condition simplifies to x ∈ {a, b}.
steps.code:
have h : symmDiff (∅ : Finset α) {a, b} = {a, b} := by
    ext x; simp [Finset.mem_symmDiff]

steps.claim: The cardinality of the symmetric difference is 2, which is not 1.
steps.explanation: Rewriting with the identity h replaces ∅ △ {a, b} with {a, b}. Because a ≠ b by hypothesis `hab`, `Finset.card_pair` evaluates |{a, b}| to 2. This reduces the goal to ¬ (2 = 1), which is closed by computational decision (`decide`).
steps.code:
rw [h, Finset.card_pair hab]
  decide

glossary.Finset.mem_symmDiff: An element belongs to the symmetric difference of two finite sets if and only if it belongs to one of the sets and not the other.
glossary.Finset.card_pair: A pair {a, b} of distinct elements (a ≠ b) has cardinality 2.

caveats: The subtype representations ⟨∅, ...⟩ and ⟨{a, b}, ...⟩ require explicit membership proofs that ∅ and {a, b} belong to {∅, {a, b}}; on line 4, these obligations are discharged inline by `simp`.

declarations.name: nat_prime_power_parts
declarations.informal: S(q): the set of maximal prime-power divisors of q, i.e. p^(v_p(q)) for each prime p dividing q.
declarations.statement: def nat_prime_power_parts (q : ℕ) : Finset ℕ
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.11098 (An improved lower bound for separating words by permutation automata), Lemma 2.3 (the set S(q) of maximal prime-power divisors of q).

declarations.name: nat_prime_power_parts_prime_pow
declarations.informal: For a prime p and k ≥ 1, S(p^k) = {p^k}.
declarations.statement:
theorem nat_prime_power_parts_prime_pow {p k : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    nat_prime_power_parts (p ^ k) = {p ^ k}
declarations.source:
theorem nat_prime_power_parts_prime_pow {p k : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    nat_prime_power_parts (p ^ k) = {p ^ k} := by
  unfold nat_prime_power_parts
  rw [Nat.primeFactors_prime_pow hk hp]
  simp [Nat.factorization_pow, hp.factorization_self]
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for nat_prime_power_parts (arXiv:2610.11098 (An improved lower bound for separating words by permutation automata)).

explanation.summary: By definition, the prime power parts of a number are obtained by raising each of its prime factors to its full multiplicity. Since p is prime and k ≥ 1, the only prime factor of p^k is p, with multiplicity k. Thus the set of prime power parts reduces to the singleton {p^k}.

steps.claim: By definition, the prime power parts of p^k is the image of the prime factors of p^k under the map q ↦ q ^ ((p^k).factorization q).
steps.explanation: Unfold the definition of `nat_prime_power_parts`.
steps.code: unfold nat_prime_power_parts

steps.claim: The domain of prime factors reduces to the singleton {p}.
steps.explanation: Because p is prime and k ≠ 0, the only prime factor of p^k is p. Applying `Nat.primeFactors_prime_pow` replaces (p ^ k).primeFactors with {p}.
steps.code: rw [Nat.primeFactors_prime_pow hk hp]

steps.claim: The prime power parts of p^k equals {p^k}.
steps.explanation: The image of {p} under q ↦ q ^ ((p^k).factorization q) evaluates at p to p ^ ((p^k).factorization p). By `Nat.factorization_pow`, the exponent is k * (p.factorization p), which simplifies to k * 1 = k via `hp.factorization_self`. Simplifying the singleton image closes the goal.
steps.code: simp [Nat.factorization_pow, hp.factorization_self]

glossary.Nat.primeFactors_prime_pow: For a prime p and k ≠ 0, the set of prime factors of p^k is {p}.
glossary.Nat.factorization_pow: The prime factorization of n^k is k times the prime factorization of n.
glossary.hp.factorization_self: For a prime p, the multiplicity of p in its own prime factorization is 1.

explanation.summary: The theorem asserts that the set of prime-power parts of 1 is empty. By definition, the prime-power parts of 1 are obtained by mapping each prime factor p of 1 to p^(v_p(1)). Because 1 has no prime factors, this initial set is empty, and the image of the empty set is empty.

steps.claim: nat_prime_power_parts 1 = ∅
