declarations.name: isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul
declarations.informal: For any matching M in a graph G, the number of vertices in M is at most twice the number of edges in M.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (M : G.Subgraph)
    (hM : M.IsMatching) : M.verts.encard ≤ 2 * M.edgeSet.encard
declarations.source:
noncomputable def isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul_endpoint {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (M : G.Subgraph)
    (x : M.edgeSet × Fin 2) : M.verts :=
  let p := Quot.out x.1.val
  have hAdj : M.Adj p.1 p.2 := by
    have h := x.1.2
    have hq := Quot.out_eq x.1.val
    rw [← hq] at h
    exact M.mem_edgeSet.mp h
  Fin.cases ⟨p.1, M.edge_vert hAdj⟩ (fun _ => ⟨p.2, M.edge_vert hAdj.symm⟩) x.2

lemma isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul_endpoint_surjective {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (M : G.Subgraph)
    (hM : M.IsMatching) : Function.Surjective (isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul_endpoint M) := by
  intro ⟨v, hv⟩
  obtain ⟨w, hw, -⟩ := hM hv
  have he : s(v, w) ∈ M.edgeSet := M.mem_edgeSet.mpr hw
  let e : M.edgeSet := ⟨s(v, w), he⟩
  have hq : Quot.mk (Sym2.Rel V) (Quot.out e.val) = s(v, w) := Quot.out_eq e.val
  have h_eq : s((Quot.out e.val).1, (Quot.out e.val).2) = s(v, w) := hq
  rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at h_eq
  rcases h_eq with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
  · use (e, 0)
    exact Subtype.ext h1
  · use (e, 1)
    exact Subtype.ext h2

/-- In any simple graph, the number of vertices in a matching M is at most twice the number of edges in M. -/
theorem isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} (M : G.Subgraph)
    (hM : M.IsMatching) : M.verts.encard ≤ 2 * M.edgeSet.encard := by
  have hsurj := isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul_endpoint_surjective M hM
  have hle : ENat.card M.verts ≤ ENat.card (M.edgeSet × Fin 2) :=
    ENat.card_le_card_of_injective (Function.injective_surjInv hsurj)
  rw [ENat.card_prod] at hle
  have hFin2 : ENat.card (Fin 2) = 2 := by simp
  rw [hFin2, mul_comm, ENat.card_coe_set_eq, ENat.card_coe_set_eq] at hle
  exact hle

    (hM : M.IsMatching) : M.verts.encard ≤ 2 * M.edgeSet.encard := by
  have hsurj := isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul_endpoint_surjective M hM
  have hle : ENat.card M.verts ≤ ENat.card (M.edgeSet × Fin 2) :=
    ENat.card_le_card_of_injective (Function.injective_surjInv hsurj)
  rw [ENat.card_prod] at hle
  have hFin2 : ENat.card (Fin 2) = 2 := by simp
  rw [hFin2, mul_comm, ENat.card_coe_set_eq, ENat.card_coe_set_eq] at hle
  exact hle

declarations.name: exists_isMatching_isVertexCover
declarations.informal: In any finite graph G, there exists a matching M such that M.verts is a vertex cover of G (i.e. an inclusion-maximal matching).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isMatching_isVertexCover {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    ∃ M : G.Subgraph, M.IsMatching ∧ G.IsVertexCover M.verts
declarations.source:
/-- In any finite simple graph G, there exists a matching M whose vertex set M.verts is a vertex cover of G. -/
theorem exists_isMatching_isVertexCover {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    ∃ M : G.Subgraph, M.IsMatching ∧ G.IsVertexCover M.verts := by
  classical
  have hbot : (⊥ : G.Subgraph).IsMatching := fun v hv => False.elim (by simp at hv)
  obtain ⟨⟨M, hM⟩, hmax⟩ :=
    @Finite.exists_max { M : G.Subgraph // M.IsMatching } ℕ _ ⟨⟨⊥, hbot⟩⟩ _
      (fun M => M.val.verts.ncard)
  refine ⟨M, hM, fun v w hvw => ?_⟩
  by_contra h
  have hv : v ∉ M.verts := fun hvin => h (Or.inl hvin)
  have hw : w ∉ M.verts := fun hwin => h (Or.inr hwin)
  let M' : G.Subgraph := M ⊔ G.subgraphOfAdj hvw
  have hd : Disjoint M.support (G.subgraphOfAdj hvw).support := by
    rw [hM.support_eq_verts, (SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.subgraphOfAdj hvw).support_eq_verts,
      SimpleGraph.subgraphOfAdj_verts]
    rw [Set.disjoint_insert_right, Set.disjoint_singleton_right]
    exact ⟨hv, hw⟩
  have hM' : M'.IsMatching := hM.sup (SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.subgraphOfAdj hvw) hd
  have hle := hmax ⟨M', hM'⟩
  dsimp at hle
  have hverts : M'.verts = M.verts ∪ {v, w} := by
    change (M ⊔ G.subgraphOfAdj hvw).verts = _
    rw [SimpleGraph.Subgraph.verts_sup, SimpleGraph.subgraphOfAdj_verts]
  have hss : M.verts ⊂ M'.verts := by
    rw [hverts]
    refine ⟨Set.subset_union_left, ?_⟩
    intro heq
    have hvin : v ∈ M.verts ∪ {v, w} := by simp
    have : v ∈ M.verts := heq hvin
    contradiction
  have hlt : M.verts.ncard < M'.verts.ncard := Set.ncard_lt_ncard hss
  omega

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by choosing a matching M of maximum vertex cardinality, which exists because the set of matchings in a finite graph is finite and nonempty (the empty subgraph is a matching). If M.verts were not a vertex cover, there would be an edge v ∼ w with neither endpoint in M.verts. Adding this edge to M would produce a valid matching M' with strictly more vertices, contradicting the maximality of M.

steps.claim: There exists a matching M maximizing the number of vertices, and it suffices to show that its vertex set covers every edge.
steps.explanation: The empty subgraph ⊥ is vacuously a matching because it has no vertices (using `False.elim`). Since the vertex set V is finite, the collection of all matchings in G is finite and nonempty. By `Finite.exists_max`, there exists a matching M maximizing `M.verts.ncard`. We witness the existential goal with M, leaving the goal of showing that for any edge v ∼ w in G, at least one endpoint belongs to M.verts.
steps.code:
classical
  have hbot : (⊥ : G.Subgraph).IsMatching := fun v hv => False.elim (by simp at hv)
  obtain ⟨⟨M, hM⟩, hmax⟩ :=
    @Finite.exists_max { M : G.Subgraph // M.IsMatching } ℕ _ ⟨⟨⊥, hbot⟩⟩ _
      (fun M => M.val.verts.ncard)
  refine ⟨M, hM, fun v w hvw => ?_⟩

steps.claim: Assuming for contradiction that the edge {v, w} is uncovered, neither v nor w belongs to M.verts.
steps.explanation: We assume for contradiction (`by_contra`) that neither endpoint is in M.verts, i.e., ¬(v ∈ M.verts ∨ w ∈ M.verts). From this, v ∉ M.verts and w ∉ M.verts, since if either belonged to M.verts, `Or.inl` or `Or.inr` would yield the disjunction.
steps.code:
by_contra h
  have hv : v ∉ M.verts := fun hvin => h (Or.inl hvin)
  have hw : w ∉ M.verts := fun hwin => h (Or.inr hwin)

steps.claim: The augmented subgraph M' obtained by adding the edge {v, w} to M is also a matching.
steps.explanation: Define M' = M ⊔ G.subgraphOfAdj(v ∼ w). The single edge {v, w} is itself a matching by `SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.subgraphOfAdj`, with vertex set {v, w} by `SimpleGraph.subgraphOfAdj_verts`. For any matching, its support equals its vertex set. Since neither v nor w is in M.verts, M is disjoint from {v, w} by `Set.disjoint_insert_right` and `Set.disjoint_singleton_right`. Because their supports are disjoint, the union of the two matchings is again a matching.
steps.code:
let M' : G.Subgraph := M ⊔ G.subgraphOfAdj hvw
  have hd : Disjoint M.support (G.subgraphOfAdj hvw).support := by
    rw [hM.support_eq_verts, (SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.subgraphOfAdj hvw).support_eq_verts,
      SimpleGraph.subgraphOfAdj_verts]
    rw [Set.disjoint_insert_right, Set.disjoint_singleton_right]
    exact ⟨hv, hw⟩
  have hM' : M'.IsMatching := hM.sup (SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.subgraphOfAdj hvw) hd

steps.claim: The vertex set of M is strictly contained in that of M', while maximality requires |M'.verts| ≤ |M.verts|.
steps.explanation: By the maximality of M, |M'.verts| ≤ |M.verts|. The vertex set of M' is M.verts ∪ {v, w} by `SimpleGraph.Subgraph.verts_sup` and `SimpleGraph.subgraphOfAdj_verts`. Thus M.verts ⊆ M'.verts via `Set.subset_union_left`. Furthermore, this inclusion is strict: if M'.verts ⊆ M.verts, then v ∈ M'.verts would imply v ∈ M.verts, contradicting v ∉ M.verts.
steps.code:
have hle := hmax ⟨M', hM'⟩
  dsimp at hle
  have hverts : M'.verts = M.verts ∪ {v, w} := by
    change (M ⊔ G.subgraphOfAdj hvw).verts = _
    rw [SimpleGraph.Subgraph.verts_sup, SimpleGraph.subgraphOfAdj_verts]
  have hss : M.verts ⊂ M'.verts := by
    rw [hverts]
    refine ⟨Set.subset_union_left, ?_⟩
    intro heq
    have hvin : v ∈ M.verts ∪ {v, w} := by simp
    have : v ∈ M.verts := heq hvin
    contradiction

steps.claim: The strict inclusion implies |M.verts| < |M'.verts|, contradicting |M'.verts| ≤ |M.verts|.
steps.explanation: By `Set.ncard_lt_ncard`, strict inclusion between finite sets gives |M.verts| < |M'.verts|. The `omega` tactic detects the contradiction between |M.verts| < |M'.verts| and |M'.verts| ≤ |M.verts| by linear integer arithmetic.
steps.code:
have hlt : M.verts.ncard < M'.verts.ncard := Set.ncard_lt_ncard hss
  omega

glossary.False.elim: From a contradiction (`False`), any statement follows.
glossary.Finite.exists_max: Any function from a finite, nonempty type to a linearly ordered type attains a maximum value.
glossary.Or.inl: From a proof of `a`, deduces the disjunction `a ∨ b`.
glossary.Or.inr: From a proof of `b`, deduces the disjunction `a ∨ b`.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching.subgraph: For an edge `v ∼ w` in a graph, the subgraph induced by this single edge is a matching.
glossary.SimpleGraph.subgraphOfAdj_verts: The vertex set of the single-edge subgraph induced by `v ∼ w` is `{v, w}`.
glossary.Set.disjoint_insert_right: A set `s` is disjoint from `insert a t` if and only if `a ∉ s` and `s` is disjoint from `t`.
glossary.Set.disjoint_singleton_right: A set `s` is disjoint from the singleton `{a}` if and only if `a ∉ s`.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Subgraph.verts_sup: The vertex set of the union (supremum) of two subgraphs is the union of their vertex sets.
glossary.Set.subset_union_left: A set `s` is a subset of `s ∪ t`.
glossary.Set.ncard_lt_ncard: If `s ⊂ t` and `t` is finite, then the cardinality of `s` is strictly less than the cardinality of `t`.

caveats: Mathlib defines `SimpleGraph.Subgraph.IsMatching M` to mean that every vertex in `M.verts` has degree exactly 1 in `M`. Consequently, the empty subgraph ⊥ has an empty vertex set and is vacuously a matching.

Rather than choosing an inclusion-maximal matching directly, the proof chooses a matching of maximum vertex cardinality `M.verts.ncard`. In a finite graph, such a maximum matching is necessarily inclusion-maximal, so its vertices form a vertex cover.

declarations.name: vertex_cover_num_le_two_mul_matching_num
declarations.informal: In any finite simple graph G, the vertex cover number is at most twice the matching number: G.vertexCoverNum ≤ 2 * graph_matching_num G.
declarations.statement:
theorem vertex_cover_num_le_two_mul_matching_num {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    G.vertexCoverNum ≤ 2 * graph_matching_num G
declarations.source:
/-- The vertex cover number is at most twice the matching number in any finite simple graph. -/
theorem vertex_cover_num_le_two_mul_matching_num {V : Type*} [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    G.vertexCoverNum ≤ 2 * graph_matching_num G := by
  obtain ⟨M, hM, hcov⟩ := exists_isMatching_isVertexCover G
  have h1 : G.vertexCoverNum ≤ M.verts.encard := by
    unfold SimpleGraph.vertexCoverNum
    exact iInf_le_of_le M.verts (iInf_le (fun (_ : G.IsVertexCover M.verts) => M.verts.encard) hcov)
  have h2 : M.verts.encard ≤ 2 * M.edgeSet.encard :=
    isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul M hM
  have h3 : M.edgeSet.encard ≤ graph_matching_num G := by
    unfold graph_matching_num
    exact le_iSup_of_le M (le_iSup (fun (_ : M.IsMatching) => M.edgeSet.encard) hM)
  have h4 : 2 * M.edgeSet.encard ≤ 2 * graph_matching_num G :=
    mul_le_mul_right h3 2
  exact h1.trans (h2.trans h4)
declarations.reading: For every finite type `V` and every simple graph `G` on `V`, the vertex cover number of `G` (`G.vertexCoverNum`) is less than or equal to 2 times the matching number of `G` (`graph_matching_num G`).

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by choosing a matching M of G whose vertices form a vertex cover of G (which exists in any finite graph, for example by taking a maximal matching). Because the vertices of M form a vertex cover, the vertex cover number τ(G) is at most |V(M)|. Since M is a matching, its vertices consist of at most two endpoints per edge, so |V(M)| ≤ 2 |E(M)|. Finally, the number of edges in M is at most the matching number ν(G), yielding the chain of inequalities τ(G) ≤ |V(M)| ≤ 2 |E(M)| ≤ 2 ν(G).

steps.claim: There exists a matching M in G whose vertices form a vertex cover of G.
steps.explanation: By `exists_isMatching_isVertexCover`, any finite simple graph contains a matching M whose vertex set covers all edges of G. We obtain such a matching M, along with the proofs that M is a matching (`hM`) and that its vertices cover G (`hcov`).
steps.code: obtain ⟨M, hM, hcov⟩ := exists_isMatching_isVertexCover G

steps.claim: The vertex cover number of G is at most the number of vertices in M.
steps.explanation: The vertex cover number of G is defined as the infimum of the cardinalities of all vertex covers of G. Since the vertex set of M is a vertex cover (`hcov`), this infimum is at most the cardinality of M's vertices, established by applying `iInf_le_of_le` and `iInf_le`.
steps.code:
have h1 : G.vertexCoverNum ≤ M.verts.encard := by
    unfold SimpleGraph.vertexCoverNum
    exact iInf_le_of_le M.verts (iInf_le (fun (_ : G.IsVertexCover M.verts) => M.verts.encard) hcov)

steps.claim: The number of vertices in M is at most twice the number of edges in M.
steps.explanation: Since M is a matching (`hM`), every edge has two endpoints and no two edges share an endpoint, so the number of vertices in M is at most twice its number of edges by `isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul`.
steps.code:
have h2 : M.verts.encard ≤ 2 * M.edgeSet.encard :=
    isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul M hM

steps.claim: The number of edges in M is at most the matching number of G.
steps.explanation: The matching number of G is defined as the supremum of edge cardinalities over all matchings of G. Since M is a matching (`hM`), its edge cardinality is bounded above by this supremum, which is shown using `le_iSup_of_le` and `le_iSup`.
steps.code:
have h3 : M.edgeSet.encard ≤ graph_matching_num G := by
    unfold graph_matching_num
    exact le_iSup_of_le M (le_iSup (fun (_ : M.IsMatching) => M.edgeSet.encard) hM)

steps.claim: Twice the number of edges in M is at most twice the matching number of G.
steps.explanation: Multiplying the inequality |E(M)| ≤ graph_matching_num G on the left by 2 preserves the order, via `mul_le_mul_right`.
steps.code:
have h4 : 2 * M.edgeSet.encard ≤ 2 * graph_matching_num G :=
    mul_le_mul_right h3 2

steps.claim: The vertex cover number of G is at most twice the matching number of G.
steps.explanation: Chaining the inequalities G.vertexCoverNum ≤ |V(M)| ≤ 2 * |E(M)| ≤ 2 * graph_matching_num G together by transitivity completes the proof.
steps.code: exact h1.trans (h2.trans h4)

glossary.exists_isMatching_isVertexCover: In any finite simple graph, there exists a matching whose vertex set is a vertex cover of the graph.
glossary.iInf_le_of_le: In a complete lattice, the infimum of a family is bounded above by any upper bound of a single member of the family.
glossary.iInf_le: In a complete lattice, the infimum of a family is at most any given member of the family.
glossary.isMatching_verts_encard_le_two_mul: For any matching in a simple graph, the cardinality of its vertex set is at most twice the cardinality of its edge set.
glossary.le_iSup_of_le: In a complete lattice, any lower bound of a single member of a family is bounded above by the supremum of the family.
glossary.le_iSup: In a complete lattice, any member of a family is at most the supremum of the family.
glossary.mul_le_mul_right: If b ≤ c, then multiplying on the left by a preserves the inequality: a * b ≤ a * c.

declarations.name: finset_one_inclusion_graph_card_edgeFinset_le
declarations.informal: If a finite set system F has VC dimension at most d, its one-inclusion graph has at most d·|F| edges.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_one_inclusion_graph_card_edgeFinset_le {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (𝓕 : Finset (Finset α)) [Fintype (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).edgeSet] (d : ℕ)
    (hd : 𝓕.vcDim ≤ d) :
    (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).edgeFinset.card ≤ d * 𝓕.card
declarations.source:
/-- Ordered pairs of members of `𝒜` whose symmetric difference has exactly one element. -/
def finset_one_inclusion_pairs {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (𝒜 : Finset (Finset α)) :
    Finset (Finset α × Finset α) :=
  (𝒜 ×ˢ 𝒜).filter (fun p => (symmDiff p.1 p.2).card = 1)

theorem finset_one_inclusion_pairs_mono {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {𝒜 ℬ : Finset (Finset α)}
    (h : 𝒜 ⊆ ℬ) : finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜 ⊆ finset_one_inclusion_pairs ℬ :=
  Finset.filter_subset_filter _ (Finset.product_subset_product h h)

theorem finset_one_inclusion_pairs_inter {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (𝒜 ℬ : Finset (Finset α)) :
    finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜 ∩ finset_one_inclusion_pairs ℬ ⊆
      finset_one_inclusion_pairs (𝒜 ∩ ℬ) := by
  intro p hp
  simp only [finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_filter,
    Finset.mem_product] at hp ⊢
  exact ⟨⟨⟨hp.1.1.1, hp.2.1.1⟩, ⟨hp.1.1.2, hp.2.1.2⟩⟩, hp.1.2⟩

theorem finset_one_inclusion_pairs_card_split {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (a : α)
    (𝒜 : Finset (Finset α)) :
    (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜).card ≤
      (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (𝒜.nonMemberSubfamily a ∪ 𝒜.memberSubfamily a)).card +
      (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (𝒜.nonMemberSubfamily a ∩ 𝒜.memberSubfamily a)).card +
      2 * (𝒜.nonMemberSubfamily a ∩ 𝒜.memberSubfamily a).card := by
  set F0 := 𝒜.nonMemberSubfamily a
  set F1 := 𝒜.memberSubfamily a
  set E := finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜
  set E00 := E.filter (fun p => a ∉ p.1 ∧ a ∉ p.2)
  set E11 := E.filter (fun p => a ∈ p.1 ∧ a ∈ p.2)
  set EX := E.filter (fun p => (a ∈ p.1 ∧ a ∉ p.2) ∨ (a ∉ p.1 ∧ a ∈ p.2))
  have hsplit : E ⊆ E00 ∪ E11 ∪ EX := by
    intro p hp
    simp only [E00, E11, EX, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_filter]
    by_cases h1 : a ∈ p.1 <;> by_cases h2 : a ∈ p.2 <;> simp [h1, h2, hp]
  have hcardE : E.card ≤ E00.card + E11.card + EX.card :=
    (Finset.card_le_card hsplit).trans
      ((Finset.card_union_le _ _).trans (Nat.add_le_add_right (Finset.card_union_le _ _) _))
  -- E00 sits inside the pairs of F0
  have h00 : E00 ⊆ finset_one_inclusion_pairs F0 := by
    intro p hp
    simp only [E00, E, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product] at hp ⊢
    obtain ⟨⟨⟨hA, hB⟩, hP⟩, ha1, ha2⟩ := hp
    exact ⟨⟨Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily.2 ⟨hA, ha1⟩, Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily.2 ⟨hB, ha2⟩⟩, hP⟩
  -- E11 injects into the pairs of F1 by erasing `a`
  have h11 : E11.card ≤ (finset_one_inclusion_pairs F1).card := by
    refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun p => (p.1.erase a, p.2.erase a)) ?_ ?_
    · intro p hp
      simp only [Finset.mem_coe, E11, E, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter,
        Finset.mem_product] at hp ⊢
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨hA, hB⟩, hP⟩, ha1, ha2⟩ := hp
      refine ⟨⟨Finset.mem_memberSubfamily.2 ⟨by rwa [Finset.insert_erase ha1], by simp⟩,
        Finset.mem_memberSubfamily.2 ⟨by rwa [Finset.insert_erase ha2], by simp⟩⟩, ?_⟩
      have : symmDiff (p.1.erase a) (p.2.erase a) = symmDiff p.1 p.2 := by
        ext x
        by_cases hx : x = a
        · subst hx; simp [Finset.mem_symmDiff, ha1, ha2]
        · simp [Finset.mem_symmDiff, Finset.mem_erase, hx]
      rw [this]; exact hP
    · intro p hp q hq hpq
      simp only [Finset.mem_coe, E11, Finset.mem_filter] at hp hq
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at hpq
      have e1 : p.1 = q.1 := by
        rw [← Finset.insert_erase hp.2.1, ← Finset.insert_erase hq.2.1, hpq.1]
      have e2 : p.2 = q.2 := by
        rw [← Finset.insert_erase hp.2.2, ← Finset.insert_erase hq.2.2, hpq.2]
      exact Prod.ext e1 e2
  -- pairs differing exactly in `a`
  have hX : EX.card ≤ 2 * (F0 ∩ F1).card := by
    have hsd : ∀ p ∈ EX, symmDiff p.1 p.2 = {a} := by
      intro p hp
      simp only [EX, E, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter] at hp
      obtain ⟨⟨-, hP⟩, hx⟩ := hp
      obtain ⟨x, hx1⟩ := Finset.card_eq_one.1 hP
      have : a ∈ symmDiff p.1 p.2 := by
        rw [Finset.mem_symmDiff]; tauto
      rw [hx1, Finset.mem_singleton] at this
      rw [hx1, this]
    have hcard2 : (F0 ∩ F1).card * 2 = ((F0 ∩ F1) ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset Bool)).card := by
      rw [Finset.card_product, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_bool]
    rw [mul_comm, hcard2]
    refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun p => (p.1.erase a, decide (a ∈ p.1))) ?_ ?_
    · intro p hp
      have hs := hsd p hp
      simp only [Finset.mem_coe, EX, E, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter,
        Finset.mem_product] at hp
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨hA, hB⟩, -⟩, hx⟩ := hp
      have hiff : ∀ x, x ≠ a → (x ∈ p.1 ↔ x ∈ p.2) := by
        intro x hxa
        have : x ∉ symmDiff p.1 p.2 := by rw [hs]; simpa using hxa
        rw [Finset.mem_symmDiff] at this
        tauto
      simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_univ, and_true, Finset.mem_inter,
        Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily, Finset.mem_memberSubfamily, F0, F1]
      rcases hx with ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ | ⟨ha1, ha2⟩
      · have hBe : p.1.erase a = p.2 := by
          ext x
          by_cases hxa : x = a
          · subst hxa; simp [ha2]
          · rw [Finset.mem_erase]; exact ⟨fun h => (hiff x hxa).1 h.2, fun h => ⟨hxa, (hiff x hxa).2 h⟩⟩
        refine ⟨⟨by rw [hBe]; exact hB, by simp⟩, by rwa [Finset.insert_erase ha1], by simp⟩
      · have hAe : p.1.erase a = p.1 := Finset.erase_eq_of_notMem ha1
        have hBi : insert a p.1 = p.2 := by
          ext x
          by_cases hxa : x = a
          · subst hxa; simp [ha2]
          · rw [Finset.mem_insert]; exact ⟨fun h => h.elim (fun e => absurd e hxa) (hiff x hxa).1,
              fun h => Or.inr ((hiff x hxa).2 h)⟩
        rw [hAe]
        exact ⟨⟨hA, ha1⟩, by rw [hBi]; exact hB, ha1⟩
    · intro p hp q hq hpq
      have hsp := hsd p hp
      have hsq := hsd q hq
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq, decide_eq_decide] at hpq
      obtain ⟨he, hm⟩ := hpq
      have e1 : p.1 = q.1 := by
        by_cases ha : a ∈ p.1
        · rw [← Finset.insert_erase ha, ← Finset.insert_erase (hm.1 ha), he]
        · rw [← Finset.erase_eq_of_notMem ha, ← Finset.erase_eq_of_notMem (fun h => ha (hm.2 h)), he]
      have e2 : p.2 = q.2 := by
        have h1 : p.2 = symmDiff p.1 {a} := by rw [← hsp, symmDiff_symmDiff_cancel_left]
        have h2 : q.2 = symmDiff q.1 {a} := by rw [← hsq, symmDiff_symmDiff_cancel_left]
        rw [h1, h2, e1]
      exact Prod.ext e1 e2
  -- pairs of F0 and F1 against those of the union and the intersection
  have hUI : (finset_one_inclusion_pairs F0).card + (finset_one_inclusion_pairs F1).card ≤
      (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (F0 ∪ F1)).card + (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (F0 ∩ F1)).card := by
    rw [← Finset.card_union_add_card_inter]
    exact Nat.add_le_add
      (Finset.card_le_card (Finset.union_subset
        (finset_one_inclusion_pairs_mono Finset.subset_union_left)
        (finset_one_inclusion_pairs_mono Finset.subset_union_right)))
      (Finset.card_le_card (finset_one_inclusion_pairs_inter F0 F1))
  have := Finset.card_le_card h00
  omega

theorem finset_one_inclusion_pairs_card_le {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (u : Finset α) :
    ∀ 𝒜 : Finset (Finset α), (∀ s ∈ 𝒜, s ⊆ u) → ∀ d : ℕ, 𝒜.vcDim ≤ d →
      (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜).card ≤ 2 * (d * 𝒜.card) := by
  induction u using Finset.induction with
  | empty =>
    intro 𝒜 h𝒜 d _
    have : (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜).card = 0 := by
      rw [Finset.card_eq_zero, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
      intro p hp
      rw [Finset.mem_product] at hp
      rw [Finset.subset_empty.1 (h𝒜 _ hp.1), Finset.subset_empty.1 (h𝒜 _ hp.2)]
      simp
    omega
  | insert a u hau ih =>
    intro 𝒜 h𝒜 d hd
    set F0 := 𝒜.nonMemberSubfamily a
    set F1 := 𝒜.memberSubfamily a
    have hF0 : ∀ s ∈ F0, s ⊆ u := by
      intro s hs
      rw [Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily] at hs
      exact (Finset.subset_insert_iff_of_notMem hs.2).1 (h𝒜 s hs.1)
    have hF1 : ∀ s ∈ F1, s ⊆ u := by
      intro s hs
      rw [Finset.mem_memberSubfamily] at hs
      exact (Finset.subset_insert_iff_of_notMem hs.2).1
        ((Finset.subset_insert _ _).trans (h𝒜 _ hs.1))
    have hU : ∀ s ∈ F0 ∪ F1, s ⊆ u := by
      intro s hs
      rcases Finset.mem_union.1 hs with h | h
      exacts [hF0 s h, hF1 s h]
    have hI : ∀ s ∈ F0 ∩ F1, s ⊆ u := fun s hs => hF0 s (Finset.mem_inter.1 hs).1
    have notmem : ∀ ℬ : Finset (Finset α), (∀ s ∈ ℬ, s ⊆ u) → ∀ s, ℬ.Shatters s → a ∉ s := by
      intro ℬ hℬ s hs ha
      obtain ⟨v, hv, hsv⟩ := hs.exists_superset
      exact hau (hℬ v hv (hsv ha))
    have shU : ∀ s, (F0 ∪ F1).Shatters s → 𝒜.Shatters s := by
      intro s hs t ht
      have has := notmem _ hU s hs
      obtain ⟨w, hw, hsw⟩ := hs ht
      rcases Finset.mem_union.1 hw with hw | hw
      · rw [Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily] at hw
        exact ⟨w, hw.1, hsw⟩
      · rw [Finset.mem_memberSubfamily] at hw
        exact ⟨insert a w, hw.1, by rw [Finset.inter_insert_of_notMem has, hsw]⟩
    have shI : ∀ s, (F0 ∩ F1).Shatters s → 𝒜.Shatters (insert a s) := by
      intro s hs t ht
      have has := notmem _ hI s hs
      by_cases hat : a ∈ t
      · have hsub : t.erase a ⊆ s := by
          intro x hx
          rw [Finset.mem_erase] at hx
          have := ht hx.2
          rw [Finset.mem_insert] at this
          exact this.resolve_left hx.1
        obtain ⟨w, hw, hsw⟩ := hs hsub
        have hw1 := (Finset.mem_inter.1 hw).2
        rw [Finset.mem_memberSubfamily] at hw1
        refine ⟨insert a w, hw1.1, ?_⟩
        rw [← Finset.insert_inter_distrib, hsw, Finset.insert_erase hat]
      · have hsub : t ⊆ s := by
          intro x hx
          have := ht hx
          rw [Finset.mem_insert] at this
          exact this.resolve_left (fun e => hat (e ▸ hx))
        obtain ⟨w, hw, hsw⟩ := hs hsub
        have hw0 := (Finset.mem_inter.1 hw).1
        rw [Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily] at hw0
        refine ⟨w, hw0.1, ?_⟩
        rw [Finset.insert_inter_of_notMem hw0.2, hsw]
    have vcU : (F0 ∪ F1).vcDim ≤ d := by
      unfold Finset.vcDim
      refine Finset.sup_le fun s hs => ?_
      exact ((shU s (Finset.mem_shatterer.1 hs)).card_le_vcDim).trans hd
    have vcI : (F0 ∩ F1).vcDim ≤ d - 1 := by
      unfold Finset.vcDim
      refine Finset.sup_le fun s hs => ?_
      have hs' := Finset.mem_shatterer.1 hs
      have h1 := (shI s hs').card_le_vcDim
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (notmem _ hI s hs')] at h1
      omega
    have hIempty : d = 0 → F0 ∩ F1 = ∅ := by
      intro hd0
      by_contra hne
      have h1 := (shI ∅ (Finset.shatters_empty.2 (Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.2 hne))).card_le_vcDim
      simp only [insert_empty_eq, Finset.card_singleton] at h1
      omega
    have ihU := ih (F0 ∪ F1) hU d vcU
    have ihI := ih (F0 ∩ F1) hI (d - 1) vcI
    have hcard : 𝒜.card = (F0 ∪ F1).card + (F0 ∩ F1).card := by
      rw [Finset.card_union_add_card_inter, add_comm,
        Finset.card_memberSubfamily_add_card_nonMemberSubfamily]
    have hedge : (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜).card ≤
        (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (F0 ∪ F1)).card + (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (F0 ∩ F1)).card +
          2 * (F0 ∩ F1).card :=
      finset_one_inclusion_pairs_card_split a 𝒜
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos d with hd0 | hdpos
    · have hI0 := hIempty hd0
      subst hd0
      rw [hI0] at hedge
      have h0 : (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (∅ : Finset (Finset α))).card = 0 := by
        simp [finset_one_inclusion_pairs]
      rw [h0, Finset.card_empty] at hedge
      simp only [zero_mul, mul_zero] at ihU ⊢
      omega
    · have h1 : d * 𝒜.card = d * (F0 ∪ F1).card + d * (F0 ∩ F1).card := by
        rw [hcard, mul_add]
      have h2 : (d - 1) * (F0 ∩ F1).card + (F0 ∩ F1).card = d * (F0 ∩ F1).card := by
        obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_lt hdpos
        simp only [Nat.zero_add, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
        ring
      linarith

theorem finset_one_inclusion_graph_card_edgeFinset_le {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (𝓕 : Finset (Finset α)) [Fintype (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).edgeSet] (d : ℕ)
    (hd : 𝓕.vcDim ≤ d) :
    (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).edgeFinset.card ≤ d * 𝓕.card := by
  classical
  have hpairs := finset_one_inclusion_pairs_card_le (𝓕.sup id) 𝓕
    (fun s hs => Finset.le_sup (f := id) hs) d hd
  have hbij : ((Finset.univ : Finset (𝓕 × 𝓕)).filter
      (fun x => (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).Adj x.1 x.2)).card =
        (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝓕).card := by
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun x _ => ((x.1 : Finset α), (x.2 : Finset α)))
    · intro x hx
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hx
      simp only [finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product]
      exact ⟨⟨x.1.2, x.2.2⟩, hx⟩
    · intro x _ y _ h
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at h
      exact Prod.ext (Subtype.ext h.1) (Subtype.ext h.2)
    · intro b hb
      simp only [finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product] at hb
      refine ⟨(⟨b.1, hb.1.1⟩, ⟨b.2, hb.1.2⟩), ?_, rfl⟩
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
      exact hb.2
  have key : 2 * (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).edgeFinset.card =
      (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝓕).card := by
    rw [← hbij]
    convert SimpleGraph.two_mul_card_edgeFinset (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕)
  have h2 : 2 * (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).edgeFinset.card ≤ 2 * (d * 𝓕.card) := by
    rw [key]; exact hpairs
  exact Nat.le_of_mul_le_mul_left h2 (by norm_num)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.08151 (Polynomial-in-r bounds for forbidden traces of uniform hypergraphs), Lemma 2 (one-inclusion graph edge bound). The edge set's Fintype instance is a hypothesis; the count does not depend on it.

explanation.summary: The proof establishes that the one-inclusion graph of a finite set family 𝓕 with VC dimension at most d has at most d * |𝓕| edges. It first establishes an upper bound of 2 * d * |𝒜| on the number of ordered pairs differing by a single element, by induction on the size of the underlying universe using a subfamily decomposition (Haussler's technique). Finally, it relates this bound to the graph edges via the handshaking property that twice the number of undirected edges equals the number of ordered adjacent vertex pairs, and divides by 2.

steps.claim: The intersection of the one-inclusion pairs of 𝒜 and ℬ is contained in the one-inclusion pairs of 𝒜 ∩ ℬ.
steps.explanation: Let p = (A, B) be an ordered pair belonging to both sets of pairs. Then both A and B belong to 𝒜 and to ℬ, so they belong to 𝒜 ∩ ℬ, and their symmetric difference still has cardinality 1.
steps.code:
intro p hp
  simp only [finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_inter, Finset.mem_filter,
    Finset.mem_product] at hp ⊢
  exact ⟨⟨⟨hp.1.1.1, hp.2.1.1⟩, ⟨hp.1.1.2, hp.2.1.2⟩⟩, hp.1.2⟩

steps.claim: The one-inclusion pairs of 𝒜 are partitioned according to membership of element a, giving |E| ≤ |E₀₀| + |E₁₁| + |E_X|.
steps.explanation: We partition the pairs E into pairs E₀₀ where neither set contains a, pairs E₁₁ where both sets contain a, and pairs E_X where exactly one set contains a. By union cardinality bounds, |E| is bounded by the sum of their sizes.
steps.code:
set F0 := 𝒜.nonMemberSubfamily a
  set F1 := 𝒜.memberSubfamily a
  set E := finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜
  set E00 := E.filter (fun p => a ∉ p.1 ∧ a ∉ p.2)
  set E11 := E.filter (fun p => a ∈ p.1 ∧ a ∈ p.2)
  set EX := E.filter (fun p => (a ∈ p.1 ∧ a ∉ p.2) ∨ (a ∉ p.1 ∧ a ∈ p.2))
  have hsplit : E ⊆ E00 ∪ E11 ∪ EX := by
    intro p hp
    simp only [E00, E11, EX, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_filter]
    by_cases h1 : a ∈ p.1 <;> by_cases h2 : a ∈ p.2 <;> simp [h1, h2, hp]
  have hcardE : E.card ≤ E00.card + E11.card + EX.card :=
    (Finset.card_le_card hsplit).trans
      ((Finset.card_union_le _ _).trans (Nat.add_le_add_right (Finset.card_union_le _ _) _))
  -- E00 sits inside the pairs of F0

steps.claim: The pairs in E₀₀ form a subset of the one-inclusion pairs of F₀.
steps.explanation: For any pair (A, B) in E₀₀, neither A nor B contains a, so both belong to the non-member subfamily F₀ of 𝒜. Thus the pair is a one-inclusion pair of F₀.
steps.code:
have h00 : E00 ⊆ finset_one_inclusion_pairs F0 := by
    intro p hp
    simp only [E00, E, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product] at hp ⊢
    obtain ⟨⟨⟨hA, hB⟩, hP⟩, ha1, ha2⟩ := hp
    exact ⟨⟨Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily.2 ⟨hA, ha1⟩, Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily.2 ⟨hB, ha2⟩⟩, hP⟩

steps.claim: The cardinality of E₁₁ is at most the number of one-inclusion pairs of F₁.
steps.explanation: The map (A, B) ↦ (A \ {a}, B \ {a}) injects E₁₁ into the one-inclusion pairs of the member subfamily F₁ because removing an element common to both sets preserves their symmetric difference and can be inverted by re-inserting a.
steps.code:
have h11 : E11.card ≤ (finset_one_inclusion_pairs F1).card := by
    refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun p => (p.1.erase a, p.2.erase a)) ?_ ?_
    · intro p hp
      simp only [Finset.mem_coe, E11, E, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter,
        Finset.mem_product] at hp ⊢
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨hA, hB⟩, hP⟩, ha1, ha2⟩ := hp
      refine ⟨⟨Finset.mem_memberSubfamily.2 ⟨by rwa [Finset.insert_erase ha1], by simp⟩,
        Finset.mem_memberSubfamily.2 ⟨by rwa [Finset.insert_erase ha2], by simp⟩⟩, ?_⟩
      have : symmDiff (p.1.erase a) (p.2.erase a) = symmDiff p.1 p.2 := by
        ext x
        by_cases hx : x = a
        · subst hx; simp [Finset.mem_symmDiff, ha1, ha2]
        · simp [Finset.mem_symmDiff, Finset.mem_erase, hx]
      rw [this]; exact hP
    · intro p hp q hq hpq
      simp only [Finset.mem_coe, E11, Finset.mem_filter] at hp hq
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at hpq
      have e1 : p.1 = q.1 := by
        rw [← Finset.insert_erase hp.2.1, ← Finset.insert_erase hq.2.1, hpq.1]
      have e2 : p.2 = q.2 := by
        rw [← Finset.insert_erase hp.2.2, ← Finset.insert_erase hq.2.2, hpq.2]
      exact Prod.ext e1 e2

steps.claim: The cardinality of E_X is at most 2 * |F₀ ∩ F₁|.
steps.explanation: For any pair (A, B) in E_X, their symmetric difference has size 1 and crosses a, so symmDiff A B = {a}. Therefore, one set is s and the other is s ∪ {a}, where s belongs to both F₀ and F₁. Mapping (A, B) to (A \ {a}, decide(a ∈ A)) gives an injection into (F₀ ∩ F₁) × Bool, which has size 2 * |F₀ ∩ F₁|.
steps.code:
have hX : EX.card ≤ 2 * (F0 ∩ F1).card := by
    have hsd : ∀ p ∈ EX, symmDiff p.1 p.2 = {a} := by
      intro p hp
      simp only [EX, E, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter] at hp
      obtain ⟨⟨-, hP⟩, hx⟩ := hp
      obtain ⟨x, hx1⟩ := Finset.card_eq_one.1 hP
      have : a ∈ symmDiff p.1 p.2 := by
        rw [Finset.mem_symmDiff]; tauto
      rw [hx1, Finset.mem_singleton] at this
      rw [hx1, this]
    have hcard2 : (F0 ∩ F1).card * 2 = ((F0 ∩ F1) ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset Bool)).card := by
      rw [Finset.card_product, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_bool]
    rw [mul_comm, hcard2]
    refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun p => (p.1.erase a, decide (a ∈ p.1))) ?_ ?_
    · intro p hp
      have hs := hsd p hp
      simp only [Finset.mem_coe, EX, E, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter,
        Finset.mem_product] at hp
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨hA, hB⟩, -⟩, hx⟩ := hp
      have hiff : ∀ x, x ≠ a → (x ∈ p.1 ↔ x ∈ p.2) := by
        intro x hxa
        have : x ∉ symmDiff p.1 p.2 := by rw [hs]; simpa using hxa
        rw [Finset.mem_symmDiff] at this
        tauto
      simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_univ, and_true, Finset.mem_inter,
        Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily, Finset.mem_memberSubfamily, F0, F1]
      rcases hx with ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ | ⟨ha1, ha2⟩
      · have hBe : p.1.erase a = p.2 := by
          ext x
          by_cases hxa : x = a
          · subst hxa; simp [ha2]
          · rw [Finset.mem_erase]; exact ⟨fun h => (hiff x hxa).1 h.2, fun h => ⟨hxa, (hiff x hxa).2 h⟩⟩
        refine ⟨⟨by rw [hBe]; exact hB, by simp⟩, by rwa [Finset.insert_erase ha1], by simp⟩
      · have hAe : p.1.erase a = p.1 := Finset.erase_eq_of_notMem ha1
        have hBi : insert a p.1 = p.2 := by
          ext x
          by_cases hxa : x = a
          · subst hxa; simp [ha2]
          · rw [Finset.mem_insert]; exact ⟨fun h => h.elim (fun e => absurd e hxa) (hiff x hxa).1,
              fun h => Or.inr ((hiff x hxa).2 h)⟩
        rw [hAe]
        exact ⟨⟨hA, ha1⟩, by rw [hBi]; exact hB, ha1⟩
    · intro p hp q hq hpq
      have hsp := hsd p hp
      have hsq := hsd q hq
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq, decide_eq_decide] at hpq
      obtain ⟨he, hm⟩ := hpq
      have e1 : p.1 = q.1 := by
        by_cases ha : a ∈ p.1
        · rw [← Finset.insert_erase ha, ← Finset.insert_erase (hm.1 ha), he]
        · rw [← Finset.erase_eq_of_notMem ha, ← Finset.erase_eq_of_notMem (fun h => ha (hm.2 h)), he]
      have e2 : p.2 = q.2 := by
        have h1 : p.2 = symmDiff p.1 {a} := by rw [← hsp, symmDiff_symmDiff_cancel_left]
        have h2 : q.2 = symmDiff q.1 {a} := by rw [← hsq, symmDiff_symmDiff_cancel_left]
        rw [h1, h2, e1]
      exact Prod.ext e1 e2

steps.claim: The split bound |E| ≤ |pairs(F₀ ∪ F₁)| + |pairs(F₀ ∩ F₁)| + 2 * |F₀ ∩ F₁| holds.
steps.explanation: By submodularity of pairs, |pairs(F₀)| + |pairs(F₁)| ≤ |pairs(F₀ ∪ F₁)| + |pairs(F₀ ∩ F₁)|. Combining this with the bounds on E₀₀, E₁₁, and E_X, linear integer arithmetic closes the goal.
steps.code:
have hUI : (finset_one_inclusion_pairs F0).card + (finset_one_inclusion_pairs F1).card ≤
      (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (F0 ∪ F1)).card + (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (F0 ∩ F1)).card := by
    rw [← Finset.card_union_add_card_inter]
    exact Nat.add_le_add
      (Finset.card_le_card (Finset.union_subset
        (finset_one_inclusion_pairs_mono Finset.subset_union_left)
        (finset_one_inclusion_pairs_mono Finset.subset_union_right)))
      (Finset.card_le_card (finset_one_inclusion_pairs_inter F0 F1))
  have := Finset.card_le_card h00
  omega

steps.claim: In the base case where the universe u is empty, the family has 0 pairs and the bound holds.
steps.explanation: If u = ∅, every set in 𝒜 must be empty, so no two sets can have symmetric difference of size 1. The set of pairs is empty, and its cardinality is 0, satisfying 0 ≤ 2 * (d * |𝒜|).
steps.code:
induction u using Finset.induction with
  | empty =>
    intro 𝒜 h𝒜 d _
    have : (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜).card = 0 := by
      rw [Finset.card_eq_zero, finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
      intro p hp
      rw [Finset.mem_product] at hp
      rw [Finset.subset_empty.1 (h𝒜 _ hp.1), Finset.subset_empty.1 (h𝒜 _ hp.2)]
      simp
    omega

steps.claim: For u = insert a u', all sets in F₀, F₁, F₀ ∪ F₁, and F₀ ∩ F₁ are subsets of u'.
steps.explanation: By construction, members of F₀ do not contain a, and members of F₁ are formed by removing a from sets containing it. Since all original sets were in u = insert a u', removing or excluding a ensures they are subsets of u'.
steps.code:
| insert a u hau ih =>
    intro 𝒜 h𝒜 d hd
    set F0 := 𝒜.nonMemberSubfamily a
    set F1 := 𝒜.memberSubfamily a
    have hF0 : ∀ s ∈ F0, s ⊆ u := by
      intro s hs
      rw [Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily] at hs
      exact (Finset.subset_insert_iff_of_notMem hs.2).1 (h𝒜 s hs.1)
    have hF1 : ∀ s ∈ F1, s ⊆ u := by
      intro s hs
      rw [Finset.mem_memberSubfamily] at hs
      exact (Finset.subset_insert_iff_of_notMem hs.2).1
        ((Finset.subset_insert _ _).trans (h𝒜 _ hs.1))
    have hU : ∀ s ∈ F0 ∪ F1, s ⊆ u := by
      intro s hs
      rcases Finset.mem_union.1 hs with h | h
      exacts [hF0 s h, hF1 s h]
    have hI : ∀ s ∈ F0 ∩ F1, s ⊆ u := fun s hs => hF0 s (Finset.mem_inter.1 hs).1

steps.claim: The VC dimension of F₀ ∪ F₁ is at most d, that of F₀ ∩ F₁ is at most d - 1, and F₀ ∩ F₁ is empty if d = 0.
steps.explanation: Any set shattered by F₀ ∪ F₁ is also shattered by 𝒜, so vcDim(F₀ ∪ F₁) ≤ vcDim(𝒜) ≤ d. If a set s is shattered by F₀ ∩ F₁, then s ∪ {a} is shattered by 𝒜, implying |s| + 1 ≤ d, so vcDim(F₀ ∩ F₁) ≤ d - 1. When d = 0, F₀ ∩ F₁ cannot shatter ∅, so it is empty.
steps.code:
have notmem : ∀ ℬ : Finset (Finset α), (∀ s ∈ ℬ, s ⊆ u) → ∀ s, ℬ.Shatters s → a ∉ s := by
      intro ℬ hℬ s hs ha
      obtain ⟨v, hv, hsv⟩ := hs.exists_superset
      exact hau (hℬ v hv (hsv ha))
    have shU : ∀ s, (F0 ∪ F1).Shatters s → 𝒜.Shatters s := by
      intro s hs t ht
      have has := notmem _ hU s hs
      obtain ⟨w, hw, hsw⟩ := hs ht
      rcases Finset.mem_union.1 hw with hw | hw
      · rw [Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily] at hw
        exact ⟨w, hw.1, hsw⟩
      · rw [Finset.mem_memberSubfamily] at hw
        exact ⟨insert a w, hw.1, by rw [Finset.inter_insert_of_notMem has, hsw]⟩
    have shI : ∀ s, (F0 ∩ F1).Shatters s → 𝒜.Shatters (insert a s) := by
      intro s hs t ht
      have has := notmem _ hI s hs
      by_cases hat : a ∈ t
      · have hsub : t.erase a ⊆ s := by
          intro x hx
          rw [Finset.mem_erase] at hx
          have := ht hx.2
          rw [Finset.mem_insert] at this
          exact this.resolve_left hx.1
        obtain ⟨w, hw, hsw⟩ := hs hsub
        have hw1 := (Finset.mem_inter.1 hw).2
        rw [Finset.mem_memberSubfamily] at hw1
        refine ⟨insert a w, hw1.1, ?_⟩
        rw [← Finset.insert_inter_distrib, hsw, Finset.insert_erase hat]
      · have hsub : t ⊆ s := by
          intro x hx
          have := ht hx
          rw [Finset.mem_insert] at this
          exact this.resolve_left (fun e => hat (e ▸ hx))
        obtain ⟨w, hw, hsw⟩ := hs hsub
        have hw0 := (Finset.mem_inter.1 hw).1
        rw [Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily] at hw0
        refine ⟨w, hw0.1, ?_⟩
        rw [Finset.insert_inter_of_notMem hw0.2, hsw]
    have vcU : (F0 ∪ F1).vcDim ≤ d := by
      unfold Finset.vcDim
      refine Finset.sup_le fun s hs => ?_
      exact ((shU s (Finset.mem_shatterer.1 hs)).card_le_vcDim).trans hd
    have vcI : (F0 ∩ F1).vcDim ≤ d - 1 := by
      unfold Finset.vcDim
      refine Finset.sup_le fun s hs => ?_
      have hs' := Finset.mem_shatterer.1 hs
      have h1 := (shI s hs').card_le_vcDim
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (notmem _ hI s hs')] at h1
      omega
    have hIempty : d = 0 → F0 ∩ F1 = ∅ := by
      intro hd0
      by_contra hne
      have h1 := (shI ∅ (Finset.shatters_empty.2 (Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.2 hne))).card_le_vcDim
      simp only [insert_empty_eq, Finset.card_singleton] at h1
      omega

steps.claim: By the induction hypotheses on F₀ ∪ F₁ and F₀ ∩ F₁, the pair bound holds for 𝒜.
steps.explanation: We apply the induction hypothesis to F₀ ∪ F₁ (with bound d) and to F₀ ∩ F₁ (with bound d - 1). Using |𝒜| = |F₀ ∪ F₁| + |F₀ ∩ F₁| and the splitting lemma, the bound follows by linear arithmetic: 2 * (d * |F₀ ∪ F₁|) + 2 * ((d - 1) * |F₀ ∩ F₁|) + 2 * |F₀ ∩ F₁| = 2 * (d * |𝒜|).
steps.code:
have ihU := ih (F0 ∪ F1) hU d vcU
    have ihI := ih (F0 ∩ F1) hI (d - 1) vcI
    have hcard : 𝒜.card = (F0 ∪ F1).card + (F0 ∩ F1).card := by
      rw [Finset.card_union_add_card_inter, add_comm,
        Finset.card_memberSubfamily_add_card_nonMemberSubfamily]
    have hedge : (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝒜).card ≤
        (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (F0 ∪ F1)).card + (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (F0 ∩ F1)).card +
          2 * (F0 ∩ F1).card :=
      finset_one_inclusion_pairs_card_split a 𝒜
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos d with hd0 | hdpos
    · have hI0 := hIempty hd0
      subst hd0
      rw [hI0] at hedge
      have h0 : (finset_one_inclusion_pairs (∅ : Finset (Finset α))).card = 0 := by
        simp [finset_one_inclusion_pairs]
      rw [h0, Finset.card_empty] at hedge
      simp only [zero_mul, mul_zero] at ihU ⊢
      omega
    · have h1 : d * 𝒜.card = d * (F0 ∪ F1).card + d * (F0 ∩ F1).card := by
        rw [hcard, mul_add]
      have h2 : (d - 1) * (F0 ∩ F1).card + (F0 ∩ F1).card = d * (F0 ∩ F1).card := by
        obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_lt hdpos
        simp only [Nat.zero_add, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
        ring
      linarith

steps.claim: Applying the pairs bound with universe u = ⋃ 𝓕 gives at most 2 * (d * |𝓕|) one-inclusion pairs in 𝓕.
steps.explanation: Setting u to the union of all sets in 𝓕 ensures every set in 𝓕 is contained in u. Since vcDim(𝓕) ≤ d, finset_one_inclusion_pairs_card_le yields |finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝓕| ≤ 2 * (d * |𝓕|).
steps.code:
classical
  have hpairs := finset_one_inclusion_pairs_card_le (𝓕.sup id) 𝓕
    (fun s hs => Finset.le_sup (f := id) hs) d hd

steps.claim: Ordered pairs of adjacent vertices in the one-inclusion graph biject with finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝓕.
steps.explanation: We exhibit a bijection between pairs of adjacent vertices in the graph and elements of finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝓕 via the canonical inclusion of vertices as sets.
steps.code:
have hbij : ((Finset.univ : Finset (𝓕 × 𝓕)).filter
      (fun x => (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).Adj x.1 x.2)).card =
        (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝓕).card := by
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun x _ => ((x.1 : Finset α), (x.2 : Finset α)))
    · intro x hx
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hx
      simp only [finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product]
      exact ⟨⟨x.1.2, x.2.2⟩, hx⟩
    · intro x _ y _ h
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at h
      exact Prod.ext (Subtype.ext h.1) (Subtype.ext h.2)
    · intro b hb
      simp only [finset_one_inclusion_pairs, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product] at hb
      refine ⟨(⟨b.1, hb.1.1⟩, ⟨b.2, hb.1.2⟩), ?_, rfl⟩
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
      exact hb.2

steps.claim: Twice the number of edges equals the number of one-inclusion pairs in 𝓕.
steps.explanation: By SimpleGraph.two_mul_card_edgeFinset, the number of directed edges (adjacent vertex pairs) in a simple graph is twice the number of undirected edges.
steps.code:
have key : 2 * (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).edgeFinset.card =
      (finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝓕).card := by
    rw [← hbij]
    convert SimpleGraph.two_mul_card_edgeFinset (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕)

steps.claim: The number of edges in the one-inclusion graph is at most d * |𝓕|.
steps.explanation: Combining 2 * |E| = |finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝓕| with the bound |finset_one_inclusion_pairs 𝓕| ≤ 2 * (d * |𝓕|) and dividing by 2 yields |E| ≤ d * |𝓕|.
steps.code:
have h2 : 2 * (finset_one_inclusion_graph 𝓕).edgeFinset.card ≤ 2 * (d * 𝓕.card) := by
    rw [key]; exact hpairs
  exact Nat.le_of_mul_le_mul_left h2 (by norm_num)

glossary.Finset.mem_inter: An element belongs to the intersection of two finsets if and only if it belongs to both.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If a finite set is a subset of another, its cardinality is at most the other set's cardinality.
glossary.Finset.card_union_le: The cardinality of the union of two finsets is at most the sum of their cardinalities.
glossary.Finset.mem_nonMemberSubfamily: A set s belongs to the non-member subfamily of a with respect to 𝒜 if and only if s is in 𝒜 and a ∉ s.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn: If a function maps a finite set injectively into another, the domain's cardinality is at most the codomain's cardinality.
glossary.Fintype.card_bool: The type Bool has exactly two elements.
glossary.Finset.card_union_add_card_inter: For any two finsets s and t, |s ∪ t| + |s ∩ t| = |s| + |t|.
glossary.finset_one_inclusion_pairs_mono: If 𝒜 ⊆ ℬ, then the one-inclusion pairs of 𝒜 form a subset of the one-inclusion pairs of ℬ.
glossary.finset_one_inclusion_pairs_inter: The intersection of the one-inclusion pairs of 𝒜 and of ℬ is a subset of the one-inclusion pairs of 𝒜 ∩ ℬ.
glossary.Finset.card_eq_zero: A finset has cardinality 0 if and only if it is empty.
glossary.Finset.subset_empty: A finset is a subset of the empty set if and only if it is empty.
glossary.Finset.subset_insert_iff_of_notMem: When an element a is not in s, s is a subset of insert a t if and only if s is a subset of t.
glossary.Finset.sup_le: The supremum of a finite set is at most a given upper bound if each element is at most that bound.
glossary.Finset.Shatters.card_le_vcDim: If a family shatters a set s, then |s| is at most the VC dimension of the family.
glossary.Finset.card_insert_of_notMem: Inserting an element not in s increases the cardinality of s by 1.
glossary.Finset.card_memberSubfamily_add_card_non: The cardinality of the member subfamily plus that of the non-member subfamily with respect to an element equals the cardinality of the full family.
glossary.finset_one_inclusion_pairs_card_split: Splitting a family 𝒜 along an element a bounds its one-inclusion pairs by the pairs of the union, the pairs of the intersection, and twice the size of the intersection of its subfamilies.
glossary.finset_one_inclusion_pairs_card_le: If every set in 𝒜 is a subset of a finite universe u and 𝒜 has VC dimension at most d, then 𝒜 has at most 2 * (d * |𝒜|) one-inclusion pairs.
glossary.Finset.le_sup: Any element of a finset is less than or equal to the supremum of the finset under a function.
glossary.Finset.card_bij: A bijection between two finsets proves they have the same cardinality.
glossary.SimpleGraph.two_mul_card_edgeFinset: In a finite simple graph, twice the number of edges equals the number of ordered pairs of adjacent vertices.
glossary.Nat.le_of_mul_le_mul_left: If c * a ≤ c * b and c > 0, then a ≤ b for natural numbers.

declarations.name: simple_graph_card_le_choose_add_one_of_regular_triangle_distinct
declarations.informal: An r-regular triangle-distinct graph has at most C(r, 2) + 1 vertices: its triangle-degrees are pairwise distinct and lie in {0, …, C(r, 2)}.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_card_le_choose_add_one_of_regular_triangle_distinct {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (r : ℕ)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree r) (htd : simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct G) :
    Fintype.card V ≤ r.choose 2 + 1
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_card_le_choose_add_one_of_regular_triangle_distinct {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (r : ℕ)
    (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree r) (htd : simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct G) :
    Fintype.card V ≤ r.choose 2 + 1 := by
  have hmaps : ∀ v ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset V),
      simple_graph_triangle_degree G v ∈ Finset.range (r.choose 2 + 1) := by
    intro v _
    have h1 := simple_graph_triangle_degree_le_choose G v
    rw [hreg v] at h1
    rw [Finset.mem_range]
    omega
  have := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn _ hmaps htd.injOn
  simpa using this
declarations.citation: Pigeonhole bound used for OP-123 (arXiv:2610.08478 (Regular K_3-Irregular Graphs of Every Regularity at Least Nine), Sec. 1).

explanation.summary: The proof applies the pigeonhole principle to the triangle-degree function on the vertices. In an r-regular graph, every vertex has degree r, so each vertex can be part of at most C(r, 2) triangles. Because the graph is triangle-distinct, no two vertices share the same triangle-degree. The triangle-degree map is therefore an injection from the vertex set into {0, …, C(r, 2)}, forcing the number of vertices to be at most C(r, 2) + 1.

steps.claim: For every vertex v, its triangle-degree is at most C(r, 2), so it belongs to {0, …, C(r, 2)}.
steps.explanation: For an arbitrary vertex v, the number of triangles containing v is at most C(deg(v), 2) by simple_graph_triangle_degree_le_choose. Since the graph is r-regular (hreg), deg(v) = r, which bounds the triangle-degree by C(r, 2). Rewriting with Finset.mem_range expresses membership in the range of C(r, 2) + 1 as being strictly less than C(r, 2) + 1, which holds by linear arithmetic (omega).
steps.code:
have hmaps : ∀ v ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset V),
      simple_graph_triangle_degree G v ∈ Finset.range (r.choose 2 + 1) := by
    intro v _
    have h1 := simple_graph_triangle_degree_le_choose G v
    rw [hreg v] at h1
    rw [Finset.mem_range]
    omega

steps.claim: The number of vertices |V| is at most C(r, 2) + 1.
steps.explanation: Because G is triangle-distinct (htd), the triangle-degree map is injective. Since it maps the finite set of all vertices into the range {0, …, C(r, 2)}, the pigeonhole principle for finite sets (Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn) implies that the number of vertices cannot exceed the size of the codomain, which is C(r, 2) + 1. Simplifying the cardinalities (simpa) concludes the proof.
steps.code:
have := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn _ hmaps htd.injOn
  simpa using this

glossary.simple_graph_triangle_degree_le_choose: The triangle-degree of any vertex v in a graph is at most the number of pairs of its neighbors, C(deg(v), 2).
glossary.Finset.mem_range: A natural number m belongs to Finset.range n if and only if m < n.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn: An injective map from a finite set s to a finite set t implies |s| ≤ |t|.

declarations.name: regular_eight_triangle_distinct_card_ge_fifteen
declarations.informal: Every 8-regular triangle-distinct graph with at least one vertex has at least 15 vertices: its complement is (n − 9)-regular and triangle-distinct, so n ≤ C(n − 9, 2) + 1, which fails for 9 ≤ n ≤ 14.
declarations.statement:
theorem regular_eight_triangle_distinct_card_ge_fifteen {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    [Nonempty V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree 8)
    (htd : simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct G) : 15 ≤ Fintype.card V
declarations.source:
theorem regular_eight_triangle_distinct_card_ge_fifteen {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    [Nonempty V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree 8)
    (htd : simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct G) : 15 ≤ Fintype.card V := by
  obtain ⟨v⟩ := ‹Nonempty V›
  have h9 : 9 ≤ Fintype.card V := by
    have := G.degree_lt_card_verts v
    rw [hreg v] at this
    omega
  obtain ⟨hcreg, hctd⟩ :=
    simple_graph_compl_regular_triangle_distinct G 8 (Fintype.card V) rfl hreg htd
  have hb := simple_graph_card_le_choose_add_one_of_regular_triangle_distinct Gᶜ _ hcreg hctd
  by_contra hlt
  push Not at hlt
  interval_cases h : Fintype.card V <;> simp_all [Nat.choose]
declarations.citation: Partial result towards OP-123 (arXiv:2610.08478 (Regular K_3-Irregular Graphs of Every Regularity at Least Nine), Lemma 2.1 complementation and Sec. 1); the earlier work cited there narrows the regularity-8 case further, to six orders.

explanation.summary: Since the graph is 8-regular and nonempty, every vertex has degree 8 < |V|, establishing the lower bound |V| ≥ 9. Its complement graph is (|V| − 9)-regular and triangle-distinct, which yields the upper bound |V| ≤ C(|V| − 9, 2) + 1. A finite case analysis over the integers 9 ≤ |V| ≤ 14 shows that none satisfies this bound, so |V| must be at least 15.

steps.claim: The graph has at least 9 vertices (|V| ≥ 9).
steps.explanation: Since V is nonempty, we can pick a vertex v ∈ V. In any simple graph, the degree of a vertex is strictly less than the total number of vertices. Since G is 8-regular, the degree of v is 8, which implies 8 < |V|, and therefore |V| ≥ 9.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨v⟩ := ‹Nonempty V›
  have h9 : 9 ≤ Fintype.card V := by
    have := G.degree_lt_card_verts v
    rw [hreg v] at this
    omega

steps.claim: The complement graph Gᶜ is (|V| − 9)-regular and triangle-distinct.
steps.explanation: Applying simple_graph_compl_regular_triangle_distinct to the 8-regular triangle-distinct graph G on |V| vertices shows that its complement graph Gᶜ is regular of degree |V| − 8 − 1 = |V| − 9 and remains triangle-distinct.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨hcreg, hctd⟩ :=
    simple_graph_compl_regular_triangle_distinct G 8 (Fintype.card V) rfl hreg htd

steps.claim: The number of vertices satisfies |V| ≤ C(|V| − 9, 2) + 1.
steps.explanation: Applying simple_graph_card_le_choose_add_one_of_regular_triangle_distinct to the complement graph Gᶜ, any r-regular triangle-distinct graph has at most C(r, 2) + 1 vertices. Since Gᶜ has degree r = |V| − 9, this gives the upper bound |V| ≤ C(|V| − 9, 2) + 1.
steps.code: have hb := simple_graph_card_le_choose_add_one_of_regular_triangle_distinct Gᶜ _ hcreg hctd

steps.claim: The graph has at least 15 vertices (|V| ≥ 15).
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that |V| < 15. Combined with |V| ≥ 9, this leaves only the cases |V| ∈ {9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14}. Evaluating the inequality n ≤ C(n − 9, 2) + 1 for each of these six integers yields a contradiction in every case: 9 ≤ 1, 10 ≤ 1, 11 ≤ 2, 12 ≤ 4, 13 ≤ 7, and 14 ≤ 11 are all false. Therefore, |V| ≥ 15.
steps.code:
by_contra hlt
  push Not at hlt
  interval_cases h : Fintype.card V <;> simp_all [Nat.choose]

glossary.G.degree_lt_card_verts: In any finite simple graph, the degree of any vertex is strictly less than the total number of vertices in the graph.
glossary.simple_graph_compl_regular_triangle_dist: If a graph on N vertices is r-regular and triangle-distinct, then its complement graph is (N − r − 1)-regular and triangle-distinct.
glossary.simple_graph_card_le_choose_add_one_of_r: Every r-regular triangle-distinct graph on a finite vertex set has at most C(r, 2) + 1 vertices.
glossary.Nat.choose: The binomial coefficient C(n, k), representing the number of k-element subsets of an n-element set.

declarations.name: simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_superset
declarations.informal: In a finite graph every independent set is contained in a maximal independent set.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_superset {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (H : SimpleGraph V) (Y : Finset V) (hY : H.IsIndepSet (Y : Set V)) :
    ∃ Z : Finset V, Y ⊆ Z ∧ Maximal (fun u : Finset V => H.IsIndepSet (u : Set V)) Z
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_superset {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (H : SimpleGraph V) (Y : Finset V) (hY : H.IsIndepSet (Y : Set V)) :
    ∃ Z : Finset V, Y ⊆ Z ∧ Maximal (fun u : Finset V => H.IsIndepSet (u : Set V)) Z := by
  classical
  set S := (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset V)).filter (fun Z => Y ⊆ Z ∧ H.IsIndepSet (Z : Set V))
  have hYS : Y ∈ S := by simp [S, hY]
  obtain ⟨Z, hZS, hZmax⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image S Finset.card ⟨Y, hYS⟩
  simp only [S, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hZS
  refine ⟨Z, hZS.1, hZS.2, fun Z' hZ' hsub => ?_⟩
  have hZ'S : Z' ∈ S := by
    simp only [S, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
    exact ⟨hZS.1.trans hsub, hZ'⟩
  have := Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le hsub (hZmax Z' hZ'S)
  rw [this]
declarations.citation: Standard; serves simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball_union_subset (arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), proof of Lemma 2.7).

explanation.summary: In a finite graph, the collection $S$ of all independent sets containing $Y$ is finite and nonempty since $Y \in S$. We choose an element $Z \in S$ of maximum cardinality. If $Z'$ is any independent superset of $Z$, it also contains $Y$ and thus belongs to $S$, so by cardinality maximality $|Z'| \le |Z|$; combined with $Z \subseteq Z'$, this forces $Z = Z'$, showing that $Z$ is maximal.

steps.claim: The family $S$ of independent supersets of $Y$ is defined, and $Y \in S$.
steps.explanation: We work classically and define $S$ to be the finite collection of all subsets of $V$ that contain $Y$ and are independent in $H$. Since $Y \subseteq Y$ and $Y$ is independent by hypothesis, $Y$ belongs to $S$, showing that $S$ is nonempty.
steps.code:
classical
  set S := (Finset.univ : Finset (Finset V)).filter (fun Z => Y ⊆ Z ∧ H.IsIndepSet (Z : Set V))
  have hYS : Y ∈ S := by simp [S, hY]

steps.claim: There exists a set $Z \in S$ of maximum cardinality, which is an independent superset of $Y$.
steps.explanation: Because $S$ is nonempty, `Finset.exists_max_image` yields an element $Z \in S$ maximizing `Finset.card`. Unfolding the definition of $S$ via `Finset.mem_filter`, `Finset.mem_univ`, and `true_and` unpacks the membership $Z \in S$ into $Y \subseteq Z$ and the fact that $Z$ is independent.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨Z, hZS, hZmax⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image S Finset.card ⟨Y, hYS⟩
  simp only [S, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hZS

steps.claim: Choosing $Z$ reduces the goal to showing that any independent superset $Z' \supseteq Z$ satisfies $Z' \subseteq Z$.
steps.explanation: We provide $Z$ as the witness. We have already established that $Y \subseteq Z$ and that $Z$ is independent. By definition of `Maximal`, it remains to show that whenever $Z'$ is independent and $Z \subseteq Z'$, we have $Z' \subseteq Z$.
steps.code: refine ⟨Z, hZS.1, hZS.2, fun Z' hZ' hsub => ?_⟩

steps.claim: Any independent superset $Z'$ of $Z$ belongs to $S$.
steps.explanation: By transitivity of inclusion, $Y \subseteq Z$ and $Z \subseteq Z'$ imply $Y \subseteq Z'$. Since $Z'$ is also independent, it satisfies the membership condition for $S$ after simplifying with `Finset.mem_filter`, `Finset.mem_univ`, and `true_and`.
steps.code:
have hZ'S : Z' ∈ S := by
    simp only [S, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
    exact ⟨hZS.1.trans hsub, hZ'⟩

steps.claim: $Z = Z'$, which implies $Z' \subseteq Z$ and completes the proof.
steps.explanation: Since $Z' \in S$, the maximality of $Z$ in $S$ implies $|Z'| \le |Z|$. By `Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le`, the inclusion $Z \subseteq Z'$ combined with $|Z'| \le |Z|$ forces $Z = Z'$. Substituting this equality into $Z' \subseteq Z$ closes the goal.
steps.code:
have := Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le hsub (hZmax Z' hZ'S)
  rw [this]

glossary.Finset.exists_max_image: In any nonempty finite set, a function into a linearly ordered type achieves a maximum at some element.
glossary.Finset.card: The cardinality (number of elements) of a finite set as a natural number.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to the filtered set `Finset.filter p s` if and only if it belongs to `s` and satisfies predicate `p`.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finset `Finset.univ`.
glossary.true_and: The proposition `True ∧ p` is logically equivalent to `p`.
glossary.Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le: If finite sets satisfy `s ⊆ t` and `card t ≤ card s`, then `s = t`.

declarations.name: simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball_union_subset
declarations.informal: Let G be a finite graph and d ≥ 1 with G^d well-covered. Then there are no vertices s, t, w with d_G(s, t) ≥ d + 1 and B_d(s) ∪ B_d(t) ⊆ B_d(w), where B_d(x) is the set of vertices at distance at most d from x.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball_union_subset {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
    (hwc : simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)) (s t w : V)
    (hst : ((d + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ G.edist s t) :
    ¬ ∀ x : V, (G.edist s x ≤ d ∨ G.edist t x ≤ d) → G.edist w x ≤ d
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball_union_subset {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (d : ℕ) (hd : 1 ≤ d)
    (hwc : simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)) (s t w : V)
    (hst : ((d + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ G.edist s t) :
    ¬ ∀ x : V, (G.edist s x ≤ d ∨ G.edist t x ≤ d) → G.edist w x ≤ d := by
  intro hball
  set P := simple_graph_power G d
  have hsw : G.edist w s ≤ d := hball s (Or.inl (by simp))
  have htw : G.edist w t ≤ d := hball t (Or.inr (by simp))
  have hlt : ∀ x y : V, G.edist x y ≤ d → ¬ ((d + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ G.edist x y := by
    intro x y h1 h2
    have := h2.trans h1
    norm_cast at this
    omega
  have hst_ne : s ≠ t := by
    intro h; subst h; simp at hst
  have hws : w ≠ s := by
    intro h; subst h; exact hlt w t htw hst
  have hwt : w ≠ t := by
    intro h; subst h; rw [SimpleGraph.edist_comm] at hsw; exact hlt s w hsw hst
  have hadjw : ∀ x, x ≠ w → (G.edist s x ≤ d ∨ G.edist t x ≤ d) → P.Adj w x :=
    fun x hx h => ⟨fun e => hx e.symm, hball x h⟩
  obtain ⟨X, hwX, hX⟩ := simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_superset P {w} (by simp)
  have hwX' : w ∈ X := hwX (Finset.mem_singleton_self w)
  have hsX : s ∉ X := fun h => hX.1 hwX' h hws (hadjw s hws.symm (Or.inl (by simp)))
  have htX : t ∉ X := fun h => hX.1 hwX' h hwt (hadjw t hwt.symm (Or.inr (by simp)))
  set Y := X.erase w ∪ {s, t}
  have hYind : P.IsIndepSet (Y : Set V) := by
    have key : ∀ x ∈ X.erase w, ∀ y ∈ ({s, t} : Finset V), ¬ P.Adj y x := by
      intro x hx y hy hadj
      rw [Finset.mem_erase] at hx
      have hyx : G.edist y x ≤ d := hadj.2
      simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hy
      have : P.Adj w x := by
        rcases hy with rfl | rfl
        · exact hadjw x hx.1 (Or.inl hyx)
        · exact hadjw x hx.1 (Or.inr hyx)
      exact hX.1 hwX' hx.2 (fun e => hx.1 e.symm) this
    intro x hx y hy hxy hadj
    simp only [Y, Finset.coe_union, Set.mem_union, Finset.mem_coe] at hx hy
    rcases hx with hx | hx <;> rcases hy with hy | hy
    · exact hX.1 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hx) (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hy) hxy hadj
    · exact key x hx y hy hadj.symm
    · exact key y hy x hx hadj
    · simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx hy
      have hst' : ¬ P.Adj s t := fun h => hlt s t h.2 hst
      rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy with rfl | rfl
      · exact hxy rfl
      · exact hst' hadj
      · exact hst' hadj.symm
      · exact hxy rfl
  obtain ⟨Z, hYZ, hZ⟩ := simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_superset P Y hYind
  have hcardY : Y.card = X.card + 1 := by
    have hdisj : Disjoint (X.erase w) {s, t} := by
      rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
      intro x hx hx'
      simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx'
      rcases hx' with rfl | rfl
      · exact hsX (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hx)
      · exact htX (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hx)
    rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hwX',
      Finset.card_pair hst_ne]
    have : 1 ≤ X.card := Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨w, hwX'⟩
    omega
  have h1 := Finset.card_le_card hYZ
  have h2 := hwc X Z hX hZ
  omega
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Lemma 2.7. The proof uses well-coveredness directly (two maximal independent sets of different sizes) instead of the independence number.

explanation.summary: We argue by contradiction: suppose there exist vertices s, t, w with d_G(s, t) ≥ d + 1 such that B_d(s) ∪ B_d(t) ⊆ B_d(w). In the power graph P = G^d, the vertices s and t are non-adjacent and both are distinct from w. We extend {w} to a maximal independent set X in P, which cannot contain s or t since both are adjacent to w in P. Replacing w with {s, t} gives a new independent set Y = (X \ {w}) ∪ {s, t}, because any neighbor of s or t in X \ {w} would belong to B_d(s) ∪ B_d(t) ⊆ B_d(w) and thus be adjacent to w, contradicting the independence of X. Extending Y to a maximal independent set Z gives |Z| ≥ |Y| = |X| + 1, contradicting the hypothesis that P is well-covered.

steps.claim: Assume for contradiction that B_d(s) ∪ B_d(t) ⊆ B_d(w), and deduce that d_G(w, s) ≤ d and d_G(w, t) ≤ d.
steps.explanation: We assume for contradiction that every vertex within distance d of s or t is within distance d of w (hball). We set P = simple_graph_power G d. Since d_G(s, s) = 0 ≤ d, vertex s is in B_d(s) and hence in B_d(w), showing d_G(w, s) ≤ d (hsw). Similarly, d_G(t, t) = 0 ≤ d implies d_G(w, t) ≤ d (htw).
steps.code:
intro hball
  set P := simple_graph_power G d
  have hsw : G.edist w s ≤ d := hball s (Or.inl (by simp))
  have htw : G.edist w t ≤ d := hball t (Or.inr (by simp))

steps.claim: Show that distance at most d is incompatible with distance at least d + 1, and deduce that s, t, w are pairwise distinct.
steps.explanation: First, having both d_G(x, y) ≤ d and d + 1 ≤ d_G(x, y) gives d + 1 ≤ d by transitivity, an impossibility (hlt). If s = t, then d_G(s, t) = 0 ≥ d + 1 ≥ 2, a contradiction; hence s ≠ t (hst_ne). If w = s, then d_G(s, t) = d_G(w, t) ≤ d, contradicting d_G(s, t) ≥ d + 1; hence w ≠ s (hws). Finally, if w = t, symmetry of distance (SimpleGraph.edist_comm) yields d_G(s, t) = d_G(s, w) = d_G(w, s) ≤ d, again contradicting d_G(s, t) ≥ d + 1; hence w ≠ t (hwt).
steps.code:
have hlt : ∀ x y : V, G.edist x y ≤ d → ¬ ((d + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ G.edist x y := by
    intro x y h1 h2
    have := h2.trans h1
    norm_cast at this
    omega
  have hst_ne : s ≠ t := by
    intro h; subst h; simp at hst
  have hws : w ≠ s := by
    intro h; subst h; exact hlt w t htw hst
  have hwt : w ≠ t := by
    intro h; subst h; rw [SimpleGraph.edist_comm] at hsw; exact hlt s w hsw hst

steps.claim: Extend {w} to a maximal independent set X in P, and show that neither s nor t belongs to X.
steps.explanation: Any vertex x ≠ w in B_d(s) ∪ B_d(t) has d_G(w, x) ≤ d and thus is adjacent to w in P (hadjw). The singleton {w} is independent in P, so it extends to a maximal independent set X with w ∈ X (simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_superset, Finset.mem_singleton_self). Since s ≠ w and d_G(s, s) ≤ d, vertex s is adjacent to w in P; because X is independent and w ∈ X, we have s ∉ X (hsX). By the same argument for t, t ∉ X (htX).
steps.code:
have hadjw : ∀ x, x ≠ w → (G.edist s x ≤ d ∨ G.edist t x ≤ d) → P.Adj w x :=
    fun x hx h => ⟨fun e => hx e.symm, hball x h⟩
  obtain ⟨X, hwX, hX⟩ := simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_superset P {w} (by simp)
  have hwX' : w ∈ X := hwX (Finset.mem_singleton_self w)
  have hsX : s ∉ X := fun h => hX.1 hwX' h hws (hadjw s hws.symm (Or.inl (by simp)))
  have htX : t ∉ X := fun h => hX.1 hwX' h hwt (hadjw t hwt.symm (Or.inr (by simp)))

steps.claim: The set Y = (X \ {w}) ∪ {s, t} is independent in P.
steps.explanation: We check that no two distinct vertices in Y are adjacent in P. If some x ∈ X \ {w} were adjacent to y ∈ {s, t}, then d_G(y, x) ≤ d, placing x in B_d(s) ∪ B_d(t). Since x ≠ w, this would make x adjacent to w in P, which is impossible because both w, x ∈ X and X is independent (the helper lemma key). Vertices within X \ {w} are non-adjacent because X is independent (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase). Finally, s and t cannot be adjacent in P because d_G(s, t) ≥ d + 1 > d. Thus Y is an independent set in P.
steps.code:
set Y := X.erase w ∪ {s, t}
  have hYind : P.IsIndepSet (Y : Set V) := by
    have key : ∀ x ∈ X.erase w, ∀ y ∈ ({s, t} : Finset V), ¬ P.Adj y x := by
      intro x hx y hy hadj
      rw [Finset.mem_erase] at hx
      have hyx : G.edist y x ≤ d := hadj.2
      simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hy
      have : P.Adj w x := by
        rcases hy with rfl | rfl
        · exact hadjw x hx.1 (Or.inl hyx)
        · exact hadjw x hx.1 (Or.inr hyx)
      exact hX.1 hwX' hx.2 (fun e => hx.1 e.symm) this
    intro x hx y hy hxy hadj
    simp only [Y, Finset.coe_union, Set.mem_union, Finset.mem_coe] at hx hy
    rcases hx with hx | hx <;> rcases hy with hy | hy
    · exact hX.1 (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hx) (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hy) hxy hadj
    · exact key x hx y hy hadj.symm
    · exact key y hy x hx hadj
    · simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx hy
      have hst' : ¬ P.Adj s t := fun h => hlt s t h.2 hst
      rcases hx with rfl | rfl <;> rcases hy with rfl | rfl
      · exact hxy rfl
      · exact hst' hadj
      · exact hst' hadj.symm
      · exact hxy rfl

steps.claim: Extend Y to a maximal independent set Z in P, and show |Y| = |X| + 1.
steps.explanation: The independent set Y extends to a maximal independent set Z in P (simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_superset). Since neither s nor t is in X, the sets X \ {w} and {s, t} are disjoint (Finset.disjoint_left). The cardinality of their union is therefore |X \ {w}| + |{s, t}| (Finset.card_union_of_disjoint). Since w ∈ X, erasing w gives |X| - 1 (Finset.card_erase_of_mem), and because s ≠ t, |{s, t}| = 2 (Finset.card_pair). Thus |Y| = (|X| - 1) + 2 = |X| + 1.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨Z, hYZ, hZ⟩ := simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_superset P Y hYind
  have hcardY : Y.card = X.card + 1 := by
    have hdisj : Disjoint (X.erase w) {s, t} := by
      rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
      intro x hx hx'
      simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hx'
      rcases hx' with rfl | rfl
      · exact hsX (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hx)
      · exact htX (Finset.mem_of_mem_erase hx)
    rw [Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hwX',
      Finset.card_pair hst_ne]
    have : 1 ≤ X.card := Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨w, hwX'⟩
    omega

steps.claim: Derive a contradiction: |Z| ≥ |X| + 1 contradicts well-coveredness, which requires |Z| = |X|.
steps.explanation: Since Y ⊆ Z, we have |Y| ≤ |Z| (Finset.card_le_card), so |Z| ≥ |X| + 1. But P is well-covered (hwc), so all maximal independent sets have the same size, which forces |X| = |Z|. This gives |X| ≥ |X| + 1, an arithmetic impossibility that omega resolves to conclude False.
steps.code:
have h1 := Finset.card_le_card hYZ
  have h2 := hwc X Z hX hZ
  omega

glossary.SimpleGraph.edist_comm: Extended distance between vertices in a graph is symmetric: d_G(u, v) = d_G(v, u).
glossary.simple_graph_exists_maximal_indep_supers: Every independent set in a finite graph extends to an inclusion-maximal independent set.
glossary.Finset.mem_singleton_self: An element is a member of its own singleton set: a ∈ {a}.
glossary.Finset.mem_erase: An element is in s.erase b if and only if it is in s and distinct from b.
glossary.Finset.mem_insert: An element belongs to insert b s if and only if it equals b or is in s.
glossary.Finset.mem_singleton: An element belongs to {a} if and only if it equals a.
glossary.Finset.coe_union: The coercion of a union of finite sets to a Set equals the union of their coercions: ↑(s₁ ∪ s₂) = ↑s₁ ∪ ↑s₂.
glossary.Set.mem_union: An element belongs to a ∪ b if and only if it belongs to a or to b.
glossary.Finset.mem_coe: Membership in the coerced Set ↑s is equivalent to membership in the Finset s.
glossary.Finset.mem_of_mem_erase: If an element belongs to s.erase a, then it belongs to s.
glossary.Finset.disjoint_left: Two finite sets are disjoint if and only if no element of the first belongs to the second.
glossary.Finset.card_union_of_disjoint: If two finite sets are disjoint, the cardinality of their union is the sum of their cardinalities.
glossary.Finset.card_erase_of_mem: Removing an element a from a finite set s of which it is a member decreases its cardinality by 1.
glossary.Finset.card_pair: If two elements are distinct, the pair {a, b} has cardinality 2.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If s ⊆ t for finite sets, then |s| ≤ |t|.

caveats: The power graph simple_graph_power G d defines an edge between distinct vertices u ≠ v whenever their extended distance G.edist u v in G is at most d.
The helper lemma hlt casts distances from ℕ∞ to ℕ so that the contradictory inequality d + 1 ≤ d can be resolved by omega.
