declarations.name: simple_graph_eccent_eq_diam_of_power_well_covered
declarations.informal: Let G be a finite connected graph of diameter D ≥ 2 such that G^{D−1} is well-covered. Then every vertex of G has eccentricity D (G is self-centered).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_eccent_eq_diam_of_power_well_covered {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hconn : G.Connected) (hD : 2 ≤ G.diam)
    (hwc : simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G (G.diam - 1))) (v : V) :
    G.eccent v = G.diam
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_eccent_eq_diam_of_power_well_covered {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hconn : G.Connected) (hD : 2 ≤ G.diam)
    (hwc : simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G (G.diam - 1))) (v : V) :
    G.eccent v = G.diam := by
  have : Nonempty V := hconn.nonempty
  have htop : G.ediam ≠ ⊤ := (SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top).1 hconn
  have hdiam : (G.diam : ℕ∞) = G.ediam := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.diam]; exact ENat.natCast_toNat htop
  apply le_antisymm (hdiam ▸ G.eccent_le_ediam)
  by_contra hlt
  rw [not_le] at hlt
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ : ∃ e : ℕ, G.eccent v = e := ⟨(G.eccent v).toNat,
    (ENat.natCast_toNat (ne_top_of_lt hlt)).symm⟩
  rw [he] at hlt
  norm_cast at hlt
  obtain ⟨s, t, hst⟩ := G.exists_edist_eq_ediam_of_finite
  refine simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball_union_subset G (G.diam - 1) (by omega) hwc s t v
    ?_ ?_
  · rw [hst, ← hdiam]; norm_cast; omega
  · intro x _
    calc G.edist v x ≤ G.eccent v := SimpleGraph.edist_le_eccent
      _ = e := he
      _ ≤ ((G.diam - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by norm_cast; omega
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Lemma 2.5, for D ≥ 2 (for D ≤ 1 the power G^{D−1} is edgeless); proof via Lemma 2.7 (simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball_union_subset) with w the vertex of small eccentricity.

explanation.summary: By definition, the eccentricity of any vertex v is at most the diameter D. Supposing for contradiction that ecc(v) < D, the eccentricity must satisfy ecc(v) ≤ D − 1, which means the closed ball B_{D−1}(v) covers all vertices in the graph. In particular, choosing two vertices s and t at maximal distance D ≥ (D − 1) + 1, the ball B_{D−1}(v) would contain the union B_{D−1}(s) ∪ B_{D−1}(t); but this contradicts the structural theorem simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball_union_subset for well-covered powers of graphs.

steps.claim: The extended diameter of G is finite and equals the diameter G.diam coerced to ℕ∞.
steps.explanation: Because G is connected, its vertex set is non-empty. For a finite connected graph, the extended diameter cannot be infinite (SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top). By definition of the diameter G.diam as ediam.toNat, casting it back to ℕ∞ recovers the extended diameter via ENat.natCast_toNat.
steps.code:
have : Nonempty V := hconn.nonempty
  have htop : G.ediam ≠ ⊤ := (SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top).1 hconn
  have hdiam : (G.diam : ℕ∞) = G.ediam := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.diam]; exact ENat.natCast_toNat htop

steps.claim: It suffices to show that G.diam ≤ G.eccent v.
steps.explanation: The eccentricity of v is always at most the graph diameter (G.eccent_le_ediam). By antisymmetry of ≤ (le_antisymm), equality reduces to the reverse inequality G.diam ≤ G.eccent v.
steps.code: apply le_antisymm (hdiam ▸ G.eccent_le_ediam)

steps.claim: Assuming the contrary, the eccentricity of v is a finite natural number e with e < G.diam.
steps.explanation: We assume for contradiction that G.diam ≤ G.eccent v is false, so G.eccent v < G.diam (not_le). Since it is strictly bounded by a finite value, the eccentricity cannot be ∞ (ne_top_of_lt), so it equals a natural number e (ENat.natCast_toNat) satisfying e < G.diam.
steps.code:
by_contra hlt
  rw [not_le] at hlt
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ : ∃ e : ℕ, G.eccent v = e := ⟨(G.eccent v).toNat,
    (ENat.natCast_toNat (ne_top_of_lt hlt)).symm⟩
  rw [he] at hlt
  norm_cast at hlt

steps.claim: There exist vertices s and t in G whose distance equals the diameter of G.
steps.explanation: Because G is finite, there exists a pair of vertices s and t attaining the diameter: dist(s, t) = ediam(G) (G.exists_edist_eq_ediam_of_finite).
steps.code: obtain ⟨s, t, hst⟩ := G.exists_edist_eq_ediam_of_finite

steps.claim: The contradiction reduces to showing that dist(s, t) ≥ (G.diam − 1) + 1 and that the ball B_{D−1}(v) contains B_{D−1}(s) ∪ B_{D−1}(t).
steps.explanation: Since G.diam ≥ 2, setting d = G.diam − 1 gives d ≥ 1. By the lemma simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball_union_subset, when G^d is well-covered and dist(s, t) ≥ d + 1, no single ball of radius d can contain the union of the balls of radius d around s and t. Applying this lemma leaves two obligations: confirming the distance between s and t is at least d + 1, and showing every vertex in the union of the balls around s and t is within distance d of v.
steps.code:
refine simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball_union_subset G (G.diam - 1) (by omega) hwc s t v
    ?_ ?_

steps.claim: The distance between s and t is at least (G.diam − 1) + 1.
steps.explanation: By construction, dist(s, t) = ediam(G) = G.diam. The inequality (G.diam − 1) + 1 ≤ G.diam holds by standard arithmetic since G.diam ≥ 2.
steps.code: · rw [hst, ← hdiam]; norm_cast; omega

steps.claim: Every vertex in the graph lies within distance G.diam − 1 of v, completing the contradiction.
steps.explanation: For any vertex x, the distance dist(v, x) is bounded by the eccentricity ecc(v) (SimpleGraph.edist_le_eccent), which equals e. Since e < G.diam, we have e ≤ G.diam − 1, so every vertex x in G is within distance G.diam − 1 of v. In particular, B_{D−1}(v) contains B_{D−1}(s) ∪ B_{D−1}(t), contradicting the lemma.
steps.code:
· intro x _
    calc G.edist v x ≤ G.eccent v := SimpleGraph.edist_le_eccent
      _ = e := he
      _ ≤ ((G.diam - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by norm_cast; omega

glossary.SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top: A finite non-empty graph is connected if and only if its extended diameter is not ∞.
glossary.SimpleGraph.diam: The natural-number diameter of a graph, defined by converting its extended diameter in ℕ∞ to ℕ.
glossary.ENat.natCast_toNat: For any element n of ℕ∞ with n ≠ ⊤, casting its conversion to ℕ back to ℕ∞ returns n.
glossary.le_antisymm: In a partial order, if a ≤ b and b ≤ a, then a = b.
glossary.G.eccent_le_ediam: The eccentricity of any vertex in a graph is at most the graph's extended diameter.
glossary.not_le: In a linear order, not being less than or equal to an element is equivalent to being strictly greater than it.
glossary.ne_top_of_lt: In a preorder with a top element ⊤, an element strictly smaller than another cannot be ⊤.
glossary.G.exists_edist_eq_ediam_of_finite: In a finite non-empty graph, there exists a pair of vertices whose distance equals the extended diameter.
glossary.simple_graph_power_well_covered_not_ball: If the d-th power of a graph is well-covered (with d ≥ 1) and two vertices s, t are at distance at least d + 1, then no vertex w has its closed ball of radius d contain the union of the closed balls of radius d centered at s and t.
glossary.SimpleGraph.edist_le_eccent: The distance between any vertex u and another vertex v is at most the eccentricity of u.

caveats: Coercions between ℕ and ℕ∞ are handled formally by ENat.natCast_toNat and norm_cast.

declarations.name: simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_covered
declarations.informal: Let G be a finite connected graph of diameter D ≥ 2 such that G^{D−1} is well-covered. Then G has no leaves (no vertex of degree 1).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_covered {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hconn : G.Connected) (hD : 2 ≤ G.diam)
    (hwc : simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G (G.diam - 1))) (v : V) :
    G.degree v ≠ 1
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_covered {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hconn : G.Connected) (hD : 2 ≤ G.diam)
    (hwc : simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G (G.diam - 1))) (v : V) :
    G.degree v ≠ 1 := by
  intro hdeg
  obtain ⟨u, hvu, huniq⟩ := (SimpleGraph.degree_eq_one_iff_existsUnique_adj).1 hdeg
  have : Nonempty V := hconn.nonempty
  have htop : G.ediam ≠ ⊤ := (SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top).1 hconn
  have hdiam : (G.diam : ℕ∞) = G.ediam := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.diam]; exact ENat.natCast_toNat htop
  have hecc := simple_graph_eccent_eq_diam_of_power_well_covered G hconn hD hwc u
  have hle : G.eccent u ≤ ((G.diam - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.eccent_le_iff]
    intro w
    by_cases hwv : w = v
    · subst hwv
      rw [SimpleGraph.edist_comm, SimpleGraph.edist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 hvu]
      norm_cast; omega
    · obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := (hconn v w).exists_walk_length_eq_edist
      cases p with
      | nil => exact absurd rfl hwv
      | cons h p' =>
        rename_i x
        have hx : x = u := huniq x h
        subst hx
        have h1 : G.edist x w ≤ p'.length := SimpleGraph.edist_le p'
        have h2 : G.edist v w ≤ G.diam := by rw [hdiam]; exact SimpleGraph.edist_le_ediam
        rw [← hp, SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons] at h2
        have h3 : p'.length + 1 ≤ G.diam := by exact_mod_cast h2
        calc G.edist x w ≤ p'.length := h1
          _ ≤ ((G.diam - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by norm_cast; omega
  rw [hecc] at hle
  norm_cast at hle
  omega
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Corollary 2.6.

explanation.summary: We argue by contradiction: suppose G has a leaf v, and let u be its unique neighbor. Because the power graph G^{D-1} is well-covered and D = diam(G) ≥ 2, every vertex has eccentricity D, so eccent(u) = D. On the other hand, eccent(u) ≤ D - 1: the distance from u to v is 1 ≤ D - 1, and for any w ≠ v, any shortest walk from v to w must start by stepping to u, so edist(u, w) ≤ edist(v, w) - 1 ≤ D - 1. The two bounds give D ≤ D - 1, an impossibility.

steps.claim: Assume for contradiction that v has degree 1, and obtain its unique neighbor u.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that G has a leaf v, meaning deg(v) = 1 (hdeg). By SimpleGraph.degree_eq_one_iff_existsUnique_adj, a vertex has degree 1 if and only if it has a unique neighbor. Let u be this unique neighbor, so v is adjacent to u and any neighbor of v must equal u.
steps.code:
intro hdeg
  obtain ⟨u, hvu, huniq⟩ := (SimpleGraph.degree_eq_one_iff_existsUnique_adj).1 hdeg

steps.claim: The diameter of G is finite and the eccentricity of u equals the diameter of G.
steps.explanation: Since G is connected and finite, the vertex set is nonempty and the extended diameter ediam(G) is finite by SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top. Hence the integer diameter diam(G) coerced to ℕ∞ equals ediam(G) (using SimpleGraph.diam and ENat.natCast_toNat). Because G^{diam(G)-1} is well-covered and diam(G) ≥ 2, the prior lemma simple_graph_eccent_eq_diam_of_power_well_covered implies that every vertex has eccentricity equal to diam(G), so eccent(u) = diam(G).
steps.code:
have : Nonempty V := hconn.nonempty
  have htop : G.ediam ≠ ⊤ := (SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top).1 hconn
  have hdiam : (G.diam : ℕ∞) = G.ediam := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.diam]; exact ENat.natCast_toNat htop
  have hecc := simple_graph_eccent_eq_diam_of_power_well_covered G hconn hD hwc u

steps.claim: To bound the eccentricity of u by diam(G) - 1, it suffices to bound the distance from u to any vertex w by diam(G) - 1.
steps.explanation: By SimpleGraph.eccent_le_iff, the eccentricity of u is at most a bound k if and only if the distance from u to every vertex is at most k. Setting k = diam(G) - 1, we introduce an arbitrary vertex w and aim to show edist(u, w) ≤ diam(G) - 1.
steps.code:
have hle : G.eccent u ≤ ((G.diam - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.eccent_le_iff]
    intro w

steps.claim: In the case w = v, the distance between u and w is 1, which is at most diam(G) - 1.
steps.explanation: We perform a case split on whether w = v. If w = v, the distance edist(u, v) equals edist(v, u) = 1 because u and v are adjacent (SimpleGraph.edist_comm, SimpleGraph.edist_eq_one_iff_adj). Since diam(G) ≥ 2, linear arithmetic (omega) closes the inequality 1 ≤ diam(G) - 1.
steps.code:
by_cases hwv : w = v
    · subst hwv
      rw [SimpleGraph.edist_comm, SimpleGraph.edist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 hvu]
      norm_cast; omega

steps.claim: In the case w ≠ v, any shortest walk from v to w must pass through u, establishing edist(u, w) ≤ diam(G) - 1 and thus eccent(u) ≤ diam(G) - 1.
steps.explanation: When w ≠ v, connectivity guarantees a walk p from v to w whose length equals edist(v, w) (exists_walk_length_eq_edist). The walk p cannot be the empty walk nil because w ≠ v. Thus p starts with an edge from v to some vertex x, followed by a walk p' from x to w. Since x is adjacent to v, uniqueness of v's neighbor forces x = u. The length of p is p'.length + 1 by SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons. Since edist(v, w) ≤ diam(G) by SimpleGraph.edist_le_ediam, we have p'.length + 1 ≤ diam(G), which gives p'.length ≤ diam(G) - 1. Finally, edist(u, w) ≤ p'.length by SimpleGraph.edist_le, yielding edist(u, w) ≤ diam(G) - 1. This completes the bound eccent(u) ≤ diam(G) - 1 for all w.
steps.code:
· obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := (hconn v w).exists_walk_length_eq_edist
      cases p with
      | nil => exact absurd rfl hwv
      | cons h p' =>
        rename_i x
        have hx : x = u := huniq x h
        subst hx
        have h1 : G.edist x w ≤ p'.length := SimpleGraph.edist_le p'
        have h2 : G.edist v w ≤ G.diam := by rw [hdiam]; exact SimpleGraph.edist_le_ediam
        rw [← hp, SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons] at h2
        have h3 : p'.length + 1 ≤ G.diam := by exact_mod_cast h2
        calc G.edist x w ≤ p'.length := h1
          _ ≤ ((G.diam - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by norm_cast; omega

steps.claim: The equality eccent(u) = diam(G) and the inequality eccent(u) ≤ diam(G) - 1 yield a contradiction.
steps.explanation: Substituting eccent(u) = diam(G) into the inequality eccent(u) ≤ diam(G) - 1 gives diam(G) ≤ diam(G) - 1. Linear arithmetic (omega) derives False from diam(G) ≤ diam(G) - 1 and diam(G) ≥ 2, contradicting the existence of the leaf v.
steps.code:
rw [hecc] at hle
  norm_cast at hle
  omega

glossary.ENat.natCast_toNat: Casting an extended natural number n to ℕ and back yields n, provided n is finite (n ≠ ⊤).
glossary.SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top: A nonempty finite simple graph is connected if and only if its extended diameter is not ⊤.
glossary.SimpleGraph.degree_eq_one_iff_existsUniq: A vertex in a simple graph has degree 1 if and only if there exists a unique vertex adjacent to it.
glossary.SimpleGraph.diam: The diameter of a simple graph is defined as the natural number obtained by truncating its extended diameter.
glossary.SimpleGraph.eccent_le_iff: The eccentricity of a vertex u is at most k if and only if the extended distance from u to every vertex is at most k.
glossary.SimpleGraph.edist_comm: Extended distance in a simple graph is symmetric: edist u v = edist v u.
glossary.SimpleGraph.edist_eq_one_iff_adj: In a simple graph, two vertices have extended distance 1 if and only if they are adjacent.
glossary.SimpleGraph.edist_le: The extended distance between two vertices is at most the length of any walk connecting them.
glossary.SimpleGraph.edist_le_ediam: The extended distance between any two vertices in a graph is at most the graph's extended diameter.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.length_cons: Prepending an edge to a walk increases its length by 1.
glossary.exists_walk_length_eq_edist: Between any two reachable vertices, there exists a walk whose length equals their extended distance.
glossary.simple_graph_eccent_eq_diam_of_power_wel: In a finite connected graph of diameter D ≥ 2 whose power G^{D-1} is well-covered, every vertex has eccentricity equal to D.

caveats: Connecting the natural number diameter diam with the extended natural number diameter ediam requires the coercion lemma ENat.natCast_toNat, which holds because connectivity ensures ediam ≠ ⊤.
The contradiction in the nil case of walk induction (line 21) is a formal detail: a walk of length 0 starts and ends at the same vertex, contradicting w ≠ v.

declarations.name: forall_power_well_covered_of_well_covered_diam_le_two
declarations.informal: Let G be a finite connected well-covered graph of diameter at most 2. Then G^d is well-covered for every d ≥ 1.
declarations.statement:
theorem forall_power_well_covered_of_well_covered_diam_le_two {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hconn : G.Connected) (hdiam : G.diam ≤ 2)
    (hwc : simple_graph_is_well_covered G) :
    ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)
declarations.source:
theorem forall_power_well_covered_of_well_covered_diam_le_two {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hconn : G.Connected) (hdiam : G.diam ≤ 2)
    (hwc : simple_graph_is_well_covered G) :
    ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d) := by
  intro d hd
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge d 2 with h1 | h2
  · have : d = 1 := by omega
    subst this
    rw [simple_graph_power_one]
    exact hwc
  · have : Nonempty V := hconn.nonempty
    have htop : G.ediam ≠ ⊤ := (SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top).1 hconn
    have hed : ∀ u v : V, G.edist u v ≤ d := by
      intro u v
      calc G.edist u v ≤ G.ediam := SimpleGraph.edist_le_ediam
        _ = G.diam := by rw [SimpleGraph.diam]; exact (ENat.natCast_toNat htop).symm
        _ ≤ d := by exact_mod_cast hdiam.trans h2
    have hcard : ∀ s : Finset V,
        Maximal (fun u : Finset V => (simple_graph_power G d).IsIndepSet (u : Set V)) s →
          s.card = 1 := by
      intro s hs
      rw [Finset.card_eq_one]
      obtain ⟨v⟩ := ‹Nonempty V›
      by_cases hne : s.Nonempty
      · obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
        refine ⟨a, Finset.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.2 ⟨ha, fun b hb => ?_⟩⟩
        by_contra hba
        exact hs.1 hb ha hba ⟨hba, hed b a⟩
      · rw [Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at hne
        subst hne
        have hv : (simple_graph_power G d).IsIndepSet (({v} : Finset V) : Set V) := by simp
        have := hs.2 hv (Finset.empty_subset _)
        simp at this
    intro s t hs ht
    rw [hcard s hs, hcard t ht]
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Sec. 3, remark before Question 3.9 ('every well-covered graph of diameter 2 automatically satisfies this condition'); stated for diameter at most 2.

explanation.summary: To show that G^d is well-covered for all d ≥ 1, the proof splits into two cases: d = 1 and d ≥ 2. When d = 1, the power graph G^1 is G itself, which is well-covered by hypothesis. When d ≥ 2, the assumption diam(G) ≤ 2 implies that every pair of distinct vertices has distance at most d and is therefore adjacent in G^d. Consequently, G^d is a complete graph, so every maximal independent set has size exactly 1, proving that G^d is well-covered.

steps.claim: For d = 1, the power graph G^1 is well-covered.
steps.explanation: We introduce the exponent d ≥ 1 and divide into cases d < 2 and d ≥ 2. In the case d < 2, linear arithmetic implies d = 1. The first power G^1 is identically G, so well-coveredness follows immediately from the assumption that G is well-covered.
steps.code:
intro d hd
  rcases Nat.lt_or_ge d 2 with h1 | h2
  · have : d = 1 := by omega
    subst this
    rw [simple_graph_power_one]
    exact hwc

steps.claim: When d ≥ 2, the distance in G between any two vertices is at most d.
steps.explanation: For d ≥ 2, graph connectedness implies the vertex set V is nonempty and the extended diameter ediam(G) is finite. The distance between any two vertices u, v ∈ V is at most ediam(G), which equals diam(G) because the extended diameter is finite. Since diam(G) ≤ 2 ≤ d, the distance between u and v is at most d.
steps.code:
· have : Nonempty V := hconn.nonempty
    have htop : G.ediam ≠ ⊤ := (SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top).1 hconn
    have hed : ∀ u v : V, G.edist u v ≤ d := by
      intro u v
      calc G.edist u v ≤ G.ediam := SimpleGraph.edist_le_ediam
        _ = G.diam := by rw [SimpleGraph.diam]; exact (ENat.natCast_toNat htop).symm
        _ ≤ d := by exact_mod_cast hdiam.trans h2

steps.claim: When d ≥ 2, every maximal independent set in G^d has cardinality 1.
steps.explanation: Let s be a maximal independent set in G^d. To show |s| = 1, we show s = {a} for some vertex a. If s were empty, any singleton {v} from the nonempty vertex set would be an independent set, contradicting the maximality of ∅. Thus s is nonempty, containing some vertex a. If s contained another vertex b ≠ a, then since dist(b, a) ≤ d, vertices b and a would be adjacent in G^d, contradicting that s is independent. Hence a is the unique element of s, so s = {a} and |s| = 1.
steps.code:
have hcard : ∀ s : Finset V,
        Maximal (fun u : Finset V => (simple_graph_power G d).IsIndepSet (u : Set V)) s →
          s.card = 1 := by
      intro s hs
      rw [Finset.card_eq_one]
      obtain ⟨v⟩ := ‹Nonempty V›
      by_cases hne : s.Nonempty
      · obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
        refine ⟨a, Finset.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem.2 ⟨ha, fun b hb => ?_⟩⟩
        by_contra hba
        exact hs.1 hb ha hba ⟨hba, hed b a⟩
      · rw [Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at hne
        subst hne
        have hv : (simple_graph_power G d).IsIndepSet (({v} : Finset V) : Set V) := by simp
        have := hs.2 hv (Finset.empty_subset _)
        simp at this

steps.claim: When d ≥ 2, G^d is well-covered.
steps.explanation: Given two maximal independent sets s and t of G^d, each has cardinality 1 by the previous step. Thus |s| = |t| = 1, which proves that G^d is well-covered.
steps.code:
intro s t hs ht
    rw [hcard s hs, hcard t ht]

glossary.Nat.lt_or_ge: For any natural numbers n and m, either n < m or n ≥ m.
glossary.simple_graph_power_one: The first power of a simple graph G is equal to G itself.
glossary.SimpleGraph.connected_iff_ediam_ne_top: A nonempty finite graph is connected if and only if its extended diameter is not infinite (⊤).
glossary.SimpleGraph.edist_le_ediam: The extended distance between any two vertices in a graph is bounded by its extended diameter.
glossary.SimpleGraph.diam: The definition of graph diameter as the natural number value of the extended diameter.
glossary.ENat.natCast_toNat: Casting a finite extended natural number to a natural number and back yields the original value.
glossary.Finset.card_eq_one: A finite set has cardinality 1 if and only if it is a singleton {a}.
glossary.Finset.eq_singleton_iff_unique_mem: A finite set s equals {a} if and only if a ∈ s and every element of s equals a.
glossary.Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty: A finite set is not nonempty if and only if it is empty.
glossary.Finset.empty_subset: The empty set is a subset of any finite set.

caveats: In the formal proof, the graph diameter is represented both as an extended natural number (ediam ∈ ℕ∞) and as a natural number (diam ∈ ℕ). Equating them requires explicitly verifying that ediam ≠ ⊤ via connectedness.
When d ≥ 2 and diam(G) ≤ 2, every pair of distinct vertices in G has distance at most d, so the power graph G^d is the complete graph on V, whose only non-empty independent sets are singletons.

declarations.name: diam_le_one_of_forall_power_well_covered_of_degree_eq_one
declarations.informal: If a finite connected graph G has a vertex of degree 1 and G^d is well-covered for every d ≥ 1, then diam(G) ≤ 1 (G is K_2). In particular OP-160's diameter bound holds, with room to spare, for graphs with a leaf, e.g. trees.
declarations.statement:
theorem diam_le_one_of_forall_power_well_covered_of_degree_eq_one {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hconn : G.Connected)
    (hwc : ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)) (v : V)
    (hleaf : G.degree v = 1) : G.diam ≤ 1
declarations.source:
theorem diam_le_one_of_forall_power_well_covered_of_degree_eq_one {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hconn : G.Connected)
    (hwc : ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)) (v : V)
    (hleaf : G.degree v = 1) : G.diam ≤ 1 := by
  by_contra h
  rw [not_le] at h
  exact simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_covered G hconn (by omega) (hwc _ (by omega)) v hleaf
declarations.citation: Partial result on OP-160 (arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Question 3.9); a direct consequence of the paper's Corollary 2.6 (simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_covered).

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by contradiction. Assuming diam(G) > 1, the diameter is at least 2, which allows setting d = diam(G) - 1 ≥ 1. Since all powers of G from degree 1 onwards are assumed to be well-covered, G^(diam(G) - 1) is well-covered; but by simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_covered, such a connected graph cannot contain any vertex of degree 1, contradicting the hypothesis that G has a leaf.

steps.claim: Assume for contradiction that diam(G) > 1.
steps.explanation: We begin a proof by contradiction by assuming ¬ (G.diam ≤ 1). Rewriting along not_le turns this into 1 < G.diam.
steps.code:
by_contra h
  rw [not_le] at h

steps.claim: Contradiction: G cannot have a vertex of degree 1.
steps.explanation: Since 1 < G.diam, integer arithmetic implies 2 ≤ G.diam and 1 ≤ G.diam - 1. Instantiating the hypothesis hwc at d = G.diam - 1 shows that G^(diam(G) - 1) is well-covered. Applying simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_covered then establishes that every vertex in G has degree different from 1, which contradicts the hypothesis that v has degree 1.
steps.code: exact simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_covered G hconn (by omega) (hwc _ (by omega)) v hleaf

glossary.not_le: For any linear order, a value is not less than or equal to another if and only if it is strictly greater: ¬ (a ≤ b) ↔ b < a.
glossary.simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_cover: In a finite connected graph G with diameter at least 2, if the power graph G^(diam(G) - 1) is well-covered, then G has no vertex of degree 1.

caveats: The conditions 2 ≤ G.diam and 1 ≤ G.diam - 1 required by simple_graph_no_leaf_of_power_well_covered and the well-coveredness hypothesis are discharged inline by the omega tactic via linear integer arithmetic from 1 < G.diam.

declarations.name: cycle_wrap_set_compl_eq_Icc_and_sum
declarations.informal: For 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, the complement in {1,…,n} of the wrap set W = {j,…,n} ∪ {1,…,i} of the n-cycle is the standard interval {i+1,…,j−1} (empty when j = i+1), and its element sum is T_n − W*, where T_n = n(n+1)/2 and W* is the element sum of W.
declarations.statement:
theorem cycle_wrap_set_compl_eq_Icc_and_sum (n i j : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hij : i < j) (hj : j ≤ n) :
    Finset.Icc 1 n \ (Finset.Icc j n ∪ Finset.Icc 1 i) = Finset.Icc (i + 1) (j - 1) ∧
    ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n \ (Finset.Icc j n ∪ Finset.Icc 1 i), x =
      n * (n + 1) / 2 - ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc j n ∪ Finset.Icc 1 i, x
declarations.source:
theorem cycle_wrap_set_compl_eq_Icc_and_sum (n i j : ℕ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) (hij : i < j) (hj : j ≤ n) :
    Finset.Icc 1 n \ (Finset.Icc j n ∪ Finset.Icc 1 i) = Finset.Icc (i + 1) (j - 1) ∧
    ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n \ (Finset.Icc j n ∪ Finset.Icc 1 i), x =
      n * (n + 1) / 2 - ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc j n ∪ Finset.Icc 1 i, x := by
  have hsub : Finset.Icc j n ∪ Finset.Icc 1 i ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_Icc] at hx ⊢
    omega
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · ext x
    simp only [Finset.mem_sdiff, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_Icc]
    omega
  · have hg : ∀ m : ℕ, (∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, x) * 2 = m * (m + 1) := by
      intro m
      induction m with
      | zero => simp
      | succ m ih => rw [Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top (by omega), add_mul, ih]; ring
    have htot : ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, x = n * (n + 1) / 2 :=
      (Nat.div_eq_of_eq_mul_left (by norm_num) (hg n).symm).symm
    rw [← htot, ← Finset.sum_sdiff hsub]
    omega
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.08889 (Consecutive Cycle Sums), Lemma 1. Wrap sets and standard intervals are written out as Finset.Icc unions; the empty interval for j = i+1 is Icc (i+1) i.

explanation.summary: The proof establishes that the wrap set W = {j,…,n} ∪ {1,…,i} is a subset of {1,…,n}, then splits the theorem into the set identity and the sum formula. The set identity is proved by extensionality, showing that an element in {1,…,n} outside W must lie between i+1 and j-1 via linear arithmetic. Finally, the sum of {1,…,n} is shown by induction to be n(n+1)/2, from which the complement sum is obtained by subtracting the sum over W.

steps.claim: The wrap set W = {j,…,n} ∪ {1,…,i} is a subset of {1,…,n}.
steps.explanation: Take an element x in the union. By definition of Finset union and closed intervals (Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_Icc), x satisfies j ≤ x ≤ n or 1 ≤ x ≤ i. Since 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, in either case 1 ≤ x ≤ n, which linear integer arithmetic (omega) verifies.
steps.code:
have hsub : Finset.Icc j n ∪ Finset.Icc 1 i ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n := by
    intro x hx
    simp only [Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_Icc] at hx ⊢
    omega

steps.claim: The complement {1,…,n} \ ({j,…,n} ∪ {1,…,i}) equals the interval {i+1,…,j-1}.
steps.explanation: Split the goal into the set identity and the sum identity (refine). By extensionality (ext x), unfold the definitions of difference, union, and interval membership (Finset.mem_sdiff, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_Icc). An element x belongs to the set difference if and only if (1 ≤ x ≤ n) and ¬(j ≤ x ≤ n ∨ 1 ≤ x ≤ i), which linear arithmetic (omega) simplifies to i + 1 ≤ x ≤ j - 1 given 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n.
steps.code:
refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · ext x
    simp only [Finset.mem_sdiff, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_Icc]
    omega

steps.claim: For every natural number m, twice the sum of {1,…,m} equals m(m+1).
steps.explanation: By induction on m. The base case m = 0 is trivial since the interval is empty (simp). For the successor m + 1, split off the top term m + 1 using Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top, distribute multiplication by 2 over addition using add_mul, apply the induction hypothesis, and conclude by algebraic ring simplification (ring).
steps.code:
· have hg : ∀ m : ℕ, (∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 m, x) * 2 = m * (m + 1) := by
      intro m
      induction m with
      | zero => simp
      | succ m ih => rw [Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top (by omega), add_mul, ih]; ring

steps.claim: The sum of the integers from 1 to n is n(n+1)/2.
steps.explanation: Applying Nat.div_eq_of_eq_mul_left with 0 < 2 converts the identity 2 * ∑_{x=1}^n x = n(n+1) into the closed-form division ∑_{x=1}^n x = n(n+1)/2.
steps.code:
have htot : ∑ x ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, x = n * (n + 1) / 2 :=
      (Nat.div_eq_of_eq_mul_left (by norm_num) (hg n).symm).symm

steps.claim: The sum over the complement is n(n+1)/2 − ∑_{x ∈ W} x.
steps.explanation: Using the inclusion W ⊆ {1,…,n}, partition the sum over {1,…,n} into the sum over {1,…,n} \ W plus the sum over W (Finset.sum_sdiff). Rewriting with the total sum n(n+1)/2 reduces the equation to the natural number identity (A + B) − B = A, which omega finishes.
steps.code:
rw [← htot, ← Finset.sum_sdiff hsub]
    omega

glossary.Finset.mem_union: An element belongs to the union of two finite sets if and only if it belongs to either set: x ∈ s ∪ t ↔ x ∈ s ∨ x ∈ t.
glossary.Finset.mem_Icc: An element x belongs to the closed interval [a, b] if and only if a ≤ x ≤ b.
glossary.Finset.mem_sdiff: An element belongs to the set difference s \ t if and only if it belongs to s and not to t.
glossary.Finset.sum_Icc_succ_top: A sum over an interval [a, b+1] can be split into the sum over [a, b] plus the top term at b+1, provided a ≤ b+1.
glossary.add_mul: Right distributivity of multiplication over addition: (a + b) * c = a * c + b * c.
glossary.Nat.div_eq_of_eq_mul_left: If 0 < n and m = k * n, then m / n = k for natural numbers.
glossary.Finset.sum_sdiff: If s₁ ⊆ s₂, the sum of a function over s₂ \ s₁ plus its sum over s₁ equals the sum over s₂.

caveats: Because division in the natural numbers is truncated division, the closed-form sum of the first n integers is established by first proving by induction that twice the sum equals n(n+1) before dividing by 2.

declarations.name: simple_graph_sum_choose_degree_two_le_choose_card_edgeFinset
declarations.informal: In any finite simple graph, the number of pairs of edges sharing a vertex, ∑_v C(d(v),2), is at most C(|E|,2): two distinct edges share at most one vertex.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_sum_choose_degree_two_le_choose_card_edgeFinset {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card.choose 2
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_sum_choose_degree_two_le_choose_card_edgeFinset {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] :
    ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card.choose 2 := by
  classical
  have hdeg : ∀ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 = ((G.incidenceFinset v).powersetCard 2).card := by
    intro v
    rw [Finset.card_powersetCard, SimpleGraph.card_incidenceFinset_eq_degree]
  simp_rw [hdeg]
  rw [← Finset.card_sigma, ← Finset.card_powersetCard]
  apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun p => p.2)
  · intro p hp
    simp only [Finset.coe_sigma, Set.mem_sigma_iff, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
      Finset.mem_powersetCard] at hp ⊢
    exact ⟨hp.1.trans (fun e he => by
      have := (SimpleGraph.incidenceFinset_subset G p.1) he
      exact this), hp.2⟩
  · intro p hp q hq hpq
    simp only [Finset.coe_sigma, Set.mem_sigma_iff, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
      Finset.mem_powersetCard] at hp hq
    simp only at hpq
    obtain ⟨v, s⟩ := p
    obtain ⟨w, t⟩ := q
    simp only at hpq hp hq
    subst hpq
    by_cases hvw : v = w
    · subst hvw; rfl
    · exfalso
      obtain ⟨e₁, e₂, hne, rfl⟩ := Finset.card_eq_two.1 hp.2
      have h1v := hp.1 (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _)
      have h2v := hp.1 (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem (Finset.mem_singleton_self _))
      have h1w := hq.1 (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _)
      have h2w := hq.1 (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem (Finset.mem_singleton_self _))
      rw [SimpleGraph.mem_incidenceFinset] at h1v h2v h1w h2w
      apply hne
      have key : ∀ e ∈ G.incidenceSet v, e ∈ G.incidenceSet w → e = s(v, w) := by
        intro e hev hew
        obtain ⟨he, hve⟩ := hev
        obtain ⟨_, hwe⟩ := hew
        exact (Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff hvw).1 ⟨hve, hwe⟩
      rw [key _ h1v h1w, key _ h2v h2w]
declarations.citation: Helper for arXiv:2610.12109 (Sharp linear Turán remainders for cycle and edge extremality), Lemma 2.5 (upper bound σ₂(T) ≤ C(k−1,2)); holds for every simple graph.

explanation.summary: The inequality is proved by constructing an injection from pairs of incident edges to pairs of edges of the graph. The sum ∑_v C(d(v), 2) is expressed as the cardinality of the set of pairs (v, s), where v is a vertex and s is a 2-element set of edges incident to v. The projection map (v, s) ↦ s sends each incident pair to a 2-element subset of the graph's edge set, which has cardinality C(|E|, 2). This map is injective because in a simple graph, two distinct vertices can share at most one common incident edge, so no two distinct edges can be incident to two different vertices.

steps.claim: The inequality reduces to showing that the projection map (v, s) ↦ s from the disjoint union ∑_{v} C(E(v), 2) into C(E, 2) is well-defined and injective.
steps.explanation: For each vertex v, C(d(v), 2) is rewritten as the cardinality of the 2-element subsets of the incidence set E(v) using Finset.card_powersetCard and SimpleGraph.card_incidenceFinset_eq_degree. Summing these over all vertices gives the cardinality of the disjoint union (sigma Finset) via Finset.card_sigma. Likewise, C(|E|, 2) is rewritten as the cardinality of the 2-element subsets of the edge set E. Applying Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn reduces the inequality to showing that the projection (v, s) ↦ s maps into 2-element edge sets and is injective.
steps.code:
classical
  have hdeg : ∀ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 = ((G.incidenceFinset v).powersetCard 2).card := by
    intro v
    rw [Finset.card_powersetCard, SimpleGraph.card_incidenceFinset_eq_degree]
  simp_rw [hdeg]
  rw [← Finset.card_sigma, ← Finset.card_powersetCard]
  apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun p => p.2)

steps.claim: The projection map sends each pair (v, s) to a 2-element subset of edges of G.
steps.explanation: Given a pair (v, s) where s ⊆ E(v) has cardinality 2, each edge in s is incident to v and thus belongs to the graph's edge set E by SimpleGraph.incidenceFinset_subset. Therefore s ⊆ E with |s| = 2, meaning s is a valid 2-element subset of edges.
steps.code:
· intro p hp
    simp only [Finset.coe_sigma, Set.mem_sigma_iff, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
      Finset.mem_powersetCard] at hp ⊢
    exact ⟨hp.1.trans (fun e he => by
      have := (SimpleGraph.incidenceFinset_subset G p.1) he
      exact this), hp.2⟩

steps.claim: For pairs p = (v, s) and q = (w, t) with s = t, the case v = w immediately yields p = q, reducing injectivity to ruling out v ≠ w.
steps.explanation: Suppose p = (v, s) and q = (w, t) have the same projection, so s = t. If v = w, then p = q holds trivially because both components coincide. Thus, establishing injectivity requires only showing that the distinct-vertex case v ≠ w is impossible.
steps.code:
· intro p hp q hq hpq
    simp only [Finset.coe_sigma, Set.mem_sigma_iff, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
      Finset.mem_powersetCard] at hp hq
    simp only at hpq
    obtain ⟨v, s⟩ := p
    obtain ⟨w, t⟩ := q
    simp only at hpq hp hq
    subst hpq
    by_cases hvw : v = w
    · subst hvw; rfl

steps.claim: The case v ≠ w is impossible because two distinct edges cannot both be incident to both v and w.
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that v ≠ w. Since |s| = 2, by Finset.card_eq_two.1 we write s = {e₁, e₂} with e₁ ≠ e₂. Since s ⊆ E(v) and s ⊆ E(w), both e₁ and e₂ are incident to both v and w (using Finset.mem_insert_self, Finset.mem_insert_of_mem, Finset.mem_singleton_self, and SimpleGraph.mem_incidenceFinset). But by Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff, any edge containing two distinct vertices v and w must be the edge s(v, w). Therefore e₁ = s(v, w) = e₂, contradicting e₁ ≠ e₂.
steps.code:
· exfalso
      obtain ⟨e₁, e₂, hne, rfl⟩ := Finset.card_eq_two.1 hp.2
      have h1v := hp.1 (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _)
      have h2v := hp.1 (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem (Finset.mem_singleton_self _))
      have h1w := hq.1 (Finset.mem_insert_self _ _)
      have h2w := hq.1 (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem (Finset.mem_singleton_self _))
      rw [SimpleGraph.mem_incidenceFinset] at h1v h2v h1w h2w
      apply hne
      have key : ∀ e ∈ G.incidenceSet v, e ∈ G.incidenceSet w → e = s(v, w) := by
        intro e hev hew
        obtain ⟨he, hve⟩ := hev
        obtain ⟨_, hwe⟩ := hew
        exact (Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff hvw).1 ⟨hve, hwe⟩
      rw [key _ h1v h1w, key _ h2v h2w]

glossary.Finset.card_powersetCard: The number of k-element subsets of a finite set s is C(|s|, k).
glossary.SimpleGraph.card_incidenceFinset_eq_degr: The number of edges incident to a vertex v equals the degree of v.
glossary.Finset.card_sigma: The cardinality of a disjoint union of finite sets (a sigma Finset) is the sum of their cardinalities.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn: If a map between finite sets is injective on the source set, then the cardinality of the source is at most that of the target.
glossary.SimpleGraph.incidenceFinset_subset: The set of edges incident to a vertex v is a subset of the graph's total edge set.
glossary.Finset.card_eq_two.1: If a finite set has cardinality 2, it is of the form {x, y} for two distinct elements x ≠ y.
glossary.Finset.mem_insert_self: An element a belongs to the set obtained by inserting a into s.
glossary.Finset.mem_insert_of_mem: If an element belongs to s, it also belongs to insert b s.
glossary.Finset.mem_singleton_self: An element belongs to the singleton set containing it.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_incidenceFinset: An edge belongs to the finite incidence set of a vertex v if and only if it belongs to the incidence set of v.
glossary.Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff: For distinct vertices x ≠ y, an unordered pair contains both x and y if and only if it equals the pair s(x, y).

caveats: In Lean's SimpleGraph library, edges are represented as unordered pairs of vertices of type Sym2 V, denoted s(v, w). The geometric fact that two distinct vertices determine at most one edge is captured via Sym2.mem_and_mem_iff.
The sum ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) is represented formally as the cardinality of a sigma Finset, which packs each vertex v together with a 2-element subset of its incident edges.

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_tree_card_sub_two_le_sum_choose_degree_le_choose
declarations.informal: For a tree T on k ≥ 2 vertices, σ₂(T) = ∑_v C(d_T(v),2) satisfies k − 2 ≤ σ₂(T) ≤ C(k−1,2).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_tree_card_sub_two_le_sum_choose_degree_le_choose {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hT : G.IsTree)
    (hk : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    Fintype.card V - 2 ≤ ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 ∧
      ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 ≤ (Fintype.card V - 1).choose 2
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_tree_card_sub_two_le_sum_choose_degree_le_choose {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hT : G.IsTree)
    (hk : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    Fintype.card V - 2 ≤ ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 ∧
      ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 ≤ (Fintype.card V - 1).choose 2 := by
  have hE : G.edgeFinset.card + 1 = Fintype.card V := hT.card_edgeFinset
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · have hsum := G.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges
    have hz : ((Fintype.card V : ℤ) - 2) ≤ ∑ v, ((G.degree v).choose 2 : ℤ) := by
      have h1 : ∀ v, ((G.degree v : ℤ) - 1) ≤ ((G.degree v).choose 2 : ℤ) := by
        intro v
        generalize G.degree v = d
        rcases d with _ | m
        · simp
        · rw [Nat.choose_succ_succ, Nat.choose_one_right]
          push_cast
          omega
      calc ((Fintype.card V : ℤ) - 2) = ∑ v, ((G.degree v : ℤ) - 1) := by
            rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
            simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one]
            have : (∑ v, (G.degree v : ℤ)) = 2 * G.edgeFinset.card := by exact_mod_cast hsum
            rw [this]
            have : (G.edgeFinset.card : ℤ) + 1 = Fintype.card V := by exact_mod_cast hE
            linarith
        _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_le_sum fun v _ => h1 v
    have : ((Fintype.card V - 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ ((∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
      push_cast
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hk]
      push_cast
      exact hz
    exact_mod_cast this
  · have h := simple_graph_sum_choose_degree_two_le_choose_card_edgeFinset G
    rwa [show G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V - 1 by omega] at h
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.12109 (Sharp linear Turán remainders for cycle and edge extremality), Lemma 2.5, the two inequalities (the equality cases are stated as separate nodes).

explanation.summary: The proof establishes the lower and upper bounds separately using the tree relation |E| = |V| - 1. For the lower bound, the local inequality d(v) - 1 ≤ C(d(v), 2) is verified for every vertex degree by Pascal's identity; summing it over all vertices and applying Euler's handshaking lemma ∑ v, d(v) = 2|E| = 2(|V| - 1) gives ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) ≥ 2(|V| - 1) - |V| = |V| - 2. For the upper bound, a general graph inequality bounds ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) ≤ C(|E|, 2), which immediately evaluates to C(|V| - 1, 2) upon substituting |E| = |V| - 1.

steps.claim: The tree has |E| = |V| - 1 edges, and the theorem splits into proving the lower bound and the upper bound separately.
steps.explanation: Because G is a tree, its edge count satisfies |E| + 1 = |V| (hT.card_edgeFinset). We split the conjunction into the lower bound |V| - 2 ≤ ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) and the upper bound ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) ≤ C(|V| - 1, 2).
steps.code:
have hE : G.edgeFinset.card + 1 = Fintype.card V := hT.card_edgeFinset
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: For every vertex v, the inequality d(v) - 1 ≤ C(d(v), 2) holds in ℤ, and the degree sum is 2|E|.
steps.explanation: We record the handshaking lemma (G.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges). For the vertex inequality, setting d = d(v), we split into cases: if d = 0, then 0 - 1 ≤ C(0, 2) = 0 holds; if d = m + 1, Pascal's identity (Nat.choose_succ_succ) and C(m, 1) = m (Nat.choose_one_right) give C(m + 1, 2) = m + C(m, 2), so (m + 1) - 1 = m ≤ m + C(m, 2) because C(m, 2) ≥ 0.
steps.code:
· have hsum := G.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges
    have hz : ((Fintype.card V : ℤ) - 2) ≤ ∑ v, ((G.degree v).choose 2 : ℤ) := by
      have h1 : ∀ v, ((G.degree v : ℤ) - 1) ≤ ((G.degree v).choose 2 : ℤ) := by
        intro v
        generalize G.degree v = d
        rcases d with _ | m
        · simp
        · rw [Nat.choose_succ_succ, Nat.choose_one_right]
          push_cast
          omega

steps.claim: In ℤ, the lower bound |V| - 2 ≤ ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) holds.
steps.explanation: Distributing the subtraction across the sum (Finset.sum_sub_distrib), the sum ∑ v, (d(v) - 1) equals ∑ v, d(v) - |V| by evaluating the constant sum of 1s (Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one). Substituting ∑ v, d(v) = 2|E| and |E| + 1 = |V|, linear arithmetic shows that 2|E| - |V| = 2(|V| - 1) - |V| = |V| - 2. Summing the pointwise inequality d(v) - 1 ≤ C(d(v), 2) over all vertices via Finset.sum_le_sum completes the lower bound in ℤ.
steps.code:
calc ((Fintype.card V : ℤ) - 2) = ∑ v, ((G.degree v : ℤ) - 1) := by
            rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
            simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one]
            have : (∑ v, (G.degree v : ℤ)) = 2 * G.edgeFinset.card := by exact_mod_cast hsum
            rw [this]
            have : (G.edgeFinset.card : ℤ) + 1 = Fintype.card V := by exact_mod_cast hE
            linarith
        _ ≤ _ := Finset.sum_le_sum fun v _ => h1 v

steps.claim: The lower bound |V| - 2 ≤ ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) holds in ℕ.
steps.explanation: Since 2 ≤ |V|, casting the natural subtraction |V| - 2 into ℤ matches the integer subtraction (Nat.cast_sub). The integer inequality established previously then carries over to ℕ.
steps.code:
have : ((Fintype.card V - 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ ((∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
      push_cast
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hk]
      push_cast
      exact hz
    exact_mod_cast this

steps.claim: The upper bound ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) ≤ C(|V| - 1, 2) holds.
steps.explanation: By simple_graph_sum_choose_degree_two_le_choose_card_edgeFinset, every simple graph satisfies ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) ≤ C(|E|, 2). Since |E| + 1 = |V|, we have |E| = |V| - 1, which rewrites the upper bound to C(|V| - 1, 2).
steps.code:
· have h := simple_graph_sum_choose_degree_two_le_choose_card_edgeFinset G
    rwa [show G.edgeFinset.card = Fintype.card V - 1 by omega] at h

glossary.hT.card_edgeFinset: In a finite tree, the number of edges plus one equals the number of vertices (|E| + 1 = |V|).
glossary.G.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges: Euler's handshaking lemma: the sum of vertex degrees in a finite graph equals twice the number of edges (∑ v, d(v) = 2|E|).
glossary.Nat.choose_succ_succ: Pascal's recurrence for binomial coefficients: C(n + 1, k + 1) = C(n, k) + C(n, k + 1).
glossary.Nat.choose_one_right: For any natural number n, C(n, 1) = n.
glossary.Finset.sum_sub_distrib: Subtraction distributes over finite sums: ∑ x ∈ s, (f(x) - g(x)) = ∑ x ∈ s, f(x) - ∑ x ∈ s, g(x).
glossary.Finset.sum_const: The sum of a constant b over a finite set s equals |s| • b.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset of a finite type is the cardinality of the type.
glossary.nsmul_eq_mul: Scalar multiplication by a natural number n on a semiring equals multiplication by the cast of n.
glossary.mul_one: Multiplication by 1 on the right is the identity: a * 1 = a.
glossary.Finset.sum_le_sum: If f(i) ≤ g(i) for all elements i of a finite set s, then ∑ i ∈ s, f(i) ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, g(i).
glossary.Nat.cast_sub: For natural numbers m ≤ n, the integer cast of n - m is the difference of their integer casts: ↑(n - m) = ↑n - ↑m.
glossary.simple_graph_sum_choose_degree_two_le_ch: In any finite simple graph, ∑ v, C(d(v), 2) ≤ C(|E|, 2).

caveats: The lower bound is evaluated in the integers (ℤ) to avoid natural number subtraction underflow, then converted back to ℕ using the assumption 2 ≤ Fintype.card V.

declarations.name: word_occurrence_coverage
declarations.informal: The coverage Cov_w(x) of a word x in a finite word w: the union of the intervals [p, p+|x|−1] over all (1-based) occurrence starts p of x in w, i.e. all p with w[p..p+|x|−1] = x.
declarations.statement: def word_occurrence_coverage {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w x : List α) : Finset ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- Coverage of `x` in `w`: the union of the (1-based) intervals `[p, p+|x|-1]` over all starts `p` of occurrences of `x` in `w`. -/
def word_occurrence_coverage {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w x : List α) : Finset ℕ :=
  ((Finset.Icc 1 w.length).filter (fun p => (w.drop (p - 1)).take x.length = x)).biUnion
    (fun p => Finset.Icc p (p + x.length - 1))
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Sec. 3.1, equation (1). Positions are 1-based as in the paper.

declarations.name: word_occurrence_coverage_subset
declarations.informal: Every coverage Cov_w(x) is a set of positions of w, i.e. contained in [1, |w|].
declarations.statement:
theorem word_occurrence_coverage_subset {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w x : List α) :
    word_occurrence_coverage w x ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 w.length
declarations.source:
theorem word_occurrence_coverage_subset {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w x : List α) :
    word_occurrence_coverage w x ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 w.length := by
  intro q hq
  simp only [word_occurrence_coverage, Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_filter,
    Finset.mem_Icc] at hq ⊢
  obtain ⟨p, ⟨⟨hp1, hpw⟩, hocc⟩, hpq, hqx⟩ := hq
  have hlen := congrArg List.length hocc
  rw [List.length_take, List.length_drop] at hlen
  omega
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for word_occurrence_coverage (arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Sec. 3.1).

explanation.summary: To show that every position in the coverage of x in w lies in [1, |w|], we consider an arbitrary position q in the coverage and obtain an occurrence start position p ∈ [1, |w|] such that q ∈ [p, p + |x| - 1]. Taking lengths of both sides of the occurrence match equation shows that |x| ≤ |w| - (p - 1), meaning the occurrence cannot extend beyond the end of w. Linear arithmetic then immediately establishes 1 ≤ q ≤ |w|.

steps.claim: Every element q of the coverage belongs to an interval [p, p + |x| - 1] for some occurrence start position p ∈ [1, |w|], and it suffices to show 1 ≤ q ≤ |w|.
steps.explanation: Let q be an arbitrary position in the coverage of x in w. By expanding the definition of coverage as the union of intervals [p, p + |x| - 1] over all p ∈ [1, |w|] satisfying take(|x|, drop(p - 1, w)) = x, we obtain a witness position p such that 1 ≤ p ≤ |w|, the occurrence equation holds, and p ≤ q ≤ p + |x| - 1. The goal reduces to showing 1 ≤ q ≤ |w|.
steps.code:
intro q hq
  simp only [word_occurrence_coverage, Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_filter,
    Finset.mem_Icc] at hq ⊢
  obtain ⟨p, ⟨⟨hp1, hpw⟩, hocc⟩, hpq, hqx⟩ := hq

steps.explanation: Taking the length of both sides of the occurrence equation take(|x|, drop(p - 1, w)) = x yields |take(|x|, drop(p - 1, w))| = |x|. Rewriting the left-hand side with the formulas for the length of a prefix (List.length_take) and the length of a suffix (List.length_drop) produces min(|x|, |w| - (p - 1)) = |x|.
steps.code:
have hlen := congrArg List.length hocc
  rw [List.length_take, List.length_drop] at hlen

steps.explanation: From min(|x|, |w| - (p - 1)) = |x|, we have |x| ≤ |w| - (p - 1), which implies p + |x| - 1 ≤ |w|. Combined with p ≤ q ≤ p + |x| - 1 and 1 ≤ p, this yields 1 ≤ q ≤ |w|. Linear integer arithmetic (omega) closes the goal.
steps.code: omega

glossary.word_occurrence_coverage: The definition of word occurrence coverage: the union of intervals [p, p + |x| - 1] over all positions p ∈ [1, |w|] at which x occurs in w.
glossary.Finset.mem_biUnion: An element b belongs to a union of finsets ⋃_{a ∈ s} t(a) if and only if there is some a ∈ s such that b ∈ t(a).
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element a belongs to {x ∈ s | p(x)} if and only if a ∈ s and p(a) holds.
glossary.Finset.mem_Icc: An element x belongs to the closed discrete interval [a, b] if and only if a ≤ x and x ≤ b.
glossary.congrArg: Equality is preserved under function application: if a₁ = a₂, then f(a₁) = f(a₂).
glossary.List.length_take: The length of the prefix obtained by taking the first i elements of a list l is min(i, |l|).
glossary.List.length_drop: The length of the suffix obtained by dropping the first i elements of a list l is |l| - i.

caveats: Positions in the coverage are 1-based (ranging from 1 to |w|), while Lean's list operations `List.drop` and `List.take` use 0-based indexing, which accounts for the `p - 1` offsets.

declarations.name: word_occurrence_coverage_ababa_aba
declarations.informal: The paper's example: in w = ababa the factor aba occurs at positions 1 and 3, so Cov_w(aba) = [1,3] ∪ [3,5] = [1,5] (letters a, b encoded as 0, 1).
declarations.statement:
theorem word_occurrence_coverage_ababa_aba :
    word_occurrence_coverage [0, 1, 0, 1, 0] [0, 1, 0] = Finset.Icc 1 5
declarations.source:
theorem word_occurrence_coverage_ababa_aba :
    word_occurrence_coverage [0, 1, 0, 1, 0] [0, 1, 0] = Finset.Icc 1 5 := by
  decide
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for word_occurrence_coverage: the example after Definition 3.1 of arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words).

explanation.summary: The theorem verifies the paper's running example: in the word $w = ababa$ (encoded as $[0, 1, 0, 1, 0]$), the factor $aba$ (encoded as $[0, 1, 0]$) occurs at positions 1 and 3, yielding coverage $[1, 3] \cup [3, 5] = [1, 5]$. Since all inputs are concrete finite lists and all operations on finite sets are decidable, the equality is proved by direct computation.

steps.claim: The coverage of the pattern `[0, 1, 0]` in the word `[0, 1, 0, 1, 0]` equals the integer interval `[1, 5]`.
steps.explanation: Because both words are explicit finite lists, their occurrence positions (indices 1 and 3) and the resulting union of intervals $[1, 3] \cup [3, 5] = [1, 5]$ are completely computable. The `decide` tactic evaluates the finite set operations and confirms the equality algorithmically.
steps.code: decide

caveats: The proof relies entirely on computational reflection (`decide`), evaluating finite set operations directly on concrete lists.

declarations.name: word_occurrence_coverage_nonempty
declarations.informal: The coverage of a nonempty factor of w is nonempty.
declarations.statement:
theorem word_occurrence_coverage_nonempty {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {w x : List α}
    (hx : x ≠ []) (hxw : x <:+: w) : (word_occurrence_coverage w x).Nonempty
declarations.source:
theorem word_occurrence_coverage_nonempty {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {w x : List α}
    (hx : x ≠ []) (hxw : x <:+: w) : (word_occurrence_coverage w x).Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨s, t, rfl⟩ := hxw
  refine ⟨s.length + 1, ?_⟩
  have hlen : 0 < x.length := List.length_pos_iff.2 hx
  simp only [word_occurrence_coverage, Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc,
    List.length_append]
  refine ⟨s.length + 1, ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, ?_⟩, le_rfl, by omega⟩
  simp
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for word_occurrence_coverage (arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Sec. 3.1).

explanation.summary: To show that the coverage of a nonempty factor $x$ in $w$ is nonempty, we decompose $w$ as $s ++ x ++ t$ using the factor assumption. We then exhibit the 1-based starting position $|s| + 1$ as an element of the coverage set. Since $|x| > 0$, this position satisfies the index bounds for an occurrence of $x$, and the factor starting at $|s| + 1$ is identically $x$.

steps.claim: Decomposing $w = s ++ x ++ t$, it suffices to show that the starting index $|s| + 1$ belongs to the coverage of $x$, where $|x| > 0$.
steps.explanation: Since $x$ is an infix (factor) of $w$ ($x <:+: w$), we can write $w = s ++ x ++ t$ for some prefix $s$ and suffix $t$. To show that the coverage of $x$ is nonempty, it suffices to exhibit an element in it; we choose the 1-based position $|s| + 1$ where this occurrence of $x$ begins. Furthermore, since $x$ is nonempty ($x \neq []$), its length is strictly positive by `List.length_pos_iff.2`.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨s, t, rfl⟩ := hxw
  refine ⟨s.length + 1, ?_⟩
  have hlen : 0 < x.length := List.length_pos_iff.2 hx

steps.claim: Membership of $|s| + 1$ in the coverage set reduces to finding an occurrence of $x$ that covers $|s| + 1$.
steps.explanation: Unfolding `word_occurrence_coverage` and rewriting Finset membership with `Finset.mem_biUnion`, `Finset.mem_filter`, `Finset.mem_Icc`, and `List.length_append`, the goal becomes finding a valid starting position $a \in [1, |s| + |x| + |t|]$ where the factor of length $|x|$ is $x$, such that $|s| + 1 \in [a, a + |x| - 1]$.
steps.code:
simp only [word_occurrence_coverage, Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_Icc,
    List.length_append]

steps.claim: The occurrence at index $a = |s| + 1$ is valid and covers the index $|s| + 1$.
steps.explanation: We instantiate the occurrence position $a$ with $|s| + 1$. The inequalities $1 \le |s| + 1 \le |s| + |x| + |t|$ and $|s| + 1 \le (|s| + 1) + |x| - 1$ follow by linear arithmetic (`omega`) using $|x| > 0$, while $|s| + 1 \le |s| + 1$ holds by reflexivity (`le_rfl`). Finally, dropping $|s|$ elements from $s ++ x ++ t$ leaves $x ++ t$, and taking the first $|x|$ elements yields $x$, which is verified by list simplification (`simp`).
steps.code:
refine ⟨s.length + 1, ⟨⟨by omega, by omega⟩, ?_⟩, le_rfl, by omega⟩
  simp

glossary.List.length_pos_iff.2: A list has strictly positive length if it is nonempty.
glossary.word_occurrence_coverage: The set of indices covered by occurrences of a factor in a word, defined as the union of intervals $[p, p + |x| - 1]$ over all positions $p$ where $x$ occurs.
glossary.Finset.mem_biUnion: An element belongs to a indexed union of finsets if and only if it belongs to the component finset for some index in the base finset.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finset if and only if it belongs to the base finset and satisfies the predicate.
glossary.Finset.mem_Icc: An element belongs to the closed interval $[a, b]$ if and only if it is between $a$ and $b$ inclusive.
glossary.List.length_append: The length of the concatenation of two lists is the sum of their lengths.
glossary.le_rfl: The partial order relation $\le$ is reflexive: $a \le a$.

caveats: Indices in `word_occurrence_coverage` are 1-based, running from 1 to the word's length.
The arithmetic inequalities verifying that the starting index $|s| + 1$ is within the valid range are discharged by `omega`, and the list slice equality is closed by `simp`.

declarations.name: is_string_attractor
declarations.informal: A set Γ ⊆ [1, |w|] of positions is a string attractor of the finite word w if Γ ∩ Cov_w(x) ≠ ∅ for every nonempty factor x of w.
declarations.statement: def is_string_attractor {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α) (Γ : Finset ℕ) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- `Γ` is a string attractor of `w`: a set of (1-based) positions of `w` meeting the coverage of every nonempty factor of `w`. -/
def is_string_attractor {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α) (Γ : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  Γ ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 w.length ∧
    ∀ x : List α, x ≠ [] → x <:+: w → (Γ ∩ word_occurrence_coverage w x).Nonempty
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Definition 3.1. Factor = contiguous sublist (List.IsInfix).

declarations.name: is_string_attractor_Icc
declarations.informal: The set of all positions [1, |w|] is a string attractor of w.
declarations.statement:
theorem is_string_attractor_Icc {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α) :
    is_string_attractor w (Finset.Icc 1 w.length)
declarations.source:
theorem is_string_attractor_Icc {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α) :
    is_string_attractor w (Finset.Icc 1 w.length) := by
  refine ⟨subset_rfl, fun x hx hxw => ?_⟩
  rw [Finset.inter_eq_right.2 (word_occurrence_coverage_subset w x)]
  exact word_occurrence_coverage_nonempty hx hxw
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for is_string_attractor (arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Definition 3.1).

explanation.summary: By definition, a set Γ is a string attractor of a word w if Γ ⊆ [1, |w|] and Γ intersects the set of positions covered by occurrences of every nonempty factor x of w. For Γ = [1, |w|], the inclusion condition holds reflexively. Furthermore, the occurrence coverage of any factor is entirely contained within [1, |w|], so the intersection is just the coverage itself, which is nonempty whenever x is a nonempty factor of w.

steps.claim: To show that [1, |w|] is a string attractor of w, it suffices to show that for any nonempty factor x of w, the set [1, |w|] intersects the occurrence coverage of x.
steps.explanation: By definition, a set Γ is a string attractor of w if Γ ⊆ [1, |w|] and Γ intersects the occurrence coverage of every nonempty factor of w. For Γ = [1, |w|], the subset condition [1, |w|] ⊆ [1, |w|] holds reflexively by subset_rfl. We then introduce an arbitrary factor x of w (hxw) that is nonempty (hx).
steps.code: refine ⟨subset_rfl, fun x hx hxw => ?_⟩

steps.claim: The intersection [1, |w|] ∩ word_occurrence_coverage(w, x) is nonempty.
steps.explanation: Since all occurrences of any factor of w lie within the bounds [1, |w|], the coverage of x is a subset of [1, |w|] (by word_occurrence_coverage_subset). Therefore, their intersection simplifies to just the coverage of x itself via Finset.inter_eq_right.2. Because x is nonempty and occurs in w, its occurrence coverage is nonempty (by word_occurrence_coverage_nonempty), completing the proof.
steps.code:
rw [Finset.inter_eq_right.2 (word_occurrence_coverage_subset w x)]
  exact word_occurrence_coverage_nonempty hx hxw

glossary.subset_rfl: A set is a subset of itself: s ⊆ s.
glossary.Finset.inter_eq_right.2: If s ⊆ t, then t ∩ s = s.
glossary.word_occurrence_coverage_subset: The positions covered by all occurrences of a factor x in w form a subset of [1, |w|].
glossary.word_occurrence_coverage_nonempty: If x is a nonempty factor of w, the set of positions covered by its occurrences in w is nonempty.

declarations.name: not_is_string_attractor_empty
declarations.informal: The empty set is not a string attractor of a nonempty word.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_is_string_attractor_empty {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {w : List α} (hw : w ≠ []) :
    ¬ is_string_attractor w ∅
declarations.source:
theorem not_is_string_attractor_empty {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] {w : List α} (hw : w ≠ []) :
    ¬ is_string_attractor w ∅ := by
  rintro ⟨-, h⟩
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := h w hw (List.infix_refl w)
  simp at hx
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for is_string_attractor (arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Definition 3.1).

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by contradiction. If the empty set were a string attractor of a nonempty word $w$, then every nonempty factor of $w$ would have an occurrence intersecting $\emptyset$. But $w$ is a nonempty factor of itself, which would require $\emptyset$ to intersect the coverage of $w$—an impossibility since the empty set contains no elements.

steps.claim: Assume for contradiction that $\emptyset$ is a string attractor of $w$, extracting the condition that every nonempty factor of $w$ intersects $\emptyset$.
steps.explanation: By definition, a set $\Gamma$ is a string attractor of $w$ if $\Gamma \subseteq \{1, \dots, |w|\}$ and every nonempty factor of $w$ has an occurrence intersecting $\Gamma$. Assuming for contradiction that $\emptyset$ is an attractor, we discard the trivial inclusion $\emptyset \subseteq \{1, \dots, |w|\}$ and retain the hypothesis (named $h$) that every nonempty factor of $w$ has an occurrence whose coverage intersects $\emptyset$.
steps.code: rintro ⟨-, h⟩

steps.claim: Specializing the attractor condition to $w$ itself derives a contradiction.
steps.explanation: Since $w$ is nonempty by hypothesis ($hw$) and is an infix of itself (by `List.infix_refl`), the attractor hypothesis $h$ guarantees that $\emptyset \cap \text{word\_occurrence\_coverage } w\ w$ is nonempty. This yields a witness $x$ belonging to this intersection ($hx$). Simplifying this membership condition immediately produces a contradiction, since no element can belong to the empty set.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := h w hw (List.infix_refl w)
  simp at hx

glossary.List.infix_refl: Every list is an infix (contiguous sublist) of itself: $l <:+: l$.

declarations.name: word_factor_coverages
declarations.informal: H(w): the family of coverages Cov_w(x) of the nonempty factors x of w.
declarations.statement: def word_factor_coverages {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α) : Set (Finset ℕ)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Sec. 3.2.

declarations.name: word_min_factor_coverages
declarations.informal: H_min(w): the inclusion-minimal members of H(w), the family of factor coverages of w.
declarations.statement: def word_min_factor_coverages {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α) : Set (Finset ℕ)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Sec. 3.2.

declarations.name: word_min_factor_coverages_subset
declarations.informal: Every inclusion-minimal factor coverage is a factor coverage: H_min(w) ⊆ H(w).
declarations.statement:
theorem word_min_factor_coverages_subset {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α) :
    word_min_factor_coverages w ⊆ word_factor_coverages w
declarations.source:
theorem word_min_factor_coverages_subset {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α) :
    word_min_factor_coverages w ⊆ word_factor_coverages w :=
  fun _ hC => hC.1
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for word_min_factor_coverages (arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Sec. 3.2).

explanation.summary: By definition, an inclusion-minimal factor coverage of a word w is a factor coverage satisfying an additional minimality condition. To show that the set of minimal factor coverages is a subset of the set of all factor coverages, the proof takes an arbitrary element of the former and projects out the first conjunct of its defining property.

steps.claim: Every element of word_min_factor_coverages w belongs to word_factor_coverages w.
steps.explanation: To prove the subset relation, let C be an arbitrary element of word_min_factor_coverages w with membership hypothesis hC. By definition, word_min_factor_coverages w consists of those sets C that belong to word_factor_coverages w and are minimal with respect to inclusion. The hypothesis hC is therefore a conjunction whose first conjunct (hC.1) is precisely the statement that C ∈ word_factor_coverages w.
steps.code: fun _ hC => hC.1

declarations.name: exists_min_factor_coverage_subset
declarations.informal: Every factor coverage D ∈ H(w) contains some inclusion-minimal factor coverage C ∈ H_min(w).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_min_factor_coverage_subset {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α)
    {D : Finset ℕ} (hD : D ∈ word_factor_coverages w) :
    ∃ C ∈ word_min_factor_coverages w, C ⊆ D
declarations.source:
theorem exists_min_factor_coverage_subset {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α] (w : List α)
    {D : Finset ℕ} (hD : D ∈ word_factor_coverages w) :
    ∃ C ∈ word_min_factor_coverages w, C ⊆ D := by
  obtain ⟨C, ⟨hCH, hCD⟩, hmin⟩ := (measure Finset.card).wf.has_min
    {C | C ∈ word_factor_coverages w ∧ C ⊆ D} ⟨D, hD, subset_rfl⟩
  refine ⟨C, ⟨hCH, fun E hE hEC => ?_⟩, hCD⟩
  by_contra hne
  exact hmin E ⟨hE, hEC.trans hCD⟩ (Finset.card_lt_card (Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.2 ⟨hEC, hne⟩))
declarations.citation: Helper for arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Proposition 3.2 (every member of the finite family H(w) lies above a minimal one).

explanation.summary: We consider the collection of all factor coverages of w that are subsets of D. Because D itself belongs to this collection, it is non-empty, and by the well-foundedness of finite set cardinality, it contains an element C of minimal cardinality. If there were a factor coverage E strictly contained in C, it would also be a subset of D with strictly smaller cardinality, contradicting the choice of C. Hence C is inclusion-minimal and satisfies C ⊆ D.

steps.claim: There exists a factor coverage C ⊆ D of minimal cardinality among all factor coverages contained in D.
steps.explanation: The set S = {C ∈ word_factor_coverages w | C ⊆ D} is non-empty because D ∈ word_factor_coverages w and D ⊆ D (by subset_rfl). Since the cardinality of finite sets is a well-founded measure on Finset ℕ, every non-empty collection has an element C of minimal cardinality, so no element in S has strictly smaller cardinality than C.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨C, ⟨hCH, hCD⟩, hmin⟩ := (measure Finset.card).wf.has_min
    {C | C ∈ word_factor_coverages w ∧ C ⊆ D} ⟨D, hD, subset_rfl⟩

steps.claim: To show that C is an inclusion-minimal factor coverage contained in D, it suffices to show that every factor coverage E ⊆ C satisfies E = C.
steps.explanation: We provide C as the candidate minimal factor coverage. We already know C is a factor coverage and C ⊆ D. By the definition of word_min_factor_coverages, C is inclusion-minimal if every factor coverage E contained in C is equal to C.
steps.code: refine ⟨C, ⟨hCH, fun E hE hEC => ?_⟩, hCD⟩

steps.claim: Any factor coverage E ⊆ C must equal C.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that E ≠ C (hne). Because E ⊆ C and E ≠ C, E is a strict subset of C (Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.2), which implies |E| < |C| by Finset.card_lt_card. Moreover, E is a factor coverage and E ⊆ D by transitivity (hEC.trans hCD), so E belongs to the collection S. This contradicts the cardinality-minimality of C (hmin).
steps.code:
by_contra hne
  exact hmin E ⟨hE, hEC.trans hCD⟩ (Finset.card_lt_card (Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.2 ⟨hEC, hne⟩))

glossary.subset_rfl: Any set is a subset of itself: a ⊆ a.
glossary.Finset.card_lt_card: A strict subset of a finite set has strictly smaller cardinality: if s ⊂ t, then |s| < |t|.
glossary.Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.2: If s is a subset of t and s ≠ t, then s is a strict subset of t (s ⊂ t).

declarations.name: is_string_attractor_iff_forall_min_factor_coverage
declarations.informal: For every finite word w and every Γ ⊆ [1, |w|], Γ is a string attractor of w if and only if Γ ∩ C ≠ ∅ for every inclusion-minimal factor coverage C ∈ H_min(w).
declarations.statement:
theorem is_string_attractor_iff_forall_min_factor_coverage {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (w : List α) (Γ : Finset ℕ) (hΓ : Γ ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 w.length) :
    is_string_attractor w Γ ↔ ∀ C ∈ word_min_factor_coverages w, (Γ ∩ C).Nonempty
declarations.source:
theorem is_string_attractor_iff_forall_min_factor_coverage {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    (w : List α) (Γ : Finset ℕ) (hΓ : Γ ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 w.length) :
    is_string_attractor w Γ ↔ ∀ C ∈ word_min_factor_coverages w, (Γ ∩ C).Nonempty := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨-, h⟩ C ⟨⟨x, hx, hxw, rfl⟩, -⟩
    exact h x hx hxw
  · intro h
    refine ⟨hΓ, fun x hx hxw => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨C, hC, hCD⟩ := exists_min_factor_coverage_subset w ⟨x, hx, hxw, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := h C hC
    exact ⟨p, Finset.inter_subset_inter_left hCD hp⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.10950 (Smallest String Attractors and Minimal Coverage Certificates of Thue–Morse Words), Proposition 3.2 (minimal-coverage reduction).

explanation.summary: A set of positions Γ is a string attractor of w if and only if it intersects every minimal factor coverage in H_min(w). The forward direction holds because every minimal factor coverage is itself the occurrence coverage of some non-empty factor. The reverse direction holds because every factor coverage contains an inclusion-minimal factor coverage, so a set that intersects all minimal factor coverages automatically intersects every factor coverage.

steps.claim: If Γ is a string attractor of w, then Γ intersects every minimal factor coverage C ∈ H_min(w).
steps.explanation: We split the equivalence into two implications. In the forward direction, assume Γ is a string attractor. By definition, a minimal factor coverage C is in particular a factor coverage, meaning C is the occurrence coverage of some non-empty factor x of w. The definition of a string attractor directly guarantees that Γ intersects the occurrence coverage of x, which is C.
steps.code:
constructor
  · rintro ⟨-, h⟩ C ⟨⟨x, hx, hxw, rfl⟩, -⟩
    exact h x hx hxw

steps.claim: To show that Γ is a string attractor under the hypothesis that it intersects every minimal factor coverage, it suffices to show that Γ intersects the occurrence coverage of an arbitrary non-empty factor x of w.
steps.explanation: In the reverse direction, we assume that Γ intersects every minimal factor coverage C. By definition, Γ is a string attractor if Γ ⊆ [1, |w|] (which is provided by hypothesis hΓ) and Γ intersects the occurrence coverage of every non-empty factor x of w. We fix an arbitrary non-empty factor x of w.
steps.code:
· intro h
    refine ⟨hΓ, fun x hx hxw => ?_⟩

steps.claim: Γ intersects the occurrence coverage of x, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: Because x is a non-empty factor of w, its occurrence coverage is a factor coverage. By `exists_min_factor_coverage_subset`, it contains an inclusion-minimal factor coverage C. Applying our hypothesis to C yields an element p ∈ Γ ∩ C. Since C is a subset of the occurrence coverage of x, `Finset.inter_subset_inter_left` implies p is also in Γ ∩ word_occurrence_coverage w x, showing that the intersection is non-empty.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨C, hC, hCD⟩ := exists_min_factor_coverage_subset w ⟨x, hx, hxw, rfl⟩
    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := h C hC
    exact ⟨p, Finset.inter_subset_inter_left hCD hp⟩

glossary.exists_min_factor_coverage_subset: Every factor coverage of a word w contains an inclusion-minimal factor coverage as a subset.
glossary.Finset.inter_subset_inter_left: If t ⊆ u, then s ∩ t ⊆ s ∩ u for any sets s, t, u.
