declarations.name: urm_halts_toStandardForm_of_halts
declarations.informal: If a URM program p halts on inputs, then its standard form p.toStandardForm halts on inputs.
declarations.statement:
open Cslib.URM in
theorem urm_halts_toStandardForm_of_halts (p : Program) (inputs : List ℕ)
    (h : Halts p inputs) : Halts p.toStandardForm inputs
declarations.source:
open Cslib.URM in
/-- If a URM program halts on an input list, then its standard form also halts on that input list. -/
theorem urm_halts_toStandardForm_of_halts (p : Program) (inputs : List ℕ)
    (h : Halts p inputs) : Halts p.toStandardForm inputs := by
  rcases h with ⟨s_halt, hsteps, hhalt⟩
  suffices ∀ s, Steps p s s_halt → ∃ s', Steps p.toStandardForm s s' ∧ s'.isHalted p.toStandardForm from
    this (State.init inputs) hsteps
  intro s hs
  induction hs using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on with
  | refl =>
    refine ⟨s_halt, Relation.ReflTransGen.refl, ?_⟩
    rwa [State.isHalted_iff, Program.toStandardForm_length, ← State.isHalted_iff]
  | head hstep hrest ih =>
    rcases Step.toStandardForm hstep with h1 | ⟨_, s₂, hstep₂, hhalt₂, _⟩
    · rcases ih with ⟨s', hsteps', hhalt'⟩
      exact ⟨s', Relation.ReflTransGen.head h1 hsteps', hhalt'⟩
    · exact ⟨s₂, Relation.ReflTransGen.single hstep₂, hhalt₂⟩
declarations.citation: Cutland, Computability: An Introduction to Recursive Function Theory
declarations.reading: For any program `p : Cslib.URM.Program` and any list of natural numbers `inputs : List ℕ`, if `p` halts on `inputs` (`Cslib.URM.Halts p inputs`), then the standard-form version of `p` (`p.toStandardForm`) also halts on `inputs` (`Cslib.URM.Halts p.toStandardForm inputs`).

explanation.summary: To prove that p.toStandardForm halts whenever p halts, we generalize the claim to all states that can reach the halting state of p and argue by head-induction along the execution path. In the base case of zero steps, the terminal state is already halted under p.toStandardForm because standard form preserves program length. In the inductive step, Step.toStandardForm ensures that each transition of p is either directly simulated by p.toStandardForm or replaced by a single step directly into a halted state.

steps.claim: It suffices to show that any state from which p can reach the terminal state s_halt also reaches a halted state under p.toStandardForm.
steps.explanation: From the assumption that p halts on the given inputs, we obtain a terminal state s_halt reachable from State.init inputs that is halted under p. We generalize the goal to prove that every state s reaching s_halt under p can reach some halted state under p.toStandardForm; instantiating this claim with the initial state State.init inputs yields the theorem.
steps.code:
rcases h with ⟨s_halt, hsteps, hhalt⟩
  suffices ∀ s, Steps p s s_halt → ∃ s', Steps p.toStandardForm s s' ∧ s'.isHalted p.toStandardForm from
    this (State.init inputs) hsteps

steps.claim: The generalized claim reduces to verifying a zero-step base case and an induction step for prepending an execution step.
steps.explanation: We fix an arbitrary state s that reaches s_halt in some sequence of steps hs. Performing head-induction on this reflexive-transitive step relation using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on decomposes the path into the base case where s = s_halt (zero steps) and the inductive step where an initial step s → c is followed by a path c →* s_halt satisfying the induction hypothesis.
steps.code:
intro s hs
  induction hs using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on with

steps.claim: When s = s_halt, the state is already halted under p.toStandardForm in zero steps.
steps.explanation: In zero steps (via Relation.ReflTransGen.refl), the state remains s_halt. By State.isHalted_iff, a state is halted if and only if its program counter is at least the length of the program. Since Program.toStandardForm_length states that p.toStandardForm has the same length as p, s_halt being halted under p implies it is also halted under p.toStandardForm.
steps.code:
| refl =>
    refine ⟨s_halt, Relation.ReflTransGen.refl, ?_⟩
    rwa [State.isHalted_iff, Program.toStandardForm_length, ← State.isHalted_iff]

steps.claim: If s steps to c and c reaches s_halt, then s reaches a halted state under p.toStandardForm.
steps.explanation: We analyze the first step s → c using Step.toStandardForm. In the first case, p.toStandardForm can perform the exact same transition s → c; prepending this step to the execution path from c to a halted state s' provided by the induction hypothesis (using Relation.ReflTransGen.head) shows that s halts. In the second case, Step.toStandardForm provides a direct single-step transition from s to a state s₂ that is already halted under p.toStandardForm, which yields a one-step halting execution path (using Relation.ReflTransGen.single).
steps.code:
| head hstep hrest ih =>
    rcases Step.toStandardForm hstep with h1 | ⟨_, s₂, hstep₂, hhalt₂, _⟩
    · rcases ih with ⟨s', hsteps', hhalt'⟩
      exact ⟨s', Relation.ReflTransGen.head h1 hsteps', hhalt'⟩
    · exact ⟨s₂, Relation.ReflTransGen.single hstep₂, hhalt₂⟩

glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on: Induction on a path in the reflexive-transitive closure: to prove a property holds for a path from a to b, it suffices to prove it for the empty path at b, and that it is preserved when prepending a single step a → c before a path from c to b.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.refl: The reflexive-transitive closure of any relation is reflexive; every state can reach itself in zero steps.
glossary.State.isHalted_iff: A state is halted under program p if and only if its program counter is at least the length of p.
glossary.Program.toStandardForm_length: The standard form of a program has the same number of instructions as the original program.
glossary.Step.toStandardForm: A single step s → s' of program p is either also a step of p.toStandardForm, or s' is halted under p and p.toStandardForm can step from s in one step to a state that is halted under p.toStandardForm.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.head: Prepending a single transition a → b to a path from b to c in the reflexive-transitive closure yields a path from a to c.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.single: A single transition a → b yields a one-step path in the reflexive-transitive closure.

declarations.name: urm_halts_toStandardForm
declarations.informal: For any URM program p and input list inputs, p halts on inputs if and only if its standard form p.toStandardForm halts on inputs.
declarations.statement:
open Cslib.URM in
theorem urm_halts_toStandardForm (p : Program) (inputs : List ℕ) :
    Halts p.toStandardForm inputs ↔ Halts p inputs
declarations.source:
open Cslib.URM in
/-- A URM program halts on an input list if and only if its standard form halts on that input list. -/
theorem urm_halts_toStandardForm (p : Program) (inputs : List ℕ) :
    Halts p.toStandardForm inputs ↔ Halts p inputs := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, urm_halts_toStandardForm_of_halts p inputs⟩
  rcases h with ⟨s_halt, hsteps, hhalt⟩
  suffices ∀ s, Steps p.toStandardForm s s_halt → ∃ s', Steps p s s' ∧ s'.isHalted p from
    this (State.init inputs) hsteps
  intro s hs
  induction hs using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on with
  | refl =>
    refine ⟨s_halt, Relation.ReflTransGen.refl, ?_⟩
    rwa [State.isHalted_iff, ← Program.toStandardForm_length, ← State.isHalted_iff]
  | head hstep hrest ih =>
    rcases Step.from_toStandardForm hstep with h1 | ⟨_, s₂, hstep₂, hhalt₂, _⟩
    · rcases ih with ⟨s', hsteps', hhalt'⟩
      exact ⟨s', Relation.ReflTransGen.head h1 hsteps', hhalt'⟩
    · exact ⟨s₂, Relation.ReflTransGen.single hstep₂, hhalt₂⟩
declarations.citation: Cutland, Computability: An Introduction to Recursive Function Theory
declarations.reading: For every program `p` (of type `Cslib.URM.Program`) and every list of natural numbers `inputs`, `p.toStandardForm` halts on `inputs` if and only if `p` halts on `inputs`.

explanation.summary: The theorem reduces to the forward direction because the reverse direction was already established by urm_halts_toStandardForm_of_halts. The forward direction is proved by generalizing to all states that reach the final halted state in p.toStandardForm, and proceeding by head induction on the multi-step execution. In the base case, halting coincides because standard form preserves program length; in the inductive step, each transition in standard form either mimics a step in p or directly steps to a halted state.

steps.claim: The equivalence reduces to the forward direction: if p.toStandardForm halts on inputs, then p halts on inputs.
steps.explanation: The theorem is an 'if and only if'. Line 5 provides the reverse direction directly from the previously proved lemma urm_halts_toStandardForm_of_halts, leaving only the forward implication.
steps.code: refine ⟨fun h => ?_, urm_halts_toStandardForm_of_halts p inputs⟩

steps.claim: Assuming p.toStandardForm halts at state s_halt, it suffices to show that any state that can reach s_halt under p.toStandardForm also halts under p.
steps.explanation: Line 6 unpacks the assumption that p.toStandardForm halts on the inputs into an execution sequence from the initial state to a halted state s_halt. Lines 7–8 generalize the goal: if every state reaching s_halt under p.toStandardForm can reach a halted state under p, then applying this to the initial state proves that p halts.
steps.code:
rcases h with ⟨s_halt, hsteps, hhalt⟩
  suffices ∀ s, Steps p.toStandardForm s s_halt → ∃ s', Steps p s s' ∧ s'.isHalted p from
    this (State.init inputs) hsteps

steps.claim: The generalized claim is set up for proof by head induction on the execution sequence from s to s_halt in p.toStandardForm.
steps.explanation: Line 9 introduces an arbitrary state s and an execution path hs from s to s_halt under p.toStandardForm. Line 10 sets up induction on the first step of this path using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on, yielding a base case (zero steps, s = s_halt) and an inductive step (s steps to an intermediate state c).
steps.code:
intro s hs
  induction hs using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on with

steps.claim: In the base case (s = s_halt), s_halt is already halted under p.
steps.explanation: For s = s_halt, zero steps in p are needed by Relation.ReflTransGen.refl. By State.isHalted_iff, being halted means the program counter is at least the length of the program. Since Program.toStandardForm_length ensures p and p.toStandardForm have identical lengths, the fact that s_halt is halted under p.toStandardForm implies it is also halted under p.
steps.code:
| refl =>
    refine ⟨s_halt, Relation.ReflTransGen.refl, ?_⟩
    rwa [State.isHalted_iff, ← Program.toStandardForm_length, ← State.isHalted_iff]

steps.claim: In the inductive step, if s steps to c under p.toStandardForm and c halts under p, then s also halts under p.
steps.explanation: By Step.from_toStandardForm, the step s → c in p.toStandardForm falls into two cases: either it is also a valid step in p, so prepending it to the execution from c (provided by the induction hypothesis) via Relation.ReflTransGen.head reaches a halted state; or it represents a jump out of bounds in standard form, in which case p takes a single step via Relation.ReflTransGen.single to a state s₂ that is already halted under p.
steps.code:
| head hstep hrest ih =>
    rcases Step.from_toStandardForm hstep with h1 | ⟨_, s₂, hstep₂, hhalt₂, _⟩
    · rcases ih with ⟨s', hsteps', hhalt'⟩
      exact ⟨s', Relation.ReflTransGen.head h1 hsteps', hhalt'⟩
    · exact ⟨s₂, Relation.ReflTransGen.single hstep₂, hhalt₂⟩

glossary.urm_halts_toStandardForm_of_halts: If a URM program p halts on an input list, then its standard form p.toStandardForm also halts on that input list.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on: Head-induction principle for the reflexive transitive closure of a relation: to prove a property of a path from a to b, it suffices to show it for the reflexive base case at b, and that prepending a single step a → c preserves the property.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.refl: Every element is related to itself in zero steps in the reflexive transitive closure of a relation.
glossary.State.isHalted_iff: A state s is halted under program p if and only if its program counter is at least the length of p.
glossary.Program.toStandardForm_length: The standard form p.toStandardForm has the same number of instructions as p.
glossary.Step.from_toStandardForm: A step in p.toStandardForm from s to s' either is also a valid step in p, or s' is halted in p.toStandardForm and s steps in p to an already-halted state s₂ with the same registers as s'.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.head: Prepending a single transition step to a multi-step sequence in the reflexive transitive closure yields a valid multi-step sequence.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.single: A single transition step forms a path of length one in the reflexive transitive closure.

declarations.name: path_graph_three_stacking_number_eq_tree_estimate
declarations.informal: Conjecture 5.6 (OP-144) holds for the path on three vertices: stack(P₃) = estim(P₃) (both equal 7).
declarations.statement:
theorem path_graph_three_stacking_number_eq_tree_estimate
    [DecidableRel (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).Adj] :
    graph_stacking_number (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) =
      simple_graph_tree_estimate (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3)
declarations.source:
/-- Stacked triple on the three vertices of `P₃`. -/
def path_graph_three_stacked (a b c : ℕ) : Bool :=
  (0 < a && b = 0 && c = 0) || (a = 0 && 0 < b && c = 0) || (a = 0 && b = 0 && 0 < c)

/-- Bounded search for a stacking sequence on `P₃` (moves 0→1, 1→0, 1→2, 2→1). -/
def path_graph_three_stk : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Bool
  | 0, a, b, c => path_graph_three_stacked a b c
  | k + 1, a, b, c => path_graph_three_stacked a b c ||
      (2 ≤ a && path_graph_three_stk k (a - 2) (b + 1) c) ||
      (2 ≤ b && path_graph_three_stk k (a + 1) (b - 2) c) ||
      (2 ≤ b && path_graph_three_stk k a (b - 2) (c + 1)) ||
      (2 ≤ c && path_graph_three_stk k a (b + 1) (c - 2))

/-- No configuration reachable on `P₃` is stacked (fuel bounds the number of steps). -/
def path_graph_three_dead : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Bool
  | 0, a, b, c => !path_graph_three_stacked a b c && a < 2 && b < 2 && c < 2
  | k + 1, a, b, c => !path_graph_three_stacked a b c &&
      (a < 2 || path_graph_three_dead k (a - 2) (b + 1) c) &&
      (b < 2 || path_graph_three_dead k (a + 1) (b - 2) c) &&
      (b < 2 || path_graph_three_dead k a (b - 2) (c + 1)) &&
      (c < 2 || path_graph_three_dead k a (b + 1) (c - 2))

theorem path_graph_three_adj_iff (u v : Fin 3) :
    (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).Adj u v ↔
      (u = 0 ∧ v = 1) ∨ (u = 1 ∧ v = 0) ∨ (u = 1 ∧ v = 2) ∨ (u = 2 ∧ v = 1) := by
  rw [SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj]
  fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> decide

theorem path_graph_three_stacked_iff (c : Fin 3 → ℕ) :
    path_graph_three_stacked (c 0) (c 1) (c 2) = true ↔ ∃ v, 0 < c v ∧ ∀ w, w ≠ v → c w = 0 := by
  simp only [path_graph_three_stacked, Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq]
  constructor
  · rintro ((⟨⟨h0, h1⟩, h2⟩ | ⟨⟨h0, h1⟩, h2⟩) | ⟨⟨h0, h1⟩, h2⟩)
    · exact ⟨0, h0, fun w hw => by fin_cases w <;> simp_all⟩
    · exact ⟨1, h1, fun w hw => by fin_cases w <;> simp_all⟩
    · exact ⟨2, h2, fun w hw => by fin_cases w <;> simp_all⟩
  · rintro ⟨v, hv, hw⟩
    fin_cases v
    · exact Or.inl (Or.inl ⟨⟨hv, hw 1 (by decide)⟩, hw 2 (by decide)⟩)
    · exact Or.inl (Or.inr ⟨⟨hw 0 (by decide), hv⟩, hw 2 (by decide)⟩)
    · exact Or.inr ⟨⟨hw 0 (by decide), hw 1 (by decide)⟩, hv⟩

theorem path_graph_three_step_iff (c d : Fin 3 → ℕ) :
    graph_pebbling_step (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c d ↔
      (2 ≤ c 0 ∧ d = ![c 0 - 2, c 1 + 1, c 2]) ∨ (2 ≤ c 1 ∧ d = ![c 0 + 1, c 1 - 2, c 2]) ∨
      (2 ≤ c 1 ∧ d = ![c 0, c 1 - 2, c 2 + 1]) ∨ (2 ≤ c 2 ∧ d = ![c 0, c 1 + 1, c 2 - 2]) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨u, v, huv, hu, rfl⟩
    rw [path_graph_three_adj_iff] at huv
    rcases huv with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    · refine Or.inl ⟨hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hu, ?_⟩)
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hu, ?_⟩))
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hu, ?_⟩))
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
  · rintro (⟨hu, rfl⟩ | ⟨hu, rfl⟩ | ⟨hu, rfl⟩ | ⟨hu, rfl⟩)
    · refine ⟨0, 1, (path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide), hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine ⟨1, 0, (path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide), hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine ⟨1, 2, (path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide), hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine ⟨2, 1, (path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide), hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp

theorem path_graph_three_stk_sound (k : ℕ) (c : Fin 3 → ℕ)
    (h : path_graph_three_stk k (c 0) (c 1) (c 2) = true) :
    graph_config_stackable (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c := by
  induction k generalizing c with
  | zero =>
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hw⟩ := (path_graph_three_stacked_iff c).1 h
    exact ⟨c, Relation.ReflTransGen.refl, v, hv, hw⟩
  | succ k ih =>
    have back : ∀ d, graph_pebbling_step (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c d →
        path_graph_three_stk k (d 0) (d 1) (d 2) = true →
        graph_config_stackable (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c := by
      intro d hd hk
      obtain ⟨e, he, hst⟩ := ih d hk
      exact ⟨e, Relation.ReflTransGen.head hd he, hst⟩
    simp only [path_graph_three_stk, Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
    rcases h with (((h | ⟨ha, h⟩) | ⟨hb, h⟩) | ⟨hb, h⟩) | ⟨hc, h⟩
    · obtain ⟨v, hv, hw⟩ := (path_graph_three_stacked_iff c).1 h
      exact ⟨c, Relation.ReflTransGen.refl, v, hv, hw⟩
    · exact back _ ((path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).2 (Or.inl ⟨ha, rfl⟩)) (by simpa using h)
    · exact back _ ((path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).2 (Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hb, rfl⟩))) (by simpa using h)
    · exact back _ ((path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).2 (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hb, rfl⟩))))
        (by simpa using h)
    · exact back _ ((path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).2 (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hc, rfl⟩))))
        (by simpa using h)

theorem path_graph_three_dead_sound (k : ℕ) (c : Fin 3 → ℕ)
    (h : path_graph_three_dead k (c 0) (c 1) (c 2) = true) :
    ¬ graph_config_stackable (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c := by
  rintro ⟨e, he, hst⟩
  induction he using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on generalizing k with
  | refl =>
    cases k <;>
    · simp only [path_graph_three_dead, Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.not_eq_true'] at h
      have := (path_graph_three_stacked_iff _).2 hst
      simp_all
  | head hd _ ih =>
    rename_i c c'
    cases k with
    | zero =>
      simp only [path_graph_three_dead, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      rcases (path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).1 hd with ⟨h', -⟩ | ⟨h', -⟩ | ⟨h', -⟩ | ⟨h', -⟩ <;>
        omega
    | succ k =>
      simp only [path_graph_three_dead, Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.or_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨-, h0⟩, h1⟩, h2⟩, h3⟩ := h
      rcases (path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).1 hd with ⟨h', rfl⟩ | ⟨h', rfl⟩ | ⟨h', rfl⟩ | ⟨h', rfl⟩
      · exact ih k (by simpa using h0.resolve_left (by omega))
      · exact ih k (by simpa using h1.resolve_left (by omega))
      · exact ih k (by simpa using h2.resolve_left (by omega))
      · exact ih k (by simpa using h3.resolve_left (by omega))

theorem path_graph_three_stk_seven :
    ∀ a ≤ 7, ∀ b ≤ 7 - a, path_graph_three_stk 7 a b (7 - a - b) = true := by
  decide

theorem path_graph_three_dead_examples :
    path_graph_three_dead 2 1 0 1 = true ∧ path_graph_three_dead 3 1 1 1 = true ∧
      path_graph_three_dead 4 3 0 1 = true ∧ path_graph_three_dead 5 3 1 1 = true ∧
      path_graph_three_dead 6 5 0 1 = true := by
  decide

theorem path_graph_three_stacking_number : graph_stacking_number (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) = 7 := by
  have hvec : ∀ c : Fin 3 → ℕ, c = ![c 0, c 1, c 2] := fun c => by
    funext i; fin_cases i <;> rfl
  have h7 : 7 ∈ {t : ℕ | 2 ≤ t ∧ ∀ c : Fin 3 → ℕ, ∑ v, c v = t →
      graph_config_stackable (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c} := by
    refine ⟨by norm_num, fun c hc => ?_⟩
    rw [Fin.sum_univ_three] at hc
    apply path_graph_three_stk_sound 7
    have := path_graph_three_stk_seven (c 0) (by omega) (c 1) (by omega)
    rwa [show 7 - c 0 - c 1 = c 2 by omega] at this
  have hdead : ∀ t, 2 ≤ t → t < 7 → ∃ c : Fin 3 → ℕ, ∑ v, c v = t ∧
      ¬ graph_config_stackable (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c := by
    obtain ⟨d2, d3, d4, d5, d6⟩ := path_graph_three_dead_examples
    intro t ht2 ht7
    interval_cases t
    · exact ⟨![1, 0, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 2 _ d2⟩
    · exact ⟨![1, 1, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 3 _ d3⟩
    · exact ⟨![3, 0, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 4 _ d4⟩
    · exact ⟨![3, 1, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 5 _ d5⟩
    · exact ⟨![5, 0, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 6 _ d6⟩
  unfold graph_stacking_number
  apply le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le h7)
  refine le_csInf ⟨7, h7⟩ fun t ⟨ht2, hall⟩ => ?_
  by_contra hlt
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hns⟩ := hdead t ht2 (by omega)
  exact hns (hall c hc)

theorem path_graph_three_degree [DecidableRel (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).Adj] (v : Fin 3) :
    (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).degree v = if v = 1 then 2 else 1 := by
  rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
  have : (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).neighborFinset v =
      Finset.univ.filter (fun w => (v = 0 ∧ w = 1) ∨ (v = 1 ∧ w = 0) ∨ (v = 1 ∧ w = 2) ∨
        (v = 2 ∧ w = 1)) := by
    ext w
    simp only [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
      path_graph_three_adj_iff]
  rw [this]
  fin_cases v <;> decide

theorem path_graph_three_tree_estimate [DecidableRel (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).Adj] :
    simple_graph_tree_estimate (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) = 7 := by
  unfold simple_graph_tree_estimate
  simp only [path_graph_three_degree]
  have hd01 : (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).dist 0 1 = 1 :=
    SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 ((path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide))
  have hd21 : (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).dist 2 1 = 1 :=
    SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 ((path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide))
  have h : ∀ r : Fin 3,
      (∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v = r ∨ 1 < if v = 1 then 2 else 1),
        (if v = 1 then 2 else 1) * 2 ^ (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).dist r v) +
        (Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v ≠ r ∧ (if v = 1 then 2 else 1) = 1)).card =
      if r = 1 then 4 else 6 := by
    intro r
    fin_cases r <;> dsimp only <;> simp only [Fin.zero_eta, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk]
    · rw [show Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v = 0 ∨ 1 < if v = 1 then 2 else 1) = {0, 1}
        by decide]
      rw [Finset.sum_pair (by decide), SimpleGraph.dist_self, hd01]
      decide
    · rw [show Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v = 1 ∨ 1 < if v = 1 then 2 else 1) = {1}
        by decide]
      rw [Finset.sum_singleton, SimpleGraph.dist_self]
      decide
    · rw [show Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v = 2 ∨ 1 < if v = 1 then 2 else 1) = {2, 1}
        by decide]
      rw [Finset.sum_pair (by decide), SimpleGraph.dist_self, hd21]
      decide
  simp only [h]
  decide

theorem path_graph_three_stacking_number_eq_tree_estimate
    [DecidableRel (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).Adj] :
    graph_stacking_number (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) =
      simple_graph_tree_estimate (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) := by
  rw [path_graph_three_stacking_number, path_graph_three_tree_estimate]
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.09650 (The Almost Stacked Hypothesis: A Conjectural Analogue of Sjöstrand's Cover Pebbling Theorem), Conjecture 5.6 for the path P₃; consistent with stack(P_n) = 2^n − 1 (Theorem 4.4, from earlier work).

explanation.summary: Conjecture 5.6 holds for the path graph on three vertices P₃ by showing that both its stacking number stack(P₃) and its tree estimate estim(P₃) equal 7. The stacking number is verified by computational enumeration: an exhaustive search confirms that every 7-pebble configuration can be stacked in at most 7 moves, while explicit unstackable counterexamples are verified for all pebble counts from 2 to 6. Separately, the tree estimate is calculated directly from its definition by evaluating the vertex degrees and graph distances across all possible rootings.

steps.claim: The adjacency relation on P₃ consists of the edges {0, 1} and {1, 2}.
steps.explanation: We rewrite with SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj, which states that vertices are adjacent when their indices differ by 1, and exhaustively check all pairs of vertices in Fin 3 using fin_cases and decide.
steps.code:
rw [SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj]
  fin_cases u <;> fin_cases v <;> decide

steps.claim: A pebble configuration on P₃ is stacked according to path_graph_three_stacked if and only if all pebbles reside on a single vertex.
steps.explanation: We expand the definition of path_graph_three_stacked and simplify Boolean connectives to logical ones. In each direction, exactly one vertex has strictly positive pebbles while all other vertices have zero pebbles.
steps.code:
simp only [path_graph_three_stacked, Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq]
  constructor
  · rintro ((⟨⟨h0, h1⟩, h2⟩ | ⟨⟨h0, h1⟩, h2⟩) | ⟨⟨h0, h1⟩, h2⟩)
    · exact ⟨0, h0, fun w hw => by fin_cases w <;> simp_all⟩
    · exact ⟨1, h1, fun w hw => by fin_cases w <;> simp_all⟩
    · exact ⟨2, h2, fun w hw => by fin_cases w <;> simp_all⟩
  · rintro ⟨v, hv, hw⟩
    fin_cases v
    · exact Or.inl (Or.inl ⟨⟨hv, hw 1 (by decide)⟩, hw 2 (by decide)⟩)
    · exact Or.inl (Or.inr ⟨⟨hw 0 (by decide), hv⟩, hw 2 (by decide)⟩)
    · exact Or.inr ⟨⟨hw 0 (by decide), hw 1 (by decide)⟩, hv⟩

steps.claim: A single pebbling step on P₃ is valid if and only if it is one of the four moves 0→1, 1→0, 1→2, or 2→1, each consuming 2 pebbles from the source and adding 1 to the destination.
steps.explanation: A pebbling step requires two adjacent vertices with at least 2 pebbles at the source. Using path_graph_three_adj_iff, the only possible edges are {0, 1} and {1, 2}. Case analysis on the edge and direction characterizes all possible single-step transitions.
steps.code:
constructor
  · rintro ⟨u, v, huv, hu, rfl⟩
    rw [path_graph_three_adj_iff] at huv
    rcases huv with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    · refine Or.inl ⟨hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hu, ?_⟩)
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hu, ?_⟩))
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hu, ?_⟩))
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
  · rintro (⟨hu, rfl⟩ | ⟨hu, rfl⟩ | ⟨hu, rfl⟩ | ⟨hu, rfl⟩)
    · refine ⟨0, 1, (path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide), hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine ⟨1, 0, (path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide), hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine ⟨1, 2, (path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide), hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp
    · refine ⟨2, 1, (path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide), hu, ?_⟩
      funext i; fin_cases i <;> simp

steps.claim: The search procedure path_graph_three_stk is sound: returning true within fuel k implies the configuration is stackable.
steps.explanation: By induction on the fuel k: for k = 0, the configuration is already stacked; for k + 1, if it is not already stacked, the search branches over all four possible pebbling moves. If any move yields a configuration that succeeds with fuel k, the induction hypothesis provides reachability to a stacked state, which is prepended using Relation.ReflTransGen.head.
steps.code:
induction k generalizing c with
  | zero =>
    obtain ⟨v, hv, hw⟩ := (path_graph_three_stacked_iff c).1 h
    exact ⟨c, Relation.ReflTransGen.refl, v, hv, hw⟩
  | succ k ih =>
    have back : ∀ d, graph_pebbling_step (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c d →
        path_graph_three_stk k (d 0) (d 1) (d 2) = true →
        graph_config_stackable (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c := by
      intro d hd hk
      obtain ⟨e, he, hst⟩ := ih d hk
      exact ⟨e, Relation.ReflTransGen.head hd he, hst⟩
    simp only [path_graph_three_stk, Bool.or_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
    rcases h with (((h | ⟨ha, h⟩) | ⟨hb, h⟩) | ⟨hb, h⟩) | ⟨hc, h⟩
    · obtain ⟨v, hv, hw⟩ := (path_graph_three_stacked_iff c).1 h
      exact ⟨c, Relation.ReflTransGen.refl, v, hv, hw⟩
    · exact back _ ((path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).2 (Or.inl ⟨ha, rfl⟩)) (by simpa using h)
    · exact back _ ((path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).2 (Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hb, rfl⟩))) (by simpa using h)
    · exact back _ ((path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).2 (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨hb, rfl⟩))))
        (by simpa using h)
    · exact back _ ((path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).2 (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨hc, rfl⟩))))
        (by simpa using h)

steps.claim: The procedure path_graph_three_dead is sound: returning true for fuel k certifies that no stacked configuration can ever be reached.
steps.explanation: Assuming reachability to a stacked state, we induct on the step sequence via Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on. In the base case of zero steps, the configuration is stacked, contradicting path_graph_three_dead. In the inductive step, each valid move reduces the available fuel by 1 and preserves deadness, deriving a contradiction via the induction hypothesis.
steps.code:
rintro ⟨e, he, hst⟩
  induction he using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on generalizing k with
  | refl =>
    cases k <;>
    · simp only [path_graph_three_dead, Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.not_eq_true'] at h
      have := (path_graph_three_stacked_iff _).2 hst
      simp_all
  | head hd _ ih =>
    rename_i c c'
    cases k with
    | zero =>
      simp only [path_graph_three_dead, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      rcases (path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).1 hd with ⟨h', -⟩ | ⟨h', -⟩ | ⟨h', -⟩ | ⟨h', -⟩ <;>
        omega
    | succ k =>
      simp only [path_graph_three_dead, Bool.and_eq_true, Bool.or_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
      obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨-, h0⟩, h1⟩, h2⟩, h3⟩ := h
      rcases (path_graph_three_step_iff _ _).1 hd with ⟨h', rfl⟩ | ⟨h', rfl⟩ | ⟨h', rfl⟩ | ⟨h', rfl⟩
      · exact ih k (by simpa using h0.resolve_left (by omega))
      · exact ih k (by simpa using h1.resolve_left (by omega))
      · exact ih k (by simpa using h2.resolve_left (by omega))
      · exact ih k (by simpa using h3.resolve_left (by omega))

steps.claim: Every configuration of 7 pebbles on P₃ can reach a stacked configuration in at most 7 moves.
steps.explanation: The decide tactic evaluates the search procedure path_graph_three_stk with fuel 7 for all partitions of 7 pebbles among the three vertices, verifying it returns true in every case.
steps.code: decide

steps.claim: Specific configurations of sizes 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 pebbles are verified to be dead.
steps.explanation: The decide tactic verifies that path_graph_three_dead returns true on (1,0,1), (1,1,1), (3,0,1), (3,1,1), and (5,0,1) with fuels 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 respectively.
steps.code: decide

steps.claim: Every configuration of 7 pebbles on P₃ is stackable, so 7 is an upper bound in the definition of the stacking number.
steps.explanation: Any configuration c with sum equal to 7 is parameterized as (c 0, c 1, 7 - c 0 - c 1). By path_graph_three_stk_seven and path_graph_three_stk_sound, every such configuration is stackable.
steps.code:
have hvec : ∀ c : Fin 3 → ℕ, c = ![c 0, c 1, c 2] := fun c => by
    funext i; fin_cases i <;> rfl
  have h7 : 7 ∈ {t : ℕ | 2 ≤ t ∧ ∀ c : Fin 3 → ℕ, ∑ v, c v = t →
      graph_config_stackable (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c} := by
    refine ⟨by norm_num, fun c hc => ?_⟩
    rw [Fin.sum_univ_three] at hc
    apply path_graph_three_stk_sound 7
    have := path_graph_three_stk_seven (c 0) (by omega) (c 1) (by omega)
    rwa [show 7 - c 0 - c 1 = c 2 by omega] at this

steps.claim: For each pebble count t from 2 to 6, there exists a configuration that cannot be stacked.
steps.explanation: Using interval_cases on t ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, we exhibit the explicit witness verified in path_graph_three_dead_examples and apply path_graph_three_dead_sound to prove it is unstackable.
steps.code:
have hdead : ∀ t, 2 ≤ t → t < 7 → ∃ c : Fin 3 → ℕ, ∑ v, c v = t ∧
      ¬ graph_config_stackable (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3) c := by
    obtain ⟨d2, d3, d4, d5, d6⟩ := path_graph_three_dead_examples
    intro t ht2 ht7
    interval_cases t
    · exact ⟨![1, 0, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 2 _ d2⟩
    · exact ⟨![1, 1, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 3 _ d3⟩
    · exact ⟨![3, 0, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 4 _ d4⟩
    · exact ⟨![3, 1, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 5 _ d5⟩
    · exact ⟨![5, 0, 1], by decide, path_graph_three_dead_sound 6 _ d6⟩

steps.claim: The stacking number of P₃ is 7.
steps.explanation: The stacking number is defined as the infimum of all t ≥ 2 such that every t-pebble configuration is stackable. Since 7 satisfies this property and no smaller t ≥ 2 does, the infimum is 7 by le_antisymm, Nat.sInf_le, and le_csInf.
steps.code:
unfold graph_stacking_number
  apply le_antisymm (Nat.sInf_le h7)
  refine le_csInf ⟨7, h7⟩ fun t ⟨ht2, hall⟩ => ?_
  by_contra hlt
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hns⟩ := hdead t ht2 (by omega)
  exact hns (hall c hc)

steps.claim: The vertex degrees of P₃ are deg(1) = 2 and deg(0) = deg(2) = 1.
steps.explanation: We express degree as the cardinality of the neighbor finset using SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, filter by adjacency via path_graph_three_adj_iff, and compute the cardinality by case analysis on v.
steps.code:
rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
  have : (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).neighborFinset v =
      Finset.univ.filter (fun w => (v = 0 ∧ w = 1) ∨ (v = 1 ∧ w = 0) ∨ (v = 1 ∧ w = 2) ∨
        (v = 2 ∧ w = 1)) := by
    ext w
    simp only [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and,
      path_graph_three_adj_iff]
  rw [this]
  fin_cases v <;> decide

steps.claim: The tree estimate of P₃ equals 7.
steps.explanation: We unfold simple_graph_tree_estimate and plug in the degrees. Evaluating the formula for root r = 1 gives 4, and for roots r = 0 and r = 2 gives 6. Taking the supremum over roots yields 1 + max(6, 4, 6) = 7, and max(2, 7) = 7.
steps.code:
unfold simple_graph_tree_estimate
  simp only [path_graph_three_degree]
  have hd01 : (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).dist 0 1 = 1 :=
    SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 ((path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide))
  have hd21 : (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).dist 2 1 = 1 :=
    SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj.2 ((path_graph_three_adj_iff _ _).2 (by decide))
  have h : ∀ r : Fin 3,
      (∑ v ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v = r ∨ 1 < if v = 1 then 2 else 1),
        (if v = 1 then 2 else 1) * 2 ^ (SimpleGraph.pathGraph 3).dist r v) +
        (Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v ≠ r ∧ (if v = 1 then 2 else 1) = 1)).card =
      if r = 1 then 4 else 6 := by
    intro r
    fin_cases r <;> dsimp only <;> simp only [Fin.zero_eta, Fin.mk_one, Fin.reduceFinMk]
    · rw [show Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v = 0 ∨ 1 < if v = 1 then 2 else 1) = {0, 1}
        by decide]
      rw [Finset.sum_pair (by decide), SimpleGraph.dist_self, hd01]
      decide
    · rw [show Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v = 1 ∨ 1 < if v = 1 then 2 else 1) = {1}
        by decide]
      rw [Finset.sum_singleton, SimpleGraph.dist_self]
      decide
    · rw [show Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin 3 => v = 2 ∨ 1 < if v = 1 then 2 else 1) = {2, 1}
        by decide]
      rw [Finset.sum_pair (by decide), SimpleGraph.dist_self, hd21]
      decide
  simp only [h]
  decide

steps.claim: The stacking number of P₃ equals its tree estimate.
steps.explanation: Both quantities were shown to equal 7; rewriting by path_graph_three_stacking_number and path_graph_three_tree_estimate completes the proof.
steps.code: rw [path_graph_three_stacking_number, path_graph_three_tree_estimate]

glossary.SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj: Two vertices in a path graph P_n are adjacent if and only if their indices differ by 1.
glossary.path_graph_three_stacked: A Boolean function indicating whether pebbles are concentrated entirely on one of the three vertices of P₃.
glossary.Bool.or_eq_true: A Boolean disjunction evaluates to true if and only if at least one operand is true.
glossary.Bool.and_eq_true: A Boolean conjunction evaluates to true if and only if both operands are true.
glossary.decide_eq_true_eq: The decision function decide(p) equals true if and only if the proposition p is true.
glossary.path_graph_three_adj_iff: The edges of the 3-vertex path graph P₃ are precisely {0, 1} and {1, 2}.
glossary.path_graph_three_stacked_iff: A configuration on P₃ satisfies path_graph_three_stacked if and only if all pebbles reside on a single vertex.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.refl: Every element is reachable from itself in zero steps in the reflexive-transitive closure.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.head: A single step prepended to a multi-step reachability path yields a valid reachability path.
glossary.path_graph_three_stk: A bounded recursive search function testing whether a configuration on P₃ can reach a stacked state in at most k pebbling steps.
glossary.path_graph_three_step_iff: A single pebbling step on P₃ is valid if and only if it is one of the four moves 0→1, 1→0, 1→2, or 2→1, each consuming 2 pebbles at the source and adding 1 at the destination.
glossary.Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on: Induction principle for reflexive-transitive reachability decomposing a sequence of steps from the head.
glossary.path_graph_three_dead: A bounded search function certifying that no sequence of pebbling steps of length at most k can reach a stacked configuration.
glossary.Fin.sum_univ_three: The sum of a function over Fin 3 equals f(0) + f(1) + f(2).
glossary.path_graph_three_stk_sound: If path_graph_three_stk returns true for fuel k and configuration c, then c is stackable on P₃.
glossary.path_graph_three_stk_seven: Every 7-pebble configuration on P₃ can be stacked in at most 7 moves.
glossary.path_graph_three_dead_examples: The specific configurations (1,0,1), (1,1,1), (3,0,1), (3,1,1), and (5,0,1) are verified to be dead configurations.
glossary.path_graph_three_dead_sound: If path_graph_three_dead returns true for fuel k and configuration c, then c cannot be stacked on P₃.
glossary.le_antisymm: If a ≤ b and b ≤ a, then a = b.
glossary.Nat.sInf_le: The infimum of a set of natural numbers is less than or equal to any element in that set.
glossary.le_csInf: If a is a lower bound for a nonempty set bounded below, then a ≤ sInf(s).
glossary.SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degre: The degree of a vertex in a simple graph equals the size of its neighbor finset.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset: A vertex w is in the neighbor finset of v if and only if v and w are adjacent.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finset if and only if it belongs to the base finset and satisfies the predicate.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to its universal finset.
glossary.true_and: True ∧ p is equivalent to p.
glossary.path_graph_three_degree: In P₃, the middle vertex 1 has degree 2, while the endpoints 0 and 2 have degree 1.
glossary.SimpleGraph.dist_self: The graph distance from any vertex to itself is 0.
glossary.Finset.sum_pair: The sum of a function over a pair of distinct elements {a, b} equals f(a) + f(b).

declarations.name: path_graph_degree_le_two
declarations.informal: Every vertex of the path graph P_k has degree at most 2.
declarations.statement:
theorem path_graph_degree_le_two (k : ℕ) [DecidableRel (SimpleGraph.pathGraph k).Adj]
    (i : Fin k) : (SimpleGraph.pathGraph k).degree i ≤ 2
declarations.source:
theorem path_graph_degree_le_two (k : ℕ) [DecidableRel (SimpleGraph.pathGraph k).Adj]
    (i : Fin k) : (SimpleGraph.pathGraph k).degree i ≤ 2 := by
  classical
  rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
  calc ((SimpleGraph.pathGraph k).neighborFinset i).card
      ≤ ({(i : ℕ) - 1, (i : ℕ) + 1} : Finset ℕ).card := by
        apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun j : Fin k => (j : ℕ))
        · intro j hj
          rw [Finset.mem_coe, SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj] at hj
          simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Finset.coe_singleton, Set.mem_insert_iff,
            Set.mem_singleton_iff]
          omega
        · intro j _ j' _ h
          exact Fin.ext h
    _ ≤ 2 := Finset.card_le_two
declarations.citation: Helper for arXiv:2610.12109 (Sharp linear Turán remainders for cycle and edge extremality), Lemma 2.5 (equality case of the lower bound: the extremal tree is a path).

explanation.summary: The degree of a vertex i in the path graph P_k is the number of its neighbors. By definition of adjacency in P_k, any neighbor j must satisfy j = i - 1 or j = i + 1 as natural numbers. We embed the neighbor set of i injectively into the two-element set of natural numbers {i - 1, i + 1}, bounding the degree by |{i - 1, i + 1}|. Since every two-element set has cardinality at most 2, the degree is at most 2.

steps.claim: The degree of vertex i equals the cardinality of its neighbor finset, so it suffices to show that |N(i)| ≤ 2.
steps.explanation: After enabling classical reasoning for decidability, SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree rewrites the degree of i as the cardinality of its neighbor finset.
steps.code:
classical
  rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]

steps.claim: The number of neighbors of i is at most the cardinality of {i - 1, i + 1} in ℕ.
steps.explanation: By Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn, an injective map from a finite set into another bounds its cardinality. We embed the neighbor finset into ℕ by sending each vertex to its underlying natural number. First, any neighbor j satisfies i + 1 = j or j + 1 = i by SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj, which implies j = i - 1 or j = i + 1, so the map lands in {i - 1, i + 1}. Second, the map is injective because vertices in Fin k with identical natural values are equal by Fin.ext.
steps.code:
calc ((SimpleGraph.pathGraph k).neighborFinset i).card
      ≤ ({(i : ℕ) - 1, (i : ℕ) + 1} : Finset ℕ).card := by
        apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn (fun j : Fin k => (j : ℕ))
        · intro j hj
          rw [Finset.mem_coe, SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj] at hj
          simp only [Finset.coe_insert, Finset.coe_singleton, Set.mem_insert_iff,
            Set.mem_singleton_iff]
          omega
        · intro j _ j' _ h
          exact Fin.ext h

steps.claim: The degree of vertex i is at most 2.
steps.explanation: By Finset.card_le_two, any pair set {a, b} has at most two elements. Chaining this with the inequality |N(i)| ≤ |{i - 1, i + 1}| completes the proof.
steps.code: _ ≤ 2 := Finset.card_le_two

glossary.SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degre: The degree of a vertex in a simple graph equals the cardinality of its neighbor finset.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn: If a function maps a finite set s into a finite set t and is injective on s, then the cardinality of s is at most that of t.
glossary.Finset.mem_coe: An element belongs to the coercion of a finset to a set if and only if it belongs to the finset.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset: A vertex w belongs to the neighbor finset of v if and only if v and w are adjacent.
glossary.SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj: In the path graph on n vertices, two vertices u and v are adjacent if and only if u + 1 = v or v + 1 = u.
glossary.Finset.coe_insert: Coercing the insertion of an element into a finset to a set equals inserting the element into the coerced set.
glossary.Finset.coe_singleton: Coercing a singleton finset to a set yields the singleton set.
glossary.Set.mem_insert_iff: An element belongs to insert a s if and only if it equals a or belongs to s.
glossary.Set.mem_singleton_iff: An element belongs to the singleton set {b} if and only if it equals b.
glossary.Fin.ext: Two elements of Fin n are equal if and only if their underlying natural numbers are equal.
glossary.Finset.card_le_two: Any finite set of the form {a, b} has cardinality at most 2.

caveats: The proof embeds the vertices from Fin k into ℕ via the canonical coercion. Defining the target set {i - 1, i + 1} in ℕ avoids edge-case handling for endpoint vertices (i = 0 or i = k - 1), since truncated natural subtraction safely evaluates 0 - 1 = 0 in ℕ.

declarations.name: simple_graph_connected_degree_pos
declarations.informal: In a connected graph with at least two vertices every vertex has positive degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_connected_degree_pos {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hconn : G.Connected) (hk : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (v : V) : 0 < G.degree v
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_connected_degree_pos {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hconn : G.Connected) (hk : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V)
    (v : V) : 0 < G.degree v := by
  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := Fintype.exists_ne_of_one_lt_card (by omega) v
  obtain ⟨p⟩ := hconn.preconnected v w
  cases p with
  | nil => exact absurd rfl hw
  | @cons _ x _ h _ =>
    rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
    exact Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨x, (SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset _ _ _).2 h⟩
declarations.citation: Helper for arXiv:2610.12109 (Sharp linear Turán remainders for cycle and edge extremality), Lemma 2.5 (equality case of the lower bound: the extremal tree is a path).

explanation.summary: Since the graph has at least two vertices, we can choose a vertex w distinct from v. Because the graph is connected, there exists a walk from v to w. This walk cannot be empty because its endpoints are distinct, so it must begin with an edge connecting v to some neighbor x. The existence of this neighbor shows that the neighbor set of v is nonempty, so v has strictly positive degree.

steps.claim: There exists a vertex w distinct from v, and a walk p connecting v to w.
steps.explanation: Since the vertex type has cardinality at least 2, its cardinality is strictly greater than 1 (by linear arithmetic via omega). By Fintype.exists_ne_of_one_lt_card, there exists a vertex w ≠ v. Because G is connected (hconn.preconnected), there exists a walk p from v to w.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := Fintype.exists_ne_of_one_lt_card (by omega) v
  obtain ⟨p⟩ := hconn.preconnected v w

steps.claim: The walk p cannot be empty.
steps.explanation: We split into cases on the structure of the walk p. If p is the empty walk (nil), its endpoints coincide, giving v = w. This contradicts the fact that w ≠ v (hw), ruling out this case.
steps.code:
cases p with
  | nil => exact absurd rfl hw

steps.claim: The degree of v is strictly positive.
steps.explanation: In the non-empty walk case (cons), p begins with an edge from v to some vertex x, establishing that v is adjacent to x. By SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree, the degree of v equals the cardinality of its neighbor finset. Since x belongs to this neighbor finset by SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset, the finset is nonempty, and Finset.card_pos.2 implies its cardinality—and therefore the degree of v—is strictly positive.
steps.code:
| @cons _ x _ h _ =>
    rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
    exact Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨x, (SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset _ _ _).2 h⟩

glossary.Fintype.exists_ne_of_one_lt_card: In a finite type with cardinality strictly greater than 1, every element has a distinct counterpart.
glossary.SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degre: The degree of a vertex equals the cardinality of its neighbor finset.
glossary.Finset.card_pos.2: A finite set has strictly positive cardinality if it is nonempty.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset: A vertex is in the neighbor finset of v if and only if it is adjacent to v.

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_tree_nonempty_iso_path_graph_of_degree_le_two
declarations.informal: A finite tree in which every vertex has degree at most 2 is isomorphic to the path P_k, k = |V|.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_tree_nonempty_iso_path_graph_of_degree_le_two {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hT : G.IsTree)
    (hdeg : ∀ v, G.degree v ≤ 2) : Nonempty (G ≃g SimpleGraph.pathGraph (Fintype.card V))
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_tree_nonempty_iso_path_graph_of_degree_le_two {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hT : G.IsTree)
    (hdeg : ∀ v, G.degree v ≤ 2) : Nonempty (G ≃g SimpleGraph.pathGraph (Fintype.card V)) := by
  classical
  let P : ℕ → Prop := fun n => ∃ u v : V, ∃ p : G.Walk u v, p.IsPath ∧ p.length = n
  obtain ⟨u₀⟩ := hT.1.nonempty
  have hP0 : P 0 := ⟨u₀, u₀, .nil, SimpleGraph.Walk.IsPath.nil, rfl⟩
  obtain ⟨u, v, p, hp, hpN⟩ := Nat.findGreatest_spec (P := P) (Nat.zero_le (Fintype.card V)) hP0
  have hmax : ∀ u' v' (q : G.Walk u' v'), q.IsPath → q.length ≤ p.length := fun u' v' q hq => by
    rw [hpN]
    exact Nat.le_findGreatest hq.length_lt.le ⟨u', v', q, hq, rfl⟩
  -- the longest path visits every vertex
  have hall : ∀ x, x ∈ p.support := by
    by_contra hcon
    push Not at hcon
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hcon
    obtain ⟨q⟩ := hT.1.preconnected u x
    obtain ⟨d, -, hd1, hd2⟩ := q.exists_boundary_dart {y | y ∈ p.support} p.start_mem_support hx
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hd1 hd2
    obtain ⟨i, hi, hile⟩ := SimpleGraph.Walk.mem_support_iff_exists_getVert.1 hd1
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos i with rfl | hipos
    · have hau : d.fst = u := by rw [← hi, p.getVert_zero]
      have hadj : G.Adj d.snd u := hau ▸ d.adj.symm
      have := hmax _ _ (SimpleGraph.Walk.cons hadj p) (hp.cons hd2)
      simp at this
    · rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hile with heq | hlt
      · have hav : d.fst = v := by rw [← hi, heq, p.getVert_length]
        have hadj : G.Adj v d.snd := hav ▸ d.adj
        have := hmax _ _ (p.concat hadj) (hp.concat hd2 hadj)
        simp [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_concat] at this
      · have h1 : G.Adj d.fst (p.getVert (i - 1)) := by
          have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := i - 1) (by omega)
          rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel hipos, hi] at this
          exact this.symm
        have h2 : G.Adj d.fst (p.getVert (i + 1)) := by
          have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := i) hlt
          rwa [hi] at this
        have h3 : G.Adj d.fst d.snd := d.adj
        have hne12 : p.getVert (i - 1) ≠ p.getVert (i + 1) := fun h => by
          have := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
            (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h
          omega
        have hne13 : p.getVert (i - 1) ≠ d.snd := fun h => hd2 (h ▸ p.getVert_mem_support _)
        have hne23 : p.getVert (i + 1) ≠ d.snd := fun h => hd2 (h ▸ p.getVert_mem_support _)
        have h3le : 3 ≤ G.degree d.fst := by
          rw [← G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
          have hsub : ({p.getVert (i - 1), p.getVert (i + 1), d.snd} : Finset V) ⊆
              G.neighborFinset d.fst := by
            intro y hy
            simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hy
            rw [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset]
            rcases hy with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> assumption
          calc 3 = ({p.getVert (i - 1), p.getVert (i + 1), d.snd} : Finset V).card := by
                rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (by simp [hne12, hne13]), Finset.card_pair hne23]
            _ ≤ _ := Finset.card_le_card hsub
        have := hdeg d.fst
        omega
  have hlen : p.length + 1 = Fintype.card V := by
    have huniv : p.support.toFinset = Finset.univ :=
      Finset.eq_univ_of_forall fun x => List.mem_toFinset.2 (hall x)
    rw [← Finset.card_univ, ← huniv, List.toFinset_card_of_nodup hp.support_nodup,
      p.length_support]
  let φ : Fin (Fintype.card V) → V := fun i => p.getVert i
  have hinj : Function.Injective φ := fun i j h =>
    Fin.ext (hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
      (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h)
  have hsurj : Function.Surjective φ := fun x => by
    obtain ⟨n, hn, hnl⟩ := SimpleGraph.Walk.mem_support_iff_exists_getVert.1 (hall x)
    exact ⟨⟨n, by omega⟩, hn⟩
  -- every edge is an edge of the path: the path already has |E| = card V − 1 edges
  have hedge : ∀ a b, G.Adj a b →
      ∃ m : ℕ, m < p.length ∧ s(a, b) = s(p.getVert m, p.getVert (m + 1)) := by
    intro a b hab
    let f : Fin p.length → Sym2 V := fun m => s(p.getVert m, p.getVert (m + 1))
    have hfinj : Function.Injective f := by
      intro m m' h
      simp only [f, Sym2.eq_iff] at h
      rcases h with ⟨h1, -⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
      · exact Fin.ext (hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
          (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h1)
      · have e1 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
          (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h1
        have e2 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
          (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h2
        omega
    have hsub : Finset.univ.image f ⊆ G.edgeFinset := by
      intro e he
      simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at he
      obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := he
      rw [SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset]
      exact p.adj_getVert_succ m.2
    have hcard : G.edgeFinset.card ≤ (Finset.univ.image f).card := by
      rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hfinj, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
      have := hT.card_edgeFinset
      omega
    have heq := Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le hsub hcard
    have hmem : s(a, b) ∈ G.edgeFinset := by rwa [SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset]
    rw [← heq] at hmem
    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hmem
    obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := hmem
    exact ⟨m, m.2, hm.symm⟩
  let e : Fin (Fintype.card V) ≃ V := Equiv.ofBijective φ ⟨hinj, hsurj⟩
  refine ⟨⟨e.symm, @fun a b => ?_⟩⟩
  obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := hsurj a
  obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := hsurj b
  have hi : e.symm (φ i) = i := e.symm_apply_apply i
  have hj : e.symm (φ j) = j := e.symm_apply_apply j
  rw [hi, hj, SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj]
  constructor
  · rintro (h | h)
    · have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := i) (by omega)
      simp only [φ]
      rwa [show (j : ℕ) = i + 1 by omega]
    · have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := j) (by omega)
      simp only [φ]
      rw [show (i : ℕ) = j + 1 by omega]
      exact this.symm
  · intro hadj
    obtain ⟨m, hm, hmeq⟩ := hedge _ _ hadj
    rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at hmeq
    rcases hmeq with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
    · have e1 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
        (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h1
      have e2 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
        (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h2
      left
      omega
    · have e1 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
        (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h1
      have e2 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
        (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h2
      right
      omega
declarations.citation: Helper for arXiv:2610.12109 (Sharp linear Turán remainders for cycle and edge extremality), Lemma 2.5 (equality case of the lower bound: the extremal tree is a path).

explanation.summary: To show that a finite tree with maximum degree at most 2 is isomorphic to a path graph, we take a simple path p of maximal length. By connectivity and the degree constraint, p must visit every vertex: an unvisited vertex would yield an edge leaving p, which would either extend p at an endpoint (contradicting maximality) or attach to an internal vertex (forcing degree at least 3). Counting tree edges shows that every edge of G lies along p, and enumerating the vertices along p yields the desired isomorphism with the path graph.

steps.claim: There exists a path p in G of maximal length.
steps.explanation: We define the property P(n) asserting that G contains a simple path of length n. Since G is a tree, it is nonempty, providing a vertex u₀ and thus a trivial path of length 0. Bounding lengths by |V|, we obtain via Nat.findGreatest a path p from u to v of maximal length.
steps.code:
classical
  let P : ℕ → Prop := fun n => ∃ u v : V, ∃ p : G.Walk u v, p.IsPath ∧ p.length = n
  obtain ⟨u₀⟩ := hT.1.nonempty
  have hP0 : P 0 := ⟨u₀, u₀, .nil, SimpleGraph.Walk.IsPath.nil, rfl⟩
  obtain ⟨u, v, p, hp, hpN⟩ := Nat.findGreatest_spec (P := P) (Nat.zero_le (Fintype.card V)) hP0

steps.claim: No simple path in G has length strictly greater than that of p.
steps.explanation: Any path q in G has length strictly less than |V|, so Nat.le_findGreatest implies that q.length ≤ p.length.
steps.code:
have hmax : ∀ u' v' (q : G.Walk u' v'), q.IsPath → q.length ≤ p.length := fun u' v' q hq => by
    rw [hpN]
    exact Nat.le_findGreatest hq.length_lt.le ⟨u', v', q, hq, rfl⟩

steps.claim: If p does not visit every vertex, there is an edge crossing from the vertices of p to an unvisited vertex.
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that some vertex x is not in the support of p. Since trees are connected, there is a walk q from u to x. Along this walk, there must exist a transition dart d = (d.fst, d.snd) with d.fst in the support of p and d.snd outside it. We express d.fst as p.getVert i for some index i ≤ p.length.
steps.code:
have hall : ∀ x, x ∈ p.support := by
    by_contra hcon
    push Not at hcon
    obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hcon
    obtain ⟨q⟩ := hT.1.preconnected u x
    obtain ⟨d, -, hd1, hd2⟩ := q.exists_boundary_dart {y | y ∈ p.support} p.start_mem_support hx
    simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hd1 hd2
    obtain ⟨i, hi, hile⟩ := SimpleGraph.Walk.mem_support_iff_exists_getVert.1 hd1

steps.claim: The crossing dart cannot attach at the start vertex u (case i = 0).
steps.explanation: If i = 0, d.fst = u, so the edge between d.snd and u can be prepended to p using Walk.cons to form a strictly longer path, contradicting the maximality of p.
steps.code:
rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos i with rfl | hipos
    · have hau : d.fst = u := by rw [← hi, p.getVert_zero]
      have hadj : G.Adj d.snd u := hau ▸ d.adj.symm
      have := hmax _ _ (SimpleGraph.Walk.cons hadj p) (hp.cons hd2)
      simp at this

steps.claim: The crossing dart cannot attach at the end vertex v (case i = p.length).
steps.explanation: If i = p.length, d.fst = v, so the edge between v and d.snd can be appended to p using Walk.concat to form a strictly longer path, again contradicting the maximality of p.
steps.code:
· rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hile with heq | hlt
      · have hav : d.fst = v := by rw [← hi, heq, p.getVert_length]
        have hadj : G.Adj v d.snd := hav ▸ d.adj
        have := hmax _ _ (p.concat hadj) (hp.concat hd2 hadj)
        simp [SimpleGraph.Walk.length_concat] at this

steps.claim: The crossing dart cannot attach at an internal vertex of p (case 0 < i < p.length).
steps.explanation: If 0 < i < p.length, the vertex d.fst is adjacent to its predecessor p.getVert (i - 1), its successor p.getVert (i + 1), and d.snd. Because p is a path, the predecessor and successor are distinct, and because d.snd is not on p, it differs from both. This gives d.fst at least 3 distinct neighbors, contradicting the degree bound deg(v) ≤ 2. Hence every vertex of G lies on p.
steps.code:
· have h1 : G.Adj d.fst (p.getVert (i - 1)) := by
          have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := i - 1) (by omega)
          rw [Nat.sub_add_cancel hipos, hi] at this
          exact this.symm
        have h2 : G.Adj d.fst (p.getVert (i + 1)) := by
          have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := i) hlt
          rwa [hi] at this
        have h3 : G.Adj d.fst d.snd := d.adj
        have hne12 : p.getVert (i - 1) ≠ p.getVert (i + 1) := fun h => by
          have := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
            (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h
          omega
        have hne13 : p.getVert (i - 1) ≠ d.snd := fun h => hd2 (h ▸ p.getVert_mem_support _)
        have hne23 : p.getVert (i + 1) ≠ d.snd := fun h => hd2 (h ▸ p.getVert_mem_support _)
        have h3le : 3 ≤ G.degree d.fst := by
          rw [← G.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
          have hsub : ({p.getVert (i - 1), p.getVert (i + 1), d.snd} : Finset V) ⊆
              G.neighborFinset d.fst := by
            intro y hy
            simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hy
            rw [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset]
            rcases hy with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> assumption
          calc 3 = ({p.getVert (i - 1), p.getVert (i + 1), d.snd} : Finset V).card := by
                rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (by simp [hne12, hne13]), Finset.card_pair hne23]
            _ ≤ _ := Finset.card_le_card hsub
        have := hdeg d.fst
        omega

steps.claim: The length of p is |V| - 1.
steps.explanation: Since the support of p contains every vertex and has no duplicates, its cardinality equals |V|. But the support of any walk has length p.length + 1, so p.length + 1 = |V|.
steps.code:
have hlen : p.length + 1 = Fintype.card V := by
    have huniv : p.support.toFinset = Finset.univ :=
      Finset.eq_univ_of_forall fun x => List.mem_toFinset.2 (hall x)
    rw [← Finset.card_univ, ← huniv, List.toFinset_card_of_nodup hp.support_nodup,
      p.length_support]

steps.claim: The indexing map φ : Fin |V| → V along p is a bijection.
steps.explanation: We define φ(i) = p.getVert i. Injectivity follows because p is a simple path (no repeated vertices). Surjectivity follows because every vertex of G is visited by p.
steps.code:
let φ : Fin (Fintype.card V) → V := fun i => p.getVert i
  have hinj : Function.Injective φ := fun i j h =>
    Fin.ext (hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
      (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h)
  have hsurj : Function.Surjective φ := fun x => by
    obtain ⟨n, hn, hnl⟩ := SimpleGraph.Walk.mem_support_iff_exists_getVert.1 (hall x)
    exact ⟨⟨n, by omega⟩, hn⟩

steps.claim: Every edge of G is a step along the path p.
steps.explanation: Consider the map f sending each step index m < p.length to the undirected edge s(p.getVert m, p.getVert (m + 1)). Injectivity of φ makes f injective, so its image has size p.length = |V| - 1. In a tree, the total number of edges is |V| - 1. A subset of size |V| - 1 inside a set of size |V| - 1 must be the entire edge set, so every edge of G is of the form s(p.getVert m, p.getVert (m + 1)).
steps.code:
have hedge : ∀ a b, G.Adj a b →
      ∃ m : ℕ, m < p.length ∧ s(a, b) = s(p.getVert m, p.getVert (m + 1)) := by
    intro a b hab
    let f : Fin p.length → Sym2 V := fun m => s(p.getVert m, p.getVert (m + 1))
    have hfinj : Function.Injective f := by
      intro m m' h
      simp only [f, Sym2.eq_iff] at h
      rcases h with ⟨h1, -⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
      · exact Fin.ext (hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
          (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h1)
      · have e1 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
          (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h1
        have e2 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
          (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h2
        omega
    have hsub : Finset.univ.image f ⊆ G.edgeFinset := by
      intro e he
      simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at he
      obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := he
      rw [SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset]
      exact p.adj_getVert_succ m.2
    have hcard : G.edgeFinset.card ≤ (Finset.univ.image f).card := by
      rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ hfinj, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
      have := hT.card_edgeFinset
      omega
    have heq := Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le hsub hcard
    have hmem : s(a, b) ∈ G.edgeFinset := by rwa [SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset]
    rw [← heq] at hmem
    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hmem
    obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := hmem
    exact ⟨m, m.2, hm.symm⟩

steps.claim: The inverse bijection e.symm defines an isomorphism G ≃g pathGraph |V|.
steps.explanation: We promote φ to an equivalence e : Fin |V| ≃ V and use its inverse. Two vertices φ(i) and φ(j) are adjacent in G if and only if they form an edge of p, which by injectivity means j = i + 1 or i = j + 1. This matches precisely the adjacency condition for the standard path graph on Fin |V|.
steps.code:
let e : Fin (Fintype.card V) ≃ V := Equiv.ofBijective φ ⟨hinj, hsurj⟩
  refine ⟨⟨e.symm, @fun a b => ?_⟩⟩
  obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ := hsurj a
  obtain ⟨j, rfl⟩ := hsurj b
  have hi : e.symm (φ i) = i := e.symm_apply_apply i
  have hj : e.symm (φ j) = j := e.symm_apply_apply j
  rw [hi, hj, SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj]
  constructor
  · rintro (h | h)
    · have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := i) (by omega)
      simp only [φ]
      rwa [show (j : ℕ) = i + 1 by omega]
    · have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := j) (by omega)
      simp only [φ]
      rw [show (i : ℕ) = j + 1 by omega]
      exact this.symm
  · intro hadj
    obtain ⟨m, hm, hmeq⟩ := hedge _ _ hadj
    rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at hmeq
    rcases hmeq with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
    · have e1 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
        (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h1
      have e2 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
        (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h2
      left
      omega
    · have e1 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
        (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h1
      have e2 := hp.getVert_injOn (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega)
        (by simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq]; omega) h2
      right
      omega

glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.IsPath.nil: The trivial walk of length 0 consisting of a single vertex is a path.
glossary.Nat.findGreatest_spec: If P holds for some m ≤ n, then findGreatest P n satisfies P.
glossary.Nat.zero_le: For every natural number n, 0 ≤ n.
glossary.Nat.le_findGreatest: If m ≤ n and P m holds, then m ≤ findGreatest P n.
glossary.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element x belongs to {y | p y} if and only if p x holds.
glossary.Nat.eq_zero_or_pos: Every natural number is either 0 or strictly positive.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.cons: Prepending an adjacent vertex to a walk produces a new walk.
glossary.eq_or_lt_of_le: If a ≤ b, then either a = b or a < b.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.length_concat: Appending an edge to a walk increases its length by 1.
glossary.Nat.sub_add_cancel: If m ≤ n, then (n - m) + m = n.
glossary.Finset.mem_insert: An element belongs to insert a s if and only if it equals a or belongs to s.
glossary.Finset.mem_singleton: An element belongs to {a} if and only if it equals a.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset: A vertex w is in the neighbor Finset of v if and only if v and w are adjacent.
glossary.Finset.card_insert_of_notMem: If a is not in s, inserting a into s increases its cardinality by 1.
glossary.Finset.card_pair: A set containing two distinct elements has cardinality 2.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If s ⊆ t, then |s| ≤ |t|.
glossary.Finset.eq_univ_of_forall: If every element of a finite type is in s, then s is univ.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal Finset of α is Fintype.card α.
glossary.List.toFinset_card_of_nodup: If a list has no duplicate elements, its conversion to a Finset preserves length.
glossary.Fin.ext: Two elements of Fin n are equal if and only if their underlying values are equal.
glossary.Sym2.eq_iff: Two unordered pairs s(x, y) and s(z, w) are equal if and only if (x = z ∧ y = w) or (x = w ∧ y = z).
glossary.Finset.mem_image: An element is in image f s if and only if it equals f x for some x ∈ s.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element is in Finset.univ.
glossary.true_and: True ∧ p is logically equivalent to p.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset: An unordered pair is in edgeFinset if and only if it is an edge of the graph.
glossary.Finset.card_image_of_injective: The image of a Finset under an injective function has the same cardinality as the Finset.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The cardinality of Fin n is n.
glossary.Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le: If s ⊆ t and |t| ≤ |s|, then s = t.
glossary.Equiv.ofBijective: A bijective function can be promoted to an equivalence.
glossary.SimpleGraph.pathGraph_adj: Vertices u and v in Fin n are adjacent in the path graph if and only if u + 1 = v or v + 1 = u.

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_tree_sum_choose_degree_eq_iff_path
declarations.informal: For a tree T on k ≥ 2 vertices, σ₂(T) = k − 2 if and only if T is isomorphic to the path P_k.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_tree_sum_choose_degree_eq_iff_path {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hT : G.IsTree)
    (hk : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 = Fintype.card V - 2 ↔
      Nonempty (G ≃g SimpleGraph.pathGraph (Fintype.card V))
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_tree_sum_choose_degree_eq_iff_path {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hT : G.IsTree)
    (hk : 2 ≤ Fintype.card V) :
    ∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 = Fintype.card V - 2 ↔
      Nonempty (G ≃g SimpleGraph.pathGraph (Fintype.card V)) := by
  classical
  have hE : G.edgeFinset.card + 1 = Fintype.card V := hT.card_edgeFinset
  have hsumdeg : (∑ v, (G.degree v : ℤ)) = 2 * (Fintype.card V - 1) := by
    have := G.sum_degrees_eq_twice_card_edges
    have h' : (∑ v, (G.degree v : ℤ)) = 2 * G.edgeFinset.card := by exact_mod_cast this
    rw [h']
    have : (G.edgeFinset.card : ℤ) + 1 = Fintype.card V := by exact_mod_cast hE
    linarith
  -- ∑ (d − 1) = k − 2 in ℤ
  have hsub1 : (∑ v, ((G.degree v : ℤ) - 1)) = Fintype.card V - 2 := by
    rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hsumdeg]
    simp only [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_one]
    ring
  have hle : ∀ v, ((G.degree v : ℤ) - 1) ≤ ((G.degree v).choose 2 : ℤ) := by
    intro v
    generalize G.degree v = d
    rcases d with _ | m
    · simp
    · rw [Nat.choose_succ_succ, Nat.choose_one_right]
      push_cast
      omega
  constructor
  · intro hsum
    apply simple_graph_is_tree_nonempty_iso_path_graph_of_degree_le_two G hT
    have hz : (∑ v, ((G.degree v).choose 2 : ℤ)) = ∑ v, ((G.degree v : ℤ) - 1) := by
      rw [hsub1]
      have : ((∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) = ((Fintype.card V - 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
        rw [hsum]
      push_cast at this
      rw [this]
      omega
    have heach := (Finset.sum_eq_sum_iff_of_le (fun v _ => hle v)).1 hz.symm
    intro v
    have hv := heach v (Finset.mem_univ v)
    by_contra hlt
    push Not at hlt
    obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ : ∃ m, G.degree v = m + 3 := ⟨G.degree v - 3, by omega⟩
    rw [hm, Nat.choose_succ_succ, Nat.choose_one_right] at hv
    have hpos : 0 < (m + 2).choose 2 := Nat.choose_pos (by omega)
    push_cast at hv
    omega
  · rintro ⟨f⟩
    have hdeg2 : ∀ v, G.degree v ≤ 2 := by
      intro v
      calc G.degree v ≤ (SimpleGraph.pathGraph (Fintype.card V)).degree (f v) := by
            rw [← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree,
              ← SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree]
            apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn f
            · intro w hw
              rw [Finset.mem_coe, SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset] at hw ⊢
              exact f.map_adj_iff.2 hw
            · intro w _ w' _ h
              exact f.injective h
        _ ≤ 2 := path_graph_degree_le_two _ _
    have hpos : ∀ v, 0 < G.degree v := simple_graph_connected_degree_pos G hT.1 hk
    have hz : (∑ v, ((G.degree v).choose 2 : ℤ)) ≤ ∑ v, ((G.degree v : ℤ) - 1) := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro v _
      have h1 := hdeg2 v
      have h2 := hpos v
      generalize G.degree v = d at h1 h2
      interval_cases d <;> simp
    have hlow := (simple_graph_is_tree_card_sub_two_le_sum_choose_degree_le_choose G hT hk).1
    rw [hsub1] at hz
    have : ((∑ v, (G.degree v).choose 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ ((Fintype.card V - 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
      push_cast
      rw [Nat.cast_sub hk]
      push_cast
      exact hz
    have := Int.ofNat_le.1 this
    omega
