declarations.name: schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound
declarations.informal: Let G be a commutative group, q a prime, and g in G an element of order q. Let pk, a₁, a₂ in Subgroup.zpowers g. For any challenges c₁, c₂ in ZMod q and responses s₁, s₂ in ZMod q, if transcript 1 does not satisfy Schnorr.Verify g pk a₁ c₁ s₁, then the set of linear batching weights α in ZMod q for which g^((s₁ + α * s₂).val) = a₁ * a₂^(α.val) * pk^((c₁ + α * c₂).val) holds has cardinality at most 1.
declarations.statement:
theorem schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound
    {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] [DecidableEq G] {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (g : G)
    (hg : orderOf g = q) (pk a₁ a₂ : G)
    (hpk : pk ∈ Subgroup.zpowers g)
    (ha₁ : a₁ ∈ Subgroup.zpowers g)
    (ha₂ : a₂ ∈ Subgroup.zpowers g)
    (c₁ c₂ s₁ s₂ : ZMod q)
    (hnot : ¬ Schnorr.Verify g pk a₁ c₁ s₁) :
    (Finset.filter (fun α : ZMod q =>
      g ^ (s₁ + α * s₂).val = a₁ * a₂ ^ α.val * pk ^ (c₁ + α * c₂).val) Finset.univ).card ≤ 1
declarations.source:
theorem schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_eq_pow_zmod_val
    {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (g : G)
    (hg : orderOf g = q) (n : ℕ) :
    g ^ n = g ^ (n : ZMod q).val := by
  have : NeZero q := ⟨Nat.Prime.ne_zero Fact.out⟩
  have h2 := schnorr_zpow_eq_pow_zmod_val g hg (n : ℤ)
  push_cast at h2
  rw [← zpow_natCast, h2]

theorem schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_pow_eq_pow_mul_zmod
    {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (g : G)
    (hg : orderOf g = q) (x y : ZMod q) :
    (g ^ x.val) ^ y.val = g ^ (x * y).val := by
  have : NeZero q := ⟨Nat.Prime.ne_zero Fact.out⟩
  rw [← pow_mul, schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_eq_pow_zmod_val g hg (x.val * y.val)]
  congr 1
  push_cast
  simp

theorem schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_mul_pow_eq_pow_add_zmod
    {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (g : G)
    (hg : orderOf g = q) (x y : ZMod q) :
    g ^ x.val * g ^ y.val = g ^ (x + y).val := by
  have : NeZero q := ⟨Nat.Prime.ne_zero Fact.out⟩
  rw [← pow_add, schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_eq_pow_zmod_val g hg (x.val + y.val)]
  congr 1
  push_cast
  simp

theorem schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_g_pow_inj
    {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (g : G)
    (hg : orderOf g = q) (k₁ k₂ : ZMod q) :
    g ^ k₁.val = g ^ k₂.val ↔ k₁ = k₂ := by
  have : NeZero q := ⟨Nat.Prime.ne_zero Fact.out⟩
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [pow_eq_pow_iff_modEq, hg] at h
    have hs₁ := ZMod.val_lt k₁
    have hs₂ := ZMod.val_lt k₂
    change k₁.val % q = k₂.val % q at h
    rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hs₁, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hs₂] at h
    exact ZMod.val_injective q h
  · rintro rfl
    rfl

theorem schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_verify_iff
    {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (g : G)
    (hg : orderOf g = q) (r₁ w c₁ s₁ : ZMod q) :
    Schnorr.Verify g (g ^ w.val) (g ^ r₁.val) c₁ s₁ ↔ s₁ = r₁ + c₁ * w := by
  change g ^ s₁.val = g ^ r₁.val * (g ^ w.val) ^ c₁.val ↔ s₁ = r₁ + c₁ * w
  rw [schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_pow_eq_pow_mul_zmod g hg w c₁]
  rw [schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_mul_pow_eq_pow_add_zmod g hg r₁ (w * c₁)]
  have h_exp : r₁ + w * c₁ = r₁ + c₁ * w := by ring
  rw [h_exp]
  exact schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_g_pow_inj g hg s₁ (r₁ + c₁ * w)

theorem schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_batch_eq_iff
    {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (g : G)
    (hg : orderOf g = q) (r₁ r₂ w c₁ c₂ s₁ s₂ α : ZMod q) :
    g ^ (s₁ + α * s₂).val = (g ^ r₁.val) * (g ^ r₂.val) ^ α.val * (g ^ w.val) ^ (c₁ + α * c₂).val ↔
    s₁ + α * s₂ = r₁ + c₁ * w + α * (r₂ + c₂ * w) := by
  have h_rhs : (g ^ r₁.val) * (g ^ r₂.val) ^ α.val * (g ^ w.val) ^ (c₁ + α * c₂).val =
      g ^ (r₁ + c₁ * w + α * (r₂ + c₂ * w)).val := by
    rw [schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_pow_eq_pow_mul_zmod g hg r₂ α]
    rw [schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_pow_eq_pow_mul_zmod g hg w (c₁ + α * c₂)]
    rw [schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_mul_pow_eq_pow_add_zmod g hg r₁ (r₂ * α)]
    rw [schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_pow_mul_pow_eq_pow_add_zmod g hg (r₁ + r₂ * α) (w * (c₁ + α * c₂))]
    congr 2
    ring
  rw [h_rhs]
  exact schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_g_pow_inj g hg (s₁ + α * s₂) (r₁ + c₁ * w + α * (r₂ + c₂ * w))

theorem schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_linear_batch_eq_unique
    {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (r₁ r₂ w c₁ c₂ s₁ s₂ α₁ α₂ : R)
    (h₁ : s₁ + α₁ * s₂ = r₁ + c₁ * w + α₁ * (r₂ + c₂ * w))
    (h₂ : s₁ + α₂ * s₂ = r₁ + c₁ * w + α₂ * (r₂ + c₂ * w))
    (h_not : s₁ ≠ r₁ + c₁ * w) :
    α₁ = α₂ := by
  have h_diff : (α₁ - α₂) * (s₂ - (r₂ + c₂ * w)) = 0 := by
    calc (α₁ - α₂) * (s₂ - (r₂ + c₂ * w))
      _ = (s₁ + α₁ * s₂ - (r₁ + c₁ * w + α₁ * (r₂ + c₂ * w))) -
          (s₁ + α₂ * s₂ - (r₁ + c₁ * w + α₂ * (r₂ + c₂ * w))) := by ring
      _ = 0 - 0 := by rw [sub_eq_zero.mpr h₁, sub_eq_zero.mpr h₂]
      _ = 0 := sub_zero 0
  cases mul_eq_zero.mp h_diff with
  | inl h_sub => exact sub_eq_zero.mp h_sub
  | inr h_B =>
    have h_B_eq : s₂ = r₂ + c₂ * w := sub_eq_zero.mp h_B
    rw [h_B_eq] at h₁
    have h_contr : s₁ = r₁ + c₁ * w := by
      calc s₁ = (s₁ + α₁ * (r₂ + c₂ * w)) - α₁ * (r₂ + c₂ * w) := by ring
      _ = (r₁ + c₁ * w + α₁ * (r₂ + c₂ * w)) - α₁ * (r₂ + c₂ * w) := by rw [h₁]
      _ = r₁ + c₁ * w := by ring
    exact (h_not h_contr).elim

/-- Quantitative soundness bound for linear batch verification of Schnorr transcripts: at most one linear weight accepts an invalid transcript. -/
theorem schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound
    {G : Type*} [CommGroup G] [DecidableEq G] {q : ℕ} [Fact q.Prime] (g : G)
    (hg : orderOf g = q) (pk a₁ a₂ : G)
    (hpk : pk ∈ Subgroup.zpowers g)
    (ha₁ : a₁ ∈ Subgroup.zpowers g)
    (ha₂ : a₂ ∈ Subgroup.zpowers g)
    (c₁ c₂ s₁ s₂ : ZMod q)
    (hnot : ¬ Schnorr.Verify g pk a₁ c₁ s₁) :
    (Finset.filter (fun α : ZMod q =>
      g ^ (s₁ + α * s₂).val = a₁ * a₂ ^ α.val * pk ^ (c₁ + α * c₂).val) Finset.univ).card ≤ 1 := by
  obtain ⟨w, rfl⟩ := schnorr_mem_zpowers_iff_exists_zmod g hg pk hpk
  obtain ⟨r₁, rfl⟩ := schnorr_mem_zpowers_iff_exists_zmod g hg a₁ ha₁
  obtain ⟨r₂, rfl⟩ := schnorr_mem_zpowers_iff_exists_zmod g hg a₂ ha₂
  have hnot_alg : s₁ ≠ r₁ + c₁ * w := by
    intro h_eq
    apply hnot
    rwa [schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_verify_iff g hg]
  rw [Finset.card_le_one_iff]
  intro α₁ α₂ hα₁ hα₂
  rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hα₁ hα₂
  rw [schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_batch_eq_iff g hg] at hα₁ hα₂
  exact schnorr_linear_batch_soundness_bound_linear_batch_eq_unique r₁ r₂ w c₁ c₂ s₁ s₂ α₁ α₂ hα₁.2 hα₂.2 hnot_alg
declarations.citation: Bellare, Garay, and Ralf 1998, Fast Batch Verification of Signatures
declarations.reading: Let `G` be a commutative group with decidable equality. Let `q` be a prime natural number. Let `g : G` be an element whose order in `G` equals `q`. Let `pk`, `a₁`, and `a₂` be elements of `G` each belonging to the cyclic subgroup generated by `g` (`Subgroup.zpowers g`). Let `c₁`, `c₂`, `s₁`, and `s₂` be elements of `ZMod q`. declarations.name: poset_hypomorphic_card_lt_pairs_eq
declarations.informal: The number of comparable pairs is reconstructible: if finite ordered sets P and Q with |P| ≥ 3 have the same deck, they have the same number of pairs a < b. (Each such pair survives in exactly |P| − 2 of the cards, so the count is the sum over the deck divided by |P| − 2.)
declarations.statement:
theorem poset_hypomorphic_card_lt_pairs_eq (P Q : Type) [Fintype P] [Fintype Q]
    [PartialOrder P] [PartialOrder Q] [DecidableRel ((· < ·) : P → P → Prop)]
    [DecidableRel ((· < ·) : Q → Q → Prop)] (hn : 3 ≤ Fintype.card P)
    (h : poset_hypomorphic P Q) :
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : P × P => p.1 < p.2)).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Q × Q => p.1 < p.2)).card
declarations.source:
theorem poset_hypomorphic_card_lt_pairs_eq (P Q : Type) [Fintype P] [Fintype Q]
    [PartialOrder P] [PartialOrder Q] [DecidableRel ((· < ·) : P → P → Prop)]
    [DecidableRel ((· < ·) : Q → Q → Prop)] (hn : 3 ≤ Fintype.card P)
    (h : poset_hypomorphic P Q) :
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : P × P => p.1 < p.2)).card =
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Q × Q => p.1 < p.2)).card := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨σ, hσ⟩ := h
  have hcard : Fintype.card Q = Fintype.card P := (Fintype.card_congr σ).symm
  have sumP : ∀ (R : Type) [Fintype R] [PartialOrder R] [DecidableRel ((· < ·) : R → R → Prop)],
      ∑ x : R, (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : R × R => p.1 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ≠ x ∧ p.2 ≠ x)).card =
        (Fintype.card R - 2) * (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : R × R => p.1 < p.2)).card := by
    intro R _ _ _
    simp only [Finset.card_filter]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm, Finset.mul_sum]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro p _
    by_cases hp : p.1 < p.2
    · simp only [hp, true_and, if_true, mul_one]
      rw [← Finset.card_filter]
      have hfil : Finset.univ.filter (fun x => p.1 ≠ x ∧ p.2 ≠ x) =
          (Finset.univ.erase p.1).erase p.2 := by
        ext x
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_erase, and_true]
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩; exact ⟨fun h' => h2 h'.symm, fun h' => h1 h'.symm⟩
        · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩; exact ⟨fun h' => h2 h'.symm, fun h' => h1 h'.symm⟩
      rw [hfil, Finset.card_erase_of_mem, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _),
        Finset.card_univ]
      · omega
      · exact Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hp.ne', Finset.mem_univ _⟩
    · simp [hp]
  have subcount : ∀ (R : Type) [Fintype R] [PartialOrder R]
      [DecidableRel ((· < ·) : R → R → Prop)] (x : R),
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : {y : R // y ≠ x} × {y : R // y ≠ x} => p.1 < p.2)).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : R × R => p.1 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ≠ x ∧ p.2 ≠ x)).card := by
    intro R _ _ _ x
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun p _ => ((p.1 : R), (p.2 : R)))
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hab ⊢
      exact ⟨hab, a.2, b.2⟩
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ _ ⟨c, d⟩ _ hh
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at hh
      rw [Subtype.ext hh.1, Subtype.ext hh.2]
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hab
      refine ⟨(⟨a, hab.2.1⟩, ⟨b, hab.2.2⟩), ?_, rfl⟩
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
      exact hab.1
  have isoc : ∀ x : P,
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : {y : P // y ≠ x} × {y : P // y ≠ x} => p.1 < p.2)).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter
          (fun p : {y : Q // y ≠ σ x} × {y : Q // y ≠ σ x} => p.1 < p.2)).card := by
    intro x
    obtain ⟨e⟩ := hσ x
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun p _ => (e p.1, e p.2))
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hab ⊢
      exact e.lt_iff_lt.mpr hab
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ _ ⟨c, d⟩ _ hh
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at hh
      rw [e.injective hh.1, e.injective hh.2]
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hab
      refine ⟨(e.symm a, e.symm b), ?_, by simp⟩
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
      exact e.symm.lt_iff_lt.mpr hab
  have hsum : ∑ x : P, (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : P × P => p.1 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ≠ x ∧ p.2 ≠ x)).card =
      ∑ y : Q, (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Q × Q => p.1 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ≠ y ∧ p.2 ≠ y)).card := by
    rw [← Equiv.sum_comp σ]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro x _
    rw [← subcount P x, ← subcount Q (σ x), isoc x]
  rw [sumP P, sumP Q, hcard] at hsum
  exact Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left (by omega) hsum
declarations.citation: The standard counting lemma of reconstruction theory, applied to comparabilities; serves the height-one reconstruction question of arXiv:2610.12690 (Reconstruction of Finite Posets of Width Three), Sec. 9. The bound |P| ≥ 3 is needed: the 2-chain and the 2-antichain have the same deck.

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by double counting comparable pairs across the deck of single-element deleted subposets. In any finite poset R, each strict inequality a < b survives in exactly |R| − 2 cards (namely those excluding neither a nor b), so summing the comparable pairs over all cards yields (|R| − 2) times the total number of comparable pairs. Because P and Q are hypomorphic, each card of P is order-isomorphic to the corresponding card of Q and therefore contains the same number of comparable pairs. Since |P| = |Q| ≥ 3, the factor |P| − 2 is strictly positive, and cancelling it establishes that P and Q have the same total number of comparable pairs.

steps.claim: The posets P and Q have equal cardinality, and their deck of deleted subposets is matched by a bijection σ : P ≃ Q.
steps.explanation: Unpacking the hypomorphism hypothesis yields a bijection σ : P ≃ Q such that for every x ∈ P, the single-element deleted subposet P \ {x} is order-isomorphic to Q \ {σ x}. By Fintype.card_congr, the existence of σ implies |Q| = |P|.
steps.code:
classical
  obtain ⟨σ, hσ⟩ := h
  have hcard : Fintype.card Q = Fintype.card P := (Fintype.card_congr σ).symm

steps.claim: For any finite poset R, the sum over x ∈ R of the number of comparable pairs avoiding x equals (|R| − 2) times the total number of comparable pairs in R.
steps.explanation: Rewriting set cardinalities as sums of indicators and exchanging the order of summation reduces the identity to evaluating the inner sum for each pair p = (a, b). If a < b, strict inequality ensures a ≠ b, so x avoids both a and b for every element of R except a and b; erasing these two elements leaves |R| − 2 choices. If a ≮ b, the indicator is 0. Summing |R| − 2 over all comparable pairs yields the result.
steps.code:
have sumP : ∀ (R : Type) [Fintype R] [PartialOrder R] [DecidableRel ((· < ·) : R → R → Prop)],
      ∑ x : R, (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : R × R => p.1 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ≠ x ∧ p.2 ≠ x)).card =
        (Fintype.card R - 2) * (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : R × R => p.1 < p.2)).card := by
    intro R _ _ _
    simp only [Finset.card_filter]
    rw [Finset.sum_comm, Finset.mul_sum]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro p _
    by_cases hp : p.1 < p.2
    · simp only [hp, true_and, if_true, mul_one]
      rw [← Finset.card_filter]
      have hfil : Finset.univ.filter (fun x => p.1 ≠ x ∧ p.2 ≠ x) =
          (Finset.univ.erase p.1).erase p.2 := by
        ext x
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_erase, and_true]
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩; exact ⟨fun h' => h2 h'.symm, fun h' => h1 h'.symm⟩
        · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩; exact ⟨fun h' => h2 h'.symm, fun h' => h1 h'.symm⟩
      rw [hfil, Finset.card_erase_of_mem, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _),
        Finset.card_univ]
      · omega
      · exact Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨hp.ne', Finset.mem_univ _⟩
    · simp [hp]

steps.claim: For any x ∈ R, the comparable pairs in the subposet R \ {x} correspond bijectively to pairs (a, b) in R satisfying a < b with a ≠ x and b ≠ x.
steps.explanation: Using Finset.card_bij, the canonical projection sending a pair of subtype elements ((a, ha), (b, hb)) to the pair of their underlying elements in R is shown to be a bijection: it maps into pairs avoiding x, is injective by Subtype.ext, and is surjective because every avoiding pair lifts to the subtype.
steps.code:
have subcount : ∀ (R : Type) [Fintype R] [PartialOrder R]
      [DecidableRel ((· < ·) : R → R → Prop)] (x : R),
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : {y : R // y ≠ x} × {y : R // y ≠ x} => p.1 < p.2)).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : R × R => p.1 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ≠ x ∧ p.2 ≠ x)).card := by
    intro R _ _ _ x
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun p _ => ((p.1 : R), (p.2 : R)))
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hab ⊢
      exact ⟨hab, a.2, b.2⟩
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ _ ⟨c, d⟩ _ hh
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at hh
      rw [Subtype.ext hh.1, Subtype.ext hh.2]
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hab
      refine ⟨(⟨a, hab.2.1⟩, ⟨b, hab.2.2⟩), ?_, rfl⟩
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
      exact hab.1

steps.claim: For each x ∈ P, the card P \ {x} has the same number of comparable pairs as the corresponding card Q \ {σ x}.
steps.explanation: By the hypomorphism assumption, there exists an order isomorphism e between P \ {x} and Q \ {σ x}. Mapping each comparable pair (a, b) to (e a, e b) defines a bijection via Finset.card_bij, because e is an order isomorphism and thus preserves strict inequality in both directions and is injective.
steps.code:
have isoc : ∀ x : P,
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : {y : P // y ≠ x} × {y : P // y ≠ x} => p.1 < p.2)).card =
        (Finset.univ.filter
          (fun p : {y : Q // y ≠ σ x} × {y : Q // y ≠ σ x} => p.1 < p.2)).card := by
    intro x
    obtain ⟨e⟩ := hσ x
    apply Finset.card_bij (fun p _ => (e p.1, e p.2))
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hab ⊢
      exact e.lt_iff_lt.mpr hab
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ _ ⟨c, d⟩ _ hh
      simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at hh
      rw [e.injective hh.1, e.injective hh.2]
    · rintro ⟨a, b⟩ hab
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hab
      refine ⟨(e.symm a, e.symm b), ?_, by simp⟩
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
      exact e.symm.lt_iff_lt.mpr hab

steps.claim: The sum over x ∈ P of the counts of comparable pairs in P \ {x} equals the corresponding sum over Q.
steps.explanation: Using Equiv.sum_comp, the sum over Q is reindexed via the bijection σ : P ≃ Q. By the subtype equivalence and the isomorphism between cards, the summand at each x ∈ P equals the summand at σ x in Q, so the two sums are identical by Finset.sum_congr.
steps.code:
have hsum : ∑ x : P, (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : P × P => p.1 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ≠ x ∧ p.2 ≠ x)).card =
      ∑ y : Q, (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Q × Q => p.1 < p.2 ∧ p.1 ≠ y ∧ p.2 ≠ y)).card := by
    rw [← Equiv.sum_comp σ]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro x _
    rw [← subcount P x, ← subcount Q (σ x), isoc x]

steps.claim: The total number of comparable pairs in P equals the total number of comparable pairs in Q.
steps.explanation: Rewriting both sides of the sum equality with the double-counting formula gives (|P| − 2) * card(P's pairs) = (|P| − 2) * card(Q's pairs), since |Q| = |P|. Because |P| ≥ 3, the factor |P| − 2 is strictly positive (verified by linear arithmetic), and cancelling it via Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left concludes the proof.
steps.code:
rw [sumP P, sumP Q, hcard] at hsum
  exact Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left (by omega) hsum

glossary.Fintype.card_congr: A bijection between two finite types implies they have the same cardinality.
glossary.Finset.card_filter: The cardinality of a filtered finset equals the sum of indicator values of the predicate over the finset.
glossary.Finset.sum_comm: Double summation over finite sets can be interchanged.
glossary.Finset.mul_sum: Multiplication distributes over a finite sum from the left.
glossary.Finset.sum_congr: Two finite sums are equal if their domains are equal and their summands agree at every point.
glossary.true_and: Conjunction with True simplifies to the second conjunct.
glossary.if_true: An if-then-else expression whose condition is True evaluates to the then-branch.
glossary.mul_one: Multiplying by 1 leaves an element unchanged.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finset if and only if it belongs to the base finset and satisfies the predicate.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finset.
glossary.Finset.mem_erase: An element belongs to s with b removed if and only if it is not equal to b and belongs to s.
glossary.and_true: Conjunction with True on the right simplifies to the first conjunct.
glossary.Finset.card_erase_of_mem: Erasing an element from a finset decreases its cardinality by 1.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset equals the cardinality of the underlying finite type.
glossary.Finset.mem_erase.mpr: If an element is not equal to b and belongs to s, it belongs to s with b removed.
glossary.Finset.card_bij: A map between two finsets that is well-defined, injective, and surjective establishes that the finsets have equal cardinality.
glossary.Prod.mk.injEq: Two pairs are equal if and only if their first and second components are respectively equal.
glossary.Subtype.ext: Two subtype elements are equal if their underlying values are equal.
glossary.Equiv.sum_comp: Reindexing a finite sum by an equivalence does not change the sum.
glossary.Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left: If n is strictly positive and n * m = n * k, then m = k.

caveats: The definition of hypomorphic posets in this formalization explicitly provides a bijection between the elements along with order isomorphisms between corresponding deleted subposets, rather than equality of cards as an unlabelled multiset.
To count pairs in subposets, the formal proof repeatedly moves between pairs of subtype elements and pairs in the ambient product type avoiding an element via explicit bijections.

declarations.name: tournament_min_rank_le_inversion_number
declarations.informal: For a finite tournament D: tmr(D) ≤ inv(D).
declarations.statement:
theorem tournament_min_rank_le_inversion_number (V : Type) [Fintype V] (D : Digraph V)
    (h : digraph_is_tournament D) :
    tournament_min_rank D ≤ digraph_inversion_number D
declarations.source:
theorem tournament_min_rank_le_inversion_number (V : Type) [Fintype V] (D : Digraph V)
    (h : digraph_is_tournament D) :
    tournament_min_rank D ≤ digraph_inversion_number D := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨Xs, hXl, hXa⟩ := tournament_exists_family_length_eq_inversion_number V D h
  let A : {n : ℕ} → (Fin n → Set V) → Matrix V (Fin n) (ZMod 2) :=
    fun X x i => if x ∈ X i then 1 else 0
  let N : Set V → Matrix V V (ZMod 2) :=
    fun X x y => (if x ∈ X then 1 else 0) * (if y ∈ X then 1 else 0)
  have h11 : (1 : ZMod 2) + 1 = 0 := rfl
  have h01 : (0 : ZMod 2) ≠ 1 := by decide
  have two : ∀ a : ZMod 2, a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by decide
  have flip_add : ∀ (E : Digraph V) (P M : Matrix V V (ZMod 2)), (∀ x y, P y x = P x y) →
      digraph_flip_by_matrix (digraph_flip_by_matrix E P) M =
        digraph_flip_by_matrix E (P + M) := by
    intro E P M hP
    ext x y
    simp only [digraph_flip_by_matrix, Matrix.add_apply, hP x y]
    rcases two (P x y) with ha | ha <;> rcases two (M x y) with hb | hb <;>
      simp [ha, hb, h11]
  have hN : ∀ (E : Digraph V) (X : Set V), digraph_invert E X = digraph_flip_by_matrix E (N X) := by
    intro E X
    ext x y
    simp only [digraph_flip_by_matrix, digraph_invert, N]
    by_cases hx : x ∈ X <;> by_cases hy : y ∈ X <;> simp [hx, hy]
  have key : ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Fin n → Set V) (E : Digraph V),
      digraph_flip_by_matrix E (A X * (A X).transpose) = (List.ofFn X).foldl digraph_invert E := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero =>
      intro X E
      ext x y
      simp [digraph_flip_by_matrix, Matrix.mul_apply]
    | succ n ih =>
      intro X E
      rw [List.ofFn_succ, List.foldl_cons, ← ih (fun i => X i.succ), hN, flip_add]
      · congr 1
        ext x y
        simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply, Fin.sum_univ_succ]
        rfl
      · intro x y
        simp only [N]
        ring
  have hsymm : (A Xs.get * (A Xs.get).transpose).IsSymm := by
    apply Matrix.IsSymm.ext
    intro i j
    simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun k _ => mul_comm _ _)
  have hac : digraph_is_acyclic (digraph_flip_by_matrix D (A Xs.get * (A Xs.get).transpose)) := by
    rw [key, List.ofFn_get]
    exact hXa
  calc tournament_min_rank D ≤ (A Xs.get * (A Xs.get).transpose).rank :=
        Nat.sInf_le ⟨_, hsymm, hac, rfl⟩
    _ ≤ (A Xs.get).rank := Matrix.rank_mul_le_left _ _
    _ ≤ Fintype.card (Fin Xs.length) := Matrix.rank_le_card_width _
    _ = digraph_inversion_number D := by simp [hXl]
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.13798 (On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins), inequality (1.2), quoting an earlier paper (the sum of the rank-one matrices 1_X 1_Xᵀ over a decycling family is a decycling matrix of rank at most the family size).

explanation.summary: To show that the tournament minimum rank tmr(D) is at most the inversion number inv(D), we take an optimal sequence of vertex subsets X₀, ..., X_{k-1} of length k = inv(D) whose sequential inversion makes D acyclic. We form the V × k vertex-subset incidence matrix A over ℤ/2 and its symmetric Gram matrix M = A Aᵀ. By induction, flipping edges of D according to M is equivalent to sequentially inverting along the subsets Xᵢ, producing an acyclic tournament. Consequently, tmr(D) ≤ rank(M) ≤ rank(A) ≤ k = inv(D).

steps.claim: Obtain an optimal sequence of vertex subsets achieving the inversion number and define the incidence and rank-one matrices.
steps.explanation: By tournament_exists_family_length_eq_inversion_number, there exists a list Xs of k = inv(D) vertex subsets whose successive inversion leaves D acyclic. We define the V × k incidence matrix A where A x i = 1 if x ∈ Xs i and 0 otherwise, and for any set X ⊆ V, the rank-one outer product matrix N(X) where N(X) x y = 1 if both x, y ∈ X and 0 otherwise, working over ℤ/2.

steps.claim: Flipping a digraph by a symmetric matrix P and then by a matrix M is equivalent to flipping by P + M.
steps.explanation: After noting basic arithmetic in ℤ/2 (1 + 1 = 0, 0 ≠ 1, and every element is 0 or 1), we compare the adjacency conditions. Flipping by P swaps an edge (x, y) if P x y = 1, and flipping again by M swaps it if M x y = 1. Using the symmetry of P (P y x = P x y) and checking all four possible value pairs for (P x y, M x y) in {0, 1}², the composed flip agrees with flipping whenever (P + M) x y = 1.
steps.code:
have h11 : (1 : ZMod 2) + 1 = 0 := rfl
  have h01 : (0 : ZMod 2) ≠ 1 := by decide
  have two : ∀ a : ZMod 2, a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by decide
  have flip_add : ∀ (E : Digraph V) (P M : Matrix V V (ZMod 2)), (∀ x y, P y x = P x y) →
      digraph_flip_by_matrix (digraph_flip_by_matrix E P) M =
        digraph_flip_by_matrix E (P + M) := by
    intro E P M hP
    ext x y
    simp only [digraph_flip_by_matrix, Matrix.add_apply, hP x y]
    rcases two (P x y) with ha | ha <;> rcases two (M x y) with hb | hb <;>
      simp [ha, hb, h11]

steps.claim: Inverting a digraph along a subset X is equivalent to flipping edges by the matrix N(X).
steps.explanation: Inverting along X reverses an edge (x, y) if and only if both x ∈ X and y ∈ X. Since N(X) x y = 1 precisely when x, y ∈ X, this coincides with flipping edges by N(X), verified by a case analysis on whether x ∈ X and y ∈ X.
steps.code:
have hN : ∀ (E : Digraph V) (X : Set V), digraph_invert E X = digraph_flip_by_matrix E (N X) := by
    intro E X
    ext x y
    simp only [digraph_flip_by_matrix, digraph_invert, N]
    by_cases hx : x ∈ X <;> by_cases hy : y ∈ X <;> simp [hx, hy]

steps.claim: Flipping by the Gram matrix A(X) * A(X)ᵀ is equivalent to sequentially inverting the family of subsets X.
steps.explanation: By induction on the length n of the sequence X. For n = 0, A(X) * A(X)ᵀ is the zero matrix, which flips no edges, matching the empty sequence of inversions. For n + 1, the matrix product decomposes via Fin.sum_univ_succ into N(X 0) + A(X') * A(X')ᵀ, where X' is the tail of the sequence. Because N(X 0) is symmetric, flip_add shows that flipping by this sum equals flipping by N(X 0) followed by A(X') * A(X')ᵀ. By the induction hypothesis and hN, this matches inverting X 0 followed by inverting the remaining subsets.
steps.code:
have key : ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Fin n → Set V) (E : Digraph V),
      digraph_flip_by_matrix E (A X * (A X).transpose) = (List.ofFn X).foldl digraph_invert E := by
    intro n
    induction n with
    | zero =>
      intro X E
      ext x y
      simp [digraph_flip_by_matrix, Matrix.mul_apply]
    | succ n ih =>
      intro X E
      rw [List.ofFn_succ, List.foldl_cons, ← ih (fun i => X i.succ), hN, flip_add]
      · congr 1
        ext x y
        simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply, Fin.sum_univ_succ]
        rfl
      · intro x y
        simp only [N]
        ring

steps.claim: The Gram matrix M = A(Xs) * A(Xs)ᵀ is symmetric.
steps.explanation: By Matrix.IsSymm.ext, it suffices to show M j i = M i j. Using Matrix.mul_apply and Matrix.transpose_apply, the entry M i j is ∑ k, A i k * A j k. By commutativity of multiplication (mul_comm and Finset.sum_congr), this equals ∑ k, A j k * A i k = M j i.
steps.code:
have hsymm : (A Xs.get * (A Xs.get).transpose).IsSymm := by
    apply Matrix.IsSymm.ext
    intro i j
    simp only [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.transpose_apply]
    exact Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun k _ => mul_comm _ _)

steps.claim: Flipping D by M = A(Xs) * A(Xs)ᵀ produces an acyclic tournament.
steps.explanation: Using key to rewrite the matrix flip as sequential inversion and List.ofFn_get to identify the indexing function with the list Xs, flipping D by M yields the tournament obtained by sequentially inverting Xs. This digraph is acyclic by the choice of Xs (hypothesis hXa).
steps.code:
have hac : digraph_is_acyclic (digraph_flip_by_matrix D (A Xs.get * (A Xs.get).transpose)) := by
    rw [key, List.ofFn_get]
    exact hXa

steps.claim: The tournament minimum rank of D is at most its inversion number.
steps.explanation: Since M = A(Xs) * A(Xs)ᵀ is a symmetric matrix over ℤ/2 that flips D to an acyclic tournament, its rank is an upper bound for tournament_min_rank(D) by Nat.sInf_le. The rank of A * Aᵀ is at most the rank of A by Matrix.rank_mul_le_left, which in turn is bounded by the number of columns |Xs| by Matrix.rank_le_card_width. Because |Xs| = inv(D), we conclude tournament_min_rank(D) ≤ inv(D).
steps.code:
calc tournament_min_rank D ≤ (A Xs.get * (A Xs.get).transpose).rank :=
        Nat.sInf_le ⟨_, hsymm, hac, rfl⟩
    _ ≤ (A Xs.get).rank := Matrix.rank_mul_le_left _ _
    _ ≤ Fintype.card (Fin Xs.length) := Matrix.rank_le_card_width _
    _ = digraph_inversion_number D := by simp [hXl]

declarations.name: digraph_reverse
declarations.informal: The reverse D̄ of a digraph D: the digraph on the same vertices with every arc turned around.
declarations.statement: def digraph_reverse {V : Type*} (D : Digraph V) : Digraph V
declarations.source:
/-- The reverse of a digraph: every arc turned around. -/
def digraph_reverse {V : Type*} (D : Digraph V) : Digraph V where
  Adj x y := D.Adj y x
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.13798 (On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins), Sec. 4 (D̄, the tournament obtained by flipping every arc of D).

declarations.name: digraph_reverse_is_tournament
declarations.informal: The reverse of a tournament is a tournament.
declarations.statement:
theorem digraph_reverse_is_tournament {V : Type*} (D : Digraph V)
    (h : digraph_is_tournament D) : digraph_is_tournament (digraph_reverse D)
declarations.source:
theorem digraph_reverse_is_tournament {V : Type*} (D : Digraph V)
    (h : digraph_is_tournament D) : digraph_is_tournament (digraph_reverse D) :=
  ⟨fun x => h.1 x, fun x y hxy => h.2 y x (Ne.symm hxy)⟩

explanation.summary: To prove that the reversal of a tournament D is itself a tournament, we verify its two defining conditions: looplessness and the tournament edge condition between distinct vertices. Both hold directly by unpacking the definition of the reversed graph: a self-loop in the reverse is a self-loop in D, and the condition for an edge between distinct x and y in the reverse is the tournament condition of D applied to the pair (y, x).

steps.claim: The reversal of D is loopless and has exactly one directed edge between any pair of distinct vertices.
steps.explanation: By definition, a tournament requires two properties. First, it has no self-loops: for any vertex x, the reversed graph has no loop at x if and only if ¬ D.Adj x x, which is provided directly by the loopless property of D (h.1 x). Second, for any two vertices x and y with x ≠ y, there must be an edge from x to y in the reversed graph if and only if there is not an edge from y to x; by definition of digraph_reverse, this unfolds to D.Adj y x ↔ ¬ D.Adj x y. Since x ≠ y implies y ≠ x by Ne.symm, this equivalence is precisely the tournament condition of D applied to the pair (y, x) (h.2 y x).
steps.code: ⟨fun x => h.1 x, fun x y hxy => h.2 y x (Ne.symm hxy)⟩

glossary.Ne.symm: Inequality is symmetric: if a ≠ b, then b ≠ a.

declarations.name: digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse
declarations.informal: If G's arcs are E's arcs pulled back along a map f and reversed (x → y in G iff f y → f x in E), and E is a finite tournament, then inv(G) ≤ inv(E): a decycling family of E pulls back to one of G of the same length.
declarations.statement:
theorem digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse {U U' : Type} [Fintype U']
    (G : Digraph U) (E : Digraph U') (f : U → U') (hE : digraph_is_tournament E)
    (hGE : ∀ x y, G.Adj x y ↔ E.Adj (f y) (f x)) :
    digraph_inversion_number G ≤ digraph_inversion_number E
declarations.source:
theorem digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse {U U' : Type} [Fintype U']
    (G : Digraph U) (E : Digraph U') (f : U → U') (hE : digraph_is_tournament E)
    (hGE : ∀ x y, G.Adj x y ↔ E.Adj (f y) (f x)) :
    digraph_inversion_number G ≤ digraph_inversion_number E := by
  obtain ⟨Zs, hZl, hZa⟩ := tournament_exists_family_length_eq_inversion_number U' E hE
  have rev : ∀ (Zs : List (Set U')) (E : Digraph U') (G : Digraph U),
      (∀ x y, G.Adj x y ↔ E.Adj (f y) (f x)) →
      ∀ x y, ((Zs.map (f ⁻¹' ·)).foldl digraph_invert G).Adj x y ↔
        (Zs.foldl digraph_invert E).Adj (f y) (f x) := by
    intro Zs
    induction Zs with
    | nil => intro E G hGE; simpa using hGE
    | cons Z Zs ih =>
      intro E G hGE
      simp only [List.map_cons, List.foldl_cons]
      apply ih
      intro x y
      simp only [digraph_invert, Set.mem_preimage, hGE]
      tauto
  apply Nat.sInf_le
  refine ⟨Zs.map (f ⁻¹' ·), by simp [hZl], ?_⟩
  intro x hx
  apply hZa (f x)
  have hr := rev Zs E G hGE
  have key : ∀ x y, Relation.TransGen ((Zs.map (f ⁻¹' ·)).foldl digraph_invert G).Adj x y →
      Relation.TransGen (Zs.foldl digraph_invert E).Adj (f y) (f x) := by
    intro x y hxy
    induction hxy with
    | single h => exact .single ((hr _ _).1 h)
    | tail _ h ih => exact .head ((hr _ _).1 h) ih
  exact key x x hx
declarations.citation: Helper for the reduction in arXiv:2610.13798 (On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins), Sec. 4 (a set of inversions decycles D iff it decycles D̄; inv(D₂ → D₁) = inv(D̄₁ → D̄₂)).

explanation.summary: To show that inv(G) ≤ inv(E), we take an optimal decycling family Zs for the tournament E, of length inv(E), and pull it back to G via preimages under f. An induction on the list of subsets shows that inverting G along preimages preserves the reversed adjacency relation at each step: x → y in the inverted G if and only if f(y) → f(x) in the inverted E. Consequently, every directed path in the inverted G reverses to a directed path in the inverted E. Any cycle in the inverted G would therefore push forward to a cycle in the inverted E, contradicting its acyclicity and establishing that the pulled-back family decycles G.

steps.claim: There exists an optimal decycling family for the tournament E whose length equals the inversion number of E.
steps.explanation: Applying tournament_exists_family_length_eq_inversion_number to the finite tournament E provides a list Zs of vertex subsets whose length is inv(E) and such that inverting E successively along Zs produces an acyclic digraph.
steps.code: obtain ⟨Zs, hZl, hZa⟩ := tournament_exists_family_length_eq_inversion_number U' E hE

steps.claim: Inverting G along the preimages f⁻¹(Z) preserves the reversed adjacency relation with the inverted tournament E.
steps.explanation: We prove by induction on Zs that an arc exists from x to y in the inverted G if and only if an arc exists from f(y) to f(x) in the inverted E. The base case (an empty list) is the initial hypothesis. For the inductive step, inverting along f⁻¹(Z) reverses adjacency between x and y precisely when both vertices lie in f⁻¹(Z), which is equivalent to f(x) and f(y) both lying in Z; thus the single-step inversion preserves the reversed adjacency relation, and the induction hypothesis applies to the rest of the list.
steps.code:
have rev : ∀ (Zs : List (Set U')) (E : Digraph U') (G : Digraph U),
      (∀ x y, G.Adj x y ↔ E.Adj (f y) (f x)) →
      ∀ x y, ((Zs.map (f ⁻¹' ·)).foldl digraph_invert G).Adj x y ↔
        (Zs.foldl digraph_invert E).Adj (f y) (f x) := by
    intro Zs
    induction Zs with
    | nil => intro E G hGE; simpa using hGE
    | cons Z Zs ih =>
      intro E G hGE
      simp only [List.map_cons, List.foldl_cons]
      apply ih
      intro x y
      simp only [digraph_invert, Set.mem_preimage, hGE]
      tauto

steps.claim: The inversion number of G is at most that of E, provided that inverting G along the preimage family yields an acyclic digraph.
steps.explanation: By definition, the inversion number is the infimum of the lengths of decycling families. The pulled-back family of subsets Zs.map (f ⁻¹' ·) has length equal to the length of Zs, which equals inv(E). By Nat.sInf_le, showing that this family decycles G bounds inv(G) ≤ inv(E).
steps.code:
apply Nat.sInf_le
  refine ⟨Zs.map (f ⁻¹' ·), by simp [hZl], ?_⟩

steps.claim: The digraph obtained by inverting G along the preimage family is acyclic.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that there is a cycle at vertex x in the inverted G. By induction on paths (TransGen), any directed path from u to v in the inverted G reverses to a directed path from f(v) to f(u) in the inverted E, because every individual step reverses by the lemma rev proved in the second step. In particular, the cycle at x in G yields a cycle at f(x) in the inverted E, contradicting the fact that inverting E along Zs yields an acyclic digraph.
steps.code:
intro x hx
  apply hZa (f x)
  have hr := rev Zs E G hGE
  have key : ∀ x y, Relation.TransGen ((Zs.map (f ⁻¹' ·)).foldl digraph_invert G).Adj x y →
      Relation.TransGen (Zs.foldl digraph_invert E).Adj (f y) (f x) := by
    intro x y hxy
    induction hxy with
    | single h => exact .single ((hr _ _).1 h)
    | tail _ h ih => exact .head ((hr _ _).1 h) ih
  exact key x x hx

glossary.List.map_cons: mapping a function over a cons list applies the function to the head and maps over the tail
glossary.List.foldl_cons: folding over a cons list applies the fold operation to the accumulator and the head, then continues over the tail

glossary.Set.mem_preimage: an element belongs to the preimage of a set under a map if and only if its image belongs to the set

declarations.name: tournament_inversion_number_reverse
declarations.informal: For a finite tournament D: inv(D̄) = inv(D), where D̄ is D with every arc reversed.
declarations.statement:
theorem tournament_inversion_number_reverse (V : Type) [Fintype V] (D : Digraph V)
    (h : digraph_is_tournament D) :
    digraph_inversion_number (digraph_reverse D) = digraph_inversion_number D
declarations.source:
theorem tournament_inversion_number_reverse (V : Type) [Fintype V] (D : Digraph V)
    (h : digraph_is_tournament D) :
    digraph_inversion_number (digraph_reverse D) = digraph_inversion_number D := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse _ D id h (fun x y => Iff.rfl)
  · exact digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse D (digraph_reverse D) id
      (digraph_reverse_is_tournament D h) (fun x y => Iff.rfl)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.13798 (On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins), Sec. 4 ("a set of inversions decycle D if and only if they decycle D̄, so inv(D) = inv(D̄)").

explanation.summary: The equality is proved by establishing the mutual bounds inv(D̄) ≤ inv(D) and inv(D) ≤ inv(D̄) via antisymmetry. Each direction applies an existing lemma stating that an arc-reversing vertex map from a digraph into a tournament bounds the inversion number; the identity map gives the required reversal in both directions, using the fact that reversing a tournament produces another tournament.

steps.claim: To show inv(D̄) = inv(D), it suffices to prove inv(D̄) ≤ inv(D) and inv(D) ≤ inv(D̄).
steps.explanation: By the antisymmetry of the partial order on natural numbers (le_antisymm), an equality follows from proving inequalities in both directions.
steps.code: apply le_antisymm

steps.claim: inv(D̄) ≤ inv(D)
steps.explanation: We apply the comparison lemma digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse with G = D̄, E = D, and the identity map. The hypothesis that D is a tournament is given by h, and the adjacency-reversal condition (D̄.Adj x y ↔ D.Adj y x) holds definitionally by reflexivity of equivalence (Iff.rfl).
steps.code: · exact digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse _ D id h (fun x y => Iff.rfl)

steps.claim: inv(D) ≤ inv(D̄)
steps.explanation: We apply the same comparison lemma in the opposite direction, with G = D, E = D̄, and the identity map. The requirement that D̄ is a tournament is supplied by digraph_reverse_is_tournament, and the adjacency condition (D.Adj x y ↔ D̄.Adj y x) again holds definitionally by reflexivity (Iff.rfl).
steps.code:
· exact digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse D (digraph_reverse D) id
      (digraph_reverse_is_tournament D h) (fun x y => Iff.rfl)

glossary.le_antisymm: If a ≤ b and b ≤ a in a partial order, then a = b.
glossary.digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_r: If E is a finite tournament and f reverses adjacencies between G and E (that is, G.Adj x y ↔ E.Adj (f y) (f x)), then digraph_inversion_number G ≤ digraph_inversion_number E.
glossary.digraph_reverse_is_tournament: The reversal of any tournament is also a tournament.
glossary.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is logically equivalent to itself (P ↔ P).

declarations.name: tournament_dijoin_swap_inversion_number_eq_reverse
declarations.informal: For finite tournaments D₁, D₂: inv(D₂ → D₁) = inv(D̄₁ → D̄₂). So the symmetry conjecture inv(D₁ → D₂) = inv(D₂ → D₁) says exactly that the inversion number of a dijoin is unchanged when both parts are reversed.
declarations.statement:
theorem tournament_dijoin_swap_inversion_number_eq_reverse
    (V W : Type) [Fintype V] [Fintype W] (D₁ : Digraph V) (D₂ : Digraph W)
    (h₁ : digraph_is_tournament D₁) (h₂ : digraph_is_tournament D₂) :
    digraph_inversion_number (digraph_dijoin D₂ D₁) =
      digraph_inversion_number (digraph_dijoin (digraph_reverse D₁) (digraph_reverse D₂))
declarations.source:
theorem tournament_dijoin_swap_inversion_number_eq_reverse
    (V W : Type) [Fintype V] [Fintype W] (D₁ : Digraph V) (D₂ : Digraph W)
    (h₁ : digraph_is_tournament D₁) (h₂ : digraph_is_tournament D₂) :
    digraph_inversion_number (digraph_dijoin D₂ D₁) =
      digraph_inversion_number (digraph_dijoin (digraph_reverse D₁) (digraph_reverse D₂)) := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse _ _ Sum.swap
      (digraph_dijoin_is_tournament _ _ (digraph_reverse_is_tournament D₁ h₁)
        (digraph_reverse_is_tournament D₂ h₂))
    intro x y
    rcases x with a | a <;> rcases y with b | b <;> simp [digraph_dijoin, digraph_reverse]
  · apply digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse _ _ Sum.swap
      (digraph_dijoin_is_tournament _ _ h₂ h₁)
    intro x y
    rcases x with a | a <;> rcases y with b | b <;> simp [digraph_dijoin, digraph_reverse]
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.13798 (On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins), Sec. 4, reduction after Conjecture 4.1 (the reverse of D₂ → D₁ is D̄₁ → D̄₂).

explanation.summary: The equality is established by antisymmetry, reducing to proving both directions of the inequality between inv(D₂ → D₁) and inv(D̄₁ → D̄₂). In each direction, the inversion number is bounded using `digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse` via the swap map `Sum.swap`, which interchanges the two summands. A four-way case analysis on vertex summands confirms that `Sum.swap` acts as an anti-isomorphism by directly unfolding the definitions of dijoin and reversal.

steps.claim: It suffices to show that inv(D₂ → D₁) ≤ inv(D̄₁ → D̄₂) and inv(D̄₁ → D̄₂) ≤ inv(D₂ → D₁).
steps.explanation: By antisymmetry of the partial order on natural numbers (`le_antisymm`), the two inversion numbers are equal if each is less than or equal to the other.
steps.code: apply le_antisymm

steps.claim: inv(D₂ → D₁) ≤ inv(D̄₁ → D̄₂)
steps.explanation: By `digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse`, an inversion number inequality holds whenever there is an adjacency-reversing map into a tournament. The target dijoin D̄₁ → D̄₂ is a tournament because the reversal of a tournament is a tournament (`digraph_reverse_is_tournament`) and the dijoin of tournaments is a tournament (`digraph_dijoin_is_tournament`). Using the canonical swap map `Sum.swap : W ⊕ V → V ⊕ W`, it remains to show that x → y in D₂ → D₁ if and only if y.swap → x.swap in D̄₁ → D̄₂. Case analysis on whether x and y originate from W or V yields four cases; in each case, unfolding the definitions of dijoin and reverse digraph simplifies the equivalence to an identity.
steps.code:
· apply digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse _ _ Sum.swap
      (digraph_dijoin_is_tournament _ _ (digraph_reverse_is_tournament D₁ h₁)
        (digraph_reverse_is_tournament D₂ h₂))
    intro x y
    rcases x with a | a <;> rcases y with b | b <;> simp [digraph_dijoin, digraph_reverse]

steps.claim: inv(D̄₁ → D̄₂) ≤ inv(D₂ → D₁)
steps.explanation: By the same lemma `digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse` applied in the reverse direction with `Sum.swap : V ⊕ W → W ⊕ V`, and using that D₂ → D₁ is a tournament (`digraph_dijoin_is_tournament`), the inequality reduces to the reversed adjacency condition. Case analysis on whether x, y ∈ V ⊕ W come from V or W followed by unfolding the definitions of dijoin and reverse digraph closes all four cases.
steps.code:
· apply digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_reverse _ _ Sum.swap
      (digraph_dijoin_is_tournament _ _ h₂ h₁)
    intro x y
    rcases x with a | a <;> rcases y with b | b <;> simp [digraph_dijoin, digraph_reverse]

glossary.le_antisymm: In a partial order, if a ≤ b and b ≤ a, then a = b.
glossary.digraph_inversion_number_le_of_adj_iff_r: If E is a finite tournament and f : U → U' is an adjacency-reversing map from G to E (so x is adjacent to y in G iff f(y) is adjacent to f(x) in E), then the inversion number of G is at most that of E.
glossary.digraph_dijoin_is_tournament: The dijoin of two tournaments is a tournament.
glossary.digraph_reverse_is_tournament: The reversal of a tournament is a tournament.

declarations.name: card_le_twenty_nine_of_regular_eight_triangle_distinct
declarations.informal: Every 8-regular triangle-distinct graph has at most 29 vertices: its triangle-degrees are pairwise distinct and each is at most C(8, 2) = 28.
declarations.statement:
theorem card_le_twenty_nine_of_regular_eight_triangle_distinct {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree 8)
    (htd : simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct G) : Fintype.card V ≤ 29
declarations.source:
theorem card_le_twenty_nine_of_regular_eight_triangle_distinct {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hreg : G.IsRegularOfDegree 8)
    (htd : simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct G) : Fintype.card V ≤ 29 := by
  have hmaps : ∀ v ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset V),
      simple_graph_triangle_degree G v ∈ Finset.range 29 := by
    intro v _
    have h1 := simple_graph_triangle_degree_le_choose G v
    rw [hreg v] at h1
    simp only [Finset.mem_range]
    have : (8 : ℕ).choose 2 = 28 := by decide
    omega
  have := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn _ hmaps (htd.injOn)
  simpa using this
declarations.citation: Pigeonhole bound towards OP-123 (arXiv:2610.08478, Sec. 1). Its recorded dependency on the unproved exists_regular_eight_triangle_distinct blocks the offline build; the r = 8 case of the proved simple_graph_card_le_choose_add_one_of_regular_triangle_distinct is the same bound.

explanation.summary: The proof bounds the number of vertices by viewing the triangle-degree function as an injection into a small set of integers. Since G is 8-regular, any vertex has 8 neighbors and can participate in at most C(8, 2) = 28 triangles, meaning every triangle-degree is an integer in {0, ..., 28}. Because G is triangle-distinct, distinct vertices have distinct triangle-degrees, so the triangle-degree map is injective; by the pigeonhole principle, the graph can have at most 29 vertices.

steps.claim: For every vertex v, its triangle-degree is at most 28, so it belongs to {0, ..., 28} (Finset.range 29).
steps.explanation: For any vertex v, its triangle-degree is bounded by C(deg(v), 2) using simple_graph_triangle_degree_le_choose. Since G is 8-regular (hreg v), this bound is C(8, 2). A direct calculation (decide) evaluates C(8, 2) = 28. Using Finset.mem_range to rephrase membership in Finset.range 29 as being strictly less than 29, linear arithmetic (omega) closes the goal from triangle-degree ≤ 28.
steps.code:
have hmaps : ∀ v ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset V),
      simple_graph_triangle_degree G v ∈ Finset.range 29 := by
    intro v _
    have h1 := simple_graph_triangle_degree_le_choose G v
    rw [hreg v] at h1
    simp only [Finset.mem_range]
    have : (8 : ℕ).choose 2 = 28 := by decide
    omega

steps.claim: The vertex set of G has cardinality at most 29.
steps.explanation: By hypothesis htd, the triangle-degree map is injective on the entire vertex set. Applying Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn to this map from Finset.univ into Finset.range 29 shows that the number of vertices |Finset.univ| is at most |Finset.range 29|. Simplifying cardinalities (simpa) yields |V| ≤ 29.
steps.code:
have := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn _ hmaps (htd.injOn)
  simpa using this

glossary.simple_graph_triangle_degree_le_choose: In any simple graph, the triangle-degree of a vertex v is at most C(degree(v), 2), the number of pairs of its neighbors.
glossary.Finset.mem_range: A natural number m belongs to Finset.range n if and only if m < n.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn: If a function maps a finite set s into a finite set t injectively, then |s| ≤ |t|.

declarations.name: tournament_of_symm_matrix
declarations.informal: The tournament T(G) of a symmetric n × n matrix G over F₂, on vertices 1, …, n: for i < j the arc goes i → j if G_ij = 0 and j → i if G_ij = 1.
declarations.statement:
def tournament_of_symm_matrix {n : ℕ} (G : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2)) :
    Digraph (Fin n)
declarations.source:
/-- The tournament `T(G)` of a matrix over `𝔽₂`: for `i < j` the arc is `i → j` when
`G i j = 0` and `j → i` when `G i j = 1`. -/
def tournament_of_symm_matrix {n : ℕ} (G : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2)) :
    Digraph (Fin n) where
  Adj i j := (i < j ∧ G i j = 0) ∨ (j < i ∧ G j i = 1)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.13798 (On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins), Sec. 2.2 / Proposition 3.1 (the tournament T(G) of a symmetric matrix).

declarations.name: lower_ones_matrix
declarations.informal: The n × n lower triangular matrix L over F₂ with all entries on and below the diagonal equal to 1: L_ij = 1 iff j ≤ i.
declarations.statement: def lower_ones_matrix (n : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.13798 (On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins), Sec. 3 (the matrix L of Proposition 3.1).

declarations.name: tournament_of_symm_matrix_is_tournament
declarations.informal: T(G) is a tournament for every matrix G over F₂ (only the entries above the diagonal are read).
declarations.statement:
theorem tournament_of_symm_matrix_is_tournament {n : ℕ} (G : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2)) :
    digraph_is_tournament (tournament_of_symm_matrix G)
declarations.source:
theorem tournament_of_symm_matrix_is_tournament {n : ℕ} (G : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2)) :
    digraph_is_tournament (tournament_of_symm_matrix G) := by
  have two : ∀ a : ZMod 2, a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by decide
  refine ⟨fun i => ?_, fun i j hij => ?_⟩
  · simp [tournament_of_symm_matrix]
  · simp only [tournament_of_symm_matrix]
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hij with h | h
    · rcases two (G i j) with h0 | h0 <;> simp [h, h0, not_lt_of_gt h]
    · rcases two (G j i) with h0 | h0 <;> simp [h, h0, not_lt_of_gt h]

explanation.summary: To show that the graph defined by G is a tournament, the proof checks that there are no self-loops and that between any two distinct vertices exactly one directed edge is present. The absence of self-loops holds because adjacency requires a strict inequality between vertex indices, which is impossible for a vertex and itself. For distinct vertices i ≠ j, trichotomy divides into the cases i < j and j < i; in each case, whether the corresponding matrix entry is 0 or 1 uniquely determines which of the two directed edges is present.

steps.claim: Every element of ℤ/2ℤ is either 0 or 1.
steps.explanation: Since ℤ/2ℤ has only two elements, the disjunction a = 0 ∨ a = 1 holds for all elements by finite exhaustion, verified by decide.
steps.code: have two : ∀ a : ZMod 2, a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by decide

steps.claim: To show that the constructed graph is a tournament, it suffices to prove that it has no self-loops and that between any two distinct vertices there is a directed edge in exactly one direction.
steps.explanation: By definition, a directed graph is a tournament (digraph_is_tournament) if no vertex has a self-loop (∀ i, ¬ Adj i i) and for all distinct pairs i ≠ j, having an edge from i to j is equivalent to not having an edge from j to i (Adj i j ↔ ¬ Adj j i). We split the proof into these two independent goals.
steps.code: refine ⟨fun i => ?_, fun i j hij => ?_⟩

steps.claim: The graph contains no self-loops.
steps.explanation: By definition of tournament_of_symm_matrix, an edge from i to j requires either i < j or j < i. When i = j, the strict inequality i < i is false in both disjuncts, so ¬ Adj i i holds immediately.
steps.code: · simp [tournament_of_symm_matrix]

steps.claim: For distinct vertices i ≠ j, it suffices to consider separately the cases i < j and j < i.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of adjacency between i and j, we must show that (i < j ∧ G i j = 0 ∨ j < i ∧ G j i = 1) is equivalent to ¬ (j < i ∧ G j i = 0 ∨ i < j ∧ G i j = 1). Since i ≠ j, totality of the linear order on Fin n gives either i < j or j < i.
steps.code:
· simp only [tournament_of_symm_matrix]
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hij with h | h

steps.claim: When i < j, exactly one directed edge connects i and j.
steps.explanation: Since i < j, the reverse inequality j < i is false (by not_lt_of_gt). The matrix entry G i j must be either 0 or 1: if G i j = 0, then the directed edge (i, j) exists and (j, i) does not; if G i j = 1, then (i, j) does not exist and (j, i) does. In both cases, the equivalence holds.
steps.code: · rcases two (G i j) with h0 | h0 <;> simp [h, h0, not_lt_of_gt h]

steps.claim: When j < i, exactly one directed edge connects i and j.
steps.explanation: Symmetrically, since j < i, the reverse inequality i < j is false (by not_lt_of_gt). The matrix entry G j i is either 0 or 1: if G j i = 0, the edge (j, i) exists and (i, j) does not; if G j i = 1, the edge (i, j) exists and (j, i) does not. In both cases, the equivalence holds.
steps.code: · rcases two (G j i) with h0 | h0 <;> simp [h, h0, not_lt_of_gt h]

glossary.lt_or_gt_of_ne: In a linear order, any two distinct elements satisfy a < b or b < a.
glossary.not_lt_of_gt: In a preorder, if a < b then b < a is false.

declarations.name: lower_ones_matrix_apply_self
declarations.informal: The diagonal entries of L are 1.
declarations.statement: theorem lower_ones_matrix_apply_self (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) : lower_ones_matrix n i i = 1
declarations.source:
theorem lower_ones_matrix_apply_self (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) : lower_ones_matrix n i i = 1 := by
  simp [lower_ones_matrix]

explanation.summary: The proof unfolds the definition of `lower_ones_matrix` at the diagonal entry (i, i). Because i ≤ i holds reflexively for any index i, the conditional expression if i ≤ i then 1 else 0 simplifies directly to 1.

steps.claim: lower_ones_matrix n i i = 1
steps.explanation: The simplifier unfolds the definition of `lower_ones_matrix`, which evaluates the entry at (i, i) to `if i ≤ i then 1 else 0`. Since the inequality i ≤ i holds by reflexivity, the `if` condition is true, simplifying the expression to 1.
steps.code: simp [lower_ones_matrix]

declarations.name: tournament_min_rank_dijoin_le_of_symm_inv
declarations.informal: Let B be an invertible symmetric n × n matrix over F₂, L the lower triangular all-ones matrix, and A = L B⁻¹ Lᵀ. Then the tournaments D₁ = T(A) and D₂ = T(B) satisfy tmr(D₁ → D₂) ≤ n.
declarations.statement:
theorem tournament_min_rank_dijoin_le_of_symm_inv (n : ℕ) (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2))
    (hB : B.IsSymm) (hdet : IsUnit B.det) :
    tournament_min_rank (digraph_dijoin
      (tournament_of_symm_matrix (lower_ones_matrix n * B⁻¹ * (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose))
      (tournament_of_symm_matrix B)) ≤ n
declarations.source:
theorem tournament_min_rank_dijoin_le_of_symm_inv (n : ℕ) (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2))
    (hB : B.IsSymm) (hdet : IsUnit B.det) :
    tournament_min_rank (digraph_dijoin
      (tournament_of_symm_matrix (lower_ones_matrix n * B⁻¹ * (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose))
      (tournament_of_symm_matrix B)) ≤ n := by
  have two : ∀ a : ZMod 2, a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by decide
  have hBinvT : (B⁻¹).transpose = B⁻¹ := by rw [Matrix.transpose_nonsing_inv, hB.eq]
  -- the diagonal blocks reverse exactly the arcs of `T(G)` that go downwards
  have diag : ∀ G : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2), G.IsSymm → ∀ i j : Fin n,
      (G i j = 1 ∧ (tournament_of_symm_matrix G).Adj j i) ∨
        (G i j ≠ 1 ∧ (tournament_of_symm_matrix G).Adj i j) → (i : ℕ) < j := by
    intro G hG i j h
    have hs : G j i = G i j := by
      have := congrFun (congrFun hG.eq i) j
      simpa [Matrix.transpose_apply] using this
    simp only [tournament_of_symm_matrix, hs] at h
    rcases two (G i j) with h0 | h0 <;> simp [h0] at h <;>
      exact h
  have hdec : ∀ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2), A.IsSymm →
      digraph_is_acyclic (digraph_flip_by_matrix
        (digraph_dijoin (tournament_of_symm_matrix A) (tournament_of_symm_matrix B))
        (Matrix.fromBlocks A (lower_ones_matrix n) (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose B)) := by
    intro A hA
    apply digraph_is_acyclic_of_rank _
      (Sum.elim (fun i : Fin n => 2 * (i : ℕ) + 1) (fun j : Fin n => 2 * (j : ℕ)))
    intro x y hxy
    rcases x with i | i <;> rcases y with j | j
    · have := diag A hA i j hxy
      simp only [Sum.elim_inl]
      omega
    · rcases hxy with ⟨_, h⟩ | ⟨h, _⟩
      · exact h.elim
      · have hji : ¬ j ≤ i := fun hji => h (by simp [Matrix.fromBlocks, lower_ones_matrix, hji])
        have hij : (i : ℕ) < j := by rw [not_le] at hji; exact hji
        simp only [Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr]
        omega
    · rcases hxy with ⟨h, _⟩ | ⟨_, h⟩
      · have hij : i ≤ j := by
          by_contra hc
          simp [Matrix.fromBlocks, lower_ones_matrix, hc] at h
        have hij' : (i : ℕ) ≤ j := hij
        simp only [Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr]
        omega
      · exact h.elim
    · have := diag B hB i j hxy
      simp only [Sum.elim_inr]
      omega
  -- the rank is at most `n`: the block matrix is `P B Pᵀ` with `P` of width `n`
  have hrank : ∀ L : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2),
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (L * B⁻¹ * L.transpose) L L.transpose B).rank ≤ n := by
    intro L
    have hMP : Matrix.fromBlocks (L * B⁻¹ * L.transpose) L L.transpose B =
        Matrix.fromRows (L * B⁻¹) 1 * B * (Matrix.fromRows (L * B⁻¹) 1).transpose := by
      rw [Matrix.fromRows_mul, Matrix.transpose_fromRows, Matrix.fromRows_mul_fromCols]
      congr 1
      · rw [Matrix.mul_assoc L B⁻¹ B, Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul B hdet, Matrix.mul_one,
          Matrix.transpose_mul, hBinvT, Matrix.mul_assoc]
      · rw [Matrix.transpose_one, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.mul_assoc, Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul B hdet,
          Matrix.mul_one]
      · rw [Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.transpose_mul, hBinvT, ← Matrix.mul_assoc,
          Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv B hdet, Matrix.one_mul]
      · rw [Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.transpose_one, Matrix.mul_one]
    rw [hMP]
    calc _ ≤ (Matrix.fromRows (L * B⁻¹) 1 * B).rank := Matrix.rank_mul_le_left _ _
      _ ≤ (Matrix.fromRows (L * B⁻¹) (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2))).rank :=
          Matrix.rank_mul_le_left _ _
      _ ≤ Fintype.card (Fin n) := Matrix.rank_le_card_width _
      _ = n := Fintype.card_fin n
  have hAs : (lower_ones_matrix n * B⁻¹ * (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose).IsSymm := by
    unfold Matrix.IsSymm
    rw [Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_transpose, hBinvT,
      Matrix.mul_assoc]
  have hMs : (Matrix.fromBlocks (lower_ones_matrix n * B⁻¹ * (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose)
      (lower_ones_matrix n) (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose B).IsSymm :=
    Matrix.IsSymm.fromBlocks hAs rfl hB
  exact le_trans (Nat.sInf_le ⟨_, hMs, hdec _ hAs, rfl⟩) (hrank _)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.13798 (On the failure of additivity of inversion numbers for dijoins), Proposition 3.1. Stated here is the bound tmr(T(A) → T(B)) ≤ n; the proposition's remark that A is again invertible symmetric is not part of the statement (its symmetry is proved inside the proof).

explanation.summary: To bound the tournament minimum rank of the dijoin T(A) → T(B) by n, we construct a 2n × 2n symmetric block matrix M over 𝔽₂ whose blocks are A = L B⁻¹ Lᵀ, L, Lᵀ, and B. We show that flipping the dijoin along M yields an acyclic tournament using an explicit potential function that assigns odd values 2i + 1 to vertices in T(A) and even values 2j to vertices in T(B). Finally, factoring M as P B Pᵀ for a 2n × n matrix P bounds the rank of M by n, which upper bounds the minimum rank.

steps.claim: The field 𝔽₂ has only two elements (0 and 1), and the inverse matrix B⁻¹ is symmetric.
steps.explanation: Every element of ℤ/2ℤ is decided to be either 0 or 1. Since B is symmetric and invertible, its inverse B⁻¹ is also symmetric because transposition commutes with matrix inversion for invertible matrices.
steps.code:
have two : ∀ a : ZMod 2, a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by decide
  have hBinvT : (B⁻¹).transpose = B⁻¹ := by rw [Matrix.transpose_nonsing_inv, hB.eq]

steps.claim: For any symmetric matrix G, flipping the tournament T(G) by G directs all edges towards larger indices: any arc i → j in the flipped graph satisfies i < j.
steps.explanation: By symmetry, G j i = G i j. By definition, T(G) has an arc i → j if either i < j with G i j = 0, or j < i with G j i = 1. Flipping T(G) by G keeps or reverses each edge depending on whether G i j = 1 or G i j ≠ 1. In both cases (G i j = 0 and G i j = 1), the condition simplifies directly to i < j.
steps.code:
have diag : ∀ G : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2), G.IsSymm → ∀ i j : Fin n,
      (G i j = 1 ∧ (tournament_of_symm_matrix G).Adj j i) ∨
        (G i j ≠ 1 ∧ (tournament_of_symm_matrix G).Adj i j) → (i : ℕ) < j := by
    intro G hG i j h
    have hs : G j i = G i j := by
      have := congrFun (congrFun hG.eq i) j
      simpa [Matrix.transpose_apply] using this
    simp only [tournament_of_symm_matrix, hs] at h
    rcases two (G i j) with h0 | h0 <;> simp [h0] at h <;>
      exact h

steps.claim: For any symmetric matrix A, flipping the dijoin tournament T(A) → T(B) by the block matrix M = [A, L; Lᵀ, B] produces an acyclic directed graph.
steps.explanation:
We show acyclicity by exhibiting a ranking function f strictly increasing along every edge of the flipped graph, mapping inl i to 2i + 1 and inr j to 2j. We analyze an edge x → y in the flipped graph by cases on where x and y lie:
1. Both in T(A): the edge is in the flipped T(A), so i < j by the diagonal block property, which implies 2i + 1 < 2j + 1.
2. x in T(A) and y in T(B): the dijoin contains no reverse edges from inr to inl, so this edge must be an unflipped forward edge with matrix entry L i j ≠ 1. By definition of L, this requires ¬(j ≤ i), so i < j, which yields 2i + 1 < 2j.
3. x in T(B) and y in T(A): the dijoin has no edges from inr to inl, so this edge must arise from flipping an existing forward dijoin edge from inl to inr with matrix entry Lᵀ i j = L j i = 1. By definition of L, this requires i ≤ j, which gives 2i < 2j + 1.
4. Both in T(B): the edge is in the flipped T(B), so i < j by the diagonal block property, which implies 2i < 2j.
In every case, f(x) < f(y), so the flipped graph is acyclic.
steps.code:
have hdec : ∀ A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2), A.IsSymm →
      digraph_is_acyclic (digraph_flip_by_matrix
        (digraph_dijoin (tournament_of_symm_matrix A) (tournament_of_symm_matrix B))
        (Matrix.fromBlocks A (lower_ones_matrix n) (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose B)) := by
    intro A hA
    apply digraph_is_acyclic_of_rank _
      (Sum.elim (fun i : Fin n => 2 * (i : ℕ) + 1) (fun j : Fin n => 2 * (j : ℕ)))
    intro x y hxy
    rcases x with i | i <;> rcases y with j | j
    · have := diag A hA i j hxy
      simp only [Sum.elim_inl]
      omega
    · rcases hxy with ⟨_, h⟩ | ⟨h, _⟩
      · exact h.elim
      · have hji : ¬ j ≤ i := fun hji => h (by simp [Matrix.fromBlocks, lower_ones_matrix, hji])
        have hij : (i : ℕ) < j := by rw [not_le] at hji; exact hji
        simp only [Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr]
        omega
    · rcases hxy with ⟨h, _⟩ | ⟨_, h⟩
      · have hij : i ≤ j := by
          by_contra hc
          simp [Matrix.fromBlocks, lower_ones_matrix, hc] at h
        have hij' : (i : ℕ) ≤ j := hij
        simp only [Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr]
        omega
      · exact h.elim
    · have := diag B hB i j hxy
      simp only [Sum.elim_inr]
      omega

steps.claim: For any matrix L, the block matrix [L B⁻¹ Lᵀ, L; Lᵀ, B] has rank at most n.
steps.explanation: The block matrix factors as P * B * Pᵀ, where P = [L B⁻¹; I] is the 2n × n matrix obtained by stacking L B⁻¹ above the identity matrix I. Expanding the block multiplication and using B⁻¹ * B = I, B * B⁻¹ = I, and (B⁻¹)ᵀ = B⁻¹ verifies that the four blocks match. The rank of P * B * Pᵀ is bounded by the rank of P, and since P has width n, its rank is at most n.
steps.code:
have hrank : ∀ L : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2),
      (Matrix.fromBlocks (L * B⁻¹ * L.transpose) L L.transpose B).rank ≤ n := by
    intro L
    have hMP : Matrix.fromBlocks (L * B⁻¹ * L.transpose) L L.transpose B =
        Matrix.fromRows (L * B⁻¹) 1 * B * (Matrix.fromRows (L * B⁻¹) 1).transpose := by
      rw [Matrix.fromRows_mul, Matrix.transpose_fromRows, Matrix.fromRows_mul_fromCols]
      congr 1
      · rw [Matrix.mul_assoc L B⁻¹ B, Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul B hdet, Matrix.mul_one,
          Matrix.transpose_mul, hBinvT, Matrix.mul_assoc]
      · rw [Matrix.transpose_one, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.mul_assoc, Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul B hdet,
          Matrix.mul_one]
      · rw [Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.transpose_mul, hBinvT, ← Matrix.mul_assoc,
          Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv B hdet, Matrix.one_mul]
      · rw [Matrix.one_mul, Matrix.transpose_one, Matrix.mul_one]
    rw [hMP]
    calc _ ≤ (Matrix.fromRows (L * B⁻¹) 1 * B).rank := Matrix.rank_mul_le_left _ _
      _ ≤ (Matrix.fromRows (L * B⁻¹) (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (ZMod 2))).rank :=
          Matrix.rank_mul_le_left _ _
      _ ≤ Fintype.card (Fin n) := Matrix.rank_le_card_width _
      _ = n := Fintype.card_fin n

steps.claim: The block matrix M = [L B⁻¹ Lᵀ, L; Lᵀ, B] is symmetric, certifying that the tournament minimum rank of the dijoin is at most n.
steps.explanation: The matrix A = L B⁻¹ Lᵀ is symmetric because Aᵀ = (Lᵀ)ᵀ (B⁻¹)ᵀ Lᵀ = L B⁻¹ Lᵀ = A. Therefore, the block matrix M is symmetric because its diagonal blocks A and B are symmetric and its off-diagonal blocks are mutual transposes. Since M is symmetric and flips the dijoin tournament into an acyclic graph, its rank belongs to the set whose infimum defines the tournament minimum rank. Because the rank of M is at most n, the infimum is at most n as well.
steps.code:
have hAs : (lower_ones_matrix n * B⁻¹ * (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose).IsSymm := by
    unfold Matrix.IsSymm
    rw [Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_mul, Matrix.transpose_transpose, hBinvT,
      Matrix.mul_assoc]
  have hMs : (Matrix.fromBlocks (lower_ones_matrix n * B⁻¹ * (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose)
      (lower_ones_matrix n) (lower_ones_matrix n).transpose B).IsSymm :=
    Matrix.IsSymm.fromBlocks hAs rfl hB
  exact le_trans (Nat.sInf_le ⟨_, hMs, hdec _ hAs, rfl⟩) (hrank _)

glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The number of elements in Fin n is n.
glossary.Matrix.IsSymm.fromBlocks: A 2 × 2 block matrix is symmetric if its diagonal blocks are symmetric and each off-diagonal block is the transpose of the other.
glossary.Matrix.fromRows_mul_fromCols: Multiplying a column of two blocks by a row of two blocks results in the corresponding 2 × 2 block matrix of products.
glossary.Matrix.fromRows_mul: Multiplying a two-row block matrix by a matrix on the right distributes to each block row.
glossary.Matrix.mul_assoc: Matrix multiplication is associative: (L * M) * N = L * (M * N).
glossary.Matrix.mul_nonsing_inv: Multiplying an invertible matrix on the right by its inverse gives the identity matrix.
glossary.Matrix.mul_one: Multiplying any matrix on the right by the identity matrix leaves it unchanged.
glossary.Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul: Multiplying an invertible matrix on the left by its inverse gives the identity matrix.
glossary.Matrix.one_mul: Multiplying any matrix on the left by the identity matrix leaves it unchanged.
glossary.Matrix.rank_le_card_width: The rank of a matrix is at most the number of its columns.
glossary.Matrix.rank_mul_le_left: The rank of a matrix product A * B is at most the rank of the left factor A.
glossary.Matrix.transpose_apply: The (i, j)-entry of the transpose of a matrix M is the (j, i)-entry of M.
glossary.Matrix.transpose_fromRows: The transpose of a matrix formed by stacking two block rows is formed by stacking the transposes of the blocks as columns.
glossary.Matrix.transpose_mul: The transpose of a matrix product is the product of the transposes in reverse order: (M * N)ᵀ = Nᵀ * Mᵀ.
glossary.Matrix.transpose_nonsing_inv: For any invertible matrix, the transpose of its inverse is the inverse of its transpose.
glossary.Matrix.transpose_one: The transpose of the identity matrix is the identity matrix.
glossary.Matrix.transpose_transpose: Taking the transpose of a matrix twice yields the original matrix: (Mᵀ)ᵀ = M.
glossary.Nat.sInf_le: The infimum of a set of natural numbers is at most any element of that set.
glossary.Sum.elim_inl: Applying a function defined on a disjoint union by cases to a left-injected element yields the value of the left case function.
glossary.Sum.elim_inr: Applying a function defined on a disjoint union by cases to a right-injected element yields the value of the right case function.
glossary.congrFun: If two functions are equal, then their evaluations at any given argument are equal.
glossary.digraph_is_acyclic_of_rank: A directed graph is acyclic if there exists a ranking function into the natural numbers that strictly increases along every directed edge.
glossary.le_trans: The less-than-or-equal relation is transitive: if a ≤ b and b ≤ c, then a ≤ c.
glossary.not_le: For elements of a linear order, a is not less than or equal to b if and only if b < a.

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_k_independent
declarations.informal: A vertex set I of a graph G is k-independent when the induced subgraph G[I] has maximum degree less than k: every vertex of I has fewer than k neighbours in I.
declarations.statement: def simple_graph_is_k_independent {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) (I : Finset V) : Prop
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Sec. 1 (k-independent set: Δ(G[I]) < k).

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_k_star_forming
declarations.informal: A vertex set S is k-star-forming when, for every vertex v outside S, the induced graph G[S ∪ {v}] contains a copy of the star K_{1,k} that contains v (v as the centre or as a leaf).
declarations.statement: def simple_graph_is_k_star_forming {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) (S : Finset V) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A vertex set `S` is `k`-star-forming when every `v ∉ S` lies in a copy of `K_{1,k}` in `G[S ∪ {v}]`. -/
def simple_graph_is_k_star_forming {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) (S : Finset V) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, v ∉ S → ∃ c : V, ∃ L : Finset V, (c = v ∨ c ∈ S) ∧ (∀ x ∈ L, x = v ∨ x ∈ S) ∧
    L.card = k ∧ (∀ x ∈ L, G.Adj c x) ∧ (v = c ∨ v ∈ L)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Definition 2.1.

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming
declarations.informal: A minimal k-star-forming set: a k-star-forming set no proper subset of which is k-star-forming.
declarations.statement:
def simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ)
    (S : Finset V) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A minimal `k`-star-forming set: `k`-star-forming, and no proper subset is. -/
def simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ)
    (S : Finset V) : Prop :=
  simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k S ∧ ∀ T ⊂ S, ¬ simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k T
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Definition 2.1 (minimality).

declarations.name: simple_graph_k_independence_number
declarations.informal: β_k(G): the maximum cardinality of a k-independent vertex set of G.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def simple_graph_k_independence_number {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Sec. 1 (β_k).

declarations.name: simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number
declarations.informal: SF_k(G): the maximum cardinality of a minimal k-star-forming vertex set of G.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (k : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- `SF_k(G)`: the maximum cardinality of a minimal `k`-star-forming vertex set. -/
noncomputable def simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {n | ∃ S : Finset V, simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming G k S ∧ S.card = n}
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Definition 2.1 (SF_k).

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_k_independent_empty
declarations.informal: The empty vertex set is k-independent, for every k.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_independent_empty {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) :
    simple_graph_is_k_independent G k ∅
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_independent_empty {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) :
    simple_graph_is_k_independent G k ∅ := by
  intro v hv; simp at hv
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for the definition of k-independence, arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination).

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by vacuous truth. By definition, a subset of vertices is $k$-independent if each of its vertices has fewer than $k$ neighbors in the subset. Since the empty set contains no vertices, this condition holds trivially.

steps.claim: The neighborhood cardinality condition holds vacuously for all vertices in the empty set.
steps.explanation: By definition, a vertex set is $k$-independent if every vertex in the set has strictly fewer than $k$ neighbors within the set. Assuming there is a vertex $v \in \emptyset$ (introduced as `hv`), the simplifier recognizes that the empty set has no elements, turning the assumption into `False` and completing the proof by contradiction.
steps.code: intro v hv; simp at hv

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_univ
declarations.informal: In a finite graph the whole vertex set is k-star-forming, for every k (there is no vertex outside it).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_univ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) :
    simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k Finset.univ
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_univ {V : Type*} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) :
    simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k Finset.univ := by
  intro v hv; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ v) hv
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for the definition of k-star-forming sets, arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination).

explanation.summary: The property of being k-star-forming requires a certain condition for every vertex outside the given set S. When S is the full vertex set Finset.univ, there are no vertices outside S, as every vertex belongs to Finset.univ. The condition is therefore vacuously satisfied.

steps.claim: The universal set Finset.univ is vacuously k-star-forming for any k.
steps.explanation: By definition, a vertex set S is k-star-forming if every vertex v ∉ S can be extended to a k-star. For S = Finset.univ, suppose there were some vertex v ∉ Finset.univ (hv). But by Finset.mem_univ, every vertex v of the finite type V belongs to Finset.univ, which directly contradicts hv. From this contradiction, the condition holds vacuously.
steps.code: intro v hv; exact absurd (Finset.mem_univ v) hv

glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to its universal finset Finset.univ.
