declarations.name: simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_mono
declarations.informal: Every superset of a k-star-forming set is k-star-forming.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_mono {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (k : ℕ) {S T : Finset V} (hST : S ⊆ T) (hS : simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k S) :
    simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k T
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_mono {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (k : ℕ) {S T : Finset V} (hST : S ⊆ T) (hS : simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k S) :
    simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k T := by
  intro v hv
  obtain ⟨c, L, hc, hL, hcard, hadj, hvc⟩ := hS v (fun h => hv (hST h))
  exact ⟨c, L, hc.imp_right (fun h => hST h), fun x hx => (hL x hx).imp_right (fun h => hST h),
    hcard, hadj, hvc⟩
declarations.citation: Monotonicity used implicitly in arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination) (Lemma 2.2 and the minimality arguments).

explanation.summary: To show that any superset T of a k-star-forming set S is also k-star-forming, take any vertex v ∉ T. Because S ⊆ T, v also lies outside S, so by hypothesis there is a k-star containing v whose center and leaves lie in {v} ∪ S. Since S ⊆ T, these vertices also lie in {v} ∪ T, fulfilling the definition for T.

steps.claim: Fix an arbitrary vertex v ∉ T
steps.explanation: To show that T is k-star-forming, let v be any vertex not in T.
steps.code: intro v hv

steps.claim: There exist a center c and a leaf set L forming a k-star at v with vertices in {v} ∪ S
steps.explanation: Since S ⊆ T and v ∉ T, we have v ∉ S. Applying the k-star-forming property of S to v yields a center c and a leaf set L of size k such that all vertices belong to {v} ∪ S, each leaf is adjacent to c, and v is either c or one of the leaves.
steps.code: obtain ⟨c, L, hc, hL, hcard, hadj, hvc⟩ := hS v (fun h => hv (hST h))

steps.claim: The pair (c, L) satisfies the k-star-forming conditions for T
steps.explanation: Since S ⊆ T, any vertex in {v} ∪ S is also in {v} ∪ T. Using Or.imp_right on the memberships hc and hL shows c ∈ {v} ∪ T and L ⊆ {v} ∪ T, while the cardinality, adjacency, and incidence conditions remain identical.
steps.code:
exact ⟨c, L, hc.imp_right (fun h => hST h), fun x hx => (hL x hx).imp_right (fun h => hST h),
    hcard, hadj, hvc⟩

glossary.Or.imp_right: if b implies c, then a ∨ b implies a ∨ c

declarations.name: simple_graph_k_independent_is_k_independent_one_iff
declarations.informal: A vertex set is 1-independent exactly when it is independent: no two of its vertices are adjacent.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_k_independent_is_k_independent_one_iff {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (I : Finset V) :
    simple_graph_is_k_independent G 1 I ↔ ∀ u ∈ I, ∀ v ∈ I, ¬ G.Adj u v
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_k_independent_is_k_independent_one_iff {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (I : Finset V) :
    simple_graph_is_k_independent G 1 I ↔ ∀ u ∈ I, ∀ v ∈ I, ¬ G.Adj u v := by
  unfold simple_graph_is_k_independent
  have hfin : ∀ u, ({w | w ∈ I ∧ G.Adj u w} : Set V).Finite :=
    fun u => I.finite_toSet.subset (fun w hw => hw.1)
  constructor
  · intro h u hu v hv huv
    have := h u hu
    rw [Nat.lt_one_iff, Set.ncard_eq_zero (hfin u)] at this
    have hmem : v ∈ ({w | w ∈ I ∧ G.Adj u w} : Set V) := ⟨hv, huv⟩
    rw [this] at hmem
    exact hmem
  · intro h u hu
    rw [Nat.lt_one_iff, Set.ncard_eq_zero (hfin u), Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    exact fun v hv => h u hu v hv.1 hv.2
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma: β_1 = α, as noted in arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Sec. 2 (1).

explanation.summary: A set of vertices I is defined to be 1-independent if every vertex in I has strictly fewer than 1 neighbor in I. Because cardinality is a natural number and the neighbor set is finite, having fewer than 1 neighbor is equivalent to the neighbor set being empty. The proof splits the equivalence into two directions: if I is 1-independent, any adjacent pair in I would produce an element in an empty set; conversely, if no two vertices in I are adjacent, the neighbor set of any vertex is empty and thus has cardinality zero.

steps.claim: For every vertex u, the set of its neighbors in I is finite.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of 1-independence, the condition requires that each vertex in I has fewer than 1 neighbor in I. For each vertex u, the set {w ∈ I | G.Adj u w} of its neighbors in I is a subset of the finite set I, and is therefore finite.
steps.code:
unfold simple_graph_is_k_independent
  have hfin : ∀ u, ({w | w ∈ I ∧ G.Adj u w} : Set V).Finite :=
    fun u => I.finite_toSet.subset (fun w hw => hw.1)

steps.claim: If I is 1-independent, then no two vertices in I are adjacent.
steps.explanation: We split the if-and-only-if into two implications. For the forward direction, assume I is 1-independent, and suppose for contradiction that some u, v ∈ I are adjacent. By 1-independence, the number of neighbors of u in I is strictly less than 1. By Nat.lt_one_iff and Set.ncard_eq_zero, this cardinality being less than 1 means it is 0, so the neighbor set of u in I is empty. However, v is in I and adjacent to u, which places v in this neighbor set, contradicting the fact that it is empty.
steps.code:
constructor
  · intro h u hu v hv huv
    have := h u hu
    rw [Nat.lt_one_iff, Set.ncard_eq_zero (hfin u)] at this
    have hmem : v ∈ ({w | w ∈ I ∧ G.Adj u w} : Set V) := ⟨hv, huv⟩
    rw [this] at hmem
    exact hmem

steps.claim: If no two vertices in I are adjacent, then I is 1-independent.
steps.explanation: For the reverse direction, assume no two vertices in I are adjacent. Given any vertex u ∈ I, we must show that its neighbor set in I has cardinality strictly less than 1. Rewriting with Nat.lt_one_iff, Set.ncard_eq_zero, and Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem, this is equivalent to showing that no vertex belongs to this neighbor set. If some v belonged to it, then v would be in I and adjacent to u, which directly contradicts our assumption.
steps.code:
· intro h u hu
    rw [Nat.lt_one_iff, Set.ncard_eq_zero (hfin u), Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    exact fun v hv => h u hu v hv.1 hv.2

glossary.Nat.lt_one_iff: A natural number is strictly less than 1 if and only if it equals 0.
glossary.Set.ncard_eq_zero: A finite set has cardinality 0 if and only if it is the empty set.
glossary.Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem: A set is empty if and only if no element belongs to it.

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_chain_graph
declarations.informal: G is a chain graph with bipartition (A, V \ A): every edge joins A to its complement, and the neighbourhoods of the vertices of A are totally ordered by inclusion.
declarations.statement: def simple_graph_is_chain_graph {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (A : Set V) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A chain graph with bipartition `(A, Aᶜ)`: bipartite, with the neighbourhoods of the vertices of `A` nested. -/
def simple_graph_is_chain_graph {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (A : Set V) : Prop :=
  (∀ u v, G.Adj u v → (u ∈ A ↔ v ∉ A)) ∧
    ∀ a₁ ∈ A, ∀ a₂ ∈ A, G.neighborSet a₁ ⊆ G.neighborSet a₂ ∨ G.neighborSet a₂ ⊆ G.neighborSet a₁
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Sec. 6 (chain graphs: bipartite graphs whose neighbourhoods on one side are nested).

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_chain_graph_complete_bipartite
declarations.informal: The complete bipartite graph K_{a,b} is a chain graph (all vertices on one side have the same neighbourhood).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_chain_graph_complete_bipartite (a b : ℕ) :
    simple_graph_is_chain_graph (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b)) (Set.range Sum.inl)
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_chain_graph_complete_bipartite (a b : ℕ) :
    simple_graph_is_chain_graph (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b)) (Set.range Sum.inl) := by
  constructor
  · rintro (u | u) (v | v) h <;> simp_all
  · rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩ _ ⟨y, rfl⟩
    left
    intro w hw
    rcases w with w | w <;> simp_all
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for the definition of chain graphs, arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination).

explanation.summary: To show that the complete bipartite graph $K_{a,b}$ is a chain graph with respect to the left part $A = \operatorname{range}(\operatorname{inl})$, the proof verifies the two defining conditions: bipartiteness and nested neighborhoods. First, a case analysis on the sides of two adjacent vertices confirms that edges only connect vertices on opposite sides. Second, because every vertex on the left has the exact same neighborhood (the entire right side), any two left vertices have identical neighborhoods, which trivially implies that one neighborhood is a subset of the other.

steps.claim: The goal reduces to proving bipartiteness and the nested neighborhood property for vertices in $A = \operatorname{range}(\operatorname{inl})$.
steps.explanation: By definition, a graph is a chain graph with respect to a vertex subset $A$ if (1) every edge connects a vertex in $A$ to a vertex outside $A$, and (2) for any two vertices in $A$, their neighborhoods are totally ordered by inclusion. Splitting the conjunction produces these two subgoals.
steps.code: constructor

steps.claim: Every edge in the complete bipartite graph connects a vertex in $A$ to a vertex outside $A$.
steps.explanation: We consider the four cases for the parts containing adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$. If both lie in the left part $\operatorname{Fin}(a)$ or both in the right part $\operatorname{Fin}(b)$, they cannot be adjacent by definition of the complete bipartite graph, which contradicts the edge hypothesis. If one lies on the left and the other on the right, exactly one belongs to $A = \operatorname{range}(\operatorname{inl})$, so $u \in A \iff v \notin A$ holds in both cross cases.
steps.code: · rintro (u | u) (v | v) h <;> simp_all

steps.claim: For any two vertices $\operatorname{inl}(x), \operatorname{inl}(y) \in A$, it suffices to show that the neighborhood of $\operatorname{inl}(x)$ is a subset of the neighborhood of $\operatorname{inl}(y)$.
steps.explanation: Any vertices in $A = \operatorname{range}(\operatorname{inl})$ can be written as $\operatorname{inl}(x)$ and $\operatorname{inl}(y)$ for some $x, y \in \operatorname{Fin}(a)$. To establish that one neighborhood is contained in the other, we choose the forward inclusion $N(\operatorname{inl}(x)) \subseteq N(\operatorname{inl}(y))$.
steps.code:
· rintro _ ⟨x, rfl⟩ _ ⟨y, rfl⟩
    left

steps.claim: Every neighbor of $\operatorname{inl}(x)$ is also a neighbor of $\operatorname{inl}(y)$.
steps.explanation: Let $w$ be a neighbor of $\operatorname{inl}(x)$. We case-split on whether $w$ belongs to the left or right part. If $w = \operatorname{inl}(w')$, both $w$ and $\operatorname{inl}(x)$ lie in the left part, contradicting their adjacency. Thus $w = \operatorname{inr}(w')$ lies in the right part, and by the definition of the complete bipartite graph, it is adjacent to every vertex in the left part, in particular to $\operatorname{inl}(y)$.
steps.code:
intro w hw
    rcases w with w | w <;> simp_all

caveats: The automated tactic `simp_all` discharges several cases by unfolding the definitions of `completeBipartiteGraph` and `Set.range Sum.inl`, identifying that there are no edges within a part and that every cross-part pair is adjacent.

declarations.name: greedy_distinct_diff_next
declarations.informal: Given the terms so far (most recent first), the next greedy term: the least positive integer not used yet whose absolute difference with the last term differs from every consecutive difference so far.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def greedy_distinct_diff_next (l : List ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- The next term of the greedy sequence with distinct consecutive differences. -/
noncomputable def greedy_distinct_diff_next (l : List ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {c : ℕ | 0 < c ∧ c ∉ l ∧
    Int.natAbs ((c : ℤ) - l.headD 0) ∉ (l.zip l.tail).map (fun p => Int.natAbs ((p.1 : ℤ) - p.2))}
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.15860 (A note on the Slater–Vélez permutation), first paragraph (the greedy rule), and the 1977 paper it cites, 'Permutations of the positive integers with restrictions on the sequence of differences'.

declarations.name: greedy_distinct_diff_history
declarations.informal: The first n + 2 terms of the greedy sequence started at a₁, a₂, most recent first.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def greedy_distinct_diff_history (a₁ a₂ : ℕ) : ℕ → List ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- The first `n + 2` terms of the greedy sequence started at `a₁, a₂`, most recent first. -/
noncomputable def greedy_distinct_diff_history (a₁ a₂ : ℕ) : ℕ → List ℕ
  | 0 => [a₂, a₁]
  | n + 1 => greedy_distinct_diff_next (greedy_distinct_diff_history a₁ a₂ n) ::
      greedy_distinct_diff_history a₁ a₂ n
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.15860 (A note on the Slater–Vélez permutation), first paragraph (the greedy rule, here with arbitrary starting terms).

declarations.name: greedy_distinct_diff_seq
declarations.informal: The greedy sequence with distinct consecutive differences started at a₁, a₂ (term 0 is a₁, term 1 is a₂; each later term is the least unused positive integer whose difference with the previous term is new).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def greedy_distinct_diff_seq (a₁ a₂ : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- The greedy sequence with distinct consecutive differences started at `a₁, a₂` (0-indexed). -/
noncomputable def greedy_distinct_diff_seq (a₁ a₂ : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => a₁
  | n + 1 => (greedy_distinct_diff_history a₁ a₂ n).headD 0
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.15860 (A note on the Slater–Vélez permutation), first paragraph (the greedy rule, here with arbitrary starting terms).

declarations.name: greedy_distinct_diff_seq_one_two_two
declarations.informal: The greedy sequence started at 1, 2 has third term 4 (3 is refused since |3 − 2| = 1 is already a difference).
declarations.statement: theorem greedy_distinct_diff_seq_one_two_two : greedy_distinct_diff_seq 1 2 2 = 4
declarations.source:
theorem greedy_distinct_diff_seq_one_two_two : greedy_distinct_diff_seq 1 2 2 = 4 := by
  show greedy_distinct_diff_next [2, 1] = 4
  unfold greedy_distinct_diff_next
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply Nat.sInf_le
    simp
  · apply le_csInf ⟨4, by simp⟩
    rintro c ⟨hc0, hc1, hc2⟩
    simp at hc1 hc2
    omega
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for the definition of the greedy sequence, arXiv:2610.15860 (A note on the Slater–Vélez permutation) (the sequence 1, 2, 4, 7, 3, 8, …).

explanation.summary: The greedy sequence started at 1, 2 chooses at step 2 the smallest positive integer not in {1, 2} whose distance from the preceding term 2 is not equal to |2 − 1| = 1. The proof unfolds this definition to an infimum of admissible candidates and shows it equals 4 by antisymmetry. The upper bound holds because 4 belongs to the candidate set, while the lower bound holds because candidates cannot be 1 or 2 (already used) or 3 (giving duplicate difference |3 − 2| = 1), forcing every candidate to be at least 4.

steps.claim: The goal reduces to showing that the infimum of the admissible candidate set after sequence [2, 1] is 4.
steps.explanation: By definition, the third term of the greedy sequence (at index 2) is the greedy choice following the history [2, 1]. Unfolding `greedy_distinct_diff_next`, this choice is defined as the infimum of all positive integers c that do not already appear in [2, 1] and whose absolute difference with 2 is not equal to any existing consecutive difference (the only existing difference being |2 − 1| = 1).
steps.code:
show greedy_distinct_diff_next [2, 1] = 4
  unfold greedy_distinct_diff_next

steps.claim: It suffices to prove sInf S ≤ 4 and 4 ≤ sInf S.
steps.explanation: By the antisymmetry of the partial order on natural numbers (`le_antisymm`), establishing equality reduces to proving the two inequalities.
steps.code: apply le_antisymm

steps.claim: sInf S ≤ 4.
steps.explanation: By `Nat.sInf_le`, the infimum of a set of natural numbers is at most any element of the set. Simplification verifies that 4 satisfies all membership conditions: 0 < 4, 4 ∉ [2, 1], and |4 − 2| = 2 ≠ 1.
steps.code:
· apply Nat.sInf_le
    simp

steps.claim: 4 ≤ sInf S.
steps.explanation: By `le_csInf`, a lower bound on every element of a nonempty set is a lower bound on its infimum; nonemptiness is witnessed by 4 ∈ S. For any candidate c in the set, simplifying its defining conditions gives c > 0, c ≠ 1, c ≠ 2, and |c − 2| ≠ 1. This rules out 1, 2, and 3, which implies 4 ≤ c by linear integer arithmetic (`omega`).
steps.code:
· apply le_csInf ⟨4, by simp⟩
    rintro c ⟨hc0, hc1, hc2⟩
    simp at hc1 hc2
    omega

glossary.le_antisymm: In a partial order, if a ≤ b and b ≤ a, then a = b.
glossary.Nat.sInf_le: If an element m belongs to a set of natural numbers s, then the infimum of s is at most m.
glossary.le_csInf: In a conditionally complete lattice, if a set s is nonempty and a is a lower bound for s, then a ≤ sInf s.

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_iff
declarations.informal: For k ≥ 1, a vertex set S is k-star-forming if and only if every vertex v outside S has at least k neighbours in S, or has a neighbour u in S with at least k − 1 neighbours in S.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_iff {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (S : Finset V) :
    simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k S ↔ ∀ v, v ∉ S →
      k ≤ (S.filter (G.Adj v)).card ∨ ∃ u ∈ S, G.Adj v u ∧ k - 1 ≤ (S.filter (G.Adj u)).card
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_iff {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (S : Finset V) :
    simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k S ↔ ∀ v, v ∉ S →
      k ≤ (S.filter (G.Adj v)).card ∨ ∃ u ∈ S, G.Adj v u ∧ k - 1 ≤ (S.filter (G.Adj u)).card := open Finset in by
  constructor
  · intro h v hv
    obtain ⟨c, L, hc, hL, hcard, hadj, hvc⟩ := h v hv
    rcases hvc with rfl | hvL
    · left
      rw [← hcard]
      apply card_le_card
      intro x hx
      rw [mem_filter]
      rcases hL x hx with rfl | hxS
      · exact absurd (hadj _ hx) G.irrefl
      · exact ⟨hxS, hadj x hx⟩
    · right
      have hcv : c ≠ v := fun h => G.irrefl (by have := hadj v hvL; rwa [← h] at this)
      have hcS : c ∈ S := hc.resolve_left hcv
      refine ⟨c, hcS, (hadj v hvL).symm, ?_⟩
      have : (L.erase v).card = k - 1 := by rw [card_erase_of_mem hvL, hcard]
      rw [← this]
      apply card_le_card
      intro x hx
      rw [mem_erase] at hx
      rw [mem_filter]
      exact ⟨(hL x hx.2).resolve_left hx.1, hadj x hx.2⟩
  · intro h v hv
    rcases h v hv with h1 | ⟨u, huS, hvu, h2⟩
    · obtain ⟨L, hLs, hLc⟩ := exists_subset_card_eq h1
      refine ⟨v, L, Or.inl rfl, fun x hx => Or.inr (mem_filter.1 (hLs hx)).1, hLc,
        fun x hx => (mem_filter.1 (hLs hx)).2, Or.inl rfl⟩
    · obtain ⟨L, hLs, hLc⟩ := exists_subset_card_eq h2
      have hvL : v ∉ L := fun h => hv (mem_filter.1 (hLs h)).1
      refine ⟨u, insert v L, Or.inr huS, ?_, ?_, ?_, Or.inr (mem_insert_self v L)⟩
      · intro x hx
        rcases mem_insert.1 hx with rfl | hx
        · exact Or.inl rfl
        · exact Or.inr (mem_filter.1 (hLs hx)).1
      · rw [card_insert_of_notMem hvL, hLc]
        omega
      · intro x hx
        rcases mem_insert.1 hx with rfl | hx
        · exact hvu.symm
        · exact (mem_filter.1 (hLs hx)).2
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Lemma 2.2.

explanation.summary: The equivalence is proved by case analysis in both directions. If $S$ is $k$-star-forming, any vertex $v \notin S$ is either the center or a leaf of a $k$-star whose vertices lie in $S \cup \{v\}$; irreflexivity of the graph forces all leaves to lie in $S$ when $v$ is the center (yielding $k$ neighbours), or forces the center to lie in $S$ with $k - 1$ other leaves in $S$ when $v$ is a leaf. Conversely, $k$ neighbours of $v$ in $S$ form the leaves of a star centered at $v$, while a neighbour $u \in S$ with $k - 1$ neighbours in $S$ serves as the center of a star whose leaves are $v$ together with those $k - 1$ neighbours.

steps.claim: To establish the forward direction, consider any $v \notin S$ and distinguish whether $v$ is the center or a leaf of the witnessing $k$-star.
steps.explanation: We split the bi-implication using `constructor`. Assuming $S$ is $k$-star-forming and taking $v \notin S$, the definition provides a star with center $c$ and leaf set $L$ of size $k$ such that all vertices lie in $S \cup \{v\}$, $c$ is adjacent to each leaf, and $v = c$ or $v \in L$. We split into these two cases.
steps.code:
constructor
  · intro h v hv
    obtain ⟨c, L, hc, hL, hcard, hadj, hvc⟩ := h v hv
    rcases hvc with rfl | hvL

steps.claim: If $v$ is the center of the star, then $v$ has at least $k$ neighbours in $S$.
steps.explanation: When $v = c$, the center is $v$ and the leaf set $L$ has cardinality $k$. Because simple graphs have no self-loops (`G.irrefl`), no leaf in $L$ can equal $v$. Since every leaf is in $S \cup \{v\}$, all leaves must belong to $S$. Thus $L$ is a subset of the neighbours of $v$ in $S$ (`mem_filter`), which by monotonicity of cardinality (`card_le_card`) implies that $v$ has at least $|L| = k$ neighbours in $S$.
steps.code:
· left
      rw [← hcard]
      apply card_le_card
      intro x hx
      rw [mem_filter]
      rcases hL x hx with rfl | hxS
      · exact absurd (hadj _ hx) G.irrefl
      · exact ⟨hxS, hadj x hx⟩

steps.claim: If $v$ is a leaf of the star, then $v$ has a neighbour $c \in S$ with at least $k - 1$ neighbours in $S$.
steps.explanation: When $v \in L$, the center $c$ is adjacent to $v$. By irreflexivity (`G.irrefl`), $c \ne v$, and since $c \in S \cup \{v\}$, this forces $c \in S$. Removing $v$ from $L$ leaves a set $L \setminus \{v\}$ of size $k - 1$ (`card_erase_of_mem`). Every $x \in L \setminus \{v\}$ is adjacent to $c$, and since $x \ne v$ (`mem_erase`) and $x \in S \cup \{v\}$, every such $x$ lies in $S$. Hence $L \setminus \{v\}$ is a subset of the neighbours of $c$ in $S$ (`mem_filter`), so $c$ has at least $k - 1$ neighbours in $S$ by cardinality monotonicity (`card_le_card`).
steps.code:
· right
      have hcv : c ≠ v := fun h => G.irrefl (by have := hadj v hvL; rwa [← h] at this)
      have hcS : c ∈ S := hc.resolve_left hcv
      refine ⟨c, hcS, (hadj v hvL).symm, ?_⟩
      have : (L.erase v).card = k - 1 := by rw [card_erase_of_mem hvL, hcard]
      rw [← this]
      apply card_le_card
      intro x hx
      rw [mem_erase] at hx
      rw [mem_filter]
      exact ⟨(hL x hx.2).resolve_left hx.1, hadj x hx.2⟩

steps.claim: In the reverse direction, if $v \notin S$ has at least $k$ neighbours in $S$, then a $k$-star centered at $v$ witnesses the star-forming property.
steps.explanation: Assuming the disjunction holds and taking $v \notin S$, we first consider the case where $v$ has at least $k$ neighbours in $S$. We pick a subset $L \subseteq S \cap N(v)$ of size $k$ (`exists_subset_card_eq`). Choosing $v$ as the center and $L$ as the leaf set satisfies all required conditions: the center is $v$, every leaf is in $S$, $|L| = k$, $v$ is adjacent to every leaf, and $v$ is the center.
steps.code:
· intro h v hv
    rcases h v hv with h1 | ⟨u, huS, hvu, h2⟩
    · obtain ⟨L, hLs, hLc⟩ := exists_subset_card_eq h1
      refine ⟨v, L, Or.inl rfl, fun x hx => Or.inr (mem_filter.1 (hLs hx)).1, hLc,
        fun x hx => (mem_filter.1 (hLs hx)).2, Or.inl rfl⟩

steps.claim: In the reverse direction, if $v \notin S$ has a neighbour $u \in S$ with at least $k - 1$ neighbours in $S$, then a $k$-star centered at $u$ witnesses the star-forming property.
steps.explanation: In the second case, $v$ has a neighbour $u \in S$ with at least $k - 1$ neighbours in $S$. We pick a subset $L \subseteq S \cap N(u)$ of size $k - 1$ (`exists_subset_card_eq`). Since $L \subseteq S$ and $v \notin S$, $v \notin L$. We choose $u$ as the center and $\{v\} \cup L$ as the leaf set (`mem_insert_self`). All leaves belong to $S \cup \{v\}$, $u$ is adjacent to $v$ and to all elements of $L$, and the number of leaves is $(k - 1) + 1 = k$ (`card_insert_of_notMem`), using $k \ge 1$ via linear arithmetic (`omega`). Thus this star witnesses star-formation for $v$.
steps.code:
· obtain ⟨L, hLs, hLc⟩ := exists_subset_card_eq h2
      have hvL : v ∉ L := fun h => hv (mem_filter.1 (hLs h)).1
      refine ⟨u, insert v L, Or.inr huS, ?_, ?_, ?_, Or.inr (mem_insert_self v L)⟩
      · intro x hx
        rcases mem_insert.1 hx with rfl | hx
        · exact Or.inl rfl
        · exact Or.inr (mem_filter.1 (hLs hx)).1
      · rw [card_insert_of_notMem hvL, hLc]
        omega
      · intro x hx
        rcases mem_insert.1 hx with rfl | hx
        · exact hvu.symm
        · exact (mem_filter.1 (hLs hx)).2

glossary.card_le_card: If $s \subseteq t$ for finite sets $s$ and $t$, then $|s| \le |t|$.
glossary.mem_filter: An element $a$ belongs to the sub-finset of $s$ filtered by predicate $p$ if and only if $a \in s$ and $p(a)$ holds.
glossary.G.irrefl: In a simple graph $G$, no vertex is adjacent to itself (adjacency is irreflexive).
glossary.card_erase_of_mem: If an element $a$ belongs to a finite set $s$, then the cardinality of $s \setminus \{a\}$ is $|s| - 1$.
glossary.mem_erase: An element $a$ belongs to $s \setminus \{b\}$ if and only if $a \ne b$ and $a \in s$.
glossary.exists_subset_card_eq: If a finite set $s$ satisfies $n \le |s|$, then there exists a subset $t \subseteq s$ with $|t| = n$.
glossary.mem_insert_self: The element $a$ is an element of the set $\{a\} \cup s$ obtained by inserting $a$ into $s$.
glossary.card_insert_of_notMem: If $a \notin s$ for a finite set $s$, then $|\{a\} \cup s| = |s| + 1$.

caveats: The arithmetic equality $(k - 1) + 1 = k$ for $k \ge 1$ in the second construction is solved automatically by linear arithmetic (`omega`).

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff
declarations.informal: With decidable adjacency, a vertex set I is k-independent iff every v ∈ I has fewer than k neighbours in the finset I.filter (G.Adj v).
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) (I : Finset V) :
    simple_graph_is_k_independent G k I ↔ ∀ v ∈ I, (I.filter (G.Adj v)).card < k
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) (I : Finset V) :
    simple_graph_is_k_independent G k I ↔ ∀ v ∈ I, (I.filter (G.Adj v)).card < k := open Finset in by
  unfold simple_graph_is_k_independent
  have : ∀ v, ({u | u ∈ I ∧ G.Adj v u} : Set V).ncard = (I.filter (G.Adj v)).card := by
    intro v
    rw [← Set.ncard_coe_finset, coe_filter]
  simp only [this]
declarations.citation: Computable form of k-independence for arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination) (used for Proposition 7.1 and Theorem 3.2).

explanation.summary: By definition, a finset $I$ is $k$-independent in a graph $G$ if for each vertex $v \in I$, the set of neighbors of $v$ belonging to $I$, $\{u \in I \mid G.\text{Adj}(v, u)\}$, has set cardinality strictly less than $k$. The theorem establishes that this condition is equivalent to the finset filter $I.\text{filter}(G.\text{Adj}(v))$ having cardinality strictly less than $k$. The proof unfolds the definition of $k$-independence, shows that the set-theoretic cardinality equals the finset filter cardinality by coercing the finset to a set, and substitutes this equality into the equivalence.

steps.claim: The definition of $k$-independence is expanded into a condition on set cardinality.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition `simple_graph_is_k_independent` reformulates the left-hand side as the condition that for every $v \in I$, the set cardinality of $\{u \in V \mid u \in I \wedge G.\text{Adj}(v, u)\}$ is strictly less than $k$.
steps.code: unfold simple_graph_is_k_independent

steps.claim: For every vertex $v$, the set cardinality of $\{u \in V \mid u \in I \wedge G.\text{Adj}(v, u)\}$ equals the finset cardinality of $I.\text{filter}(G.\text{Adj}(v))$.
steps.explanation: Fixing an arbitrary vertex $v$, the finset cardinality of $I.\text{filter}(G.\text{Adj}(v))$ is rewritten into the cardinality of its coerced set using `Set.ncard_coe_finset`. Then, `coe_filter` identifies the coerced finset with the set comprehension $\{u \in V \mid u \in I \wedge G.\text{Adj}(v, u)\}$.
steps.code:
have : ∀ v, ({u | u ∈ I ∧ G.Adj v u} : Set V).ncard = (I.filter (G.Adj v)).card := by
    intro v
    rw [← Set.ncard_coe_finset, coe_filter]

steps.claim: A vertex set $I$ is $k$-independent if and only if each $v \in I$ has fewer than $k$ neighbors in $I$.filter $(G.\text{Adj}(v))$.
steps.explanation: Rewriting the goal with the established equality of cardinalities makes both sides of the equivalence identical, which completes the proof.
steps.code: simp only [this]

glossary.Set.ncard_coe_finset: The set cardinality (`Set.ncard`) of a coerced finite set is equal to its finset cardinality (`Finset.card`).
glossary.coe_filter: The coercion of a filtered finset `Finset.filter p s` to a set is the set comprehension `{x | x ∈ s ∧ p x}`.

declarations.name: simple_graph_is_k_independent_mono
declarations.informal: Every subset of a k-independent vertex set is k-independent.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_independent_mono {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ)
    {I J : Finset V} (hIJ : I ⊆ J) (hJ : simple_graph_is_k_independent G k J) :
    simple_graph_is_k_independent G k I
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_is_k_independent_mono {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ)
    {I J : Finset V} (hIJ : I ⊆ J) (hJ : simple_graph_is_k_independent G k J) :
    simple_graph_is_k_independent G k I := open Finset in by
  intro v hv
  refine lt_of_le_of_lt (Set.ncard_le_ncard ?_ (J.finite_toSet.subset (fun w hw => hw.1)))
    (hJ v (hIJ hv))
  exact fun w hw => ⟨hIJ hw.1, hw.2⟩
declarations.citation: Monotonicity of k-independence, used in arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination) (Sec. 2 and Proposition 7.1).

explanation.summary: The proof shows that any vertex v in the subset I has strictly fewer than k neighbors in I. Since I ⊆ J, the set of neighbors of v in I is contained in the set of neighbors of v in J. Because J is finite, the number of neighbors in I is at most the number of neighbors in J, which is strictly less than k by the k-independence of J.

steps.claim: To show that I is k-independent, it suffices to show that each vertex v ∈ I has strictly fewer than k neighbors in I.
steps.explanation: By definition, a vertex set I is k-independent in G if every vertex v ∈ I has strictly fewer than k neighbors in I. We fix an arbitrary vertex v and assume v ∈ I.
steps.code: intro v hv

steps.claim: The vertex v has strictly fewer than k neighbors in I.
steps.explanation: Every neighbor of v in I is also a neighbor of v in J because I ⊆ J, so {u ∈ I | G.Adj v u} ⊆ {u ∈ J | G.Adj v u}. Since J is finite, this superset of neighbors is finite, and Set.ncard_le_ncard gives that v has at most as many neighbors in I as in J. Moreover, because v ∈ I ⊆ J, the k-independence of J implies that v has strictly fewer than k neighbors in J. Transitivity of ≤ and < via lt_of_le_of_lt concludes that v has strictly fewer than k neighbors in I.
steps.code:
refine lt_of_le_of_lt (Set.ncard_le_ncard ?_ (J.finite_toSet.subset (fun w hw => hw.1)))
    (hJ v (hIJ hv))
  exact fun w hw => ⟨hIJ hw.1, hw.2⟩

glossary.lt_of_le_of_lt: In a preorder, if a ≤ b and b < c, then a < c.
glossary.Set.ncard_le_ncard: If s ⊆ t and t is finite, then the cardinality of s is at most the cardinality of t.

declarations.name: complete_bipartite_k_independence_number_eq_upper_k_star_forming_number
declarations.informal: For k ≥ 2 and a, b ≥ k, the complete bipartite graph K_{a,b} has β_k(K_{a,b}) = SF_k(K_{a,b}) = max{a, b, 2k − 2}.
declarations.statement:
theorem complete_bipartite_k_independence_number_eq_upper_k_star_forming_number
    (k a b : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (ha : k ≤ a) (hb : k ≤ b) :
    simple_graph_k_independence_number (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b)) k =
        max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) ∧
      simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b)) k =
        max a (max b (2 * k - 2))
declarations.source:
theorem complete_bipartite_k_independence_number_eq_upper_k_star_forming_number
    (k a b : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (ha : k ≤ a) (hb : k ≤ b) :
    simple_graph_k_independence_number (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b)) k =
        max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) ∧
      simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b)) k =
        max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) := open Finset in by
  classical
  set K := completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b) with hK
  unfold simple_graph_k_independence_number simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number
  -- neighbourhoods inside a set, in terms of the two sides
  have hNl : ∀ (S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b)) i, (S.filter (K.Adj (Sum.inl i))).card = S.toRight.card := by
    intro S i
    have : S.filter (K.Adj (Sum.inl i)) = S.toRight.map Function.Embedding.inr := by
      ext w
      rcases w with w | w <;> simp [hK]
    rw [this, card_map]
  have hNr : ∀ (S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b)) j, (S.filter (K.Adj (Sum.inr j))).card = S.toLeft.card := by
    intro S j
    have : S.filter (K.Adj (Sum.inr j)) = S.toLeft.map Function.Embedding.inl := by
      ext w
      rcases w with w | w <;> simp [hK]
    rw [this, card_map]
  have hcard : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.card = S.toLeft.card + S.toRight.card :=
    fun S => card_toLeft_add_card_toRight.symm
  have hxa : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toLeft.card ≤ a := fun S =>
    (card_le_univ _).trans (by simp)
  have hyb : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toRight.card ≤ b := fun S =>
    (card_le_univ _).trans (by simp)
  have hxa' : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toLeft.card = a ↔ ∀ i, Sum.inl i ∈ S := by
    intro S
    constructor
    · intro h i
      have : S.toLeft = univ := eq_univ_of_card _ (by simpa using h)
      rw [← mem_toLeft, this]
      exact mem_univ i
    · intro h
      have : S.toLeft = univ := eq_univ_of_forall (fun i => mem_toLeft.2 (h i))
      rw [this]
      simp
  have hyb' : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toRight.card = b ↔ ∀ j, Sum.inr j ∈ S := by
    intro S
    constructor
    · intro h j
      have : S.toRight = univ := eq_univ_of_card _ (by simpa using h)
      rw [← mem_toRight, this]
      exact mem_univ j
    · intro h
      have : S.toRight = univ := eq_univ_of_forall (fun j => mem_toRight.2 (h j))
      rw [this]
      simp
  have hx0 : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toLeft.card = 0 ↔ ∀ i, Sum.inl i ∉ S := by
    intro S
    rw [card_eq_zero, eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    simp
  have hy0 : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toRight.card = 0 ↔ ∀ j, Sum.inr j ∉ S := by
    intro S
    rw [card_eq_zero, eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    simp
  -- k-independence and star-forming in terms of the counts
  have hind : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), simple_graph_is_k_independent K k S ↔
      (S.toLeft.card = 0 ∨ S.toRight.card < k) ∧ (S.toRight.card = 0 ∨ S.toLeft.card < k) := by
    intro S
    rw [simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff]
    constructor
    · intro h
      constructor
      · by_cases h0 : S.toLeft.card = 0
        · exact Or.inl h0
        · right
          obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, Sum.inl i ∈ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; exact h0 ((hx0 S).2 hn)
          have := h _ hi
          rwa [hNl] at this
      · by_cases h0 : S.toRight.card = 0
        · exact Or.inl h0
        · right
          obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, Sum.inr j ∈ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; exact h0 ((hy0 S).2 hn)
          have := h _ hj
          rwa [hNr] at this
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ v hv
      rcases v with i | j
      · rw [hNl]
        exact h1.resolve_left (fun h => (hx0 S).1 h i hv)
      · rw [hNr]
        exact h2.resolve_left (fun h => (hy0 S).1 h j hv)
  have hsf : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), simple_graph_is_k_star_forming K k S ↔
      (S.toLeft.card = a ∨ k ≤ S.toRight.card ∨ (1 ≤ S.toRight.card ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toLeft.card)) ∧
      (S.toRight.card = b ∨ k ≤ S.toLeft.card ∨ (1 ≤ S.toLeft.card ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toRight.card)) := by
    intro S
    rw [simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_iff K k (by omega)]
    constructor
    · intro h
      constructor
      · by_cases hx : S.toLeft.card = a
        · exact Or.inl hx
        · right
          obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, Sum.inl i ∉ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; exact hx ((hxa' S).2 hn)
          rcases h _ hi with h1 | ⟨u, huS, hvu, h2⟩
          · left; rwa [hNl] at h1
          · right
            rcases u with u | u
            · simp [hK] at hvu
            · rw [hNr] at h2
              refine ⟨?_, h2⟩
              rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero]
              exact fun h0 => (hy0 S).1 h0 u huS
      · by_cases hy : S.toRight.card = b
        · exact Or.inl hy
        · right
          obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, Sum.inr j ∉ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; exact hy ((hyb' S).2 hn)
          rcases h _ hj with h1 | ⟨u, huS, hvu, h2⟩
          · left; rwa [hNr] at h1
          · right
            rcases u with u | u
            · rw [hNl] at h2
              refine ⟨?_, h2⟩
              rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero]
              exact fun h0 => (hx0 S).1 h0 u huS
            · simp [hK] at hvu
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ v hv
      rcases v with i | j
      · have hx : S.toLeft.card ≠ a := fun h => hv ((hxa' S).1 h i)
        rcases h1.resolve_left hx with h1 | ⟨hy1, hx1⟩
        · left; rwa [hNl]
        · right
          obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, Sum.inr j ∈ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; have := (hy0 S).2 hn; omega
          exact ⟨Sum.inr j, hj, by simp [hK], by rwa [hNr]⟩
      · have hy : S.toRight.card ≠ b := fun h => hv ((hyb' S).1 h j)
        rcases h2.resolve_left hy with h2 | ⟨hx1, hy1⟩
        · left; rwa [hNr]
        · right
          obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, Sum.inl i ∈ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; have := (hx0 S).2 hn; omega
          exact ⟨Sum.inl i, hi, by simp [hK], by rwa [hNl]⟩
  have hmin : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming K k S →
      S.card ≤ max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) := by
    rintro S ⟨hS, hm⟩
    have hS' := (hsf S).1 hS
    have hl : 1 ≤ S.toLeft.card → ¬ ((S.toLeft.card - 1 = a ∨ k ≤ S.toRight.card ∨
        (1 ≤ S.toRight.card ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toLeft.card - 1)) ∧
        (S.toRight.card = b ∨ k ≤ S.toLeft.card - 1 ∨
          (1 ≤ S.toLeft.card - 1 ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toRight.card))) := by
      intro h1 hc
      obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, Sum.inl i ∈ S := by
        by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; have := (hx0 S).2 hn; omega
      have e1 : (S.erase (Sum.inl i)).toLeft.card = S.toLeft.card - 1 := by
        have : (S.erase (Sum.inl i)).toLeft = S.toLeft.erase i := by
          ext j; simp
        rw [this, card_erase_of_mem (mem_toLeft.2 hi)]
      have e2 : (S.erase (Sum.inl i)).toRight = S.toRight := by
        ext j; simp
      apply hm _ (erase_ssubset hi)
      rw [hsf, e1, e2]
      exact hc
    have hr : 1 ≤ S.toRight.card → ¬ ((S.toLeft.card = a ∨ k ≤ S.toRight.card - 1 ∨
        (1 ≤ S.toRight.card - 1 ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toLeft.card)) ∧
        (S.toRight.card - 1 = b ∨ k ≤ S.toLeft.card ∨
          (1 ≤ S.toLeft.card ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toRight.card - 1))) := by
      intro h1 hc
      obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, Sum.inr j ∈ S := by
        by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; have := (hy0 S).2 hn; omega
      have e1 : (S.erase (Sum.inr j)).toRight.card = S.toRight.card - 1 := by
        have : (S.erase (Sum.inr j)).toRight = S.toRight.erase j := by
          ext i; simp
        rw [this, card_erase_of_mem (mem_toRight.2 hj)]
      have e2 : (S.erase (Sum.inr j)).toLeft = S.toLeft := by
        ext i; simp
      apply hm _ (erase_ssubset hj)
      rw [hsf, e1, e2]
      exact hc
    have := hxa S
    have := hyb S
    rw [hcard]
    omega
  -- sets with prescribed counts
  have hmk : ∀ x y, x ≤ a → y ≤ b → ∃ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b),
      S.toLeft.card = x ∧ S.toRight.card = y := by
    intro x y hx hy
    refine ⟨(univ.map (Fin.castLEEmb hx)).disjSum (univ.map (Fin.castLEEmb hy)), ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp
  have hbddI : BddAbove {n | ∃ I : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b),
      simple_graph_is_k_independent K k I ∧ I.card = n} :=
    ⟨a + b, fun n ⟨I, _, hn⟩ => hn ▸ (card_le_univ I).trans (by simp)⟩
  have hbddS : BddAbove {n | ∃ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b),
      simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming K k S ∧ S.card = n} :=
    ⟨a + b, fun n ⟨S, _, hn⟩ => hn ▸ (card_le_univ S).trans (by simp)⟩
  -- the three extremal count pairs
  have hpairs : ∃ x y, x ≤ a ∧ y ≤ b ∧ x + y = max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) ∧
      (x = 0 ∨ y < k) ∧ (y = 0 ∨ x < k) ∧
      ((x = a ∨ k ≤ y ∨ (1 ≤ y ∧ k - 1 ≤ x)) ∧ (y = b ∨ k ≤ x ∨ (1 ≤ x ∧ k - 1 ≤ y))) ∧
      (1 ≤ x → ¬ ((x - 1 = a ∨ k ≤ y ∨ (1 ≤ y ∧ k - 1 ≤ x - 1)) ∧
        (y = b ∨ k ≤ x - 1 ∨ (1 ≤ x - 1 ∧ k - 1 ≤ y)))) ∧
      (1 ≤ y → ¬ ((x = a ∨ k ≤ y - 1 ∨ (1 ≤ y - 1 ∧ k - 1 ≤ x)) ∧
        (y - 1 = b ∨ k ≤ x ∨ (1 ≤ x ∧ k - 1 ≤ y - 1)))) := by
    by_cases h1 : b ≤ a ∧ 2 * k - 2 ≤ a
    · exact ⟨a, 0, le_rfl, Nat.zero_le _, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega,
        by omega⟩
    · by_cases h2 : a ≤ b ∧ 2 * k - 2 ≤ b
      · exact ⟨0, b, Nat.zero_le _, le_rfl, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega,
          by omega⟩
      · exact ⟨k - 1, k - 1, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega,
          by omega, by omega⟩
  obtain ⟨x, y, hx, hy, hxy, hi1, hi2, hs1, hs2, hs3⟩ := hpairs
  obtain ⟨S₀, hS₀x, hS₀y⟩ := hmk x y hx hy
  constructor
  · apply le_antisymm
    · refine csSup_le (Set.nonempty_of_mem (x := 0) ⟨∅, fun v hv => by simp at hv, rfl⟩) ?_
      rintro n ⟨I, hI, rfl⟩
      have := (hind I).1 hI
      have := hxa I
      have := hyb I
      rw [hcard]
      omega
    · apply le_csSup hbddI
      refine ⟨S₀, (hind S₀).2 ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [hS₀x, hS₀y]; exact ⟨hi1, hi2⟩
      · rw [hcard, hS₀x, hS₀y, hxy]
  · have hmem : max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) ∈ {n | ∃ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b),
        simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming K k S ∧ S.card = n} := by
      refine ⟨S₀, ⟨(hsf S₀).2 (by rw [hS₀x, hS₀y]; exact hs1), ?_⟩, by rw [hcard, hS₀x, hS₀y, hxy]⟩
      intro T hT hTsf
      obtain ⟨s, hsS, hsT⟩ := exists_of_ssubset hT
      have hsub : T ⊆ S₀.erase s := fun t ht => mem_erase.2 ⟨fun h => hsT (h ▸ ht), hT.1 ht⟩
      have h2 := (hsf _).1 (simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_mono K k hsub hTsf)
      rcases s with i | j
      · have e1 : (S₀.erase (Sum.inl i)).toLeft.card = x - 1 := by
          have : (S₀.erase (Sum.inl i)).toLeft = S₀.toLeft.erase i := by
            ext j; simp
          rw [this, card_erase_of_mem (mem_toLeft.2 hsS), hS₀x]
        have e2 : (S₀.erase (Sum.inl i)).toRight = S₀.toRight := by
          ext j; simp
        have hx1 : 1 ≤ x := by
          rw [← hS₀x]; exact card_pos.2 ⟨i, mem_toLeft.2 hsS⟩
        rw [e1, e2, hS₀y] at h2
        exact hs2 hx1 h2
      · have e1 : (S₀.erase (Sum.inr j)).toRight.card = y - 1 := by
          have : (S₀.erase (Sum.inr j)).toRight = S₀.toRight.erase j := by
            ext i; simp
          rw [this, card_erase_of_mem (mem_toRight.2 hsS), hS₀y]
        have e2 : (S₀.erase (Sum.inr j)).toLeft = S₀.toLeft := by
          ext i; simp
        have hy1 : 1 ≤ y := by
          rw [← hS₀y]; exact card_pos.2 ⟨j, mem_toRight.2 hsS⟩
        rw [e1, e2, hS₀x] at h2
        exact hs3 hy1 h2
    apply le_antisymm
    · refine csSup_le ⟨_, hmem⟩ ?_
      rintro n ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩
      exact hmin S hS
    · exact le_csSup hbddS hmem
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Theorem 3.2.

explanation.summary: To compute β_k(K_{a,b}) and SF_k(K_{a,b}), the proof characterizes both the k-independence and k-star-forming properties in terms of the counts of chosen vertices from each bipartite side, |S ∩ A| and |S ∩ B|. It shows that the maximum cardinality in both cases is achieved either by taking an entire side of the graph (yielding max{a, b}) when max{a, b} ≥ 2k − 2, or by taking k − 1 vertices from each side (yielding 2k − 2) otherwise. The upper bounds follow from the neighborhood size characterizations and the minimality condition on star-forming sets, while the lower bounds are established by constructing an explicit set matching these optimal counts.

steps.claim: Let K be the complete bipartite graph K_{a,b} on vertices Fin a ⊕ Fin b, and express β_k(K) and SF_k(K) as suprema of cardinalities of k-independent sets and minimal k-star-forming sets, respectively.
steps.explanation: We introduce the graph K = completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b) and unfold the definitions of simple_graph_k_independence_number and simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number into suprema over sizes of subsets satisfying simple_graph_is_k_independent and simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming.
steps.code:
classical
  set K := completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b) with hK
  unfold simple_graph_k_independence_number simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number

steps.claim: For any vertex subset S, the neighborhood in S of any left vertex has size |S.toRight|, the neighborhood of any right vertex has size |S.toLeft|, and |S| = |S.toLeft| + |S.toRight| with |S.toLeft| ≤ a and |S.toRight| ≤ b.
steps.explanation: Because K is bipartite with all edges running between the two parts, the neighbors in S of any left vertex Sum.inl i are exactly the right elements of S embedded via inr, so filtering gives a set of size |S.toRight| (using card_map); symmetrically, a right vertex has |S.toLeft| neighbors in S. The total size is the sum of the component counts (card_toLeft_add_card_toRight), which are bounded by the ambient part sizes a and b (card_le_univ).
steps.code:
have hNl : ∀ (S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b)) i, (S.filter (K.Adj (Sum.inl i))).card = S.toRight.card := by
    intro S i
    have : S.filter (K.Adj (Sum.inl i)) = S.toRight.map Function.Embedding.inr := by
      ext w
      rcases w with w | w <;> simp [hK]
    rw [this, card_map]
  have hNr : ∀ (S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b)) j, (S.filter (K.Adj (Sum.inr j))).card = S.toLeft.card := by
    intro S j
    have : S.filter (K.Adj (Sum.inr j)) = S.toLeft.map Function.Embedding.inl := by
      ext w
      rcases w with w | w <;> simp [hK]
    rw [this, card_map]
  have hcard : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.card = S.toLeft.card + S.toRight.card :=
    fun S => card_toLeft_add_card_toRight.symm
  have hxa : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toLeft.card ≤ a := fun S =>
    (card_le_univ _).trans (by simp)
  have hyb : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toRight.card ≤ b := fun S =>
    (card_le_univ _).trans (by simp)

steps.claim: A subset S contains all left vertices if and only if |S.toLeft| = a, all right vertices if and only if |S.toRight| = b, no left vertices if and only if |S.toLeft| = 0, and no right vertices if and only if |S.toRight| = 0.
steps.explanation: A finset on Fin a has size a if and only if it equals the universal set (eq_univ_of_card, eq_univ_of_forall), which holds precisely when every left vertex belongs to S (mem_toLeft, mem_univ), and similarly for the right side (mem_toRight). A component has size 0 if and only if it is empty (card_eq_zero, eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem).
steps.code:
have hxa' : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toLeft.card = a ↔ ∀ i, Sum.inl i ∈ S := by
    intro S
    constructor
    · intro h i
      have : S.toLeft = univ := eq_univ_of_card _ (by simpa using h)
      rw [← mem_toLeft, this]
      exact mem_univ i
    · intro h
      have : S.toLeft = univ := eq_univ_of_forall (fun i => mem_toLeft.2 (h i))
      rw [this]
      simp
  have hyb' : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toRight.card = b ↔ ∀ j, Sum.inr j ∈ S := by
    intro S
    constructor
    · intro h j
      have : S.toRight = univ := eq_univ_of_card _ (by simpa using h)
      rw [← mem_toRight, this]
      exact mem_univ j
    · intro h
      have : S.toRight = univ := eq_univ_of_forall (fun j => mem_toRight.2 (h j))
      rw [this]
      simp
  have hx0 : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toLeft.card = 0 ↔ ∀ i, Sum.inl i ∉ S := by
    intro S
    rw [card_eq_zero, eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    simp
  have hy0 : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), S.toRight.card = 0 ↔ ∀ j, Sum.inr j ∉ S := by
    intro S
    rw [card_eq_zero, eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
    simp

steps.claim: A subset S is k-independent if and only if (|S.toLeft| = 0 ∨ |S.toRight| < k) and (|S.toRight| = 0 ∨ |S.toLeft| < k).
steps.explanation: By simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff, every vertex in S must have fewer than k neighbors in S. If S contains any left vertex, its neighborhood in S has size |S.toRight|, forcing |S.toRight| < k; if it contains none, |S.toLeft| = 0. Symmetrical conditions apply to the right vertices.

have hind : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), simple_graph_is_k_independent K k S ↔
      (S.toLeft.card = 0 ∨ S.toRight.card < k) ∧ (S.toRight.card = 0 ∨ S.toLeft.card < k) := by
    intro S
    rw [simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff]
    constructor
    · intro h
      constructor
      · by_cases h0 : S.toLeft.card = 0
        · exact Or.inl h0
        · right
          obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, Sum.inl i ∈ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; exact h0 ((hx0 S).2 hn)
          have := h _ hi
          rwa [hNl] at this
      · by_cases h0 : S.toRight.card = 0
        · exact Or.inl h0
        · right
          obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, Sum.inr j ∈ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; exact h0 ((hy0 S).2 hn)
          have := h _ hj
          rwa [hNr] at this
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ v hv
      rcases v with i | j
      · rw [hNl]
        exact h1.resolve_left (fun h => (hx0 S).1 h i hv)
      · rw [hNr]
        exact h2.resolve_left (fun h => (hy0 S).1 h j hv)

steps.claim: A subset S is k-star-forming if and only if (|S.toLeft| = a ∨ k ≤ |S.toRight| ∨ (1 ≤ |S.toRight| ∧ k - 1 ≤ |S.toLeft|)) and (|S.toRight| = b ∨ k ≤ |S.toLeft| ∨ (1 ≤ |S.toLeft| ∧ k - 1 ≤ |S.toRight|)).
steps.explanation: By simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_iff, any vertex v ∉ S must either have at least k neighbors in S, or have a neighbor u ∈ S with at least k - 1 neighbors in S. If v is a left vertex not in S (which exists unless |S.toLeft| = a), its neighbors in S are all in S.toRight, so either |S.toRight| ≥ k, or there is some right vertex u ∈ S (requiring |S.toRight| ≥ 1, via Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero) whose neighbors in S are S.toLeft, requiring |S.toLeft| ≥ k - 1. Symmetrical reasoning applies to unchosen right vertices.
steps.code:
have hsf : ∀ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b), simple_graph_is_k_star_forming K k S ↔
      (S.toLeft.card = a ∨ k ≤ S.toRight.card ∨ (1 ≤ S.toRight.card ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toLeft.card)) ∧
      (S.toRight.card = b ∨ k ≤ S.toLeft.card ∨ (1 ≤ S.toLeft.card ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toRight.card)) := by
    intro S
    rw [simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_iff K k (by omega)]
    constructor
    · intro h
      constructor
      · by_cases hx : S.toLeft.card = a
        · exact Or.inl hx
        · right
          obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, Sum.inl i ∉ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; exact hx ((hxa' S).2 hn)
          rcases h _ hi with h1 | ⟨u, huS, hvu, h2⟩
          · left; rwa [hNl] at h1
          · right
            rcases u with u | u
            · simp [hK] at hvu
            · rw [hNr] at h2
              refine ⟨?_, h2⟩
              rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero]
              exact fun h0 => (hy0 S).1 h0 u huS
      · by_cases hy : S.toRight.card = b
        · exact Or.inl hy
        · right
          obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, Sum.inr j ∉ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; exact hy ((hyb' S).2 hn)
          rcases h _ hj with h1 | ⟨u, huS, hvu, h2⟩
          · left; rwa [hNr] at h1
          · right
            rcases u with u | u
            · rw [hNl] at h2
              refine ⟨?_, h2⟩
              rw [Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero]
              exact fun h0 => (hx0 S).1 h0 u huS
            · simp [hK] at hvu
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩ v hv
      rcases v with i | j
      · have hx : S.toLeft.card ≠ a := fun h => hv ((hxa' S).1 h i)
        rcases h1.resolve_left hx with h1 | ⟨hy1, hx1⟩
        · left; rwa [hNl]
        · right
          obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, Sum.inr j ∈ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; have := (hy0 S).2 hn; omega
          exact ⟨Sum.inr j, hj, by simp [hK], by rwa [hNr]⟩
      · have hy : S.toRight.card ≠ b := fun h => hv ((hyb' S).1 h j)
        rcases h2.resolve_left hy with h2 | ⟨hx1, hy1⟩
        · left; rwa [hNr]
        · right
          obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ : ∃ i, Sum.inl i ∈ S := by
            by_contra hn; push_neg at hn; have := (hx0 S).2 hn; omega
          exact ⟨Sum.inl i, hi, by simp [hK], by rwa [hNl]⟩

steps.claim: Every minimal k-star-forming set S satisfies |S| ≤ max a (max b (2 * k - 2)).
steps.explanation: If S is minimal k-star-forming, removing any vertex s ∈ S produces a proper subset S \ {s} (erase_ssubset) which cannot be k-star-forming. Removing a left vertex decreases |S.toLeft| by 1 (card_erase_of_mem) while keeping |S.toRight| fixed, so the star-forming condition must fail for the decreased counts; symmetrically, removing a right vertex decreases |S.toRight| by 1. Combining these necessary failure conditions with |S.toLeft| ≤ a and |S.toRight| ≤ b, Presburger linear arithmetic (omega) deduces that |S| = |S.toLeft| + |S.toRight| ≤ max a (max b (2 * k - 2)).

      have e1 : (S.erase (Sum.inl i)).toLeft.card = S.toLeft.card - 1 := by

          ext j; simp
        rw [this, card_erase_of_mem (mem_toLeft.2 hi)]
      have e2 : (S.erase (Sum.inl i)).toRight = S.toRight := by
        ext j; simp

    have hr : 1 ≤ S.toRight.card → ¬ ((S.toLeft.card = a ∨ k ≤ S.toRight.card - 1 ∨
        (1 ≤ S.toRight.card - 1 ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toLeft.card)) ∧
        (S.toRight.card - 1 = b ∨ k ≤ S.toLeft.card ∨
          (1 ≤ S.toLeft.card ∧ k - 1 ≤ S.toRight.card - 1))) := by
      intro h1 hc
      obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ : ∃ j, Sum.inr j ∈ S := by

      have e1 : (S.erase (Sum.inr j)).toRight.card = S.toRight.card - 1 := by
        have : (S.erase (Sum.inr j)).toRight = S.toRight.erase j := by
          ext i; simp

        ext i; simp

    have := hyb S
    rw [hcard]

steps.claim: For any x ≤ a and y ≤ b, there exists a subset S with |S.toLeft| = x and |S.toRight| = y; moreover, the size sets for k-independent and minimal k-star-forming sets are bounded above by a + b.
steps.explanation: We construct a subset with counts (x, y) by mapping Fin x and Fin y into Fin a and Fin b via Fin.castLEEmb and taking their disjoint sum. The sizes of vertex subsets are trivially bounded above by the total number of vertices a + b (card_le_univ), providing the upper bound required for BddAbove.
steps.code:
have hmk : ∀ x y, x ≤ a → y ≤ b → ∃ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b),
      S.toLeft.card = x ∧ S.toRight.card = y := by
    intro x y hx hy
    refine ⟨(univ.map (Fin.castLEEmb hx)).disjSum (univ.map (Fin.castLEEmb hy)), ?_, ?_⟩ <;> simp
  have hbddI : BddAbove {n | ∃ I : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b),
      simple_graph_is_k_independent K k I ∧ I.card = n} :=
    ⟨a + b, fun n ⟨I, _, hn⟩ => hn ▸ (card_le_univ I).trans (by simp)⟩
  have hbddS : BddAbove {n | ∃ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b),
      simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming K k S ∧ S.card = n} :=
    ⟨a + b, fun n ⟨S, _, hn⟩ => hn ▸ (card_le_univ S).trans (by simp)⟩

steps.claim: There exists an optimal count pair (x, y) with x + y = max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) and a subset S₀ with these component counts that satisfies the k-independence, k-star-forming, and minimality count conditions.
steps.explanation: We perform a three-way case split on the maximum: if a ≥ b and a ≥ 2k - 2, we choose (x, y) = (a, 0) using le_rfl and Nat.zero_le; if b ≥ a and b ≥ 2k - 2, we choose (0, b); otherwise, 2k - 2 dominates and we choose (k - 1, k - 1). Linear arithmetic verifies that these choices satisfy the k-independence and star-forming conditions as well as the minimality conditions. We then instantiate S₀ with these exact left and right counts using hmk.
steps.code:
have hpairs : ∃ x y, x ≤ a ∧ y ≤ b ∧ x + y = max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) ∧
      (x = 0 ∨ y < k) ∧ (y = 0 ∨ x < k) ∧
      ((x = a ∨ k ≤ y ∨ (1 ≤ y ∧ k - 1 ≤ x)) ∧ (y = b ∨ k ≤ x ∨ (1 ≤ x ∧ k - 1 ≤ y))) ∧
      (1 ≤ x → ¬ ((x - 1 = a ∨ k ≤ y ∨ (1 ≤ y ∧ k - 1 ≤ x - 1)) ∧
        (y = b ∨ k ≤ x - 1 ∨ (1 ≤ x - 1 ∧ k - 1 ≤ y)))) ∧
      (1 ≤ y → ¬ ((x = a ∨ k ≤ y - 1 ∨ (1 ≤ y - 1 ∧ k - 1 ≤ x)) ∧
        (y - 1 = b ∨ k ≤ x ∨ (1 ≤ x ∧ k - 1 ≤ y - 1)))) := by
    by_cases h1 : b ≤ a ∧ 2 * k - 2 ≤ a
    · exact ⟨a, 0, le_rfl, Nat.zero_le _, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega,
        by omega⟩
    · by_cases h2 : a ≤ b ∧ 2 * k - 2 ≤ b
      · exact ⟨0, b, Nat.zero_le _, le_rfl, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega,
          by omega⟩
      · exact ⟨k - 1, k - 1, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega,
          by omega, by omega⟩
  obtain ⟨x, y, hx, hy, hxy, hi1, hi2, hs1, hs2, hs3⟩ := hpairs
  obtain ⟨S₀, hS₀x, hS₀y⟩ := hmk x y hx hy
  constructor

steps.claim: The k-independence number β_k(K_{a,b}) equals max a (max b (2 * k - 2)).
steps.explanation: We establish equality by le_antisymm. For the upper bound, every k-independent set I satisfies the count condition of hind, which combined with the capacity constraints implies |I| ≤ max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) via omega, showing the supremum is at most this value (csSup_le, Set.nonempty_of_mem). For the lower bound, S₀ is k-independent and has cardinality x + y = max a (max b (2 * k - 2)), so the supremum is at least this value (le_csSup).
steps.code:
· apply le_antisymm
    · refine csSup_le (Set.nonempty_of_mem (x := 0) ⟨∅, fun v hv => by simp at hv, rfl⟩) ?_
      rintro n ⟨I, hI, rfl⟩
      have := (hind I).1 hI
      have := hxa I
      have := hyb I
      rw [hcard]
      omega
    · apply le_csSup hbddI
      refine ⟨S₀, (hind S₀).2 ?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [hS₀x, hS₀y]; exact ⟨hi1, hi2⟩
      · rw [hcard, hS₀x, hS₀y, hxy]

steps.claim: The witness subset S₀ is minimal k-star-forming, so max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) belongs to the set of cardinalities of minimal k-star-forming sets.
steps.explanation: S₀ is k-star-forming by hsf and the choice of (x, y). For minimality, if T ⊂ S₀ is a proper subset, it is missing some vertex s (exists_of_ssubset), so T ⊆ S₀ \ {s} (mem_erase). By monotonicity of star-forming sets (simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_mono), if T were star-forming, then S₀ \ {s} would be as well. But deleting a vertex decreases the corresponding component count by 1 (card_erase_of_mem, card_pos), which contradicts the minimality conditions hs2 or hs3 satisfied by (x, y).
steps.code:
· have hmem : max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) ∈ {n | ∃ S : Finset (Fin a ⊕ Fin b),
        simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming K k S ∧ S.card = n} := by
      refine ⟨S₀, ⟨(hsf S₀).2 (by rw [hS₀x, hS₀y]; exact hs1), ?_⟩, by rw [hcard, hS₀x, hS₀y, hxy]⟩
      intro T hT hTsf
      obtain ⟨s, hsS, hsT⟩ := exists_of_ssubset hT
      have hsub : T ⊆ S₀.erase s := fun t ht => mem_erase.2 ⟨fun h => hsT (h ▸ ht), hT.1 ht⟩
      have h2 := (hsf _).1 (simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_mono K k hsub hTsf)
      rcases s with i | j
      · have e1 : (S₀.erase (Sum.inl i)).toLeft.card = x - 1 := by
          have : (S₀.erase (Sum.inl i)).toLeft = S₀.toLeft.erase i := by
            ext j; simp
          rw [this, card_erase_of_mem (mem_toLeft.2 hsS), hS₀x]
        have e2 : (S₀.erase (Sum.inl i)).toRight = S₀.toRight := by
          ext j; simp
        have hx1 : 1 ≤ x := by
          rw [← hS₀x]; exact card_pos.2 ⟨i, mem_toLeft.2 hsS⟩
        rw [e1, e2, hS₀y] at h2
        exact hs2 hx1 h2
      · have e1 : (S₀.erase (Sum.inr j)).toRight.card = y - 1 := by
          have : (S₀.erase (Sum.inr j)).toRight = S₀.toRight.erase j := by
            ext i; simp
          rw [this, card_erase_of_mem (mem_toRight.2 hsS), hS₀y]
        have e2 : (S₀.erase (Sum.inr j)).toLeft = S₀.toLeft := by
          ext i; simp
        have hy1 : 1 ≤ y := by
          rw [← hS₀y]; exact card_pos.2 ⟨j, mem_toRight.2 hsS⟩
        rw [e1, e2, hS₀x] at h2
        exact hs3 hy1 h2

steps.claim: The upper k-star-forming number SF_k(K_{a,b}) equals max a (max b (2 * k - 2)).
steps.explanation: By le_antisymm: every minimal k-star-forming set has cardinality at most max a (max b (2 * k - 2)) by hmin, so the supremum is at most this value (csSup_le). Conversely, since S₀ is minimal k-star-forming and achieves this size, the supremum is at least this value (le_csSup).
steps.code:
apply le_antisymm
    · refine csSup_le ⟨_, hmem⟩ ?_
      rintro n ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩
      exact hmin S hS
    · exact le_csSup hbddS hmem

glossary.BddAbove: A set of numbers is bounded above if there is an element greater than or equal to all members of the set.
glossary.card_erase_of_mem: Removing an element from a finite set decreases its cardinality by 1.
glossary.card_eq_zero: A finite set has cardinality zero if and only if it is empty.
glossary.card_le_univ: Any finite subset of a finite type has cardinality at most the cardinality of the ambient type.
glossary.card_map: An injective mapping (embedding) between finite sets preserves cardinality.
glossary.card_pos: A finite set has strictly positive cardinality if and only if it is nonempty.
glossary.card_toLeft_add_card_toRight: The cardinality of a finite subset of a disjoint sum V ⊕ W equals the sum of the cardinalities of its left and right components.
glossary.completeBipartiteGraph: The complete bipartite graph on two vertex types V and W, with edges precisely between V and W.
glossary.csSup_le: If a nonempty set of numbers has an upper bound a, then its supremum is at most a.
glossary.eq_univ_of_card: A finite subset of a finite type whose cardinality equals that of the ambient type is the entire type (univ).
glossary.eq_univ_of_forall: A subset of a finite type containing every element of the type is the universal set.
glossary.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem: A set is empty if and only if it contains no elements.
glossary.erase_ssubset: Removing an element that belongs to a set yields a strictly smaller (proper) subset.
glossary.exists_of_ssubset: If s₁ is a proper subset of s₂, there exists an element belonging to s₂ that is not in s₁.
glossary.Fin.castLEEmb: The canonical embedding from Fin n into Fin m whenever n ≤ m.
glossary.le_antisymm: If a ≤ b and b ≤ a, then a = b.
glossary.le_csSup: If a set is bounded above and contains an element a, then a is at most the supremum of the set.
glossary.le_rfl: Reflexivity of the ordering: a ≤ a for any element a.
glossary.mem_erase: An element x belongs to s \ {y} if and only if x ∈ s and x ≠ y.
glossary.mem_toLeft: An element a belongs to the left part of a subset of V ⊕ W if and only if Sum.inl a belongs to the subset.
glossary.mem_toRight: An element b belongs to the right part of a subset of V ⊕ W if and only if Sum.inr b belongs to the subset.
glossary.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to its universal set.
glossary.Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero: A natural number is at least 1 if and only if it is nonzero.
glossary.Nat.zero_le: Zero is less than or equal to any natural number.
glossary.Or.inl: Infers the disjunction A ∨ B from a proof of the left disjunct A.
glossary.Set.nonempty_of_mem: If a set contains an element, it is nonempty.
glossary.simple_graph_k_independence_number: The k-independence number β_k(G), defined as the supremum of cardinalities of all k-independent vertex sets in G.
glossary.simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff: A vertex set I is k-independent if and only if every vertex in I has strictly fewer than k neighbors in I.
glossary.simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_iff: For k ≥ 1, a set S is k-star-forming if and only if every vertex outside S either has at least k neighbors in S, or is adjacent to a vertex in S with at least k - 1 neighbors in S.
glossary.simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_mono: The k-star-forming property is monotone under set inclusion: if S ⊆ T and S is k-star-forming, then T is also k-star-forming.
glossary.simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number: The upper k-star-forming number SF_k(G), defined as the supremum of cardinalities of all minimal k-star-forming vertex sets in G.

caveats: The arithmetic deductions throughout the proof—including bounding the cardinality of minimal k-star-forming sets in `hmin`, verifying the case split for the optimal count pair in `hpairs`, and deriving the upper bound on k-independent sets—are handled by the `omega` tactic for Presburger linear arithmetic.

declarations.name: exists_triangle_free_k_independence_number_lt_upper_k_star_forming_number
declarations.informal: There is a triangle-free graph H on 10 vertices with β_4(H) = 7 < 8 = SF_4(H).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_triangle_free_k_independence_number_lt_upper_k_star_forming_number :
    ∃ H : SimpleGraph (Fin 10), H.CliqueFree 3 ∧
      simple_graph_k_independence_number H 4 = 7 ∧
      simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number H 4 = 8
declarations.source:
def star_forming_example_edges : List (ℕ × ℕ) :=
  [(0,2),(0,8),(0,9),(0,1),(1,3),(1,5),(1,4),(1,6),(2,4),(2,5),(2,6),(3,7),(4,7),(5,7),(6,7),(7,8)]

def star_forming_example_graph : SimpleGraph (Fin 10) where
  Adj i j := (i.val, j.val) ∈ star_forming_example_edges ∨ (j.val, i.val) ∈ star_forming_example_edges
  symm := ⟨fun _ _ h => Or.symm h⟩
  loopless := ⟨by decide⟩

instance : DecidableRel star_forming_example_graph.Adj := fun i j => by
  unfold star_forming_example_graph
  infer_instance

theorem exists_triangle_free_k_independence_number_lt_upper_k_star_forming_number :
    ∃ H : SimpleGraph (Fin 10), H.CliqueFree 3 ∧
      simple_graph_k_independence_number H 4 = 7 ∧
      simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number H 4 = 8 := open Finset in by
  set H := star_forming_example_graph with hH
  unfold simple_graph_k_independence_number simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number
  refine ⟨H, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro s hs
    rw [SimpleGraph.is3Clique_iff] at hs
    obtain ⟨a, b, c, hab, hac, hbc, -⟩ := hs
    have key : ∀ a b c : Fin 10, H.Adj a b → H.Adj a c → H.Adj b c → False := by
      decide
    exact key a b c hab hac hbc
  · -- β_4(H) = 7
    have hbdd : BddAbove {n | ∃ I : Finset (Fin 10), simple_graph_is_k_independent H 4 I ∧
        I.card = n} := ⟨10, fun n ⟨I, _, hn⟩ => hn ▸ (card_le_univ I).trans (by simp)⟩
    apply le_antisymm
    · refine csSup_le (Set.nonempty_of_mem (x := 0) ⟨∅, fun v hv => by simp at hv, rfl⟩) ?_
      rintro n ⟨I, hI, rfl⟩
      by_contra hlt
      push_neg at hlt
      obtain ⟨J, hJI, hJc⟩ := exists_subset_card_eq (show 8 ≤ I.card by omega)
      have hJ := simple_graph_is_k_independent_mono H 4 hJI hI
      rw [simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff] at hJ
      have hc : (univ \ J).card = 2 := by
        rw [card_sdiff_of_subset (subset_univ J), card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, hJc]
      obtain ⟨x, y, hxy, hxyJ⟩ := card_eq_two.1 hc
      have hJeq : J = univ.filter (fun u => u ≠ x ∧ u ≠ y) := by
        ext u
        have := congrArg (u ∈ ·) hxyJ
        simp only [mem_sdiff, mem_univ, true_and, mem_insert, mem_singleton, eq_iff_iff] at this
        simp only [mem_filter, mem_univ, true_and]
        tauto
      rw [hJeq] at hJ
      have key : ∀ x y : Fin 10, x ≠ y → ∃ v, v ≠ x ∧ v ≠ y ∧
          4 ≤ ((univ.filter (fun u => u ≠ x ∧ u ≠ y)).filter (H.Adj v)).card := by
        decide
      obtain ⟨v, hvx, hvy, hv⟩ := key x y hxy
      have := hJ v (by simp [hvx, hvy])
      omega
    · apply le_csSup hbdd
      refine ⟨{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8}, ?_, rfl⟩
      rw [simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff]
      decide
  · -- SF_4(H) = 8
    have hloc := simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_iff H 4 (by norm_num)
    have hbdd : BddAbove {n | ∃ S : Finset (Fin 10),
        simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming H 4 S ∧ S.card = n} :=
      ⟨10, fun n ⟨S, _, hn⟩ => hn ▸ (card_le_univ S).trans (by simp)⟩
    have hmem : 8 ∈ {n | ∃ S : Finset (Fin 10),
        simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming H 4 S ∧ S.card = n} := by
      refine ⟨{0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9}, ⟨?_, ?_⟩, rfl⟩
      · rw [hloc]
        decide
      · intro T hT hTsf
        obtain ⟨s, hsS, hsT⟩ := exists_of_ssubset hT
        have hsub : T ⊆ ({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9} : Finset (Fin 10)).erase s := by
          intro x hx
          rw [mem_erase]
          exact ⟨fun h => hsT (h ▸ hx), hT.1 hx⟩
        have h2 := simple_graph_is_k_star_forming_mono H 4 hsub hTsf
        rw [hloc] at h2
        have key : ∀ s ∈ ({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9} : Finset (Fin 10)), ¬ ∀ v,
            v ∉ ({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9} : Finset (Fin 10)).erase s →
            4 ≤ ((({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9} : Finset (Fin 10)).erase s).filter (H.Adj v)).card ∨
              ∃ u ∈ ({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9} : Finset (Fin 10)).erase s, H.Adj v u ∧
                4 - 1 ≤ ((({0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9} : Finset (Fin 10)).erase s).filter
                  (H.Adj u)).card := by
          decide
        exact key s hsS h2
    apply le_antisymm
    · refine csSup_le ⟨8, hmem⟩ ?_
      rintro n ⟨S, ⟨hS, hmin⟩, rfl⟩
      by_contra hlt
      push_neg at hlt
      have hc : (univ \ S).card ≤ 1 := by
        rw [card_sdiff_of_subset (subset_univ S), card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
        omega
      -- some vertex `r ∈ S` can be removed
      have key1 : ∃ r : Fin 10, ∀ v, v ∉ univ.erase r →
          4 ≤ ((univ.erase r).filter (H.Adj v)).card ∨
            ∃ u ∈ univ.erase r, H.Adj v u ∧ 4 - 1 ≤ ((univ.erase r).filter (H.Adj u)).card := by
        decide
      have key2 : ∀ x : Fin 10, ∃ r, r ≠ x ∧ ∀ v, v ∉ ((univ.erase x).erase r) →
          4 ≤ (((univ.erase x).erase r).filter (H.Adj v)).card ∨
            ∃ u ∈ ((univ.erase x).erase r), H.Adj v u ∧
              4 - 1 ≤ ((((univ.erase x).erase r)).filter (H.Adj u)).card := by
        decide
      rcases card_le_one_iff_subset_singleton.1 hc with ⟨x, hx⟩
      by_cases hxS : x ∈ S
      · have hSu : S = univ := by
          ext u
          simp only [mem_univ, iff_true]
          by_contra hu
          have : u ∈ univ \ S := by simp [hu]
          have := hx this
          rw [mem_singleton] at this
          exact hu (this ▸ hxS)
        obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := key1
        exact hmin (univ.erase r) (by rw [hSu]; exact erase_ssubset (mem_univ r)) ((hloc _).2 hr)
      · have hSu : S = univ.erase x := by
          ext u
          simp only [mem_erase, mem_univ, and_true]
          constructor
          · intro hu h
            exact hxS (h ▸ hu)
          · intro hu
            by_contra hu'
            have : u ∈ univ \ S := by simp [hu']
            exact hu (mem_singleton.1 (hx this))
        obtain ⟨r, hrx, hr⟩ := key2 x
        exact hmin ((univ.erase x).erase r)
          (by rw [hSu]; exact erase_ssubset (mem_erase.2 ⟨hrx, mem_univ r⟩)) ((hloc _).2 hr)
    · exact le_csSup hbdd hmem

explanation.summary: The proof constructs an explicit graph H on 10 vertices and establishes that it is triangle-free by exhaustive verification (`decide`). It proves that the 4-independence number β₄(H) is 7 by exhibiting a 7-element 4-independent set and using finite case exhaustion to show that any 8-element subset contains a vertex of degree at least 4 in that subset. Finally, it proves that the upper 4-star-forming number SF₄(H) is 8 by exhibiting a minimal 4-star-forming set of size 8 and verifying by finite search that every subset of size 9 or 10 properly contains a 4-star-forming set, precluding larger minimal sets.

steps.claim: The graph star_forming_example_graph has no self-loops.
steps.explanation: The loopless condition requires that no vertex i is adjacent to itself, which means (i, i) does not appear in the edge list star_forming_example_edges. This is verified by finite computation via decide.
steps.code: loopless := ⟨by decide⟩

steps.claim: Adjacency in star_forming_example_graph is decidable.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the graph definition star_forming_example_graph reveals that adjacency is given by membership of a pair of vertices in a concrete list of edges, which Lean's typeclass synthesis automatically decides via infer_instance.
steps.code:
unfold star_forming_example_graph
  infer_instance

steps.claim: The candidate graph H is triangle-free.
steps.explanation: We instantiate the candidate graph H as star_forming_example_graph and unfold the definitions of the 4-independence number and the upper 4-star-forming number. To show H is triangle-free, we assume s is a 3-clique, use SimpleGraph.is3Clique_iff to write it as three pairwise adjacent vertices a, b, c, and conclude by a finite exhaustive check (decide) that no three vertices in H are pairwise adjacent.
steps.code:
set H := star_forming_example_graph with hH
  unfold simple_graph_k_independence_number simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number
  refine ⟨H, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro s hs
    rw [SimpleGraph.is3Clique_iff] at hs
    obtain ⟨a, b, c, hab, hac, hbc, -⟩ := hs
    have key : ∀ a b c : Fin 10, H.Adj a b → H.Adj a c → H.Adj b c → False := by
      decide
    exact key a b c hab hac hbc

steps.claim: The 4-independence number of H is at most 7: β₄(H) ≤ 7.
steps.explanation: The set of sizes of 4-independent sets is bounded above by 10 (card_le_univ). To show that the supremum is at most 7, we take an arbitrary 4-independent set I and argue by contradiction: if |I| ≥ 8, there exists a subset J ⊆ I of size 8 (exists_subset_card_eq), which must also be 4-independent by monotonicity (simple_graph_is_k_independent_mono). The complement of J has size 10 - 8 = 2 (card_sdiff_of_subset, subset_univ, card_univ, Fintype.card_fin), so it consists of two distinct vertices x, y (card_eq_two). Thus J is the set of all vertices other than x and y (congrArg, mem_sdiff, mem_univ, true_and, mem_insert, mem_singleton, eq_iff_iff, mem_filter). A finite exhaustive check (decide) over all pairs of distinct vertices x, y shows that there is always some vertex v ∉ {x, y} having at least 4 neighbors in J, contradicting the definition of 4-independence (simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff).
steps.code:
· -- β_4(H) = 7
    have hbdd : BddAbove {n | ∃ I : Finset (Fin 10), simple_graph_is_k_independent H 4 I ∧
        I.card = n} := ⟨10, fun n ⟨I, _, hn⟩ => hn ▸ (card_le_univ I).trans (by simp)⟩
    apply le_antisymm
    · refine csSup_le (Set.nonempty_of_mem (x := 0) ⟨∅, fun v hv => by simp at hv, rfl⟩) ?_
      rintro n ⟨I, hI, rfl⟩
      by_contra hlt
      push_neg at hlt
      obtain ⟨J, hJI, hJc⟩ := exists_subset_card_eq (show 8 ≤ I.card by omega)
      have hJ := simple_graph_is_k_independent_mono H 4 hJI hI
      rw [simple_graph_is_k_independent_iff] at hJ
      have hc : (univ \ J).card = 2 := by
        rw [card_sdiff_of_subset (subset_univ J), card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, hJc]
      obtain ⟨x, y, hxy, hxyJ⟩ := card_eq_two.1 hc
      have hJeq : J = univ.filter (fun u => u ≠ x ∧ u ≠ y) := by

The complement Finset.univ \ S has cardinality at most 1 (card_sdiff_of_subset, subset_univ, card_univ, Fintype.card_fin), so it is contained in a singleton {x} (card_le_one_iff_subset_singleton). If x ∈ S, then S is the entire vertex set Finset.univ (mem_univ, iff_true, mem_singleton); but an exhaustive check (decide) shows there is a vertex r such that Finset.univ \ {r} is 4-star-forming (erase_ssubset, mem_univ), contradicting the minimality of S. If x ∉ S, then S = Finset.univ \ {x} (mem_erase, mem_univ, and_true, mem_singleton); another exhaustive check (decide) shows there is some r ≠ x such that Finset.univ \ {x, r} is 4-star-forming (erase_ssubset, mem_erase, mem_univ), again contradicting minimality. apply le_antisymm
    · refine csSup_le ⟨8, hmem⟩ ?_
      rintro n ⟨S, ⟨hS, hmin⟩, rfl⟩
      by_contra hlt
      push_neg at hlt
      have hc : (univ \ S).card ≤ 1 := by
        rw [card_sdiff_of_subset (subset_univ S), card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
        omega
      -- some vertex `r ∈ S` can be removed
      have key1 : ∃ r : Fin 10, ∀ v, v ∉ univ.erase r →
          4 ≤ ((univ.erase r).filter (H.Adj v)).card ∨
            ∃ u ∈ univ.erase r, H.Adj v u ∧ 4 - 1 ≤ ((univ.erase r).filter (H.Adj u)).card := by
        decide
      have key2 : ∀ x : Fin 10, ∃ r, r ≠ x ∧ ∀ v, v ∉ ((univ.erase x).erase r) →
          4 ≤ (((univ.erase x).erase r).filter (H.Adj v)).card ∨
            ∃ u ∈ ((univ.erase x).erase r), H.Adj v u ∧
              4 - 1 ≤ ((((univ.erase x).erase r)).filter (H.Adj u)).card := by
        decide
      rcases card_le_one_iff_subset_singleton.1 hc with ⟨x, hx⟩
      by_cases hxS : x ∈ S
      · have hSu : S = univ := by
          ext u
          simp only [mem_univ, iff_true]
          by_contra hu
          have : u ∈ univ \ S := by simp [hu]
          have := hx this
          rw [mem_singleton] at this
          exact hu (this ▸ hxS)
        obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := key1
        exact hmin (univ.erase r) (by rw [hSu]; exact erase_ssubset (mem_univ r)) ((hloc _).2 hr)
      · have hSu : S = univ.erase x := by
          ext u
          simp only [mem_erase, mem_univ, and_true]
          constructor
          · intro hu h
            exact hxS (h ▸ hu)
          · intro hu
            by_contra hu'
            have : u ∈ univ \ S := by simp [hu']
            exact hu (mem_singleton.1 (hx this))
        obtain ⟨r, hrx, hr⟩ := key2 x
        exact hmin ((univ.erase x).erase r)
          (by rw [hSu]; exact erase_ssubset (mem_erase.2 ⟨hrx, mem_univ r⟩)) ((hloc _).2 hr)
