declarations.name: simple_graph_k_independence_number_eq_card_of_degree_lt
declarations.informal: If every vertex of the finite graph G has degree less than k, then β_k(G) = SF_k(G) = |V(G)|.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_k_independence_number_eq_card_of_degree_lt {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) (h : ∀ v, G.degree v < k) :
    simple_graph_k_independence_number G k = Fintype.card V ∧
      simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number G k = Fintype.card V
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_k_independence_number_eq_card_of_degree_lt {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) (h : ∀ v, G.degree v < k) :
    simple_graph_k_independence_number G k = Fintype.card V ∧
      simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number G k = Fintype.card V := open Finset in by
  have h_ind : simple_graph_is_k_independent G k Finset.univ := by
    intro v _
    have h_set : ({u | u ∈ (univ : Finset V) ∧ G.Adj v u} : Set V) = G.neighborSet v := by
      ext u
      simp
    rw [h_set, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card', ← G.neighborFinset_def]
    exact h v
  have h_sf_univ : simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k Finset.univ :=
    fun v hv => absurd (Finset.mem_univ v) hv
  have h_not_sf : ∀ T ⊂ (univ : Finset V), ¬ simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k T := by
    intro T hT hsf
    obtain ⟨s, -, hsT⟩ := Finset.exists_of_ssubset hT
    obtain ⟨c, L, -, -, hcard, hadj, -⟩ := hsf s hsT
    have h_sub : (L : Set V) ⊆ G.neighborSet c := by
      intro x hx
      exact hadj x (Finset.mem_coe.mp hx)
    have h_le := Set.ncard_le_ncard h_sub (Set.toFinite (G.neighborSet c))
    rw [Set.ncard_coe_finset, hcard, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card', ← G.neighborFinset_def] at h_le
    have h_lt := h c
    change (G.neighborFinset c).card < k at h_lt
    omega
  have h_min_sf : simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming G k Finset.univ :=
    ⟨h_sf_univ, h_not_sf⟩
  constructor
  · dsimp [simple_graph_k_independence_number]
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply csSup_le
      · exact ⟨Fintype.card V, univ, h_ind, card_univ⟩
      · rintro n ⟨I, -, rfl⟩
        exact card_le_univ I
    · apply le_csSup
      · refine ⟨Fintype.card V, ?_⟩
        rintro n ⟨I, -, rfl⟩
        exact card_le_univ I
      · exact ⟨univ, h_ind, card_univ⟩
  · dsimp [simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number]
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply csSup_le
      · exact ⟨Fintype.card V, univ, h_min_sf, card_univ⟩
      · rintro n ⟨S, -, rfl⟩
        exact card_le_univ S
    · apply le_csSup
      · refine ⟨Fintype.card V, ?_⟩
        rintro n ⟨S, -, rfl⟩
        exact card_le_univ S
      · exact ⟨univ, h_min_sf, card_univ⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Proposition 3.1.

explanation.summary: Assuming every vertex of G has degree strictly less than k, the entire vertex set V is k-independent because no vertex has k or more neighbors. Furthermore, V is vacuously k-star-forming, whereas no proper subset of V can be k-star-forming because forming a k-star would require a center of degree at least k; hence V is minimal k-star-forming. Since no subset can exceed |V|, the suprema defining the k-independence number β_k(G) and the upper k-star-forming number SF_k(G) are both attained by V and therefore equal |V|.

steps.claim: The universal vertex set V is k-independent.
steps.explanation: By definition, a set is k-independent if every vertex has strictly fewer than k neighbors in that set. For the full vertex set V (Finset.univ), the set of neighbors of any v ∈ V in Finset.univ is exactly the entire open neighborhood neighborSet v. Rewriting its cardinality into the degree of v, the condition holds immediately from the hypothesis that every vertex has degree strictly less than k.
steps.code:
have h_ind : simple_graph_is_k_independent G k Finset.univ := by
    intro v _
    have h_set : ({u | u ∈ (univ : Finset V) ∧ G.Adj v u} : Set V) = G.neighborSet v := by
      ext u
      simp
    rw [h_set, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card', ← G.neighborFinset_def]
    exact h v

steps.claim: The universal vertex set V is k-star-forming.
steps.explanation: A set S is k-star-forming if every vertex v ∉ S belongs to some star with center and leaves in S ∪ {v}. For S = V (Finset.univ), no vertex lies outside V by Finset.mem_univ, so the condition is vacuously satisfied.
steps.code:
have h_sf_univ : simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k Finset.univ :=
    fun v hv => absurd (Finset.mem_univ v) hv

steps.claim: No proper subset of V is k-star-forming.
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that some proper subset T ⊂ V is k-star-forming. Since T is a strict subset, there exists a vertex s ∉ T. By the definition of k-star-forming applied to s, there must exist a center c and a set L of k leaves adjacent to c in G. Hence L is a subset of the neighborhood of c, which implies k = |L| ≤ deg(c). But the global hypothesis guarantees deg(c) < k, a contradiction.
steps.code:
have h_not_sf : ∀ T ⊂ (univ : Finset V), ¬ simple_graph_is_k_star_forming G k T := by
    intro T hT hsf
    obtain ⟨s, -, hsT⟩ := Finset.exists_of_ssubset hT
    obtain ⟨c, L, -, -, hcard, hadj, -⟩ := hsf s hsT
    have h_sub : (L : Set V) ⊆ G.neighborSet c := by
      intro x hx
      exact hadj x (Finset.mem_coe.mp hx)
    have h_le := Set.ncard_le_ncard h_sub (Set.toFinite (G.neighborSet c))
    rw [Set.ncard_coe_finset, hcard, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card', ← G.neighborFinset_def] at h_le
    have h_lt := h c
    change (G.neighborFinset c).card < k at h_lt
    omega

steps.claim: The universal vertex set V is minimal k-star-forming.
steps.explanation: A set is minimal k-star-forming if it is k-star-forming and no strictly smaller subset is k-star-forming. Combining the facts that V is k-star-forming and that no proper subset of V is k-star-forming gives the result.
steps.code:
have h_min_sf : simple_graph_is_minimal_k_star_forming G k Finset.univ :=
    ⟨h_sf_univ, h_not_sf⟩

steps.claim: The k-independence number β_k(G) equals |V|.
steps.explanation: Splitting the conjunction, the first goal is to evaluate β_k(G), the supremum of sizes of k-independent sets. By antisymmetry (le_antisymm): (1) the supremum is at most |V| via csSup_le because the set of sizes is nonempty (witnessed by V of size |V|) and every set of vertices has cardinality at most |V| (card_le_univ); (2) |V| is at most the supremum via le_csSup because the set of sizes is bounded above by |V| and contains |V| (witnessed by V, which is k-independent).
steps.code:
constructor
  · dsimp [simple_graph_k_independence_number]
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply csSup_le
      · exact ⟨Fintype.card V, univ, h_ind, card_univ⟩
      · rintro n ⟨I, -, rfl⟩
        exact card_le_univ I
    · apply le_csSup
      · refine ⟨Fintype.card V, ?_⟩
        rintro n ⟨I, -, rfl⟩
        exact card_le_univ I
      · exact ⟨univ, h_ind, card_univ⟩

steps.claim: The upper k-star-forming number SF_k(G) equals |V|.
steps.explanation: The second goal is to evaluate SF_k(G), the supremum of sizes of minimal k-star-forming sets. Again by antisymmetry: (1) the supremum is at most |V| via csSup_le because V is a minimal k-star-forming set of size |V| and every subset has size at most |V|; (2) |V| is at most the supremum via le_csSup because the set of sizes is bounded above by |V| and contains |V| as a member.
steps.code:
· dsimp [simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number]
    apply le_antisymm
    · apply csSup_le
      · exact ⟨Fintype.card V, univ, h_min_sf, card_univ⟩
      · rintro n ⟨S, -, rfl⟩
        exact card_le_univ S
    · apply le_csSup
      · refine ⟨Fintype.card V, ?_⟩
        rintro n ⟨S, -, rfl⟩
        exact card_le_univ S
      · exact ⟨univ, h_min_sf, card_univ⟩

glossary.Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card': For any set s with finite subtype, its set cardinality s.ncard equals the cardinality of its finset representation s.toFinset.card.
glossary.G.neighborFinset_def: For any vertex v in G, the finset of its neighbors is by definition the neighborhood set G.neighborSet v converted to a finset.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finset Finset.univ.
glossary.Finset.exists_of_ssubset: If s₁ ⊂ s₂ is a strict subset, then there exists an element x ∈ s₂ such that x ∉ s₁.
glossary.Finset.mem_coe.mp: If an element belongs to the set coercion of a finset, then it belongs to the finset.
glossary.Set.ncard_le_ncard: If s ⊆ t and t is finite, then the set cardinality of s is at most the set cardinality of t.
glossary.Set.toFinite: A set whose subtype is finite is finite as a set.
glossary.Set.ncard_coe_finset: The set cardinality of a coerced finset equals its finset cardinality.
glossary.le_antisymm: If a ≤ b and b ≤ a in a partial order, then a = b.
glossary.csSup_le: The supremum of a nonempty set s is at most a if every element of s is at most a.
glossary.card_univ: The cardinality of Finset.univ equals Fintype.card α.
glossary.card_le_univ: The cardinality of any finset of α is at most Fintype.card α.
glossary.le_csSup: If a set s is bounded above, then any element in s is at most the supremum of s.

caveats: The definitions of β_k(G) and SF_k(G) use `sSup` over sets of natural numbers rather than maximum over a finite set, requiring explicit proofs of nonemptiness and upper-boundedness before taking suprema.
In line 25, the `omega` tactic automatically handles the linear integer arithmetic contradiction between k ≤ deg(c) and deg(c) < k.

declarations.name: exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf
declarations.informal: Let E, F be k-dimensional subspaces of a finite-dimensional vector space with dim(E ∩ F) = k − j, 0 ≤ j ≤ k. Then some k-dimensional subspace W has dim(E ∩ W) = dim(W ∩ F) = k − j.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V]
    [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (k j : ℕ) (hjk : j ≤ k) (E F : Submodule K V)
    (hE : Module.finrank K E = k) (hF : Module.finrank K F = k)
    (hEF : Module.finrank K ↥(E ⊓ F) = k - j) :
    ∃ W : Submodule K V, Module.finrank K W = k ∧ Module.finrank K ↥(E ⊓ W) = k - j ∧
      Module.finrank K ↥(W ⊓ F) = k - j
declarations.source:
open Submodule

lemma exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_relative_complement
    {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    {C E : Submodule K V} (hCE : C ≤ E) :
    ∃ E₁ : Submodule K V, E₁ ≤ E ∧ C ⊔ E₁ = E ∧ C ⊓ E₁ = ⊥ := by
  obtain ⟨E₁', hcomp⟩ := Submodule.exists_isCompl (C.comap E.subtype)
  refine ⟨E₁'.map E.subtype, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact Submodule.map_subtype_le E E₁'
  · have hC : C = map E.subtype (comap E.subtype C) := by
      rw [map_comap_subtype, inf_comm, inf_of_le_left hCE]
    rw [hC, ← Submodule.map_sup, hcomp.sup_eq_top, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype]
  · have hC : C = map E.subtype (comap E.subtype C) := by
      rw [map_comap_subtype, inf_comm, inf_of_le_left hCE]
    rw [hC, ← Submodule.map_inf E.subtype (Submodule.subtype_injective E), hcomp.inf_eq_bot, Submodule.map_bot]

def exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap
    {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    (E₁ F₁ : Submodule K V) (f : ↥E₁ ≃ₗ[K] ↥F₁) : ↥E₁ →ₗ[K] V :=
  E₁.subtype + F₁.subtype.comp f.toLinearMap

lemma exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap_apply
    {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    (E₁ F₁ : Submodule K V) (f : ↥E₁ ≃ₗ[K] ↥F₁) (x : E₁) :
    exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap E₁ F₁ f x = (x : V) + (f x : V) := by
  simp [exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap]

lemma exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap_injective
    {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    {E F E₁ F₁ : Submodule K V} (hE₁ : E₁ ≤ E) (hF₁ : F₁ ≤ F)
    (hC_E₁ : (E ⊓ F) ⊓ E₁ = ⊥) (f : ↥E₁ ≃ₗ[K] ↥F₁) :
    Function.Injective (exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap E₁ F₁ f) := by
  rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, LinearMap.ker_eq_bot']
  intro x hx
  rw [exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap_apply] at hx
  have hx_eq : (x : V) = - (f x : V) := eq_neg_of_add_eq_zero_left hx
  have h1 : (x : V) ∈ E := hE₁ x.2
  have h2 : (x : V) ∈ F := by
    rw [hx_eq]
    exact Submodule.neg_mem F (hF₁ (f x).2)
  have h3 : (x : V) ∈ (E ⊓ F) ⊓ E₁ := Submodule.mem_inf.mpr ⟨Submodule.mem_inf.mpr ⟨h1, h2⟩, x.2⟩
  rw [hC_E₁] at h3
  exact Subtype.ext (Submodule.mem_bot (R := K).mp h3)

lemma exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_range_graphMap_inf_E_eq_bot
    {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    {E F E₁ F₁ : Submodule K V}
    (hE₁ : E₁ ≤ E) (hF₁ : F₁ ≤ F) (hC_F₁ : (E ⊓ F) ⊓ F₁ = ⊥)
    (f : ↥E₁ ≃ₗ[K] ↥F₁) :
    (exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap E₁ F₁ f).range ⊓ E = ⊥ := by
  rw [Submodule.eq_bot_iff]
  intro v hv
  rw [Submodule.mem_inf] at hv
  rcases hv with ⟨hvG, hvE⟩
  rw [LinearMap.mem_range] at hvG
  rcases hvG with ⟨x, rfl⟩
  have hfx : (f x : V) = (exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap E₁ F₁ f x) - (x : V) := by
    rw [exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap_apply, add_sub_cancel_left]
  have hfx_in_E : (f x : V) ∈ E := by
    rw [hfx]
    exact Submodule.sub_mem E hvE (hE₁ x.2)
  have hfx_in_F : (f x : V) ∈ F := hF₁ (f x).2
  have hfx_in_C_F₁ : (f x : V) ∈ (E ⊓ F) ⊓ F₁ :=
    Submodule.mem_inf.mpr ⟨Submodule.mem_inf.mpr ⟨hfx_in_E, hfx_in_F⟩, (f x).2⟩
  rw [hC_F₁, Submodule.mem_bot (R := K)] at hfx_in_C_F₁
  have hfx0 : f x = 0 := Subtype.ext hfx_in_C_F₁
  have hx0 : x = 0 := map_eq_zero_iff f.toLinearMap (LinearEquiv.injective f) |>.mp hfx0
  simp [hx0, exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap_apply]

lemma exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_range_graphMap_inf_F_eq_bot
    {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    {E F E₁ F₁ : Submodule K V}
    (hE₁ : E₁ ≤ E) (hF₁ : F₁ ≤ F) (hC_E₁ : (E ⊓ F) ⊓ E₁ = ⊥)
    (f : ↥E₁ ≃ₗ[K] ↥F₁) :
    (exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap E₁ F₁ f).range ⊓ F = ⊥ := by
  rw [Submodule.eq_bot_iff]
  intro v hv
  rw [Submodule.mem_inf] at hv
  rcases hv with ⟨hvG, hvF⟩
  rw [LinearMap.mem_range] at hvG
  rcases hvG with ⟨x, rfl⟩
  have hx_sub : (x : V) = (exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap E₁ F₁ f x) - (f x : V) := by
    rw [exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap_apply, add_sub_cancel_right]
  have hx_in_F : (x : V) ∈ F := by
    rw [hx_sub]
    exact Submodule.sub_mem F hvF (hF₁ (f x).2)
  have hx_in_E : (x : V) ∈ E := hE₁ x.2
  have hx_in_C_E₁ : (x : V) ∈ (E ⊓ F) ⊓ E₁ :=
    Submodule.mem_inf.mpr ⟨Submodule.mem_inf.mpr ⟨hx_in_E, hx_in_F⟩, x.2⟩
  rw [hC_E₁, Submodule.mem_bot (R := K)] at hx_in_C_E₁
  have hx0 : x = 0 := Subtype.ext hx_in_C_E₁
  simp [hx0, exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap_apply]

theorem exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf {K V : Type*} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V]
    [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (k j : ℕ) (hjk : j ≤ k) (E F : Submodule K V)
    (hE : Module.finrank K E = k) (hF : Module.finrank K F = k)
    (hEF : Module.finrank K ↥(E ⊓ F) = k - j) :
    ∃ W : Submodule K V, Module.finrank K W = k ∧ Module.finrank K ↥(E ⊓ W) = k - j ∧
      Module.finrank K ↥(W ⊓ F) = k - j := by
  set C := E ⊓ F
  have hCE : C ≤ E := inf_le_left
  have hCF : C ≤ F := inf_le_right
  obtain ⟨E₁, hE₁le, hCE_sup, hCE_inf⟩ :=
    exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_relative_complement hCE
  obtain ⟨F₁, hF₁le, hCF_sup, hCF_inf⟩ :=
    exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_relative_complement hCF
  have h_dim_E₁ : Module.finrank K ↥E₁ = j := by
    have h := Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq C E₁
    rw [hCE_sup, hCE_inf, finrank_bot, hE, hEF] at h
    omega
  have h_dim_F₁ : Module.finrank K ↥F₁ = j := by
    have h := Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq C F₁
    rw [hCF_sup, hCF_inf, finrank_bot, hF, hEF] at h
    omega
  have h_dim_eq : Module.finrank K ↥E₁ = Module.finrank K ↥F₁ := by
    rw [h_dim_E₁, h_dim_F₁]
  let f : ↥E₁ ≃ₗ[K] ↥F₁ := LinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq (↥E₁) (↥F₁) h_dim_eq
  let g := exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap E₁ F₁ f
  let Γ := g.range
  have hginj : Function.Injective g :=
    exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_graphMap_injective hE₁le hF₁le hCE_inf f
  have h_dim_Γ : Module.finrank K ↥Γ = j := by
    rw [LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj hginj, h_dim_E₁]
  have hΓE : Γ ⊓ E = ⊥ :=
    exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_range_graphMap_inf_E_eq_bot hE₁le hF₁le hCF_inf f
  have hΓF : Γ ⊓ F = ⊥ :=
    exists_submodule_finrank_inf_eq_of_finrank_inf_range_graphMap_inf_F_eq_bot hE₁le hF₁le hCE_inf f
  let W := C ⊔ Γ
  refine ⟨W, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [W]
    have hCΓ_le : C ⊓ Γ ≤ E ⊓ Γ := inf_le_inf_right Γ hCE
    have hEΓ : E ⊓ Γ = ⊥ := by rw [inf_comm, hΓE]
    have hCΓ : C ⊓ Γ = ⊥ := le_bot_iff.mp (hCΓ_le.trans (le_of_eq hEΓ))
    have h := Submodule.finrank_sup_add_finrank_inf_eq C Γ
    rw [hCΓ, finrank_bot, hEF, h_dim_Γ] at h
    omega
  · have hEW : E ⊓ W = C := by
      rw [inf_comm]
      change (C ⊔ Γ) ⊓ E = C
      rw [sup_inf_assoc_of_le _ hCE, hΓE, sup_bot_eq]
    rw [hEW, hEF]
  · have hWF : W ⊓ F = C := by
      change (C ⊔ Γ) ⊓ F = C
      rw [sup_inf_assoc_of_le _ hCF, hΓF, sup_bot_eq]
    rw [hWF, hEF]

explanation.summary: Let $C = E \\cap F$. Choose relative complements $E_1 \\le E$ and $F_1 \\le F$ of $C$, each of dimension $j$. Choosing an isomorphism $f : E_1 \\to F_1$, define the graph subspace $\\Gamma = \\{x + f(x) : x \\in E_1\\}$. Then $\\Gamma$ has dimension $j$ and intersects both $E$ and $F$ in $\\{0\\}$. The subspace $W = C \\oplus \\Gamma$ has dimension $(k - j) + j = k$ and satisfies $E \\cap W = C$ and $W \\cap F = C$ by modularity.

declarations.name: dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound
declarations.informal: Let f(p, d) ≥ 0 and g(p) ≥ 0 with g nondecreasing, f(p, k) ≤ p·g(p) for p ≥ 1, and for every p ≥ 1, d > k there are positive integers p_i ≤ p/2 with Σ p_i ≤ p and f(p, d) ≤ f(p, d−1) + Σ f(p_i, d). Then f(p, d) ≤ p·g(p)·C(⌊log₂ p⌋ + d − k, d − k) for all p ≥ 1, d ≥ k.
declarations.statement:
theorem dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound (k : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (g : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ p d, 0 ≤ f p d) (hg : ∀ p, 0 ≤ g p) (hmono : Monotone g)
    (hbase : ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → f p k ≤ p * g p)
    (hrec : ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → ∀ d, k < d → ∃ ps : List ℕ, (∀ x ∈ ps, 1 ≤ x ∧ 2 * x ≤ p) ∧
      ps.sum ≤ p ∧ f p d ≤ f p (d - 1) + (ps.map (fun x => f x d)).sum) :
    ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → ∀ d, k ≤ d → f p d ≤ p * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p + (d - k)).choose (d - k))
declarations.source:
lemma dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound_choose_pascal_step (L m : ℕ) (hL : 1 ≤ L) :
    (L + m).choose m + (L - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) = (L + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) := by
  have heq : L - 1 + (m + 1) = L + m := by lia
  rw [heq]
  have h_id := (Nat.choose_succ_succ (L + m) m).symm
  have heq2 : (L + m).succ = L + (m + 1) := by lia
  rw [heq2] at h_id
  exact h_id

lemma dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound_list_sum_bound (ps : List ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℝ) (C : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ x ∈ ps, f x ≤ (x : ℝ) * C) :
    (ps.map f).sum ≤ (ps.sum : ℝ) * C := by
  induction ps with
  | nil => simp
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, Nat.cast_add]
    have hx : f x ≤ (x : ℝ) * C := h x (List.mem_cons_self ..)
    have hxs : (xs.map f).sum ≤ (xs.sum : ℝ) * C :=
      ih (fun y hy => h y (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hy))
    linarith

theorem dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound (k : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (g : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ p d, 0 ≤ f p d) (hg : ∀ p, 0 ≤ g p) (hmono : Monotone g)
    (hbase : ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → f p k ≤ p * g p)
    (hrec : ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → ∀ d, k < d → ∃ ps : List ℕ, (∀ x ∈ ps, 1 ≤ x ∧ 2 * x ≤ p) ∧
      ps.sum ≤ p ∧ f p d ≤ f p (d - 1) + (ps.map (fun x => f x d)).sum) :
    ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → ∀ d, k ≤ d → f p d ≤ p * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p + (d - k)).choose (d - k)) := by
  have H : ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → f p (k + m) ≤ p * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p + m).choose m) := by
    intro m
    induction m with
    | zero =>
      intro p hp
      simp only [add_zero, Nat.choose_zero_right, Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
      exact hbase p hp
    | succ m ih =>
      intro p
      induction p using Nat.strong_induction_on with
      | h p ih_p =>
        intro hp
        rcases (Nat.lt_or_ge 1 p) with hp_gt | hp_le
        · -- p ≥ 2
          have hp2 : 2 ≤ p := hp_gt
          obtain ⟨ps, hps_prop, hps_sum, hrec_le⟩ := hrec p hp (k + (m + 1)) (by lia)
          have h_pred : k + (m + 1) - 1 = k + m := by lia
          rw [h_pred] at hrec_le
          have h_ih_p : f p (k + m) ≤ p * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p + m).choose m) := ih p hp
          let C : ℝ := g p * ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ)
          have h_elem : ∀ x ∈ ps, f x (k + (m + 1)) ≤ (x : ℝ) * C := by
            intro x hx
            have hx_prop := hps_prop x hx
            have hx1 : 1 ≤ x := hx_prop.1
            have hxp : 2 * x ≤ p := hx_prop.2
            have hx_lt_p : x < p := by lia
            have hx_ih := ih_p x hx_lt_p hx1
            have hx_le_p : x ≤ p := by lia
            have hg_le : g x ≤ g p := hmono hx_le_p
            have hlog_le : Nat.log 2 x + 1 ≤ Nat.log 2 p := by
              have h1 : Nat.log 2 (x * 2) ≤ Nat.log 2 p := by
                rw [Nat.mul_comm]
                exact Nat.log_mono_right hxp
              have h2 : Nat.log 2 (x * 2) = Nat.log 2 x + 1 :=
                Nat.log_mul_base (by decide) (by lia)
              rwa [h2] at h1
            have hchoose_le : (Nat.log 2 x + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) ≤
                (Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) :=
              Nat.choose_le_choose (m + 1) (by lia)
            refine hx_ih.trans ?_
            have h1 : (x : ℝ) * g x ≤ (x : ℝ) * g p :=
              mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hg_le (Nat.cast_nonneg x)
            have hstep1 : (x : ℝ) * g x * ((Nat.log 2 x + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) ≤
                (x : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 x + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) :=
              mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h1 (Nat.cast_nonneg _)
            have hchoose_cast : ((Nat.log 2 x + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) ≤
                ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) := by
              exact_mod_cast hchoose_le
            have hstep2 : (x : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 x + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) ≤
                (x : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) :=
              mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hchoose_cast (mul_nonneg (Nat.cast_nonneg x) (hg p))
            have hstep_comb : (x : ℝ) * g x * ((Nat.log 2 x + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) ≤
                (x : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) :=
              hstep1.trans hstep2
            have heq_C : (x : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) =
                (x : ℝ) * C := by
              dsimp [C]
              ring
            rw [heq_C] at hstep_comb
            exact hstep_comb
          have h_sum_le := dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound_list_sum_bound ps (fun x => f x (k + (m + 1))) C h_elem
          have hC_nonneg : 0 ≤ C := mul_nonneg (hg p) (Nat.cast_nonneg _)
          have h_sum_le_p : (ps.sum : ℝ) * C ≤ (p : ℝ) * C := by
            have : (ps.sum : ℝ) ≤ (p : ℝ) := Nat.cast_le.mpr hps_sum
            nlinarith
          have h_sum_final : (ps.map (fun x => f x (k + (m + 1)))).sum ≤ (p : ℝ) * C :=
            h_sum_le.trans h_sum_le_p
          have hL_pos : 1 ≤ Nat.log 2 p := Nat.log_pos (by decide) hp2
          have h_pascal := dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound_choose_pascal_step (Nat.log 2 p) m hL_pos
          have h_pascal_R : ((Nat.log 2 p + m).choose m : ℝ) +
              ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) =
              ((Nat.log 2 p + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) := by
            exact_mod_cast h_pascal
          have h_sum_bound : (p : ℝ) * C =
              (p : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) := by
            dsimp [C]
            ring
          rw [h_sum_bound] at h_sum_final
          refine hrec_le.trans ?_
          calc f p (k + m) + (ps.map (fun x => f x (k + (m + 1)))).sum
            ≤ (p : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p + m).choose m : ℝ) +
              (p : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) :=
              add_le_add h_ih_p h_sum_final
            _ = (p : ℝ) * g p * (((Nat.log 2 p + m).choose m : ℝ) +
              ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ)) := by ring
            _ = (p : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) := by rw [h_pascal_R]
        · -- p = 1
          have hp1 : p = 1 := by lia
          subst hp1
          obtain ⟨ps, hps_prop, _, hrec_le⟩ := hrec 1 (by lia) (k + (m + 1)) (by lia)
          have hps_nil : ps = [] := by
            cases ps with
            | nil => rfl
            | cons x xs =>
              have := (hps_prop x (List.mem_cons_self ..)).2
              have := (hps_prop x (List.mem_cons_self ..)).1
              lia
          rw [hps_nil] at hrec_le
          simp only [List.map_nil, List.sum_nil, add_zero] at hrec_le
          have h_pred : k + (m + 1) - 1 = k + m := by lia
          rw [h_pred] at hrec_le
          have h_ih := ih 1 (by lia)
          have h_log : Nat.log 2 1 = 0 := Nat.log_one_right 2
          rw [h_log] at h_ih ⊢
          simp only [zero_add, Nat.choose_self, Nat.cast_one, mul_one] at h_ih ⊢
          exact hrec_le.trans h_ih
  intro p hp d hd
  have h := H (d - k) p hp
  rwa [Nat.add_sub_of_le hd] at h

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by induction on the dimension difference m = d - k. For the inductive step, strong induction on p bounds each term in the partition ps: because every part satisfies x ≤ p/2, the logarithmic term drops by at least 1, allowing the strong induction hypothesis and the monotonicity of g to bound the partition's total sum by p · g(p) · C(⌊log₂ p⌋ - 1 + (m + 1), m + 1). Adding this to the inductive bound on f(p, k + m) and applying Pascal's recurrence identity completes the step for p ≥ 2, while the case p = 1 is immediate because any valid partition must be empty.

steps.claim: For any positive integer L and any m, C(L + m, m) + C(L - 1 + (m + 1), m + 1) = C(L + (m + 1), m + 1).
steps.explanation: Since L ≥ 1, linear integer arithmetic gives (L - 1) + (m + 1) = L + m. Substituting this equality into the second term changes it to C(L + m, m + 1). By Pascal's recurrence Nat.choose_succ_succ with n = L + m and k = m, the sum equals C((L + m) + 1, m + 1) = C(L + (m + 1), m + 1).
steps.code:
lemma dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound_choose_pascal_step (L m : ℕ) (hL : 1 ≤ L) :
    (L + m).choose m + (L - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) = (L + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) := by
  have heq : L - 1 + (m + 1) = L + m := by lia
  rw [heq]
  have h_id := (Nat.choose_succ_succ (L + m) m).symm
  have heq2 : (L + m).succ = L + (m + 1) := by lia
  rw [heq2] at h_id
  exact h_id

steps.claim: If each element x of a list ps satisfies f(x) ≤ x · C, then the sum of f over ps is bounded by (Σ ps) · C.
steps.explanation: The claim is proved by structural induction on ps. The empty list case is trivial (0 ≤ 0). For a cons list x :: xs, the sum splits into f(x) + Σ_{y ∈ xs} f(y). Applying the hypothesis f(x) ≤ x · C to the head and the induction hypothesis Σ_{y ∈ xs} f(y) ≤ (Σ xs) · C to the tail, linear arithmetic combines the bounds to (x + Σ xs) · C.
steps.code:
lemma dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound_list_sum_bound (ps : List ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℝ) (C : ℝ)
    (h : ∀ x ∈ ps, f x ≤ (x : ℝ) * C) :
    (ps.map f).sum ≤ (ps.sum : ℝ) * C := by
  induction ps with
  | nil => simp
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, Nat.cast_add]
    have hx : f x ≤ (x : ℝ) * C := h x (List.mem_cons_self ..)
    have hxs : (xs.map f).sum ≤ (xs.sum : ℝ) * C :=
      ih (fun y hy => h y (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hy))
    linarith

steps.claim: The theorem is reparameterized by induction on m = d - k, and the base case m = 0 holds: f(p, k) ≤ p · g(p) · C(⌊log₂ p⌋ + 0, 0) for all p ≥ 1.
steps.explanation: We formulate an induction hypothesis H asserting that for all m and all p ≥ 1, f(p, k + m) ≤ p · g(p) · C(⌊log₂ p⌋ + m, m), and proceed by induction on m. In the base case m = 0, the dimension is k + 0 = k and C(⌊log₂ p⌋ + 0, 0) = 1. The target simplifies to f(p, k) ≤ p · g(p), which is directly assumed by the base hypothesis hbase.
steps.code:
theorem dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound (k : ℕ) (f : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ) (g : ℕ → ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ p d, 0 ≤ f p d) (hg : ∀ p, 0 ≤ g p) (hmono : Monotone g)
    (hbase : ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → f p k ≤ p * g p)
    (hrec : ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → ∀ d, k < d → ∃ ps : List ℕ, (∀ x ∈ ps, 1 ≤ x ∧ 2 * x ≤ p) ∧
      ps.sum ≤ p ∧ f p d ≤ f p (d - 1) + (ps.map (fun x => f x d)).sum) :
    ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → ∀ d, k ≤ d → f p d ≤ p * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p + (d - k)).choose (d - k)) := by
  have H : ∀ m : ℕ, ∀ p, 1 ≤ p → f p (k + m) ≤ p * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p + m).choose m) := by
    intro m
    induction m with
    | zero =>
      intro p hp
      simp only [add_zero, Nat.choose_zero_right, Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
      exact hbase p hp

steps.claim: For the induction step from m to m + 1, strong induction on p ≥ 1 is set up, and for p ≥ 2, the recurrence unpacks a partition ps and bounds the lower-dimension term f(p, k + m).
steps.explanation: To prove the statement for m + 1, we use strong induction on p with Nat.strong_induction_on, assuming the bound holds for all positive x < p at dimension k + m + 1. We split cases on p using Nat.lt_or_ge: either p ≥ 2 or p ≤ 1. For p ≥ 2, the recurrence hypothesis hrec at dimension k + (m + 1) > k yields a list ps of positive integers with 2x ≤ p for all x ∈ ps, Σ ps ≤ p, and f(p, k + m + 1) ≤ f(p, k + m) + Σ_{x ∈ ps} f(x, k + m + 1). The outer induction hypothesis on m bounds the first term by f(p, k + m) ≤ p · g(p) · C(⌊log₂ p⌋ + m, m).
steps.code:
| succ m ih =>
      intro p
      induction p using Nat.strong_induction_on with
      | h p ih_p =>
        intro hp
        rcases (Nat.lt_or_ge 1 p) with hp_gt | hp_le
        · -- p ≥ 2
          have hp2 : 2 ≤ p := hp_gt
          obtain ⟨ps, hps_prop, hps_sum, hrec_le⟩ := hrec p hp (k + (m + 1)) (by lia)
          have h_pred : k + (m + 1) - 1 = k + m := by lia
          rw [h_pred] at hrec_le
          have h_ih_p : f p (k + m) ≤ p * g p * ((Nat.log 2 p + m).choose m) := ih p hp

steps.claim: Each partition element x ∈ ps satisfies f(x, k + m + 1) ≤ x · C, where C = g(p) · C(⌊log₂ p⌋ - 1 + (m + 1), m + 1).
steps.explanation: For each x ∈ ps, the recurrence guarantees 1 ≤ x and 2x ≤ p, so x < p. The inner strong induction hypothesis on p applies to x at dimension k + m + 1, giving f(x, k + m + 1) ≤ x · g(x) · C(⌊log₂ x⌋ + m + 1, m + 1). Since x ≤ p and g is monotone, g(x) ≤ g(p). From 2x ≤ p, monotonicity of the base-2 logarithm gives ⌊log₂(2x)⌋ ≤ ⌊log₂ p⌋. Since ⌊log₂(2x)⌋ = ⌊log₂ x⌋ + 1 by Nat.log_mul_base, we have ⌊log₂ x⌋ + 1 ≤ ⌊log₂ p⌋, which implies ⌊log₂ x⌋ ≤ ⌊log₂ p⌋ - 1. Monotonicity of binomial coefficients then bounds C(⌊log₂ x⌋ + m + 1, m + 1) ≤ C(⌊log₂ p⌋ - 1 + (m + 1), m + 1). Combining these inequalities yields f(x, k + m + 1) ≤ x · C.

          have h_elem : ∀ x ∈ ps, f x (k + (m + 1)) ≤ (x : ℝ) * C := by

            have hstep1 : (x : ℝ) * g x * ((Nat.log 2 x + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) ≤

              mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right h1 (Nat.cast_nonneg _)
            have hchoose_cast : ((Nat.log 2 x + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) ≤
                ((Nat.log 2 p - 1 + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) := by
              exact_mod_cast hchoose_le
            have hstep2 : (x : ℝ) * g p * ((Nat.log 2 x + (m + 1)).choose (m + 1) : ℝ) ≤

have h_sum_le := dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound_list_sum_bound ps (fun x => f x (k + (m + 1))) C h_elem

steps.claim: For p = 1, the partition ps is necessarily empty, and the bound follows directly from the induction hypothesis on m.
steps.explanation: When p = 1, any element x ∈ ps must satisfy 1 ≤ x and 2x ≤ 1, which has no integer solution. Thus ps = [], so the partition sum is zero and f(1, k + m + 1) ≤ f(1, k + m). Since ⌊log₂ 1⌋ = 0, C(⌊log₂ 1⌋ + m, m) = C(m, m) = 1, so the outer induction hypothesis gives f(1, k + m) ≤ g(1). Similarly, the target bound at m + 1 evaluates to 1 · g(1) · C(0 + m + 1, m + 1) = g(1). Transitivity closes the case p = 1.

· -- p = 1
          have hp1 : p = 1 := by lia
          subst hp1
          obtain ⟨ps, hps_prop, _, hrec_le⟩ := hrec 1 (by lia) (k + (m + 1)) (by lia)
          have hps_nil : ps = [] := by
            cases ps with
            | nil => rfl
            | cons x xs =>
              have := (hps_prop x (List.mem_cons_self ..)).2
              have := (hps_prop x (List.mem_cons_self ..)).1
              lia
          rw [hps_nil] at hrec_le

          rw [h_pred] at hrec_le
          have h_ih := ih 1 (by lia)

steps.claim: Specializing H with m = d - k yields the theorem for all p ≥ 1 and d ≥ k.
steps.explanation: Given p ≥ 1 and d ≥ k, we instantiate H with m = d - k. Since k ≤ d, Nat.add_sub_of_le gives k + (d - k) = d. Rewriting this sum in H completes the proof.
steps.code:
intro p hp d hd
  have h := H (d - k) p hp
  rwa [Nat.add_sub_of_le hd] at h

glossary.Nat.choose_succ_succ: Pascal's recurrence for binomial coefficients: Nat.choose (n + 1) (k + 1) = Nat.choose n k + Nat.choose n (k + 1).
glossary.List.map_cons: Mapping a function over a cons list applies the function to the head and maps over the tail: List.map f (a :: l) = f a :: List.map f l.
glossary.List.sum_cons: The sum of a cons list is the head element plus the sum of the tail: (a :: l).sum = a + l.sum.
glossary.Nat.cast_add: The cast from natural numbers to real numbers preserves addition: ↑(m + n) = ↑m + ↑n.
glossary.List.mem_cons_self: The head element of a list is a member of that list: a ∈ a :: l.
glossary.List.mem_cons_of_mem: If an element belongs to the tail of a list, it belongs to the whole list: a ∈ l → a ∈ y :: l.
glossary.add_zero: Adding zero to any element leaves it unchanged: a + 0 = a.
glossary.Nat.choose_zero_right: Choosing 0 from any natural number n equals 1: Nat.choose n 0 = 1.
glossary.Nat.cast_one: The cast of 1 as a natural number is 1 in the target semiring: ↑1 = 1.
glossary.mul_one: Multiplying any element by 1 leaves it unchanged: a * 1 = a.
glossary.Nat.strong_induction_on: Principle of strong induction on natural numbers: to prove P(n) for all n, it suffices to prove P(n) assuming P(m) holds for all m < n.
glossary.Nat.lt_or_ge: For any two natural numbers n and m, either n < m or n ≥ m.
glossary.Nat.mul_comm: Multiplication of natural numbers is commutative: n * m = m * n.
glossary.Nat.log_mono_right: The discrete base-b logarithm is nondecreasing in its argument: if n ≤ m, then Nat.log b n ≤ Nat.log b m.
glossary.Nat.log_mul_base: For base b > 1 and n ≠ 0, multiplying n by b increases its discrete logarithm by 1: Nat.log b (n * b) = Nat.log b n + 1.
glossary.Nat.choose_le_choose: The binomial coefficient Nat.choose a c is nondecreasing in a: if a ≤ b, then Nat.choose a c ≤ Nat.choose b c.
glossary.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left: Multiplying an inequality by a nonnegative element on the left preserves the inequality: if b ≤ c and 0 ≤ a, then a * b ≤ a * c.
glossary.Nat.cast_nonneg: The cast of any natural number to an ordered semiring is nonnegative: 0 ≤ ↑n.
glossary.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right: Multiplying an inequality by a nonnegative element on the right preserves the inequality: if b ≤ c and 0 ≤ a, then b * a ≤ c * a.
glossary.mul_nonneg: The product of two nonnegative elements is nonnegative: if 0 ≤ a and 0 ≤ b, then 0 ≤ a * b.
glossary.dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound_list_: If each element x of a list ps satisfies f(x) ≤ x * C, then the sum of f(x) over ps is bounded by (ps.sum) * C.
glossary.Nat.cast_le: The cast from natural numbers to real numbers preserves non-strict inequalities: ↑m ≤ ↑n ↔ m ≤ n.
glossary.Nat.log_pos: For base b > 1, if b ≤ n, then Nat.log b n is strictly positive (at least 1).
glossary.dimension_lifting_recurrence_bound_choos: For L ≥ 1, Nat.choose (L + m) m + Nat.choose (L - 1 + (m + 1)) (m + 1) = Nat.choose (L + (m + 1)) (m + 1).
glossary.add_le_add: Adding two inequalities preserves the inequality: if a ≤ b and c ≤ d, then a + c ≤ b + d.
glossary.List.map_nil: Mapping a function over the empty list produces the empty list: List.map f [] = [].
glossary.List.sum_nil: The sum of the empty list is zero: [].sum = 0.
glossary.Nat.log_one_right: The logarithm of 1 in any base is 0: Nat.log b 1 = 0.
glossary.zero_add: Zero is the left identity for addition: 0 + a = a.
glossary.Nat.choose_self: Choosing n from n equals 1: Nat.choose n n = 1.
glossary.Nat.add_sub_of_le: If a ≤ b, then a + (b - a) = b for natural numbers.

declarations.name: exists_bin_packing_of_total_capacity_ge
declarations.informal: If b bins have capacities C_j and current loads L_j ≤ C_j with Σ L_j + (m + b)η ≤ Σ C_j (η > 0), then m items of size η can be added to the bins without exceeding any capacity.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bin_packing_of_total_capacity_ge {b m : ℕ} (C L : Fin b → ℝ) (η : ℝ)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hL : ∀ j, L j ≤ C j) (h : ∑ j, L j + (m + b) * η ≤ ∑ j, C j) :
    ∃ f : Fin m → Fin b, ∀ j, L j + (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => f i = j)).card * η ≤ C j
declarations.source:
theorem exists_bin_packing_of_total_capacity_ge {b m : ℕ} (C L : Fin b → ℝ) (η : ℝ)
    (hη : 0 < η) (hL : ∀ j, L j ≤ C j) (h : ∑ j, L j + (m + b) * η ≤ ∑ j, C j) :
    ∃ f : Fin m → Fin b, ∀ j, L j + (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => f i = j)).card * η ≤ C j := by
  revert L
  induction m with
  | zero =>
    intro L hL h
    refine ⟨fun i => i.elim0, ?_⟩
    intro j
    have : (Finset.univ.filter (fun (i : Fin 0) => (fun _ => i.elim0) i = j)) = ∅ := by
      rw [Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
      intro i
      exact i.elim0
    rw [this, Finset.card_empty, Nat.cast_zero, MulZeroClass.zero_mul, add_zero]
    exact hL j
  | succ m ih =>
    intro L hL h
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos b with rfl | hb
    · simp only [Finset.univ_eq_empty, Finset.sum_empty, zero_add] at h
      have hpos : 0 < ((m + 1 : ℝ) * η) := by positivity
      push_cast at h
      linarith
    · have hex : ∃ j₀ : Fin b, L j₀ + η ≤ C j₀ := by
        by_contra! h_all
        have h_ne : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin b)).Nonempty :=
          Finset.univ_nonempty_iff.mpr (Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp hb)
        have h1 : ∑ j, C j < ∑ j, (L j + η) := Finset.sum_lt_sum_of_nonempty h_ne (fun j _ => h_all j)
        rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul] at h1
        have hm : 0 ≤ (m : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg m
        have h_exp : (↑(m + 1) + ↑b : ℝ) * η = (m : ℝ) * η + η + (b : ℝ) * η := by
          push_cast
          ring
        nlinarith
      rcases hex with ⟨j₀, hj₀⟩
      set L' := Function.update L j₀ (L j₀ + η) with hL'_def
      have hL' : ∀ j, L' j ≤ C j := by
        intro j
        by_cases hj : j = j₀
        · subst hj
          rw [hL'_def, Function.update_self]
          exact hj₀
        · rw [hL'_def, Function.update_of_ne hj]
          exact hL j
      have h_sum' : ∑ j, L' j + ((m : ℝ) + (b : ℝ)) * η ≤ ∑ j, C j := by
        have hi : j₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin b)) := Finset.mem_univ j₀
        have h1 := Finset.sum_update_of_mem hi L (L j₀ + η)
        rw [Finset.sdiff_singleton_eq_erase] at h1
        have h2 := Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ L hi
        have h_sum : ∑ j, L' j = (∑ j, L j) + η := by
          rw [hL'_def, h1]
          linarith
        have : (↑(m + 1) + ↑b : ℝ) * η = (↑m + ↑b) * η + η := by
          push_cast
          ring
        linarith
      rcases ih L' hL' h_sum' with ⟨f', hf'⟩
      refine ⟨Fin.cons (α := fun _ => Fin b) j₀ f', ?_⟩
      intro j
      have h_card := @Fin.card_filter_univ_succ m (fun (i : Fin (m + 1)) => (Fin.cons (α := fun _ => Fin b) j₀ f') i = j) _
      simp only [Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ] at h_card
      have h_ih_j := hf' j
      by_cases hj : j₀ = j
      · subst hj
        rw [hL'_def, Function.update_self] at h_ih_j
        rw [h_card, if_pos rfl]
        push_cast
        linarith
      · rw [hL'_def, Function.update_of_ne (Ne.symm hj)] at h_ih_j
        rw [h_card, if_neg hj]
        exact h_ih_j
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.15520 (Improving the bounds on approximating weighted maximin shares of chores), Lemma 5.4.

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by induction on the number of items m, universally quantified over the load vector L. In the inductive step from m to m + 1, assuming b > 0 (as b = 0 contradicts the capacity inequality), an averaging argument proves that at least one bin j₀ has room for an item of size η, because otherwise all bins would strictly exceed their capacity. Placing one item into bin j₀ increases the total load by η, which exactly matches the reduction of the remaining slack term from (m + 1 + b)η to (m + b)η. Applying the induction hypothesis to the updated loads packs the remaining m items, and prepending j₀ yields a valid packing of all m + 1 items.

steps.claim: The base case m = 0 holds: with zero items to place, the empty assignment leaves the loads L_j ≤ C_j unchanged.
steps.explanation: We universally quantify over the initial loads L and induct on the number of items m. When m = 0, no items need to be assigned, so we choose the empty assignment function (from Fin 0). Since the preimage of any bin j under this function is empty, the item count in each bin is 0, and the capacity check reduces directly to the initial hypothesis L_j ≤ C_j.
steps.code:
revert L
  induction m with
  | zero =>
    intro L hL h
    refine ⟨fun i => i.elim0, ?_⟩
    intro j
    have : (Finset.univ.filter (fun (i : Fin 0) => (fun _ => i.elim0) i = j)) = ∅ := by
      rw [Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
      intro i
      exact i.elim0
    rw [this, Finset.card_empty, Nat.cast_zero, MulZeroClass.zero_mul, add_zero]
    exact hL j

steps.claim: For the inductive step m + 1, we may assume b > 0, since b = 0 contradicts the total capacity condition.
steps.explanation: We assume the inductive hypothesis for m and introduce the loads L for m + 1 items. If there are no bins (b = 0), all sums over bins are empty and vanish, reducing the hypothesis to (m + 1)η ≤ 0. But m + 1 ≥ 1 and η > 0 imply (m + 1)η > 0, yielding a contradiction. Hence b > 0.
steps.code:
| succ m ih =>
    intro L hL h
    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos b with rfl | hb
    · simp only [Finset.univ_eq_empty, Finset.sum_empty, zero_add] at h
      have hpos : 0 < ((m + 1 : ℝ) * η) := by positivity
      push_cast at h
      linarith

steps.claim: There exists at least one bin j₀ that can accommodate an item of size η, that is, L_{j₀} + η ≤ C_{j₀}.
steps.explanation: Suppose, for contradiction, that every bin satisfies C_j < L_j + η. Because b > 0, the set of bins is nonempty. Summing these strict inequalities across all b bins gives ∑ C_j < ∑ L_j + bη. However, the total capacity hypothesis guarantees ∑ L_j + (m + 1 + b)η ≤ ∑ C_j. Since (m + 1)η > 0, this implies ∑ L_j + bη < ∑ C_j ≤ ∑ C_j - (m + 1)η, a contradiction. We obtain a bin j₀ satisfying L_{j₀} + η ≤ C_{j₀}.
steps.code:
· have hex : ∃ j₀ : Fin b, L j₀ + η ≤ C j₀ := by
        by_contra! h_all
        have h_ne : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin b)).Nonempty :=
          Finset.univ_nonempty_iff.mpr (Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp hb)
        have h1 : ∑ j, C j < ∑ j, (L j + η) := Finset.sum_lt_sum_of_nonempty h_ne (fun j _ => h_all j)
        rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin, nsmul_eq_mul] at h1
        have hm : 0 ≤ (m : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg m
        have h_exp : (↑(m + 1) + ↑b : ℝ) * η = (m : ℝ) * η + η + (b : ℝ) * η := by
          push_cast
          ring
        nlinarith
      rcases hex with ⟨j₀, hj₀⟩

steps.claim: Updating the load of bin j₀ by η yields loads L' that respect every bin capacity (L'_j ≤ C_j for all j).
steps.explanation: We define the new load function L' by increasing bin j₀'s load to L_{j₀} + η and keeping all other bin loads unchanged. For j = j₀, L'_{j₀} = L_{j₀} + η ≤ C_{j₀} by the choice of j₀. For j ≠ j₀, L'_j = L_j ≤ C_j by the initial load hypothesis.
steps.code:
set L' := Function.update L j₀ (L j₀ + η) with hL'_def
      have hL' : ∀ j, L' j ≤ C j := by
        intro j
        by_cases hj : j = j₀
        · subst hj
          rw [hL'_def, Function.update_self]
          exact hj₀
        · rw [hL'_def, Function.update_of_ne hj]
          exact hL j

steps.claim: The updated loads L' satisfy the total capacity condition for the remaining m items: ∑ L'_j + (m + b)η ≤ ∑ C_j.
steps.explanation: Because L' differs from L only at j₀ where its load increases by η, the total load increases by exactly η: ∑ L'_j = ∑ L_j + η. Rewriting (m + 1 + b)η as (m + b)η + η, the original inequality ∑ L_j + (m + 1 + b)η ≤ ∑ C_j rearranges via linear arithmetic to ∑ L'_j + (m + b)η ≤ ∑ C_j.
steps.code:
have h_sum' : ∑ j, L' j + ((m : ℝ) + (b : ℝ)) * η ≤ ∑ j, C j := by
        have hi : j₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin b)) := Finset.mem_univ j₀
        have h1 := Finset.sum_update_of_mem hi L (L j₀ + η)
        rw [Finset.sdiff_singleton_eq_erase] at h1
        have h2 := Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ L hi
        have h_sum : ∑ j, L' j = (∑ j, L j) + η := by
          rw [hL'_def, h1]
          linarith
        have : (↑(m + 1) + ↑b : ℝ) * η = (↑m + ↑b) * η + η := by
          push_cast
          ring
        linarith

steps.claim: By the induction hypothesis, there is a packing f' for the remaining m items, and assigning the first item to j₀ decomposes each bin's count into the first item plus the rest.
steps.explanation: Applying the induction hypothesis to the loads L' and remaining m items gives a valid packing f' : Fin m → Fin b. We define an assignment for all m + 1 items by mapping the first item (index 0) to j₀ and the remaining m items according to f'. Using the counting lemma Fin.card_filter_univ_succ, the total number of items assigned to bin j is |(f')⁻¹(j)| + 1 if j = j₀, and |(f')⁻¹(j)| if j ≠ j₀.
steps.code:
rcases ih L' hL' h_sum' with ⟨f', hf'⟩
      refine ⟨Fin.cons (α := fun _ => Fin b) j₀ f', ?_⟩
      intro j
      have h_card := @Fin.card_filter_univ_succ m (fun (i : Fin (m + 1)) => (Fin.cons (α := fun _ => Fin b) j₀ f') i = j) _
      simp only [Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ] at h_card
      have h_ih_j := hf' j

steps.claim: Every bin j respects its capacity under the extended packing: L_j + |f⁻¹(j)|η ≤ C_j.
steps.explanation: We split into cases on whether j = j₀: if j = j₀, the bin receives the first item, so its load is L_{j₀} + (|(f')⁻¹(j₀)| + 1)η = (L_{j₀} + η) + |(f')⁻¹(j₀)|η = L'_{j₀} + |(f')⁻¹(j₀)|η ≤ C_{j₀}, which holds by the induction hypothesis on f'. If j ≠ j₀, the bin receives no additional item, so its load is L_j + |(f')⁻¹(j)|η = L'_j + |(f')⁻¹(j)|η ≤ C_j, which also holds by the induction hypothesis on f'.
steps.code:
by_cases hj : j₀ = j
      · subst hj
        rw [hL'_def, Function.update_self] at h_ih_j
        rw [h_card, if_pos rfl]
        push_cast
        linarith
      · rw [hL'_def, Function.update_of_ne (Ne.symm hj)] at h_ih_j
        rw [h_card, if_neg hj]
        exact h_ih_j

glossary.add_zero: Adding zero to an element leaves it unchanged (a + 0 = a).
glossary.Fin.cons_zero: Evaluating the tuple extension `Fin.cons x p` at index 0 yields the head element x.
glossary.Fin.cons_succ: Evaluating the tuple extension `Fin.cons x p` at a successor index i.succ yields p(i).
glossary.Fin.card_filter_univ_succ: The count of elements in Fin (n + 1) satisfying predicate p is the count on Fin n (via successor) plus 1 if 0 satisfies p, and 0 otherwise.
glossary.Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp: If n > 0, then the type Fin n is nonempty.
glossary.Finset.add_sum_erase: Adding f(a) to the sum of f over a finset s with a erased yields the full sum over s.
glossary.Finset.card_empty: The cardinality of the empty finset is 0.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset on a finite type equals the cardinality of the type.
glossary.Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff: A filtered finset is empty if and only if no element in the finset satisfies the filtering predicate.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to its universal finset.
glossary.Finset.sdiff_singleton_eq_erase: Removing a singleton {a} from a finset by set difference is equivalent to erasing a.
glossary.Finset.sum_add_distrib: The sum of a pointwise sum of functions over a finset equals the sum of the individual sums.
glossary.Finset.sum_const: Summing a constant over a finset equals the cardinality of the finset multiplied by the constant.
glossary.Finset.sum_empty: The sum of any function over the empty finset is 0.
glossary.Finset.sum_lt_sum_of_nonempty: If a finset is nonempty and f(i) < g(i) for all elements i in the finset, then the sum of f is strictly less than the sum of g.
glossary.Finset.sum_update_of_mem: The sum over a finset s of a function updated at i ∈ s with value b equals b plus the sum of the original function over s with i removed.
glossary.Finset.univ_eq_empty: The universal finset of an empty type is the empty finset.
glossary.Finset.univ_nonempty_iff.mpr: If a finite type is nonempty, then its universal finset is nonempty.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The cardinality of Fin n is n.
glossary.Function.update_self: An updated function f[a ↦ v] evaluated at a equals v.
glossary.Function.update_of_ne: An updated function f[a' ↦ v] evaluated at an input a ≠ a' equals the original value f(a).
glossary.if_neg: If condition c is false, then `if c then t else e` reduces to e.
glossary.if_pos: If condition c is true, then `if c then t else e` reduces to t.
glossary.MulZeroClass.zero_mul: Zero multiplied by any element is zero (0 * a = 0).
glossary.Nat.cast_zero: The coercion of the natural number 0 into an additive monoid with one is 0.
glossary.Nat.cast_nonneg: The coercion of any natural number into an ordered semiring is non-negative (0 ≤ n).
glossary.Nat.eq_zero_or_pos: Every natural number is either equal to 0 or strictly positive.
glossary.Ne.symm: Inequality is symmetric: if a ≠ b, then b ≠ a.
glossary.nsmul_eq_mul: Scalar multiplication by a natural number n • a is equal to the ring product (n : R) * a.
glossary.zero_add: Adding zero on the left leaves an element unchanged (0 + a = a).

caveats: The case b = 0 is handled as a separate degenerate case: with no bins, the capacity inequality forces (m + 1)η ≤ 0, which contradicts m + 1 ≥ 1 and η > 0.

The lemma Fin.card_filter_univ_succ is a formal bookkeeping lemma for counting preimages in Fin (m + 1): it proves that prepending j₀ to f' increases the count of items in bin j by 1 if j = j₀ and leaves it unchanged otherwise.

declarations.name: subset_sum_to_partition_equivalence
declarations.informal: Let w : U → ℕ be a weight function on a finite type U, and let T : ℕ satisfy T ≤ ∑ a, w a. Then the Subset Sum instance (w, T) has a solution if and only if the augmented Partition instance with weight function SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight w T has a solution.
declarations.statement:
theorem subset_sum_to_partition_equivalence {U : Type*} [Fintype U] [DecidableEq U]
    (w : U → ℕ) (T : ℕ) (h : T ≤ ∑ a, w a) :
    SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSum w T ↔
      SubsetSumToPartition.Partition (SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight w T)
declarations.source:
/-- Correctness of the Subset Sum to Partition reduction under the target bound T ≤ ∑ a, w a. -/
theorem subset_sum_to_partition_equivalence {U : Type*} [Fintype U] [DecidableEq U]
    (w : U → ℕ) (T : ℕ) (h : T ≤ ∑ a, w a) :
    SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSum w T ↔
      SubsetSumToPartition.Partition (SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight w T) := ⟨SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitionCompleteness w T h,
   SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitionSoundness w T h⟩
declarations.citation: Karp (1972), 'Reducibility among Combinatorial Problems'; Garey & Johnson (1979)
declarations.reading: For any type `U` equipped with `Fintype U` and `DecidableEq U`, any weight function `w : U → ℕ`, any target `T : ℕ`, and any proof `h` that `T ≤ ∑ a : U, w a` (the sum over all elements of `U`), `SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSum w T` holds if and only if `SubsetSumToPartition.Partition (SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight w T)` holds.

explanation.summary: The theorem establishes the correctness of Karp's reduction from Subset Sum to Partition under the target bound T ≤ ∑ a, w a. The proof packages the equivalence directly from two auxiliary theorems: completeness, which shows that any valid subset summing to T yields a balanced partition in the augmented instance, and soundness, which reconstructs a subset summing to T from any balanced partition.

steps.claim: The Subset Sum instance has a solution if and only if the augmented Partition instance has a solution.
steps.explanation: The logical equivalence (↔) is established by pairing its two directions. The forward direction (completeness) is given by SubsetSumToPartitionCompleteness, which asserts that any subset with sum T induces an equal-weight bipartition in the augmented instance. The reverse direction (soundness) is given by SubsetSumToPartitionSoundness, which extracts a subset with sum T from any equal-weight bipartition of the augmented instance.
steps.code:
SubsetSumToPartition.Partition (SubsetSumToPartition.partitionWeight w T) := ⟨SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitionCompleteness w T h,
   SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitionSoundness w T h⟩

glossary.SubsetSumToPartition.SubsetSumToPartitio: If a weight function w on a finite type has a subset summing to T (with T ≤ ∑ a, w a), then the augmented instance partitionWeight w T admits a balanced bipartition.
If the augmented instance partitionWeight w T admits a balanced bipartition (with T ≤ ∑ a, w a), then the original instance has a subset summing to T.

declarations.name: simple_graph_triangle_packing_number
declarations.informal: ν(G): the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles of G (two triangles are edge-disjoint when they share at most one vertex).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def simple_graph_triangle_packing_number {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- `ν(G)`: the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles of `G`. -/
noncomputable def simple_graph_triangle_packing_number {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sSup {n | ∃ T : Finset (Finset V), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) ∧
    (T : Set (Finset V)).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) ∧ T.card = n}
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.15539 (Tuza's conjecture under an edge-count condition), Sec. 1 (ν(G), the triangle packing number).

declarations.name: simple_graph_triangle_cover_number
declarations.informal: τ(G): the minimum number of edges of G such that every triangle of G contains one of them.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def simple_graph_triangle_cover_number {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- `τ(G)`: the minimum number of edges of `G` meeting every triangle of `G`. -/
noncomputable def simple_graph_triangle_cover_number {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ F : Finset (Sym2 V), (∀ e ∈ F, e ∈ G.edgeSet) ∧
    (∀ t : Finset V, G.IsNClique 3 t → ∃ e ∈ F, ∀ x ∈ e, x ∈ t) ∧ F.card = n}
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.15539 (Tuza's conjecture under an edge-count condition), Sec. 1 (τ(G), the triangle cover number).

declarations.name: simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_eq_zero_of_clique_free
declarations.informal: A triangle-free graph has triangle cover number 0.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_eq_zero_of_clique_free {V : Type*}
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : G.CliqueFree 3) : simple_graph_triangle_cover_number G = 0
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_eq_zero_of_clique_free {V : Type*}
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : G.CliqueFree 3) : simple_graph_triangle_cover_number G = 0 := by
  apply Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero
  apply Nat.sInf_le
  exact ⟨∅, by simp, fun t ht => absurd ht (h t), rfl⟩
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for the triangle cover number, arXiv:2610.15539 (Tuza's conjecture under an edge-count condition).

explanation.summary: The triangle cover number of a graph is defined as the minimum size of an edge set that intersects every triangle (3-clique). Since the graph is assumed to be triangle-free, the empty set of edges vacuously covers every triangle. Because the empty set has size 0 and the cover number is a non-negative integer, the triangle cover number must be 0.

steps.claim: It suffices to show that 0 is the cardinality of a valid triangle cover of G.
steps.explanation: The triangle cover number of G is defined as the infimum of the sizes of edge sets that cover all 3-cliques. Since any natural number less than or equal to 0 must be 0 (by Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero), and the infimum of a set of natural numbers is bounded above by any member of the set (by Nat.sInf_le), it suffices to exhibit a valid triangle cover of size 0.
steps.code:
apply Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero
  apply Nat.sInf_le

steps.claim: The empty set of edges is a valid triangle cover of size 0.
steps.explanation: We choose the edge set F = ∅. Vacuously, all of its elements are edges of G, and its cardinality is 0. Furthermore, the requirement that every 3-clique contains an edge of F is vacuously satisfied because G is assumed to be clique-free of order 3 (h), so no 3-cliques exist in G.
steps.code: exact ⟨∅, by simp, fun t ht => absurd ht (h t), rfl⟩

glossary.Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero: A natural number that is less than or equal to 0 is equal to 0.
glossary.Nat.sInf_le: The infimum of a set of natural numbers is at most any element of the set.

declarations.name: simple_graph_triangle_packing_number_eq_zero_of_clique_free
declarations.informal: A triangle-free graph has triangle packing number 0.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_triangle_packing_number_eq_zero_of_clique_free {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : G.CliqueFree 3) : simple_graph_triangle_packing_number G = 0
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_triangle_packing_number_eq_zero_of_clique_free {V : Type*} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (h : G.CliqueFree 3) : simple_graph_triangle_packing_number G = 0 := by
  unfold simple_graph_triangle_packing_number
  have : {n | ∃ T : Finset (Finset V), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) ∧
      (T : Set (Finset V)).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) ∧ T.card = n} = {0} := by
    ext n
    simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨T, hT, -, rfl⟩
      rw [Finset.card_eq_zero, Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
      exact fun t ht => h t (hT t ht)
    · rintro rfl
      exact ⟨∅, by simp, by simp, rfl⟩
  rw [this, csSup_singleton]
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for the triangle packing number, arXiv:2610.15539 (Tuza's conjecture under an edge-count condition).

explanation.summary: The triangle packing number of a graph is the supremum of the cardinalities of collections of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles. Because the graph is assumed to be triangle-free (3-clique-free), it cannot contain any triangles, so any valid triangle packing must be empty. Consequently, the only achievable packing cardinality is 0 (witnessed by the empty packing), and the packing number is the supremum of {0}, which is 0.

steps.claim: The triangle packing number of G is, by definition, the supremum of the cardinalities of all families of pairwise almost-disjoint triangles in G.
steps.explanation: We unfold the definition of `simple_graph_triangle_packing_number`, transforming the goal into showing that the supremum of the set of integers n for which there exists a triangle packing of size n is 0.
steps.code: unfold simple_graph_triangle_packing_number

steps.claim: The set of sizes of valid triangle packings in G is the singleton {0}, which reduces to showing that an integer n is an achievable packing size if and only if n = 0.
steps.explanation: We assert that the set of achievable packing sizes is {0}. By set extensionality (`ext`) and unfolding set membership (`Set.mem_ofPred_eq`, `Set.mem_singleton_iff`), this equality is equivalent to proving that a packing of size n exists if and only if n = 0.
steps.code:
have : {n | ∃ T : Finset (Finset V), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) ∧
      (T : Set (Finset V)).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) ∧ T.card = n} = {0} := by
    ext n
    simp only [Set.mem_ofPred_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
    constructor

steps.claim: Any valid triangle packing in G must be empty, so its cardinality is 0.
steps.explanation: Suppose T is a triangle packing in G of size n. A finite set has cardinality 0 if and only if it is empty, which in turn means it contains no elements (`Finset.card_eq_zero`, `Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem`). If T contained any element t, then t would be a 3-clique in G, contradicting the hypothesis h that G has no 3-cliques. Hence T must be empty and n = |T| = 0.
steps.code:
· rintro ⟨T, hT, -, rfl⟩
      rw [Finset.card_eq_zero, Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
      exact fun t ht => h t (hT t ht)

steps.claim: The packing size 0 is achievable by taking the empty collection of triangles.
steps.explanation: Conversely, for n = 0, the empty set ∅ provides the required witness: vacuously, every element of ∅ is a 3-clique and any two elements meet in at most one vertex, and |∅| = 0.
steps.code:
· rintro rfl
      exact ⟨∅, by simp, by simp, rfl⟩

steps.claim: The supremum of the set of packing sizes is 0, concluding the proof.
steps.explanation: Substituting the established equality that the set of packing sizes is {0}, the goal simplifies to sSup {0} = 0, which holds by `csSup_singleton`.
steps.code: rw [this, csSup_singleton]

glossary.Set.mem_ofPred_eq: An element belongs to the set defined by a predicate if and only if the predicate holds for that element.
glossary.Set.mem_singleton_iff: An element belongs to the singleton set {b} if and only if it equals b.
glossary.Finset.card_eq_zero: A finite set has cardinality 0 if and only if it is the empty set.
glossary.Finset.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem: A finite set is empty if and only if it contains no elements.
glossary.csSup_singleton: The supremum of a singleton set {a} in a conditionally complete order is a.

declarations.name: simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_le_three_mul_packing_number
declarations.informal: Every finite graph satisfies τ(G) ≤ 3ν(G): the edges of a maximum family of edge-disjoint triangles meet every triangle.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_le_three_mul_packing_number {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    simple_graph_triangle_cover_number G ≤ 3 * simple_graph_triangle_packing_number G
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_le_three_mul_packing_number {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    simple_graph_triangle_cover_number G ≤ 3 * simple_graph_triangle_packing_number G := by
  classical
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty V with hV | hV
  · rw [simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_eq_zero_of_clique_free G (fun t ht => by
        have := ht.card_eq
        rw [Finset.eq_empty_of_isEmpty t, Finset.card_empty] at this
        omega)]
    exact Nat.zero_le _
  set P : Set ℕ := {n | ∃ T : Finset (Finset V), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) ∧
    (T : Set (Finset V)).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) ∧ T.card = n} with hP
  have hbdd : BddAbove P := by
    refine ⟨(Finset.univ : Finset (Finset V)).card, ?_⟩
    rintro n ⟨T, -, -, rfl⟩
    exact Finset.card_le_univ T
  have hne : P.Nonempty := ⟨0, ∅, by simp, by simp, rfl⟩
  obtain ⟨T, hT, hTp, hTc⟩ := Nat.sSup_mem hne hbdd
  have hmax : ∀ T' : Finset (Finset V), (∀ t ∈ T', G.IsNClique 3 t) →
      (T' : Set (Finset V)).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) → T'.card ≤ T.card := by
    intro T' h1 h2
    rw [hTc]
    exact le_csSup hbdd ⟨T', h1, h2, rfl⟩
  -- three edges of each triangle
  have h3 : ∀ t ∈ T, ∃ x y z : V, x ≠ y ∧ x ≠ z ∧ y ≠ z ∧ t = {x, y, z} := by
    intro t ht
    exact Finset.card_eq_three.1 (hT t ht).card_eq
  choose! fx fy fz hxy hxz hyz hxyz using h3
  set E : Finset V → Finset (Sym2 V) :=
    fun t => {s(fx t, fy t), s(fy t, fz t), s(fx t, fz t)} with hE
  set F := T.biUnion E with hF
  have hFcard : F.card ≤ 3 * T.card := by
    calc F.card ≤ ∑ t ∈ T, (E t).card := Finset.card_biUnion_le
      _ ≤ ∑ _t ∈ T, 3 := by
          apply Finset.sum_le_sum
          intro t _
          simp only [hE]
          exact (Finset.card_insert_le _ _).trans
            (Nat.succ_le_succ ((Finset.card_insert_le _ _).trans (by simp)))
      _ = 3 * T.card := by rw [Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
  have hFedge : ∀ e ∈ F, e ∈ G.edgeSet := by
    intro e he
    simp only [hF, Finset.mem_biUnion] at he
    obtain ⟨t, ht, he⟩ := he
    have hcl := (hT t ht).isClique
    have hsub : ∀ x ∈ ({fx t, fy t, fz t} : Finset V), x ∈ t := by
      intro x hx
      rw [← hxyz t ht] at hx
      exact hx
    have hx : fx t ∈ t := hsub _ (by simp)
    have hy : fy t ∈ t := hsub _ (by simp)
    have hz : fz t ∈ t := hsub _ (by simp)
    simp only [hE, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at he
    rcases he with rfl | rfl | rfl
    · exact hcl hx hy (hxy t ht)
    · exact hcl hy hz (hyz t ht)
    · exact hcl hx hz (hxz t ht)
  -- every pair of distinct vertices of a packing triangle spans one of its three edges
  have hpair : ∀ s ∈ T, ∀ u ∈ s, ∀ w ∈ s, u ≠ w → s(u, w) ∈ E s := by
    intro s hs u hu w hw huw
    rw [hxyz s hs] at hu hw
    simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hu hw
    simp only [hE, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]
    rcases hu with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases hw with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
      first
      | exact absurd rfl huw
      | simp [Sym2.eq_swap]
  have hcover : ∀ t : Finset V, G.IsNClique 3 t → ∃ e ∈ F, ∀ x ∈ e, x ∈ t := by
    intro t ht
    -- some packing triangle shares two vertices with `t`
    have : ∃ s ∈ T, 2 ≤ (s ∩ t).card := by
      by_contra hno
      push_neg at hno
      have htT : t ∉ T := by
        intro htT
        have := hno t htT
        rw [Finset.inter_self, ht.card_eq] at this
        omega
      have h1 : ∀ s ∈ insert t T, G.IsNClique 3 s := by
        intro s hs
        rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hs with rfl | hs
        · exact ht
        · exact hT s hs
      have h2 : ((insert t T : Finset (Finset V)) : Set (Finset V)).Pairwise
          (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) := by
        rw [Finset.coe_insert]
        refine hTp.insert ?_
        intro s hs _
        have := hno s hs
        exact ⟨by rw [Finset.inter_comm]; omega, by omega⟩
      have := hmax _ h1 h2
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem htT] at this
      omega
    obtain ⟨s, hs, hst⟩ := this
    obtain ⟨u, hu, w, hw, huw⟩ := Finset.one_lt_card.1 hst
    rw [Finset.mem_inter] at hu hw
    refine ⟨s(u, w), Finset.mem_biUnion.2 ⟨s, hs, hpair s hs u hu.1 w hw.1 huw⟩, ?_⟩
    intro x hx
    rw [Sym2.mem_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl
    · exact hu.2
    · exact hw.2
  calc simple_graph_triangle_cover_number G ≤ F.card :=
        Nat.sInf_le ⟨F, hFedge, hcover, rfl⟩
    _ ≤ 3 * T.card := hFcard
    _ = 3 * simple_graph_triangle_packing_number G := by
        rw [hTc]; rfl
declarations.citation: The trivial bound ν(G) ≤ τ(G) ≤ 3ν(G), recalled in arXiv:2610.15539 (Tuza's conjecture under an edge-count condition), Sec. 1 (display after Conjecture 1.1); the bound Tuza's conjecture improves to 2ν.

explanation.summary: To prove τ(G) ≤ 3ν(G), we choose a maximum family T of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles in G, so that |T| = ν(G). Let F be the set of all edges of the triangles in T; then |F| ≤ 3|T| = 3ν(G). By the maximality of T, every triangle in G must share at least two vertices with some triangle in T, meaning that it contains at least one edge of that triangle. Thus F is an edge cover of all triangles in G, which implies τ(G) ≤ |F| ≤ 3ν(G).

steps.claim: If the vertex set V is empty, the theorem holds trivially because there are no triangles.
steps.explanation: We case-split on whether V is empty or nonempty using `isEmpty_or_nonempty`. When V is empty, any triangle (3-clique) would have 3 vertices in an empty set, yielding 0 = 3 via `Finset.card_empty` and `Finset.eq_empty_of_isEmpty`, an arithmetic contradiction. Thus G has no triangles, so `simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_eq_zero_of_clique_free` shows τ(G) = 0, and 0 ≤ 3ν(G) holds by `Nat.zero_le`.
steps.code:
classical
  rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty V with hV | hV
  · rw [simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_eq_zero_of_clique_free G (fun t ht => by
        have := ht.card_eq
        rw [Finset.eq_empty_of_isEmpty t, Finset.card_empty] at this
        omega)]
    exact Nat.zero_le _

steps.claim: There exists a maximum family T of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles in G, with |T| = ν(G).
steps.explanation: We define P to be the set of sizes of all collections of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles in G. The set P is bounded above by the total number of vertex subsets via `Finset.card_le_univ`, and nonempty because the empty family ∅ has size 0. By `Nat.sSup_mem`, P contains its supremum. Letting T be a packing achieving this maximum size, we have |T| = ν(G), and by `le_csSup`, any other edge-disjoint triangle packing has size at most |T|.
steps.code:
set P : Set ℕ := {n | ∃ T : Finset (Finset V), (∀ t ∈ T, G.IsNClique 3 t) ∧
    (T : Set (Finset V)).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) ∧ T.card = n} with hP
  have hbdd : BddAbove P := by
    refine ⟨(Finset.univ : Finset (Finset V)).card, ?_⟩
    rintro n ⟨T, -, -, rfl⟩
    exact Finset.card_le_univ T
  have hne : P.Nonempty := ⟨0, ∅, by simp, by simp, rfl⟩
  obtain ⟨T, hT, hTp, hTc⟩ := Nat.sSup_mem hne hbdd
  have hmax : ∀ T' : Finset (Finset V), (∀ t ∈ T', G.IsNClique 3 t) →
      (T' : Set (Finset V)).Pairwise (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) → T'.card ≤ T.card := by
    intro T' h1 h2
    rw [hTc]
    exact le_csSup hbdd ⟨T', h1, h2, rfl⟩

steps.claim: Each triangle in T consists of three distinct vertices, and F is defined as the union of the edges of all triangles in T.
steps.explanation: Every triangle t ∈ T has cardinality 3, so by `Finset.card_eq_three.1`, it can be written as {x, y, z} with x, y, z pairwise distinct. By `choose!`, we extract vertex choice functions fx, fy, fz. We then define E(t) to be the set of the three edges of t, and F to be the union of E(t) over all t ∈ T.
steps.code:
-- three edges of each triangle
  have h3 : ∀ t ∈ T, ∃ x y z : V, x ≠ y ∧ x ≠ z ∧ y ≠ z ∧ t = {x, y, z} := by
    intro t ht
    exact Finset.card_eq_three.1 (hT t ht).card_eq
  choose! fx fy fz hxy hxz hyz hxyz using h3
  set E : Finset V → Finset (Sym2 V) :=
    fun t => {s(fx t, fy t), s(fy t, fz t), s(fx t, fz t)} with hE
  set F := T.biUnion E with hF

steps.claim: The candidate edge cover F has cardinality at most 3|T|.
steps.explanation: By subadditivity of the union (`Finset.card_biUnion_le`), |F| ≤ ∑_{t ∈ T} |E(t)|. Each E(t) is defined by three vertex insertions, so |E(t)| ≤ 3 by `Finset.card_insert_le` and `Nat.succ_le_succ`. Summing this upper bound over all t ∈ T using `Finset.sum_le_sum` gives |F| ≤ ∑_{t ∈ T} 3 = 3|T| via `Finset.sum_const`, `smul_eq_mul`, and `mul_comm`.
steps.code:
have hFcard : F.card ≤ 3 * T.card := by
    calc F.card ≤ ∑ t ∈ T, (E t).card := Finset.card_biUnion_le
      _ ≤ ∑ _t ∈ T, 3 := by
          apply Finset.sum_le_sum
          intro t _
          simp only [hE]
          exact (Finset.card_insert_le _ _).trans
            (Nat.succ_le_succ ((Finset.card_insert_le _ _).trans (by simp)))
      _ = 3 * T.card := by rw [Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]

steps.claim: Every element of F is an edge of the graph G.
steps.explanation: Any edge e ∈ F belongs to E(t) for some triangle t ∈ T by `Finset.mem_biUnion`. The three vertices fx(t), fy(t), fz(t) belong to t. Since t is a 3-clique in G, every pair of distinct vertices in t is adjacent in G. Checking each of the three edges in E(t) using `Finset.mem_insert` and `Finset.mem_singleton`, we find that e is an edge of G.
steps.code:
have hFedge : ∀ e ∈ F, e ∈ G.edgeSet := by
    intro e he
    simp only [hF, Finset.mem_biUnion] at he
    obtain ⟨t, ht, he⟩ := he
    have hcl := (hT t ht).isClique
    have hsub : ∀ x ∈ ({fx t, fy t, fz t} : Finset V), x ∈ t := by
      intro x hx
      rw [← hxyz t ht] at hx
      exact hx
    have hx : fx t ∈ t := hsub _ (by simp)
    have hy : fy t ∈ t := hsub _ (by simp)
    have hz : fz t ∈ t := hsub _ (by simp)
    simp only [hE, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at he
    rcases he with rfl | rfl | rfl
    · exact hcl hx hy (hxy t ht)
    · exact hcl hy hz (hyz t ht)
    · exact hcl hx hz (hxz t ht)

steps.claim: Any two distinct vertices of a triangle s ∈ T form one of its three edges in E(s).
steps.explanation: Since s = {fx(s), fy(s), fz(s)}, any distinct vertices u, w ∈ s are two distinct vertices among fx(s), fy(s), fz(s). A case analysis on all pairs, using symmetry of unordered pairs (`Sym2.eq_swap`), confirms that the unordered pair {u, w} is in E(s).
steps.code:
-- every pair of distinct vertices of a packing triangle spans one of its three edges
  have hpair : ∀ s ∈ T, ∀ u ∈ s, ∀ w ∈ s, u ≠ w → s(u, w) ∈ E s := by
    intro s hs u hu w hw huw
    rw [hxyz s hs] at hu hw
    simp only [Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hu hw
    simp only [hE, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton]
    rcases hu with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases hw with rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
      first
      | exact absurd rfl huw
      | simp [Sym2.eq_swap]

steps.claim: The edge set F covers every triangle in G: every triangle contains at least one edge from F.
steps.explanation: Let t be a triangle in G. If t shared at most one vertex with every triangle s ∈ T, then t could not already be in T (since |t ∩ t| = 3 by `Finset.inter_self`), and T ∪ {t} would be a pairwise edge-disjoint packing of size |T| + 1 by `Finset.card_insert_of_notMem`. This would contradict the maximality of T. Hence some triangle s ∈ T must share at least two vertices with t: |s ∩ t| ≥ 2. By `Finset.one_lt_card.1`, s ∩ t contains two distinct vertices u and w. Then {u, w} is an edge in E(s) ⊆ F whose endpoints both lie in t.
steps.code:
have hcover : ∀ t : Finset V, G.IsNClique 3 t → ∃ e ∈ F, ∀ x ∈ e, x ∈ t := by
    intro t ht
    -- some packing triangle shares two vertices with `t`
    have : ∃ s ∈ T, 2 ≤ (s ∩ t).card := by
      by_contra hno
      push_neg at hno
      have htT : t ∉ T := by
        intro htT
        have := hno t htT
        rw [Finset.inter_self, ht.card_eq] at this
        omega
      have h1 : ∀ s ∈ insert t T, G.IsNClique 3 s := by
        intro s hs
        rcases Finset.mem_insert.1 hs with rfl | hs
        · exact ht
        · exact hT s hs
      have h2 : ((insert t T : Finset (Finset V)) : Set (Finset V)).Pairwise
          (fun s t => (s ∩ t).card ≤ 1) := by
        rw [Finset.coe_insert]
        refine hTp.insert ?_
        intro s hs _
        have := hno s hs
        exact ⟨by rw [Finset.inter_comm]; omega, by omega⟩
      have := hmax _ h1 h2
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem htT] at this
      omega
    obtain ⟨s, hs, hst⟩ := this
    obtain ⟨u, hu, w, hw, huw⟩ := Finset.one_lt_card.1 hst
    rw [Finset.mem_inter] at hu hw
    refine ⟨s(u, w), Finset.mem_biUnion.2 ⟨s, hs, hpair s hs u hu.1 w hw.1 huw⟩, ?_⟩
    intro x hx
    rw [Sym2.mem_iff] at hx
    rcases hx with rfl | rfl
    · exact hu.2
    · exact hw.2

steps.claim: The triangle cover number satisfies τ(G) ≤ 3ν(G).
steps.explanation: Since F is a valid triangle cover of G, the minimum cover size τ(G) is at most |F| by `Nat.sInf_le`. Chaining this with |F| ≤ 3|T| and |T| = ν(G) yields τ(G) ≤ 3ν(G).
steps.code:
calc simple_graph_triangle_cover_number G ≤ F.card :=
        Nat.sInf_le ⟨F, hFedge, hcover, rfl⟩
    _ ≤ 3 * T.card := hFcard
    _ = 3 * simple_graph_triangle_packing_number G := by
        rw [hTc]; rfl

glossary.isEmpty_or_nonempty: Every type is either empty or nonempty.
glossary.simple_graph_triangle_cover_number_eq_ze: If a simple graph contains no triangles (is 3-clique free), its triangle cover number is 0.
glossary.Finset.eq_empty_of_isEmpty: Any finite set over an empty type is the empty set.
glossary.Finset.card_empty: The cardinality of the empty set is 0.
glossary.Nat.zero_le: 0 is less than or equal to any natural number.
glossary.Finset.card_le_univ: The cardinality of any finite subset is at most the cardinality of the full finite type.
glossary.Nat.sSup_mem: A nonempty set of natural numbers that is bounded above contains its supremum (maximum).
glossary.le_csSup: Any element in a bounded-above set is at most the supremum of the set.
glossary.Finset.card_eq_three.1: If a finite set has cardinality 3, then it consists of three pairwise distinct elements.
glossary.Finset.card_biUnion_le: The cardinality of a union of finite sets is at most the sum of their individual cardinalities.
glossary.Finset.sum_le_sum: A sum of terms is bounded by the sum of termwise upper bounds.
glossary.Finset.card_insert_le: Inserting an element into a finite set increases its cardinality by at most 1.
glossary.Nat.succ_le_succ: If n ≤ m, then n + 1 ≤ m + 1.
glossary.Finset.sum_const: Summing a constant over a finite set equals the cardinality of the set times the constant.
glossary.smul_eq_mul: Scalar multiplication of natural numbers coincides with ordinary multiplication.
glossary.mul_comm: Multiplication of natural numbers is commutative.
glossary.Finset.mem_biUnion: An element belongs to a union of sets ⋃_{a ∈ s} t(a) if and only if it belongs to t(a) for some a ∈ s.
glossary.Finset.mem_insert: An element belongs to {a} ∪ s if and only if it equals a or belongs to s.
glossary.Finset.mem_singleton: An element belongs to the singleton {a} if and only if it equals a.
glossary.Sym2.eq_swap: An unordered pair is symmetric: s(a, b) = s(b, a).
glossary.Finset.inter_self: The intersection of a finite set with itself is the set itself.
glossary.Finset.mem_insert.1: If an element belongs to {a} ∪ s, it equals a or belongs to s.
glossary.Finset.coe_insert: The coercion of {a} ∪ s to a set equals the set insertion of a into the coercion of s.
glossary.Finset.inter_comm: Intersection of finite sets is commutative.
glossary.Finset.card_insert_of_notMem: Inserting an element not already in a finite set increases its cardinality by 1.
glossary.Finset.one_lt_card.1: If a finite set has cardinality strictly greater than 1, it contains two distinct elements.
glossary.Finset.mem_inter: An element belongs to the intersection of two finite sets if and only if it belongs to both sets.
glossary.Finset.mem_biUnion.2: If an element belongs to t(a) for some a ∈ s, it belongs to ⋃_{a ∈ s} t(a).
