declarations.name: mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition
declarations.informal: For positive integers p, q of the same parity with q < p < 7q, the seven rectangles R₁, …, R₇ have positive integer sides, partition the 105q × 105q square, and are pairwise noncongruent.
declarations.statement:
theorem mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition (p q : ℕ) (hpar : p % 2 = q % 2) (hqp : q < p)
    (hp : p < 7 * q) :
    mondrian_is_partition (105 * q) (mondrian_seven_rects p q)
declarations.source:
theorem mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition (p q : ℕ) (hpar : p % 2 = q % 2) (hqp : q < p)
    (hp : p < 7 * q) :
    mondrian_is_partition (105 * q) (mondrian_seven_rects p q) := by
  have ha : 7 * (7 * q - p) + 7 * p = 49 * q := by omega
  have hd : 5 * (8 * q - p) + 5 * p = 40 * q := by omega
  have he : 5 * (13 * q - p) + 5 * p = 65 * q := by omega
  have hf : 2 * (15 * (7 * q + p) / 2) = 105 * q + 15 * p := by omega
  have hdisj : ∀ r s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ, (r.2.1 ≤ s.1 ∨ s.2.1 ≤ r.1 ∨ r.2.2.2 ≤ s.2.2.1 ∨
      s.2.2.2 ≤ r.2.2.1) → Disjoint (mondrian_rect_cells r) (mondrian_rect_cells s) := by
    intro r s h
    rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
    rintro ⟨x, y⟩ h1 h2
    simp only [mondrian_rect_cells, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_Ico] at h1 h2
    omega
  unfold mondrian_seven_rects
  generalize 7 * (7 * q - p) = a at ha ⊢
  generalize 5 * (8 * q - p) = d at hd ⊢
  generalize 5 * (13 * q - p) = e at he ⊢
  generalize 15 * (7 * q + p) / 2 = f at hf ⊢
  generalize hc : 7 * (7 * q + p) = c
  refine ⟨by simp, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro r hr
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hr
    rcases hr with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> dsimp only <;> omega
  · simp only [List.pairwise_cons, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil,
      or_false, forall_eq_or_imp, forall_eq, List.Pairwise.nil, and_true]
    and_intros
    all_goals first
      | exact fun _ h => h.elim
      | exact hdisj _ _ (by dsimp only; omega)
      | (simp only [mondrian_rect_congruent, mondrian_rect_width, mondrian_rect_height]; omega)
  · ext ⟨x, y⟩
    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion, List.mem_toFinset, List.mem_cons,
      List.not_mem_nil, or_false, mondrian_rect_cells, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_Ico,
      Finset.mem_range]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨r, hr, h⟩
      rcases hr with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> dsimp only at h <;> omega
    · intro h
      by_cases h1 : y < d
      · by_cases h2 : x < a
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inl rfl), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inl rfl, by dsimp only; omega⟩
      by_cases h3 : y < e
      · by_cases h2 : x < a
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inl rfl), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        by_cases h4 : x < 42 * q
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
      by_cases h5 : y < f
      · by_cases h2 : x < a
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inl rfl), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        by_cases h4 : x < 42 * q
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        by_cases h6 : x < c
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr rfl))))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
      by_cases h6 : x < c
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)), by dsimp only; omega⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.19193 (A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem), Sec. 2 (the dissection (3) is a partition) and Proposition 1 (pairwise noncongruence); serves mondrian_seven_rects_partition_defect.

explanation.summary: The proof establishes that the seven parameterized rectangles form a valid Mondrian partition of the 105q × 105q square for any positive integers p, q of the same parity with q < p < 7q. After establishing four arithmetic identities and a general geometric separation criterion for disjointness, the partition condition is split into non-degeneracy, pairwise disjointness and non-congruence, and coverage of the square. Each condition is verified by case analysis on the rectangles and resolved via integer linear arithmetic using Lean's omega tactic, with coverage settled by a coordinate-based decision tree.

steps.claim: Four linear arithmetic identities hold relating the coordinate parameters to multiples of q and p.
steps.explanation: Under the conditions that p and q share parity with q < p < 7q, we establish four algebraic relations: 7(7q - p) + 7p = 49q (for coordinate a), 5(8q - p) + 5p = 40q (for coordinate d), 5(13q - p) + 5p = 65q (for coordinate e), and 2 · ⌊15(7q + p) / 2⌋ = 105q + 15p (for coordinate f, which is an integer because 7q + p is even). All four identities follow directly by linear integer arithmetic.
steps.code:
have ha : 7 * (7 * q - p) + 7 * p = 49 * q := by omega
  have hd : 5 * (8 * q - p) + 5 * p = 40 * q := by omega
  have he : 5 * (13 * q - p) + 5 * p = 65 * q := by omega
  have hf : 2 * (15 * (7 * q + p) / 2) = 105 * q + 15 * p := by omega

steps.claim: A geometric criterion for disjointness of two axis-aligned rectangles.
steps.explanation: If two rectangles r = [x₁, x₂) × [y₁, y₂) and s = [x'₁, x'₂) × [y'₁, y'₂) are separated horizontally (x₂ ≤ x'₁ or x'₂ ≤ x₁) or vertically (y₂ ≤ y'₁ or y'₂ ≤ y₁), their cell sets are disjoint. Rewriting disjointness with Finset.disjoint_left and expanding cell membership in the Cartesian product of intervals, an element in the intersection would satisfy contradictory linear inequalities, which omega refutes.
steps.code:
have hdisj : ∀ r s : ℕ × ℕ × ℕ × ℕ, (r.2.1 ≤ s.1 ∨ s.2.1 ≤ r.1 ∨ r.2.2.2 ≤ s.2.2.1 ∨
      s.2.2.2 ≤ r.2.2.1) → Disjoint (mondrian_rect_cells r) (mondrian_rect_cells s) := by
    intro r s h
    rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
    rintro ⟨x, y⟩ h1 h2
    simp only [mondrian_rect_cells, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_Ico] at h1 h2
    omega

steps.claim: The list of seven rectangles is rewritten using compact coordinate names a, d, e, f, c.
steps.explanation: Unfolding mondrian_seven_rects, we introduce abbreviations for the five key division lines: a = 7(7q - p), d = 5(8q - p), e = 5(13q - p), f = 15(7q + p) / 2, and c = 7(7q + p). This simplifies the coordinates of the seven rectangles and re-expresses the goal and earlier identities in terms of these parameters.
steps.code:
unfold mondrian_seven_rects
  generalize 7 * (7 * q - p) = a at ha ⊢
  generalize 5 * (8 * q - p) = d at hd ⊢
  generalize 5 * (13 * q - p) = e at he ⊢
  generalize 15 * (7 * q + p) / 2 = f at hf ⊢
  generalize hc : 7 * (7 * q + p) = c

steps.claim: The partition property reduces to non-degeneracy, pairwise disjointness/non-congruence, and square coverage.
steps.explanation: The definition mondrian_is_partition requires four conditions: that the list has length at least 2, that every rectangle has strictly positive width and height, that rectangles are pairwise disjoint and non-congruent, and that their union equals the (105q) × (105q) grid. The length condition 2 ≤ 7 is discharged immediately by simplification, leaving the remaining three properties as subgoals.
steps.code: refine ⟨by simp, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: Every rectangle in the collection has strictly positive width and height.
steps.explanation: For each rectangle r in the 7-element list, we case-split on which rectangle it is. In each of the seven cases, the positivity requirements x₁ < x₂ and y₁ < y₂ reduce to linear inequalities in p and q (such as a < 105q and 0 < d), which follow from q < p < 7q and are closed by omega.
steps.code:
· intro r hr
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hr
    rcases hr with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> dsimp only <;> omega

steps.claim: The seven rectangles are pairwise disjoint and pairwise non-congruent.
steps.explanation: Expanding the pairwise relation over the 7-element list yields 21 pairs of distinct rectangles, each requiring proofs of disjointness and non-congruence. Each disjointness goal is discharged by the geometric criterion hdisj, checking the coordinate separation with omega. Each non-congruence goal expands the definition of congruence (matching side lengths up to rotation) and is refuted by omega from the parameter bounds q < p < 7q.
steps.code:
· simp only [List.pairwise_cons, List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil,
      or_false, forall_eq_or_imp, forall_eq, List.Pairwise.nil, and_true]
    and_intros
    all_goals first
      | exact fun _ h => h.elim
      | exact hdisj _ _ (by dsimp only; omega)
      | (simp only [mondrian_rect_congruent, mondrian_rect_width, mondrian_rect_height]; omega)

steps.claim: Every cell in any of the seven rectangles lies within the 105q × 105q square.
steps.explanation: By extensionality on cells (x, y), coverage reduces to two inclusions. For the forward inclusion (⊆), suppose a cell (x, y) belongs to some rectangle r in the list. Splitting across the seven rectangles, the bounds x₁ ≤ x < x₂ and y₁ ≤ y < y₂ guarantee that x < 105q and y < 105q, verified in each case by omega.
steps.code:
· ext ⟨x, y⟩
    simp only [Finset.mem_biUnion, List.mem_toFinset, List.mem_cons,
      List.not_mem_nil, or_false, mondrian_rect_cells, Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_Ico,
      Finset.mem_range]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨r, hr, h⟩
      rcases hr with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> dsimp only at h <;> omega

steps.claim: Every cell in the 105q × 105q square is covered by one of the seven rectangles.
steps.explanation: For the reverse inclusion (⊇), given a cell (x, y) with x < 105q and y < 105q, a decision tree on the coordinates identifies which rectangle contains it: testing y < d routes to R₂ (if x < a) or R₁; testing y < e routes to R₂ (if x < a), R₆ (if x < 42q), or R₅; testing y < f routes to R₂ (if x < a), R₆ (if x < 42q), R₇ (if x < c), or R₄; and if y ≥ f, testing x < c routes to R₃ or R₄. In each branch, omega verifies that (x, y) satisfies the boundary conditions of the selected rectangle.
steps.code:
· intro h
      by_cases h1 : y < d
      · by_cases h2 : x < a
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inl rfl), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inl rfl, by dsimp only; omega⟩
      by_cases h3 : y < e
      · by_cases h2 : x < a
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inl rfl), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        by_cases h4 : x < 42 * q
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
      by_cases h5 : y < f
      · by_cases h2 : x < a
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inl rfl), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        by_cases h4 : x < 42 * q
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        by_cases h6 : x < c
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr rfl))))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
        · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))), by dsimp only; omega⟩
      by_cases h6 : x < c
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl)), by dsimp only; omega⟩
      · exact ⟨_, Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inr (Or.inl rfl))), by dsimp only; omega⟩

glossary.Finset.disjoint_left: Two finite sets are disjoint if and only if no element of the first belongs to the second.
glossary.Finset.mem_product: A pair belongs to a Cartesian product of finite sets if and only if its first coordinate belongs to the first set and its second coordinate belongs to the second.
glossary.Finset.mem_Ico: A value belongs to the half-open interval [a, b) if and only if it is at least a and strictly less than b.
glossary.List.mem_cons: An element belongs to a prepended list b :: l if and only if it equals b or belongs to l.
glossary.List.not_mem_nil: No element belongs to the empty list.
glossary.or_false: Disjunction with false is logically equivalent to the original proposition: (P ∨ False) ↔ P.
glossary.List.pairwise_cons: A relation holds pairwise on a :: l if and only if a is related to every element of l and the relation holds pairwise on l.
glossary.forall_eq_or_imp: A universal quantification over a = a' ∨ Q a is equivalent to the property at a' together with universal quantification over Q a.
glossary.forall_eq: A universal quantification over elements equal to a' is equivalent to evaluating the predicate at a'.
glossary.List.Pairwise.nil: Any relation holds pairwise vacuously on the empty list.
glossary.and_true: Conjunction with true is logically equivalent to the original proposition: (P ∧ True) ↔ P.
glossary.Finset.mem_biUnion: An element belongs to an indexed union of finite sets if and only if it belongs to one of the component sets.
glossary.List.mem_toFinset: An element belongs to the finite set formed from a list if and only if it belongs to the list.
glossary.Finset.mem_range: A natural number belongs to the range {0, …, n - 1} if and only if it is strictly less than n.
glossary.Or.inl: From a proof of A, deduce A ∨ B.
glossary.Or.inr: From a proof of B, deduce A ∨ B.

caveats: The pairwise disjointness and non-congruence checks in Step 6, as well as the rectangle coverage in Steps 7 and 8, involve dozens of arithmetic cases that Lean resolves using the `omega` decision procedure.

declarations.name: mondrian_seven_rects_defect
declarations.informal: With E = p² − 19q², the defect of the seven-rectangle dissection is 140|E|.
declarations.statement:
theorem mondrian_seven_rects_defect (p q : ℕ) (hpar : p % 2 = q % 2) (hqp : q < p)
    (hp : p < 7 * q) :
    (mondrian_defect (mondrian_seven_rects p q) : ℤ) = 140 * |(p : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2|
declarations.source:
theorem mondrian_seven_rects_defect (p q : ℕ) (hpar : p % 2 = q % 2) (hqp : q < p)
    (hp : p < 7 * q) :
    (mondrian_defect (mondrian_seven_rects p q) : ℤ) = 140 * |(p : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2| := by
  obtain ⟨s, rfl⟩ : ∃ s, p = q + 2 * s := ⟨(p - q) / 2, by omega⟩
  have hs3 : s < 3 * q := by omega
  have hmap : (mondrian_seven_rects (q + 2 * s) q).map mondrian_rect_area =
      [(63 * q + 14 * s) * (35 * q - 10 * s), (42 * q - 14 * s) * (60 * q + 15 * s),
       (56 * q + 14 * s) * (45 * q - 15 * s), (49 * q - 14 * s) * (45 * q + 10 * s),
       (63 * q) * (25 * q), (14 * s) * (25 * q + 25 * s), (14 * q + 14 * s) * (25 * s)] := by
    simp only [mondrian_seven_rects, List.map_cons, List.map_nil, mondrian_rect_area,
      mondrian_rect_width, mondrian_rect_height, List.cons.injEq, and_true]
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> congr 1 <;> omega
  rw [mondrian_defect, hmap]
  have c1 : 10 * s ≤ 35 * q := by omega
  have c2 : 14 * s ≤ 42 * q := by omega
  have c3 : 15 * s ≤ 45 * q := by omega
  have c4 : 14 * s ≤ 49 * q := by omega
  -- F = 2 s² + 2 q s − 9 q², so that p² − 19 q² = 2F
  obtain ⟨F, hF⟩ : ∃ F : ℤ, F = 2 * (s : ℤ) ^ 2 + 2 * (q : ℤ) * s - 9 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have hE : ((q + 2 * s : ℕ) : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 = 2 * F := by rw [hF]; push_cast; ring
  rw [hE]
  have A1 : (((63 * q + 14 * s) * (35 * q - 10 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 - 70 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast [Nat.cast_sub c1]; ring
  have A2 : (((42 * q - 14 * s) * (60 * q + 15 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 - 105 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast [Nat.cast_sub c2]; ring
  have A3 : (((56 * q + 14 * s) * (45 * q - 15 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 - 105 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast [Nat.cast_sub c3]; ring
  have A4 : (((49 * q - 14 * s) * (45 * q + 10 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 - 70 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast [Nat.cast_sub c4]; ring
  have A5 : (((63 * q) * (25 * q) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 := by push_cast; ring
  have A6 : (((14 * s) * (25 * q + 25 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 + 175 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast; ring
  have A7 : (((14 * q + 14 * s) * (25 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 + 175 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast; ring
  generalize (63 * q + 14 * s) * (35 * q - 10 * s) = x1 at A1 ⊢
  generalize (42 * q - 14 * s) * (60 * q + 15 * s) = x2 at A2 ⊢
  generalize (56 * q + 14 * s) * (45 * q - 15 * s) = x3 at A3 ⊢
  generalize (49 * q - 14 * s) * (45 * q + 10 * s) = x4 at A4 ⊢
  generalize (63 * q) * (25 * q) = x5 at A5 ⊢
  generalize (14 * s) * (25 * q + 25 * s) = x6 at A6 ⊢
  generalize (14 * q + 14 * s) * (25 * s) = x7 at A7 ⊢
  clear hF hE
  generalize (q : ℤ) ^ 2 = Q at *
  rcases le_or_gt 0 F with hF0 | hF0
  · have hmax : [x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7].max? = some x6 := by
      rw [List.max?_eq_some_iff']
      refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
      intro b hb
      simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> omega
    have hmin : [x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7].min? = some x2 := by
      rw [List.min?_eq_some_iff']
      refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
      intro b hb
      simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> omega
    rw [hmax, hmin, Option.getD_some, Option.getD_some, abs_of_nonneg (by omega)]
    omega
  · have hmax : [x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7].max? = some x2 := by
      rw [List.max?_eq_some_iff']
      refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
      intro b hb
      simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> omega
    have hmin : [x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7].min? = some x6 := by
      rw [List.min?_eq_some_iff']
      refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
      intro b hb
      simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> omega
    rw [hmax, hmin, Option.getD_some, Option.getD_some, abs_of_neg (by omega)]
    omega

explanation.summary: Since $p$ and $q$ have the same parity and $q < p < 7q$, we write $p = q + 2s$ with $s < 3q$. Evaluating the areas of the seven rectangles in the dissection reveals that each area in $\mathbb{Z}$ has the form $1575q^2 + c_i F$, where $F = 2s^2 + 2qs - 9q^2 = \frac{1}{2}(p^2 - 19q^2)$ and the coefficients $c_i$ belong to $\{-105, -70, 0, 175\}$. A case split on the sign of $F$ determines which rectangle attains the maximum area and which attains the minimum area. In both cases, the difference between the maximum and minimum area evaluates to $(175 - (-105))|F| = 280|F| = 140|p^2 - 19q^2|$, establishing the defect formula.

steps.claim: $p$ can be written as $q + 2s$ for some $s < 3q$.
steps.explanation: Because $p$ and $q$ have the same parity ($p \equiv q \pmod 2$) and $q < p$, their difference $p - q$ is positive and even, so $p = q + 2s$ with $s = (p - q) / 2$. The hypothesis $p < 7q$ translates to $q + 2s < 7q$, which gives $s < 3q$ by linear arithmetic (`omega`).
steps.code:
obtain ⟨s, rfl⟩ : ∃ s, p = q + 2 * s := ⟨(p - q) / 2, by omega⟩
  have hs3 : s < 3 * q := by omega

steps.claim: The areas of the seven rectangles in `mondrian_seven_rects (q + 2 * s) q` evaluate to explicit factored forms in $q$ and $s$.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definitions of `mondrian_seven_rects`, `mondrian_rect_area`, `mondrian_rect_width`, and `mondrian_rect_height`, and simplifying list mapping with `List.map_cons`, `List.map_nil`, `List.cons.injEq`, and `and_true`, reduces the evaluation to verifying seven width-height products. Each linear factor simplifies to the required form by linear arithmetic (`omega`).
steps.code:
have hmap : (mondrian_seven_rects (q + 2 * s) q).map mondrian_rect_area =
      [(63 * q + 14 * s) * (35 * q - 10 * s), (42 * q - 14 * s) * (60 * q + 15 * s),
       (56 * q + 14 * s) * (45 * q - 15 * s), (49 * q - 14 * s) * (45 * q + 10 * s),
       (63 * q) * (25 * q), (14 * s) * (25 * q + 25 * s), (14 * q + 14 * s) * (25 * s)] := by
    simp only [mondrian_seven_rects, List.map_cons, List.map_nil, mondrian_rect_area,
      mondrian_rect_width, mondrian_rect_height, List.cons.injEq, and_true]
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> congr 1 <;> omega

steps.claim: The defect of the dissection is expressed as the difference between the maximum and minimum of the seven rectangle areas.
steps.explanation: Rewriting with the definition of `mondrian_defect` and the computed list of areas `hmap` replaces the defect with the difference between the maximum and minimum elements of the list of seven areas.
steps.code: rw [mondrian_defect, hmap]

steps.claim: The four subtractions inside the rectangle dimensions do not underflow: $10s \le 35q$, $14s \le 42q$, $15s \le 45q$, and $14s \le 49q$.
steps.explanation: Since $s < 3q$, each inequality follows directly by linear arithmetic (`omega`).
steps.code:
have c1 : 10 * s ≤ 35 * q := by omega
  have c2 : 14 * s ≤ 42 * q := by omega
  have c3 : 15 * s ≤ 45 * q := by omega
  have c4 : 14 * s ≤ 49 * q := by omega

steps.claim: With $F = 2s^2 + 2qs - 9q^2 \in \mathbb{Z}$, the quantity $p^2 - 19q^2$ equals $2F$.
steps.explanation: We introduce the integer variable $F = 2s^2 + 2qs - 9q^2$. Substituting $p = q + 2s$, the expression $(q + 2s)^2 - 19q^2$ expands algebraically to $4s^2 + 4qs - 18q^2 = 2F$, verified by polynomial ring arithmetic (`ring`). We then rewrite the theorem's goal using this relation.
steps.code:
-- F = 2 s² + 2 q s − 9 q², so that p² − 19 q² = 2F
  obtain ⟨F, hF⟩ : ∃ F : ℤ, F = 2 * (s : ℤ) ^ 2 + 2 * (q : ℤ) * s - 9 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 := ⟨_, rfl⟩
  have hE : ((q + 2 * s : ℕ) : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 = 2 * F := by rw [hF]; push_cast; ring
  rw [hE]

steps.explanation: Each product is expanded in $\mathbb{Z}$. Subtractions in natural numbers are converted to integer subtractions using `Nat.cast_sub` with the non-negativity bounds $c_1, \dots, c_4$. Expanding $F = 2s^2 + 2qs - 9q^2$ and simplifying by ring arithmetic (`ring`) shows that every area takes the form $1575q^2 + c_i F$ for coefficients $c_i \in \{-105, -70, 0, 175\}$.
steps.code:
have A1 : (((63 * q + 14 * s) * (35 * q - 10 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 - 70 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast [Nat.cast_sub c1]; ring
  have A2 : (((42 * q - 14 * s) * (60 * q + 15 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 - 105 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast [Nat.cast_sub c2]; ring
  have A3 : (((56 * q + 14 * s) * (45 * q - 15 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 - 105 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast [Nat.cast_sub c3]; ring
  have A4 : (((49 * q - 14 * s) * (45 * q + 10 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 - 70 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast [Nat.cast_sub c4]; ring
  have A5 : (((63 * q) * (25 * q) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 := by push_cast; ring
  have A6 : (((14 * s) * (25 * q + 25 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 + 175 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast; ring
  have A7 : (((14 * q + 14 * s) * (25 * s) : ℕ) : ℤ) = 1575 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 + 175 * F := by
    rw [hF]; push_cast; ring

steps.claim: The area expressions and $q^2$ are abstracted into variables $x_1, \dots, x_7$ and $Q$.
steps.explanation: We replace the seven explicit area expressions with names $x_1, \dots, x_7$ and substitute $Q = q^2$. This isolates the area comparisons to their linear dependence on $F$.
steps.code:
generalize (63 * q + 14 * s) * (35 * q - 10 * s) = x1 at A1 ⊢
  generalize (42 * q - 14 * s) * (60 * q + 15 * s) = x2 at A2 ⊢
  generalize (56 * q + 14 * s) * (45 * q - 15 * s) = x3 at A3 ⊢
  generalize (49 * q - 14 * s) * (45 * q + 10 * s) = x4 at A4 ⊢
  generalize (63 * q) * (25 * q) = x5 at A5 ⊢
  generalize (14 * s) * (25 * q + 25 * s) = x6 at A6 ⊢
  generalize (14 * q + 14 * s) * (25 * s) = x7 at A7 ⊢
  clear hF hE
  generalize (q : ℤ) ^ 2 = Q at *

steps.claim: The argument divides into two cases: $F \ge 0$ and $F < 0$.
steps.explanation: By linear order trichotomy (`le_or_gt`), either $0 \le F$ or $F < 0$.
steps.code: rcases le_or_gt 0 F with hF0 | hF0

steps.claim: When $F \ge 0$, the maximum area is $x_6$, the minimum area is $x_2$, and the defect is $140|E|$.
steps.explanation: Because $F \ge 0$, the areas $1575Q + c_i F$ are ordered by their coefficients $c_i$. The maximal coefficient is $+175$ (giving $x_6$ as maximum) and the minimal coefficient is $-105$ (giving $x_2$ as minimum). Using `List.max?_eq_some_iff'` and `List.min?_eq_some_iff'`, membership in the list is decomposed by `List.mem_cons`, `List.not_mem_nil`, and `or_false`, with all comparisons verified by `omega`. The defect is therefore $x_6 - x_2 = (1575Q + 175F) - (1575Q - 105F) = 280F$. Since $F \ge 0$, we have $|2F| = 2F$ by `abs_of_nonneg`, so $140|2F| = 280F$, which matches.

· have hmax : [x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7].max? = some x6 := by
      rw [List.max?_eq_some_iff']
      refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
      intro b hb
      simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> omega
    have hmin : [x1, x2, x3, x4, x5, x6, x7].min? = some x2 := by

      refine ⟨by simp, ?_⟩
      intro b hb
      simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hb
      rcases hb with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> omega
    rw [hmax, hmin, Option.getD_some, Option.getD_some, abs_of_nonneg (by omega)]
    omega

steps.explanation: Because $F < 0$, the order of the coefficients reverses: the negative coefficient $-105$ yields the maximum area $x_2$, while $+175$ yields the minimum area $x_6$. Again, `List.max?_eq_some_iff'` and `List.min?_eq_some_iff'` identify the extremes, with membership checked by `List.mem_cons`, `List.not_mem_nil`, and `or_false`. The defect is $x_2 - x_6 = -280F$. Since $F < 0$, $|2F| = -2F$ by `abs_of_neg`, giving $140|2F| = -280F$, which concludes the proof.

glossary.mondrian_seven_rects: the dissection into seven rectangles $(x_1, x_2, y_1, y_2)$ parameterized by natural numbers $p$ and $q$
glossary.List.map_cons: mapping a function over a non-empty list applies it to the head and recurses on the tail: `List.map f (a :: l) = f a :: List.map f l`
glossary.List.map_nil: mapping a function over the empty list gives the empty list: `List.map f [] = []`
glossary.mondrian_rect_area: the area of a rectangle, defined as width times height
glossary.mondrian_rect_width: the width of a rectangle $(x_1, x_2, y_1, y_2)$, defined as $x_2 - x_1$
glossary.mondrian_rect_height: the height of a rectangle $(x_1, x_2, y_1, y_2)$, defined as $y_2 - y_1$
glossary.List.cons.injEq: two non-empty lists are equal if and only if their heads are equal and their tails are equal
glossary.mondrian_defect: the defect of a dissection, defined as the maximum rectangle area minus the minimum rectangle area (defaulting to 0 on an empty list)
glossary.Nat.cast_sub: for natural numbers $m \le n$, the integer cast of their difference is the difference of their integer casts: $\uparrow(n - m) = \uparrow n - \uparrow m$
glossary.le_or_gt: in a linear order, either $a \le b$ or $b < a$
glossary.List.max?_eq_some_iff': the maximum of a list of natural numbers is `some a` if and only if $a$ is in the list and every element $b$ in the list satisfies $b \le a$
glossary.List.min?_eq_some_iff': the minimum of a list of natural numbers is `some a` if and only if $a$ is in the list and every element $b$ in the list satisfies $a \le b$
glossary.List.mem_cons: an element belongs to $b :: l$ if and only if it equals $b$ or belongs to $l$
glossary.List.not_mem_nil: the empty list contains no elements
glossary.Option.getD_some: extracting a value from `some a` with default fallback $b$ returns $a$: `(some a).getD b = a`

caveats: The rectangle dimensions and area identities involve extensive polynomial and linear arithmetic over ℕ and ℤ, which Lean verifies using `omega`, `ring`, and `push_cast`.

declarations.name: mondrian_seven_rects_partition_defect
declarations.informal: Let p, q be positive integers of the same parity with q < p < 7q, n = 105q and E = p² − 19q². The seven rectangles R₁, …, R₇ of (2)–(3) have positive integer sides, partition the n×n square and are pairwise noncongruent, and the defect of this partition is 140|E|.
declarations.statement:
theorem mondrian_seven_rects_partition_defect (p q : ℕ) (hpar : p % 2 = q % 2) (hqp : q < p)
    (hp : p < 7 * q) :
    mondrian_is_partition (105 * q) (mondrian_seven_rects p q) ∧
      (mondrian_defect (mondrian_seven_rects p q) : ℤ) = 140 * |(p : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2|
declarations.source:
theorem mondrian_seven_rects_partition_defect (p q : ℕ) (hpar : p % 2 = q % 2) (hqp : q < p)
    (hp : p < 7 * q) :
    mondrian_is_partition (105 * q) (mondrian_seven_rects p q) ∧
      (mondrian_defect (mondrian_seven_rects p q) : ℤ) = 140 * |(p : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2| :=
  ⟨mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition p q hpar hqp hp, mondrian_seven_rects_defect p q hpar hqp hp⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.19193 (A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem), Proposition 1 (with the partition property stated before it).

explanation.summary: The theorem asserts both that the seven rectangles form a valid Mondrian partition of the $(105q) \times (105q)$ square and that the defect of this partition is $140 |p^2 - 19q^2|$. The proof directly combines the two previously proven results for these two facts into a single conjunction.

steps.claim: The seven rectangles partition the $(105q) \times (105q)$ square into pairwise noncongruent rectangles, and the defect of the partition is $140 |p^2 - 19q^2|$.
steps.explanation: The goal is a conjunction of two assertions. The first conjunct, that the seven rectangles form a valid partition of the $(105q) \times (105q)$ square into pairwise noncongruent rectangles, is established directly by mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition. The second conjunct, that the defect between the maximum and minimum rectangle areas is $140 |p^2 - 19q^2|$, is established directly by mondrian_seven_rects_defect. Constructing the pair completes the proof.
steps.code: ⟨mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition p q hpar hqp hp, mondrian_seven_rects_defect p q hpar hqp hp⟩

glossary.mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition: For integers $p, q$ of the same parity with $q < p < 7q$, the seven specified rectangles form a valid partition of the $(105q) \times (105q)$ square into pairwise disjoint, noncongruent rectangles with positive integer dimensions.
glossary.mondrian_seven_rects_defect: For integers $p, q$ of the same parity with $q < p < 7q$, the defect of the partition (the difference between its largest and smallest rectangle areas) equals $140 |p^2 - 19q^2|$.

declarations.name: mondrian_seven_rects_defect_ge
declarations.informal: Within the seven-rectangle family, the defect is always at least 280 (in particular never 0): if p, q are odd then p² − 19q² ≡ 2 (mod 4), and if both are even then 4 ∣ E with E ≠ 0, so |E| ≥ 2.
declarations.statement:
theorem mondrian_seven_rects_defect_ge (p q : ℕ) (hpar : p % 2 = q % 2) (hqp : q < p)
    (hp : p < 7 * q) :
    280 ≤ mondrian_defect (mondrian_seven_rects p q)
declarations.source:
theorem mondrian_seven_rects_defect_ge (p q : ℕ) (hpar : p % 2 = q % 2) (hqp : q < p)
    (hp : p < 7 * q) :
    280 ≤ mondrian_defect (mondrian_seven_rects p q) := by
  have h := mondrian_seven_rects_defect p q hpar hqp hp
  have hne : (p : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 ≠ 0 := by
    intro hE
    have hEq : p ^ 2 = 19 * q ^ 2 := by exact_mod_cast (sub_eq_zero.mp hE)
    have hq0 : q ≠ 0 := by omega
    have hp0 : p ≠ 0 := by omega
    haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 19) := ⟨by norm_num⟩
    have hv := congrArg (padicValNat 19) hEq
    rw [padicValNat.pow, padicValNat.mul (by norm_num) (pow_ne_zero 2 hq0),
      padicValNat.pow, padicValNat_self] at hv
    omega
  obtain ⟨s, rfl⟩ : ∃ s, p = q + 2 * s := ⟨(p - q) / 2, by omega⟩
  have hF : ((q + 2 * s : ℕ) : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 =
      2 * (2 * (s : ℤ) ^ 2 + 2 * q * s - 9 * q ^ 2) := by push_cast; ring
  rw [hF] at h hne
  have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ |2 * (s : ℤ) ^ 2 + 2 * q * s - 9 * q ^ 2| := by
    apply Int.one_le_abs
    intro h0
    apply hne
    rw [h0, mul_zero]
  rw [abs_mul, abs_of_pos (by norm_num : (0 : ℤ) < 2)] at h
  have h2 : (280 : ℤ) ≤ (mondrian_defect (mondrian_seven_rects (q + 2 * s) q) : ℤ) := by
    rw [h]; linarith
  exact_mod_cast h2
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.19193 (A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem), Proposition 2.

explanation.summary: The proof uses the known formula expressing the defect of the seven-rectangle configuration as 140 · |p² − 19q²|. It first proves that p² − 19q² ≠ 0 using 19-adic valuations: since 19 is prime, p² = 19q² would require 2 · v₁₉(p) = 1 + 2 · v₁₉(q), which is impossible by parity. Next, since p and q share parity with q < p, writing p = q + 2s reveals that p² − 19q² = 2 · (2s² + 2qs − 9q²). Because this nonzero integer has an explicit factor of 2, its absolute value is at least 2, ensuring that the defect is at least 140 · 2 = 280.

steps.claim: The defect of the seven-rectangle dissection is 140 · |p² − 19q²| as an integer
steps.explanation: We instantiate the known defect formula `mondrian_seven_rects_defect` using the assumed parity condition p % 2 = q % 2 and the inequalities q < p < 7q.
steps.code: have h := mondrian_seven_rects_defect p q hpar hqp hp

steps.claim: p² − 19q² ≠ 0
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that p² − 19q² = 0, so p² = 19q² with p, q > 0 (via `sub_eq_zero.mp`). Since 19 is prime, applying the 19-adic valuation v₁₉ to both sides (via `congrArg`) and expanding using valuation rules for products and powers (`padicValNat.pow`, `padicValNat.mul`, `pow_ne_zero`, `padicValNat_self`) produces the identity 2 · v₁₉(p) = 1 + 2 · v₁₉(q). This equates an even integer with an odd integer, which is impossible.
steps.code:
have hne : (p : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 ≠ 0 := by
    intro hE
    have hEq : p ^ 2 = 19 * q ^ 2 := by exact_mod_cast (sub_eq_zero.mp hE)
    have hq0 : q ≠ 0 := by omega
    have hp0 : p ≠ 0 := by omega
    haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 19) := ⟨by norm_num⟩
    have hv := congrArg (padicValNat 19) hEq
    rw [padicValNat.pow, padicValNat.mul (by norm_num) (pow_ne_zero 2 hq0),
      padicValNat.pow, padicValNat_self] at hv
    omega

steps.claim: There exists a natural number s such that p = q + 2s
steps.explanation: Because p and q share the same parity (p % 2 = q % 2) and q < p, their difference p − q is a positive even integer, so setting s = (p − q) / 2 provides the required witness.
steps.code: obtain ⟨s, rfl⟩ : ∃ s, p = q + 2 * s := ⟨(p - q) / 2, by omega⟩

steps.claim: p² − 19q² factors as 2 · (2s² + 2qs − 9q²), and this product is nonzero
steps.explanation: Substituting p = q + 2s into p² − 19q² and expanding algebraically yields 2 · (2s² + 2qs − 9q²). Rewriting this expression into both the defect equation and the nonvanishing hypothesis shows that the defect is 140 · |2 · (2s² + 2qs − 9q²)| and that this product does not vanish.
steps.code:
have hF : ((q + 2 * s : ℕ) : ℤ) ^ 2 - 19 * (q : ℤ) ^ 2 =
      2 * (2 * (s : ℤ) ^ 2 + 2 * q * s - 9 * q ^ 2) := by push_cast; ring
  rw [hF] at h hne

steps.claim: The integer factor |2s² + 2qs − 9q²| is at least 1
steps.explanation: Any nonzero integer has absolute value at least 1 (`Int.one_le_abs`). If 2s² + 2qs − 9q² were zero, multiplying it by 2 would give 0 (`mul_zero`), contradicting our previous finding that 2 · (2s² + 2qs − 9q²) ≠ 0.
steps.code:
have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ |2 * (s : ℤ) ^ 2 + 2 * q * s - 9 * q ^ 2| := by
    apply Int.one_le_abs
    intro h0
    apply hne
    rw [h0, mul_zero]

steps.claim: The defect of the seven-rectangle dissection is at least 280
steps.explanation: Factoring out |2| = 2 from the absolute value (`abs_mul`, `abs_of_pos`) turns 140 · |2 · (2s² + 2qs − 9q²)| into 280 · |2s² + 2qs − 9q²|. Since |2s² + 2qs − 9q²| ≥ 1, linear arithmetic gives 280 ≤ defect in the integers, which `exact_mod_cast` transfers to the natural numbers to conclude the theorem.
steps.code:
rw [abs_mul, abs_of_pos (by norm_num : (0 : ℤ) < 2)] at h
  have h2 : (280 : ℤ) ≤ (mondrian_defect (mondrian_seven_rects (q + 2 * s) q) : ℤ) := by
    rw [h]; linarith
  exact_mod_cast h2

glossary.mondrian_seven_rects_defect: For natural numbers satisfying the bounds and parity conditions, the defect of the seven-rectangle dissection is 140 · |p² − 19q²|
glossary.sub_eq_zero.mp: If a − b = 0, then a = b
glossary.congrArg: If two inputs are equal, applying any function to them yields equal outputs: a = b implies f(a) = f(b)
glossary.padicValNat.pow: The p-adic valuation of a power is vₚ(aⁿ) = n · vₚ(a)
glossary.padicValNat.mul: For nonzero natural numbers a and b, the p-adic valuation of their product is vₚ(ab) = vₚ(a) + vₚ(b)
glossary.pow_ne_zero: In a domain with no zero divisors, powers of a nonzero element are nonzero: a ≠ 0 implies aⁿ ≠ 0
glossary.padicValNat_self: For any prime p, the p-adic valuation of p is 1, i.e., vₚ(p) = 1
glossary.Int.one_le_abs: Any nonzero integer has absolute value at least 1
glossary.mul_zero: Multiplying any element by zero gives zero: a · 0 = 0
glossary.abs_mul: The absolute value of a product is the product of the absolute values: |ab| = |a| · |b|
glossary.abs_of_pos: If an element is strictly positive, its absolute value equals itself: a > 0 implies |a| = a

declarations.name: mondrian_pell_family_defect_280
declarations.informal: For n₀ = 315, n₁ = 106785, n_{j+2} = 340n_{j+1} − n_j: for every j the n_j×n_j square has a Mondrian partition into seven pairwise noncongruent integer rectangles with defect 280, and n_j ≡ 315 (mod 630).
declarations.statement:
theorem mondrian_pell_family_defect_280 (j : ℕ) :
    (∃ P, mondrian_is_partition (mondrian_pell_side j) P ∧ P.length = 7 ∧ mondrian_defect P = 280) ∧
      mondrian_pell_side j % 630 = 315
declarations.source:
theorem mondrian_pell_family_defect_280 (j : ℕ) :
    (∃ P, mondrian_is_partition (mondrian_pell_side j) P ∧ P.length = 7 ∧ mondrian_defect P = 280) ∧
      mondrian_pell_side j % 630 = 315 := by
  refine ⟨?_, mondrian_pell_side_mod j⟩
  obtain ⟨p, q, hp1, hq1, hqp, hp7, hE, hn⟩ := mondrian_pell_side_eq j
  have hpar : p % 2 = q % 2 := by omega
  refine ⟨mondrian_seven_rects p q, ?_, by simp [mondrian_seven_rects], ?_⟩
  · rw [hn]
    exact mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition p q hpar hqp hp7
  · have h := mondrian_seven_rects_defect p q hpar hqp hp7
    rw [hE] at h
    norm_num at h
    exact_mod_cast h
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.19193 (A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem), Theorem 1.1 (the liminf consequence is stated separately as mondrian_liminf_min_defect_seven_le).

explanation.summary: The modular condition on the side length n_j ≡ 315 (mod 630) is established immediately by an existing lemma. To produce the partition, the side length is represented as n_j = 105q using parameters from a Pell-type equation p² − 19q² = −2 with q < p < 7q. An explicit seven-rectangle geometric configuration is then instantiated: its validity as a noncongruent partition is guaranteed by these bounds, and its defect evaluates to 140|p² − 19q²| = 140 × 2 = 280.

steps.claim: The modular condition on the side length holds, reducing the theorem to constructing the required partition.
steps.explanation: The second conjunct, mondrian_pell_side j % 630 = 315, is resolved directly by the lemma mondrian_pell_side_mod, leaving only the existential claim for the 7-rectangle partition of defect 280.
steps.code: refine ⟨?_, mondrian_pell_side_mod j⟩

steps.claim: There exist odd integers p and q satisfying q < p < 7q, p² − 19q² = −2, n_j = 105q, and p ≡ q (mod 2).
steps.explanation: The lemma mondrian_pell_side_eq supplies parameters p and q satisfying the Pell-type equation p² − 19q² = −2, the side length relation n_j = 105q, and the bounds q < p < 7q. Since both p and q are odd, linear integer arithmetic (omega) establishes that they have identical parity.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨p, q, hp1, hq1, hqp, hp7, hE, hn⟩ := mondrian_pell_side_eq j
  have hpar : p % 2 = q % 2 := by omega

steps.claim: The list of rectangles mondrian_seven_rects p q is chosen as the candidate partition.
steps.explanation: We instantiate the existential witness with the explicit configuration mondrian_seven_rects p q. Unfolding its definition confirms it contains exactly seven rectangles, leaving two subgoals: verifying it partitions the n_j × n_j square and computing its defect.
steps.code: refine ⟨mondrian_seven_rects p q, ?_, by simp [mondrian_seven_rects], ?_⟩

steps.claim: The candidate rectangles form a valid Mondrian partition of the n_j × n_j square.
steps.explanation: Rewriting the side length n_j to 105q using the equality from the Pell parameters, the partition property follows from mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition, since p and q satisfy the required parity equality and bounds q < p < 7q.
steps.code:
· rw [hn]
    exact mondrian_seven_rects_is_partition p q hpar hqp hp7

steps.claim: The defect of the partition is 280.
steps.explanation: By mondrian_seven_rects_defect, the defect of this configuration is 140|p² − 19q²|. Substituting p² − 19q² = −2 yields 140|−2| = 280, which simplifies by arithmetic (norm_num) and is cast from integers to natural numbers.
steps.code:
· have h := mondrian_seven_rects_defect p q hpar hqp hp7
    rw [hE] at h
    norm_num at h
    exact_mod_cast h

glossary.mondrian_seven_rects_defect: If p and q have the same parity and q < p < 7q, the defect of the partition mondrian_seven_rects p q equals 140|p² − 19q²|.

declarations.name: mondrian_liminf_min_defect_seven_le
declarations.informal: liminf_{n→∞} M₇(n) ≤ 280: infinitely many squares have a seven-rectangle Mondrian partition with defect at most 280.
declarations.statement:
theorem mondrian_liminf_min_defect_seven_le :
    Filter.liminf (fun n => mondrian_min_defect_seven n) Filter.atTop ≤ 280
declarations.source:
theorem mondrian_liminf_min_defect_seven_le :
    Filter.liminf (fun n => mondrian_min_defect_seven n) Filter.atTop ≤ 280 := by
  have hgrow : ∀ j, j ≤ mondrian_pell_side j := by
    have key : ∀ j, j + 315 ≤ mondrian_pell_side j ∧ mondrian_pell_side j + 1 ≤ mondrian_pell_side (j + 1) := by
      intro j
      induction j with
      | zero => simp [mondrian_pell_side]
      | succ n ih =>
        obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := ih
        have e : mondrian_pell_side (n + 2) = 340 * mondrian_pell_side (n + 1) - mondrian_pell_side n := rfl
        refine ⟨by omega, ?_⟩
        rw [e]; omega
    exact fun j => by have := (key j).1; omega
  apply Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le'
  rw [Filter.frequently_atTop]
  intro N
  refine ⟨mondrian_pell_side N, hgrow N, ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨⟨P, hP, hlen, hdef⟩, -⟩ := mondrian_pell_family_defect_280 N
  calc mondrian_min_defect_seven (mondrian_pell_side N) ≤ (mondrian_defect P : ℕ∞) :=
        iInf₂_le P ⟨hP, hlen⟩
    _ = 280 := by rw [hdef]; rfl
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.19193 (A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem), Theorem 1.1 ('Consequently liminf M(n) ≤ 280'; the partitions used have seven rectangles, so the bound holds for M₇).

explanation.summary: To show that liminf_{n→∞} M₇(n) ≤ 280, it suffices to find an unbounded sequence of square side lengths admitting a 7-rectangle Mondrian partition of defect at most 280. We consider the sequence s_j = mondrian_pell_side j generated by a Pell-type recurrence, which is shown by induction to satisfy s_j ≥ j and thus grow to infinity. For each j, the lemma mondrian_pell_family_defect_280 provides an explicit 7-rectangle partition of the s_j × s_j square with defect 280, showing M₇(s_j) ≤ 280 holds frequently and yielding the liminf bound.

steps.claim: The sequence of square side lengths satisfies j ≤ mondrian_pell_side j for all j, and in particular grows without bound.
steps.explanation: We prove a stronger invariant by induction on j: j + 315 ≤ mondrian_pell_side j and mondrian_pell_side j + 1 ≤ mondrian_pell_side (j + 1). For j = 0, the side lengths are mondrian_pell_side 0 = 315 and mondrian_pell_side 1 = 106785, which satisfy both inequalities. In the inductive step from n to n + 1, the first inequality (n + 1) + 315 ≤ mondrian_pell_side (n + 1) follows from the induction hypotheses n + 315 ≤ mondrian_pell_side n and mondrian_pell_side n < mondrian_pell_side (n + 1). The second inequality uses the recurrence mondrian_pell_side (n + 2) = 340 * mondrian_pell_side (n + 1) - mondrian_pell_side n; since mondrian_pell_side n < mondrian_pell_side (n + 1), linear arithmetic confirms it exceeds mondrian_pell_side (n + 1) + 1. Finally, j ≤ j + 315 ≤ mondrian_pell_side j yields j ≤ mondrian_pell_side j.
steps.code:
have hgrow : ∀ j, j ≤ mondrian_pell_side j := by
    have key : ∀ j, j + 315 ≤ mondrian_pell_side j ∧ mondrian_pell_side j + 1 ≤ mondrian_pell_side (j + 1) := by
      intro j
      induction j with
      | zero => simp [mondrian_pell_side]
      | succ n ih =>
        obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := ih
        have e : mondrian_pell_side (n + 2) = 340 * mondrian_pell_side (n + 1) - mondrian_pell_side n := rfl
        refine ⟨by omega, ?_⟩
        rw [e]; omega
    exact fun j => by have := (key j).1; omega

steps.claim: To show liminf_{n→∞} M₇(n) ≤ 280, it suffices to show that for every threshold N, M₇(mondrian_pell_side N) ≤ 280.
steps.explanation: By Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le', the limit inferior along Filter.atTop is at most 280 if M₇(n) ≤ 280 holds frequently. Rewriting this condition with Filter.frequently_atTop means that for any threshold N, there must exist some b ≥ N with M₇(b) ≤ 280. Choosing b = mondrian_pell_side N, the growth lemma guarantees N ≤ mondrian_pell_side N, so it suffices to show M₇(mondrian_pell_side N) ≤ 280.
steps.code:
apply Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le'
  rw [Filter.frequently_atTop]
  intro N
  refine ⟨mondrian_pell_side N, hgrow N, ?_⟩

steps.claim: M₇(mondrian_pell_side N) ≤ 280, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: The lemma mondrian_pell_family_defect_280 provides a partition P of the square of side mondrian_pell_side N into 7 rectangles with defect exactly 280. Because M₇(n) is defined as the infimum of defects over all valid 7-rectangle partitions of an n × n square, iInf₂_le bounds this infimum by the defect of P, which is 280.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨⟨P, hP, hlen, hdef⟩, -⟩ := mondrian_pell_family_defect_280 N
  calc mondrian_min_defect_seven (mondrian_pell_side N) ≤ (mondrian_defect P : ℕ∞) :=
        iInf₂_le P ⟨hP, hlen⟩
    _ = 280 := by rw [hdef]; rfl

glossary.Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le': If a property holds frequently along a filter, then the limit inferior along that filter is bounded above by any value that bounds the property.
glossary.Filter.frequently_atTop: A predicate holds frequently along the atTop filter if and only if for every threshold a, there exists some b ≥ a satisfying the predicate.
glossary.mondrian_pell_family_defect_280: For every index j, there exists a 7-rectangle Mondrian partition of the square of side mondrian_pell_side j with defect 280, and the side length is congruent to 315 modulo 630.
glossary.iInf₂_le: The infimum of a doubly indexed family ⨅ i, ⨅ j, f i j is bounded above by any particular entry f i j.

declarations.name: zero_sum_basis_seq_w_bad
declarations.informal: For n > 1 and r ≥ 1, the admissible sequence E_{r,n} (length 2r(n−1)) has no nonempty subsequence whose sum is ≡ 0 (mod n) but ≢ 0 (mod n²).
declarations.statement:
theorem zero_sum_basis_seq_w_bad (r n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) :
    zero_sum_w_bad n (zero_sum_basis_seq r n) ∧ (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).length = 2 * r * (n - 1)
declarations.source:
theorem zero_sum_basis_seq_w_bad (r n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) :
    zero_sum_w_bad n (zero_sum_basis_seq r n) ∧ (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).length = 2 * r * (n - 1) := by
  have hpos : ∀ j : Fin r,
      ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).map (fun a => max (a j) 0)).sum = ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
    intro j
    simp [zero_sum_basis_seq, List.flatMap, List.sum_flatten, Function.comp_def, Pi.single_apply]
    rw [← Fin.sum_univ_def, ← Fin.sum_univ_def]
    have h1 : ∀ i : Fin r, max (if j = i then (1 : ℤ) else 0) 0 = if j = i then 1 else 0 := by
      intro i; split_ifs <;> simp
    have h2 : ∀ i : Fin r, max (-if j = i then (1 : ℤ) else 0) 0 = 0 := by
      intro i; split_ifs <;> simp
    simp [h1, h2]
  have hneg : ∀ j : Fin r,
      ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).map (fun a => max (-a j) 0)).sum = ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
    intro j
    simp [zero_sum_basis_seq, List.flatMap, List.sum_flatten, Function.comp_def, Pi.single_apply]
    rw [← Fin.sum_univ_def, ← Fin.sum_univ_def]
    have h1 : ∀ i : Fin r, max (if j = i then (1 : ℤ) else 0) 0 = if j = i then 1 else 0 := by
      intro i; split_ifs <;> simp
    have h2 : ∀ i : Fin r, max (-if j = i then (1 : ℤ) else 0) 0 = 0 := by
      intro i; split_ifs <;> simp
    simp [h1, h2]
  have hcast : ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = (n : ℤ) - 1 := by push_cast [Nat.cast_sub hn.le]; ring
  refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro a ha
    simp only [zero_sum_basis_seq, List.mem_flatMap, List.mem_finRange, true_and, List.mem_append,
      List.mem_replicate] at ha
    obtain ⟨j, (⟨-, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩)⟩ := ha
    · refine ⟨j, ?_⟩
      simp only [Pi.single_eq_same]
      intro h
      have := Int.le_of_dvd one_pos h
      omega
    · refine ⟨j, ?_⟩
      simp only [Pi.neg_apply, Pi.single_eq_same]
      intro h
      have := Int.le_of_dvd one_pos ((Int.dvd_neg).mp h)
      omega
  · rintro I ⟨-, hdiv, j, hj⟩
    apply hj
    have hup : ∑ i ∈ I, (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j ≤ ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
      calc ∑ i ∈ I, (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j
          ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, max ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j) 0 :=
            Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => le_max_left _ _)
        _ ≤ ∑ i, max ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j) 0 :=
            Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
              (fun i _ _ => le_max_right _ _)
        _ = ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).map (fun a => max (a j) 0)).sum := by
            simpa using Fin.sum_univ_fun_getElem (zero_sum_basis_seq r n) (fun a => max (a j) 0)
        _ = _ := hpos j
    have hlo : -((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j := by
      have : ∑ i ∈ I, -(zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j ≤ ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
        calc ∑ i ∈ I, -(zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j
            ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, max (-(zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j) 0 :=
              Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => le_max_left _ _)
          _ ≤ ∑ i, max (-(zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j) 0 :=
              Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
                (fun i _ _ => le_max_right _ _)
          _ = ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).map (fun a => max (-a j) 0)).sum := by
              simpa using Fin.sum_univ_fun_getElem (zero_sum_basis_seq r n) (fun a => max (-a j) 0)
          _ = _ := hneg j
      rw [Finset.sum_neg_distrib] at this
      linarith
    obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hdiv j
    rw [hk] at hup hlo ⊢
    rw [hcast] at hup hlo
    have hn' : (1 : ℤ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hn
    have hk0 : k = 0 := by
      rcases lt_trichotomy k 0 with h | h | h
      · nlinarith
      · exact h
      · nlinarith
    rw [hk0, mul_zero]
    exact dvd_zero _
  · simp [zero_sum_basis_seq, List.length_flatMap]
    ring
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.19965 (Proofs and disproofs of some conjectures on zero-sum problems), Lemma 3.1 (first part; the bound on w_r(n) is zero_sum_w_ge).

explanation.summary: The sequence E_{r,n} is formed by concatenating n - 1 copies of e_j and n - 1 copies of -e_j for each of the r standard basis vectors, giving total length 2r(n - 1). Every element has a coordinate of ±1, which cannot be divisible by n > 1, so the sequence is admissible. For any subsequence and any coordinate j, the coordinate sum is bounded between -(n - 1) and n - 1 because the positive and negative entries across the entire sequence each sum to n - 1. Any integer in this range divisible by n must be 0, which is divisible by n², precluding any subsequence whose sum is ≡ 0 (mod n) but ≢ 0 (mod n²).

steps.claim: For every coordinate j, the sum of the positive parts max(a j, 0) over all vectors a in the sequence equals n - 1.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of the sequence, each basis direction i contributes n - 1 copies of e_i and n - 1 copies of -e_i. Projecting onto coordinate j and taking max(·, 0), only the n - 1 copies of e_j contribute a value of 1, while all -e_i and all other e_i (i ≠ j) contribute 0. Summing across all indices yields (n - 1) · 1 = n - 1.
steps.code:
have hpos : ∀ j : Fin r,
      ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).map (fun a => max (a j) 0)).sum = ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
    intro j
    simp [zero_sum_basis_seq, List.flatMap, List.sum_flatten, Function.comp_def, Pi.single_apply]
    rw [← Fin.sum_univ_def, ← Fin.sum_univ_def]
    have h1 : ∀ i : Fin r, max (if j = i then (1 : ℤ) else 0) 0 = if j = i then 1 else 0 := by
      intro i; split_ifs <;> simp
    have h2 : ∀ i : Fin r, max (-if j = i then (1 : ℤ) else 0) 0 = 0 := by
      intro i; split_ifs <;> simp
    simp [h1, h2]

steps.claim: For every coordinate j, the sum of the negative parts max(-a j, 0) over all vectors a in the sequence equals n - 1.
steps.explanation: Similarly, taking max(-a j, 0) isolates negative entries. At coordinate j, only the n - 1 copies of -e_j evaluate to 1, while all other vectors evaluate to 0, giving a total sum of n - 1.
steps.code:
have hneg : ∀ j : Fin r,
      ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).map (fun a => max (-a j) 0)).sum = ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
    intro j
    simp [zero_sum_basis_seq, List.flatMap, List.sum_flatten, Function.comp_def, Pi.single_apply]
    rw [← Fin.sum_univ_def, ← Fin.sum_univ_def]
    have h1 : ∀ i : Fin r, max (if j = i then (1 : ℤ) else 0) 0 = if j = i then 1 else 0 := by
      intro i; split_ifs <;> simp
    have h2 : ∀ i : Fin r, max (-if j = i then (1 : ℤ) else 0) 0 = 0 := by
      intro i; split_ifs <;> simp
    simp [h1, h2]

steps.claim: The cast of n - 1 from ℕ to ℤ equals (n : ℤ) - 1.
steps.explanation: Since n > 1, we have 1 ≤ n, so natural subtraction n - 1 commutes with the integer cast.
steps.code: have hcast : ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = (n : ℤ) - 1 := by push_cast [Nat.cast_sub hn.le]; ring

steps.claim: The goal is split into admissibility, absence of good subsequences, and sequence length, and admissibility is established.
steps.explanation: The proof decomposes into three conjuncts. To show admissibility, any vector a in the sequence is either e_j or -e_j for some index j. Its j-th coordinate is therefore 1 or -1. Since n > 1, n cannot divide 1 or -1 (which would force n ≤ 1), so coordinate j is not divisible by n.
steps.code:
refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro a ha
    simp only [zero_sum_basis_seq, List.mem_flatMap, List.mem_finRange, true_and, List.mem_append,
      List.mem_replicate] at ha
    obtain ⟨j, (⟨-, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩)⟩ := ha
    · refine ⟨j, ?_⟩
      simp only [Pi.single_eq_same]
      intro h
      have := Int.le_of_dvd one_pos h
      omega
    · refine ⟨j, ?_⟩
      simp only [Pi.neg_apply, Pi.single_eq_same]
      intro h
      have := Int.le_of_dvd one_pos ((Int.dvd_neg).mp h)
      omega

steps.claim: For any subsequence I and any coordinate j, the coordinate sum is bounded between -(n - 1) and n - 1.
steps.explanation: For the upper bound, each entry A_i(j) is bounded by max(A_i(j), 0). Summing over the subcollection I is at most summing over the entire sequence (since max(·, 0) ≥ 0), which equals n - 1 by the earlier positive sum calculation. Similarly, summing -A_i(j) over I is at most n - 1 by the negative sum calculation, which negates to the lower bound -(n - 1) ≤ ∑_{i ∈ I} A_i(j).
steps.code:
· rintro I ⟨-, hdiv, j, hj⟩
    apply hj
    have hup : ∑ i ∈ I, (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j ≤ ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
      calc ∑ i ∈ I, (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j
          ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, max ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j) 0 :=
            Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => le_max_left _ _)
        _ ≤ ∑ i, max ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j) 0 :=
            Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
              (fun i _ _ => le_max_right _ _)
        _ = ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).map (fun a => max (a j) 0)).sum := by
            simpa using Fin.sum_univ_fun_getElem (zero_sum_basis_seq r n) (fun a => max (a j) 0)
        _ = _ := hpos j
    have hlo : -((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j := by
      have : ∑ i ∈ I, -(zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j ≤ ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
        calc ∑ i ∈ I, -(zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j
            ≤ ∑ i ∈ I, max (-(zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j) 0 :=
              Finset.sum_le_sum (fun i _ => le_max_left _ _)
          _ ≤ ∑ i, max (-(zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j) 0 :=
              Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg (Finset.subset_univ _)
                (fun i _ _ => le_max_right _ _)
          _ = ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).map (fun a => max (-a j) 0)).sum := by
              simpa using Fin.sum_univ_fun_getElem (zero_sum_basis_seq r n) (fun a => max (-a j) 0)
          _ = _ := hneg j
      rw [Finset.sum_neg_distrib] at this
      linarith

steps.claim: No subsequence has all coordinate sums divisible by n and at least one not divisible by n².
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that I is such a subsequence, so n divides every coordinate sum, but n² does not divide the sum at some coordinate j. Writing the j-th coordinate sum as n · k for an integer k, the bounds -(n - 1) ≤ n · k ≤ n - 1 together with n > 1 force k = 0 (as k ≤ -1 gives n · k ≤ -n < -(n - 1) and k ≥ 1 gives n · k ≥ n > n - 1). Thus the sum is 0, which is divisible by n², a contradiction.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hdiv j
    rw [hk] at hup hlo ⊢
    rw [hcast] at hup hlo
    have hn' : (1 : ℤ) < n := by exact_mod_cast hn
    have hk0 : k = 0 := by
      rcases lt_trichotomy k 0 with h | h | h
      · nlinarith
      · exact h
      · nlinarith
    rw [hk0, mul_zero]
    exact dvd_zero _

steps.claim: The sequence has length 2 * r * (n - 1).
steps.explanation: The sequence consists of r blocks, each containing two sublists of length n - 1, giving total length r · ((n - 1) + (n - 1)) = 2 · r · (n - 1).
steps.code:
· simp [zero_sum_basis_seq, List.length_flatMap]
    ring

glossary.Fin.sum_univ_def: The sum of a function over Fin n equals the sum over the list of all indices in Fin n.
glossary.Fin.sum_univ_fun_getElem: The sum of f evaluated at each element of a list l equals the sum of the mapped list l.map f.
glossary.Finset.sum_le_sum: If f i ≤ g i for all i in a finite set, then ∑ i, f i ≤ ∑ i, g i.
glossary.Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg: If s ⊆ t and f is non-negative on t \ s, then the sum of f over s is at most the sum of f over t.
glossary.Finset.sum_neg_distrib: The sum of -f i over a finite set equals the negation of the sum of f i.
glossary.Finset.subset_univ: Any finite subset of a finite type is a subset of the full universe Finset.univ.
glossary.Function.comp_def: The definition of function composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)).
glossary.Int.dvd_neg: An integer divides -b if and only if it divides b.
glossary.Int.le_of_dvd: If b > 0 and a divides b, then a ≤ b.
glossary.List.flatMap: Maps a function that returns lists over a list and flattens the resulting list of lists.
glossary.List.length_flatMap: The length of a flat-mapped list is the sum of the lengths of the resulting sublists.
glossary.List.mem_append: An element belongs to the concatenation s ++ t if and only if it belongs to s or to t.
glossary.List.mem_finRange: Every element of Fin n belongs to List.finRange n.
glossary.List.mem_flatMap: An element belongs to a flat-mapped list if and only if it belongs to the image list of some element in the original list.
glossary.List.mem_replicate: An element b belongs to List.replicate n a if and only if n ≠ 0 and b = a.
glossary.List.sum_flatten: The sum of the elements of a concatenated list of lists equals the sum of the sums of each inner list.
glossary.Nat.cast_sub: For m ≤ n, casting n - m to an additive group with one yields ↑n - ↑m.
glossary.Pi.neg_apply: Pointwise negation of a function: (-f) i = -f i.
glossary.Pi.single_apply: The indicator function Pi.single i x evaluated at index i' equals x if i' = i and 0 otherwise.
glossary.Pi.single_eq_same: The indicator function Pi.single i x evaluated at the same index i equals x.
glossary.le_max_left: Any element a satisfies a ≤ max a b.
glossary.le_max_right: Any element b satisfies b ≤ max a b.
glossary.lt_trichotomy: In any linear order, exactly one of a < b, a = b, or b < a holds.
glossary.mul_zero: Multiplying any element by zero yields zero: a * 0 = 0.
glossary.true_and: True ∧ p is equivalent to p.

declarations.name: zero_sum_w_ge
declarations.informal: w_r(n) ≥ 2r(n−1) + 1 for all r ≥ 1 and n > 1.
declarations.statement: theorem zero_sum_w_ge (r n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : ((2 * r * (n - 1) + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ zero_sum_w r n
declarations.source:
theorem zero_sum_w_ge (r n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : ((2 * r * (n - 1) + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤ zero_sum_w r n := by
  unfold zero_sum_w
  refine le_iInf₂ (fun N hN => ?_)
  by_contra hlt
  rw [not_le] at hlt
  have hle : N ≤ 2 * r * (n - 1) := by
    have := (Nat.cast_lt (α := ℕ∞)).mp hlt
    omega
  obtain ⟨hbad, hlen⟩ := zero_sum_basis_seq_w_bad r n hn
  have htl : ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).take N).length ≤ (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).length := by
    simp
  obtain ⟨I, hIne, hIdiv, j, hj⟩ := hN ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).take N) (by simp [hlen]; omega)
    (fun a ha => hbad.1 a (List.mem_of_mem_take ha))
  have hsum : ∀ j, ∑ i ∈ I.map ⟨Fin.castLE htl, Fin.castLE_injective htl⟩,
      (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j = ∑ i ∈ I, ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).take N).get i j := by
    intro j
    rw [Finset.sum_map]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
    simp [List.getElem_take]
  apply hbad.2 (I.map ⟨Fin.castLE htl, Fin.castLE_injective htl⟩)
  refine ⟨hIne.map, fun j => ?_, j, ?_⟩
  · rw [hsum]; exact hIdiv j
  · rw [hsum]; exact hj

explanation.summary: The constant $w_r(n)$ is defined as the infimum of all sequence lengths $N$ such that every admissible sequence in $(\mathbb{Z}/n^2\mathbb{Z})^r$ of length $N$ contains a good zero-sum subsequence. To establish the lower bound $w_r(n) \ge 2r(n-1)+1$, it suffices to show that any such length $N$ satisfies $N \ge 2r(n-1)+1$. Assuming for contradiction that $N \le 2r(n-1)$, we truncate the known admissible sequence `zero_sum_basis_seq r n` of length $2r(n-1)$ to its first $N$ elements. This prefix is an admissible sequence of length $N$ and must therefore contain a good subsequence; but embedding this subsequence back into the original sequence produces a good subsequence of `zero_sum_basis_seq r n`, contradicting the fact that this sequence was constructed to contain none.

steps.claim: To show $w_r(n) \ge 2r(n-1) + 1$, it suffices to show that any candidate length $N$ guaranteeing a good subsequence satisfies $N \ge 2r(n-1) + 1$.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of $w_r(n)$, it is the infimum over all sequence lengths $N$ such that every admissible sequence of length $N$ has a good subsequence. By `le_iInf₂`, a number is a lower bound for this infimum if it is bounded above by every such $N$.
steps.code:
unfold zero_sum_w
  refine le_iInf₂ (fun N hN => ?_)

steps.claim: Assume for contradiction that $N \le 2r(n-1)$.
steps.explanation: Assuming for contradiction that $2r(n-1) + 1 \le N$ is false, `not_le` gives $N < 2r(n-1) + 1$. Stripping the coercion to $\mathbb{N}_\infty$ using `Nat.cast_lt`, linear arithmetic (`omega`) implies $N \le 2r(n-1)$.
steps.code:
by_contra hlt
  rw [not_le] at hlt
  have hle : N ≤ 2 * r * (n - 1) := by
    have := (Nat.cast_lt (α := ℕ∞)).mp hlt
    omega

steps.claim: The prefix of length $N$ of `zero_sum_basis_seq r n` is admissible and must contain a good subsequence indexed by $I$.
steps.explanation: By `zero_sum_basis_seq_w_bad`, there is an admissible sequence `zero_sum_basis_seq r n` of length $2r(n-1)$ that contains no good subsequence. Since $N \le 2r(n-1)$, taking its prefix of length $N$ gives a sequence of length exactly $N$. Every vector in this prefix is in the original sequence (`List.mem_of_mem_take`), so the prefix is also admissible. By the hypothesis on $N$, this prefix must contain a good subsequence, giving a nonempty index set $I$ whose coordinate sums are divisible by $n$, with some coordinate $j$ not divisible by $n^2$.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨hbad, hlen⟩ := zero_sum_basis_seq_w_bad r n hn
  have htl : ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).take N).length ≤ (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).length := by
    simp
  obtain ⟨I, hIne, hIdiv, j, hj⟩ := hN ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).take N) (by simp [hlen]; omega)
    (fun a ha => hbad.1 a (List.mem_of_mem_take ha))

steps.claim: The coordinate sums over $I$ in the prefix equal the coordinate sums over the embedded indices in the full sequence.
steps.explanation: Because the prefix length $N$ is at most the total length, indices of the prefix embed injectively into indices of the full sequence via `Fin.castLE`. Using `Finset.sum_map`, the sum over the mapped indices equals the sum over $I$ evaluated at the mapped positions. Since the prefix shares its elements at each index with the full sequence (`List.getElem_take`), `Finset.sum_congr` confirms that every coordinate sum is preserved.
steps.code:
have hsum : ∀ j, ∑ i ∈ I.map ⟨Fin.castLE htl, Fin.castLE_injective htl⟩,
      (zero_sum_basis_seq r n).get i j = ∑ i ∈ I, ((zero_sum_basis_seq r n).take N).get i j := by
    intro j
    rw [Finset.sum_map]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
    simp [List.getElem_take]

steps.claim: The embedded subsequence is a good subsequence of `zero_sum_basis_seq r n`, yielding a contradiction.
steps.explanation: The image of $I$ under the embedding is nonempty because $I$ is nonempty. Rewriting the coordinate sums of the full sequence to those of the prefix, the sums are all divisible by $n$, and the $j$-th coordinate sum is not divisible by $n^2$. Thus the mapped index set is a good subsequence of `zero_sum_basis_seq r n`, contradicting the fact that `zero_sum_basis_seq r n` has no good subsequence.
steps.code:
apply hbad.2 (I.map ⟨Fin.castLE htl, Fin.castLE_injective htl⟩)
  refine ⟨hIne.map, fun j => ?_, j, ?_⟩
  · rw [hsum]; exact hIdiv j
  · rw [hsum]; exact hj

glossary.le_iInf₂: A lower bound for all terms in a doubly indexed family is a lower bound for its infimum.
glossary.not_le: In a linear order, $\neg (a \le b)$ is equivalent to $b < a$.
glossary.Nat.cast_lt: The strict inequality $m < n$ between natural numbers is preserved under coercion to $\mathbb{N}_\infty$.
glossary.zero_sum_basis_seq_w_bad: The canonical sequence `zero_sum_basis_seq r n` has length $2r(n-1)$ and is bad: it is admissible, but contains no good subsequence.
glossary.List.mem_of_mem_take: Any element belonging to a prefix `List.take i l` is also an element of the original list $l$.
glossary.Fin.castLE: Embeds $\text{Fin } n$ into $\text{Fin } m$ whenever $n \le m$.
glossary.Fin.castLE_injective: The canonical embedding from $\text{Fin } n$ to $\text{Fin } m$ when $n \le m$ is injective.
glossary.Finset.sum_map: Summing a function over the image of a finite set under an embedding equals summing the pull-back of that function over the original finite set.
glossary.Finset.sum_congr: Two finite sums are equal if their index sets are equal and their summands agree on each index.
glossary.List.getElem_take: The $i$-th element of a prefix `List.take j xs` is equal to the $i$-th element of the list `xs`.

caveats: The quantity $w_r(n)$ takes values in $\mathbb{N}_\infty = \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$, where an empty infimum evaluates to $\infty$. The lower bound is therefore stated and proven in $\mathbb{N}_\infty$.

Vectors in the group are formalized as integer-valued functions $\text{Fin } r \to \mathbb{Z}$, and a subsequence of a list $A$ is represented by a set of position indices $I \subseteq \text{Fin } A.\text{length}$.

declarations.name: kayak_paddle_hop_maps_second_cycle
declarations.informal: In KP(k, m, l) with m even, every hop maps the vertex set of the second cycle (the m-cycle) into itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem kayak_paddle_hop_maps_second_cycle (k m l : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hl : 1 ≤ l)
    (he : Even m) (h : Equiv.Perm (Fin (k + m + l - 1)))
    (hh : simple_graph_is_hop (simple_graph_kayak_paddle k m l) h) (v : Fin (k + m + l - 1))
    (hv : k + l - 1 ≤ (v : ℕ)) : k + l - 1 ≤ (h v : ℕ)
declarations.source:
theorem kayak_paddle_hop_maps_second_cycle (k m l : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hl : 1 ≤ l)
    (he : Even m) (h : Equiv.Perm (Fin (k + m + l - 1)))
    (hh : simple_graph_is_hop (simple_graph_kayak_paddle k m l) h) (v : Fin (k + m + l - 1))
    (hv : k + l - 1 ≤ (v : ℕ)) : k + l - 1 ≤ (h v : ℕ) := by
  set s := k + l - 1 with hs
  -- neighbours of the open path T = {v | s < v} stay in the second cycle
  have stepA : ∀ u w : Fin (k + m + l - 1), s < (w : ℕ) →
      (simple_graph_kayak_paddle k m l).Adj w u → s ≤ (u : ℕ) := by
    intro u w hw hadj
    simp only [simple_graph_kayak_paddle, SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj] at hadj
    omega
  -- adjacency inside T is adjacency along the path
  have stepB : ∀ u w : Fin (k + m + l - 1), s < (u : ℕ) → s < (w : ℕ) →
      (simple_graph_kayak_paddle k m l).Adj u w → (w : ℕ) = u + 1 ∨ (u : ℕ) = w + 1 := by
    intro u w hu hw hadj
    have hu' := u.isLt
    have hw' := w.isLt
    simp only [simple_graph_kayak_paddle, SimpleGraph.fromRel_adj] at hadj
    obtain ⟨-, h1 | h1⟩ := hadj
    · rcases h1 with h1 | h1 | h1 | ⟨-, -, h1⟩
      · omega
      · omega
      · omega
      · rcases Nat.lt_or_ge ((u : ℕ) - s + 1) m with h2 | h2
        · rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h2] at h1; omega
        · have : (u : ℕ) - s + 1 = m := by omega
          rw [this, Nat.mod_self] at h1; omega
    · rcases h1 with h1 | h1 | h1 | ⟨-, -, h1⟩
      · omega
      · omega
      · omega
      · rcases Nat.lt_or_ge ((w : ℕ) - s + 1) m with h2 | h2
        · rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt h2] at h1; omega
        · have : (w : ℕ) - s + 1 = m := by omega
          rw [this, Nat.mod_self] at h1; omega
  -- first: h s lies in the second cycle
  have hN : s < k + m + l - 1 := by omega
  have hjun : s ≤ (h ⟨s, hN⟩ : ℕ) := by
    by_contra hlt
    rw [not_le] at hlt
    obtain ⟨m2, hm2⟩ := he
    -- g = h⁻¹ maps T into T, moving each point by one along the path
    set g := h⁻¹ with hg
    have gT : ∀ t : Fin (k + m + l - 1), s < (t : ℕ) →
        s < (g t : ℕ) ∧ ((g t : ℕ) = t + 1 ∨ (t : ℕ) = g t + 1) := by
      intro t ht
      have hadj : (simple_graph_kayak_paddle k m l).Adj (g t) t := by
        have := hh (g t)
        simpa [hg] using this
      have h1 : s ≤ (g t : ℕ) := stepA (g t) t ht hadj.symm
      have h2 : (g t : ℕ) ≠ s := by
        intro heq
        have : g t = ⟨s, hN⟩ := Fin.ext heq
        have hgt : h (g t) = t := by simp [hg]
        rw [this] at hgt
        rw [hgt] at hlt
        omega
      have h3 : s < (g t : ℕ) := by omega
      exact ⟨h3, (stepB (g t) t h3 ht hadj).symm⟩
    -- counting: odd offsets map injectively to even offsets
    let ψ : ℕ → ℕ := fun a => if ha : a < k + m + l - 1 then (g ⟨a, ha⟩ : ℕ) else 0
    let A : Finset ℕ := (Finset.range (m / 2)).image (fun t => s + 1 + 2 * t)
    let B : Finset ℕ := (Finset.range (m / 2 - 1)).image (fun t => s + 2 + 2 * t)
    have hA : A.card = m / 2 :=
      by rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (fun x y hxy => by simp at hxy; omega), Finset.card_range]
    have hB : B.card = m / 2 - 1 :=
      by rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ (fun x y hxy => by simp at hxy; omega), Finset.card_range]
    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ A, ψ a ∈ B := by
      intro a ha
      simp only [A, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_range] at ha
      obtain ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩ := ha
      have hlt' : s + 1 + 2 * t < k + m + l - 1 := by omega
      have hgt := gT ⟨s + 1 + 2 * t, hlt'⟩ (by show s < s + 1 + 2 * t; omega)
      simp only [Fin.val_mk] at hgt
      have hbound := (g ⟨s + 1 + 2 * t, hlt'⟩).isLt
      simp only [ψ, B, Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_range]
      rw [dif_pos hlt']
      generalize hx : ((g ⟨s + 1 + 2 * t, hlt'⟩ : Fin _) : ℕ) = x at hgt hbound ⊢
      rcases hgt with ⟨h1, h2 | h2⟩
      · exact ⟨t, by omega, by omega⟩
      · exact ⟨t - 1, by omega, by omega⟩
    have hinj : Set.InjOn ψ A := by
      intro a ha b hb hab
      simp only [A, Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_range] at ha hb
      obtain ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩ := ha
      obtain ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩ := hb
      have h1 : s + 1 + 2 * t < k + m + l - 1 := by omega
      have h2 : s + 1 + 2 * u < k + m + l - 1 := by omega
      simp only [ψ] at hab
      rw [dif_pos h1, dif_pos h2] at hab
      have := g.injective (Fin.ext hab)
      simpa using congrArg Fin.val this
    have := Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn ψ hmaps hinj
    rw [hA, hB] at this
    omega
  -- then every vertex of the second cycle stays there
  rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le hv with hv' | hv'
  · have : v = ⟨s, hN⟩ := Fin.ext hv'.symm
    rw [this]; exact hjun
  · exact stepA (h v) v hv' (hh v)
