declarations.name: exists_complete_mapping_stabilizing_sylow_two_of_normal
declarations.informal: Let G be a finite group, N a normal subgroup and P a Sylow 2-subgroup of G. If N has a complete mapping stabilizing P ∩ N and G/N has a complete mapping stabilizing PN/N, then G has a complete mapping stabilizing P.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_complete_mapping_stabilizing_sylow_two_of_normal {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G]
    (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] (P : Sylow 2 G)
    (hN : ∃ φ : N → N, group_is_complete_mapping φ ∧
      φ '' {x : N | (x : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G)} = {x : N | (x : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G)})
    (hQ : ∃ θ : G ⧸ N → G ⧸ N, group_is_complete_mapping θ ∧
      θ '' ((P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) : Set (G ⧸ N)) =
        ((P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) : Set (G ⧸ N))) :
    ∃ θ : G → G, group_is_complete_mapping θ ∧
      θ '' ((P : Subgroup G) : Set G) = ((P : Subgroup G) : Set G)
declarations.source:
theorem exists_complete_mapping_stabilizing_sylow_two_of_normal {G : Type*} [Group G] [Finite G]
    (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal] (P : Sylow 2 G)
    (hN : ∃ φ : N → N, group_is_complete_mapping φ ∧
      φ '' {x : N | (x : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G)} = {x : N | (x : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G)})
    (hQ : ∃ θ : G ⧸ N → G ⧸ N, group_is_complete_mapping θ ∧
      θ '' ((P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) : Set (G ⧸ N)) =
        ((P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) : Set (G ⧸ N))) :
    ∃ θ : G → G, group_is_complete_mapping θ ∧
      θ '' ((P : Subgroup G) : Set G) = ((P : Subgroup G) : Set G) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨φ, ⟨hφ, hφc⟩, hφP⟩ := hN
  obtain ⟨τ, ⟨hτ, hτc⟩, hτP⟩ := hQ
  have hφP' : ∀ n : N, (n : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G) → (φ n : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G) := by
    intro n hn
    have : φ n ∈ φ '' {x : N | (x : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G)} := ⟨n, hn, rfl⟩
    rw [hφP] at this
    exact this
  have hτP' : ∀ t, t ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) →
      τ t ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) := by
    intro t ht
    have : τ t ∈ τ '' ((P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) : Set (G ⧸ N)) := ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩
    rw [hτP] at this
    exact this
  -- representatives, chosen in P over the image of P
  have hrep : ∀ t : G ⧸ N, ∃ g : G, (g : G ⧸ N) = t ∧
      (t ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) → g ∈ (P : Subgroup G)) := by
    intro t
    by_cases ht : t ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N)
    · obtain ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩ := Subgroup.mem_map.1 ht
      exact ⟨p, rfl, fun _ => hp⟩
    · obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective t
      exact ⟨g, rfl, fun h => absurd h ht⟩
  choose x hx hxP using hrep
  have hmkN : ∀ n : N, ((n : G) : G ⧸ N) = 1 := fun n => (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff (n : G)).2 n.2
  let A : (G ⧸ N) × N → G := fun p => x p.1 * x (τ p.1) * (p.2 : G) * (x (τ p.1))⁻¹
  let B : (G ⧸ N) × N → G := fun p => x (τ p.1) * (φ p.2 : G)
  have hAmk : ∀ p, ((A p : G) : G ⧸ N) = p.1 := by
    intro p
    simp only [A, QuotientGroup.mk_mul, QuotientGroup.mk_inv, hx, hmkN]
    group
  have hBmk : ∀ p, ((B p : G) : G ⧸ N) = τ p.1 := by
    intro p
    simp only [B, QuotientGroup.mk_mul, hx, hmkN, mul_one]
  have hAB : ∀ p, A p * B p = x p.1 * x (τ p.1) * ((p.2 * φ p.2 : N) : G) := by
    intro p
    simp only [A, B, Subgroup.coe_mul]
    group
  have hcard : Nat.card G ≤ Nat.card ((G ⧸ N) × N) := by
    rw [Nat.card_prod, ← Subgroup.card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card_subgroup]
  have hAinj : Function.Injective A := by
    rintro ⟨t, n⟩ ⟨t', n'⟩ h
    have ht : t = t' := by
      have e1 := hAmk (t, n)
      have e2 := hAmk (t', n')
      rw [h] at e1
      exact e1.symm.trans e2
    subst ht
    simp only [A, mul_left_inj, mul_right_inj] at h
    exact Prod.ext rfl (Subtype.ext h)
  have hBinj : Function.Injective B := by
    rintro ⟨t, n⟩ ⟨t', n'⟩ h
    have ht : t = t' := hτ.1 (by rw [← hBmk (t, n), ← hBmk (t', n'), h])
    subst ht
    simp only [B, mul_right_inj] at h
    exact Prod.ext rfl (hφ.1 (Subtype.ext h))
  have hCinj : Function.Injective fun p => A p * B p := by
    rintro ⟨t, n⟩ ⟨t', n'⟩ h
    have h' : A (t, n) * B (t, n) = A (t', n') * B (t', n') := h
    have ht : t = t' := by
      apply hτc.1
      have e1 := hAmk (t, n)
      have e2 := hBmk (t, n)
      have e3 := hAmk (t', n')
      have e4 := hBmk (t', n')
      have := congrArg (fun g : G => (g : G ⧸ N)) h'
      simp only [QuotientGroup.mk_mul] at this
      rw [e1, e2, e3, e4] at this
      exact this
    subst ht
    rw [hAB, hAB] at h'
    simp only [mul_right_inj] at h'
    exact Prod.ext rfl (hφc.1 (Subtype.ext h'))
  have hAbij : Function.Bijective A := hAinj.bijective_of_nat_card_le hcard
  have hBbij : Function.Bijective B := hBinj.bijective_of_nat_card_le hcard
  have hCbij : Function.Bijective fun p => A p * B p := hCinj.bijective_of_nat_card_le hcard
  let eA := Equiv.ofBijective A hAbij
  have heA : ∀ g, A (eA.symm g) = g := fun g => eA.apply_symm_apply g
  refine ⟨fun g => B (eA.symm g), ⟨hBbij.comp eA.symm.bijective, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · have : (fun g => g * B (eA.symm g)) = (fun p => A p * B p) ∘ eA.symm := by
      funext g
      simp only [Function.comp, heA]
    rw [this]
    exact hCbij.comp eA.symm.bijective
  · have hsub : (fun g => B (eA.symm g)) '' ((P : Subgroup G) : Set G) ⊆ ((P : Subgroup G) : Set G) := by
      rintro _ ⟨g, hg, rfl⟩
      set p := eA.symm g with hp
      have hAp : A p = g := heA g
      have hq : p.1 ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) := by
        rw [← hAmk p, hAp]
        exact Subgroup.mem_map_of_mem _ hg
      have h1 := hxP _ hq
      have h2 := hxP _ (hτP' _ hq)
      have hn : ((p.2 : N) : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G) := by
        have : ((p.2 : N) : G) = (x p.1 * x (τ p.1))⁻¹ * g * x (τ p.1) := by
          rw [← hAp]
          simp only [A]
          group
        rw [this]
        exact mul_mem (mul_mem (inv_mem (mul_mem h1 h2)) hg) h2
      exact mul_mem h2 (hφP' _ hn)
    have hinj : Function.Injective fun g => B (eA.symm g) := hBinj.comp eA.symm.injective
    exact Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le hsub (by rw [Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ hinj])
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.17631 (Complete mappings stabilizing Sylow 2-subgroups in central quotients of special linear groups), Lemma 3.2.

explanation.summary: The proof constructs a complete mapping θ on G stabilizing P by extending the given complete mappings φ on N and τ on G/N. Coset representatives x(t) for t ∈ G/N are chosen in P whenever t belongs to the projection π(P). Two bijections A, B : (G/N) × N → G are defined such that their product is also bijective, allowing θ = B ∘ A⁻¹ to serve as a complete mapping on G. A careful containment check shows θ(P) ⊆ P, from which injectivity and finiteness imply θ(P) = P.

steps.claim: Obtain complete mappings φ on N and τ on G/N, and record that they map elements of P ∩ N into P and cosets in π(P) into π(P).
steps.explanation: From the hypotheses hN and hQ, we extract complete mappings φ : N → N and τ : G/N → G/N stabilizing P ∩ N and π(P) respectively. Since φ(P ∩ N) = P ∩ N and τ(π(P)) = π(P), any n ∈ P ∩ N satisfies φ(n) ∈ P, and any coset t ∈ π(P) satisfies τ(t) ∈ π(P).
steps.code:
classical
  obtain ⟨φ, ⟨hφ, hφc⟩, hφP⟩ := hN
  obtain ⟨τ, ⟨hτ, hτc⟩, hτP⟩ := hQ
  have hφP' : ∀ n : N, (n : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G) → (φ n : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G) := by
    intro n hn
    have : φ n ∈ φ '' {x : N | (x : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G)} := ⟨n, hn, rfl⟩
    rw [hφP] at this
    exact this
  have hτP' : ∀ t, t ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) →
      τ t ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) := by
    intro t ht
    have : τ t ∈ τ '' ((P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) : Set (G ⧸ N)) := ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩
    rw [hτP] at this
    exact this

steps.claim: Choose coset representatives x : G/N → G such that x(t) ∈ P whenever t ∈ π(P), and note that elements of N project to 1 in G/N.
steps.explanation: For each coset t ∈ G/N, if t lies in the projection π(P), we choose a representative in P; otherwise, by surjectivity of the quotient map, we pick an arbitrary representative in G. The axiom of choice yields a selection function x : G/N → G satisfying π(x(t)) = t and x(t) ∈ P when t ∈ π(P). We also note that elements of N project to 1 in G/N.
steps.code:
-- representatives, chosen in P over the image of P
  have hrep : ∀ t : G ⧸ N, ∃ g : G, (g : G ⧸ N) = t ∧
      (t ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) → g ∈ (P : Subgroup G)) := by
    intro t
    by_cases ht : t ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N)
    · obtain ⟨p, hp, rfl⟩ := Subgroup.mem_map.1 ht
      exact ⟨p, rfl, fun _ => hp⟩
    · obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := QuotientGroup.mk_surjective t
      exact ⟨g, rfl, fun h => absurd h ht⟩
  choose x hx hxP using hrep
  have hmkN : ∀ n : N, ((n : G) : G ⧸ N) = 1 := fun n => (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff (n : G)).2 n.2

steps.claim: Define coordinate maps A, B : (G/N) × N → G and compute their projections to G/N and their product.
steps.explanation: We define A(t, n) = x(t) * x(τ(t)) * n * (x(τ(t)))⁻¹ and B(t, n) = x(τ(t)) * φ(n). In the quotient G/N, since elements of N project to 1, we compute π(A(t, n)) = t and π(B(t, n)) = τ(t). Group simplification shows that the product is A(t, n) * B(t, n) = x(t) * x(τ(t)) * (n * φ(n)).
steps.code:
let A : (G ⧸ N) × N → G := fun p => x p.1 * x (τ p.1) * (p.2 : G) * (x (τ p.1))⁻¹
  let B : (G ⧸ N) × N → G := fun p => x (τ p.1) * (φ p.2 : G)
  have hAmk : ∀ p, ((A p : G) : G ⧸ N) = p.1 := by
    intro p
    simp only [A, QuotientGroup.mk_mul, QuotientGroup.mk_inv, hx, hmkN]
    group
  have hBmk : ∀ p, ((B p : G) : G ⧸ N) = τ p.1 := by
    intro p
    simp only [B, QuotientGroup.mk_mul, hx, hmkN, mul_one]
  have hAB : ∀ p, A p * B p = x p.1 * x (τ p.1) * ((p.2 * φ p.2 : N) : G) := by
    intro p
    simp only [A, B, Subgroup.coe_mul]
    group

steps.claim: The maps A, B, and p ↦ A(p) * B(p) are all bijections between (G/N) × N and G.
steps.explanation: Lagrange's theorem shows |G| = |G/N| * |N| = |(G/N) × N|. To show A is injective, if A(t, n) = A(t', n'), projecting to G/N gives t = t', and then group cancellation yields n = n'. For B, projecting to G/N gives τ(t) = τ(t'), so t = t' by injectivity of τ, and cancelling x(τ(t)) gives φ(n) = φ(n'), whence n = n' by injectivity of φ. For A * B, projecting to G/N gives t * τ(t) = t' * τ(t'), so t = t' because τ is a complete mapping; then n * φ(n) = n' * φ(n') implies n = n' because φ is a complete mapping. Since the domain and codomain are finite of the same size, injectivity implies bijectivity for all three maps.
steps.code:
have hcard : Nat.card G ≤ Nat.card ((G ⧸ N) × N) := by
    rw [Nat.card_prod, ← Subgroup.card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card_subgroup]
  have hAinj : Function.Injective A := by
    rintro ⟨t, n⟩ ⟨t', n'⟩ h
    have ht : t = t' := by
      have e1 := hAmk (t, n)
      have e2 := hAmk (t', n')
      rw [h] at e1
      exact e1.symm.trans e2
    subst ht
    simp only [A, mul_left_inj, mul_right_inj] at h
    exact Prod.ext rfl (Subtype.ext h)
  have hBinj : Function.Injective B := by
    rintro ⟨t, n⟩ ⟨t', n'⟩ h
    have ht : t = t' := hτ.1 (by rw [← hBmk (t, n), ← hBmk (t', n'), h])
    subst ht
    simp only [B, mul_right_inj] at h
    exact Prod.ext rfl (hφ.1 (Subtype.ext h))
  have hCinj : Function.Injective fun p => A p * B p := by
    rintro ⟨t, n⟩ ⟨t', n'⟩ h
    have h' : A (t, n) * B (t, n) = A (t', n') * B (t', n') := h
    have ht : t = t' := by
      apply hτc.1
      have e1 := hAmk (t, n)
      have e2 := hBmk (t, n)
      have e3 := hAmk (t', n')
      have e4 := hBmk (t', n')
      have := congrArg (fun g : G => (g : G ⧸ N)) h'
      simp only [QuotientGroup.mk_mul] at this
      rw [e1, e2, e3, e4] at this
      exact this
    subst ht
    rw [hAB, hAB] at h'
    simp only [mul_right_inj] at h'
    exact Prod.ext rfl (hφc.1 (Subtype.ext h'))
  have hAbij : Function.Bijective A := hAinj.bijective_of_nat_card_le hcard
  have hBbij : Function.Bijective B := hBinj.bijective_of_nat_card_le hcard
  have hCbij : Function.Bijective fun p => A p * B p := hCinj.bijective_of_nat_card_le hcard

steps.claim: The map θ = B ∘ A⁻¹ : G → G is a complete mapping on G.
steps.explanation: Using the bijection A to form an equivalence eA : (G/N) × N ≃ G, we define θ(g) = B(eA.symm(g)). As a composition of bijections B and eA.symm, θ is bijective. Furthermore, g * θ(g) = A(eA.symm(g)) * B(eA.symm(g)) = (p ↦ A(p) * B(p))(eA.symm(g)), which is also a composition of bijections and thus bijective. Hence θ is a complete mapping on G.
steps.code:
let eA := Equiv.ofBijective A hAbij
  have heA : ∀ g, A (eA.symm g) = g := fun g => eA.apply_symm_apply g
  refine ⟨fun g => B (eA.symm g), ⟨hBbij.comp eA.symm.bijective, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · have : (fun g => g * B (eA.symm g)) = (fun p => A p * B p) ∘ eA.symm := by
      funext g
      simp only [Function.comp, heA]
    rw [this]
    exact hCbij.comp eA.symm.bijective

steps.claim: The complete mapping θ maps the subgroup P into itself: θ(P) ⊆ P.
steps.explanation: Let g ∈ P and write g = A(t, n) with (t, n) = eA.symm(g). Projecting to G/N gives t = π(g) ∈ π(P). By our choice of coset representatives, x(t) ∈ P, and since τ stabilizes π(P), τ(t) ∈ π(P), which gives x(τ(t)) ∈ P. Solving for n gives n = (x(t) * x(τ(t)))⁻¹ * g * x(τ(t)), which lies in P because g, x(t), and x(τ(t)) all belong to P. Thus n ∈ P ∩ N, so φ(n) ∈ P because φ stabilizes P ∩ N. It follows that θ(g) = B(t, n) = x(τ(t)) * φ(n) is a product of elements of P, hence in P.
steps.code:
· have hsub : (fun g => B (eA.symm g)) '' ((P : Subgroup G) : Set G) ⊆ ((P : Subgroup G) : Set G) := by
      rintro _ ⟨g, hg, rfl⟩
      set p := eA.symm g with hp
      have hAp : A p = g := heA g
      have hq : p.1 ∈ (P : Subgroup G).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) := by
        rw [← hAmk p, hAp]
        exact Subgroup.mem_map_of_mem _ hg
      have h1 := hxP _ hq
      have h2 := hxP _ (hτP' _ hq)
      have hn : ((p.2 : N) : G) ∈ (P : Subgroup G) := by
        have : ((p.2 : N) : G) = (x p.1 * x (τ p.1))⁻¹ * g * x (τ p.1) := by
          rw [← hAp]
          simp only [A]
          group
        rw [this]
        exact mul_mem (mul_mem (inv_mem (mul_mem h1 h2)) hg) h2
      exact mul_mem h2 (hφP' _ hn)

steps.claim: The mapping θ stabilizes P, that is, θ(P) = P.
steps.explanation: Since θ is injective, the image θ(P) has the same finite cardinality as P. Because θ(P) ⊆ P and P is finite, this implies θ(P) = P.
steps.code:
have hinj : Function.Injective fun g => B (eA.symm g) := hBinj.comp eA.symm.injective
    exact Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le hsub (by rw [Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ hinj])

glossary.Prod.ext: Two pairs are equal if and only if both their first components and their second components are equal.
glossary.QuotientGroup.mk_inv: The canonical projection from a group to a quotient group preserves inverses: π(a⁻¹) = π(a)⁻¹.
glossary.QuotientGroup.mk_mul: The canonical projection from a group to a quotient group preserves multiplication: π(a b) = π(a) π(b).
glossary.mul_one: Multiplying by the identity on the right leaves an element unchanged: a * 1 = a.
glossary.QuotientGroup.mk_surjective: The canonical projection from a group to a quotient group is surjective.
glossary.QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff: An element projects to the trivial element in the quotient group G/N if and only if it belongs to N.
glossary.Subgroup.coe_mul: The coercion of a product of subgroup elements to the ambient group equals the product of their coercions: ↑(x * y) = ↑x * ↑y.
glossary.Nat.card_prod: The cardinality of the Cartesian product of two types is the product of their cardinalities: |α × β| = |α| * |β|.
glossary.Subgroup.card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card_: Lagrange's index formula: for any subgroup N of a group G, |G| = |G/N| * |N|.
glossary.mul_left_inj: In a group, right multiplication by an element is injective: b * a = c * a ↔ b = c.
glossary.mul_right_inj: In a group, left multiplication by an element is injective: a * b = a * c ↔ b = c.
glossary.Subtype.ext: Two subtype elements are equal if their underlying values are equal.
glossary.congrArg: Equal arguments yield equal function values: if a = b then f(a) = f(b).
glossary.Equiv.ofBijective: A bijective function can be promoted to a two-sided type equivalence (a bijection with an inverse).
glossary.Function.comp: The definition of function composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)).
glossary.Subgroup.mem_map_of_mem: If x belongs to a subgroup K, its image f(x) belongs to the image subgroup f(K).
glossary.mul_mem: A subgroup is closed under multiplication: if a ∈ S and b ∈ S, then a * b ∈ S.
glossary.inv_mem: A subgroup is closed under inverses: if x ∈ S, then x⁻¹ ∈ S.
glossary.Set.eq_of_subset_of_ncard_le: If s ⊆ t and |t| ≤ |s| for a finite set t, then s = t.
glossary.Set.ncard_image_of_injective: An injective function preserves the cardinality of any set: |f '' s| = |s|.
glossary.Subgroup.mem_map.1: An element belongs to the image of a subgroup under f if and only if it is of the form f(x) for some x in the subgroup.

declarations.name: wild_number_complete_graph_min_proper_coloring_ge
declarations.informal: Let n ≥ 3 and let ρ be a minimum proper edge colouring of K_n (a proper colouring with χ'(K_n) colours). Then wld_ρ(K_n) ≥ ⌊4⌈n/2⌉/3⌋.
declarations.statement:
theorem wild_number_complete_graph_min_proper_coloring_ge (n k : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (hk : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.chromaticNumber = k)
    (c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.Coloring (Fin k)) :
    4 * ((n + 1) / 2) / 3 ≤ simple_graph_wild_number (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) c
declarations.source:
theorem wild_kn_mem {n : ℕ} {u v : Fin n} (h : u ≠ v) : s(u, v) ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet := by
  simpa using h

theorem wild_kn_same_color {n k : ℕ} (c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.Coloring (Fin k))
    {u v w : Fin n} (hv : u ≠ v) (hw : u ≠ w)
    (h : c ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem hv⟩ = c ⟨s(u, w), wild_kn_mem hw⟩) : v = w := by
  by_contra hne
  apply c.valid _ h
  refine ⟨fun h' => hne ?_, ⟨u, by simp, by simp⟩⟩
  have := congrArg Subtype.val h'
  simp only [Sym2.eq_iff] at this
  rcases this with ⟨-, h1⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
  · exact h1
  · exact h2.trans h1

/-- In a graph where u and v have no neighbours outside {u, v}, everything reachable from u is u or v. -/
theorem wild_kn_closed_pair {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (u v : V)
    (hu : ∀ x, G.Adj u x → x = v) (hv : ∀ x, G.Adj v x → x = u) {y : V} (hy : G.Reachable u y) :
    y = u ∨ y = v := by
  obtain ⟨p⟩ := hy
  have key : ∀ a b (p : G.Walk a b), (a = u ∨ a = v) → b = u ∨ b = v := by
    intro a b p
    induction p with
    | nil => exact id
    | cons h _ ih =>
      intro ha
      apply ih
      rcases ha with rfl | rfl
      · exact Or.inr (hu _ h)
      · exact Or.inl (hv _ h)
  exact key _ _ p (Or.inl rfl)

theorem wild_kn_exists_missing_color_of_odd {n k : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hodd : n % 2 = 1)
    (c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.Coloring (Fin k)) (u : Fin n) :
    ∃ e : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet, ∀ x (hx : u ≠ x), c ⟨s(u, x), wild_kn_mem hx⟩ ≠ c e := by
  classical
  by_contra hno
  push_neg at hno
  have h01 : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨1, by omega⟩ := by simp [Fin.ext_iff]
  let i0 := c ⟨s(⟨0, by omega⟩, ⟨1, by omega⟩), wild_kn_mem h01⟩
  let col : Fin n → Fin n → Fin k := fun v x => if h : v ≠ x then c ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem h⟩ else i0
  have hcol : ∀ v x (h : v ≠ x), col v x = c ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem h⟩ := fun v x h => dif_pos h
  let Cv : Fin n → Finset (Fin k) := fun v => (Finset.univ.erase v).image (col v)
  have hCv : ∀ v, (Cv v).card = n - 1 := by
    intro v
    rw [Finset.card_image_of_injOn, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _), Finset.card_univ,
      Fintype.card_fin]
    intro a ha b hb hab
    have ha' := Ne.symm (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase ha)
    have hb' := Ne.symm (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hb)
    rw [hcol v a ha', hcol v b hb'] at hab
    exact wild_kn_same_color c ha' hb' hab
  -- every colour used anywhere is a colour at u, so every vertex sees all of them
  have hsub : ∀ v, Cv v ⊆ Cv u := by
    intro v j hj
    obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hj
    have hx' := Ne.symm (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hx)
    obtain ⟨y, hy, hyc⟩ := hno ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem hx'⟩
    refine Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨y, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨Ne.symm hy, Finset.mem_univ _⟩, ?_⟩
    rw [hcol u y hy, hcol v x hx']
    exact hyc
  have heq : ∀ v, Cv v = Cv u := fun v =>
    Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le (hsub v) (by rw [hCv, hCv])
  have hi0 : i0 ∈ Cv u := by
    rw [← heq ⟨0, by omega⟩]
    refine Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨⟨1, by omega⟩, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨Ne.symm h01, Finset.mem_univ _⟩, ?_⟩
    rw [hcol _ _ h01]
  have hall : ∀ v, ∃ x, ∃ hx : v ≠ x, c ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem hx⟩ = i0 := by
    intro v
    rw [← heq v] at hi0
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxc⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hi0
    have hx' := Ne.symm (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hx)
    exact ⟨x, hx', by rw [← hcol v x hx']; exact hxc⟩
  choose partner hpne hpi using hall
  have hpp : ∀ v, partner (partner v) = v := by
    intro v
    have h1 := hpi (partner v)
    have h2 := hpi v
    have h2' : c ⟨s(partner v, v), wild_kn_mem (Ne.symm (hpne v))⟩ = i0 := by
      rw [← h2]; congr 2; exact Sym2.eq_swap
    exact wild_kn_same_color c (hpne (partner v)) (Ne.symm (hpne v)) (h1.trans h2'.symm)
  let e : Fin n → Sym2 (Fin n) := fun v => s(v, partner v)
  have hfib : ∀ v, (Finset.univ.filter fun w => e w = e v) = {v, partner v} := by
    intro v
    ext w
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_insert,
      Finset.mem_singleton, e, Sym2.eq_iff]
    constructor
    · rintro (⟨h, -⟩ | ⟨h, -⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr h
    · rintro (rfl | rfl)
      · exact Or.inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
      · exact Or.inr ⟨rfl, hpp v⟩
  have hsum := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := e) (s := Finset.univ)
    (t := Finset.univ.image e) (fun x _ => Finset.mem_image_of_mem e (Finset.mem_univ x))
  have h2 : ∀ b ∈ Finset.univ.image e, (Finset.univ.filter fun a => e a = b).card = 2 := by
    intro b hb
    obtain ⟨v, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hb
    rw [hfib v, Finset.card_pair (hpne v)]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl h2, Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul, Finset.card_univ,
    Fintype.card_fin] at hsum
  omega

theorem wild_number_complete_graph_min_proper_coloring_ge (n k : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (hk : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.chromaticNumber = k)
    (c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.Coloring (Fin k)) :
    4 * ((n + 1) / 2) / 3 ≤ simple_graph_wild_number (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) c := by
  classical
  -- the class of colour i together with W
  let G' : Finset (Sym2 (Fin n)) → Fin k → SimpleGraph (Fin n) := fun W i =>
    SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet ({f | ∃ hf : f ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet, c ⟨f, hf⟩ = i} ∪ ↑W)
  have hG'adj : ∀ W i x y, (G' W i).Adj x y ↔ x ≠ y ∧
      ((∃ h : x ≠ y, c ⟨s(x, y), wild_kn_mem h⟩ = i) ∨ s(x, y) ∈ W) := by
    intro W i x y
    simp only [G', SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_coe]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h | h, hxy⟩
      · exact ⟨hxy, Or.inl ⟨hxy, h.2⟩⟩
      · exact ⟨hxy, Or.inr h⟩
    · rintro ⟨hxy, ⟨h, hc⟩ | h⟩
      · exact ⟨Or.inl ⟨wild_kn_mem h, hc⟩, hxy⟩
      · exact ⟨Or.inr h, hxy⟩
  -- a third vertex always exists
  have third : ∀ u v : Fin n, ∃ w, w ≠ u ∧ w ≠ v := by
    intro u v
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    have : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) ⊆ {u, v} := fun w _ => by
      by_cases hw : w = u
      · simp [hw]
      · simp [h w hw]
    have := Finset.card_le_card this
    rw [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at this
    have := Finset.card_le_two (a := u) (b := v)
    omega
  have hlow : ∀ W : Finset (Sym2 (Fin n)),
      simple_graph_is_color_connecting (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) c ↑W →
        4 * ((n + 1) / 2) / 3 ≤ W.card := by
    intro W hW
    have conn : ∀ (u v : Fin n) (huv : u ≠ v), (G' W (c ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem huv⟩)).Connected :=
      fun u v huv => hW.2 ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem huv⟩
    -- (F) a closed pair contradicts connectivity
    have no_closed : ∀ (u v : Fin n) (huv : u ≠ v),
        (∀ x, (G' W (c ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem huv⟩)).Adj u x → x = v) →
        (∀ x, (G' W (c ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem huv⟩)).Adj v x → x = u) → False := by
      intro u v huv h1 h2
      obtain ⟨w, hwu, hwv⟩ := third u v
      rcases wild_kn_closed_pair _ u v h1 h2 ((conn u v huv).preconnected u w) with h | h
      · exact hwu h
      · exact hwv h
    let touched : Finset (Fin n) := Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∃ f ∈ W, v ∈ f
    -- (F1) at most one vertex is untouched
    have F1 : n - 1 ≤ touched.card := by
      have : (Finset.univ.filter fun v => v ∉ touched).card ≤ 1 := by
        rw [Finset.card_le_one]
        intro u hu v hv
        by_contra huv
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, touched, not_exists,
          not_and] at hu hv
        apply no_closed u v huv
        · intro x hx
          rw [hG'adj] at hx
          obtain ⟨hux, ⟨h, hc⟩ | hw⟩ := hx
          · exact wild_kn_same_color c h huv hc
          · exact absurd (Sym2.mem_mk_left u x) (hu _ hw)
        · intro x hx
          rw [hG'adj] at hx
          obtain ⟨hvx, ⟨h, hc⟩ | hw⟩ := hx
          · have hc' : c ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem h⟩ = c ⟨s(v, u), wild_kn_mem (Ne.symm huv)⟩ := by
              rw [hc]; congr 2; exact Sym2.eq_swap
            exact wild_kn_same_color c h (Ne.symm huv) hc'
          · exact absurd (Sym2.mem_mk_left v x) (hv _ hw)
      have hsplit := Finset.card_filter_add_card_filter_not (s := Finset.univ)
        (p := fun v => v ∈ touched)
      rw [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at hsplit
      have htt : (Finset.univ.filter fun v => v ∈ touched) = touched := by
        ext v; simp
      rw [htt] at hsplit
      omega
    -- (F1') for odd n every vertex is touched
    have F1' : n % 2 = 1 → n ≤ touched.card := by
      intro hodd
      have : touched = Finset.univ := by
        rw [Finset.eq_univ_iff_forall]
        intro u
        by_contra hu
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, touched, not_exists,
          not_and] at hu
        obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := wild_kn_exists_missing_color_of_odd hn hodd c u
        obtain ⟨w, hwu, -⟩ := third u u
        obtain ⟨p⟩ := (hW.2 e).preconnected u w
        cases p with
        | nil => exact hwu rfl
        | cons h _ =>
          have h' : (G' W (c e)).Adj u _ := h
          rw [hG'adj] at h'
          obtain ⟨-, ⟨hx, hc⟩ | hw⟩ := h'
          · exact he _ hx hc
          · exact hu _ hw (Sym2.mem_mk_left _ _)
      rw [this, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
    -- degrees in W
    let d : Fin n → ℕ := fun v => (W.filter fun f => v ∈ f).card
    have hhand : ∑ v, d v = 2 * W.card := by
      simp only [d, Finset.card_filter]
      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
      rw [mul_comm, Finset.card_eq_sum_ones, Finset.sum_mul]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun f hf => ?_
      have hfE : f ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet := hW.1 (Finset.mem_coe.2 hf)
      induction f using Sym2.ind with
      | h a b =>
        have hab : a ≠ b := by simpa using hfE
        rw [← Finset.card_filter, one_mul]
        have : (Finset.univ.filter fun v => v ∈ s(a, b)) = {a, b} := by
          ext v; simp
        rw [this, Finset.card_pair hab]
    -- a leaf's edge is shared with no other leaf
    let L : Finset (Fin n) := Finset.univ.filter fun v => d v = 1
    let Bg : Finset (Fin n) := Finset.univ.filter fun v => 2 ≤ d v
    have htouch : touched = L ∪ Bg := by
      ext v
      simp only [touched, L, Bg, d, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_union]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨f, hf, hvf⟩
        have : 1 ≤ (W.filter fun f => v ∈ f).card :=
          Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨f, Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨hf, hvf⟩⟩
        omega
      · intro h
        have : 0 < (W.filter fun f => v ∈ f).card := by omega
        obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := Finset.card_pos.1 this
        exact ⟨f, (Finset.mem_filter.1 hf).1, (Finset.mem_filter.1 hf).2⟩
    have hdisj : Disjoint L Bg := by
      rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
      intro v hv hv'
      simp only [L, Bg, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hv hv'
      omega
    have hdeg : L.card + 2 * Bg.card ≤ ∑ v, d v := by
      calc L.card + 2 * Bg.card = ∑ v ∈ L, 1 + ∑ v ∈ Bg, 2 := by simp [mul_comm]
        _ ≤ ∑ v ∈ L, d v + ∑ v ∈ Bg, d v := by
          gcongr with v hv v hv
          · simp only [L, Finset.mem_filter] at hv; omega
          · simp only [Bg, Finset.mem_filter] at hv; omega
        _ = ∑ v ∈ L ∪ Bg, d v := (Finset.sum_union hdisj).symm
        _ ≤ ∑ v, d v := Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset (Finset.subset_univ _)
    have hleaf : ∀ v ∈ L, ∃ f, W.filter (fun f => v ∈ f) = {f} := by
      intro v hv
      simp only [L, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, d] at hv
      exact Finset.card_eq_one.1 hv
    haveI : Nonempty (Sym2 (Fin n)) := ⟨s(⟨0, by omega⟩, ⟨0, by omega⟩)⟩
    choose! ef hef using hleaf
    have hLW : L.card ≤ W.card := by
      refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn ef (fun v hv => ?_) (fun u hu v hv huv => ?_)
      · have := (Finset.mem_filter.1 ((hef v hv).symm ▸ Finset.mem_singleton_self (ef v))).1
        exact this
      · by_contra hne
        have hu' := (Finset.mem_filter.1 ((hef u hu).symm ▸ Finset.mem_singleton_self (ef u)))
        have hv' := (Finset.mem_filter.1 ((hef v hv).symm ▸ Finset.mem_singleton_self (ef v)))
        -- ef u = s(u, v)
        have huvf : ef u = s(u, v) := by
          have h1 : u ∈ ef u := hu'.2
          have h2 : v ∈ ef u := huv ▸ hv'.2
          have hE : ef u ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet := hW.1 (Finset.mem_coe.2 hu'.1)
          revert h1 h2 hE
          induction ef u using Sym2.ind with
          | h a b =>
            intro h1 h2 hE
            have hab : a ≠ b := by simpa using hE
            simp only [Sym2.mem_iff] at h1 h2
            rw [Sym2.eq_iff]
            rcases h1 with rfl | rfl <;> rcases h2 with rfl | rfl
            · exact absurd rfl hne
            · exact Or.inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
            · exact Or.inr ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
            · exact absurd rfl hne
        have only : ∀ w, w ∈ L → ∀ f ∈ W, w ∈ f → f = ef w := by
          intro w hw f hf hwf
          have : f ∈ W.filter (fun f => w ∈ f) := Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨hf, hwf⟩
          rw [hef w hw] at this
          exact Finset.mem_singleton.1 this
        apply no_closed u v hne
        · intro x hx
          rw [hG'adj] at hx
          obtain ⟨hux, ⟨h, hc⟩ | hw⟩ := hx
          · exact wild_kn_same_color c h hne hc
          · have := only u hu _ hw (Sym2.mem_mk_left u x)
            rw [huvf, Sym2.eq_iff] at this
            rcases this with ⟨-, h⟩ | ⟨h1, -⟩
            · exact h
            · exact absurd h1 hne
        · intro x hx
          rw [hG'adj] at hx
          obtain ⟨hvx, ⟨h, hc⟩ | hw⟩ := hx
          · have hc' : c ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem h⟩ = c ⟨s(v, u), wild_kn_mem (Ne.symm hne)⟩ := by
              rw [hc]; congr 2; exact Sym2.eq_swap
            exact wild_kn_same_color c h (Ne.symm hne) hc'
          · have := only v hv _ hw (Sym2.mem_mk_left v x)
            rw [← huv, huvf, Sym2.eq_iff] at this
            rcases this with ⟨h1, -⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
            · exact absurd h1.symm hne
            · exact h
    have htc : touched.card = L.card + Bg.card := by
      rw [htouch, Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj]
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one n with h0 | h1
    · omega
    · have := F1' h1
      omega
  -- the edge set of K_n is colour-connecting, so the infimum is over a nonempty set
  have hne : (Finset.univ.filter fun f : Sym2 (Fin n) => f ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet).card ∈
      {k | ∃ W : Finset (Sym2 (Fin n)), W.card = k ∧
        simple_graph_is_color_connecting (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) c ↑W} := by
    refine ⟨_, rfl, ?_, fun e => ?_⟩
    · intro f hf; simpa using hf
    · haveI : Nonempty (Fin n) := ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩⟩
      refine SimpleGraph.connected_top.mono ?_
      intro a b hab
      rw [SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj]
      refine ⟨Or.inr (by simpa using hab), hab⟩
  exact le_csInf ⟨_, hne⟩ fun j ⟨W, hj, hW⟩ => by rw [← hj]; exact hlow W hW
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.22142 (Wild number for spanning trees in complete and complete bipartite graphs), Theorem 3.4. ⌈n/2⌉ is written (n + 1) / 2 in ℕ; a minimum proper colouring is a colouring of the line graph by Fin k with k = χ'(K_n) = chromatic number of the line graph.

explanation.summary: To prove that any proper edge colouring of K_n with χ'(K_n) colours has wild number at least ⌊4⌈n/2⌉/3⌋, we analyse any colour-connecting edge set W. We show that vertices of degree 1 in W (leaves) cannot share an edge in W, bounding their number by |W|, and that at most one vertex is untouched by W (none if n is odd). Combining the degree sum formula with these bounds yields 3|W| ≥ 2|touched|, from which linear arithmetic over integer division establishes the required lower bound.

steps.claim: In the complete graph K_n, any pair of distinct vertices forms an edge.
steps.explanation: By definition of the complete graph, an edge exists between any two distinct vertices.
steps.code:
theorem wild_kn_mem {n : ℕ} {u v : Fin n} (h : u ≠ v) : s(u, v) ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet := by
  simpa using h

steps.claim: In a proper edge colouring, two distinct edges sharing an endpoint cannot have the same colour.
steps.explanation: By contradiction, if they had the same colour, they would be adjacent edges in the line graph with identical colours, violating properness.
steps.code:
theorem wild_kn_same_color {n k : ℕ} (c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.Coloring (Fin k))
    {u v w : Fin n} (hv : u ≠ v) (hw : u ≠ w)
    (h : c ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem hv⟩ = c ⟨s(u, w), wild_kn_mem hw⟩) : v = w := by
  by_contra hne
  apply c.valid _ h
  refine ⟨fun h' => hne ?_, ⟨u, by simp, by simp⟩⟩
  have := congrArg Subtype.val h'
  simp only [Sym2.eq_iff] at this
  rcases this with ⟨-, h1⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
  · exact h1
  · exact h2.trans h1

steps.claim: In a graph where u and v have no neighbours outside {u, v}, anything reachable from u is u or v.
steps.explanation: By induction on the length of a walk starting at u or v, every step must remain in {u, v}.
steps.code:
/-- In a graph where u and v have no neighbours outside {u, v}, everything reachable from u is u or v. -/
theorem wild_kn_closed_pair {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (u v : V)
    (hu : ∀ x, G.Adj u x → x = v) (hv : ∀ x, G.Adj v x → x = u) {y : V} (hy : G.Reachable u y) :
    y = u ∨ y = v := by
  obtain ⟨p⟩ := hy
  have key : ∀ a b (p : G.Walk a b), (a = u ∨ a = v) → b = u ∨ b = v := by
    intro a b p
    induction p with
    | nil => exact id
    | cons h _ ih =>
      intro ha
      apply ih
      rcases ha with rfl | rfl
      · exact Or.inr (hu _ h)
      · exact Or.inl (hv _ h)
  exact key _ _ p (Or.inl rfl)

steps.claim: If every edge colour appeared at u, all vertices would see the exact same set of colours.
steps.explanation: Each vertex has degree n - 1, so it sees n - 1 distinct colours. By assumption each colour at any vertex appears at u, so the colour sets are identical by cardinality.
steps.code:
theorem wild_kn_exists_missing_color_of_odd {n k : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hodd : n % 2 = 1)
    (c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.Coloring (Fin k)) (u : Fin n) :
    ∃ e : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet, ∀ x (hx : u ≠ x), c ⟨s(u, x), wild_kn_mem hx⟩ ≠ c e := by
  classical
  by_contra hno
  push_neg at hno
  have h01 : (⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n) ≠ ⟨1, by omega⟩ := by simp [Fin.ext_iff]
  let i0 := c ⟨s(⟨0, by omega⟩, ⟨1, by omega⟩), wild_kn_mem h01⟩
  let col : Fin n → Fin n → Fin k := fun v x => if h : v ≠ x then c ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem h⟩ else i0
  have hcol : ∀ v x (h : v ≠ x), col v x = c ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem h⟩ := fun v x h => dif_pos h
  let Cv : Fin n → Finset (Fin k) := fun v => (Finset.univ.erase v).image (col v)
  have hCv : ∀ v, (Cv v).card = n - 1 := by
    intro v
    rw [Finset.card_image_of_injOn, Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _), Finset.card_univ,
      Fintype.card_fin]
    intro a ha b hb hab
    have ha' := Ne.symm (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase ha)
    have hb' := Ne.symm (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hb)
    rw [hcol v a ha', hcol v b hb'] at hab
    exact wild_kn_same_color c ha' hb' hab
  -- every colour used anywhere is a colour at u, so every vertex sees all of them
  have hsub : ∀ v, Cv v ⊆ Cv u := by
    intro v j hj
    obtain ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hj
    have hx' := Ne.symm (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hx)
    obtain ⟨y, hy, hyc⟩ := hno ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem hx'⟩
    refine Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨y, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨Ne.symm hy, Finset.mem_univ _⟩, ?_⟩
    rw [hcol u y hy, hcol v x hx']
    exact hyc
  have heq : ∀ v, Cv v = Cv u := fun v =>
    Finset.eq_of_subset_of_card_le (hsub v) (by rw [hCv, hCv])

steps.claim: For odd n, there is always a colour missing at any vertex u.
steps.explanation: If every colour appeared at u, a chosen colour would be incident to every vertex, yielding a 1-factor and forcing n to be even, contradiction.
steps.code:
have hi0 : i0 ∈ Cv u := by
    rw [← heq ⟨0, by omega⟩]
    refine Finset.mem_image.2 ⟨⟨1, by omega⟩, Finset.mem_erase.2 ⟨Ne.symm h01, Finset.mem_univ _⟩, ?_⟩
    rw [hcol _ _ h01]
  have hall : ∀ v, ∃ x, ∃ hx : v ≠ x, c ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem hx⟩ = i0 := by
    intro v
    rw [← heq v] at hi0
    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxc⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hi0
    have hx' := Ne.symm (Finset.ne_of_mem_erase hx)
    exact ⟨x, hx', by rw [← hcol v x hx']; exact hxc⟩
  choose partner hpne hpi using hall
  have hpp : ∀ v, partner (partner v) = v := by
    intro v
    have h1 := hpi (partner v)
    have h2 := hpi v
    have h2' : c ⟨s(partner v, v), wild_kn_mem (Ne.symm (hpne v))⟩ = i0 := by
      rw [← h2]; congr 2; exact Sym2.eq_swap
    exact wild_kn_same_color c (hpne (partner v)) (Ne.symm (hpne v)) (h1.trans h2'.symm)
  let e : Fin n → Sym2 (Fin n) := fun v => s(v, partner v)
  have hfib : ∀ v, (Finset.univ.filter fun w => e w = e v) = {v, partner v} := by
    intro v
    ext w
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_insert,
      Finset.mem_singleton, e, Sym2.eq_iff]
    constructor
    · rintro (⟨h, -⟩ | ⟨h, -⟩)
      · exact Or.inl h
      · exact Or.inr h
    · rintro (rfl | rfl)
      · exact Or.inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
      · exact Or.inr ⟨rfl, hpp v⟩
  have hsum := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := e) (s := Finset.univ)
    (t := Finset.univ.image e) (fun x _ => Finset.mem_image_of_mem e (Finset.mem_univ x))
  have h2 : ∀ b ∈ Finset.univ.image e, (Finset.univ.filter fun a => e a = b).card = 2 := by
    intro b hb
    obtain ⟨v, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.1 hb
    rw [hfib v, Finset.card_pair (hpne v)]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl h2, Finset.sum_const, smul_eq_mul, Finset.card_univ,
    Fintype.card_fin] at hsum
  omega

steps.claim: Adjacency in G'(W, i) means two distinct vertices share an edge of colour i or an edge in W.
steps.explanation: This rewrites adjacency in the subgraph formed by the union of edges of colour i and W.
steps.code:
theorem wild_number_complete_graph_min_proper_coloring_ge (n k : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (hk : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.chromaticNumber = k)
    (c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).lineGraph.Coloring (Fin k)) :
    4 * ((n + 1) / 2) / 3 ≤ simple_graph_wild_number (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) c := by
  classical
  -- the class of colour i together with W
  let G' : Finset (Sym2 (Fin n)) → Fin k → SimpleGraph (Fin n) := fun W i =>
    SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet ({f | ∃ hf : f ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet, c ⟨f, hf⟩ = i} ∪ ↑W)
  have hG'adj : ∀ W i x y, (G' W i).Adj x y ↔ x ≠ y ∧
      ((∃ h : x ≠ y, c ⟨s(x, y), wild_kn_mem h⟩ = i) ∨ s(x, y) ∈ W) := by
    intro W i x y
    simp only [G', SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj, Set.mem_union, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.mem_coe]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h | h, hxy⟩
      · exact ⟨hxy, Or.inl ⟨hxy, h.2⟩⟩
      · exact ⟨hxy, Or.inr h⟩
    · rintro ⟨hxy, ⟨h, hc⟩ | h⟩
      · exact ⟨Or.inl ⟨wild_kn_mem h, hc⟩, hxy⟩
      · exact ⟨Or.inr h, hxy⟩

steps.claim: For n ≥ 3, any pair of vertices has a third vertex outside the pair.
steps.explanation: If all vertices belonged to a two-element set, the total number of vertices would be at most 2, contradicting n ≥ 3.
steps.code:
-- a third vertex always exists
  have third : ∀ u v : Fin n, ∃ w, w ≠ u ∧ w ≠ v := by
    intro u v
    by_contra h
    push_neg at h
    have : (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) ⊆ {u, v} := fun w _ => by
      by_cases hw : w = u
      · simp [hw]
      · simp [h w hw]
    have := Finset.card_le_card this
    rw [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at this
    have := Finset.card_le_two (a := u) (b := v)
    omega

steps.claim: A closed pair {u, v} cannot exist in G'(W, c(uv)).
steps.explanation: If u and v only connected to each other, a third vertex would be unreachable from u, contradicting connectivity.
steps.code:
have hlow : ∀ W : Finset (Sym2 (Fin n)),
      simple_graph_is_color_connecting (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) c ↑W →
        4 * ((n + 1) / 2) / 3 ≤ W.card := by
    intro W hW
    have conn : ∀ (u v : Fin n) (huv : u ≠ v), (G' W (c ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem huv⟩)).Connected :=
      fun u v huv => hW.2 ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem huv⟩
    -- (F) a closed pair contradicts connectivity
    have no_closed : ∀ (u v : Fin n) (huv : u ≠ v),
        (∀ x, (G' W (c ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem huv⟩)).Adj u x → x = v) →
        (∀ x, (G' W (c ⟨s(u, v), wild_kn_mem huv⟩)).Adj v x → x = u) → False := by
      intro u v huv h1 h2
      obtain ⟨w, hwu, hwv⟩ := third u v
      rcases wild_kn_closed_pair _ u v h1 h2 ((conn u v huv).preconnected u w) with h | h
      · exact hwu h
      · exact hwv h
    let touched : Finset (Fin n) := Finset.univ.filter fun v => ∃ f ∈ W, v ∈ f

steps.explanation: Two untouched vertices would form a closed pair in the subgraph of their connecting colour, contradicting connectivity.

steps.claim: For odd n, every vertex is touched by W, so |touched| ≥ n.
steps.explanation: If some vertex u were untouched, by the missing colour lemma for odd n there is a colour missing at u, leaving u with degree 0 in that colour's subgraph, contradicting connectivity.
steps.code:
have F1' : n % 2 = 1 → n ≤ touched.card := by
      intro hodd
      have : touched = Finset.univ := by
        rw [Finset.eq_univ_iff_forall]
        intro u
        by_contra hu
        simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, touched, not_exists,
          not_and] at hu
        obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := wild_kn_exists_missing_color_of_odd hn hodd c u
        obtain ⟨w, hwu, -⟩ := third u u
        obtain ⟨p⟩ := (hW.2 e).preconnected u w
        cases p with
        | nil => exact hwu rfl
        | cons h _ =>
          have h' : (G' W (c e)).Adj u _ := h
          rw [hG'adj] at h'
          obtain ⟨-, ⟨hx, hc⟩ | hw⟩ := h'
          · exact he _ hx hc
          · exact hu _ hw (Sym2.mem_mk_left _ _)
      rw [this, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]

steps.claim: The sum of degrees in W equals 2|W|.
steps.explanation: By the handshaking lemma, summing vertex degrees in the subgraph W counts each edge in W twice.
steps.code:
-- degrees in W
    let d : Fin n → ℕ := fun v => (W.filter fun f => v ∈ f).card
    have hhand : ∑ v, d v = 2 * W.card := by
      simp only [d, Finset.card_filter]
      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
      rw [mul_comm, Finset.card_eq_sum_ones, Finset.sum_mul]
      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun f hf => ?_
      have hfE : f ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet := hW.1 (Finset.mem_coe.2 hf)
      induction f using Sym2.ind with
      | h a b =>
        have hab : a ≠ b := by simpa using hfE
        rw [← Finset.card_filter, one_mul]
        have : (Finset.univ.filter fun v => v ∈ s(a, b)) = {a, b} := by
          ext v; simp
        rw [this, Finset.card_pair hab]
    -- a leaf's edge is shared with no other leaf

steps.claim: Partitioning touched vertices into leaves and higher-degree vertices gives |L| + 2|Bg| ≤ 2|W|.
steps.explanation: Every touched vertex has degree 1 or degree at least 2 in W. Summing lower bounds on degrees over L and Bg gives the inequality.
steps.code:
let L : Finset (Fin n) := Finset.univ.filter fun v => d v = 1
    let Bg : Finset (Fin n) := Finset.univ.filter fun v => 2 ≤ d v
    have htouch : touched = L ∪ Bg := by
      ext v
      simp only [touched, L, Bg, d, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_union]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨f, hf, hvf⟩
        have : 1 ≤ (W.filter fun f => v ∈ f).card :=
          Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨f, Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨hf, hvf⟩⟩
        omega
      · intro h
        have : 0 < (W.filter fun f => v ∈ f).card := by omega
        obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := Finset.card_pos.1 this
        exact ⟨f, (Finset.mem_filter.1 hf).1, (Finset.mem_filter.1 hf).2⟩
    have hdisj : Disjoint L Bg := by
      rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
      intro v hv hv'
      simp only [L, Bg, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hv hv'
      omega
    have hdeg : L.card + 2 * Bg.card ≤ ∑ v, d v := by
      calc L.card + 2 * Bg.card = ∑ v ∈ L, 1 + ∑ v ∈ Bg, 2 := by simp [mul_comm]
        _ ≤ ∑ v ∈ L, d v + ∑ v ∈ Bg, d v := by
          gcongr with v hv v hv
          · simp only [L, Finset.mem_filter] at hv; omega
          · simp only [Bg, Finset.mem_filter] at hv; omega
        _ = ∑ v ∈ L ∪ Bg, d v := (Finset.sum_union hdisj).symm
        _ ≤ ∑ v, d v := Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset (Finset.subset_univ _)

steps.claim: Leaves in W do not share an edge, so |L| ≤ |W|.
steps.explanation: If two leaves shared an edge in W, that edge would be their only incident edge in W, making them a closed pair in the subgraph of that edge's colour, which is impossible. Hence the map from leaves to their unique incident edges in W is injective.
steps.code:
have hleaf : ∀ v ∈ L, ∃ f, W.filter (fun f => v ∈ f) = {f} := by
      intro v hv
      simp only [L, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, d] at hv
      exact Finset.card_eq_one.1 hv
    haveI : Nonempty (Sym2 (Fin n)) := ⟨s(⟨0, by omega⟩, ⟨0, by omega⟩)⟩
    choose! ef hef using hleaf
    have hLW : L.card ≤ W.card := by
      refine Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn ef (fun v hv => ?_) (fun u hu v hv huv => ?_)
      · have := (Finset.mem_filter.1 ((hef v hv).symm ▸ Finset.mem_singleton_self (ef v))).1
        exact this
      · by_contra hne
        have hu' := (Finset.mem_filter.1 ((hef u hu).symm ▸ Finset.mem_singleton_self (ef u)))
        have hv' := (Finset.mem_filter.1 ((hef v hv).symm ▸ Finset.mem_singleton_self (ef v)))
        -- ef u = s(u, v)
        have huvf : ef u = s(u, v) := by
          have h1 : u ∈ ef u := hu'.2
          have h2 : v ∈ ef u := huv ▸ hv'.2
          have hE : ef u ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet := hW.1 (Finset.mem_coe.2 hu'.1)
          revert h1 h2 hE
          induction ef u using Sym2.ind with
          | h a b =>
            intro h1 h2 hE
            have hab : a ≠ b := by simpa using hE
            simp only [Sym2.mem_iff] at h1 h2
            rw [Sym2.eq_iff]
            rcases h1 with rfl | rfl <;> rcases h2 with rfl | rfl
            · exact absurd rfl hne
            · exact Or.inl ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
            · exact Or.inr ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
            · exact absurd rfl hne
        have only : ∀ w, w ∈ L → ∀ f ∈ W, w ∈ f → f = ef w := by
          intro w hw f hf hwf
          have : f ∈ W.filter (fun f => w ∈ f) := Finset.mem_filter.2 ⟨hf, hwf⟩
          rw [hef w hw] at this
          exact Finset.mem_singleton.1 this
        apply no_closed u v hne
        · intro x hx
          rw [hG'adj] at hx
          obtain ⟨hux, ⟨h, hc⟩ | hw⟩ := hx
          · exact wild_kn_same_color c h hne hc
          · have := only u hu _ hw (Sym2.mem_mk_left u x)
            rw [huvf, Sym2.eq_iff] at this
            rcases this with ⟨-, h⟩ | ⟨h1, -⟩
            · exact h
            · exact absurd h1 hne
        · intro x hx
          rw [hG'adj] at hx
          obtain ⟨hvx, ⟨h, hc⟩ | hw⟩ := hx
          · have hc' : c ⟨s(v, x), wild_kn_mem h⟩ = c ⟨s(v, u), wild_kn_mem (Ne.symm hne)⟩ := by
              rw [hc]; congr 2; exact Sym2.eq_swap
            exact wild_kn_same_color c h (Ne.symm hne) hc'
          · have := only v hv _ hw (Sym2.mem_mk_left v x)
            rw [← huv, huvf, Sym2.eq_iff] at this
            rcases this with ⟨h1, -⟩ | ⟨-, h⟩
            · exact absurd h1.symm hne
            · exact h
    have htc : touched.card = L.card + Bg.card := by

steps.claim: The inequalities imply |W| ≥ ⌊4⌈n/2⌉/3⌋.
steps.explanation: Combining |touched| = |L| + |Bg|, |L| + 2|Bg| ≤ 2|W|, and |L| ≤ |W| yields 2|touched| ≤ 3|W|. Using |touched| ≥ n - 1 (even n) or |touched| ≥ n (odd n) and integer division finishes the arithmetic.
steps.code:
rw [htouch, Finset.card_union_of_disjoint hdisj]
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one n with h0 | h1
    · omega
    · have := F1' h1
      omega
  -- the edge set of K_n is colour-connecting, so the infimum is over a nonempty set

steps.claim: The wild number is at least ⌊4⌈n/2⌉/3⌋.
steps.explanation: The complete graph itself is connected, so the full edge set is colour-connecting, ensuring the set of candidate sizes is nonempty. Since every colour-connecting set satisfies the lower bound, its infimum does as well.
steps.code:
have hne : (Finset.univ.filter fun f : Sym2 (Fin n) => f ∈ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet).card ∈
      {k | ∃ W : Finset (Sym2 (Fin n)), W.card = k ∧
        simple_graph_is_color_connecting (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) c ↑W} := by
    refine ⟨_, rfl, ?_, fun e => ?_⟩
    · intro f hf; simpa using hf
    · haveI : Nonempty (Fin n) := ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩⟩
      refine SimpleGraph.connected_top.mono ?_
      intro a b hab
      rw [SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj]
      refine ⟨Or.inr (by simpa using hab), hab⟩
  exact le_csInf ⟨_, hne⟩ fun j ⟨W, hj, hW⟩ => by rw [← hj]; exact hlow W hW

declarations.name: wild_number_complete_graph_le_sub_one
declarations.informal: For every n ≥ 1 and every edge colouring γ of K_n, wld_γ(K_n) ≤ n − 1 (a spanning star is colour-connecting).
declarations.statement:
theorem wild_number_complete_graph_le_sub_one {α : Type*} (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (γ : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet → α) :
    simple_graph_wild_number (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) γ ≤ n - 1
declarations.source:
theorem wild_number_complete_graph_le_sub_one {α : Type*} (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (γ : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet → α) :
    simple_graph_wild_number (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) γ ≤ n - 1 := by
  classical
  let z : Fin n := ⟨0, by omega⟩
  let W : Finset (Sym2 (Fin n)) := (Finset.univ.erase z).image fun j => s(z, j)
  have hW : simple_graph_is_color_connecting (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) γ ↑W := by
    refine ⟨?_, fun e => ?_⟩
    · intro f hf
      simp only [W, Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_erase] at hf
      obtain ⟨j, ⟨hj, -⟩, rfl⟩ := hf
      simpa using Ne.symm hj
    · rw [SimpleGraph.connected_iff_exists_forall_reachable]
      refine ⟨z, fun y => ?_⟩
      by_cases hy : y = z
      · rw [hy]
      apply SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable
      rw [SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj]
      refine ⟨Or.inr ?_, Ne.symm hy⟩
      simp only [W, Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_erase,
        Finset.mem_univ, and_true]
      exact ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
  refine (simple_graph_wild_number_le_of_is_color_connecting _ γ W hW).trans ?_
  refine Finset.card_image_le.trans ?_
  rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _), Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.22142 (Wild number for spanning trees in complete and complete bipartite graphs), Sec. 2, inequality (1) (0 ≤ wld_γ(G) ≤ n − 1 for an n-vertex connected graph), here for K_n.

explanation.summary: The proof shows that the wild number of any edge-coloured complete graph K_n (with n ≥ 1) is at most n - 1 by exhibiting an explicit color-connecting set of edges. It chooses an arbitrary vertex z and defines W to be the spanning star centered at z, consisting of the edges {z, j} for all j ≠ z. Because every vertex is directly adjacent to z along an edge in W, the graph containing W (plus any monochromatic edges) is connected, making W color-connecting. The bound follows because the star W contains at most n - 1 edges.

steps.claim: Define a candidate edge set W as the spanning star centered at vertex z = 0.
steps.explanation: Since n ≥ 1, the index 0 exists as a vertex z ∈ Fin n. We define W to be the set of unordered pairs {z, j} connecting z to all other vertices j ∈ Fin n with j ≠ z.

steps.claim: Every pair in W is an edge of the complete graph K_n.
steps.explanation: To show W ⊆ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet, take any f ∈ W. Unfolding the definition of W via Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe, and Finset.mem_erase, f has the form {z, j} for some j ≠ z. Since z ≠ j by Ne.symm, the pair {z, j} connects distinct vertices and is therefore an edge of the complete graph.
steps.code:
have hW : simple_graph_is_color_connecting (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) γ ↑W := by
    refine ⟨?_, fun e => ?_⟩
    · intro f hf
      simp only [W, Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_erase] at hf
      obtain ⟨j, ⟨hj, -⟩, rfl⟩ := hf
      simpa using Ne.symm hj

steps.claim: For every edge e, the subgraph containing all edges of color γ(e) together with W is connected, so W is color-connecting.
steps.explanation: By SimpleGraph.connected_iff_exists_forall_reachable, connectivity reduces to showing that z can reach every vertex y. If y = z, reachability is trivial. If y ≠ z, SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable shows reachability follows from adjacency. By SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj, adjacency holds because z ≠ y (from Ne.symm) and {z, y} belongs to the allowed edges: choosing the second disjunct via Or.inr, {z, y} ∈ W holds by definition of W (simplified via Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_erase, Finset.mem_univ, and and_true) because y ≠ z.
steps.code:
· rw [SimpleGraph.connected_iff_exists_forall_reachable]
      refine ⟨z, fun y => ?_⟩
      by_cases hy : y = z
      · rw [hy]
      apply SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable
      rw [SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj]
      refine ⟨Or.inr ?_, Ne.symm hy⟩
      simp only [W, Finset.coe_image, Set.mem_image, Finset.mem_coe, Finset.mem_erase,
        Finset.mem_univ, and_true]
      exact ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩

steps.claim: The wild number of K_n under γ is bounded by n - 1.
steps.explanation: By simple_graph_wild_number_le_of_is_color_connecting, the wild number is bounded above by |W|. Applying Finset.card_image_le bounds |W| by the size of (Finset.univ.erase z). Finally, removing z from Finset.univ leaves n - 1 elements by Finset.card_erase_of_mem, Finset.mem_univ, Finset.card_univ, and Fintype.card_fin.
steps.code:
refine (simple_graph_wild_number_le_of_is_color_connecting _ γ W hW).trans ?_
  refine Finset.card_image_le.trans ?_
  rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ _), Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]

glossary.and_true: For any proposition p, p ∧ True is equivalent to p.
glossary.Finset.card_erase_of_mem: Deleting an element from a finite set containing it decreases the cardinality of the set by 1.
glossary.Finset.card_image_le: The cardinality of the image of a finite set under any function is at most the cardinality of the original finite set.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset of a finite type equals the cardinality of the type.
glossary.Finset.coe_image: The set coercion of the image of a finite set under a function equals the image of its set coercion.
glossary.Finset.mem_coe: An element belongs to the set coercion of a finite set if and only if it belongs to the finite set.
glossary.Finset.mem_erase: An element a belongs to s \ {b} if and only if a ≠ b and a ∈ s.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to its universal finset.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The finite type Fin n has cardinality n.
glossary.Ne.symm: Inequality is symmetric: if a ≠ b, then b ≠ a.
glossary.Or.inr: From B, one can deduce A ∨ B.
glossary.Set.mem_image: An element y is in the image f '' s if and only if there exists x ∈ s such that f x = y.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Adj.reachable: Adjacent vertices in a graph are reachable from each other.
glossary.SimpleGraph.connected_iff_exists_forall_: A graph is connected if and only if there exists a vertex from which every vertex is reachable.
glossary.SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet_adj: Two vertices v and w are adjacent in the graph induced by edge set s if and only if {v, w} ∈ s and v ≠ w.
glossary.simple_graph_wild_number_le_of_is_color_: If a finite edge set W is color-connecting for (G, γ), then the wild number of (G, γ) is at most the cardinality of W.

declarations.name: wild_number_complete_three_min_proper_coloring_eq
declarations.informal: For every minimum proper edge colouring of K_3, the wild number is 2 = ⌊4⌈3/2⌉/3⌋: the case n = 3 of the conjecture in Sec. 6.
declarations.statement:
theorem wild_number_complete_three_min_proper_coloring_eq (k : ℕ)
    (hk : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).lineGraph.chromaticNumber = k)
    (c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).lineGraph.Coloring (Fin k)) :
    simple_graph_wild_number (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) c = 2
declarations.source:
theorem wild_number_complete_three_min_proper_coloring_eq (k : ℕ)
    (hk : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).lineGraph.chromaticNumber = k)
    (c : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).lineGraph.Coloring (Fin k)) :
    simple_graph_wild_number (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) c = 2 := by
  have h1 := wild_number_complete_graph_le_sub_one 3 (by norm_num) c
  have h2 := wild_number_complete_graph_min_proper_coloring_ge 3 k (le_refl 3) hk c
  norm_num at h1 h2
  omega
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.22142 (Wild number for spanning trees in complete and complete bipartite graphs), Theorem 3.5 (the exact values for 3 ≤ n ≤ 12), case n = 3; it is the case n = 3 of the Sec. 6 conjecture.

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by squeezing the wild number of K₃ under a minimum proper edge colouring between established general bounds. A general upper bound for complete graphs K_n shows that the wild number is at most n - 1 = 2 when n = 3. A general lower bound for minimum proper edge colourings of K_n shows that the wild number is at least ⌊4⌈n/2⌉/3⌋ = 2 when n = 3. Squeezing between these matching bounds forces the wild number to be exactly 2.

steps.claim: The wild number of K₃ under the colouring c is at most 3 - 1.
steps.explanation: Applying the general upper bound wild_number_complete_graph_le_sub_one to the complete graph on 3 vertices shows that the wild number under c is at most 3 - 1, discharging the hypothesis 1 ≤ 3 by simple arithmetic evaluation.
steps.code: have h1 := wild_number_complete_graph_le_sub_one 3 (by norm_num) c

steps.claim: The wild number of K₃ under c is at least 4 * ((3 + 1) / 2) / 3.
steps.explanation: Applying the general lower bound wild_number_complete_graph_min_proper_coloring_ge to n = 3 and colour count k establishes that any minimum proper edge colouring has wild number at least 4 * ((3 + 1) / 2) / 3. The precondition 3 ≤ 3 is supplied by reflexivity (le_refl), and the hypothesis that k is the chromatic index of K₃ comes from the theorem's assumptions.
steps.code: have h2 := wild_number_complete_graph_min_proper_coloring_ge 3 k (le_refl 3) hk c

steps.claim: The wild number of K₃ under c is equal to 2.
steps.explanation: Evaluating the integer arithmetic in both bounds simplifies the upper bound to ≤ 2 and the lower bound to ≥ 2. Since the wild number is sandwiched between 2 and 2, linear integer arithmetic (omega) closes the goal by concluding it equals 2.
steps.code:
norm_num at h1 h2
  omega

glossary.wild_number_complete_graph_le_sub_one: For any complete graph on n vertices (with n ≥ 1) and any edge colouring, the wild number is at most n - 1.
glossary.wild_number_complete_graph_min_proper_co: For any complete graph on n vertices (with n ≥ 3), if k is the chromatic index and c is a proper edge colouring using k colours, then the wild number is at least 4 * ((n + 1) / 2) / 3 in integer arithmetic (representing ⌊4⌈n/2⌉/3⌋).
glossary.le_refl: The less-than-or-equal relation is reflexive: for every element a, a ≤ a.

declarations.source:

/-- A `MatrixMap` is a linear map between squares matrices of size A to size B, over R. -/

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_matrix
declarations.informal: Choi matrix of a given linear matrix map. Note that this is defined even for things that aren't CPTP, it's just rarely talked about in those contexts. This is the inverse of `MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix`. Compare with `MatrixMap.toMatrix`, which gives the transfer matrix.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
variable {A B C D E F R : Type*} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] in
variable [Semiring R] in
def MatrixMap.choi_matrix (M : MatrixMap A B R) : Matrix (B × A) (B × A) R
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
variable {A B C D E F R : Type*} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] in
variable [Semiring R] in
/-- Choi matrix of a given linear matrix map. Note that this is defined even for things that aren't CPTP, it's just rarely talked about in those contexts. This is the inverse of `MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix`. Compare with `MatrixMap.toMatrix`, which gives the transfer matrix. -/
def MatrixMap.choi_matrix (M : MatrixMap A B R) : Matrix (B × A) (B × A) R :=
  fun (j₁,i₁) (j₂,i₂) ↦ M (Matrix.single i₁ i₂ 1) j₁ j₂

declarations.name: MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix
declarations.informal: Given the Choi matrix, generate the corresponding R-linear map between matrices as a MatrixMap. This is the inverse of `MatrixMap.choi_matrix`.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
variable {A B C D E F R : Type*} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] in
variable [Semiring R] in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
def MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix (M : Matrix (B × A) (B × A) R) : MatrixMap A B R
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
variable {A B C D E F R : Type*} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] in
variable [Semiring R] in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Given the Choi matrix, generate the corresponding R-linear map between matrices as a MatrixMap. This is the inverse of `MatrixMap.choi_matrix`. -/
def MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix (M : Matrix (B × A) (B × A) R) : MatrixMap A B R where
  toFun X := fun b₁ b₂ ↦ ∑ (a₁ : A), ∑ (a₂ : A), X a₁ a₂ * M (b₁, a₁) (b₂, a₂)
  map_add' x y := by funext b₁ b₂; simp [add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  map_smul' r x := by
    funext b₁ b₂
    simp only [Matrix.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, RingHom.id_apply, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]

declarations.name: MatrixMap.map_choi_inv
declarations.informal: Proves that `MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix` and `MatrixMap.choi_matrix` inverses.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open MatrixMap in

declarations.name: MatrixMap.choi_map_inv
declarations.informal: Proves that `MatrixMap.choi_matrix` and `MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix` inverses.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open MatrixMap in
variable {A B C D E F R : Type*} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] in
variable [Semiring R] in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
@[simp]
theorem MatrixMap.choi_map_inv (M : MatrixMap A B R) : of_choi_matrix (choi_matrix M) = M
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open MatrixMap in
variable {A B C D E F R : Type*} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] in
variable [Semiring R] in
set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Proves that `MatrixMap.choi_matrix` and `MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix` inverses. -/
@[simp]
theorem MatrixMap.choi_map_inv (M : MatrixMap A B R) : of_choi_matrix (choi_matrix M) = M := by
  -- By definition of `MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix`, we know that applying it to the Choi matrix of `M`
  -- reconstructs `M`.
  ext X b₁ b₂; simp [MatrixMap.of_choi_matrix, MatrixMap.choi_matrix];
  -- By linearity of $M$, we can distribute $M$ over the sum.
  have h_linear : M X = ∑ x : A, ∑ x_1 : A, X x x_1 • M (Matrix.single x x_1 1) := by
    have h_linear : M X = M (∑ x : A, ∑ x_1 : A, X x x_1 • Matrix.single x x_1 1) := by
      congr with i j ; simp ( config := { decide := Bool.true } ) [ Matrix.sum_apply ];
      simp ( config := { decide := Bool.true } ) [ Matrix.single ];
      rw [ Finset.sum_eq_single i ] <;> aesop;
    simp +decide only [h_linear, map_sum, LinearMap.map_smulₛₗ];
    simp +zetaDelta at *;
  -- By linearity of $M$, we can distribute $M$ over the sum and then apply it to each term.
  simp [h_linear, Matrix.sum_apply]

declarations.name: LinearEquiv.ofRelabel
declarations.informal: The `R`-linear equivalence `(d₂ → R) ≃ₗ[R] (d → R)` that relabels the coordinates of a function along an index equivalence `e : d ≃ d₂`. This is the linear-equivalence packaging of `Equiv.piCongrLeft`.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
variable {d d₁ d₂ d₃ R 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] in
variable {R : Type*} [Semiring R] in
variable (R) in
@[simps]
def LinearEquiv.ofRelabel (e : d ≃ d₂) : (d₂ → R) ≃ₗ[R] (d → R)
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
variable {d d₁ d₂ d₃ R 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] in
variable {R : Type*} [Semiring R] in
variable (R) in
/-- The `R`-linear equivalence `(d₂ → R) ≃ₗ[R] (d → R)` that relabels the coordinates of a function along an index equivalence `e : d ≃ d₂`. This is the linear-equivalence packaging of `Equiv.piCongrLeft`. -/
@[simps]
def LinearEquiv.ofRelabel (e : d ≃ d₂) : (d₂ → R) ≃ₗ[R] (d → R) := by
  refine' { e.symm.piCongrLeft (fun _ ↦ R) with .. }
  <;> (intros; ext; simp [Equiv.piCongrLeft_apply])

declarations.informal: The `𝕜`-linear equivalence `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 d₂ ≃ₗ[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 d` that relabels the coordinates of a vector along an index equivalence `e : d ≃ d₂`. This is the `EuclideanSpace` analogue of `LinearEquiv.ofRelabel`, obtained by transporting it across the `WithLp` identifications.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open LinearEquiv in
variable {d d₁ d₂ d₃ R 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] in
variable {R : Type*} [Semiring R] in
variable (e : d ≃ d₂) in
variable (𝕜) in
@[simps!]
def LinearEquiv.euclideanOfRelabel (e : d ≃ d₂) : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 d₂ ≃ₗ[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 d
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open LinearEquiv in
variable {d d₁ d₂ d₃ R 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] in
variable {R : Type*} [Semiring R] in
variable (e : d ≃ d₂) in
variable (𝕜) in
/-- The `𝕜`-linear equivalence `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 d₂ ≃ₗ[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 d` that relabels the coordinates of a vector along an index equivalence `e : d ≃ d₂`. This is the `EuclideanSpace` analogue of `LinearEquiv.ofRelabel`, obtained by transporting it across the `WithLp` identifications. -/
@[simps!]
def LinearEquiv.euclideanOfRelabel (e : d ≃ d₂) : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 d₂ ≃ₗ[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 d :=
  (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 𝕜 _).trans ((ofRelabel _ e).trans (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 𝕜 _).symm)

declarations.name: IsMaximalSelfAdjoint
declarations.informal: `IsMaximalSelfAdjoint R α` witnesses that `R` is the maximal `TrivialStar` subring of the star ring `α`, via an additive map `selfadjMap : α →+ R` collecting the self-adjoint part of each element. This lets `HermitianMat.trace` return `𝕜` when `𝕜` already has a trivial star, and the "clean" underlying type otherwise, e.g. `ℝ` when the input field is `ℂ`.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
class IsMaximalSelfAdjoint (R : outParam Type*) (α : Type*) [Star α] [Star R] [CommSemiring R]
    [Semiring α] [TrivialStar R] [Algebra R α]
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
/-- `IsMaximalSelfAdjoint R α` witnesses that `R` is the maximal `TrivialStar` subring of the star ring `α`, via an additive map `selfadjMap : α →+ R` collecting the self-adjoint part of each element. This lets `HermitianMat.trace` return `𝕜` when `𝕜` already has a trivial star, and the "clean" underlying type otherwise, e.g. `ℝ` when the input field is `ℂ`. -/
class IsMaximalSelfAdjoint (R : outParam Type*) (α : Type*) [Star α] [Star R] [CommSemiring R]
    [Semiring α] [TrivialStar R] [Algebra R α] where
  /-- The additive map sending an element of `α` to its self-adjoint part in `R`. -/
  selfadjMap : α →+ R
  /-- `selfadjMap` pulls scalar multiplication by `R` out of its argument. -/
  selfadj_smul : ∀ (r : R) (a : α), selfadjMap (r • a) = r * (selfadjMap a)
  /-- On self-adjoint elements, `selfadjMap` is a section of `algebraMap R α`. -/
  selfadj_algebra : ∀ {a : α}, IsSelfAdjoint a → algebraMap _ _ (selfadjMap a) = a

declarations.name: instTrivialStarIsMaximalSelfAdjoint
declarations.informal: Every `TrivialStar` `CommSemiring` is its own maximal self adjoints.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
instance instTrivialStarIsMaximalSelfAdjoint {R} [Star R] [TrivialStar R] [CommSemiring R] :
    IsMaximalSelfAdjoint R R
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
/-- Every `TrivialStar` `CommSemiring` is its own maximal self adjoints. -/
instance instTrivialStarIsMaximalSelfAdjoint {R} [Star R] [TrivialStar R] [CommSemiring R] :
    IsMaximalSelfAdjoint R R where
  selfadjMap := AddMonoidHom.id R
  selfadj_smul _ __ := rfl
  selfadj_algebra {_} _ := rfl

declarations.name: BoolBLR.fourier_coeff_le_of_far_from_linear
declarations.informal:
Fourier coefficient bound for functions far from linear. Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be $\varepsilon$-far from linear, meaning that $0 \le
\varepsilon \le 1$ and every linear function $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ (one satisfying
$g(x \oplus y) = g(x) \oplus g(y)$ for all $x,y$) has $\Pr_{x}[f(x) \ne g(x)] \ge
\varepsilon$ under the uniform distribution. Let $F(x) = (-1)^{f(x)}$ be the $\pm 1$
lift of $f$. Then for every subset $S \subseteq [n]$, the Fourier coefficient of $F$ at
$S$ satisfies
\[
  \hat F(S) \;=\; \E_{x}\bigl[F(x)\,\chi_S(x)\bigr] \;\le\; 1 - 2\varepsilon,
\]
where $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ is the Walsh character indexed by $S$.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Finset BoolFourier in
lemma BoolBLR.fourier_coeff_le_of_far_from_linear
    {n : ℕ}
    (f : hypercube n → Bool)
    (ε : ℝ)
    (hfar : epsilon_far_from_linear f ε) :
    ∀ S : Finset (Fin n),
      fourier_coeff (lift_pm1 f) S ≤ 1 - 2 * ε
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Finset BoolFourier in
/-- Bounds every Fourier coefficient of a function far from all linear functions. **Source:** [OD14, §1.6 (Fourier soundness proof)]. -/
lemma BoolBLR.fourier_coeff_le_of_far_from_linear
    {n : ℕ}
    (f : hypercube n → Bool)
    (ε : ℝ)
    (hfar : epsilon_far_from_linear f ε) :
    ∀ S : Finset (Fin n),
      fourier_coeff (lift_pm1 f) S ≤ 1 - 2 * ε := by
  intro S
  -- Build a linear g whose ±1 lift equals χ_S, witnessing closeness to χ_S.
  obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ : ∃ g : hypercube n → Bool, is_linear_bool g ∧ (lift_pm1 g) = (char_S S) := by
    -- First, exhibit g as parity over coordinates in S.
    obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ : ∃ g : hypercube n → Bool, lift_pm1 g = char_S S := by
      use fun x => (S.filter (fun i => x i)).card % 2 = 1;
      funext x; simp only [lift_pm1, char_S];
      -- Induction on S to compare parity-of-count vs product of (-1)^{x_i}.
      induction S using Finset.induction with
      | empty => simp [BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign]
      | insert a s ha ih =>
        simp only [BooleanAnalysis.chiS] at ih ⊢
        rw [Finset.prod_insert ha, ← ih, Finset.filter_insert]
        by_cases hx : x a = true
        · rw [if_pos hx, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem (fun h => ha (Finset.mem_filter.mp h).1)]
          rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one (s.filter (fun i => x i = true)).card with h | h <;>
            simp [h, Nat.add_mod, hx, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign]
        · simp [hx, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign]
    -- Then use linear_bool_iff_character to conclude g is linear.
    exact ⟨ g, by exact linear_bool_iff_character g |>.2 ⟨ S, hg ⟩, hg ⟩;
  -- Apply the previous lemma using the ε-farness from this specific linear g.
  exact fourier_coeff_le_of_dist_ge f g S hg.2 ( hfar.2.2 g hg.1 )

-- if f is epsilon-far from all linear functions, then the sum of cubes term is ≤ 1 - 2 * ε

declarations.name: BoolBLR.BLR_soundness_via_fourier_aux_h_bound
declarations.informal:
Per-coefficient cube bound for functions far from linear. Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be $\varepsilon$-far from linear, meaning that $0 \le
\varepsilon \le 1$ and every linear function $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ (one satisfying
$g(x \oplus y) = g(x) \oplus g(y)$ for all $x,y$) has distance $\Pr_{x}[f(x) \ne g(x)]
\ge \varepsilon$ from $f$. Write $\hat F(S) = \E[F \cdot \chi_S]$ for the Fourier
coefficient of $F = (-1)^{f}$, the $\pm 1$ lift of $f$, at a subset $S \subseteq [n]$.
Then for every such $S$,
\[
  \hat F(S)^3 \;\le\; \hat F(S)^2\,(1 - 2\varepsilon).
\]
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Finset BoolFourier in
lemma BoolBLR.BLR_soundness_via_fourier_aux_h_bound {n : ℕ} (f : BoolFourier.hypercube n → Bool) (ε : ℝ) (hfar : epsilon_far_from_linear f ε) :
    ∀ (S : Finset (Fin n)),
  BoolFourier.fourier_coeff (lift_pm1 f) S ^ 3 ≤ BoolFourier.fourier_coeff (lift_pm1 f) S ^ 2 * (1 - 2 * ε)
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Finset BoolFourier in
lemma BoolBLR.BLR_soundness_via_fourier_aux_h_bound {n : ℕ} (f : BoolFourier.hypercube n → Bool) (ε : ℝ) (hfar : epsilon_far_from_linear f ε) :
    ∀ (S : Finset (Fin n)),
  BoolFourier.fourier_coeff (lift_pm1 f) S ^ 3 ≤ BoolFourier.fourier_coeff (lift_pm1 f) S ^ 2 * (1 - 2 * ε) :=
  by
  exact fun S => by nlinarith only [ show fourier_coeff ( lift_pm1 f ) S ≤ 1 - 2 * ε by exact fourier_coeff_le_of_far_from_linear f ε hfar S ] ;

declarations.name: BoolBLR.BLR_soundness_via_fourier
declarations.informal:
Sum of cubed Fourier coefficients bounds distance to linearity. Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function and let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$
with $0 \le \varepsilon \le 1$, and suppose $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from linear: for
every linear function $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ one has $\dist(f,g) \ge \varepsilon$.
Writing $F = (-1)^{f}$ for the $\pm 1$ lift of $f$ and $\hat F(S) = \langle F,
\chi_S\rangle$ for its Fourier coefficient at $S \subseteq [n]$, the sum of the cubed
coefficients over all subsets satisfies
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \hat F(S)^3 \;\le\; 1 - 2\varepsilon.
\]
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Finset BoolFourier in
lemma BoolBLR.BLR_soundness_via_fourier {n : ℕ}
    (f : hypercube n → Bool)
    (ε : ℝ)
    (hfar : epsilon_far_from_linear f ε) :
  ∑ S : Finset (Fin n), (fourier_coeff (lift_pm1 f) S) ^ 3
    ≤ 1 - 2 * ε
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Finset BoolFourier in
/-- Proves the Fourier-analytic upper bound on BLR acceptance for far functions. **Source:** [OD14, §1.6]. -/
lemma BoolBLR.BLR_soundness_via_fourier {n : ℕ}
    (f : hypercube n → Bool)
    (ε : ℝ)
    (hfar : epsilon_far_from_linear f ε) :
  ∑ S : Finset (Fin n), (fourier_coeff (lift_pm1 f) S) ^ 3
    ≤ 1 - 2 * ε := by
    -- Parseval for ±1-valued lift_pm1: each (lift_pm1 f)(x)^2 = 1, so ‖f‖_2^2 = 1.
    -- f̂(S)^3 = f̂(S)^2 · f̂(S) ≤ f̂(S)^2 · (1 - 2ε), since f̂(S)^2 ≥ 0 and f̂(S) ≤ 1 - 2ε.
    -- Sum the per-S bound and apply Parseval.
    convert Finset.sum_le_sum fun S _ => (BLR_soundness_via_fourier_aux_h_bound f ε hfar) S using 1 <;> first | rfl | (rw [ ← Finset.sum_mul _ _ _ ] ; simp_all only [one_mul, (BLR_soundness_via_fourier_aux_hparseval f)])

declarations.name: BoolBLR.BLR_soundness
declarations.informal:
Soundness of the BLR linearity test. Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ and let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 \le
\varepsilon \le 1$. Suppose $f$ is $\varepsilon$-far from linear, meaning that every
linear function $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ (one satisfying $g(x \oplus y) = g(x) \oplus
g(y)$ for all $x, y$) has distance $\Pr_{x}[f(x) \ne g(x)] \ge \varepsilon$ from $f$.
Then the BLR acceptance probability of $f$ satisfies
\[
\E_{x}\!\left[\E_{y}\!\left[\mathbf{1}\!\left[(-1)^{f(x \oplus y)} =
(-1)^{f(x)}\,(-1)^{f(y)}\right]\right]\right] \;\le\; 1 - \varepsilon,
\]
where $x$ and $y$ range uniformly over $\{0,1\}^n$; equivalently, the test rejects $f$
with probability at least $\varepsilon$.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Finset BoolFourier in
lemma BoolBLR.BLR_soundness {n : ℕ}
    (f : hypercube n → Bool)
    (ε : ℝ)
    (hfar : epsilon_far_from_linear f ε) :
  BLR_accept_prob f ≤ 1 - ε
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Finset BoolFourier in
/-- Shows that a function `ε`-far from linearity is rejected by BLR with probability at least `ε`. **Source:** [OD14, §1.6]. -/
lemma BoolBLR.BLR_soundness {n : ℕ}
    (f : hypercube n → Bool)
    (ε : ℝ)
    (hfar : epsilon_far_from_linear f ε) :
  BLR_accept_prob f ≤ 1 - ε := by
  rw [BLR_accept_prob_pm1];
  -- Combine the cube-sum identity and the soundness bound; linarith finishes.
  linarith [ BLR_soundness_via_fourier f ε hfar, triple_expectation_eq_cube_fourier f ]
