lemma JensenOperatorInequality.star_mul_le_one [Nontrivial ℋ] (X : L ℋ) (hX : ‖X‖ ≤ 1) :
    (star X * X : L ℋ) ≤ 1 := by
  have h1 : star X * X ≤ algebraMap ℝ (L ℋ) (‖X‖ ^ 2) := by
    simpa [pow_two] using (CStarAlgebra.star_mul_le_algebraMap_norm_sq (a := X))
  have hsq : ‖X‖ ^ 2 ≤ 1 := by
    nlinarith [hX, norm_nonneg X]
  exact h1.trans (by simpa [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one] using hsq)

declarations.informal: JensenOperatorInequality.nontrivial_hsumL
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open JensenOperatorInequality in
universe u in
open LownerHeinzTheorem in
variable {ℋ : Type u} in
variable [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
omit [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
theorem JensenOperatorInequality.nontrivial_hsumL [Nontrivial ℋ] : Nontrivial (L (HSum ℋ))
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open JensenOperatorInequality in
universe u in
open LownerHeinzTheorem in
variable {ℋ : Type u} in
variable [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
omit [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
theorem JensenOperatorInequality.nontrivial_hsumL [Nontrivial ℋ] : Nontrivial (L (HSum ℋ)) := by
  have h_not_sub : ¬ Subsingleton ℋ := by
    intro hsub
    let : Subsingleton ℋ := hsub
    let : Subsingleton (L ℋ) := by infer_instance
    exact (not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton.mpr (by infer_instance))
      (inferInstance : Nontrivial (L ℋ))
  have hH_nontriv : Nontrivial ℋ := (not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial.mp h_not_sub)
  let : Nontrivial ℋ := hH_nontriv
  rcases exists_pair_ne ℋ with ⟨x, y, hxy⟩
  let w : ℋ := x - y
  have hw : w ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hxy
  have hdiag_ne_zero : (blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) (1 : L ℋ) 0 : L (HSum ℋ)) ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    have hz :
        blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) (1 : L ℋ) 0 (hsumIncl ℋ 0 w) = 0 := by
      exact congrArg (fun T : L (HSum ℋ) => T (hsumIncl ℋ 0 w)) h0
    have hw0 : w = 0 := by
      have hz0 := congrArg (fun z : HSum ℋ => hsumProj ℋ 0 z) hz
      simpa [blockDiagonal] using hz0
    exact hw hw0
  exact ⟨0, blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) (1 : L ℋ) 0, hdiag_ne_zero.symm⟩

    (u : unitary (L ℋ)) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :

set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
universe u in
open LownerHeinzTheorem in
variable {ℋ : Type u} in
variable [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
lemma JensenOperatorInequality.cfcR_conj_unitary_on (s : Set ℝ) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcont : ContinuousOn f s)
    {A : L ℋ} (hAs : spectrum ℝ A ⊆ s)
    (u : unitary (L ℋ)) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :
    cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f (star u * A * u) = star u * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f A * u := by
  let φ : L ℋ →⋆ₐ[ℝ] L ℋ := (Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℝ (L ℋ) (star u)).toStarAlgHom
  have hφ : Continuous φ := by
    have h1 : Continuous (fun x : L ℋ => (star u : L ℋ) * x * (u : L ℋ)) := by
      fun_prop
    have hEq : (fun x : L ℋ => φ x) = (fun x : L ℋ => (star u : L ℋ) * x * (u : L ℋ)) := by
      funext x
      simp [φ, Unitary.conjStarAlgAut_apply, mul_assoc]
    simpa [hEq] using h1
  have hφA : IsSelfAdjoint (φ A) := hA.map φ
  have hmap := StarAlgHom.map_cfc (φ := φ) (f := f) (a := A)
    (hf := hcont.mono hAs)
    (hφ := hφ) (ha := hA) (hφa := hφA)
  simpa [φ, cfcR, Unitary.conjStarAlgAut_apply, mul_assoc] using hmap.symm

      -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) * r) • T

set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
universe u in
open LownerHeinzTheorem in
variable {ℋ : Type u} in
variable [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
omit [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
lemma JensenOperatorInequality.complex_I_smul_real_I_smul_invTwo (r : ℝ) (T : L ℋ) :
    Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • T =
      -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) * r) • T := by
  ext x
  have hcomm : r • (Complex.I • ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • T x)) = Complex.I • (r • ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • T x)) := by
    simpa using (smul_comm r (Complex.I : ℂ) ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • T x))
  calc
    Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • T x
        = Complex.I • (r • (Complex.I • ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • T x))) := by
            rfl
    _ = Complex.I • (Complex.I • (r • ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • T x))) := by
            rw [hcomm]
    _ = ((Complex.I : ℂ) * Complex.I) • (r • ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • T x)) := by
            rw [smul_smul]
    _ = (-1 : ℂ) • (r • ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • T x)) := by
            norm_num
    _ = (-1 : ℂ) • (((r * 2⁻¹ : ℝ)) • T x) := by
            rw [smul_smul]
    _ = -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) * r) • T x := by
            simp [neg_smul, mul_comm]

    (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
        ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
          (-((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) +
            -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)))) =

set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open JensenOperatorInequality in
universe u in
open LownerHeinzTheorem in
variable {ℋ : Type u} in
variable [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
lemma JensenOperatorInequality.rightEval_topLeft_scalar
    (r : ℝ) (R0 X T : L ℋ) :
    (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
        ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
          (-((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) +
            -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)))) =
      star X * (T * X) + r • (R0 * R0) := by
  have hP :
      (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
          (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) =
        star X * (T * X) := by
    simpa using half_add_half_eq (ℋ := ℋ) (star X * (T * X))
  have hQhalf :
      -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) +
          -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) =
        r • (R0 * R0) := by
    have hterm :
        -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) =
          ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) * r) • (R0 * R0) := by
      calc
        -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0))
            = -(Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (R0 * R0)) := by
                rw [real_smul_complex_I_real_smul_complex_I_comm
                  (ℋ := ℋ) (s := (2⁻¹ : ℝ)) (r := r) (T := R0 * R0)]
        _ = ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) * r) • (R0 * R0) := by
            rw [complex_I_smul_real_I_smul_invTwo (ℋ := ℋ) (r := r) (T := R0 * R0)]
            simp
    calc
      -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) +
          -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) =
        ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) * r) • (R0 * R0) + ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) * r) • (R0 * R0) := by
          simp [hterm]
      _ = r • (R0 * R0) := half_mul_real_add_half_mul_real_eq (ℋ := ℋ) r (R0 * R0)
  calc
    (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
        ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
          (-((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) +
            -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0))))
        =
      ((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X)) +
          (2⁻¹ : ℝ) • (star X * (T * X))) +
        (-((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0)) +
          -((2⁻¹ : ℝ) • Complex.I • r • Complex.I • (R0 * R0))) := by
            abel
    _ = star X * (T * X) + r • (R0 * R0) := by rw [hP, hQhalf]

lemma GeneralizedPerspectiveFunction.spectrum_convexCombo_Ioi {A B : L ℋ} {t : ℝ}
    (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (hB : IsSelfAdjoint B) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1)
    (As : spectrum ℝ A ⊆ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)) (Bs : spectrum ℝ B ⊆ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)) :
    spectrum ℝ ((1 - t) • A + t • B) ⊆ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
universe u in
open LownerHeinzTheorem in
variable {ℋ : Type u} in
variable [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
variable [Nontrivial ℋ] in
lemma GeneralizedPerspectiveFunction.spectrum_convexCombo_Ioi {A B : L ℋ} {t : ℝ}
    (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) (hB : IsSelfAdjoint B) (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (ht1 : t ≤ 1)
    (As : spectrum ℝ A ⊆ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)) (Bs : spectrum ℝ B ⊆ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)) :
    spectrum ℝ ((1 - t) • A + t • B) ⊆ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) := by
  set C : L ℋ := (1 - t) • A + t • B
  have hC : IsSelfAdjoint C := by
    simpa [C] using (IsSelfAdjoint.all (1 - t)).smul hA |>.add ((IsSelfAdjoint.all t).smul hB)
  have hApos : ∃ r > 0, algebraMap ℝ (L ℋ) r ≤ A := by
    refine (CFC.exists_pos_algebraMap_le_iff (A := L ℋ) (a := A) (ha := hA)).2 ?_
    intro x hx
    exact As hx
  have hBpos : ∃ r > 0, algebraMap ℝ (L ℋ) r ≤ B := by
    refine (CFC.exists_pos_algebraMap_le_iff (A := L ℋ) (a := B) (ha := hB)).2 ?_
    intro x hx
    exact Bs hx
  rcases hApos with ⟨rA, hrA, hrA_le⟩
  rcases hBpos with ⟨rB, hrB, hrB_le⟩
  set rC : ℝ := (1 - t) * rA + t * rB
  have hrC : 0 < rC := by
    by_cases h1t : (1 - t) = 0
    · have ht' : t = 1 := by linarith
      subst ht'
      simpa [rC] using hrB
    · have h1t_pos : 0 < 1 - t := lt_of_le_of_ne (sub_nonneg.mpr ht1) (Ne.symm h1t)
      simpa [rC] using
        add_pos_of_pos_of_nonneg (mul_pos h1t_pos hrA) (mul_nonneg ht0 (le_of_lt hrB))
  have hrC_le : algebraMap ℝ (L ℋ) rC ≤ C := by
    have hsum :
        (1 - t) • algebraMap ℝ (L ℋ) rA + t • algebraMap ℝ (L ℋ) rB ≤ C := by
      simpa [C] using
        add_le_add (smul_le_smul_of_nonneg_left hrA_le (sub_nonneg.mpr ht1))
          (smul_le_smul_of_nonneg_left hrB_le ht0)
    have hLHS :
        (1 - t) • algebraMap ℝ (L ℋ) rA + t • algebraMap ℝ (L ℋ) rB =
          algebraMap ℝ (L ℋ) rC := by
      simp [rC, Algebra.smul_def]
    simpa [hLHS] using hsum
  intro x hx
  simpa [C] using
    (CFC.exists_pos_algebraMap_le_iff (A := L ℋ) (a := C) (ha := hC)).1 ⟨rC, hrC, hrC_le⟩ x hx

lemma GeneralizedPerspectiveFunction.conj_le_conj {X Y T : L ℋ} (hXY : X ≤ Y) (hT : IsSelfAdjoint T) :
    T * X * T ≤ T * Y * T := by
  have hnonneg : 0 ≤ Y - X := sub_nonneg.mpr hXY
  have hconj : 0 ≤ T * (Y - X) * T := by
    simpa using hT.conjugate_nonneg hnonneg
  have hsub : T * (Y - X) * T = T * Y * T - T * X * T := by
    simp [sub_eq_add_neg, mul_add, add_mul, mul_assoc]
  exact sub_nonneg.mp (by simpa [hsub] using hconj)

set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open GeneralizedPerspectiveFunction in
universe u in
open LownerHeinzTheorem in
open JensenOperatorInequality in
variable {ℋ : Type u} in
variable [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
variable [Nontrivial ℋ] in
set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
-- The generalized-perspective normalization expands several nested CFC products.
theorem GeneralizedPerspectiveFunction.theorem_2_5_forward_jointlyConvexOn_psd_pd_of_condV
    {f h : ℝ → ℝ}
    (hcoreV : CondV (ℋ := ℋ) f)
    (hconc : OperatorConcaveOn (ℋ := ℋ) (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)) h)
    (hcont : ContinuousOn h (Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)))
    (hpos : ∀ x ∈ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), 0 < h x) :
    JointlyConvexOn (psdSet (ℋ := ℋ)) (pdSet (ℋ := ℋ)) (fun A B ↦ (f Δ h) A B) := by
  intro A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ θ hA₁ hA₂ hB₁ hB₂ hθ0 hθ1
  rcases hA₁ with ⟨hA₁_sa, hA₁_spec⟩
  rcases hA₂ with ⟨hA₂_sa, hA₂_spec⟩
  rcases hB₁ with ⟨hB₁_sa, hB₁_spec⟩
  rcases hB₂ with ⟨hB₂_sa, hB₂_spec⟩
  let A : L ℋ := (1 - θ) • A₁ + θ • A₂
  let B : L ℋ := (1 - θ) • B₁ + θ • B₂
  have hA₁_nonneg : (0 : L ℋ) ≤ A₁ := by
    refine (StarOrderedRing.nonneg_iff_spectrum_nonneg (R := ℝ) A₁ (ha := hA₁_sa)).2 ?_
    intro x hx
    simpa [Set.Ici] using hA₁_spec hx
  have hA₂_nonneg : (0 : L ℋ) ≤ A₂ := by
    refine (StarOrderedRing.nonneg_iff_spectrum_nonneg (R := ℝ) A₂ (ha := hA₂_sa)).2 ?_
    intro x hx
    simpa [Set.Ici] using hA₂_spec hx
  have hB_sa : IsSelfAdjoint B := by
    dsimp [B]
    simpa using (IsSelfAdjoint.all (1 - θ)).smul hB₁_sa |>.add ((IsSelfAdjoint.all θ).smul hB₂_sa)
  have hB_spec : spectrum ℝ B ⊆ Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) :=
    spectrum_convexCombo_Ioi (ℋ := ℋ) hB₁_sa hB₂_sa hθ0 hθ1 hB₁_spec hB₂_spec
  have hB_conc :
      (1 - θ) • cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁ + θ • cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂ ≤ cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B := by
    have hconc' := hconc
    dsimp [OperatorConcaveOn, OperatorConvexOn] at hconc'
    have hneg :
        cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) (fun x : ℝ ↦ -h x) B ≤
          (1 - θ) • cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) (fun x : ℝ ↦ -h x) B₁ +
            θ • cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) (fun x : ℝ ↦ -h x) B₂ := by
      simpa [B] using
        hconc' (A := B₁) (B := B₂) (t := θ) hB₁_sa hB₂_sa hθ0 hθ1 hB₁_spec hB₂_spec
    simpa [cfcR, cfc_neg, smul_neg, neg_add, add_comm, add_left_comm, add_assoc] using
      neg_le_neg hneg
  let S : L ℋ := hSqrt (ℋ := ℋ) h B
  let IR : L ℋ := hInvSqrt (ℋ := ℋ) h B
  let S₁ : L ℋ := hSqrt (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁
  let S₂ : L ℋ := hSqrt (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂
  let IR₁ : L ℋ := hInvSqrt (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁
  let IR₂ : L ℋ := hInvSqrt (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂
  let T₁ : L ℋ := Real.sqrt (1 - θ) • (S₁ * IR)
  let T₂ : L ℋ := Real.sqrt θ • (S₂ * IR)
  let M₁ : L ℋ := IR₁ * A₁ * IR₁
  let M₂ : L ℋ := IR₂ * A₂ * IR₂
  have hS_sa : IsSelfAdjoint S := hSqrt_selfAdjoint (ℋ := ℋ) h B
  have hIR_sa : IsSelfAdjoint IR := hInvSqrt_selfAdjoint (ℋ := ℋ) h B
  have hS₁_sa : IsSelfAdjoint S₁ := hSqrt_selfAdjoint (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁
  have hS₂_sa : IsSelfAdjoint S₂ := hSqrt_selfAdjoint (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂
  have hIR₁_sa : IsSelfAdjoint IR₁ := hInvSqrt_selfAdjoint (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁
  have hIR₂_sa : IsSelfAdjoint IR₂ := hInvSqrt_selfAdjoint (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂
  have hSIR : S * IR = (1 : L ℋ) :=
    hSqrt_mul_hInvSqrt_eq_one (ℋ := ℋ) hB_sa hB_spec hcont hpos
  have hIRS : IR * S = (1 : L ℋ) :=
    hInvSqrt_mul_hSqrt_eq_one (ℋ := ℋ) hB_sa hB_spec hcont hpos
  have hS₁IR₁ : S₁ * IR₁ = (1 : L ℋ) :=
    hSqrt_mul_hInvSqrt_eq_one (ℋ := ℋ) hB₁_sa hB₁_spec hcont hpos
  have hIR₁S₁ : IR₁ * S₁ = (1 : L ℋ) :=
    hInvSqrt_mul_hSqrt_eq_one (ℋ := ℋ) hB₁_sa hB₁_spec hcont hpos
  have hS₂IR₂ : S₂ * IR₂ = (1 : L ℋ) :=
    hSqrt_mul_hInvSqrt_eq_one (ℋ := ℋ) hB₂_sa hB₂_spec hcont hpos
  have hIR₂S₂ : IR₂ * S₂ = (1 : L ℋ) :=
    hInvSqrt_mul_hSqrt_eq_one (ℋ := ℋ) hB₂_sa hB₂_spec hcont hpos
  have hM₁_nonneg : (0 : L ℋ) ≤ M₁ := by
    dsimp [M₁]
    simpa [mul_assoc] using hIR₁_sa.conjugate_nonneg hA₁_nonneg
  have hM₂_nonneg : (0 : L ℋ) ≤ M₂ := by
    dsimp [M₂]
    simpa [mul_assoc] using hIR₂_sa.conjugate_nonneg hA₂_nonneg
  have hM₁_sa : IsSelfAdjoint M₁ := IsSelfAdjoint.of_nonneg hM₁_nonneg
  have hM₂_sa : IsSelfAdjoint M₂ := IsSelfAdjoint.of_nonneg hM₂_nonneg
  have hM₁_spec : spectrum ℝ M₁ ⊆ Set.Ici (0 : ℝ) := by
    intro x hx
    simpa [Set.Ici] using spectrum_nonneg_of_nonneg hM₁_nonneg hx
  have hM₂_spec : spectrum ℝ M₂ ⊆ Set.Ici (0 : ℝ) := by
    intro x hx
    simpa [Set.Ici] using spectrum_nonneg_of_nonneg hM₂_nonneg hx
  have hT₁ :
      star T₁ * T₁ = (1 - θ) • (IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁ * IR) := by
    calc
      star T₁ * T₁
          = (Real.sqrt (1 - θ) * Real.sqrt (1 - θ)) • (IR * (S₁ * S₁) * IR) := by
              simp [T₁, hS₁_sa.star_eq, hIR_sa.star_eq, mul_assoc, smul_smul]
      _ = (1 - θ) • (IR * (S₁ * S₁) * IR) := by
              rw [Real.mul_self_sqrt (sub_nonneg.mpr hθ1)]
      _ = (1 - θ) • (IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁ * IR) := by
              rw [hSqrt_mul_hSqrt_eq (ℋ := ℋ) (B := B₁) hB₁_spec hcont hpos]
  have hT₂ :
      star T₂ * T₂ = θ • (IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂ * IR) := by
    calc
      star T₂ * T₂
          = (Real.sqrt θ * Real.sqrt θ) • (IR * (S₂ * S₂) * IR) := by
              simp [T₂, hS₂_sa.star_eq, hIR_sa.star_eq, mul_assoc, smul_smul]
      _ = θ • (IR * (S₂ * S₂) * IR) := by
              rw [Real.mul_self_sqrt hθ0]
      _ = θ • (IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂ * IR) := by
              rw [hSqrt_mul_hSqrt_eq (ℋ := ℋ) (B := B₂) hB₂_spec hcont hpos]
  have hTsum : star T₁ * T₁ + star T₂ * T₂ ≤ (1 : L ℋ) := by
    rw [hT₁, hT₂]
    have hmid :
        (1 - θ) • (IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁ * IR) + θ • (IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂ * IR)
          ≤ IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B * IR := by
      calc
        (1 - θ) • (IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁ * IR) + θ • (IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂ * IR)
            = IR * ((1 - θ) • cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₁ + θ • cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B₂) * IR := by
                simp [mul_add, add_mul, mul_assoc]
        _ ≤ IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B * IR := conj_le_conj (ℋ := ℋ) hB_conc hIR_sa
    have hunit : IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B * IR = (1 : L ℋ) := by
      calc
        IR * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) h B * IR = IR * (S * S) * IR := by
          rw [hSqrt_mul_hSqrt_eq (ℋ := ℋ) (B := B) hB_spec hcont hpos]
        _ = (IR * S) * (S * IR) := by simp [mul_assoc]
        _ = 1 := by simp [hIRS, hSIR]
    exact hmid.trans_eq hunit
  have hterm₁ :
      star T₁ * M₁ * T₁ = (1 - θ) • (IR * A₁ * IR) := by
    calc
      star T₁ * M₁ * T₁
          = (Real.sqrt (1 - θ) * Real.sqrt (1 - θ)) •
              (IR * (S₁ * (IR₁ * A₁ * IR₁) * S₁) * IR) := by
                simp [T₁, M₁, hS₁_sa.star_eq, hIR_sa.star_eq, mul_assoc, smul_smul]
      _ = (1 - θ) • (IR * (S₁ * (IR₁ * A₁ * IR₁) * S₁) * IR) := by
            rw [Real.mul_self_sqrt (sub_nonneg.mpr hθ1)]
      _ = (1 - θ) • (IR * A₁ * IR) := by
            rw [show IR * (S₁ * (IR₁ * A₁ * IR₁) * S₁) * IR =
                IR * (((S₁ * IR₁) * A₁) * (IR₁ * S₁)) * IR by simp [mul_assoc]]
            rw [hS₁IR₁, hIR₁S₁]
            simp [mul_assoc]
  have hterm₂ :
      star T₂ * M₂ * T₂ = θ • (IR * A₂ * IR) := by
    calc
      star T₂ * M₂ * T₂
          = (Real.sqrt θ * Real.sqrt θ) •
              (IR * (S₂ * (IR₂ * A₂ * IR₂) * S₂) * IR) := by
                simp [T₂, M₂, hS₂_sa.star_eq, hIR_sa.star_eq, mul_assoc, smul_smul]
      _ = θ • (IR * (S₂ * (IR₂ * A₂ * IR₂) * S₂) * IR) := by
            rw [Real.mul_self_sqrt hθ0]
      _ = θ • (IR * A₂ * IR) := by
            rw [show IR * (S₂ * (IR₂ * A₂ * IR₂) * S₂) * IR =
                IR * (((S₂ * IR₂) * A₂) * (IR₂ * S₂)) * IR by simp [mul_assoc]]
            rw [hS₂IR₂, hIR₂S₂]
            simp [mul_assoc]
  have hleft_inner :
      star T₁ * M₁ * T₁ + star T₂ * M₂ * T₂ = IR * A * IR := by
    rw [hterm₁, hterm₂]
    simp [A, mul_add, add_mul, mul_assoc]
  have hcore :=
    hcoreV (A := M₁) (B := M₂) (X := T₁) (Y := T₂) hM₁_sa hM₂_sa hM₁_spec hM₂_spec hTsum
  have houter := conj_le_conj (ℋ := ℋ) hcore hS_sa
  rw [hleft_inner] at houter
  have hright₁ :
      S * (star T₁ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₁ * T₁) * S =
        (1 - θ) • ((f Δ h) A₁ B₁) := by
    calc
      S * (star T₁ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₁ * T₁) * S
          = (Real.sqrt (1 - θ) * Real.sqrt (1 - θ)) •
              (S * IR * (S₁ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₁ * S₁) * IR * S) := by
                simp [T₁, hS₁_sa.star_eq, hIR_sa.star_eq, mul_assoc, smul_smul]
      _ = (1 - θ) • (S * IR * (S₁ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₁ * S₁) * IR * S) := by
            rw [Real.mul_self_sqrt (sub_nonneg.mpr hθ1)]
      _ = (1 - θ) • (S₁ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₁ * S₁) := by
            simp [mul_assoc, hSIR, hIRS]
      _ = (1 - θ) • ((f Δ h) A₁ B₁) := by
            rfl
  have hright₂ :
      S * (star T₂ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₂ * T₂) * S =
        θ • ((f Δ h) A₂ B₂) := by
    calc
      S * (star T₂ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₂ * T₂) * S
          = (Real.sqrt θ * Real.sqrt θ) •
              (S * IR * (S₂ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₂ * S₂) * IR * S) := by
                simp [T₂, hS₂_sa.star_eq, hIR_sa.star_eq, mul_assoc, smul_smul]
      _ = θ • (S * IR * (S₂ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₂ * S₂) * IR * S) := by
            rw [Real.mul_self_sqrt hθ0]
      _ = θ • (S₂ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₂ * S₂) := by
            simp [mul_assoc, hSIR, hIRS]
      _ = θ • ((f Δ h) A₂ B₂) := by
            rfl
  have hright :
      S * (star T₁ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₁ * T₁ + star T₂ * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f M₂ * T₂) * S =
        (1 - θ) • ((f Δ h) A₁ B₁) + θ • ((f Δ h) A₂ B₂) := by
    rw [mul_add, add_mul, hright₁, hright₂]
  have hleft :
      S * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f (IR * A * IR) * S = (f Δ h) A B := by
    rfl
  simpa [hleft, hright] using houter

open scoped Matrix in
variable {d d₂ d₃ R : Type*} in

theorem Equiv.Perm.permMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup (e : Perm d) :
    e.permMatrix R ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup d R
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open scoped Matrix in
variable {d d₂ d₃ R : Type*} in
variable [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] [Fintype d₂] [DecidableEq d₂] [Fintype d₃] [DecidableEq d₃] in
variable [CommRing R] [StarRing R] in
variable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] {A B : Matrix d d 𝕜} in
theorem Equiv.Perm.permMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup (e : Perm d) :
    e.permMatrix R ∈ Matrix.unitaryGroup d R := by
  -- Since $e$ is a permutation, its permutation matrix $P_e$ is orthogonal, meaning $P_e * P_e^T = I$.
  have h_perm_ortho : (Equiv.Perm.permMatrix R e) * (Equiv.Perm.permMatrix R e)ᵀ = 1 := by
    ext i j; rw [Matrix.mul_apply] ; aesop;
  constructor
  · simp_all only [Matrix.transpose_permMatrix]
    -- Since the conjugate transpose of a permutation matrix is the permutation matrix of the inverse permutation, we have:
    have h_conj_transpose : star (Equiv.Perm.permMatrix R e) = (Equiv.Perm.permMatrix R e)ᵀ := by
      ext i j; simp [Equiv.Perm.permMatrix] ; aesop;
    simp_all [mul_eq_one_comm]
  · simp_all only [Matrix.transpose_permMatrix]
    convert! h_perm_ortho using 2;
    simp [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose, Equiv.Perm.permMatrix]

    ‖Matrix.toEuclideanLin A x‖ = ‖x‖
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
variable {d d₁ d₂ d₃ m n : Type*} in
variable [Fintype d] [Fintype d₁] [Fintype d₂] [Fintype d₃] [Fintype m] [Fintype n] in
variable [DecidableEq d] [DecidableEq d₁] [DecidableEq d₂] [DecidableEq d₃] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] in
variable {dA dB dC dA₁ dA₂ : Type*} in
variable [Fintype dA] [Fintype dB] [Fintype dC] [Fintype dA₁] [Fintype dA₂] in
variable [DecidableEq dA] [DecidableEq dB] [DecidableEq dC] [DecidableEq dA₁] [DecidableEq dA₂] in
variable {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] in
variable {α : ℝ} in
open scoped InnerProductSpace RealInnerProductSpace Kronecker Matrix in
theorem Matrix.isometry_preserves_norm (A : Matrix n m 𝕜) (hA : A.Isometry) (x : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 m) :
    ‖Matrix.toEuclideanLin A x‖ = ‖x‖ := by
  rw [ ← sq_eq_sq₀ ( by positivity ) ( by positivity ), Matrix.Isometry ] at *;
  simp [ EuclideanSpace.norm_eq]
  have h_inner : ∀ x y : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 m, inner 𝕜 (toEuclideanLin A x) (toEuclideanLin A y) = inner 𝕜 x y := by
    intro x y
    have h_inner_eq : inner 𝕜 (toEuclideanLin A x) (toEuclideanLin A y) = inner 𝕜 x (toEuclideanLin A.conjTranspose (toEuclideanLin A y)) := by
      simp [ Matrix.toEuclideanLin, inner ];
      simp [ Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Finset.mul_sum, mul_comm, ];
      simp [ Matrix.mul_apply, mul_assoc, mul_comm, mul_left_comm, Finset.mul_sum]
      rw [Finset.sum_comm, Finset.sum_comm_cycle]
    simp_all [ Matrix.toEuclideanLin, toLpLin];
  convert congr_arg Real.sqrt ( congr_arg ( fun z => ‖z‖ ) ( h_inner x x ) ) using 1;
  · simp [ EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K ];
  · simp [ EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K ]

theorem isometry_mul_conjTranspose_le_one {m n : Type*} [Fintype m] [Fintype n]
    [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n]
    (V : Matrix m n ℂ) (hV : V.conjTranspose * V = 1) :
    V * V.conjTranspose ≤ 1 := by
  have h_pos : (1 - V * Vᴴ) * (1 - V * Vᴴ) = 1 - V * Vᴴ := by
    simp [ sub_mul, mul_sub, ← Matrix.mul_assoc ];
    simp [ Matrix.mul_assoc, hV ];
  have h_pos : (1 - V * Vᴴ) = (1 - V * Vᴴ)ᴴ * (1 - V * Vᴴ) := by
    simp_all [ Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_one, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul ];
  have h_pos : Matrix.PosSemidef (1 - V * Vᴴ) := by
    rw [ h_pos ] at *; apply Matrix.posSemidef_conjTranspose_mul_self;
  exact Matrix.le_iff.mpr h_pos

    (A.conjTranspose * B).conjTranspose * (A.conjTranspose * B) ≤ 1

theorem conjTranspose_isometry_mul_isometry_le_one {m n k : Type*}
    [Fintype m] [Fintype n] [Fintype k] [DecidableEq m] [DecidableEq n] [DecidableEq k]
    (A : Matrix k m ℂ) (B : Matrix k n ℂ)
    (hA : A.conjTranspose * A = 1) (hB : B.conjTranspose * B = 1) :
    (A.conjTranspose * B).conjTranspose * (A.conjTranspose * B) ≤ 1 := by
  have h_le : (Bᴴ * A) * (Bᴴ * A)ᴴ ≤ 1 := by
    have h_le : (Bᴴ * A) * (Bᴴ * A)ᴴ ≤ (Bᴴ * B) := by
      have h_le : (A * Aᴴ) ≤ 1 := by
        apply isometry_mul_conjTranspose_le_one A hA;
      -- Apply the fact that if $X \leq Y$, then $CXC^* \leq CYC^*$ for any matrix $C$.
      have h_conj : ∀ (C : Matrix n k ℂ) (X Y : Matrix k k ℂ), X ≤ Y → C * X * Cᴴ ≤ C * Y * Cᴴ :=
        fun C X Y a => Matrix.PosSemidef.mul_mul_conjTranspose_mono C a
      simpa [ Matrix.mul_assoc ] using h_conj Bᴴ ( A * Aᴴ ) 1 h_le;
    aesop;
  simpa [ Matrix.mul_assoc ] using h_le

    {A : Matrix d₁ d₁ 𝕜} {B : Matrix d₂ d₂ 𝕜} (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.PosDef) : (A ⊗ₖ B).PosDef
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Matrix in
open BigOperators in
variable {n 𝕜 : Type*} in
variable [RCLike 𝕜] [DecidableEq n] in
open scoped ComplexOrder MatrixOrder in
open ComplexOrder in
open Kronecker in
theorem Matrix.PosDef.kron {d₁ d₂ 𝕜 : Type*} [Fintype d₁] [DecidableEq d₁] [Fintype d₂] [DecidableEq d₂] [RCLike 𝕜]
    {A : Matrix d₁ d₁ 𝕜} {B : Matrix d₂ d₂ 𝕜} (hA : A.PosDef) (hB : B.PosDef) : (A ⊗ₖ B).PosDef := by
  rw [hA.left.spectral_theorem, hB.left.spectral_theorem]
  simp only [Unitary.conjStarAlgAut_apply]
  rw [mul_kronecker_mul, mul_kronecker_mul]
  rw [star_eq_conjTranspose, star_eq_conjTranspose]
  rw [← kroneckerMap_conjTranspose]
  rw [diagonal_kronecker_diagonal]
  apply mul_mul_conjTranspose_same
  · rw [posDef_diagonal_iff]
    rintro ⟨i₁, i₂⟩
    convert mul_pos (hA.eigenvalues_pos i₁) (hB.eigenvalues_pos i₂)
    rw [RCLike.pos_iff]
    simp
  · apply Matrix.vecMul_injective_of_isUnit
    rw [isUnit_iff_exists]
    use (star hA.left.eigenvectorUnitary.val) ⊗ₖ (star hB.left.eigenvectorUnitary.val)
    simp [← Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul]

declarations.source:

/-- The integrand of the complex Laplace transform of a possibly infinite-valued energy function. -/
noncomputable def ComplexLaplaceIntegrand {α : Type*} (E : α → WithTop ℝ) (z : ℂ) (x : α) : ℂ :=
  if h : E x = ⊤ then 0 else Complex.exp (-z * (E x).untop h : ℂ)

theorem norm_complexLaplaceIntegrand_le_envelope
    {α : Type*} {E : α → WithTop ℝ} {z w : ℂ} {δ : ℝ}
    (hw : w ∈ Metric.closedBall z δ) (x : α) :
    ‖ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E w x‖ ≤ ComplexLaplaceEnvelope E z δ x := by
  unfold ComplexLaplaceEnvelope ComplexLaplaceIntegrand
  by_cases h : E x = ⊤
  · simp [h]
  · simp only [h, dite_false]
    set e : ℝ := (E x).untop h
    have hdist : ‖w - z‖ ≤ δ := by
      simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall, dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_rev] using hw
    have hre_abs : |w.re - z.re| ≤ δ := by
      exact (Complex.abs_re_le_norm (w - z)).trans (by simpa [Complex.sub_re] using hdist)
    rw [Complex.norm_exp, Complex.norm_exp, Complex.norm_exp]
    rcases le_total 0 e with he | he
    · refine le_add_of_le_of_nonneg ?_ (Real.exp_pos _).le
      exact Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (by
        simp only [neg_mul, Complex.mul_re, Complex.neg_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im,
          mul_zero, sub_zero, Complex.sub_re]
        nlinarith [abs_le.mp hre_abs |>.1])
    · refine le_add_of_nonneg_of_le (Real.exp_pos _).le ?_
      exact Real.exp_le_exp.mpr (by
        simp only [neg_mul, Complex.mul_re, Complex.neg_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im,
          mul_zero, sub_zero, Complex.add_re]
        nlinarith [abs_le.mp hre_abs |>.2])

theorem measurable_complexLaplaceIntegrand
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] {E : α → WithTop ℝ} (hE : Measurable E) (z : ℂ) :
    Measurable (ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E z)
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
theorem measurable_complexLaplaceIntegrand
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] {E : α → WithTop ℝ} (hE : Measurable E) (z : ℂ) :
    Measurable (ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E z) := by
  rw [show ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E z =
      fun x => if E x = ⊤ then 0 else Complex.exp (-z * (((E x).untopD 0 : ℝ) : ℂ)) by
    funext x
    unfold ComplexLaplaceIntegrand
    by_cases hx : E x = ⊤
    · simp [hx]
    · simp only [hx, dite_false, ite_false]
      congr 2
      let y := E x
      have hy : y ≠ ⊤ := by simpa [y] using hx
      change ((y.untop hy : ℝ) : ℂ) = ((y.untopD 0 : ℝ) : ℂ)
      obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := WithTop.ne_top_iff_exists.mp hy
      have hUntop : y.untop hy = e := by
        apply WithTop.coe_inj.mp
        rw [WithTop.coe_untop, ← he]
      have hUntopD : y.untopD 0 = e := by
        rw [← he]
        rfl
      rw [hUntop, hUntopD]]
  exact Measurable.ite (hE (measurableSet_singleton (⊤ : WithTop ℝ))) measurable_const
    (Complex.continuous_exp.measurable.comp (by fun_prop :
      Measurable fun x => -z * (((E x).untopD 0 : ℝ) : ℂ)))

theorem continuousAt_complexLaplaceTransform_of_mem_interior_convergenceDomain
    {α : Type*} [MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace α] {E : α → WithTop ℝ} {z : ℂ}
    (hz : z ∈ interior (ComplexLaplaceConvergenceDomain E)) :
    ContinuousAt (ComplexLaplaceTransform E) z
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
theorem continuousAt_complexLaplaceTransform_of_mem_interior_convergenceDomain
    {α : Type*} [MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace α] {E : α → WithTop ℝ} {z : ℂ}
    (hz : z ∈ interior (ComplexLaplaceConvergenceDomain E)) :
    ContinuousAt (ComplexLaplaceTransform E) z := by
  rcases Metric.isOpen_iff.mp isOpen_interior z hz with ⟨ε, hε_pos, hε⟩
  have hint {w : ℂ} (hw : w ∈ Metric.ball z ε) :
      MeasureTheory.Integrable (μ := MeasureTheory.volume) (ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E w) :=
    _root_.interior_subset (s := ComplexLaplaceConvergenceDomain E) (hε hw)
  have hbound_int : MeasureTheory.Integrable (μ := MeasureTheory.volume)
      (ComplexLaplaceEnvelope E z (ε / 2)) := by
    unfold ComplexLaplaceEnvelope
    exact (hint (by
      rw [Metric.mem_ball, dist_eq_norm]
      simpa [abs_of_pos hε_pos] using show ε / 2 < ε by linarith)).norm.add (hint (by
        rw [Metric.mem_ball, dist_eq_norm]
        simpa [abs_of_pos hε_pos] using show ε / 2 < ε by linarith)).norm
  exact
    MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence
      (μ := MeasureTheory.volume) (l := nhds z)
      (F := fun w x => ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E w x)
      (f := fun x => ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E z x)
      (ComplexLaplaceEnvelope E z (ε / 2))
      ((eventually_integrable_complexLaplaceIntegrand_of_mem_interior_convergenceDomain (E := E) hz).mono
        fun _ hw => hw.aestronglyMeasurable)
      (Filter.Eventually.mono (Metric.ball_mem_nhds z (by positivity : 0 < ε / 2)) fun w hw =>
        Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => norm_complexLaplaceIntegrand_le_envelope
          (Metric.mem_closedBall.mpr (le_of_lt (Metric.mem_ball.mp hw))) x)
      hbound_int
      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => (analyticAt_complexLaplaceIntegrand E x z).continuousAt)

theorem integrable_uncurry_complexLaplaceIntegrand_horizontal
    {α : Type*} [MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace α]
    [MeasureTheory.SFinite (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure α)] {E : α → WithTop ℝ}
    {a b : ℂ}
    (hE : Measurable E)
    (ha : MeasureTheory.Integrable (μ := MeasureTheory.volume) (ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E a))
    (hb : MeasureTheory.Integrable (μ := MeasureTheory.volume)
      (ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E (b.re + a.im * Complex.I))) :
    MeasureTheory.Integrable
      (Function.uncurry fun t : ℝ => fun x : α =>
        ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E (t + a.im * Complex.I) x)
      ((MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a.re b.re)).prod MeasureTheory.volume) := by
  let μI := MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a.re b.re)
  have : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μI := ⟨by
    rw [MeasureTheory.Measure.restrict_apply_univ]
    simp [Set.uIoc]⟩
  have hsm : MeasureTheory.StronglyMeasurable (Function.uncurry fun t : ℝ => fun x : α =>
      ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E (t + a.im * Complex.I) x) := by
    refine MeasureTheory.stronglyMeasurable_uncurry_of_continuous_of_stronglyMeasurable ?_ ?_
    · intro x
      unfold ComplexLaplaceIntegrand
      split_ifs <;> fun_prop
    · intro t
      exact (measurable_complexLaplaceIntegrand hE (t + a.im * Complex.I)).stronglyMeasurable
  have henv : MeasureTheory.Integrable
      (fun p : ℝ × α => ComplexLaplaceEndpointEnvelope E a (b.re + a.im * Complex.I) p.2)
      (μI.prod MeasureTheory.volume) :=
    (ha.norm.add hb.norm).comp_snd μI
  refine henv.mono' hsm.aestronglyMeasurable ?_
  simp only [Function.uncurry]
  rw [MeasureTheory.Measure.ae_prod_iff_ae_ae (measurableSet_le
    (show Measurable fun p : ℝ × α =>
      ‖ComplexLaplaceIntegrand E (p.1 + a.im * Complex.I) p.2‖ from hsm.measurable.norm)
    (show Measurable fun p : ℝ × α =>
      ComplexLaplaceEndpointEnvelope E a (b.re + a.im * Complex.I) p.2 from
        ((measurable_complexLaplaceIntegrand hE a).norm.add
          (measurable_complexLaplaceIntegrand hE (b.re + a.im * Complex.I)).norm).comp measurable_snd))]
  filter_upwards [MeasureTheory.ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_uIoc] with t ht
  exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x =>
    norm_complexLaplaceIntegrand_horizontal_le_endpointEnvelope (Set.uIoc_subset_uIcc ht) x

    {α : Type*} [MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace α]

declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in

/-- A complex Laplace transform is analytic on the interior of its convergence domain. -/
theorem analyticAt_complexLaplaceTransform_of_mem_interior_convergenceDomain
    {α : Type*} [MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace α]
    [MeasureTheory.SFinite (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure α)] {E : α → WithTop ℝ} {z : ℂ}
    (hE : Measurable E)
    (hz : z ∈ interior (ComplexLaplaceConvergenceDomain E)) :
    AnalyticAt ℂ (ComplexLaplaceTransform E) z := by
  rcases Metric.isOpen_iff.mp isOpen_interior z hz with ⟨r, hr_pos, hr⟩
  have hcons : Complex.IsConservativeOn (ComplexLaplaceTransform E) (Metric.ball z r) := by
    intro a b hab
    rw [wedgeIntegral_complexLaplaceTransform_eq_integral hE (hab.trans hr),
      wedgeIntegral_complexLaplaceTransform_eq_integral hE (by
        simpa [Complex.Rectangle, Set.uIcc_comm] using hab.trans hr)]
    · rw [← MeasureTheory.integral_neg]
      apply MeasureTheory.integral_congr_ae
      filter_upwards with x
      exact (DifferentiableOn.isConservativeOn
        (fun y _hy => (analyticAt_complexLaplaceIntegrand E x y).differentiableAt.differentiableWithinAt))
        a b (Set.subset_univ _)
  exact ((Complex.isConservativeOn_and_continuousOn_iff_isDifferentiableOn Metric.isOpen_ball).1
    ⟨hcons, continuousOn_complexLaplaceTransform_interior_convergenceDomain.mono hr⟩).analyticAt
      (Metric.ball_mem_nhds z hr_pos)

declarations.name: ContinuousLinearMap.support_eq_sup_eigenspace_nonzero
declarations.informal: The support of a Hermitian matrix is the sum of its nonzero eigenspaces.
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open ContinuousLinearMap in
variable {n 𝕜 : Type*} [Fintype n] [RCLike 𝕜] in
theorem ContinuousLinearMap.support_eq_sup_eigenspace_nonzero (A : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n →L[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) : A.range = ⨆ μ ≠ 0, Module.End.eigenspace A μ
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open ContinuousLinearMap in
variable {n 𝕜 : Type*} [Fintype n] [RCLike 𝕜] in
/-- The support of a Hermitian matrix is the sum of its nonzero eigenspaces. -/
theorem ContinuousLinearMap.support_eq_sup_eigenspace_nonzero (A : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n →L[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n)
    (hA : A.IsSymmetric) : A.range = ⨆ μ ≠ 0, Module.End.eigenspace A μ := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · rintro x ⟨y, hy⟩
    have h_decomp : y ∈ ⨆ (μ : 𝕜), Module.End.eigenspace A.toLinearMap μ := by
      have h_orth := hA.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_eq_bot
      rw [Submodule.orthogonal_eq_bot_iff] at h_orth
      rw [h_orth]
      exact Submodule.mem_top;
    rw [Submodule.mem_iSup_iff_exists_finsupp] at h_decomp
    rcases h_decomp with ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩
    have h_apply_A : A y = ∑ i ∈ f.support, A (f i) := by
      rw [← hf₂, map_finsuppSum]
      exact rfl
    have h_eigen (i) : A (f i) = (i : 𝕜) • f i :=
      Module.End.mem_eigenspace_iff.mp (hf₁ i)
    rw [← hy, coe_coe, h_apply_A, Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ ↦ h_eigen i)]
    refine Submodule.sum_mem _ fun i _ ↦ ?_
    by_cases hi0 : i = 0
    · simp [hi0]
    · apply Submodule.smul_mem
      apply Submodule.mem_iSup_of_mem i
      exact Submodule.mem_iSup_of_mem hi0 (hf₁ i)
  · simp only [iSup_le_iff]
    intro μ hμ x hx
    use μ⁻¹ • x
    simp_all

open IsCompact in
variable {α β γ : Type*} {S : Set β} {f : γ → β → α} in
variable [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] in
variable [TopologicalSpace γ] in
variable [TopologicalSpace β] in
theorem IsCompact.sSup_image_eq_sSup_image_closure {f : β → α}
  (hS : IsCompact (closure S)) (hf : Continuous f) :
    sSup (f '' S) = sSup (f '' closure S)
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open IsCompact in
variable {α β γ : Type*} {S : Set β} {f : γ → β → α} in
variable [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] in
variable [TopologicalSpace γ] in
variable [TopologicalSpace β] in
theorem IsCompact.sSup_image_eq_sSup_image_closure {f : β → α}
  (hS : IsCompact (closure S)) (hf : Continuous f) :
    sSup (f '' S) = sSup (f '' closure S) := by
  rcases S.eq_empty_or_nonempty with rfl | h; · simp
  refine csSup_eq_of_forall_le_of_forall_lt_exists_gt (by simpa) ?_ ?_
  · rintro a ⟨w, hw, rfl⟩
    exact le_csSup (hS.image hf).bddAbove (Set.mem_image_of_mem f <| subset_closure hw)
  · intro w hw
    simp only [Set.mem_image, exists_exists_and_eq_and]
    contrapose! hw
    have h_image_closure : f '' closure S ⊆ closure (f '' S) :=
      image_closure_subset_closure_image hf
    have h_closure_image : closure (f '' S) ⊆ Set.Iic w :=
      closure_minimal (Set.image_subset_iff.mpr hw) isClosed_Iic
    exact csSup_le ((h.mono subset_closure).image f) fun y hy ↦
      (h_image_closure.trans h_closure_image) hy

declarations.name: Filter.Tendsto_inv_nat_mul_div_real
declarations.informal: Filter.Tendsto_inv_nat_mul_div_real
declarations.statement:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Topology in
theorem Filter.Tendsto_inv_nat_mul_div_real (m : ℕ)
   : Filter.Tendsto (fun (x : ℕ) => ((↑x)⁻¹ * ↑(x / m) : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 (1 / ↑m))
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Topology in
theorem Filter.Tendsto_inv_nat_mul_div_real (m : ℕ)
   : Filter.Tendsto (fun (x : ℕ) => ((↑x)⁻¹ * ↑(x / m) : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (𝓝 (1 / ↑m)) := by
  --Thanks aristotle!
  -- This simplifies to $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{\lfloor x / m \rfloor}{x} = \frac{1}{m}$ because the floor function grows asymptotically like $x / m$.
  have h_floor : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (Nat.floor (x / m : ℝ) : ℝ) / x) Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / (m : ℝ))) := by
    -- We'll use the fact that the floor function is bounded and apply the squeeze theorem.
    have h_floor_bound : ∀ x : ℕ, x > 0 → (Nat.floor (x / m : ℝ) : ℝ) / x ≥ (1 / m - 1 / x) ∧ (Nat.floor (x / m : ℝ) : ℝ) / x ≤ 1 / m := by
      cases eq_or_ne m 0
      · rename_i h
        intro x a
        subst h
        simp_all only [gt_iff_lt, CharP.cast_eq_zero, div_zero, Nat.floor_zero, zero_div, one_div, zero_sub, ge_iff_le,
          Left.neg_nonpos_iff, inv_nonneg, Nat.cast_nonneg, le_refl, and_self]
      · intro x a
        simp_all only [ne_eq, gt_iff_lt, one_div, ge_iff_le, tsub_le_iff_right]
        apply And.intro
        · rw [ inv_eq_one_div, div_add', div_le_div_iff₀ ] <;> first | positivity | nlinarith [ Nat.lt_floor_add_one ( ( x : ℝ ) / m ), show ( x : ℝ ) ≥ 1 by exact Nat.one_le_cast.mpr a, mul_div_cancel₀ ( x : ℝ ) ( show ( m : ℝ ) ≠ 0 by positivity ), inv_mul_cancel₀ ( show ( x : ℝ ) ≠ 0 by positivity ) ] ;
        · rw [ div_le_iff₀ ( by positivity ) ];
          simpa [ div_eq_inv_mul ] using Nat.floor_le ( by positivity : 0 ≤ ( x : ℝ ) / m );
    -- Apply the squeeze theorem to conclude the proof.
    have h_squeeze : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (1 / m : ℝ) - 1 / x) Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / m)) := by
      simpa using tendsto_const_nhds.sub (tendsto_inv_atTop_nhds_zero_nat (𝕜 := ℝ))
    exact tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le' h_squeeze tendsto_const_nhds ( Filter.eventually_atTop.mpr ⟨ 1, fun x hx => h_floor_bound x hx |>.1 ⟩ ) ( Filter.eventually_atTop.mpr ⟨ 1, fun x hx => h_floor_bound x hx |>.2 ⟩ );
  -- Apply the hypothesis `h_floor` to conclude the proof.
  convert h_floor using 1;
  -- By definition of floor function, we know that ⌊(x : ℝ) / m⌋₊ is the greatest integer less than or equal to (x : ℝ) / m.
  funext x; simp [Nat.floor_div_natCast];
  ring

open Topology in

theorem ENNReal.tendsto_toReal_iff_of_eventually_ne_top
  {ι} {fi : Filter ι} {f : ι → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ᶠ i in fi, f i ≠ ∞) {x : ℝ≥0∞}
    (hx : x ≠ ∞) : Tendsto (fun n => (f n).toReal) fi (𝓝 x.toReal) ↔ Tendsto f fi (𝓝 x)
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
open Topology in
open Filter Topology ENNReal in
theorem ENNReal.tendsto_toReal_iff_of_eventually_ne_top
  {ι} {fi : Filter ι} {f : ι → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : ∀ᶠ i in fi, f i ≠ ∞) {x : ℝ≥0∞}
    (hx : x ≠ ∞) : Tendsto (fun n => (f n).toReal) fi (𝓝 x.toReal) ↔ Tendsto f fi (𝓝 x) := by
  have he₁ : f =ᶠ[fi] (fun n ↦ (f n).toNNReal) := by
    rw [EventuallyEq]
    filter_upwards [hf] with i h
    simp [h]
  have he₂ : (fun n ↦ (f n).toReal) = (fun n ↦ ((f n).toNNReal : ℝ≥0∞).toReal) :=
    rfl
  rw [Filter.tendsto_congr' he₁, he₂]
  exact tendsto_toReal_iff (by finiteness) hx

lemma JensenOperatorInequality.cfcR_conj_unitary (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcont : ContinuousOn f Set.univ)
    (u : unitary (L ℋ)) (A : L ℋ) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :
    cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f (star u * A * u) = star u * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f A * u
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
universe u in
open LownerHeinzTheorem in
variable {ℋ : Type u} in
variable [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
lemma JensenOperatorInequality.cfcR_conj_unitary (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcont : ContinuousOn f Set.univ)
    (u : unitary (L ℋ)) (A : L ℋ) (hA : IsSelfAdjoint A) :
    cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f (star u * A * u) = star u * cfcR (ℋ := ℋ) f A * u := by
  let φ : L ℋ →⋆ₐ[ℝ] L ℋ := (Unitary.conjStarAlgAut ℝ (L ℋ) (star u)).toStarAlgHom
  have hφ : Continuous φ := by
    have h1 : Continuous (fun x : L ℋ => (star u : L ℋ) * x * (u : L ℋ)) := by
      fun_prop
    have hEq : (fun x : L ℋ => φ x) = (fun x : L ℋ => (star u : L ℋ) * x * (u : L ℋ)) := by
      funext x
      simp [φ, Unitary.conjStarAlgAut_apply, mul_assoc]
    simpa [hEq] using h1
  have hφA : IsSelfAdjoint (φ A) := hA.map φ
  have hmap := StarAlgHom.map_cfc (φ := φ) (f := f) (a := A)
    (hf := hcont.mono (by intro x hx; simp))
    (hφ := hφ) (ha := hA) (hφa := hφA)
  simpa [φ, cfcR, Unitary.conjStarAlgAut_apply, mul_assoc] using hmap.symm

declarations.informal: `L (HSum ℋ)` is nontrivial once `L ℋ` is.
declarations.statement:

theorem JensenOperatorInequalityScratch.nontrivial_hsumL : Nontrivial (L (HSum ℋ))
declarations.source:
set_option autoImplicit true in
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit true in
universe u in
open LownerHeinzTheorem in
open JensenOperatorInequality in
variable {ℋ : Type u} in
variable [NormedAddCommGroup ℋ] [InnerProductSpace ℂ ℋ] [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
variable [Nontrivial ℋ] in
omit [CompleteSpace ℋ] in
/-- `L (HSum ℋ)` is nontrivial once `L ℋ` is. -/
theorem JensenOperatorInequalityScratch.nontrivial_hsumL : Nontrivial (L (HSum ℋ)) := by
  have h_not_sub : ¬ Subsingleton ℋ := by
    intro hsub
    let _ : Subsingleton ℋ := hsub
    let _ : Subsingleton (L ℋ) := by infer_instance
    exact (not_nontrivial_iff_subsingleton.mpr (by infer_instance))
      (inferInstance : Nontrivial (L ℋ))
  have hH_nontriv : Nontrivial ℋ := (not_subsingleton_iff_nontrivial.mp h_not_sub)
  let _ : Nontrivial ℋ := hH_nontriv
  rcases exists_pair_ne ℋ with ⟨x, y, hxy⟩
  let w : ℋ := x - y
  have hw : w ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hxy
  have hdiag_ne_zero : (blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) (1 : L ℋ) 0 : L (HSum ℋ)) ≠ 0 := by
    intro h0
    have hz :
        blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) (1 : L ℋ) 0 (hsumIncl ℋ 0 w) = 0 := by
      simp [h0]
    have hw0 : w = 0 := by
      have hz0 := congrArg (fun z : HSum ℋ => hsumProj ℋ 0 z) hz
      simpa [blockDiagonal] using hz0
    exact hw hw0
  exact ⟨0, blockDiagonal (ℋ := ℋ) (1 : L ℋ) 0, hdiag_ne_zero.symm⟩

declarations.name: simple_graph_cycle_power
declarations.informal: The k-th power C_n^k of the cycle C_n: vertices are the residues mod n, and two distinct vertices are adjacent when their distance along the cycle, min((u - v) mod n, (v - u) mod n), is at most k.
declarations.statement: def simple_graph_cycle_power (n k : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (ZMod n)
declarations.source:
/-- The `k`-th power `C_n^k` of the `n`-cycle on `ZMod n`: distinct `u, v` are adjacent iff their cyclic distance `min ((u - v).val) ((v - u).val)` is at most `k`. -/
def simple_graph_cycle_power (n k : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (ZMod n) where
  Adj u v := u ≠ v ∧ min (u - v).val (v - u).val ≤ k
  symm := ⟨fun (u v : ZMod n) (h : u ≠ v ∧ min (u - v).val (v - u).val ≤ k) =>
    ⟨h.1.symm, by rw [min_comm]; exact h.2⟩⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun (u : ZMod n) (h : u ≠ u ∧ min (u - u).val (u - u).val ≤ k) => h.1 rfl⟩
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.15635 (Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs), Sec. 1 (definition of the k-th power of a cycle).

declarations.name: simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover
declarations.informal: G can be covered by t equivalence subgraphs: there are t spanning subgraphs of G, each a disjoint union of cliques (isolated vertices allowed), whose edge sets together cover E(G). Each one is given by a labelling c_s of the vertices whose classes are cliques of G; its edges are the pairs with equal labels.
declarations.statement: def simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- `G` is covered by `t` equivalence subgraphs. Subgraph `s` is the partition of `V` into the classes of the labelling `c s`; each class must be a clique of `G` (so the subgraph is a disjoint union of cliques of `G`), and every edge of `G` must join two vertices with the same label in some `c s`. Labels in `V` lose nothing: a partition of `V` has at most `|V|` classes. -/
def simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : Fin t → V → V,
    (∀ s u v, u ≠ v → c s u = c s v → G.Adj u v) ∧
    ∀ u v, G.Adj u v → ∃ s, c s u = c s v
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.15635 (Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs), Sec. 1 (equivalence subgraphs; the labelling c_s of components is the one used in the proofs of Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 3.4).

declarations.name: simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number
declarations.informal: The equivalence covering number eq(G): the minimum number of equivalence subgraphs of G whose edge sets cover E(G).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.15635 (Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs), Sec. 1 (definition of eq(G)).

declarations.name: simple_graph_cycle_power_six_one_sanity
declarations.informal: Sanity check: in C_6 (the first power of the 6-cycle), vertices 0 and 5 are adjacent (they wrap around) and 0 and 2 are not.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_cycle_power_six_one_sanity :
    (simple_graph_cycle_power 6 1).Adj 0 5 ∧ ¬ (simple_graph_cycle_power 6 1).Adj 0 2
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_cycle_power_six_one_sanity :
    (simple_graph_cycle_power 6 1).Adj 0 5 ∧ ¬ (simple_graph_cycle_power 6 1).Adj 0 2 := by
  show ((0 : ZMod 6) ≠ 5 ∧ _) ∧ ¬ ((0 : ZMod 6) ≠ 2 ∧ _)
  decide
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for the cycle power, arXiv:2610.15635 (Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs).

explanation.summary: The theorem verifies that in the cycle graph $C_6$ (modeled as the first power of the $6$-cycle on $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$), vertex $0$ is adjacent to $5$ but not to $2$. By definition, two vertices $u, v \in \mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$ are adjacent if $u \neq v$ and their cyclic distance $\min((u-v)\text{.val}, (v-u)\text{.val})$ is at most $1$. The proof unfolds this adjacency definition into explicit modular arithmetic inequalities and discharges them by finite computation.

steps.claim: The goal reduces to checking explicit cyclic distance inequalities in $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$ for the vertex pairs $(0, 5)$ and $(0, 2)$.
steps.explanation: By definition of `simple_graph_cycle_power`, two vertices $u, v \in \mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$ are adjacent if and only if $u \ne v$ and their cyclic distance $\min((u - v)\text{.val}, (v - u)\text{.val})$ is at most $1$. Stating this expanded form with `show` unfolds the adjacency predicate into concrete arithmetic inequalities on $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$.

steps.claim: Vertices $0$ and $5$ are adjacent, while $0$ and $2$ are not adjacent.
steps.explanation: The goal is closed by the `decide` tactic via finite evaluation in $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$. For $0$ and $5$, $(0 - 5)\text{.val} = 1$ and $(5 - 0)\text{.val} = 5$, so the cyclic distance is $\min(1, 5) = 1 \le 1$, meaning $0$ and $5$ are adjacent. For $0$ and $2$, $(0 - 2)\text{.val} = 4$ and $(2 - 0)\text{.val} = 2$, so the cyclic distance is $\min(4, 2) = 2 \not\le 1$, meaning $0$ and $2$ are not adjacent.
steps.code: decide

caveats: The `show` command on line 3 is a formal detail: it manually unfolds the definition of adjacency in `simple_graph_cycle_power` so that Lean's typeclass resolution can recognize the goal as a decidable proposition on `ZMod 6` and `ℕ`, which `decide` on line 4 can then compute.

declarations.name: simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover_mono
declarations.informal: If G is covered by s equivalence subgraphs, it is covered by any larger number t of them (pad with the edgeless equivalence subgraph).
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover_mono {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) {s t : ℕ}
    (hst : s ≤ t) (h : simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover G s) :
    simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover G t := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, hcov⟩ := h
  refine ⟨fun i => if hi : (i : ℕ) < s then c ⟨i, hi⟩ else id, fun i u v huv h => ?_,
    fun u v huv => ?_⟩
  · by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s
    · simp only [hi, dif_pos] at h; exact hc _ u v huv h
    · simp only [hi, dif_neg, not_false_eq_true, id] at h; exact absurd h huv
  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hcov u v huv
    exact ⟨⟨j, by omega⟩, by simp [j.2, hj]⟩
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for equivalence covers, arXiv:2610.15635 (Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs).

explanation.summary: To show that an equivalence cover of size s can be extended to size t whenever s ≤ t, we pad the family of s coloring functions with t - s copies of the identity function. The identity function corresponds to the discrete equivalence relation, which identifies no distinct vertices and thus trivially forms an edgeless subgraph of G. The original s functions already cover all edges of G, and since their indices are strictly less than s ≤ t, their edge coverage is preserved in the extended family.

steps.claim: Extract the given equivalence cover of size s.
steps.explanation: From the hypothesis that G has an equivalence cover of size s, we obtain a family of coloring functions c indexed by Fin s, the condition hc that any distinct vertices with the same color are adjacent in G, and the condition hcov that every edge in G is monochromatic under at least one coloring in the family.
steps.code: obtain ⟨c, hc, hcov⟩ := h

steps.claim: Extend the family to size t by padding with the identity function, reducing the goal to verifying the two cover conditions.
steps.explanation: We define a candidate cover of size t piecewise: for an index i < s, we reuse the original function c_i, while for i ≥ s, we use the identity function id on V. This reduces the goal to showing that each function in the extended family identifies only adjacent vertices, and that every edge of G is still covered.
steps.code:
refine ⟨fun i => if hi : (i : ℕ) < s then c ⟨i, hi⟩ else id, fun i u v huv h => ?_,
    fun u v huv => ?_⟩

steps.claim: Each function in the extended family satisfies the subgraph condition: distinct vertices with the same value are adjacent.
steps.explanation: For any index i in Fin t and distinct vertices u ≠ v with the same value under the i-th function, we split into cases on whether i < s. If i < s, the dependent conditional simplifies via dif_pos to c_i(u) = c_i(v), so u and v are adjacent by the soundness hc of the original cover. If i ≥ s, the conditional simplifies via dif_neg, not_false_eq_true, and id to u = v, which contradicts the hypothesis u ≠ v.
steps.code:
· by_cases hi : (i : ℕ) < s
    · simp only [hi, dif_pos] at h; exact hc _ u v huv h
    · simp only [hi, dif_neg, not_false_eq_true, id] at h; exact absurd h huv

steps.claim: Every edge of G is covered by some function in the extended family.
steps.explanation: Given an edge between u and v, the original covering property hcov yields an index j < s such that c_j(u) = c_j(v). Since s ≤ t, linear arithmetic (omega) shows j < t, so j embeds into Fin t. At this index, the condition j < s holds, so the extended function simplifies to c_j and identifies u and v.
steps.code:
· obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hcov u v huv
    exact ⟨⟨j, by omega⟩, by simp [j.2, hj]⟩

glossary.dif_pos: A dependent if-then-else expression evaluates to its then-branch when the condition is true.
glossary.dif_neg: A dependent if-then-else expression evaluates to its else-branch when the condition is false.
glossary.not_false_eq_true: The negation of False is True.
glossary.id: The identity function, sending every element to itself.

declarations.name: simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number_top
declarations.informal: Sanity check: a complete graph with at least two vertices has equivalence covering number 1.
declarations.statement:
theorem simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number_top {V : Type*} [Nontrivial V] :
    simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) = 1
declarations.source:
theorem simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number_top {V : Type*} [Nontrivial V] :
    simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) = 1 := by
  have h1 : simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) 1 := by
    obtain ⟨x⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty V)
    exact ⟨fun _ _ => x, fun _ _ _ huv _ => huv, fun _ _ _ => ⟨0, rfl⟩⟩
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact Nat.sInf_le h1
  · refine le_csInf ⟨1, h1⟩ fun t ht => ?_
    obtain ⟨c, -, hcov⟩ := ht
    obtain ⟨x, y, hxy⟩ := exists_pair_ne V
    obtain ⟨s, -⟩ := hcov x y hxy
    exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr fun h => by subst h; exact s.elim0
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for eq(G), arXiv:2610.15635 (Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs) (Theorem 1.2 uses eq(K_n) = 1).

explanation.summary: An equivalence cover of a simple graph is a family of equivalence relations whose equivalence classes are cliques, covering all edges of the graph, and the equivalence covering number is the minimum size of such a cover. For the complete graph on a nontrivial vertex set, a single equivalence relation with one equivalence class covers all pairs of vertices, showing the covering number is at most 1. Conversely, because the vertex set has at least two distinct vertices forming an edge, any valid cover must provide at least one index to cover that edge, showing the covering number is at least 1.

steps.claim: The complete graph $\\top$ has an equivalence cover of size $1$.
steps.explanation: Because $V$ is nontrivial, it is nonempty; let $x \\in V$ be any vertex. We define a single coloring function $c : \\operatorname{Fin} 1 \\to V \\to V$ that assigns the constant value $x$ to every vertex. Any two distinct vertices $u \\ne v$ are adjacent in $\\top$ by definition, so the condition that monochromatic pairs form cliques holds trivially. Furthermore, under the unique index $0$, any pair of vertices shares the same color $x$, so every edge is covered.
steps.code:
have h1 : simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) 1 := by
    obtain ⟨x⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty V)
    exact ⟨fun _ _ => x, fun _ _ _ huv _ => huv, fun _ _ _ => ⟨0, rfl⟩⟩

steps.claim: The covering number of $\\top$ is at most $1$.
steps.explanation: By antisymmetry of the order (`le_antisymm`), it suffices to show both $\\le 1$ and $\\ge 1$. Since $1$ belongs to the set of valid cover sizes by the previous step, the infimum of this set is at most $1$ by `Nat.sInf_le`.
steps.code:
apply le_antisymm
  · exact Nat.sInf_le h1

steps.claim: To show the covering number is at least $1$, it suffices to show that any valid cover size $t$ satisfies $1 \\le t$.
steps.explanation: Because the set of cover sizes is nonempty (it contains $1$), `le_csInf` implies that any lower bound on all valid cover sizes is a lower bound on their infimum.
steps.code: · refine le_csInf ⟨1, h1⟩ fun t ht => ?_

steps.claim: Every valid cover size $t$ is at least $1$.
steps.explanation: Given an equivalence cover $c$ of size $t$, nontriviality of $V$ guarantees two distinct vertices $x \\ne y$ (`exists_pair_ne`). Distinct vertices are adjacent in $\\top$, so the covering property yields an index $s \\in \\operatorname{Fin} t$ where $x$ and $y$ are identified. The existence of this index $s$ implies that $t$ cannot be $0$ (which would make $\\operatorname{Fin} 0$ empty, contradicting the existence of $s$), and therefore $1 \\le t$ by `Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr`.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨c, -, hcov⟩ := ht
    obtain ⟨x, y, hxy⟩ := exists_pair_ne V
    obtain ⟨s, -⟩ := hcov x y hxy
    exact Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr fun h => by subst h; exact s.elim0

glossary.le_antisymm: In a partial order, if $a \\le b$ and $b \\le a$, then $a = b$.
glossary.Nat.sInf_le: If a natural number $m$ belongs to a set $s \\subseteq \\mathbb{N}$, then $\\operatorname{sInf} s \\le m$.
glossary.le_csInf: In a conditionally complete lattice, if a set $s$ is nonempty and bounded below by $a$ (i.e., $a \\le b$ for all $b \\in s$), then $a \\le \\operatorname{sInf} s$.
glossary.exists_pair_ne: In any nontrivial type, there exist two distinct elements.
glossary.Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero.mpr: A natural number $n$ satisfies $1 \\le n$ whenever $n \\ne 0$.

declarations.name: mixed_graph_has_cycle
declarations.informal: A mixed graph has a cycle of length t ≥ 3: distinct vertices x_0, ..., x_{t-1} such that each x_i is joined to x_{i+1} (indices mod t) by an edge or by an arc directed from x_i to x_{i+1}.
declarations.statement: def mixed_graph_has_cycle {V : Type*} (E : SimpleGraph V) (A : V → V → Prop) (t : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- `(E, A)` has a `t`-cycle: `t ≥ 3` pairwise distinct vertices `x 0, ..., x (t-1)` with an edge `x i — x (i+1)` or an arc `x i → x (i+1)` for every `i`, indices mod `t` (`finRotate`). The paper notes cycles have length at least 3: with distinct vertices no edge is used twice. -/
def mixed_graph_has_cycle {V : Type*} (E : SimpleGraph V) (A : V → V → Prop) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  3 ≤ t ∧ ∃ x : Fin t → V, Function.Injective x ∧
    ∀ i : Fin t, E.Adj (x i) (x (finRotate t i)) ∨ A (x i) (x (finRotate t i))
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.14110 (New mixed cages, bounds and computational results), Sec. 2 (cycles of a mixed graph).

declarations.name: mixed_graph_has_girth
declarations.informal: A mixed graph has girth g: it has a cycle of length g and no shorter cycle.
declarations.statement: def mixed_graph_has_girth {V : Type*} (E : SimpleGraph V) (A : V → V → Prop) (g : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.14110 (New mixed cages, bounds and computational results), Sec. 2 (girth of a mixed graph).

declarations.name: mixed_cage_order
declarations.informal: n(r, z, g): the minimum order of an (r, z)-regular mixed graph of girth g (the order of an (r, z, g)-mixed cage).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def mixed_cage_order (r z g : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- `n(r, z, g)`: the least `n` such that some `(r, z)`-regular mixed graph on `Fin n` has girth `g` (0 if there is none). -/
noncomputable def mixed_cage_order (r z g : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ (E : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Prop),
    mixed_graph_is_valid E A ∧ mixed_graph_is_regular E A r z ∧ mixed_graph_has_girth E A g}
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.14110 (New mixed cages, bounds and computational results), Sec. 2 (mixed cages and their order n(r,z,g)).

declarations.name: mixed_graph_has_cycle_directed_triangle
declarations.informal: Sanity check: the directed triangle 0 → 1 → 2 → 0 has a 3-cycle.
declarations.statement:
theorem mixed_graph_has_cycle_directed_triangle :
    mixed_graph_has_cycle (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (fun x y => y = x + 1) 3
declarations.source:
theorem mixed_graph_has_cycle_directed_triangle :
    mixed_graph_has_cycle (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (fun x y => y = x + 1) 3 :=
  ⟨le_rfl, id, Function.injective_id, fun i => Or.inr (finRotate_apply i)⟩
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for mixed-graph cycles, arXiv:2610.14110 (New mixed cages, bounds and computational results).

explanation.summary: The theorem is proven by directly supplying the witness for the definition of a mixed graph cycle of length 3. Reflexivity gives 3 ≤ 3, the identity function on Fin 3 provides the required injective sequence of vertices, and each step along the cycle is a directed arc because the cyclic rotation permutation on Fin 3 maps i to i + 1.

steps.claim: The empty graph on Fin 3 equipped with directed edges x → x + 1 contains a cycle of length 3.
steps.explanation: By definition, a mixed graph contains a cycle of length t if 3 ≤ t and there exists an injective sequence of vertices x : Fin t → V such that successive vertices under cyclic rotation are connected by an undirected edge or a directed arc. Here t = 3, so 3 ≤ 3 holds by reflexivity (le_rfl). We take x to be the identity function on Fin 3, which is injective by Function.injective_id. For every index i ∈ Fin 3, the successor index finRotate 3 i equals i + 1 by finRotate_apply, which matches the directed arc relation id (finRotate 3 i) = id i + 1, thereby proving the right disjunct of the edge condition via Or.inr.
steps.code: ⟨le_rfl, id, Function.injective_id, fun i => Or.inr (finRotate_apply i)⟩

glossary.le_rfl: The inequality relation ≤ is reflexive: a ≤ a for any element a in a preorder.
glossary.Function.injective_id: The identity function on any type is injective.
glossary.Or.inr: If proposition b holds, then the disjunction a ∨ b holds (right introduction for disjunction).
glossary.finRotate_apply: The cyclic rotation permutation on Fin n maps each element i to i + 1.

declarations.name: mixed_graph_has_girth_directed_triangle
declarations.informal: Sanity check: the directed triangle has girth 3.
declarations.statement:
theorem mixed_graph_has_girth_directed_triangle :
    mixed_graph_has_girth (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (fun x y => y = x + 1) 3
declarations.source:
theorem mixed_graph_has_girth_directed_triangle :
    mixed_graph_has_girth (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (fun x y => y = x + 1) 3 :=
  ⟨mixed_graph_has_cycle_directed_triangle, fun _ ht h => by have := h.1; omega⟩
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for mixed-graph girth, arXiv:2610.14110 (New mixed cages, bounds and computational results).

explanation.summary: A mixed graph has girth 3 if it has a cycle of length 3 and no cycle of length strictly less than 3. The existence of a 3-cycle is given by `mixed_graph_has_cycle_directed_triangle`. The nonexistence of shorter cycles is immediate because `mixed_graph_has_cycle` requires $3 \le t$ by definition, which contradicts $t < 3$ by linear integer arithmetic.

steps.claim: The directed triangle has girth 3: it contains a 3-cycle and no cycle of length less than 3.
steps.explanation: The definition of `mixed_graph_has_girth` requires showing two conjuncts: that a cycle of length 3 exists, and that no cycle has length $t < 3$. The first conjunct is supplied by `mixed_graph_has_cycle_directed_triangle`. For the second, suppose for contradiction that there is a cycle of length $t < 3$ (hypotheses `ht : t < 3` and `h : mixed_graph_has_cycle ... t`). By definition, a cycle must have length at least 3, so `h.1` yields $3 \le t$. Linear integer arithmetic (`omega`) detects the contradiction between $t < 3$ and $3 \le t$, closing the goal.
steps.code: ⟨mixed_graph_has_cycle_directed_triangle, fun _ ht h => by have := h.1; omega⟩

glossary.mixed_graph_has_cycle_directed_triangle: The mixed graph on vertex set `Fin 3` with no undirected edges and cyclic directed edges $y = x + 1$ has a cycle of length 3.

caveats: In this development, `mixed_graph_has_cycle` requires $3 \le t$ by definition, so cycles of length 1 or 2 are ruled out purely by arithmetic without needing to check the edge relations.

declarations.name: mixed_graph_is_valid_directed_triangle
declarations.informal: Sanity check: the directed triangle is a mixed graph (no loops, no antiparallel arcs).
declarations.statement:
theorem mixed_graph_is_valid_directed_triangle :
    mixed_graph_is_valid (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (fun x y => y = x + 1)
declarations.source:
theorem mixed_graph_is_valid_directed_triangle :
    mixed_graph_is_valid (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (fun x y => y = x + 1) := by
  refine ⟨by decide, by decide, fun _ _ h => h.elim⟩
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for mixed graphs, arXiv:2610.14110 (New mixed cages, bounds and computational results).

explanation.summary: To show that the directed 3-cycle on Fin 3 with no undirected edges forms a valid mixed graph, we must verify that it has no self-loops, no antiparallel arcs, and no overlap with undirected edges. The first two conditions are checked by finite case exhaustion (decide) on Fin 3, and the third holds vacuously because the undirected edge relation is empty.

steps.claim: The directed triangle on Fin 3 with empty undirected edges is a valid mixed graph.
steps.explanation: By definition, a mixed graph is valid if its directed edge relation A has no self-loops (∀ x, ¬ A x x), has no antiparallel arcs (∀ x y, A x y → ¬ A y x), and is disjoint from its undirected edge relation E (∀ x y, E.Adj x y → ¬ A x y). Here, the vertices are Fin 3, the directed relation is cyclic successor y = x + 1, and the undirected graph is the empty graph ⊥. The refine tactic provides a witness for each of the three conjunctions: the first two (irreflexivity and asymmetry) are verified by exhaustive computation on the finite domain Fin 3 using decide, while the third holds vacuously since the empty graph has no edges (h : ⊥.Adj x y is False, eliminated via h.elim).
steps.code: refine ⟨by decide, by decide, fun _ _ h => h.elim⟩

caveats: Because the undirected edge relation is the empty graph ⊥, the adjacency hypothesis ⊥.Adj x y is definitionally False, so the third condition is dispatched directly by ex falso quodlibet (h.elim).

declarations.name: latin_square_is
declarations.informal: A Latin square of order n: an n × n array with entries in {1, ..., n} whose rows and columns are permutations of {1, ..., n}.
declarations.statement: def latin_square_is {n : ℕ} (L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n) : Prop
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.20008 (Avoiding a partial Latin square with an isotope of a given Latin square), Sec. 1 (Latin squares as functions [n]² → [n]).

declarations.name: latin_square_is_add
declarations.informal: Sanity check: the addition table of Z/n is a Latin square.
declarations.statement: theorem latin_square_is_add (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : latin_square_is fun i j : Fin n => i + j
declarations.source:
theorem latin_square_is_add (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] : latin_square_is fun i j : Fin n => i + j :=
  ⟨fun i _ _ h => add_left_cancel h, fun j _ _ h => add_right_cancel h⟩
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for Latin squares, arXiv:2610.20008 (Avoiding a partial Latin square with an isotope of a given Latin square).

explanation.summary: The theorem asserts that the addition table of Fin n defines a Latin square when n > 0. The definition of a Latin square requires each row and each column function to be injective. The proof provides a pair witnessing these two conditions: left cancellation in Fin n ensures row injectivity, and right cancellation ensures column injectivity.

steps.claim: The addition operation on Fin n forms a Latin square: each row and each column has no duplicate entries.
steps.explanation: By definition, a Latin square requires that every row map j ↦ i + j and every column map i ↦ i + j is injective. The proof supplies a pair of proofs: left cancellation (add_left_cancel) proves that i + j₁ = i + j₂ implies j₁ = j₂, establishing row injectivity; and right cancellation (add_right_cancel) proves that i₁ + j = i₂ + j implies i₁ = i₂, establishing column injectivity.
steps.code: ⟨fun i _ _ h => add_left_cancel h, fun j _ _ h => add_right_cancel h⟩

glossary.add_left_cancel: In an additive structure with left cancellation, if a + b = a + c, then b = c.
glossary.add_right_cancel: In an additive structure with right cancellation, if a + b = c + b, then a = c.

declarations.name: latin_square_exists_principal_isotope_avoiding_self
declarations.informal: The case L' = L: every Latin square of order n > 1 is avoided by one of its own principal isotopes (shift the rows cyclically).
declarations.statement:
theorem latin_square_exists_principal_isotope_avoiding_self (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n)
    (L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n) (hL : latin_square_is L) :
    ∃ π ρ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∀ i j, L (π i) (ρ j) ≠ L i j
declarations.source:
theorem latin_square_exists_principal_isotope_avoiding_self (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n)
    (L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n) (hL : latin_square_is L) :
    ∃ π ρ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∀ i j, L (π i) (ρ j) ≠ L i j := by
  refine ⟨finRotate n, 1, fun i j h => ?_⟩
  have := hL.2 j h
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 1 := ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
  rw [finRotate_apply] at this
  have : (1 : Fin (m + 1)) = 0 := by simpa using this
  exact absurd (congrArg Fin.val this) (by simp [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hn])
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.20008 (Avoiding a partial Latin square with an isotope of a given Latin square), remark after Conjecture 4 (the conjecture is trivially true when L' = L, by a cyclic permutation of the rows).

explanation.summary: The proof shows that any Latin square of order n > 1 avoids its principal isotope obtained by shifting rows cyclically by 1 and leaving columns fixed. If this isotope agreed with the original Latin square at some cell (i, j), column injectivity would force the cyclic shift to fix row i, implying i + 1 = i and therefore 1 = 0 in Fin n. Because n > 1, 1 is not congruent to 0 modulo n, producing a contradiction.

steps.claim: It suffices to show that shifting rows cyclically by finRotate n while keeping columns fixed produces no matching entry with L.
steps.explanation: We choose the candidate row permutation π to be the cyclic shift finRotate n and the column permutation ρ to be the identity permutation 1. To show they avoid L everywhere, we assume for contradiction that there exist indices i and j such that L (π i) (ρ j) = L i j, which simplifies to L (finRotate n i) j = L i j.
steps.code: refine ⟨finRotate n, 1, fun i j h => ?_⟩

steps.claim: The cyclic shift must fix the row index i, that is, (finRotate n) i = i.
steps.explanation: By definition of a Latin square, every column of L is an injective function (given by hL.2 j). Applying this injectivity to the assumption L (finRotate n i) j = L i j yields (finRotate n) i = i.
steps.code: have := hL.2 j h

steps.claim: The dimension n can be represented as a successor m + 1.
steps.explanation: Since n > 1, linear integer arithmetic establishes n = (n - 1) + 1, so we substitute n with m + 1 where m = n - 1.
steps.code: obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 1 := ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩

steps.claim: In Fin (m + 1), 1 = 0.
steps.explanation: Rewriting the cyclic rotation using finRotate_apply transforms the equality (finRotate (m + 1)) i = i into i + 1 = i. Subtracting i from both sides in Fin (m + 1) simplifies this to 1 = 0.
steps.code:
rw [finRotate_apply] at this
  have : (1 : Fin (m + 1)) = 0 := by simpa using this

steps.claim: False (contradiction).
steps.explanation: Applying congrArg with Fin.val to the identity 1 = 0 yields that 1 and 0 have the same numerical value in ℕ modulo n. However, since 1 < n, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt shows that (1 : Fin (m + 1)).val = 1 while (0 : Fin (m + 1)).val = 0, so they are not equal; absurd derives False from this contradiction.
steps.code: exact absurd (congrArg Fin.val this) (by simp [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hn])

glossary.finRotate_apply: The cyclic permutation of Fin n shifts each index by 1 modulo n, sending i to i + 1.
glossary.congrArg: If two arguments are equal, applying any function to them yields equal results: if a₁ = a₂, then f a₁ = f a₂.
glossary.Fin.val: The canonical embedding of an element of Fin n as a natural number strictly less than n.
glossary.Nat.mod_eq_of_lt: For natural numbers a and b, if a < b then the remainder a % b is simply a.
glossary.absurd: From a proposition and its negation, one can deduce any conclusion (ex falso quodlibet).

caveats: In Lean, arithmetic operations and numerals on finite types Fin n are defined when the modulus is syntactically a successor m + 1. Rewriting n = m + 1 (line 6) is a formal detail needed to perform algebraic simplifications on Fin n.

declarations.name: int_mem_h_fold_sumset_two_example
declarations.informal: Sanity check: 4 = 1 + 3 lies in 2{0, 1, 3}.
declarations.statement: theorem int_mem_h_fold_sumset_two_example : int_mem_h_fold_sumset 2 {0, 1, 3} 4
declarations.source:
theorem int_mem_h_fold_sumset_two_example : int_mem_h_fold_sumset 2 {0, 1, 3} 4 :=
  ⟨![1, 3], by decide, by simp⟩
declarations.citation: Sanity lemma for h-fold sumsets, arXiv:2610.19470 (Positivity and negativity for h-bases for n).

explanation.summary: The proof provides the explicit witness sequence (1, 3) of length 2. It then verifies by direct computation that each element belongs to {0, 1, 3} and that their sum is 1 + 3 = 4.

steps.claim: The integer 4 belongs to the 2-fold sumset of {0, 1, 3}, witnessed by the sequence (1, 3).
steps.explanation: By definition, an integer m belongs to the h-fold sumset of A if there is a sequence f of length h in A summing to m. Choosing the witness f = ![1, 3], both elements 1 and 3 belong to {0, 1, 3} (verified by exhaustive check via `decide`), and their sum 1 + 3 = 4 is verified by arithmetic simplification (`simp`).
steps.code: ⟨![1, 3], by decide, by simp⟩

declarations.name: int_mem_h_fold_sumset_of_list
declarations.informal: The sum of a list of h elements of A lies in hA.
declarations.statement:
theorem int_mem_h_fold_sumset_of_list (A : Finset ℤ) (l : List ℤ) (hA : ∀ x ∈ l, x ∈ A) :
    int_mem_h_fold_sumset l.length A l.sum
declarations.source:
theorem int_mem_h_fold_sumset_of_list (A : Finset ℤ) (l : List ℤ) (hA : ∀ x ∈ l, x ∈ A) :
    int_mem_h_fold_sumset l.length A l.sum := by
  refine ⟨fun i => l.get i, fun i => hA _ (List.get_mem l i), ?_⟩
  simpa using (List.sum_ofFn (f := fun i => l.get i)).symm.trans (by rw [List.ofFn_get])
declarations.citation: Helper for h-fold sumsets (arXiv:2610.19470 (Positivity and negativity for h-bases for n)), serving postage_stamp_basis_range_eight_neg_four_one_thirteen_fourteen.

explanation.summary: To show that the sum of a list l of elements from A belongs to the h-fold sumset of A (where h is the length of l), we need an indexing function from Fin l.length to A whose sum equals l.sum. We choose the function that retrieves the elements of the list, i ↦ l[i]. These elements lie in A by assumption, and their sum equals the sum of l because reconstructing a list from its elements yields the original list.

steps.claim: It suffices to show that ∑ i, l.get i = l.sum.
steps.explanation: By definition, an integer m is in the h-fold sumset of A if it can be written as the sum of h elements of A, indexed by Fin h. Taking h to be the length of l, we witness this existential with the indexing function i ↦ l.get i. Every element l.get i belongs to the list l by List.get_mem, and therefore belongs to A by the hypothesis hA. This leaves only the requirement that their sum equals l.sum.
steps.code: refine ⟨fun i => l.get i, fun i => hA _ (List.get_mem l i), ?_⟩

steps.claim: The sum ∑ i, l.get i is equal to l.sum.
steps.explanation: By List.sum_ofFn, the sum ∑ i, l.get i equals the sum of the list List.ofFn (fun i => l.get i). By List.ofFn_get, this reconstructed list is identical to l itself, so its sum is l.sum.
steps.code: simpa using (List.sum_ofFn (f := fun i => l.get i)).symm.trans (by rw [List.ofFn_get])

glossary.List.get_mem: For any list l and index i : Fin l.length, the element l.get i is a member of the list l.
glossary.List.sum_ofFn: The sum of the list created from a function f : Fin n → M equals the sum ∑ i, f i over Fin n.
glossary.List.ofFn_get: Converting a list to a function via get and back to a list via ofFn recovers the original list.

declarations.name: int_mem_h_fold_sumset_le_of_forall_le
declarations.informal: If every element of A is at most b, every element of hA is at most h·b.
declarations.statement:
theorem int_mem_h_fold_sumset_le_of_forall_le (h : ℕ) (A : Finset ℤ) (b : ℤ) (hb : ∀ a ∈ A, a ≤ b)
    (m : ℤ) (hm : int_mem_h_fold_sumset h A m) : m ≤ h * b
declarations.source:
theorem int_mem_h_fold_sumset_le_of_forall_le (h : ℕ) (A : Finset ℤ) (b : ℤ) (hb : ∀ a ∈ A, a ≤ b)
    (m : ℤ) (hm : int_mem_h_fold_sumset h A m) : m ≤ h * b := by
  obtain ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩ := hm
  calc ∑ i, f i ≤ ∑ _i : Fin h, b := Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => hb _ (hf i)
    _ = h * b := by simp
declarations.citation: Helper for h-fold sumsets (arXiv:2610.19470 (Positivity and negativity for h-bases for n)): the boundedness that makes n_h(A) a maximum.

explanation.summary: By definition, any element m in the h-fold sumset hA is a sum of h elements of A. Since each element of A is bounded above by b, bounding the summands termwise yields m ≤ ∑ b = h · b.

steps.claim: Represent m as a sum of h elements from A.
steps.explanation: By definition of the h-fold sumset (int_mem_h_fold_sumset), there exists a family f : Fin h → ℤ such that each f(i) ∈ A and m = ∑ i, f(i). We unpack this existential witness and substitute m with the sum.
steps.code: obtain ⟨f, hf, rfl⟩ := hm

steps.claim: ∑ i, f i ≤ ∑ _i : Fin h, b
steps.explanation: Since each f(i) is in A, the hypothesis hb implies f(i) ≤ b for every index i. We apply Finset.sum_le_sum to compare the sums termwise.
steps.code: calc ∑ i, f i ≤ ∑ _i : Fin h, b := Finset.sum_le_sum fun i _ => hb _ (hf i)

steps.claim: ∑ _i : Fin h, b = h * b
steps.explanation: Summing the constant value b over the h-element index set Fin h simplifies directly to h * b, completing the chained inequality for m.
steps.code: _ = h * b := by simp

glossary.Finset.sum_le_sum: If f(i) ≤ g(i) for all i in a finite set s, then ∑ i ∈ s, f i ≤ ∑ i ∈ s, g i.

declarations.name: postage_stamp_basis_range_eight_neg_four_one_thirteen_fourteen
declarations.informal: The set A = {−4, 1, 13, 14} is an 8-basis for 99: every integer in [0, 99] is a sum of exactly 8 elements of A, so n_8(A) ≥ 99.
declarations.statement:
theorem postage_stamp_basis_range_eight_neg_four_one_thirteen_fourteen :
    99 ≤ postage_stamp_basis_range 8 {-4, 1, 13, 14}
declarations.source:
theorem postage_stamp_basis_range_eight_neg_four_one_thirteen_fourteen :
    99 ≤ postage_stamp_basis_range 8 {-4, 1, 13, 14} := by
  have key : ∀ m : ℕ, m ≤ 99 → ∃ i j k : Fin 9, i.val + j.val + k.val ≤ 8 ∧
      (m : ℤ) = -4 * (8 - i.val - j.val - k.val : ℕ) + i.val + 13 * j.val + 14 * k.val := by
    decide +kernel
  apply le_csSup
  · refine ⟨112, fun n hn => ?_⟩
    have := int_mem_h_fold_sumset_le_of_forall_le 8 _ 14 (by decide) _ (hn n le_rfl)
    omega
