      have hne1 : G.dist b z ≠ 1 := by
        intro h
        have hzb : G.dist z b = 1 := by rw [SimpleGraph.dist_comm]; exact h
        exact hbXc (hzint b (SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj.mp hzb))
      omega
    have := Finset.le_inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z) hge2
    rw [hfval]
    exact_mod_cast this
  have hS2k : S2.card ≤ C.card := by
    have hex : ∀ b ∈ S2, ∃ c : V, G.Adj b c ∧ c ∈ X := by
      intro b hb
      rw [hS2, Finset.mem_filter] at hb
      obtain ⟨hbN, hfb⟩ := hb
      obtain ⟨z, hzmem, hzeq⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z)
      have hcast : ((X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z) : ℕ) : ℝ) = 2 := by
        rw [← hfval b]; exact hfb
      have hdseq : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z) = 2 := by exact_mod_cast hcast
      have hzdist : G.dist b z = 2 := by rw [← hzeq, hdseq]
      obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hG.exists_walk_length_eq_dist b z
      have hp2 : p.length = 2 := by rw [hp, hzdist]
      refine ⟨p.getVert 1, ?_, ?_⟩
      · have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := 0) (by rw [hp2]; omega); simpa using this
      · have hzX := (hX2sub z hzmem).2
        have hadj : G.Adj (p.getVert 1) z := by
          have h := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := 1) (by rw [hp2]; omega)
          have h2' : p.getVert 2 = z := by rw [← hp2]; exact p.getVert_length
          rwa [h2'] at h
        exact hzX _ hadj.symm
    let φ : V → Sym2 V := fun b => if h : ∃ c : V, G.Adj b c ∧ c ∈ X then s(h.choose, b) else s(b, b)
    apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn φ
    · intro b hb
      have hb' : b ∈ S2 := hb
      rw [hS2, Finset.mem_filter] at hb'
      obtain ⟨hbN, hfb⟩ := hb'
      have hbXc : b ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V) := hyint b ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G y b).mp hbN)
      rw [Finset.mem_compl] at hbXc
      have hh := hex b hb
      have hφb : φ b = s(hh.choose, b) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh
      have hspec := hh.choose_spec
      rw [Finset.mem_coe, hC, Finset.mem_filter]
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [hφb, SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset, SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet]; exact hspec.1.symm
      · rw [hφb]
        exact ⟨hh.choose, hspec.2, b, by rw [Finset.mem_compl]; exact hbXc, rfl⟩
    · intro b1 hb1 b2 hb2 heq
      have hb1' : b1 ∈ S2 := hb1
      have hb2' : b2 ∈ S2 := hb2
      rw [hS2, Finset.mem_filter] at hb1' hb2'
      obtain ⟨hb1N, _⟩ := hb1'
      obtain ⟨hb2N, _⟩ := hb2'
      have hb1Xc : b1 ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V) := hyint b1 ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G y b1).mp hb1N)
      have hb2Xc : b2 ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V) := hyint b2 ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G y b2).mp hb2N)
      rw [Finset.mem_compl] at hb1Xc hb2Xc
      have hh1 := hex b1 hb1
      have hh2 := hex b2 hb2
      have hφ1 : φ b1 = s(hh1.choose, b1) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh1
      have hφ2 : φ b2 = s(hh2.choose, b2) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh2
      rw [hφ1, hφ2] at heq
      by_contra hne
      rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at heq
      rcases heq with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
      · exact hne h2

  have hS1k : S1.card ≤ C.card := by
    have hex : ∀ b ∈ S1, ∃ w : V, G.Adj b w ∧ w ∉ X := by
      intro b hb

      obtain ⟨hbN, hbX2⟩ := hb

    let φ : V → Sym2 V := fun b => if h : ∃ w : V, G.Adj b w ∧ w ∉ X then s(b, h.choose) else s(b, b)
    apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn φ
    · intro b hb
      have hb' : b ∈ S1 := hb
      rw [hS1, Finset.mem_filter] at hb'
      obtain ⟨hbN, hbX2⟩ := hb'
      have hbX : b ∈ X := hxint b ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G x b).mp hbN)
      have hh := hex b hb
      have hφb : φ b = s(b, hh.choose) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh
      have hspec := hh.choose_spec
      rw [Finset.mem_coe, hC, Finset.mem_filter]
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [hφb, SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset, SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet]; exact hspec.1
      · rw [hφb]
        exact ⟨b, hbX, hh.choose, by rw [Finset.mem_compl]; exact hspec.2, rfl⟩
    · intro b1 hb1 b2 hb2 heq
      have hb1' : b1 ∈ S1 := hb1
      rw [hS1, Finset.mem_filter] at hb1'
      obtain ⟨hb1N, _⟩ := hb1'
      have hb1X : b1 ∈ X := hxint b1 ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G x b1).mp hb1N)
      have hh1 := hex b1 hb1
      have hh2 := hex b2 hb2
      have hφ1 : φ b1 = s(b1, hh1.choose) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh1
      have hφ2 : φ b2 = s(b2, hh2.choose) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh2
      rw [hφ1, hφ2] at heq
      by_contra hne
      rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at heq
      rcases heq with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
      · exact hne h1
      · exact hh2.choose_spec.2 (h1 ▸ hb1X)
  have hAxfull : (∑ a ∈ G.neighborFinset x, f a) = (S1.card : ℝ) := by
    have hterm : ∀ a ∈ G.neighborFinset x, f a = (if a ∉ X2 then (1:ℝ) else 0) := by
      intro a ha
      have hax : G.Adj x a := (SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G x a).mp ha
      have hdx : G.dist a x = 1 := by
        rw [SimpleGraph.dist_comm]; exact SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj.mpr hax
      have hfle : f a ≤ 1 := by
        rw [hfval]
        have h1 : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) ≤ G.dist a x := Finset.inf'_le _ hxX2
        rw [hdx] at h1
        have h2 : ((X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ 1 := by exact_mod_cast h1
        linarith
      by_cases h : a ∈ X2
      · have hz : f a = 0 := by
          rw [hfval]
          have h1 : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) ≤ G.dist a a := Finset.inf'_le _ h
          rw [SimpleGraph.dist_self] at h1
          have h2 : (0:ℕ) ≤ X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) := Nat.zero_le _
          have hinf : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) = 0 := le_antisymm h1 h2
          rw [hinf]; norm_num
        rw [hz, if_neg (by simp [h])]
      · have hge1 : 1 ≤ f a := by
          rw [hfval]

            have hne : G.dist a z ≠ 0 := by
              rw [SimpleGraph.dist_ne_zero_iff_ne_and_reachable]
              exact ⟨haz, hG a z⟩

          have := Finset.le_inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) hge'
          exact_mod_cast this
        rw [if_pos h]; linarith
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm, Finset.sum_boole, hS1]
  have hAyfull : (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (3 - f b)) ≤ (S2.card : ℝ) := by
    have hterm : ∀ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (3 - f b) ≤ (if f b = 2 then (1:ℝ) else 0) := by
      intro b hb
      have h2 := h2le b hb
      obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ : ∃ m : ℕ, f b = (m:ℝ) := ⟨_, hfval b⟩
      rw [hm] at h2 ⊢
      split_ifs with h
      · linarith
      · have hne : (2:ℝ) ≠ (m:ℝ) := fun hh => h hh.symm
        have hgt : (2:ℝ) < (m:ℝ) := lt_of_le_of_ne h2 hne
        have hgtm : 2 < m := by exact_mod_cast hgt
        have h3m : (3:ℝ) ≤ (m:ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 3 ≤ m)
        linarith
    calc (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (3 - f b))
        ≤ ∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (if f b = 2 then (1:ℝ) else 0) := Finset.sum_le_sum hterm
      _ = (S2.card : ℝ) := by rw [Finset.sum_boole, hS2]
  have hval : f y - f x = (G.dist y x : ℝ) := by rw [hfy, hfx, SimpleGraph.dist_comm, hd3]; norm_num
  have hpot := graph_lly_curvature_le_of_lipschitz_cut_potential G hG y x hxy.symm f hf hval
  have hdist : (G.dist y x : ℝ) = 3 := by rw [SimpleGraph.dist_comm, hd3]; norm_num
  rw [hdist] at hpot
  haveI : Nontrivial V := ⟨⟨x, y, hxy⟩⟩
  have hδ0 : 0 < G.minDegree := SimpleGraph.Preconnected.minDegree_pos_of_nontrivial hG.preconnected
  have hδR : (0:ℝ) < (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hδ0
  have hdyδ : (G.minDegree : ℝ) ≤ (G.degree y : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast G.minDegree_le_degree y
  have hdxδ : (G.minDegree : ℝ) ≤ (G.degree x : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast G.minDegree_le_degree x
  have hdy : (0:ℝ) < (G.degree y : ℝ) := lt_of_lt_of_le hδR hdyδ
  have hdx : (0:ℝ) < (G.degree x : ℝ) := lt_of_lt_of_le hδR hdxδ
  have hAy : 3 - (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, f b) / (G.degree y : ℝ)
      ≤ (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) := by
    have he : 3 - (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, f b) / (G.degree y : ℝ)
        = (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (3 - f b)) / (G.degree y : ℝ) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_const, SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree,

      field_simp

    exact hAyfull

      ≤ (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ) := by
    rw [hAxfull]
  have hk : (S2.card : ℝ) ≤ (C.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hS2k
  have hk1 : (S1.card : ℝ) ≤ (C.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hS1k
  have harr : (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) + (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ)
      ≤ 2 * (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by
    have h1 : (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) ≤ (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by
      calc (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) ≤ (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by gcongr
        _ ≤ (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by gcongr
    have h2 : (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ) ≤ (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by
      calc (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ) ≤ (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by gcongr
        _ ≤ (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by gcongr
    calc (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) + (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ)

  rw [graph_lly_curvature_comm]
  have e2 : 2 * (C.card : ℝ) / (3 * (G.minDegree : ℝ))
      = (2 * (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ)) / 3 := by field_simp
  rw [e2]
  refine le_trans hpot ?_
  rw [div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) < 3)]
  linarith

explanation.summary: The proof bounds the Lin–Lu–Yau (LLY) curvature $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y)$ between interior vertices $x \in X$ and $y \in X^c$ at distance 3 using the 1-Lipschitz potential function $f(v) = \operatorname{dist}(v, X_2)$, where $X_2$ is the interior of $X$. Since $f(x) = 0$ and $f(y) = 3 = \operatorname{dist}(y, x)$, a general cut-potential inequality bounds $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(y, x)$ by $\frac{1}{3}\left( \frac{1}{\deg y}\sum_{b \sim y}(3 - f(b)) + \frac{1}{\deg x}\sum_{a \sim x} f(a) \right)$. The local variations around $x$ and $y$ are then bounded by counting boundary neighbor sets $S_1 \subseteq N(x)$ and $S_2 \subseteq N(y)$, each of which injects into the cut edges $C = E(X, X^c)$. Finally, bounding vertex degrees from below by the minimum degree $\delta(G)$ and invoking the symmetry of LLY curvature yields $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y) \le \frac{2|C|}{3\delta(G)}$.

steps.claim: Define the interior $X_2 \subseteq X$ and the potential function $f(v) = \operatorname{dist}(v, X_2)$.
steps.explanation: We define $X_2 \subseteq X$ as the set of vertices in $X$ whose neighbors all lie in $X$. Since $x \in X$ and all its neighbors lie in $X$, $x \in X_2$, so $X_2$ is nonempty. We then define $f(v) = \min_{z \in X_2} \operatorname{dist}(v, z)$ as the distance from $v$ to $X_2$.
steps.code:
classical
  set X2 : Finset V := X.filter (fun z => ∀ w : V, G.Adj z w → w ∈ X) with hX2def
  have hX2sub : ∀ z ∈ X2, z ∈ X ∧ ∀ w : V, G.Adj z w → w ∈ X := by
    intro z hz; rw [hX2def, Finset.mem_filter] at hz; exact hz
  have hxX2 : x ∈ X2 := by
    rw [hX2def, Finset.mem_filter]; exact ⟨hxX, hxint⟩
  have hX2ne : X2.Nonempty := ⟨x, hxX2⟩
  let f : V → ℝ := fun v => ((X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist v z) : ℕ) : ℝ)
  have hfval : ∀ v : V, f v = ((X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist v z) : ℕ) : ℝ) := fun v => rfl

steps.explanation:
We let $C$ be the set of cut edges with one endpoint in $X$ and one in $X^c$. We set $S_2 = \{b \in N(y) \mid f(b) = 2\}$ and $S_1 = \{a \in N(x) \mid a 
otin X_2\}$. Since $\operatorname{dist}(x, y) = 3

steps.code:
set C : Finset (Sym2 V) :=
    G.edgeFinset.filter (fun e => ∃ u ∈ X, ∃ v ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V), e = s(u, v)) with hC
  set S2 : Finset V := (G.neighborFinset y).filter (fun b => f b = 2) with hS2
  set S1 : Finset V := (G.neighborFinset x).filter (fun a => a ∉ X2) with hS1
  have hxy : x ≠ y := by intro h; rw [h, SimpleGraph.dist_self] at hd3; omega

steps.explanation: Because $x \in X_2$, the distance $\operatorname{dist}(x, x) = 0$ provides an upper bound on $\inf_{z \in X_2} \operatorname{dist}(x, z)$, and since distances are non-negative, the infimum is exactly 0.
steps.code:
have hfx : f x = 0 := by
    have h1 : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist x z) ≤ G.dist x x := Finset.inf'_le _ hxX2
    rw [SimpleGraph.dist_self] at h1
    have h2 : (0:ℕ) ≤ X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist x z) := Nat.zero_le _

steps.claim: For every $z \in X_2$, $\operatorname{dist}(y, z) \ge 3$.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that $\operatorname{dist}(y, z) < 3$ for some $z \in X_2$. Since $z \in X$ and $y \in X^c$, $z \ne y$, so $\operatorname{dist}(y, z)$ is either 1 or 2. If $\operatorname{dist}(y, z) = 1$, then $y \sim z$, which contradicts the assumption that all neighbors of $y$ lie in $X^c$. If $\operatorname{dist}(y, z) = 2$, there is a path $y \sim c \sim z$; then $y \sim c$ forces $c \in X^c$, while $z \sim c$ forces $c \in X$ because $z \in X_2$, a contradiction.
steps.code:
have hge : ∀ z ∈ X2, 3 ≤ G.dist y z := by
    intro z hz
    obtain ⟨hzX, hzint⟩ := hX2sub z hz
    by_contra hlt
    push Not at hlt
    have hzy : z ≠ y := by
      intro h; rw [h] at hzX; rw [Finset.mem_compl] at hyX; exact hyX hzX
    have hyz_ne : G.dist y z ≠ 0 := by
      rw [SimpleGraph.dist_ne_zero_iff_ne_and_reachable]
      exact ⟨fun h => hzy h.symm, hG y z⟩
    have : G.dist y z = 1 ∨ G.dist y z = 2 := by omega
    rcases this with h1 | h2
    · have hadj : G.Adj y z := by rw [← SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj, h1]
      have hzc : z ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V) := hyint z hadj
      rw [Finset.mem_compl] at hzc; exact hzc hzX
    · obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hG.exists_walk_length_eq_dist y z
      have hp2 : p.length = 2 := by rw [hp, h2]
      have hadjyc : G.Adj y (p.getVert 1) := by
        have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := 0) (by rw [hp2]; omega); simpa using this
      have hadjcz : G.Adj z (p.getVert 1) := by
        have h := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := 1) (by rw [hp2]; omega)
        have h2' : p.getVert 2 = z := by rw [← hp2]; exact p.getVert_length
        rw [h2'] at h; exact h.symm
      have hcXc : p.getVert 1 ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V) := hyint _ hadjyc
      rw [Finset.mem_compl] at hcXc
      exact hcXc (hzint _ hadjcz)

steps.explanation: Since $x \in X_2$ and $\operatorname{dist}(y, x) = 3$, $f(y) \le 3$. Conversely, every $z \in X_2$ satisfies $\operatorname{dist}(y, z) \ge 3$, so $f(y) \ge 3$, proving $f(y) = 3$.

    have hle : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist y z) ≤ 3 := by

    have hinf : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist y z) = 3 := le_antisymm hle hge'

steps.claim: The potential $f$ is 1-Lipschitz: $f(a) - f(b) \le \operatorname{dist}(a, b)$ for all $a, b \in V$.
steps.explanation: For any $b$, choose a minimizer $z_0 \in X_2$ achieving $f(b) = \operatorname{dist}(b, z_0)$. By the triangle inequality, $f(a) \le \operatorname{dist}(a, z_0) \le \operatorname{dist}(a, b) + \operatorname{dist}(b, z_0) = \operatorname{dist}(a, b) + f(b)$, which rearranges to $f(a) - f(b) \le \operatorname{dist}(a, b)$.
steps.code:
have hf : ∀ a b : V, f a - f b ≤ (G.dist a b : ℝ) := by
    intro a b
    obtain ⟨z0, hz0mem, hz0eq⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z)
    have h1 : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) ≤ G.dist a z0 := Finset.inf'_le _ hz0mem
    have h2 : G.dist a z0 ≤ G.dist a b + G.dist b z0 :=
      SimpleGraph.Reachable.dist_triangle_left (hG a b) z0
    have hds : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) ≤
        X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z) + G.dist a b := by
      rw [hz0eq]; omega
    have hcast : ((X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
        ((X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z) : ℕ) : ℝ) + (G.dist a b : ℝ) := by
      have hc := (Nat.cast_le (α := ℝ)).mpr hds; rw [Nat.cast_add] at hc; exact hc
    rw [hfval, hfval]
    linarith

steps.claim: Every neighbor $b$ of $y$ satisfies $f(b) \ge 2$.
steps.explanation: Any neighbor $b$ of $y$ lies in $X^c$. For any $z \in X_2 \subseteq X$, $b \ne z$. Moreover, $b$ cannot be adjacent to $z$ because all neighbors of $z \in X_2$ belong to $X$. Hence $\operatorname{dist}(b, z) \ge 2$ for all $z \in X_2$, so $f(b) \ge 2$.
steps.code:
have h2le : ∀ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (2:ℝ) ≤ f b := by
    intro b hb
    have hyb : G.Adj y b := (SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G y b).mp hb
    have hbXc : b ∉ X := by
      have := hyint b hyb; rwa [Finset.mem_compl] at this
    have hge2 : ∀ z ∈ X2, 2 ≤ G.dist b z := by
      intro z hz
      obtain ⟨hzX, hzint⟩ := hX2sub z hz
      have hbz : b ≠ z := by intro h; exact hbXc (h ▸ hzX)
      have hne0 : G.dist b z ≠ 0 := by
        rw [SimpleGraph.dist_ne_zero_iff_ne_and_reachable]
        exact ⟨hbz, hG b z⟩
      have hne1 : G.dist b z ≠ 1 := by
        intro h
        have hzb : G.dist z b = 1 := by rw [SimpleGraph.dist_comm]; exact h
        exact hbXc (hzint b (SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj.mp hzb))
      omega
    have := Finset.le_inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z) hge2
    rw [hfval]
    exact_mod_cast this

steps.explanation: For each $b \in S_2$, $f(b) = 2$, so there is a 2-step path $b \sim c \sim z$ to some $z \in X_2$. The vertex $c$ is adjacent to $z \in X_2$, hence $c \in X$. Since $b \in N(y) \subseteq X^c$, the edge $\{c, b\}$ belongs to the cut $C$. Choosing such a neighbor $c$ for each $b$ defines a map $\phi : S_2 \to C$. This map is injective because in $\{c, b\} \in C$, $b$ is the unique endpoint lying in $X^c$, so $|S_2| \le |C|$.
steps.code:
have hS2k : S2.card ≤ C.card := by
    have hex : ∀ b ∈ S2, ∃ c : V, G.Adj b c ∧ c ∈ X := by
      intro b hb
      rw [hS2, Finset.mem_filter] at hb
      obtain ⟨hbN, hfb⟩ := hb
      obtain ⟨z, hzmem, hzeq⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_eq_inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z)
      have hcast : ((X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z) : ℕ) : ℝ) = 2 := by
        rw [← hfval b]; exact hfb
      have hdseq : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist b z) = 2 := by exact_mod_cast hcast
      have hzdist : G.dist b z = 2 := by rw [← hzeq, hdseq]
      obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hG.exists_walk_length_eq_dist b z
      have hp2 : p.length = 2 := by rw [hp, hzdist]
      refine ⟨p.getVert 1, ?_, ?_⟩
      · have := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := 0) (by rw [hp2]; omega); simpa using this
      · have hzX := (hX2sub z hzmem).2
        have hadj : G.Adj (p.getVert 1) z := by
          have h := p.adj_getVert_succ (i := 1) (by rw [hp2]; omega)
          have h2' : p.getVert 2 = z := by rw [← hp2]; exact p.getVert_length
          rwa [h2'] at h
        exact hzX _ hadj.symm
    let φ : V → Sym2 V := fun b => if h : ∃ c : V, G.Adj b c ∧ c ∈ X then s(h.choose, b) else s(b, b)
    apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn φ
    · intro b hb
      have hb' : b ∈ S2 := hb
      rw [hS2, Finset.mem_filter] at hb'
      obtain ⟨hbN, hfb⟩ := hb'
      have hbXc : b ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V) := hyint b ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G y b).mp hbN)
      rw [Finset.mem_compl] at hbXc
      have hh := hex b hb
      have hφb : φ b = s(hh.choose, b) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh
      have hspec := hh.choose_spec
      rw [Finset.mem_coe, hC, Finset.mem_filter]
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [hφb, SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset, SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet]; exact hspec.1.symm
      · rw [hφb]
        exact ⟨hh.choose, hspec.2, b, by rw [Finset.mem_compl]; exact hbXc, rfl⟩
    · intro b1 hb1 b2 hb2 heq
      have hb1' : b1 ∈ S2 := hb1
      have hb2' : b2 ∈ S2 := hb2
      rw [hS2, Finset.mem_filter] at hb1' hb2'
      obtain ⟨hb1N, _⟩ := hb1'
      obtain ⟨hb2N, _⟩ := hb2'
      have hb1Xc : b1 ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V) := hyint b1 ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G y b1).mp hb1N)
      have hb2Xc : b2 ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V) := hyint b2 ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G y b2).mp hb2N)
      rw [Finset.mem_compl] at hb1Xc hb2Xc
      have hh1 := hex b1 hb1
      have hh2 := hex b2 hb2
      have hφ1 : φ b1 = s(hh1.choose, b1) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh1
      have hφ2 : φ b2 = s(hh2.choose, b2) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh2
      rw [hφ1, hφ2] at heq
      by_contra hne
      rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at heq
      rcases heq with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
      · exact hne h2
      · exact hb1Xc (h2 ▸ hh2.choose_spec.2)

steps.explanation: For each $b \in S_1$, $b \in N(x)$ implies $b \in X$ (since $x \in X_2$), but $b \notin X_2$, so $b$ has some neighbor $w \in X^c$. Then $\{b, w\} \in C$. Mapping each $b \in S_1$ to $\{b, w\}$ gives an injection into $C$ because $b$ is the unique endpoint lying in $X$, hence $|S_1| \le |C|$.
steps.code:
have hS1k : S1.card ≤ C.card := by
    have hex : ∀ b ∈ S1, ∃ w : V, G.Adj b w ∧ w ∉ X := by
      intro b hb
      rw [hS1, Finset.mem_filter] at hb
      obtain ⟨hbN, hbX2⟩ := hb
      have hbX : b ∈ X := hxint b ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G x b).mp hbN)
      by_contra h
      push Not at h
      exact hbX2 (by rw [hX2def, Finset.mem_filter]; exact ⟨hbX, h⟩)
    let φ : V → Sym2 V := fun b => if h : ∃ w : V, G.Adj b w ∧ w ∉ X then s(b, h.choose) else s(b, b)
    apply Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn φ
    · intro b hb
      have hb' : b ∈ S1 := hb
      rw [hS1, Finset.mem_filter] at hb'
      obtain ⟨hbN, hbX2⟩ := hb'
      have hbX : b ∈ X := hxint b ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G x b).mp hbN)
      have hh := hex b hb
      have hφb : φ b = s(b, hh.choose) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh
      have hspec := hh.choose_spec
      rw [Finset.mem_coe, hC, Finset.mem_filter]
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · rw [hφb, SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset, SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet]; exact hspec.1
      · rw [hφb]
        exact ⟨b, hbX, hh.choose, by rw [Finset.mem_compl]; exact hspec.2, rfl⟩
    · intro b1 hb1 b2 hb2 heq
      have hb1' : b1 ∈ S1 := hb1
      rw [hS1, Finset.mem_filter] at hb1'
      obtain ⟨hb1N, _⟩ := hb1'
      have hb1X : b1 ∈ X := hxint b1 ((SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G x b1).mp hb1N)
      have hh1 := hex b1 hb1
      have hh2 := hex b2 hb2
      have hφ1 : φ b1 = s(b1, hh1.choose) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh1
      have hφ2 : φ b2 = s(b2, hh2.choose) := by simp only [φ]; exact dif_pos hh2
      rw [hφ1, hφ2] at heq
      by_contra hne
      rw [Sym2.eq_iff] at heq
      rcases heq with ⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩
      · exact hne h1
      · exact hh2.choose_spec.2 (h1 ▸ hb1X)

steps.explanation: For $a \in N(x)$, $f(a) \le \operatorname{dist}(a, x) = 1$. If $a \in X_2$, $f(a) = 0$. If $a \notin X_2$, $a$ is not in $X_2$ so its distance to any vertex in $X_2$ is at least 1, giving $f(a) = 1$. Thus $f(a) = 1$ exactly when $a \in S_1$, and summing over all neighbors of $x$ gives $|S_1|$.
steps.code:
have hAxfull : (∑ a ∈ G.neighborFinset x, f a) = (S1.card : ℝ) := by
    have hterm : ∀ a ∈ G.neighborFinset x, f a = (if a ∉ X2 then (1:ℝ) else 0) := by
      intro a ha
      have hax : G.Adj x a := (SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset G x a).mp ha
      have hdx : G.dist a x = 1 := by
        rw [SimpleGraph.dist_comm]; exact SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj.mpr hax
      have hfle : f a ≤ 1 := by
        rw [hfval]
        have h1 : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) ≤ G.dist a x := Finset.inf'_le _ hxX2
        rw [hdx] at h1
        have h2 : ((X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ 1 := by exact_mod_cast h1
        linarith
      by_cases h : a ∈ X2
      · have hz : f a = 0 := by
          rw [hfval]
          have h1 : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) ≤ G.dist a a := Finset.inf'_le _ h
          rw [SimpleGraph.dist_self] at h1
          have h2 : (0:ℕ) ≤ X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) := Nat.zero_le _
          have hinf : X2.inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) = 0 := le_antisymm h1 h2
          rw [hinf]; norm_num
        rw [hz, if_neg (by simp [h])]
      · have hge1 : 1 ≤ f a := by
          rw [hfval]
          have hge' : ∀ z ∈ X2, 1 ≤ G.dist a z := by
            intro z hz
            have haz : a ≠ z := by intro hh; exact h (hh ▸ hz)
            have hne : G.dist a z ≠ 0 := by
              rw [SimpleGraph.dist_ne_zero_iff_ne_and_reachable]
              exact ⟨haz, hG a z⟩
            omega
          have := Finset.le_inf' hX2ne (fun z => G.dist a z) hge'
          exact_mod_cast this
        rw [if_pos h]; linarith
    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hterm, Finset.sum_boole, hS1]

steps.explanation: For $b \in N(y)$, $f(b)$ is an integer $\ge 2$. If $f(b) = 2$, then $3 - f(b) = 1$. If $f(b) \ne 2$, then $f(b) \ge 3$, so $3 - f(b) \le 0$. Thus $3 - f(b) \le 1_{f(b) = 2}$ for all $b \in N(y)$, and summing over $N(y)$ yields $\le |S_2|$.
steps.code:
have hAyfull : (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (3 - f b)) ≤ (S2.card : ℝ) := by
    have hterm : ∀ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (3 - f b) ≤ (if f b = 2 then (1:ℝ) else 0) := by
      intro b hb
      have h2 := h2le b hb
      obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ : ∃ m : ℕ, f b = (m:ℝ) := ⟨_, hfval b⟩
      rw [hm] at h2 ⊢
      split_ifs with h
      · linarith
      · have hne : (2:ℝ) ≠ (m:ℝ) := fun hh => h hh.symm
        have hgt : (2:ℝ) < (m:ℝ) := lt_of_le_of_ne h2 hne
        have hgtm : 2 < m := by exact_mod_cast hgt
        have h3m : (3:ℝ) ≤ (m:ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast (by omega : 3 ≤ m)
        linarith
    calc (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (3 - f b))
        ≤ ∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (if f b = 2 then (1:ℝ) else 0) := Finset.sum_le_sum hterm
      _ = (S2.card : ℝ) := by rw [Finset.sum_boole, hS2]

steps.claim: Applying the potential bound yields $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(y, x) \le \frac{1}{3}\left( \frac{|S_2|}{\deg y} + \frac{|S_1|}{\deg x} \right)$.
steps.explanation: Since $f$ is 1-Lipschitz and $f(y) - f(x) = 3 = \operatorname{dist}(y, x)$, `graph_lly_curvature_le_of_lipschitz_cut_potential` bounds $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(y, x)$ by $\frac{1}{3}\left( 3 - \frac{1}{\deg y}\sum_{b \in N(y)} f(b) + \frac{1}{\deg x}\sum_{a \in N(x)} f(a) \right)$. We rewrite $3 - \frac{1}{\deg y}\sum f(b) = \frac{1}{\deg y}\sum (3 - f(b)) \le \frac{|S_2|}{\deg y}$, while the $x$-sum evaluates to $\frac{|S_1|}{\deg x}$.
steps.code:
have hval : f y - f x = (G.dist y x : ℝ) := by rw [hfy, hfx, SimpleGraph.dist_comm, hd3]; norm_num
  have hpot := graph_lly_curvature_le_of_lipschitz_cut_potential G hG y x hxy.symm f hf hval
  have hdist : (G.dist y x : ℝ) = 3 := by rw [SimpleGraph.dist_comm, hd3]; norm_num
  rw [hdist] at hpot
  haveI : Nontrivial V := ⟨⟨x, y, hxy⟩⟩
  have hδ0 : 0 < G.minDegree := SimpleGraph.Preconnected.minDegree_pos_of_nontrivial hG.preconnected
  have hδR : (0:ℝ) < (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hδ0
  have hdyδ : (G.minDegree : ℝ) ≤ (G.degree y : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast G.minDegree_le_degree y
  have hdxδ : (G.minDegree : ℝ) ≤ (G.degree x : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast G.minDegree_le_degree x
  have hdy : (0:ℝ) < (G.degree y : ℝ) := lt_of_lt_of_le hδR hdyδ
  have hdx : (0:ℝ) < (G.degree x : ℝ) := lt_of_lt_of_le hδR hdxδ
  have hAy : 3 - (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, f b) / (G.degree y : ℝ)
      ≤ (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) := by
    have he : 3 - (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, f b) / (G.degree y : ℝ)
        = (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, (3 - f b)) / (G.degree y : ℝ) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_const, SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree,
        nsmul_eq_mul]
      field_simp
    rw [he, div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hdy]
    exact hAyfull
  have hAx : (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset x, f b) / (G.degree x : ℝ)
      ≤ (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ) := by
    rw [hAxfull]
  have hk : (S2.card : ℝ) ≤ (C.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hS2k
  have hk1 : (S1.card : ℝ) ≤ (C.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hS1k

steps.claim: $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y) \le \frac{2|C|}{3 \delta(G)}$.
steps.explanation: Using $|S_2| \le |C|$ and $\deg y \ge \delta(G)$, we have $\frac{|S_2|}{\deg y} \le \frac{|C|}{\delta(G)}$, and similarly $\frac{|S_1|}{\deg x} \le \frac{|C|}{\delta(G)}$. Adding these gives $\le \frac{2|C|}{\delta(G)}$. Since $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y) = \kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(y, x)$ by symmetry, dividing by 3 concludes the proof.
steps.code:
have harr : (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) + (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ)
      ≤ 2 * (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by
    have h1 : (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) ≤ (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by
      calc (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) ≤ (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by gcongr
        _ ≤ (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by gcongr
    have h2 : (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ) ≤ (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by
      calc (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ) ≤ (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by gcongr
        _ ≤ (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by gcongr
    calc (S2.card : ℝ) / (G.degree y : ℝ) + (S1.card : ℝ) / (G.degree x : ℝ)
        ≤ (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) + (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by linarith
      _ = 2 * (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ) := by ring
  rw [graph_lly_curvature_comm]
  have e2 : 2 * (C.card : ℝ) / (3 * (G.minDegree : ℝ))
      = (2 * (C.card : ℝ) / (G.minDegree : ℝ)) / 3 := by field_simp
  rw [e2]
  refine le_trans hpot ?_
  rw [div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) < 3)]
  linarith

glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to `Finset.filter p s` if and only if it belongs to `s` and satisfies the predicate `p`.
glossary.SimpleGraph.dist_self: The graph distance from any vertex to itself is zero.
glossary.Finset.inf'_le: The infimum of a function over a nonempty finite set is bounded above by the function value at any element of the set.
glossary.Nat.zero_le: Every natural number is greater than or equal to zero.
glossary.le_antisymm: If $a \le b$ and $b \le a$, then $a = b$.
glossary.Finset.mem_compl: An element belongs to the complement of a finite set $s$ if and only if it does not belong to $s$.
glossary.SimpleGraph.dist_ne_zero_iff_ne_and_reac: The distance between two vertices is nonzero if and only if they are distinct and there is a path between them.
glossary.SimpleGraph.dist_eq_one_iff_adj: The distance between two vertices is 1 if and only if they are adjacent.
glossary.SimpleGraph.dist_comm: Graph distance is symmetric: $d(u, v) = d(v, u)$.
glossary.Finset.le_inf': If a value $a$ is bounded above by $f(b)$ for every element $b$ in a nonempty finite set, then $a \le \inf' f$.
glossary.Finset.exists_mem_eq_inf': On any nonempty finite set, the infimum of a linearly ordered function is achieved at some element of the set.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Reachable.dist_triangle_left: The triangle inequality for graph distance: $d(u, w) \le d(u, v) + d(v, w)$ when $v$ is reachable from $u$.
glossary.Nat.cast_le: An inequality $m \le n$ between natural numbers is equivalent to the corresponding inequality between their real casts.
glossary.Nat.cast_add: The cast of the sum of two natural numbers equals the sum of their casts.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset: A vertex $w$ is in the neighbor finset of $v$ if and only if $v$ and $w$ are adjacent in the graph.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn: If a map from a finite set $s$ to a finite set $t$ is injective on $s$, then $|s| \le |t|$.
glossary.dif_pos: A dependent if-then-else evaluates to the then-branch when the condition is true.
glossary.Finset.mem_coe: Membership in a coerced finset is equivalent to membership in the finset.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_edgeFinset: An unordered pair belongs to the edge finset of a graph if and only if it belongs to the edge set.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet: An unordered pair $s(v, w)$ belongs to the edge set if and only if $v$ and $w$ are adjacent.
glossary.Sym2.eq_iff: Two unordered pairs $\{x, y\}$ and $\{z, w\}$ are equal if and only if $(x = z \land y = w)$ or $(x = w \land y = z)$.
glossary.if_neg: An if-then-else expression evaluates to the else-branch when the condition is false.
glossary.if_pos: An if-then-else expression evaluates to the then-branch when the condition is true.
glossary.Finset.sum_congr: Two finite sums are equal if their index sets are equal and their summands agree on all elements.
glossary.Finset.sum_boole: The sum over a finite set of the indicator of a predicate equals the cardinality of the subset satisfying the predicate.
glossary.lt_of_le_of_ne: If $a \le b$ and $a \ne b$, then $a < b$.
glossary.Finset.sum_le_sum: If $f(i) \le g(i)$ for all elements $i$ in a finite set, then $\sum_i f(i) \le \sum_i g(i)$.
glossary.graph_lly_curvature_le_of_lipschitz_cut_: If $f$ is a 1-Lipschitz function satisfying $f(x) - f(y) = d(x, y)$, then $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y) \le \frac{1}{d(x,y)}\left( d(x,y) - \frac{1}{\deg x}\sum_{a \sim x} f(a) + \frac{1}{\deg y}\sum_{b \sim y} f(b) \right)$.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Preconnected.minDegree_pos_o: A preconnected graph on a nontrivial finite vertex type has strictly positive minimum degree.
glossary.lt_of_lt_of_le: If $a < b$ and $b \le c$, then $a < c$.
glossary.Finset.sum_sub_distrib: The sum of differences $\sum (f(x) - g(x))$ over a finite set equals $\sum f(x) - \sum g(x)$.
glossary.Finset.sum_const: The sum of a constant $b$ over a finite set $s$ equals $|s| \cdot b$.
glossary.SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degre: The number of neighbors of a vertex equals its degree.
glossary.nsmul_eq_mul: Natural scalar multiplication $n \cdot a$ equals the product of $n$ cast into the semiring with $a$.
glossary.div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right: Dividing by a strictly positive number preserves the direction of an inequality.
glossary.graph_lly_curvature_comm: Lin–Lu–Yau curvature is symmetric: $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y) = \kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(y, x)$.
glossary.le_trans: If $a \le b$ and $b \le c$, then $a \le c$.

caveats: The injections from $S_2$ and $S_1$ into the cut edge set $C = E(X, X^c)$ rely on classical choice to pick a specific crossing neighbor for each boundary vertex.

The potential bound lemma `graph_lly_curvature_le_of_lipschitz_cut_potential` is applied with the roles of $x$ and $y$ swapped because $f(y) - f(x) = d(y, x) = 3$; the bound on $\kappa_{\mathrm{LLY}}(x, y)$ is then deduced using the symmetry lemma `graph_lly_curvature_comm`.

declarations.name: exists_dist_eq_three_of_three_le_diam
declarations.informal: If the diameter of a finite connected graph is at least 3, then some pair of vertices is at distance exactly 3.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dist_eq_three_of_three_le_diam
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hd : 3 ≤ G.diam) :
    ∃ x y : V, G.dist x y = 3
declarations.source:
/-- A finite graph whose diameter is at least 3 has a pair of vertices at distance exactly 3. -/
theorem exists_dist_eq_three_of_three_le_diam
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hd : 3 ≤ G.diam) :
    ∃ x y : V, G.dist x y = 3 := by
  have hns : ¬ Subsingleton V := by
    intro hs
    have h0 : G.diam = 0 := SimpleGraph.diam_eq_zero.mpr (Or.inr hs)
    omega
  haveI : Nonempty V := by
    by_contra h
    exact hns ⟨fun a b => (h ⟨a⟩).elim⟩
  obtain ⟨u, v, huv⟩ := SimpleGraph.exists_dist_eq_diam (G := G)
  have h3 : 3 ≤ G.dist u v := by rw [huv]; exact hd
  have hne0 : G.dist u v ≠ 0 := by omega
  obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_dist_ne_zero hne0
  have hlen : 3 ≤ p.length := by rw [hp]; exact h3
  refine ⟨u, p.getVert 3, le_antisymm ?_ ?_⟩
  · have ht : (p.take 3).length = 3 := by
      rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.take_length]
      omega
    calc G.dist u (p.getVert 3) ≤ (p.take 3).length := SimpleGraph.dist_le _
      _ = 3 := ht
  · by_contra hcon
    have hcon2 : G.dist u (p.getVert 3) ≤ 2 := by omega
    have hdrop : G.dist (p.getVert 3) v ≤ (p.drop 3).length := SimpleGraph.dist_le _
    rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.drop_length] at hdrop
    have htri : G.dist u v ≤ G.dist u (p.getVert 3) + G.dist (p.getVert 3) v :=
      SimpleGraph.Reachable.dist_triangle_left (p.take 3).reachable v
    omega

explanation.summary: Since the finite graph has diameter at least 3, there exist vertices u and v realizing the diameter, connected by a shortest walk p of length at least 3. Choosing u and the vertex w at distance 3 along p (i.e. p.getVert 3), the prefix walk of length 3 shows that dist(u, w) ≤ 3. If dist(u, w) ≤ 2, bypassing the prefix with a shorter path would yield a walk from u to v of length at most 2 + (length(p) - 3) < length(p), contradicting that p is a shortest walk.

steps.claim: The vertex set V has at least two elements (it is not a subsingleton).
steps.explanation: If V had at most one vertex, the diameter of G would be 0 by `SimpleGraph.diam_eq_zero.mpr`, contradicting the hypothesis that the diameter is at least 3.
steps.code:
have hns : ¬ Subsingleton V := by
    intro hs
    have h0 : G.diam = 0 := SimpleGraph.diam_eq_zero.mpr (Or.inr hs)
    omega

steps.claim: The vertex set V is nonempty.
steps.explanation: If V were empty, then any two vertices would vacuously be equal, making V a subsingleton, which contradicts what was just shown.
steps.code:
haveI : Nonempty V := by
    by_contra h
    exact hns ⟨fun a b => (h ⟨a⟩).elim⟩

steps.claim: There exists a pair of vertices u, v at distance at least 3, so in particular dist(u, v) ≠ 0.
steps.explanation: Because V is nonempty and finite, there exist vertices u and v whose distance equals the diameter of G (`SimpleGraph.exists_dist_eq_diam`). Since the diameter is at least 3, dist(u, v) ≥ 3, which implies dist(u, v) ≠ 0.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨u, v, huv⟩ := SimpleGraph.exists_dist_eq_diam (G := G)
  have h3 : 3 ≤ G.dist u v := by rw [huv]; exact hd
  have hne0 : G.dist u v ≠ 0 := by omega

steps.claim: There exists a walk p from u to v of length equal to dist(u, v) ≥ 3.
steps.explanation: Because dist(u, v) ≠ 0, there exists a shortest walk p from u to v whose length equals dist(u, v) (`SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_dist_ne_zero`). Since dist(u, v) ≥ 3, the length of p is at least 3.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_dist_ne_zero hne0
  have hlen : 3 ≤ p.length := by rw [hp]; exact h3

steps.claim: It suffices to show that dist(u, p.getVert 3) ≤ 3 and 3 ≤ dist(u, p.getVert 3).
steps.explanation: We choose u and the third vertex along the walk p (p.getVert 3) as the candidate pair. By antisymmetry of inequality (`le_antisymm`), showing both inequalities establishes that their distance is exactly 3.
steps.code: refine ⟨u, p.getVert 3, le_antisymm ?_ ?_⟩

steps.claim: The distance from u to p.getVert 3 is at most 3.
steps.explanation: The initial segment `p.take 3` is a walk from u to p.getVert 3. Since the length of p is at least 3, the length of this prefix is min(3, length(p)) = 3 by `SimpleGraph.Walk.take_length`. Since distance is bounded by the length of any connecting walk (`SimpleGraph.dist_le`), dist(u, p.getVert 3) ≤ 3.
steps.code:
· have ht : (p.take 3).length = 3 := by
      rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.take_length]
      omega
    calc G.dist u (p.getVert 3) ≤ (p.take 3).length := SimpleGraph.dist_le _
      _ = 3 := ht

steps.claim: The distance from u to p.getVert 3 is at least 3, which finishes the proof.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that dist(u, p.getVert 3) < 3, so dist(u, p.getVert 3) ≤ 2. The remaining suffix `p.drop 3` is a walk from p.getVert 3 to v of length length(p) - 3 (`SimpleGraph.Walk.drop_length`), so dist(p.getVert 3, v) ≤ length(p) - 3 by `SimpleGraph.dist_le`. Applying the triangle inequality (`SimpleGraph.Reachable.dist_triangle_left`), we get dist(u, v) ≤ dist(u, p.getVert 3) + dist(p.getVert 3, v) ≤ 2 + (length(p) - 3) = length(p) - 1. But length(p) = dist(u, v), so dist(u, v) ≤ dist(u, v) - 1, which is impossible.
steps.code:
· by_contra hcon
    have hcon2 : G.dist u (p.getVert 3) ≤ 2 := by omega
    have hdrop : G.dist (p.getVert 3) v ≤ (p.drop 3).length := SimpleGraph.dist_le _
    rw [SimpleGraph.Walk.drop_length] at hdrop
    have htri : G.dist u v ≤ G.dist u (p.getVert 3) + G.dist (p.getVert 3) v :=
      SimpleGraph.Reachable.dist_triangle_left (p.take 3).reachable v
    omega

glossary.le_antisymm: In a partial order, if a ≤ b and b ≤ a, then a = b.
glossary.Or.inr: The second constructor of `Or`, proving `A ∨ B` given a proof of `B`.
glossary.SimpleGraph.diam_eq_zero.mpr: A graph has diameter 0 if its extended diameter is infinite or its vertex type is a subsingleton.
glossary.SimpleGraph.dist_le: The distance between the endpoints of a walk is at most the length of the walk.
glossary.SimpleGraph.exists_dist_eq_diam: In any nonempty finite graph, there exists a pair of vertices whose distance equals the diameter of the graph.
glossary.SimpleGraph.exists_walk_of_dist_ne_zero: If two vertices have nonzero distance, there exists a walk between them whose length equals their distance (a geodesic walk).
glossary.SimpleGraph.Reachable.dist_triangle_left: The triangle inequality for graph distance: if u can reach v, then dist(u, w) ≤ dist(u, v) + dist(v, w).
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.drop_length: The length of the suffix of a walk p obtained by dropping the first n steps is length(p) - n.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.reachable: A walk from u to v shows that u can reach v.
glossary.SimpleGraph.Walk.take_length: The length of the prefix of a walk p obtained by taking at most n steps is min(n, length(p)).

declarations.name: wasserstein_dist_le_of_diameter_two
declarations.informal: On any graph of diameter at most 2, the Wasserstein distance between probability measures μ and ν with d(x, y) = 1 is bounded by 2 - 2 * S0 - m_xy, where S0 = ∑ min(μ v, ν v) and m_xy is the minimum excess mass at x and y.
declarations.source:
/-- Wasserstein distance upper bound on diameter ≤ 2 graphs via an explicit 3-stage transport plan. -/
theorem wasserstein_dist_le_of_diameter_two {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (hdist2 : ∀ a b : V, (G.dist a b : ℝ) ≤ 2)
    (μ ν : V → ℝ) (hμ : ∀ a, 0 ≤ μ a) (hν : ∀ b, 0 ≤ ν b)
    (hμ1 : ∑ a, μ a = 1) (hν1 : ∑ b, ν b = 1)
    (x y : V) (hxy_dist : (G.dist x y : ℝ) = 1) :
    let S0 := ∑ v, min (μ v) (ν v)
    let μ1 (a : V) := μ a - min (μ a) (ν a)
    let ν1 (b : V) := ν b - min (μ b) (ν b)
    let m_xy := min (μ1 x) (ν1 y)
    graph_wasserstein_dist G μ ν ≤ 2 - 2 * S0 - m_xy := by
  dsimp only
  set S0 : ℝ := ∑ v, min (μ v) (ν v) with hS0
  set m1 : V → ℝ := (fun a => μ a - min (μ a) (ν a)) with hm1
  set n1 : V → ℝ := (fun b => ν b - min (μ b) (ν b)) with hn1
  set m : ℝ := min (μ x - min (μ x) (ν x)) (ν y - min (μ y) (ν y)) with hm
  have hm_eq : m = min (m1 x) (n1 y) := by rw [hm, hm1, hn1]
  set rem : ℝ := 1 - S0 - m with hrem
  set μ2 : V → ℝ := (fun a => m1 a - (if a = x then m else 0)) with hμ2
  set ν2 : V → ℝ := (fun b => n1 b - (if b = y then m else 0)) with hν2
  set π : V → V → ℝ := (fun a b => (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0)
        + (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) + μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) with hπ
  have hμ1_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ m1 a := by
    intro a; rw [hm1]; exact sub_nonneg.mpr (min_le_left _ _)
  have hν1_nonneg : ∀ b, 0 ≤ n1 b := by
    intro b; rw [hn1]; exact sub_nonneg.mpr (min_le_right _ _)
  have hsum_m1 : ∑ a, m1 a = 1 - S0 := by
    have h : ∑ a, m1 a = ∑ a, (μ a - min (μ a) (ν a)) := by rw [hm1]
    rw [h, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hμ1, hS0]
  have hsum_n1 : ∑ b, n1 b = 1 - S0 := by
    have h : ∑ b, n1 b = ∑ b, (ν b - min (μ b) (ν b)) := by rw [hn1]
    rw [h, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hν1, hS0]
  have hm_le_m1 : m ≤ m1 x := by rw [hm_eq]; exact min_le_left _ _
  have hm_le_n1 : m ≤ n1 y := by rw [hm_eq]; exact min_le_right _ _
  have hm_nonneg : 0 ≤ m := by rw [hm_eq]; exact le_min (hμ1_nonneg x) (hν1_nonneg y)
  have hm_le : m ≤ 1 - S0 := by
    calc m ≤ m1 x := hm_le_m1
      _ ≤ ∑ a, m1 a := Finset.single_le_sum (fun a _ => hμ1_nonneg a) (Finset.mem_univ x)
      _ = 1 - S0 := hsum_m1
  have hrem_nonneg : 0 ≤ rem := by rw [hrem]; linarith
  have hμ2_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ μ2 a := by
    intro a
    simp only [hμ2]
    by_cases h : a = x
    · rw [if_pos h, sub_nonneg]
      rw [h]; exact hm_le_m1
    · rw [if_neg h]; simpa using hμ1_nonneg a
  have hν2_nonneg : ∀ b, 0 ≤ ν2 b := by
    intro b
    simp only [hν2]
    by_cases h : b = y
    · rw [if_pos h, sub_nonneg]
      rw [h]; exact hm_le_n1
    · rw [if_neg h]; simpa using hν1_nonneg b
  have hsum_μ2 : ∑ a, μ2 a = rem := by
    rw [hμ2, hrem, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_ite_eq']
    simp only [Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
    rw [hsum_m1]
  have hsum_ν2 : ∑ b, ν2 b = rem := by
    rw [hν2, hrem, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_ite_eq']
    simp only [Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
    rw [hsum_n1]
  have hcoupl_row : ∀ a, ∑ b, μ2 a * ν2 b / rem = μ2 a := by
    intro a
    by_cases h0 : rem = 0
    · have hz : μ2 a = 0 := by
        have hsum0 : ∑ b, μ2 b = 0 := by rw [hsum_μ2, h0]
        exact (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun b _ => hμ2_nonneg b)).mp hsum0 a (Finset.mem_univ a)
      rw [hz]
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero; intro b _
      rw [h0]; simp
    · rw [← Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.mul_sum, hsum_ν2]
      exact mul_div_cancel_right₀ (μ2 a) h0
  have hcoupl_col : ∀ b, ∑ a, μ2 a * ν2 b / rem = ν2 b := by
    intro b
    by_cases h0 : rem = 0
    · have hz : ν2 b = 0 := by
        have hsum0 : ∑ b, ν2 b = 0 := by rw [hsum_ν2, h0]
        exact (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun b _ => hν2_nonneg b)).mp hsum0 b (Finset.mem_univ b)
      rw [hz]
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero; intro a _
      rw [h0]; simp
    · rw [← Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.sum_mul, hsum_μ2]
      exact mul_div_cancel_left₀ (ν2 b) h0
  have hπ_nonneg : ∀ a b, 0 ≤ π a b := by
    intro a b
    have h1 : (0:ℝ) ≤ (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0) := by
      by_cases h : a = b
      · rw [if_pos h]; exact le_min (hμ a) (hν a)
      · rw [if_neg h]
    have h2 : (0:ℝ) ≤ (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) := by
      by_cases hby : b = y
      · rw [if_pos hby]
        by_cases hax : a = x
        · rw [if_pos hax]; exact hm_nonneg
        · rw [if_neg hax]
      · rw [if_neg hby]
    have h3 : (0:ℝ) ≤ μ2 a * ν2 b / rem :=
      div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (hμ2_nonneg a) (hν2_nonneg b)) hrem_nonneg
    simp only [hπ]
    linarith
  have hrow : ∀ a, ∑ b, π a b = μ a := by
    intro a
    simp only [hπ]
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    have hdiag : ∑ b, (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0) = min (μ a) (ν a) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq]; simp
    have hmxy : ∑ b, (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) = (if a = x then m else 0) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq']; simp
    rw [hdiag, hmxy, hcoupl_row a]
    simp only [hμ2, hm1]
    ring
  have hcol : ∀ b, ∑ a, π a b = ν b := by
    intro b
    simp only [hπ]
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    have hdiag : ∑ a, (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0) = min (μ b) (ν b) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq']; simp
    have hmxy : ∑ a, (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) = (if b = y then m else 0) := by
      by_cases hby : b = y
      · simp [hby, Finset.sum_ite_eq']
      · simp [hby]
    rw [hdiag, hmxy, hcoupl_col b]
    simp only [hν2, hn1]
    ring
  have hcost : ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * π a b ≤ 2 - 2 * S0 - m := by
    have hsplit : ∀ a b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * π a b
        = (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0)
          + (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0)
          + (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) := by
      intro a b; simp only [hπ]; ring
    have hD : ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0) = 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro a _
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro b _
      by_cases h : a = b
      · rw [if_pos h]
        have hd : (G.dist a b : ℝ) = 0 := by rw [h]; simp
        rw [hd, zero_mul]
      · rw [if_neg h, mul_zero]
    have hM : ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) = m := by
      have inner : ∀ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0)
            = (G.dist a y : ℝ) * (if a = x then m else 0) := by
        intro a
        simp only [mul_ite, mul_zero]
        rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq']; simp
      simp only [inner]
      have inner2 : ∑ a, (G.dist a y : ℝ) * (if a = x then m else 0) = (G.dist x y : ℝ) * m := by
        simp only [mul_ite, mul_zero]
        rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq']; simp
      rw [inner2, hxy_dist]; ring
    have hC : ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) ≤ 2 * rem := by
      by_cases h0 : rem = 0
      · have hz : ∀ a b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) = 0 := by
          intro a b; rw [h0]; simp
        simp only [hz]
        simp [h0]
      · have hle : ∀ a b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) ≤ 2 * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) := by
          intro a b
          have ht : 0 ≤ μ2 a * ν2 b / rem := div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (hμ2_nonneg a) (hν2_nonneg b)) hrem_nonneg
          exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hdist2 a b) ht
        calc ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem)
            ≤ ∑ a, ∑ b, 2 * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) := by
              apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro a _
              apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro b _
              exact hle a b
          _ = 2 * rem := by
              have inner : ∀ a, ∑ b, 2 * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) = 2 * μ2 a := by
                intro a; rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hcoupl_row a]
              simp only [inner]
              rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hsum_μ2]
    calc ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * π a b
        = (∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0))
          + (∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0))
          + (∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem)) := by
            simp only [hsplit, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      _ = 0 + m + (∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem)) := by rw [hD, hM]
      _ ≤ 0 + m + 2 * rem := by linarith
      _ = 2 - 2 * S0 - m := by rw [hrem]; ring
  calc graph_wasserstein_dist G μ ν ≤ ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * π a b :=
        graph_wasserstein_dist_le_of_plan G μ ν π hπ_nonneg hrow hcol
    _ ≤ 2 - 2 * S0 - m := hcost

explanation.summary: To bound the Wasserstein distance between probability measures μ and ν on a graph of diameter at most 2, we construct an explicit three-stage transport plan π. First, mass min(μ v, ν v) is kept in place at each vertex v at distance 0, accounting for total mass S0. Second, the maximum possible excess mass m = min(m1 x, n1 y) is sent from x to y along the edge between them at distance d(x, y) = 1, costing 1 * m. Finally, the remaining mass rem = 1 - S0 - m is transported via an independent product coupling, where the graph diameter bound d(a, b) ≤ 2 ensures this remainder costs at most 2 * rem. Summing these costs gives 0 + m + 2(1 - S0 - m) = 2 - 2 * S0 - m, yielding the desired upper bound.

steps.claim: Define the intermediate excess distributions and the three-stage transport plan π
steps.explanation: Simplify the let-bindings and define the retained diagonal mass S0 = ∑ min(μ v, ν v), the excess masses m1(a) = μ(a) - min(μ a, ν a) and n1(b) = ν(b) - min(μ b, ν b), the mass m = min(m1 x, n1 y) to be transported along the edge (x, y), the remaining excess mass rem = 1 - S0 - m, the adjusted excesses μ2 and ν2, and the candidate coupling π consisting of diagonal retention, direct edge transport from x to y, and an independent product coupling of the remainder.
steps.code:
dsimp only
  set S0 : ℝ := ∑ v, min (μ v) (ν v) with hS0
  set m1 : V → ℝ := (fun a => μ a - min (μ a) (ν a)) with hm1
  set n1 : V → ℝ := (fun b => ν b - min (μ b) (ν b)) with hn1
  set m : ℝ := min (μ x - min (μ x) (ν x)) (ν y - min (μ y) (ν y)) with hm
  have hm_eq : m = min (m1 x) (n1 y) := by rw [hm, hm1, hn1]
  set rem : ℝ := 1 - S0 - m with hrem
  set μ2 : V → ℝ := (fun a => m1 a - (if a = x then m else 0)) with hμ2
  set ν2 : V → ℝ := (fun b => n1 b - (if b = y then m else 0)) with hν2
  set π : V → V → ℝ := (fun a b => (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0)
        + (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) + μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) with hπ

steps.claim: The excess measures m1, n1 are non-negative, have total mass 1 - S0, and satisfy 0 ≤ m ≤ 1 - S0, so rem ≥ 0
steps.explanation: Because min(μ a, ν a) ≤ μ a and min(μ b, ν b) ≤ ν b, m1 and n1 are pointwise non-negative. Subtracting the sum of minimums from the unit total mass of μ and ν gives ∑ m1(a) = ∑ n1(b) = 1 - S0. The mass m is non-negative and bounded by m1(x) ≤ ∑ m1(a) = 1 - S0, which ensures rem = 1 - S0 - m ≥ 0.
steps.code:
have hμ1_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ m1 a := by
    intro a; rw [hm1]; exact sub_nonneg.mpr (min_le_left _ _)
  have hν1_nonneg : ∀ b, 0 ≤ n1 b := by
    intro b; rw [hn1]; exact sub_nonneg.mpr (min_le_right _ _)
  have hsum_m1 : ∑ a, m1 a = 1 - S0 := by
    have h : ∑ a, m1 a = ∑ a, (μ a - min (μ a) (ν a)) := by rw [hm1]
    rw [h, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hμ1, hS0]
  have hsum_n1 : ∑ b, n1 b = 1 - S0 := by
    have h : ∑ b, n1 b = ∑ b, (ν b - min (μ b) (ν b)) := by rw [hn1]
    rw [h, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, hν1, hS0]
  have hm_le_m1 : m ≤ m1 x := by rw [hm_eq]; exact min_le_left _ _
  have hm_le_n1 : m ≤ n1 y := by rw [hm_eq]; exact min_le_right _ _
  have hm_nonneg : 0 ≤ m := by rw [hm_eq]; exact le_min (hμ1_nonneg x) (hν1_nonneg y)
  have hm_le : m ≤ 1 - S0 := by
    calc m ≤ m1 x := hm_le_m1
      _ ≤ ∑ a, m1 a := Finset.single_le_sum (fun a _ => hμ1_nonneg a) (Finset.mem_univ x)
      _ = 1 - S0 := hsum_m1
  have hrem_nonneg : 0 ≤ rem := by rw [hrem]; linarith

steps.claim: The second-stage excess measures μ2 and ν2 are non-negative and each sum to rem
steps.explanation: At x, μ2(x) = m1(x) - m ≥ 0 because m ≤ m1(x); for all other vertices, μ2(a) = m1(a) ≥ 0. Symmetrically, ν2 is pointwise non-negative. Summing μ2 over V subtracts m from ∑ m1(a) = 1 - S0, yielding exactly rem, and similarly for ν2.
steps.code:
have hμ2_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ μ2 a := by
    intro a
    simp only [hμ2]
    by_cases h : a = x
    · rw [if_pos h, sub_nonneg]
      rw [h]; exact hm_le_m1
    · rw [if_neg h]; simpa using hμ1_nonneg a
  have hν2_nonneg : ∀ b, 0 ≤ ν2 b := by
    intro b
    simp only [hν2]
    by_cases h : b = y
    · rw [if_pos h, sub_nonneg]
      rw [h]; exact hm_le_n1
    · rw [if_neg h]; simpa using hν1_nonneg b
  have hsum_μ2 : ∑ a, μ2 a = rem := by
    rw [hμ2, hrem, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_ite_eq']
    simp only [Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
    rw [hsum_m1]
  have hsum_ν2 : ∑ b, ν2 b = rem := by
    rw [hν2, hrem, Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.sum_ite_eq']
    simp only [Finset.mem_univ, if_true]
    rw [hsum_n1]

steps.claim: The row and column sums of the independent remainder coupling equal μ2(a) and ν2(b) respectively
steps.explanation: If rem = 0, then since μ2 ≥ 0 and ∑ μ2 = 0, μ2 is identically zero and the sum vanishes. If rem ≠ 0, factoring out μ2(a) / rem gives (μ2(a) / rem) * ∑ ν2(b) = (μ2(a) / rem) * rem = μ2(a). An identical calculation gives column sums equal to ν2(b).
steps.code:
have hcoupl_row : ∀ a, ∑ b, μ2 a * ν2 b / rem = μ2 a := by
    intro a
    by_cases h0 : rem = 0
    · have hz : μ2 a = 0 := by
        have hsum0 : ∑ b, μ2 b = 0 := by rw [hsum_μ2, h0]
        exact (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun b _ => hμ2_nonneg b)).mp hsum0 a (Finset.mem_univ a)
      rw [hz]
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero; intro b _
      rw [h0]; simp
    · rw [← Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.mul_sum, hsum_ν2]
      exact mul_div_cancel_right₀ (μ2 a) h0
  have hcoupl_col : ∀ b, ∑ a, μ2 a * ν2 b / rem = ν2 b := by
    intro b
    by_cases h0 : rem = 0
    · have hz : ν2 b = 0 := by
        have hsum0 : ∑ b, ν2 b = 0 := by rw [hsum_ν2, h0]
        exact (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun b _ => hν2_nonneg b)).mp hsum0 b (Finset.mem_univ b)
      rw [hz]
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero; intro a _
      rw [h0]; simp
    · rw [← Finset.sum_div, ← Finset.sum_mul, hsum_μ2]
      exact mul_div_cancel_left₀ (ν2 b) h0

steps.claim: The transport plan π is non-negative everywhere
steps.explanation: Each of the three terms in π(a, b) is non-negative: min(μ a, ν a) ≥ 0 on the diagonal, m ≥ 0 on (x, y), and the quotient μ2(a) * ν2(b) / rem is non-negative since both numerators and the denominator are non-negative.
steps.code:
have hπ_nonneg : ∀ a b, 0 ≤ π a b := by
    intro a b
    have h1 : (0:ℝ) ≤ (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0) := by
      by_cases h : a = b
      · rw [if_pos h]; exact le_min (hμ a) (hν a)
      · rw [if_neg h]
    have h2 : (0:ℝ) ≤ (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) := by
      by_cases hby : b = y
      · rw [if_pos hby]
        by_cases hax : a = x
        · rw [if_pos hax]; exact hm_nonneg
        · rw [if_neg hax]
      · rw [if_neg hby]
    have h3 : (0:ℝ) ≤ μ2 a * ν2 b / rem :=
      div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (hμ2_nonneg a) (hν2_nonneg b)) hrem_nonneg
    simp only [hπ]
    linarith

steps.claim: The transport plan π has marginals μ and ν
steps.explanation: Summing π(a, b) over b yields min(μ a, ν a) from the diagonal, m * 1_{a=x} from the edge term, and μ2(a) = m1(a) - m * 1_{a=x} from the product coupling. These add up to min(μ a, ν a) + m1(a) = μ(a). Symmetrically, summing over a yields ν(b).
steps.code:
have hrow : ∀ a, ∑ b, π a b = μ a := by
    intro a
    simp only [hπ]
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    have hdiag : ∑ b, (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0) = min (μ a) (ν a) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq]; simp
    have hmxy : ∑ b, (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) = (if a = x then m else 0) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq']; simp
    rw [hdiag, hmxy, hcoupl_row a]
    simp only [hμ2, hm1]
    ring
  have hcol : ∀ b, ∑ a, π a b = ν b := by
    intro b
    simp only [hπ]
    rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    have hdiag : ∑ a, (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0) = min (μ b) (ν b) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq']; simp
    have hmxy : ∑ a, (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) = (if b = y then m else 0) := by
      by_cases hby : b = y
      · simp [hby, Finset.sum_ite_eq']
      · simp [hby]
    rw [hdiag, hmxy, hcoupl_col b]
    simp only [hν2, hn1]
    ring

steps.claim: The expected transport cost of π is at most 2 - 2 * S0 - m
steps.explanation: Split the transport cost into the three stages: the diagonal terms incur distance d(a, a) = 0, contributing 0; the edge term transfers mass m across d(x, y) = 1, contributing 1 * m = m; and every remaining pair has distance d(a, b) ≤ 2 by the diameter bound, so the product coupling contributes at most 2 * rem. The total cost is at most 0 + m + 2 * rem = m + 2 * (1 - S0 - m) = 2 - 2 * S0 - m.
steps.code:
have hcost : ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * π a b ≤ 2 - 2 * S0 - m := by
    have hsplit : ∀ a b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * π a b
        = (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0)
          + (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0)
          + (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) := by
      intro a b; simp only [hπ]; ring
    have hD : ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0) = 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro a _
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro b _
      by_cases h : a = b
      · rw [if_pos h]
        have hd : (G.dist a b : ℝ) = 0 := by rw [h]; simp
        rw [hd, zero_mul]
      · rw [if_neg h, mul_zero]
    have hM : ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0) = m := by
      have inner : ∀ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0)
            = (G.dist a y : ℝ) * (if a = x then m else 0) := by
        intro a
        simp only [mul_ite, mul_zero]
        rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq']; simp
      simp only [inner]
      have inner2 : ∑ a, (G.dist a y : ℝ) * (if a = x then m else 0) = (G.dist x y : ℝ) * m := by
        simp only [mul_ite, mul_zero]
        rw [Finset.sum_ite_eq']; simp
      rw [inner2, hxy_dist]; ring
    have hC : ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) ≤ 2 * rem := by
      by_cases h0 : rem = 0
      · have hz : ∀ a b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) = 0 := by
          intro a b; rw [h0]; simp
        simp only [hz]
        simp [h0]
      · have hle : ∀ a b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) ≤ 2 * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) := by
          intro a b
          have ht : 0 ≤ μ2 a * ν2 b / rem := div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (hμ2_nonneg a) (hν2_nonneg b)) hrem_nonneg
          exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hdist2 a b) ht
        calc ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem)
            ≤ ∑ a, ∑ b, 2 * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) := by
              apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro a _
              apply Finset.sum_le_sum; intro b _
              exact hle a b
          _ = 2 * rem := by
              have inner : ∀ a, ∑ b, 2 * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem) = 2 * μ2 a := by
                intro a; rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hcoupl_row a]
              simp only [inner]
              rw [← Finset.mul_sum, hsum_μ2]
    calc ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * π a b
        = (∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if a = b then min (μ a) (ν a) else 0))
          + (∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (if b = y then (if a = x then m else 0) else 0))
          + (∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem)) := by
            simp only [hsplit, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
      _ = 0 + m + (∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * (μ2 a * ν2 b / rem)) := by rw [hD, hM]
      _ ≤ 0 + m + 2 * rem := by linarith
      _ = 2 - 2 * S0 - m := by rw [hrem]; ring

steps.claim: The Wasserstein distance is bounded by 2 - 2 * S0 - m
steps.explanation: Because π is a valid coupling between μ and ν with non-negative entries and correct marginals, the Wasserstein distance, which is the infimum over all transport plans, is bounded by the transport cost of π, which is at most 2 - 2 * S0 - m.
steps.code:
calc graph_wasserstein_dist G μ ν ≤ ∑ a, ∑ b, (G.dist a b : ℝ) * π a b :=
        graph_wasserstein_dist_le_of_plan G μ ν π hπ_nonneg hrow hcol
    _ ≤ 2 - 2 * S0 - m := hcost

glossary.sub_nonneg.mpr: if b ≤ a, then 0 ≤ a - b
glossary.min_le_left: the minimum min(a, b) is at most a
glossary.min_le_right: the minimum min(a, b) is at most b
glossary.Finset.sum_sub_distrib: a sum of differences distributes into the difference of the sums: ∑ (f x - g x) = ∑ f x - ∑ g x
glossary.le_min: if c ≤ a and c ≤ b, then c ≤ min(a, b)
glossary.Finset.single_le_sum: a single term f(a) is at most the sum ∑ x ∈ s, f(x) over a finite set containing a, provided all terms are non-negative
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finset Finset.univ
glossary.if_pos: if a condition c holds, then (if c then t else e) = t
glossary.sub_nonneg: 0 ≤ a - b if and only if b ≤ a
glossary.if_neg: if a condition c does not hold, then (if c then t else e) = e

glossary.Finset.sum_div: division by a scalar distributes over finite sums: (∑ f i) / a = ∑ (f i / a)
glossary.Finset.mul_sum: multiplication by a scalar distributes over finite sums: a * ∑ f i = ∑ (a * f i)

glossary.Finset.sum_mul: multiplication on the right distributes over finite sums: (∑ f i) * a = ∑ (f i * a)

glossary.Finset.sum_ite_eq: the sum over s of (if a = x then b(x) else 0) is b(a) if a ∈ s, and 0 otherwise

glossary.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right: if b ≤ c and 0 ≤ a, then b * a ≤ c * a

declarations.name: graph_dist_le_two_of_ediam_le_two
declarations.informal: If the extended diameter of a graph is at most 2, then every (natural-valued) distance is at most 2.
declarations.statement:
theorem graph_dist_le_two_of_ediam_le_two {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (hdiam : G.ediam ≤ 2) (u v : V) : G.dist u v ≤ 2
declarations.source:
/-- Diameter at most 2 gives all distances at most 2. -/
theorem graph_dist_le_two_of_ediam_le_two {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V)
    (hdiam : G.ediam ≤ 2) (u v : V) : G.dist u v ≤ 2 := by
  have htop : G.ediam ≠ ⊤ := by
    intro h; rw [h] at hdiam; simp at hdiam
  have h2 : G.diam ≤ 2 := by
    have := ENat.toNat_le_toNat hdiam (by simp : (2 : ℕ∞) ≠ ⊤)
    simpa [SimpleGraph.diam] using this
  have := SimpleGraph.dist_le_diam htop (u := u) (v := v)
  omega

explanation.summary: To show that every pairwise distance is at most 2, the proof first deduces that the extended diameter G.ediam is finite (not ⊤) from the hypothesis G.ediam ≤ 2. It then projects this bound from the extended natural numbers ℕ∞ to the natural numbers ℕ to show that G.diam ≤ 2. Finally, because the extended diameter is finite, every vertex-to-vertex distance is bounded by G.diam, which yields G.dist u v ≤ 2.

steps.claim: G.ediam ≠ ⊤
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that G.ediam = ⊤. Rewriting with this assumption in G.ediam ≤ 2 gives ⊤ ≤ 2, which simplifies to False since infinity is strictly greater than 2.
steps.code:
have htop : G.ediam ≠ ⊤ := by
    intro h; rw [h] at hdiam; simp at hdiam

steps.claim: G.diam ≤ 2
steps.explanation: Since G.ediam ≤ 2 and 2 ≠ ⊤ in ℕ∞, applying `ENat.toNat_le_toNat` yields G.ediam.toNat ≤ 2. Unfolding the definition of diameter (`SimpleGraph.diam`), which defines G.diam as G.ediam.toNat, simplifies this to G.diam ≤ 2.
steps.code:
have h2 : G.diam ≤ 2 := by
    have := ENat.toNat_le_toNat hdiam (by simp : (2 : ℕ∞) ≠ ⊤)
    simpa [SimpleGraph.diam] using this

steps.claim: G.dist u v ≤ 2
steps.explanation: Because G.ediam ≠ ⊤, the distance between any two vertices u and v is at most the graph diameter (`SimpleGraph.dist_le_diam`), giving G.dist u v ≤ G.diam. Combining this with G.diam ≤ 2 via linear integer arithmetic (`omega`) finishes the proof.
steps.code:
have := SimpleGraph.dist_le_diam htop (u := u) (v := v)
  omega

glossary.ENat.toNat_le_toNat: For extended natural numbers m, n ∈ ℕ∞, if m ≤ n and n ≠ ⊤, then their projections to ℕ satisfy m.toNat ≤ n.toNat.
glossary.SimpleGraph.diam: The diameter of a simple graph as a natural number, defined as the projection of its extended diameter G.ediam from ℕ∞ to ℕ.
glossary.SimpleGraph.dist_le_diam: In a simple graph with finite extended diameter (G.ediam ≠ ⊤), the distance between any two vertices u and v is at most the graph diameter G.diam.

caveats: In Mathlib, distances and diameters come in two flavours: extended values in `ℕ∞` (`ediam`, `edist`) and natural values in `ℕ` (`diam`, `dist`). By convention, if a graph is disconnected, `ediam = ⊤` while `diam = 0`. As a result, the lemma `SimpleGraph.dist_le_diam` requires the hypothesis `G.ediam ≠ ⊤` to prevent counterexamples, which is why lines 4–5 explicitly prove finiteness.

declarations.name: graph_edge_vertex_partition
declarations.informal: For an edge xy of a finite simple graph, the vertex set splits into the x-private neighbours A of x, the y-private neighbours B of y, the common neighbours C, the remaining vertices P, together with x and y themselves.
declarations.statement:
theorem graph_edge_vertex_partition {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (x y : V) (hxy : G.Adj x y) :
    ∃ (A B C P : Finset V),
      (∀ v, v ∈ A ↔ (G.Adj x v ∧ ¬ G.Adj y v ∧ v ≠ y)) ∧
      (∀ v, v ∈ B ↔ (G.Adj y v ∧ ¬ G.Adj x v ∧ v ≠ x)) ∧
      (∀ v, v ∈ C ↔ (G.Adj x v ∧ G.Adj y v)) ∧
      (∀ v, v ∈ P ↔ (¬ G.Adj x v ∧ ¬ G.Adj y v)) ∧
      (Finset.univ : Finset V) = {x} ∪ {y} ∪ A ∪ B ∪ C ∪ P ∧
      x ∉ A ∧ y ∉ A ∧ x ∉ B ∧ y ∉ B ∧ x ∉ C ∧ y ∉ C ∧ x ∉ P ∧ y ∉ P
declarations.source:
/-- The four-part partition of V induced by an edge xy. -/
theorem graph_edge_vertex_partition {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (x y : V) (hxy : G.Adj x y) :
    ∃ (A B C P : Finset V),
      (∀ v, v ∈ A ↔ (G.Adj x v ∧ ¬ G.Adj y v ∧ v ≠ y)) ∧
      (∀ v, v ∈ B ↔ (G.Adj y v ∧ ¬ G.Adj x v ∧ v ≠ x)) ∧
      (∀ v, v ∈ C ↔ (G.Adj x v ∧ G.Adj y v)) ∧
      (∀ v, v ∈ P ↔ (¬ G.Adj x v ∧ ¬ G.Adj y v)) ∧
      (Finset.univ : Finset V) = {x} ∪ {y} ∪ A ∪ B ∪ C ∪ P ∧
      x ∉ A ∧ y ∉ A ∧ x ∉ B ∧ y ∉ B ∧ x ∉ C ∧ y ∉ C ∧ x ∉ P ∧ y ∉ P := by
  classical
  let A : Finset V := Finset.univ.filter (fun v => G.Adj x v ∧ ¬ G.Adj y v ∧ v ≠ y)
  let B : Finset V := Finset.univ.filter (fun v => G.Adj y v ∧ ¬ G.Adj x v ∧ v ≠ x)
  let C : Finset V := Finset.univ.filter (fun v => G.Adj x v ∧ G.Adj y v)
  let P : Finset V := Finset.univ.filter (fun v => ¬ G.Adj x v ∧ ¬ G.Adj y v)
  refine ⟨A, B, C, P, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro v; simp [A]
  · intro v; simp [B]
  · intro v; simp [C]
  · intro v; simp [P]
  · ext v
    simp only [Finset.mem_univ, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_singleton, A, B, C, P,
      Finset.mem_filter, true_and]
    by_cases hx : G.Adj x v <;> by_cases hy : G.Adj y v <;> by_cases hvx : v = x <;> by_cases hvy : v = y <;> simp_all
  · simp [A, B, C, P, hxy, hxy.symm, SimpleGraph.irrefl]

explanation.summary: The proof explicitly constructs the four sets A, B, C, and P by filtering the vertex set V according to adjacency to x and y. Their membership equivalences hold by definition. The theorem then shows that these sets together with {x} and {y} cover all vertices by exhaustive case analysis on an arbitrary vertex's adjacency and equality to x and y. Finally, x and y are shown to be disjoint from all four sets using the irreflexivity of simple graphs and the fact that x and y are adjacent.

steps.claim: We define candidate subsets A, B, C, P of V and reduce the goal to proving six subgoals.
steps.explanation: The sets are constructed by filtering the universal finset `Finset.univ` according to the required relations: A contains vertices adjacent to x, not y, and distinct from y; B contains vertices adjacent to y, not x, and distinct from x; C contains common neighbours of x and y; and P contains non-neighbours of both. Supplying these witnesses leaves six obligations: the four membership characterizations, the partition identity, and the non-membership of x and y in all four sets.

steps.claim: Each of the four sets A, B, C, P satisfies its defining membership equivalence.
steps.explanation: For each set, membership of an arbitrary vertex v simplifies directly by definition to the condition defining the filter, since every vertex belongs to the universe.
steps.code:
· intro v; simp [A]
  · intro v; simp [B]
  · intro v; simp [C]
  · intro v; simp [P]

steps.claim: The union {x} ∪ {y} ∪ A ∪ B ∪ C ∪ P equals the entire vertex set.
steps.explanation: By extensionality, we show that every vertex v belongs to this union. Unfolding the definitions of union, singletons, and filtered sets turns the goal into a disjunction. An exhaustive case split on four conditions—whether v is adjacent to x, whether v is adjacent to y, whether v = x, and whether v = y—produces 16 subcases, each of which immediately satisfies one of the disjuncts.
steps.code:
· ext v
    simp only [Finset.mem_univ, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_singleton, A, B, C, P,
      Finset.mem_filter, true_and]
    by_cases hx : G.Adj x v <;> by_cases hy : G.Adj y v <;> by_cases hvx : v = x <;> by_cases hvy : v = y <;> simp_all

steps.claim: Neither x nor y belongs to any of the four sets A, B, C, or P.
steps.explanation: Membership of x or y in A, B, or C would require a self-loop (contradicting `SimpleGraph.irrefl`) or self-inequality (x ≠ x or y ≠ y). Membership of x or y in P would require non-adjacency to both x and y, which directly contradicts the assumption hxy that x and y are adjacent.
steps.code: · simp [A, B, C, P, hxy, hxy.symm, SimpleGraph.irrefl]

glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finset `Finset.univ`.
glossary.Finset.mem_union: An element belongs to the union of two finsets if and only if it belongs to the first or the second.
glossary.Finset.mem_singleton: An element belongs to the singleton set {a} if and only if it equals a.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to `Finset.filter p s` if and only if it belongs to s and satisfies the predicate p.
glossary.true_and: The conjunction `True ∧ p` simplifies to `p`.
glossary.SimpleGraph.irrefl: In a simple graph, adjacency is irreflexive: no vertex is adjacent to itself.
