declarations.name: tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ
declarations.informal: Dimension reduction: any query algorithm finding a fixed point in dimension k + 1 in at most q queries can be simulated in dimension k with at most q queries.
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ (n k q : ℕ)
    (h : tarski_query_complexity_le n (k + 1) q) :
    tarski_query_complexity_le n k q
declarations.source:
def tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree {n k : ℕ} :
    TarskiQueryTree n (k + 1) → TarskiQueryTree n k
  | .output z => .output (fun i => z (Fin.castSucc i))
  | .query z next =>
    .query (fun i => z (Fin.castSucc i))
      (fun y => tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree (next (Fin.snoc y (z (Fin.last k)))))

def tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map {n k : ℕ} (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) :
    (Fin (k + 1) → Fin n) → (Fin (k + 1) → Fin n) :=
  fun z => Fin.snoc (f (fun i => z (Fin.castSucc i))) (z (Fin.last k))

theorem tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map_mono {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (hf : Monotone f) :
    Monotone (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f) := by
  intro x y hxy i
  induction i using Fin.lastCases with
  | last =>
    simp only [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map, Fin.snoc_last]
    exact hxy (Fin.last k)
  | cast i =>
    simp only [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map, Fin.snoc_castSucc]
    exact hf (fun j => hxy (Fin.castSucc j)) i

theorem tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree_run {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (t : TarskiQueryTree n (k + 1)) :
    (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree t).run f =
      fun i => (t.run (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f)) (Fin.castSucc i) := by
  induction t with
  | output z =>
    rfl
  | query z next ih =>
    simp only [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree, TarskiQueryTree.run]
    have hlift : Fin.snoc (f (fun i => z (Fin.castSucc i))) (z (Fin.last k)) =
        tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f z := rfl
    rw [hlift]
    exact ih (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f z)

theorem tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree_cost {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (t : TarskiQueryTree n (k + 1)) :
    (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree t).cost f =
      t.cost (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f) := by
  induction t with
  | output z =>
    rfl
  | query z next ih =>
    simp only [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree, TarskiQueryTree.cost]
    have hlift : Fin.snoc (f (fun i => z (Fin.castSucc i))) (z (Fin.last k)) =
        tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f z := rfl
    rw [hlift]
    rw [ih (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f z)]

theorem tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree_fixed {n k : ℕ}
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (t : TarskiQueryTree n (k + 1))
    (hfix : tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f
        (t.run (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f)) =
      t.run (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f)) :
    f ((tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree t).run f) =
      (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree t).run f := by
  have hrun := tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree_run f t
  rw [hrun]
  apply funext
  intro i
  have h := congr_fun hfix (Fin.castSucc i)
  dsimp [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map] at h
  rw [Fin.snoc_castSucc] at h
  exact h

/-- Dimension reduction: any query algorithm finding a fixed point in dimension k + 1 in at most q queries can be simulated in dimension k with at most q queries. -/
theorem tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ (n k q : ℕ)
    (h : tarski_query_complexity_le n (k + 1) q) :
    tarski_query_complexity_le n k q := by
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := h
  refine ⟨tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree t, fun f hf => ?_⟩
  have hmono := tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map_mono f hf
  obtain ⟨hfix, hcost⟩ := ht (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f) hmono
  refine ⟨tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree_fixed f t hfix, ?_⟩
  rw [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree_cost]
  exact hcost

explanation.summary: To simulate a (k + 1)-dimensional query algorithm for Tarski's fixed point theorem in dimension k with at most q queries, we construct an embedded query tree that restricts all queries to the first k coordinates and keeps the last coordinate fixed. Given any monotone function f on (Fin n)^k, we lift it to a monotone function on (Fin n)^(k + 1) by applying f on the first k coordinates and acting as the identity on the last coordinate. The original (k + 1)-dimensional tree finds a fixed point of this lifted map in at most q queries, and the embedded tree faithfully traces this execution, outputting a fixed point of f within the same query bound.

steps.claim: The lifted map is monotone at the last coordinate.
steps.explanation: Let x ≤ y in (Fin n)^(k + 1). We decompose coordinate index i using Fin.lastCases. When i is the last coordinate Fin.last k, the definition of the lifted map leaves the last coordinate unchanged via Fin.snoc_last, so the inequality simplifies to x(last) ≤ y(last), which holds by x ≤ y.
steps.code:
intro x y hxy i
  induction i using Fin.lastCases with
  | last =>
    simp only [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map, Fin.snoc_last]
    exact hxy (Fin.last k)

steps.claim: The lifted map is monotone at the first k coordinates, and therefore monotone overall.
steps.explanation: When i = Fin.castSucc j for some j ∈ Fin k, simplifying with Fin.snoc_castSucc shows that the i-th coordinate is (f(x|_{1..k}))_j and (f(y|_{1..k}))_j. Since x ≤ y implies x|_{1..k} ≤ y|_{1..k}, the inequality follows directly from the assumption that f is monotone.
steps.code:
| cast i =>
    simp only [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map, Fin.snoc_castSucc]
    exact hf (fun j => hxy (Fin.castSucc j)) i

steps.claim: For an output leaf, running the embedded tree produces the projection of the original output onto the first k coordinates.
steps.explanation: By structural induction on the tree t, if t is an output leaf output z, both sides are definitionally equal to the restriction of z to the first k coordinates.
steps.code:
induction t with
  | output z =>
    rfl

steps.claim: For a query tree, running the embedded tree on f equals projecting the run of the original tree on the lifted map onto the first k coordinates.
steps.explanation: For a query node querying z with continuation next, the embedded tree queries the first k coordinates of z using f, obtaining f(z|_{1..k}). Appending the unchanged last coordinate z(last) reconstructs the lifted query response. The embedded tree then recurses on the embedding of the next tree, matching the original tree running on the lifted map by the induction hypothesis.
steps.code:
| query z next ih =>
    simp only [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree, TarskiQueryTree.run]
    have hlift : Fin.snoc (f (fun i => z (Fin.castSucc i))) (z (Fin.last k)) =
        tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f z := rfl
    rw [hlift]
    exact ih (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f z)

steps.claim: For an output leaf, the query cost of the embedded tree on f matches that of the original tree on the lifted map.
steps.explanation: In the base case of an output leaf, no queries are made by either tree, so both costs are definitionally zero.
steps.code:
induction t with
  | output z =>
    rfl

steps.claim: For query trees, the query cost of the embedded tree on f equals the cost of the original tree on the lifted map.
steps.explanation: At a query node, each tree expends exactly 1 query at the root and branches to the subtree corresponding to the response of the lifted map. By the induction hypothesis, the recursive costs of the subtrees are equal, hence the total costs match.
steps.code:
| query z next ih =>
    simp only [tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_embed_tree, TarskiQueryTree.cost]
    have hlift : Fin.snoc (f (fun i => z (Fin.castSucc i))) (z (Fin.last k)) =
        tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f z := rfl
    rw [hlift]
    rw [ih (tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ_lift_map f z)]

steps.claim: If the original tree on the lifted map finds a fixed point of that lifted map, the embedded tree on f finds a fixed point of f.
steps.explanation: By the simulation lemma, the embedded tree outputs the first k coordinates of the result of t on the lifted map. By function extensionality, it suffices to check each coordinate i < k. declarations.name: sum_perm_group_symmetrize
declarations.informal: Symmetrization preserves the total mass: the coordinates of x̄ = E_{σ∈G}[σ(x)] sum to the same value as the coordinates of x.
declarations.statement:
theorem sum_perm_group_symmetrize {m : ℕ} (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
    ∑ u, perm_group_symmetrize G x u = ∑ u, x u
declarations.source:
/-- Symmetrization over a permutation group preserves the sum of the coordinates. -/
theorem sum_perm_group_symmetrize {m : ℕ} (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
    ∑ u, perm_group_symmetrize G x u = ∑ u, x u := by
  classical
  simp only [perm_group_symmetrize]
  rw [← Finset.sum_div]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  simp only [Equiv.sum_comp]
  rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
  have hcard : ((Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G)).card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    rw [Nat.cast_ne_zero]
    exact Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr
      ⟨1, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ 1, G.one_mem⟩⟩
  exact mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ hcard

explanation.summary: The proof expands the definition of group symmetrization as an average over G and swaps the order of summation between the coordinates and the group elements. Because every permutation in G acts bijectively on the coordinate indices, re-indexing shows that the sum over coordinates is invariant under each permutation, making the inner sum constant across all |G| elements of the group. Summing this constant yields |G| * ∑_u x(u), and canceling the non-zero factor |G| (which is non-zero because the identity permutation belongs to G) leaves the original sum ∑_u x(u).

steps.claim: Expanding the definition expresses the sum of the symmetrized vector's coordinates as ∑_u ((∑_{σ ∈ G} x(σ⁻¹ u)) / |G|).
steps.explanation: We enable classical logic and unfold `perm_group_symmetrize`, which defines each coordinate u of the symmetrized vector as the average of x(σ⁻¹ u) over all permutations σ in G.

classical
  simp only [perm_group_symmetrize]

steps.claim: The sum over coordinates is rewritten as (∑_{σ ∈ G} ∑_u x(σ⁻¹ u)) / |G|.
steps.explanation: We factor the division by |G| out of the sum over u using `Finset.sum_div`, and then swap the two summations using `Finset.sum_comm` so that the outer sum runs over permutations σ ∈ G and the inner sum runs over coordinates u.
steps.code:
rw [← Finset.sum_div]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]

steps.claim: The inner sum simplifies to ∑_u x(u), and the numerator evaluates to |G| * ∑_u x(u).
steps.explanation: Because each permutation σ⁻¹ is a bijection on the index set, precomposing with it does not change the sum over all coordinates; rewriting with `Equiv.sum_comp` simplifies ∑_u x(σ⁻¹ u) to ∑_u x(u). Since this inner sum no longer depends on σ, summing it over all elements of G gives |G| * ∑_u x(u) via `Finset.sum_const` and `nsmul_eq_mul`.
steps.code:
simp only [Equiv.sum_comp]
  rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]

steps.explanation: By `Nat.cast_ne_zero`, the real cast of |G| is non-zero if and only if |G| is non-zero in ℕ. By `Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr`, this is equivalent to G being nonempty, which is witnessed by the identity permutation 1 belonging to G (`G.one_mem`) and to the universal finset (`Finset.mem_univ`, `Finset.mem_filter.mpr`).

have hcard : ((Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G)).card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    rw [Nat.cast_ne_zero]
    exact Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr
      ⟨1, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ 1, G.one_mem⟩⟩

steps.claim: Canceling |G| yields the original coordinate sum ∑_u x(u).
steps.explanation: With |G| ≠ 0 established, `mul_div_cancel_left₀` cancels |G| from the numerator and denominator of (|G| * ∑_u x(u)) / |G|, leaving ∑_u x(u).
steps.code: exact mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ hcard

glossary.perm_group_symmetrize: The symmetrization of a vector x under a subgroup G of permutations, defined at coordinate u by (1 / |G|) ∑_{σ ∈ G} x(σ⁻¹ u).
glossary.Finset.sum_div: A common divisor can be factored out of a finite sum: (∑_{i ∈ s} f(i)) / a = ∑_{i ∈ s} (f(i) / a).
glossary.Finset.sum_comm: The order of two independent finite summations can be exchanged: ∑_{x ∈ s} ∑_{y ∈ t} f(x, y) = ∑_{y ∈ t} ∑_{x ∈ s} f(x, y).
glossary.Equiv.sum_comp: Summing a function composed with a bijection over the entire finite domain equals summing the function directly: ∑_i g(e(i)) = ∑_i g(i).
glossary.Finset.sum_const: Summing a constant b over a finite set s equals |s| • b.
glossary.nsmul_eq_mul: Natural number scalar multiplication in a ring agrees with multiplication by the natural number cast: n • a = (↑n) * a.
glossary.Nat.cast_ne_zero: The cast of a natural number into a characteristic-zero ring is non-zero if and only if the natural number is non-zero: ↑n ≠ 0 ↔ n ≠ 0.
glossary.Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr: A finite set has non-zero cardinality if it is nonempty.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter.mpr: An element belongs to the filtered finset if it belongs to the ambient finset and satisfies the predicate.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finset Finset.univ.
glossary.G.one_mem: The identity element 1 belongs to any subgroup G.
glossary.mul_div_cancel_left₀: For a non-zero element a ≠ 0, (a * b) / a = b.

declarations.name: multilinear_extension_perm_invariant
declarations.informal: If a set function f is invariant under a permutation σ of the ground set, then its multilinear extension is invariant under the corresponding permutation of the coordinates: F(σ(x)) = F(x).
declarations.statement:
theorem multilinear_extension_perm_invariant {m : ℕ} (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
    (hinv : ∀ S : Finset (Fin m), f (S.map σ.toEmbedding) = f S) (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
    multilinear_extension f (fun u => x (σ⁻¹ u)) = multilinear_extension f x
declarations.source:
/-- The multilinear extension of a permutation-invariant set function is invariant under the coordinate permutation. -/
theorem multilinear_extension_perm_invariant {m : ℕ} (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ)
    (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m))
    (hinv : ∀ S : Finset (Fin m), f (S.map σ.toEmbedding) = f S) (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
    multilinear_extension f (fun u => x (σ⁻¹ u)) = multilinear_extension f x := by
  simp only [multilinear_extension]
  -- Invariance of `f` along `σ⁻¹`, derived from the hypothesis by applying it to `S.map σ⁻¹`.
  have hf : ∀ S : Finset (Fin m), f S = f (S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding) := by
    intro S
    have h := hinv (S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding)
    rwa [show (S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding).map σ.toEmbedding = S from by
      simp [Finset.map_map]] at h
  -- The `S`-product reindexes along `σ⁻¹ : S → S.map σ⁻¹`.
  have hprod : ∀ S : Finset (Fin m),
      ∏ u ∈ S, x (σ⁻¹ u) = ∏ u ∈ S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding, x u := by
    intro S
    refine Finset.prod_bij (fun u _ => σ⁻¹ u) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro u hu; exact Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩
    · intro a _ b _ hab; exact σ.symm.injective hab
    · intro b hb
      obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_map.mp hb
      exact ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    · intro a _; rfl
  -- Same for the complementary product, using `(S.map σ⁻¹)ᶜ = Sᶜ.map σ⁻¹`.
  have hprod' : ∀ S : Finset (Fin m),
      ∏ u ∈ Sᶜ, (1 - x (σ⁻¹ u)) = ∏ u ∈ (S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding)ᶜ, (1 - x u) := by
    intro S
    rw [show (S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding)ᶜ = Sᶜ.map σ.symm.toEmbedding from by ext u; simp]
    refine Finset.prod_bij (fun u _ => σ⁻¹ u) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro u hu; exact Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩
    · intro a _ b _ hab; exact σ.symm.injective hab
    · intro b hb
      obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_map.mp hb
      exact ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    · intro a _; rfl
  -- Finally reindex the whole sum over the bijection `S ↦ S.map σ⁻¹` of `Finset (Fin m)`.
  refine Finset.sum_bij' (fun S _ => S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding) (fun T _ => T.map σ.toEmbedding)
    ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro a _; simp
  · intro a _; simp
  · intro a _
    show (a.map σ.symm.toEmbedding).map σ.toEmbedding = a
    simp [Finset.map_map]
  · intro a _
    show (a.map σ.toEmbedding).map σ.symm.toEmbedding = a
    simp [Finset.map_map]
  · intro a _
    rw [hprod a, hprod' a, hf a]

explanation.summary: To show that the multilinear extension F(x) is invariant under the coordinate permutation induced by σ, the proof expands F(x ∘ σ⁻¹) into its defining sum over all subsets S ⊆ Fin m. It first establishes that the set function f is invariant under σ⁻¹ as well as σ. It then reindexes both the product over S and the complementary product over Sᶜ along the bijection u ↦ σ⁻¹(u), transforming each summand at S into the corresponding summand at σ⁻¹(S). Finally, it reindexes the outer sum over the powerset via the bijection S ↦ σ⁻¹(S), proving that F(x ∘ σ⁻¹) = F(x).

steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of multilinear_extension rewrites both sides as sums over all subsets S ⊆ Fin m of the product of f(S), the product of coordinates in S, and the product of (1 - coordinate) for coordinates outside S. For the left-hand side, each coordinate evaluation x(u) is replaced by x(σ⁻¹(u)).

steps.explanation: Applying the invariance hypothesis f(σ(T)) = f(T) to the subset T = σ⁻¹(S) gives f(σ(σ⁻¹(S))) = f(σ⁻¹(S)). Since σ and σ⁻¹ are inverse permutations, the composition σ ∘ σ⁻¹ is the identity embedding on S (via Finset.map_map), simplifying the left side to f(S).

    intro S
    have h := hinv (S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding)
    rwa [show (S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding).map σ.toEmbedding = S from by
      simp [Finset.map_map]] at h

This map carries elements of S into σ⁻¹(S) by Finset.mem_map.mpr, is injective because σ⁻¹ is injective, and is surjective onto σ⁻¹(S) by Finset.mem_map.mp. At each element, the factors x(σ⁻¹(u)) match definitionally.

have hprod : ∀ S : Finset (Fin m),
      ∏ u ∈ S, x (σ⁻¹ u) = ∏ u ∈ S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding, x u := by
    intro S
    refine Finset.prod_bij (fun u _ => σ⁻¹ u) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro u hu; exact Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩
    · intro a _ b _ hab; exact σ.symm.injective hab
    · intro b hb
      obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_map.mp hb
      exact ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    · intro a _; rfl

steps.explanation: Because permutations commute with set complements, (σ⁻¹(S))ᶜ is equal to σ⁻¹(Sᶜ). Reindexing with Finset.prod_bij along u ↦ σ⁻¹(u) from Sᶜ to σ⁻¹(Sᶜ)—using Finset.mem_map.mpr for membership, injectivity of σ⁻¹, and Finset.mem_map.mp for surjectivity—shows the products are equal.

have hprod' : ∀ S : Finset (Fin m),
      ∏ u ∈ Sᶜ, (1 - x (σ⁻¹ u)) = ∏ u ∈ (S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding)ᶜ, (1 - x u) := by
    intro S
    rw [show (S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding)ᶜ = Sᶜ.map σ.symm.toEmbedding from by ext u; simp]
    refine Finset.prod_bij (fun u _ => σ⁻¹ u) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro u hu; exact Finset.mem_map.mpr ⟨u, hu, rfl⟩
    · intro a _ b _ hab; exact σ.symm.injective hab
    · intro b hb
      obtain ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_map.mp hb
      exact ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    · intro a _; rfl

steps.explanation: We reindex the outer sum over the powerset using Finset.sum_bij' with the bijection S ↦ σ⁻¹(S) and its inverse T ↦ σ(T). Both maps preserve the set of all subsets (Finset.univ), and their compositions in both directions yield the identity on subsets via Finset.map_map. Finally, rewriting with the earlier lemmas (hf, hprod, and hprod') shows that for every subset S, the summand for S at x ∘ σ⁻¹ equals the summand for σ⁻¹(S) at x.
steps.code:
refine Finset.sum_bij' (fun S _ => S.map σ.symm.toEmbedding) (fun T _ => T.map σ.toEmbedding)
    ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  · intro a _; simp
  · intro a _; simp
  · intro a _
    show (a.map σ.symm.toEmbedding).map σ.toEmbedding = a
    simp [Finset.map_map]
  · intro a _
    show (a.map σ.toEmbedding).map σ.symm.toEmbedding = a
    simp [Finset.map_map]
  · intro a _
    rw [hprod a, hprod' a, hf a]

glossary.Finset.map_map: Applying an embedding f and then an embedding g to a finite set is the same as mapping it along their composition g ∘ f.
glossary.Finset.prod_bij: Two finite products are equal if there is a bijection between their index sets that preserves the value of each factor.
glossary.Finset.mem_map.mpr: If an element is the image of some element in a finite set s under f, it belongs to Finset.map f s.
glossary.Finset.mem_map.mp: If an element belongs to Finset.map f s, then it is the image of some element in s under f.
glossary.Finset.sum_bij': Two finite sums are equal if there are mutually inverse maps between their index sets that preserve the value of each term.

declarations.name: perm_group_symmetrize_idempotent
declarations.informal: Symmetrization is idempotent: symmetrizing twice is the same as symmetrizing once, i.e. x̄ is fixed by every element of G.
declarations.statement:
theorem perm_group_symmetrize_idempotent {m : ℕ} (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
    perm_group_symmetrize G (perm_group_symmetrize G x) = perm_group_symmetrize G x
declarations.source:
/-- The group average of a group average is the group average: symmetrization is idempotent. -/
theorem perm_group_symmetrize_idempotent {m : ℕ} (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (x : Fin m → ℝ) :
    perm_group_symmetrize G (perm_group_symmetrize G x) = perm_group_symmetrize G x := by
  classical
  have hinv : ∀ {σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m)} (hσ : σ ∈ G) (u : Fin m),
      perm_group_symmetrize G x (σ⁻¹ u) = perm_group_symmetrize G x u := by
    intro σ hσ u
    unfold perm_group_symmetrize
    congr 1
    refine Finset.sum_nbij' (fun τ => σ * τ) (fun τ => σ⁻¹ * τ) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro τ hτ
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hτ ⊢
      exact G.mul_mem hσ hτ
    · intro τ hτ
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hτ ⊢
      exact G.mul_mem (G.inv_mem hσ) hτ
    · intro τ _; simp
    · intro τ _; simp
    · intro τ _
      simp [mul_inv_rev, Equiv.Perm.mul_apply]
  funext u
  show (∑ σ ∈ Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G), perm_group_symmetrize G x (σ⁻¹ u)) /
      ((Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G)).card : ℝ) = perm_group_symmetrize G x u
  have h_eq : ∀ σ ∈ Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G),
      perm_group_symmetrize G x (σ⁻¹ u) = perm_group_symmetrize G x u := by
    intro σ hσ
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hσ
    exact hinv hσ u
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl h_eq]
  rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
  have hcard : ((Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G)).card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    rw [Nat.cast_ne_zero]
    exact Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr
      ⟨1, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ 1, G.one_mem⟩⟩
  exact mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ hcard

explanation.summary: The theorem states that averaging a vector over a permutation subgroup G twice yields the same result as averaging once (idempotence). The proof first shows that the symmetrized vector x̄ is G-invariant—that is, x̄(σ⁻¹ u) = x̄(u) for every σ ∈ G—by reindexing the sum via the bijection τ ↦ σ * τ. Applying symmetrization a second time therefore averages the constant value x̄(u) over all elements of G. Since the subgroup G contains the identity element, its cardinality is non-zero, allowing |G| to cancel from the numerator and denominator to leave x̄(u).

steps.claim: The symmetrized vector is invariant under the action of any permutation σ ∈ G: for every coordinate u, (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(σ⁻¹ u) = (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(u).
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of symmetrization, both sides are averages over the subgroup G with common denominator |G|, so it suffices to show that their numerators are equal. In the numerator for the shifted vector, each term evaluates x at τ⁻¹ (σ⁻¹ u). Reindexing the sum via Finset.sum_nbij' using the bijection τ ↦ σ * τ (with inverse τ ↦ σ⁻¹ * τ), left-multiplication by σ preserves membership in G (Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, G.mul_mem, G.inv_mem). The summand then transforms into x((σ * τ)⁻¹ u), which matches x(τ⁻¹ (σ⁻¹ u)) by group inverse laws (mul_inv_rev, Equiv.Perm.mul_apply).
steps.code:
classical
  have hinv : ∀ {σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m)} (hσ : σ ∈ G) (u : Fin m),
      perm_group_symmetrize G x (σ⁻¹ u) = perm_group_symmetrize G x u := by
    intro σ hσ u
    unfold perm_group_symmetrize
    congr 1
    refine Finset.sum_nbij' (fun τ => σ * τ) (fun τ => σ⁻¹ * τ) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro τ hτ
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hτ ⊢
      exact G.mul_mem hσ hτ
    · intro τ hτ
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hτ ⊢
      exact G.mul_mem (G.inv_mem hσ) hτ
    · intro τ _; simp
    · intro τ _; simp
    · intro τ _
      simp [mul_inv_rev, Equiv.Perm.mul_apply]

steps.claim: To show idempotence, it suffices to show that for every coordinate u, the group average of the symmetrized vector evaluated at σ⁻¹ u equals the symmetrized vector evaluated at u.
steps.explanation: By function extensionality, two functions on Fin m are equal if they agree at every coordinate u. Unfolding the definition of the outer symmetrization evaluated at u, the goal is to show that the average of (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(σ⁻¹ u) over all σ ∈ G equals (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(u).
steps.code:
funext u
  show (∑ σ ∈ Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G), perm_group_symmetrize G x (σ⁻¹ u)) /
      ((Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G)).card : ℝ) = perm_group_symmetrize G x u

steps.claim: Every term in the outer summation satisfies (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(σ⁻¹ u) = (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(u) for each σ ∈ G.
steps.explanation: For any σ belonging to the subgroup G (unpacked using Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, and true_and), the G-invariance property established in Step 1 shows that (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(σ⁻¹ u) is identical to the constant value (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(u).
steps.code:
have h_eq : ∀ σ ∈ Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G),
      perm_group_symmetrize G x (σ⁻¹ u) = perm_group_symmetrize G x u := by
    intro σ hσ
    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hσ
    exact hinv hσ u

steps.claim: The sum of the symmetrized vector over all σ ∈ G simplifies to |G| * (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(u).
steps.explanation: Rewriting each summand with the equality from Step 3 using Finset.sum_congr, the summation becomes a sum of constant terms. By Finset.sum_const and nsmul_eq_mul, summing a constant over a finite set equals the cardinality of the set multiplied by that constant.
steps.code:
rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl h_eq]
  rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]

steps.claim: The cardinality of the subgroup G, viewed as a real number, is non-zero.
steps.explanation: By Nat.cast_ne_zero, the cast of |G| into ℝ is non-zero if and only if |G| ≠ 0 as a natural number. By Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr, this holds because the set of elements in G is nonempty, containing the identity permutation 1 (G.one_mem, Finset.mem_filter.mpr, Finset.mem_univ).
steps.code:
have hcard : ((Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G)).card : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by
    rw [Nat.cast_ne_zero]
    exact Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr
      ⟨1, Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ 1, G.one_mem⟩⟩

steps.claim: Canceling the factor of |G| completes the proof.
steps.explanation: Since |G| ≠ 0 as established in Step 5, the expression (|G| * (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(u)) / |G| simplifies directly to (perm_group_symmetrize G x)(u) by mul_div_cancel_left₀.
steps.code: exact mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ hcard

glossary.Finset.sum_nbij': Two finite sums are equal if there is a bijection between their index sets such that the summands correspond under the bijection.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finset if and only if it belongs to the base finset and satisfies the filtering predicate.
glossary.Finset.mem_univ: Every element of a finite type belongs to the universal finset `Finset.univ`.
glossary.true_and: The proposition `True ∧ p` simplifies to `p`.
glossary.G.mul_mem: If two elements belong to the subgroup G, their product belongs to G.
glossary.G.inv_mem: If an element belongs to the subgroup G, its inverse belongs to G.
glossary.mul_inv_rev: The inverse of a product in a group is the product of the inverses in reverse order: (a * b)⁻¹ = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹.
glossary.Equiv.Perm.mul_apply: The composition of two permutations applied to an element is given by (f * g) x = f (g x).
glossary.Finset.sum_congr: Two sums over identical finite sets are equal if their summands agree at every element.
glossary.Finset.sum_const: The sum of a constant value over a finite set equals the cardinality of the set scalar-multiplied by that constant.
glossary.nsmul_eq_mul: Natural number scalar multiplication n • a in a semiring equals the cast ↑n multiplied by a.
glossary.Nat.cast_ne_zero: The cast of a natural number into a characteristic-zero semiring (such as ℝ) is non-zero if and only if the natural number is non-zero.
glossary.Finset.card_ne_zero.mpr: If a finite set is nonempty, its cardinality is non-zero.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter.mpr: An element belongs to a filtered finset if it belongs to the base set and satisfies the predicate.

declarations.name: perm_group_symmetrize_mem_matroid_polytope
declarations.informal: For a strongly symmetric instance, symmetrizing a point of the matroid polytope stays inside the matroid polytope.
declarations.statement:
theorem perm_group_symmetrize_mem_matroid_polytope {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (hs : is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f G) {x : Fin m → ℝ}
    (hx : x ∈ matroid_polytope M) :
    perm_group_symmetrize G x ∈ matroid_polytope M
declarations.source:
/-- Under strong symmetry the matroid polytope is invariant under symmetrization. -/
theorem perm_group_symmetrize_mem_matroid_polytope {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (hs : is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f G) {x : Fin m → ℝ}
    (hx : x ∈ matroid_polytope M) :
    perm_group_symmetrize G x ∈ matroid_polytope M := by
  classical
  set V : Set (Fin m → ℝ) := {x | ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), M.Indep ↑S ∧ x = finset_indicator_vec S}
    with hV
  have hact_ind : ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m)) (S : Finset (Fin m)),
      (fun u => finset_indicator_vec S (σ⁻¹ u)) =
        finset_indicator_vec (S.map σ.toEmbedding) := by
    intro σ S; funext u
    simp [finset_indicator_vec, Finset.mem_map_equiv, Equiv.Perm.inv_def]
  have hsymσ : ∀ σ ∈ G, ∀ S : Finset (Fin m),
      perm_group_symmetrize G (finset_indicator_vec (S.map σ.toEmbedding)) =
        perm_group_symmetrize G (finset_indicator_vec S) := by
    intro σ hσ S
    funext u
    unfold perm_group_symmetrize
    congr 1
    rw [← hact_ind]
    refine Finset.sum_nbij' (fun τ => τ * σ) (fun τ => τ * σ⁻¹) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro τ hτ
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hτ ⊢
      exact G.mul_mem hτ hσ
    · intro τ hτ
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hτ ⊢
      exact G.mul_mem hτ (G.inv_mem hσ)
    · intro τ _; simp
    · intro τ _; simp
    · intro τ _; simp [mul_inv_rev, Equiv.Perm.mul_apply]
  have hσV : ∀ σ ∈ G, ∀ y ∈ V, (fun u => y (σ⁻¹ u)) ∈ V := by
    rintro σ hσ _ ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨S.map σ.toEmbedding, ?_, hact_ind σ S⟩
    exact (hs.2 _ _ (hsymσ σ hσ S)).2 hS
  have hσP : ∀ σ ∈ G, ∀ y ∈ matroid_polytope M, (fun u => y (σ⁻¹ u)) ∈ matroid_polytope M := by
    intro σ hσ y hy
    have h1 : (fun u => y (σ⁻¹ u)) ∈ (LinearMap.funLeft ℝ ℝ ⇑σ⁻¹) '' matroid_polytope M :=
      ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
    rw [matroid_polytope, LinearMap.image_convexHull] at h1
    refine convexHull_mono ?_ h1
    rintro _ ⟨z, hz, rfl⟩
    exact hσV σ hσ z hz
  set T := Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G) with hT
  have hcard : (0 : ℝ) < T.card := by
    have : (1 : Equiv.Perm (Fin m)) ∈ T := by simp [hT, G.one_mem]
    exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨_, this⟩
  have heq : perm_group_symmetrize G x =
      ∑ σ ∈ T, (1 / (T.card : ℝ)) • (fun u => x (σ⁻¹ u)) := by
    funext u
    simp only [perm_group_symmetrize, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, hT]
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum, div_eq_inv_mul, one_div]
  rw [heq]
  refine (convex_convexHull ℝ _).sum_mem (fun _ _ => by positivity) ?_ ?_
  · rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]; field_simp
  · intro σ hσ
    exact hσP σ (by simpa [hT] using hσ) x hx

explanation.summary: To show that symmetrizing a point x of the matroid polytope remains in the polytope, the symmetrizer is expressed as a convex combination of coordinate-permuted points x ∘ σ⁻¹ over all σ ∈ G, with uniform weights 1/|G|. Strong symmetry ensures that permuting an independent set by σ ∈ G yields another independent set, which implies that the action of G preserves the vertices of the polytope. Because coordinate permutation is linear, it preserves the entire matroid polytope, and the convexity of the polytope guarantees that the convex combination remains inside.

steps.claim: Define V as the set of indicator vectors of independent sets of M.
steps.explanation: The matroid polytope is defined as the convex hull of V, the vertices corresponding to independent sets of M. Naming V allows us to reason about the polytope by first analyzing its extreme points.

steps.claim: For any permutation σ and subset S, the permuted indicator vector equals the indicator vector of σ(S).
steps.explanation: Evaluating the indicator vector 1_S at σ⁻¹ u yields 1 if and only if σ⁻¹ u ∈ S, which is equivalent to u ∈ σ(S) because σ is a bijection. Thus, permuting coordinates by σ⁻¹ carries 1_S to 1_{σ(S)}.
steps.code:
have hact_ind : ∀ (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m)) (S : Finset (Fin m)),
      (fun u => finset_indicator_vec S (σ⁻¹ u)) =
        finset_indicator_vec (S.map σ.toEmbedding) := by
    intro σ S; funext u
    simp [finset_indicator_vec, Finset.mem_map_equiv, Equiv.Perm.inv_def]

steps.claim: For any permutation σ ∈ G and subset S, symmetrizing 1_{σ(S)} produces the same vector as symmetrizing 1_S.
steps.explanation: Symmetrizing averages the permuted vector over all elements τ ∈ G. Since right multiplication by σ is a bijection of the subgroup G onto itself, reindexing the sum replaces τ with τ σ. The argument of the indicator vector becomes ((τ σ)⁻¹ u) = (σ⁻¹ τ⁻¹ u), which matches the symmetrization of 1_{σ(S)}.
steps.code:
have hsymσ : ∀ σ ∈ G, ∀ S : Finset (Fin m),
      perm_group_symmetrize G (finset_indicator_vec (S.map σ.toEmbedding)) =
        perm_group_symmetrize G (finset_indicator_vec S) := by
    intro σ hσ S
    funext u
    unfold perm_group_symmetrize
    congr 1
    rw [← hact_ind]
    refine Finset.sum_nbij' (fun τ => τ * σ) (fun τ => τ * σ⁻¹) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro τ hτ
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hτ ⊢
      exact G.mul_mem hτ hσ
    · intro τ hτ
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and] at hτ ⊢
      exact G.mul_mem hτ (G.inv_mem hσ)
    · intro τ _; simp
    · intro τ _; simp
    · intro τ _; simp [mul_inv_rev, Equiv.Perm.mul_apply]

steps.claim: Permutation by any σ ∈ G preserves the vertex set V.
steps.explanation: A vertex y ∈ V has the form 1_S for an independent set S. Its permuted vector is 1_{σ(S)}. Since 1_{σ(S)} and 1_S have identical symmetrizations, the strong symmetry hypothesis guarantees that σ(S) is independent if and only if S is independent. Therefore 1_{σ(S)} is also in V.
steps.code:
have hσV : ∀ σ ∈ G, ∀ y ∈ V, (fun u => y (σ⁻¹ u)) ∈ V := by
    rintro σ hσ _ ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨S.map σ.toEmbedding, ?_, hact_ind σ S⟩
    exact (hs.2 _ _ (hsymσ σ hσ S)).2 hS

steps.claim: Permutation by any σ ∈ G maps the matroid polytope into itself.
steps.explanation: Permuting coordinates by σ⁻¹ is a linear map on the function space. A linear map commutes with forming convex hulls, so the image of the matroid polytope conv(V) is conv((· ∘ σ⁻¹)'' V). Since every permuted vertex remains in V, monotonicity of convex hulls implies that the image is contained in conv(V).
steps.code:
have hσP : ∀ σ ∈ G, ∀ y ∈ matroid_polytope M, (fun u => y (σ⁻¹ u)) ∈ matroid_polytope M := by
    intro σ hσ y hy
    have h1 : (fun u => y (σ⁻¹ u)) ∈ (LinearMap.funLeft ℝ ℝ ⇑σ⁻¹) '' matroid_polytope M :=
      ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
    rw [matroid_polytope, LinearMap.image_convexHull] at h1
    refine convexHull_mono ?_ h1
    rintro _ ⟨z, hz, rfl⟩
    exact hσV σ hσ z hz

steps.claim: The finite subgroup G (denoted T) is nonempty and has positive cardinality.
steps.explanation: The group identity 1 belongs to G, so T contains at least one element and its cardinality |T| is strictly positive.
steps.code:
set T := Finset.univ.filter (· ∈ G) with hT
  have hcard : (0 : ℝ) < T.card := by
    have : (1 : Equiv.Perm (Fin m)) ∈ T := by simp [hT, G.one_mem]
    exact_mod_cast Finset.card_pos.2 ⟨_, this⟩

steps.claim: The symmetrizer of x is a convex combination of the permuted vectors x ∘ σ⁻¹ over σ ∈ G with uniform weights 1/|G|.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of perm_group_symmetrize and distributing the division by |T| across the sum expresses the symmetrizer coordinate-wise as the sum of (1 / |T|) • (x ∘ σ⁻¹) over all σ ∈ T.
steps.code:
have heq : perm_group_symmetrize G x =
      ∑ σ ∈ T, (1 / (T.card : ℝ)) • (fun u => x (σ⁻¹ u)) := by
    funext u
    simp only [perm_group_symmetrize, Finset.sum_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, hT]
    rw [← Finset.mul_sum, div_eq_inv_mul, one_div]
  rw [heq]

steps.claim: The symmetrized vector perm_group_symmetrize G x belongs to the matroid polytope.
steps.explanation: The matroid polytope is convex because it is a convex hull. The weights 1/|T| are positive (hence non-negative) and sum to 1 since |T| • (1/|T|) = 1. Because each permuted vector x ∘ σ⁻¹ lies in the matroid polytope, their convex combination must also lie in the matroid polytope.
steps.code:
refine (convex_convexHull ℝ _).sum_mem (fun _ _ => by positivity) ?_ ?_
  · rw [Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]; field_simp
  · intro σ hσ
    exact hσP σ (by simpa [hT] using hσ) x hx

glossary.Finset.mem_map_equiv: an element belongs to the image of a set under an equivalence if and only if its inverse image belongs to the original set
glossary.Equiv.Perm.inv_def: the group inverse of a permutation is equal to its inverse equivalence
glossary.Finset.sum_nbij': a sum over a finite set is unchanged by reindexing along a bijection
glossary.mul_inv_rev: the inverse of a product in a group is the product of the inverses in reverse order: (a * b)⁻¹ = b⁻¹ * a⁻¹
glossary.Equiv.Perm.mul_apply: composition of permutations evaluates from right to left: (f * g) x = f (g x)
glossary.LinearMap.image_convexHull: the image of a convex hull under a linear map is the convex hull of the image
glossary.convexHull_mono: the convex hull operation preserves set inclusion: if s ⊆ t, then conv(s) ⊆ conv(t)
glossary.Finset.card_pos.2: a finite set has positive cardinality if it is nonempty
glossary.Finset.sum_apply: evaluating a sum of functions at a point equals the sum of their values at that point
glossary.Pi.smul_apply: scalar multiplication on a function space is defined pointwise: (a • f) i = a • (f i)
glossary.smul_eq_mul: scalar multiplication in a ring by a scalar on itself is ring multiplication: a • b = a * b
glossary.Finset.mul_sum: multiplication distributes over finite sums: a * ∑ i, f i = ∑ i, a * f i
glossary.div_eq_inv_mul: division is multiplication by the reciprocal: a / b = b⁻¹ * a
glossary.one_div: the reciprocal 1 / a equals the inverse a⁻¹
glossary.convex_convexHull: the convex hull of any set is convex
glossary.Finset.sum_const: the sum of a constant value b over a finite set s is equal to |s| • b
glossary.nsmul_eq_mul: natural number scalar multiplication is multiplication by the coerced natural: n • a = n * a

declarations.name: sSup_indep_le_sSup_multilinear_extension
declarations.informal: The best integral value max{f(S) : S independent in M} is at most the best fractional value max_{x∈P(M)} F(x), because every independent set is a vertex of the matroid polytope.
declarations.statement:
theorem sSup_indep_le_sSup_multilinear_extension {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) :
    sSup (f '' {S : Finset (Fin m) | M.Indep ↑S})
      ≤ sSup (multilinear_extension f '' matroid_polytope M)
declarations.source:
/-- The integral optimum is at most the fractional optimum over the matroid polytope. -/
theorem sSup_indep_le_sSup_multilinear_extension {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) :
    sSup (f '' {S : Finset (Fin m) | M.Indep ↑S})
      ≤ sSup (multilinear_extension f '' matroid_polytope M) := by
  classical
  set V : Set (Fin m → ℝ) := {x | ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), M.Indep ↑S ∧ x = finset_indicator_vec S}
    with hV
  have hVfin : V.Finite :=
    (Set.finite_range (fun S : Finset (Fin m) => finset_indicator_vec S)).subset
      (by rintro x ⟨S, -, rfl⟩; exact ⟨S, rfl⟩)
  have hPc : IsCompact (matroid_polytope M) := hVfin.isCompact_convexHull (𝕜 := ℝ)
  have hF : Continuous (multilinear_extension f) := by
    unfold multilinear_extension; fun_prop
  have hbdd : BddAbove (multilinear_extension f '' matroid_polytope M) :=
    (hPc.image hF).bddAbove
  have hne : (f '' {S : Finset (Fin m) | M.Indep ↑S}).Nonempty := by
    refine ⟨f ∅, ∅, ?_, rfl⟩
    simp [M.empty_indep]
  refine csSup_le hne ?_
  rintro _ ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩
  rw [← multilinear_extension_indicator f S]
  refine le_csSup hbdd ?_
  refine ⟨finset_indicator_vec S, ?_, rfl⟩
  exact subset_convexHull ℝ _ ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩

explanation.summary: To show that the supremum of a set function f over the independent sets of a matroid M is at most the supremum of its multilinear extension F over the matroid polytope P(M), the proof bounds each value f(S) individually by the fractional supremum. For any independent set S, its indicator vector 1_S lies in the matroid polytope P(M) and satisfies F(1_S) = f(S). Because P(M) is the convex hull of finitely many indicator vectors, it is compact, and since F is a polynomial and thus continuous, the image F(P(M)) is bounded above. Finally, because the empty set is independent, the collection of independent values is nonempty, so the pointwise bound implies the bound on the supremum.

steps.claim: The matroid polytope P(M) is compact.
steps.explanation: Define V as the set of indicator vectors of all independent sets in M. Since the ground set has only finitely many subsets, the range of the indicator map is finite by `Set.finite_range`, so its subset V is finite. By definition, the matroid polytope P(M) is the convex hull of V. The convex hull of any finite subset in ℝᵐ is compact by `isCompact_convexHull`.
steps.code:
classical
  set V : Set (Fin m → ℝ) := {x | ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), M.Indep ↑S ∧ x = finset_indicator_vec S}
    with hV
  have hVfin : V.Finite :=
    (Set.finite_range (fun S : Finset (Fin m) => finset_indicator_vec S)).subset
      (by rintro x ⟨S, -, rfl⟩; exact ⟨S, rfl⟩)
  have hPc : IsCompact (matroid_polytope M) := hVfin.isCompact_convexHull (𝕜 := ℝ)

steps.claim: The multilinear extension of f is continuous.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition shows that the multilinear extension F(x) = ∑_S f(S) (∏_{u ∈ S} x_u) (∏_{u ∉ S} (1 - x_u)) is a multilinear polynomial in the coordinates of x. Lean's `fun_prop` tactic proves continuity automatically from this structure.
steps.code:
have hF : Continuous (multilinear_extension f) := by
    unfold multilinear_extension; fun_prop

steps.claim: The image of the matroid polytope under the multilinear extension is bounded above.
steps.explanation: Because the matroid polytope is compact and the multilinear extension is continuous, the image F(P(M)) is compact. Any compact subset of ℝ is bounded above.
steps.code:
have hbdd : BddAbove (multilinear_extension f '' matroid_polytope M) :=
    (hPc.image hF).bddAbove

steps.claim: The set of values of f on independent sets is nonempty.
steps.explanation: The empty set ∅ is independent in M by `M.empty_indep`, so f(∅) belongs to the set of independent values, witnessing that it is nonempty.
steps.code:
have hne : (f '' {S : Finset (Fin m) | M.Indep ↑S}).Nonempty := by
    refine ⟨f ∅, ∅, ?_, rfl⟩
    simp [M.empty_indep]

steps.claim: To bound the supremum over independent sets, it suffices to show that f(S) ≤ sup F(P(M)) for each independent set S.
steps.explanation: By `csSup_le`, since the set of values on independent sets is nonempty, its supremum is at most sup F(P(M)) as long as every element f(S) for S independent satisfies f(S) ≤ sup F(P(M)).
steps.code: refine csSup_le hne ?_

steps.claim: For every independent set S, f(S) ≤ sup F(P(M)).
steps.explanation: Let S be an independent set. By `multilinear_extension_indicator`, f(S) equals the multilinear extension evaluated at the indicator vector 1_S. Since S is independent, 1_S belongs to the vertex set V, which is contained in the matroid polytope P(M) by `subset_convexHull`. Since F(P(M)) is bounded above, F(1_S) ≤ sup F(P(M)) follows by `le_csSup`.
steps.code:
rintro _ ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩
  rw [← multilinear_extension_indicator f S]
  refine le_csSup hbdd ?_
  refine ⟨finset_indicator_vec S, ?_, rfl⟩
  exact subset_convexHull ℝ _ ⟨S, hS, rfl⟩

glossary.Set.finite_range: The range of a function defined on a finite domain is a finite set.
glossary.isCompact_convexHull: The convex hull of a finite subset of a topological real vector space is compact.
glossary.M.empty_indep: The empty set is an independent set in the matroid M.
glossary.csSup_le: If a nonempty set s in a conditionally complete lattice has an upper bound a (every element of s is at most a), then the supremum of s is at most a.
glossary.multilinear_extension_indicator: Evaluating the multilinear extension of f at the indicator vector of a finite set S yields f(S).
glossary.le_csSup: In a conditionally complete lattice, any element of a set bounded above is at most the supremum of that set.
glossary.subset_convexHull: Every set is contained in its convex hull.

caveats: The continuity of the multilinear extension (lines 13–14) is proved automatically by the `fun_prop` tactic from its polynomial definition (a finite sum of finite products of coordinates).

declarations.name: is_strongly_symmetric_instance_bot
declarations.informal: Every matroid together with any set function is a strongly symmetric instance for the trivial permutation group: a witness that the definition of strong symmetry is inhabited (non-vacuity).
declarations.statement:
theorem is_strongly_symmetric_instance_bot {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) :
    is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f ⊥
declarations.source:
/-- Non-vacuity witness: with the trivial group, every (M, f) is a strongly symmetric instance. -/
theorem is_strongly_symmetric_instance_bot {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) :
    is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f ⊥ := by
  classical
  have hsym : ∀ (y : Fin m → ℝ),
      perm_group_symmetrize (⊥ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m))) y = y := by
    intro y
    funext u
    have h1 : (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Equiv.Perm (Fin m) =>
        x ∈ (⊥ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m))))) = {1} := by
      ext x; simp [Subgroup.mem_bot]
    rw [perm_group_symmetrize, h1, Finset.sum_singleton, Finset.card_singleton,
      Nat.cast_one, div_one]
    simp
  have hmap : ∀ (S : Finset (Fin m)),
      Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding (1 : Equiv.Perm (Fin m))) S = S := by
    intro S
    ext x
    simp only [Finset.mem_map, Equiv.coe_toEmbedding, Equiv.Perm.one_apply]
    simp
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · intro σ hσ S
    rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hσ
    subst hσ
    rw [hmap]
  · intro S S' h
    rw [hsym, hsym] at h
    have hSS : S = S' := by
      ext u
      have h2 := congrFun h u
      simp only [finset_indicator_vec] at h2
      constructor <;> intro hu
      · by_contra h1
        simp [h1] at h2
        simp [hu] at h2
      · by_contra h1
        simp [h1] at h2
        simp [hu] at h2
    simp [hSS]

explanation.summary: The theorem establishes that any matroid M and set function f form a strongly symmetric instance under the trivial permutation group ⊥ = {1}. Because ⊥ contains only the identity permutation, group symmetrization is simply the identity operator on vectors, and the action on sets is trivial. Therefore, f is trivially invariant, and any two sets with equal symmetrized indicator vectors are identical, trivially preserving matroid independence.

steps.claim: Symmetrization by the trivial permutation group is the identity operator on vectors.
steps.explanation: For any vector y and element u, the set of group elements in the trivial subgroup ⊥ is just the singleton {1} by Subgroup.mem_bot. By definition, perm_group_symmetrize computes the average of y(σ⁻¹ u) over σ in the subgroup. Using Finset.sum_singleton, Finset.card_singleton, Nat.cast_one, and div_one, this average simplifies to y(1⁻¹ u), which is just y u.
steps.code:
classical
  have hsym : ∀ (y : Fin m → ℝ),
      perm_group_symmetrize (⊥ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m))) y = y := by
    intro y
    funext u
    have h1 : (Finset.univ.filter (fun x : Equiv.Perm (Fin m) =>
        x ∈ (⊥ : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m))))) = {1} := by
      ext x; simp [Subgroup.mem_bot]
    rw [perm_group_symmetrize, h1, Finset.sum_singleton, Finset.card_singleton,
      Nat.cast_one, div_one]
    simp

steps.claim: The identity permutation fixes every finset under Finset.map.
steps.explanation: By extensionality and the characterization of Finset.map (Finset.mem_map, Equiv.coe_toEmbedding, and Equiv.Perm.one_apply), an element x is in the image of S under the identity permutation if and only if x = a for some a ∈ S, which means x ∈ S.
steps.code:
have hmap : ∀ (S : Finset (Fin m)),
      Finset.map (Equiv.toEmbedding (1 : Equiv.Perm (Fin m))) S = S := by
    intro S
    ext x
    simp only [Finset.mem_map, Equiv.coe_toEmbedding, Equiv.Perm.one_apply]
    simp

steps.claim: Decompose the goal into invariance of f and independence preservation.
steps.explanation: By the definition of is_strongly_symmetric_instance, two conditions must be shown: first, f must be invariant under permutations in ⊥; second, finsets with the same symmetrized indicator vector must have equivalent matroid independence.
steps.code: refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: The set function f is invariant under permutations in the trivial group.
steps.explanation: Given σ ∈ ⊥ and a finset S, Subgroup.mem_bot shows σ = 1. Applying the lemma hmap established earlier gives Finset.map 1 S = S, so f(Finset.map σ S) = f S.
steps.code:
· intro σ hσ S
    rw [Subgroup.mem_bot] at hσ
    subst hσ
    rw [hmap]

steps.claim: Having identical symmetrizations implies having identical indicator vectors.
steps.explanation: If the symmetrized indicator vectors of S and S' under ⊥ are equal, rewriting with the fact hsym that symmetrization is the identity reduces the equality directly to finset_indicator_vec S = finset_indicator_vec S'.
steps.code:
· intro S S' h
    rw [hsym, hsym] at h

steps.claim: Equal indicator vectors imply S = S'.
steps.explanation: By extensionality, we show u ∈ S ↔ u ∈ S' for all u. Applying congrFun to the indicator equality at u gives equality of the indicator values. If u were in one set but not the other, the indicator values 1 and 0 would be equal, a contradiction.
steps.code:
have hSS : S = S' := by
      ext u
      have h2 := congrFun h u
      simp only [finset_indicator_vec] at h2
      constructor <;> intro hu
      · by_contra h1
        simp [h1] at h2
        simp [hu] at h2
      · by_contra h1
        simp [h1] at h2
        simp [hu] at h2

steps.claim: Matroid independence is preserved between S and S'.
steps.explanation: Because S = S', the condition M.Indep ↑S ↔ M.Indep ↑S' holds trivially.
steps.code: simp [hSS]

glossary.Subgroup.mem_bot: an element of the trivial subgroup ⊥ is equal to the identity element 1, and conversely
glossary.Finset.sum_singleton: the sum of a function over a singleton set {a} equals the value of the function at a
glossary.Finset.card_singleton: the cardinality of any singleton set {a} is 1
glossary.Nat.cast_one: the natural number 1 coerced into a ring or group with 1 is equal to 1
glossary.div_one: dividing any element by 1 yields the element itself
glossary.Finset.mem_map: an element b belongs to Finset.map f s for an embedding f if and only if b = f a for some a ∈ s
glossary.Equiv.coe_toEmbedding: the embedding induced by an equivalence agrees with the equivalence as a function
glossary.Equiv.Perm.one_apply: the identity permutation leaves every element unchanged (1 x = x)
glossary.congrFun: if two functions are equal, they take the same value at any given argument

declarations.name: symmetrize_image_matroid_polytope_eq_fixed
declarations.informal: For a strongly symmetric instance, the image of the matroid polytope under symmetrization is exactly the set of points of the polytope fixed by every element of G.
declarations.statement:
theorem symmetrize_image_matroid_polytope_eq_fixed {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (hs : is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f G) :
    (fun x => perm_group_symmetrize G x) '' matroid_polytope M
      = matroid_polytope M ∩ {x | perm_group_symmetrize G x = x}
declarations.source:
/-- The symmetrized matroid polytope is exactly the part of the polytope fixed by the group. -/
theorem symmetrize_image_matroid_polytope_eq_fixed {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (hs : is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f G) :
    (fun x => perm_group_symmetrize G x) '' matroid_polytope M
      = matroid_polytope M ∩ {x | perm_group_symmetrize G x = x} := by
  ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_image, Set.mem_inter_iff]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨perm_group_symmetrize_mem_matroid_polytope M f G hs hy, perm_group_symmetrize_idempotent G y⟩
  · rintro ⟨hx, hfix⟩
    exact ⟨x, hx, hfix⟩

explanation.summary: The proof establishes the equality of the two sets by extensionality, splitting the equivalence into two inclusions. For the forward inclusion, symmetrization preserves membership in the matroid polytope for a strongly symmetric instance and is an idempotent operation, so the image of any point in the polytope is both in the polytope and fixed by symmetrization. For the reverse inclusion, any point in the polytope that is already fixed by symmetrization serves as its own preimage under the symmetrization map.

steps.claim: Equality of the two sets reduces to showing mutual inclusion of their elements.
steps.explanation: By set extensionality, two sets are identical if they contain the same elements. Rewriting the membership conditions using the definitions of the image of a set under a function (`Set.mem_image`) and the intersection of two sets (`Set.mem_inter_iff`), we split the required equivalence into two separate implications.
steps.code:
ext x
  simp only [Set.mem_image, Set.mem_inter_iff]
  constructor

steps.claim: Every point in the symmetrized image of the matroid polytope belongs to the polytope and is fixed by symmetrization.
steps.explanation: Let y be a point in the matroid polytope, and consider its symmetrization x = perm_group_symmetrize G y. First, x remains in the matroid polytope by `perm_group_symmetrize_mem_matroid_polytope`, using the hypothesis that the instance is strongly symmetric. Second, x is fixed under symmetrization because group symmetrization is idempotent (`perm_group_symmetrize_idempotent`).
steps.code:
· rintro ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨perm_group_symmetrize_mem_matroid_polytope M f G hs hy, perm_group_symmetrize_idempotent G y⟩

steps.claim: Every point in the matroid polytope that is fixed by symmetrization belongs to the symmetrized image.
steps.explanation: Given a point x in the matroid polytope satisfying perm_group_symmetrize G x = x, x itself provides the required witness in the polytope whose symmetrization equals x.
steps.code:
· rintro ⟨hx, hfix⟩
    exact ⟨x, hx, hfix⟩

glossary.Set.mem_image: An element y is in the image f(s) if and only if there exists x ∈ s such that f(x) = y.
glossary.Set.mem_inter_iff: An element x is in the intersection a ∩ b if and only if x ∈ a and x ∈ b.
glossary.perm_group_symmetrize_mem_matroid_polyto: Group symmetrization preserves membership in the matroid polytope of a strongly symmetric instance.
glossary.perm_group_symmetrize_idempotent: Group symmetrization is idempotent: symmetrizing an already symmetrized point leaves it unchanged.

declarations.name: tarski_query_complexity_dim_le
declarations.informal: General dimension simulation reduction: any query algorithm finding a fixed point in dimension k in at most q queries can be simulated in any lower dimension j ≤ k with at most q queries.
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_query_complexity_dim_le (n j k q : ℕ) (hjk : j ≤ k) (h : tarski_query_complexity_le n k q) :
    tarski_query_complexity_le n j q
declarations.source:
/-- Any query algorithm finding a fixed point in dimension k in at most q queries can be simulated in any dimension j ≤ k with at most q queries. -/
theorem tarski_query_complexity_dim_le (n j k q : ℕ) (hjk : j ≤ k) (h : tarski_query_complexity_le n k q) :
    tarski_query_complexity_le n j q := by
  obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hjk
  induction d with
  | zero => simpa using h
  | succ d ih =>
      have h' : tarski_query_complexity_le n (j + d + 1) q := by
        simpa [Nat.add_assoc] using h
      have h'' : tarski_query_complexity_le n (j + d) q :=
        tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ n (j + d) q h'
      exact ih (Nat.le_add_right j d) h''

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by induction on the difference d = k - j ≥ 0. In the base case d = 0, the dimensions coincide and the claim is trivial. For the inductive step, the dimension is decreased from (j + d) + 1 to j + d using the one-step dimension reduction lemma tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ, and the induction hypothesis then reduces the problem all the way to dimension j.

steps.claim: We can express k as j + d for some natural number d.
steps.explanation: Since j ≤ k (hypothesis hjk), there exists some d such that k = j + d by Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le. We substitute j + d for k throughout.
steps.code: obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hjk

steps.claim: The base case d = 0 holds.
steps.explanation: We argue by induction on the difference d. When d = 0, the dimension j + 0 simplifies to j, so the hypothesis h immediately yields the goal tarski_query_complexity_le n j q.
steps.code:
induction d with
  | zero => simpa using h

steps.claim: The query complexity bound holds in dimension (j + d) + 1.
steps.explanation: In the inductive step d + 1, hypothesis h provides the query bound in dimension j + (d + 1). By associativity of addition (Nat.add_assoc), this is rewritten as dimension (j + d) + 1 to obtain hypothesis h'.
steps.code:
| succ d ih =>
      have h' : tarski_query_complexity_le n (j + d + 1) q := by
        simpa [Nat.add_assoc] using h

steps.claim: The query complexity bound holds in dimension j + d.
steps.explanation: Applying the single-step dimension reduction tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ to h' lowers the dimension from (j + d) + 1 to j + d with the same query bound q, giving hypothesis h''.
steps.code:
have h'' : tarski_query_complexity_le n (j + d) q :=
        tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ n (j + d) q h'

steps.claim: The query complexity bound holds in dimension j.
steps.explanation: Applying the induction hypothesis ih to h'', together with the fact that j ≤ j + d (from Nat.le_add_right), completes the proof.
steps.code: exact ih (Nat.le_add_right j d) h''

glossary.Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le: If m ≤ n, there exists a natural number k such that n = m + k.
glossary.Nat.add_assoc: Addition of natural numbers is associative: (n + m) + k = n + (m + k).
glossary.tarski_query_complexity_dim_le_succ: If the Tarski fixed-point query complexity in dimension k + 1 is at most q, then in dimension k it is also at most q.
glossary.Nat.le_add_right: For any natural numbers n and k, n ≤ n + k.

declarations.name: symmetry_gap_numerator_eq_sSup_fixed
declarations.informal: For a strongly symmetric instance the numerator of the symmetry gap, sup_{x∈P(M)} F(x̄), equals the supremum of F over the points of the matroid polytope that are fixed by the group.
declarations.statement:
theorem symmetry_gap_numerator_eq_sSup_fixed {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (hs : is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f G) :
    sSup ((fun x => multilinear_extension f (perm_group_symmetrize G x)) '' matroid_polytope M)
      = sSup (multilinear_extension f ''
          (matroid_polytope M ∩ {x | perm_group_symmetrize G x = x}))
declarations.source:
/-- The numerator of the symmetry gap is a supremum of F over the fixed polytope P(M) ∩ Fix(G). -/
theorem symmetry_gap_numerator_eq_sSup_fixed {m : ℕ} (M : Matroid (Fin m))
    (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m)))
    (hs : is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f G) :
    sSup ((fun x => multilinear_extension f (perm_group_symmetrize G x)) '' matroid_polytope M)
      = sSup (multilinear_extension f ''
          (matroid_polytope M ∩ {x | perm_group_symmetrize G x = x})) := by
  rw [← Set.image_image, symmetrize_image_matroid_polytope_eq_fixed M f G hs]

explanation.summary: The proof rewrites the set of values taken by the multilinear extension F on symmetrized points x̄ into the image under F of the symmetrized matroid polytope. By a previously established lemma for strongly symmetric instances, the image of the matroid polytope under symmetrization is exactly its fixed-point face, P(M) ∩ Fix(G). Substituting this set equality immediately yields the desired equality of suprema.

steps.claim: The supremum of the multilinear extension F over the symmetrized matroid polytope equals the supremum of F over the group-fixed points of the matroid polytope.
steps.explanation: By `Set.image_image`, the set of values F(x̄) for x in the matroid polytope P(M) is rewritten as the image under F of the symmetrized polytope, F '' (symmetrize '' P(M)). Then, by `symmetrize_image_matroid_polytope_eq_fixed`, strong symmetry implies that the symmetrized matroid polytope is exactly the fixed-point face P(M) ∩ {x | x̄ = x}. Substituting this equality leaves identical expressions on both sides.
steps.code: rw [← Set.image_image, symmetrize_image_matroid_polytope_eq_fixed M f G hs]

glossary.Set.image_image: The image of a set under a composite function g ∘ f equals the image under g of the image under f, that is, (g ∘ f) '' s = g '' (f '' s).
glossary.symmetrize_image_matroid_polytope_eq_fix: For a strongly symmetric instance, the image of the matroid polytope under group symmetrization is its intersection with the set of points fixed by the symmetrization.

declarations.name: tarski_slice_lower_bound
declarations.informal: Monotonicity preservation on coordinate slices: fixing coordinate i to any value m ≥ a_i preserves the lower subinterval invariant a_j ≤ f(a^{(i,m)})_j for all coordinates j.
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_slice_lower_bound (n k : ℕ) (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (hf : Monotone f)
    (a : Fin k → Fin n) (ha : a ≤ f a) (i : Fin k) (m : Fin n) (ham : a i ≤ m) (j : Fin k) :
    a j ≤ f (fun l => if l = i then m else a l) j
declarations.source:
/-- Monotonicity preservation on coordinate slices: increasing coordinate i from a_i to m preserves a ≤ f(a^{(i,m)}). -/
theorem tarski_slice_lower_bound (n k : ℕ) (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (hf : Monotone f)
    (a : Fin k → Fin n) (ha : a ≤ f a) (i : Fin k) (m : Fin n) (ham : a i ≤ m) (j : Fin k) :
    a j ≤ f (fun l => if l = i then m else a l) j := by
  have hle : a ≤ (fun l => if l = i then m else a l) := by
    intro l
    by_cases h : l = i
    · subst h
      simpa using ham
    · simp [h]
  have hmono := hf hle
  exact le_trans (ha j) (hmono j)

explanation.summary: The theorem establishes that if a ≤ f(a) for a monotone function f on the lattice of coordinate vectors, increasing the i-th coordinate from a_i to m ≥ a_i preserves the lower bound a_j ≤ f(a^{(i,m)})_j at every coordinate j. The proof first shows that the slice update a^{(i,m)} dominates a pointwise because it only increases coordinate i. Monotonicity of f then yields f(a) ≤ f(a^{(i,m)}), and transitivity with the invariant a ≤ f(a) yields the desired inequality at coordinate j.

steps.claim: The vector a is bounded pointwise by the modified vector that replaces coordinate i with m, that is, a ≤ (fun l => if l = i then m else a l).
steps.explanation: We check the inequality coordinatewise for an arbitrary index l. If l = i, the value at this coordinate is m, and the inequality a(i) ≤ m holds by hypothesis ham. If l ≠ i, the coordinate remains a(l), so the inequality a(l) ≤ a(l) holds by reflexivity.
steps.code:
have hle : a ≤ (fun l => if l = i then m else a l) := by
    intro l
    by_cases h : l = i
    · subst h
      simpa using ham
    · simp [h]

steps.claim: At coordinate j, a(j) ≤ f(fun l => if l = i then m else a l)(j).
steps.explanation: Applying the monotonicity of f (hf) to the pointwise bound a ≤ a^{(i, m)} (hle) yields f(a) ≤ f(a^{(i, m)}). Evaluating this inequality at coordinate j and combining it with the assumption a(j) ≤ f(a)(j) (ha) via transitivity of inequality (le_trans) concludes the proof.
steps.code:
have hmono := hf hle
  exact le_trans (ha j) (hmono j)

glossary.le_trans: In any preorder, if a ≤ b and b ≤ c, then a ≤ c.

declarations.name: tarski_slice_upper_bound
declarations.informal: Monotonicity preservation on coordinate slices (upper bound): fixing coordinate i to any value m ≤ b_i preserves the upper subinterval invariant f(b^{(i,m)})_j ≤ b_j for all coordinates j.
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_slice_upper_bound (n k : ℕ) (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (hf : Monotone f)
    (b : Fin k → Fin n) (hb : f b ≤ b) (i : Fin k) (m : Fin n) (hbm : m ≤ b i) (j : Fin k) :
    f (fun l => if l = i then m else b l) j ≤ b j
declarations.source:
/-- Monotonicity preservation on coordinate slices: decreasing coordinate i from b_i to m preserves f(b^{(i,m)}) ≤ b. -/
theorem tarski_slice_upper_bound (n k : ℕ) (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (hf : Monotone f)
    (b : Fin k → Fin n) (hb : f b ≤ b) (i : Fin k) (m : Fin n) (hbm : m ≤ b i) (j : Fin k) :
    f (fun l => if l = i then m else b l) j ≤ b j := by
  have h_le : (fun l => if l = i then m else b l) ≤ b := by
    intro l
    dsimp
    split_ifs with h
    · subst h
      exact hbm
    · exact le_rfl
  exact (hf h_le j).trans (hb j)

explanation.summary: The theorem states that decreasing coordinate i of an upper invariant point b (satisfying f(b) ≤ b) to any m ≤ b_i preserves the upper invariant f(b')_j ≤ b_j at every coordinate j. The proof first shows that the modified vector b' is pointwise bounded above by b by checking coordinate i and the remaining coordinates separately. It then applies the monotonicity of f to obtain f(b') ≤ f(b), which yields f(b')_j ≤ b_j after chaining with f(b)_j ≤ b_j by transitivity.

steps.claim: The modified vector b^{(i, m)}, obtained by setting the i-th coordinate of b to m, is pointwise less than or equal to b.
steps.explanation: To show that the updated vector is bounded by b, we inspect each coordinate l. If l = i, its value is m, which is bounded by b_i by the hypothesis hbm. If l ≠ i, its value remains b_l, which is bounded by b_l by reflexivity (le_rfl).
steps.code:
have h_le : (fun l => if l = i then m else b l) ≤ b := by
    intro l
    dsimp
    split_ifs with h
    · subst h
      exact hbm
    · exact le_rfl

steps.claim: f(b^{(i, m)})_j ≤ b_j for any coordinate j.
steps.explanation: Because f is monotone (hf), the pointwise inequality b^{(i, m)} ≤ b implies f(b^{(i, m)}) ≤ f(b), and evaluating at coordinate j gives f(b^{(i, m)})_j ≤ f(b)_j. Chaining this with the assumption f(b)_j ≤ b_j (hb j) by transitivity completes the proof.
steps.code: exact (hf h_le j).trans (hb j)

glossary.le_rfl: In any preorder, every element is less than or equal to itself: a ≤ a.

declarations.name: tarski_subinterval_slice_shrink
declarations.informal: Slicing contraction principle: if x is a fixed point of f on all coordinates j ≠ i within [a, b], then comparing f(x)_i with x_i either shows x is a fixed point, or x ≤ f(x) and f has a fixed point in [x, b], or f(x) ≤ x and f has a fixed point in [a, x].
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_subinterval_slice_shrink (n k : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (hf : Monotone f)
    (a b : Fin k → Fin n) (ha : a ≤ f a) (hb : f b ≤ b)
    (x : Fin k → Fin n) (hax : a ≤ x) (hxb : x ≤ b) (i : Fin k)
    (hslice : ∀ j : Fin k, j ≠ i → f x j = x j) :
    (f x = x) ∨ (x ≤ f x ∧ ∃ z, x ≤ z ∧ z ≤ b ∧ f z = z) ∨ (f x ≤ x ∧ ∃ z, a ≤ z ∧ z ≤ x ∧ f z = z)
declarations.source:
/-- Slicing contraction principle: a slice fixed point with all other coordinates fixed contracts the search sub-box along coordinate i while preserving the subinterval lattice invariant. -/
theorem tarski_subinterval_slice_shrink (n k : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n)) (hf : Monotone f)
    (a b : Fin k → Fin n) (ha : a ≤ f a) (hb : f b ≤ b)
    (x : Fin k → Fin n) (hax : a ≤ x) (hxb : x ≤ b) (i : Fin k)
    (hslice : ∀ j : Fin k, j ≠ i → f x j = x j) :
    (f x = x) ∨ (x ≤ f x ∧ ∃ z, x ≤ z ∧ z ≤ b ∧ f z = z) ∨ (f x ≤ x ∧ ∃ z, a ≤ z ∧ z ≤ x ∧ f z = z) := by
  rcases le_total (x i) (f x i) with h | h
  · rcases eq_or_lt_of_le h with he | hlt
    · left
      funext j
      by_cases hj : j = i
      · subst hj; exact he.symm
      · exact hslice j hj
    · right; left
      have hxf : x ≤ f x := by
        intro j
        by_cases hj : j = i
        · subst hj; exact hlt.le
        · rw [hslice j hj]
      exact ⟨hxf, tarski_subinterval_fixed_point n k f hf x b hxb hxf hb⟩
  · right; right
    have hfx : f x ≤ x := by
      intro j
      by_cases hj : j = i
      · subst hj; exact h
      · rw [hslice j hj]
    exact ⟨hfx, tarski_subinterval_fixed_point n k f hf a x hax ha hfx⟩

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by trichotomy on coordinate i, comparing x i with f(x) i. If x i = f(x) i, then f(x) = x across all coordinates because all other coordinates are already fixed by the slice hypothesis. If x i < f(x) i, then x ≤ f(x) componentwise, and Tarski's subinterval fixed point theorem on [x, b] guarantees a fixed point in that upper subinterval. Otherwise f(x) i ≤ x i, which implies f(x) ≤ x componentwise, and the theorem on [a, x] guarantees a fixed point in that lower subinterval.

steps.claim: If x i = f x i, then x is a fixed point of f (f x = x).
steps.explanation: By the totality of the linear order on Fin n (`le_total`), either x i ≤ f x i or f x i ≤ x i. In the former branch, `eq_or_lt_of_le` further splits into x i = f x i or x i < f x i. When x i = f x i, we show f x = x by function extensionality over coordinates j: if j = i, then f x i = x i by assumption; if j ≠ i, then f x j = x j by the slice fixed-point hypothesis `hslice`. This establishes the first disjunct.
steps.code:
rcases le_total (x i) (f x i) with h | h
  · rcases eq_or_lt_of_le h with he | hlt
    · left
      funext j
      by_cases hj : j = i
      · subst hj; exact he.symm
      · exact hslice j hj

steps.claim: If x i < f x i, then x ≤ f x and f has a fixed point in [x, b].
steps.explanation: Selecting the second disjunct, we first show x ≤ f x coordinatewise: at coordinate i, x i ≤ f x i follows from x i < f x i; at any other coordinate j ≠ i, x j = f x j by `hslice`, so x j ≤ f x j. Then, because x ≤ b, x ≤ f x, and f b ≤ b, `tarski_subinterval_fixed_point` applied to the subinterval [x, b] yields a fixed point z such that x ≤ z ≤ b and f z = z.
steps.code:
· right; left
      have hxf : x ≤ f x := by
        intro j
        by_cases hj : j = i
        · subst hj; exact hlt.le
        · rw [hslice j hj]
      exact ⟨hxf, tarski_subinterval_fixed_point n k f hf x b hxb hxf hb⟩

steps.claim: If f x i ≤ x i, then f x ≤ x and f has a fixed point in [a, x].
steps.explanation: Selecting the third disjunct, we first show f x ≤ x coordinatewise: at coordinate i, f x i ≤ x i is our case hypothesis; at coordinates j ≠ i, f x j = x j by `hslice`, so f x j ≤ x j. Then, because a ≤ x, a ≤ f a, and f x ≤ x, `tarski_subinterval_fixed_point` applied to the subinterval [a, x] yields a fixed point z such that a ≤ z ≤ x and f z = z.
steps.code:
· right; right
    have hfx : f x ≤ x := by
      intro j
      by_cases hj : j = i
      · subst hj; exact h
      · rw [hslice j hj]
    exact ⟨hfx, tarski_subinterval_fixed_point n k f hf a x hax ha hfx⟩

glossary.le_total: In a linear order, any two elements are comparable: either a ≤ b or b ≤ a.
glossary.eq_or_lt_of_le: In a partial order, if a ≤ b, then either a = b or a < b.
glossary.tarski_subinterval_fixed_point: A monotone map on a finite grid Fin k → Fin n has a fixed point in any subinterval [a, b] satisfying a ≤ b, a ≤ f(a), and f(b) ≤ b.

declarations.name: finset_has_no_unique_sums_decidable
declarations.informal: Having no unique sums is a decidable property for finite subsets of an additive commutative monoid with decidable equality.
declarations.statement: instance finset_has_no_unique_sums_decidable {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] [DecidableEq G] (A : Finset G) : Decidable (finset_has_no_unique_sums A)
declarations.source:
/-- Having no unique sums is a decidable property for finite subsets of an additive commutative monoid with decidable equality. -/
instance finset_has_no_unique_sums_decidable {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] [DecidableEq G] (A : Finset G) : Decidable (finset_has_no_unique_sums A) := by
  unfold finset_has_no_unique_sums
  infer_instance

declarations.name: tarski_box_query_le
declarations.informal: Box-local Tarski query invariant: for every sub-box [a,b] (a ≤ b) of [n]^k there is a single deterministic query tree — depending only on the box, not on the unknown f — that, against every monotone f with a ≤ f a and f b ≤ b, outputs a fixed point of f lying inside [a,b] using at most q queries.
declarations.statement: def tarski_box_query_le (n k q : ℕ) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Box-local Tarski query invariant: one tree, uniform in the oracle f, finds a fixed point inside any sub-box [a,b]. -/
def tarski_box_query_le (n k q : ℕ) : Prop := ∀ a b : Fin k → Fin n, a ≤ b → ∃ t : TarskiQueryTree n k,
    ∀ f : (Fin k → Fin n) → Fin k → Fin n, Monotone f → a ≤ f a → f b ≤ b →
      a ≤ TarskiQueryTree.run f t ∧ TarskiQueryTree.run f t ≤ b ∧
      f (TarskiQueryTree.run f t) = TarskiQueryTree.run f t ∧
      TarskiQueryTree.cost f t ≤ q

declarations.name: nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums
declarations.informal: If A is a subset of Z/pZ with no unique sums, then m(p) ≤ |A|.
declarations.statement: theorem nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums {p : ℕ} (A : Finset (ZMod p)) (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A) : nus_min_card p ≤ A.card
declarations.source:
/-- If A is a subset of Z/pZ with no unique sums, then m(p) ≤ |A|. -/
theorem nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums {p : ℕ} (A : Finset (ZMod p)) (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A) : nus_min_card p ≤ A.card := by
  unfold nus_min_card
  apply Nat.sInf_le
  exact ⟨A, hA, rfl⟩

explanation.summary: By definition, $m(p)$ (`nus_min_card p`) is the infimum of the cardinalities of all subsets of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ that have no unique sums. Since $A$ is assumed to have no unique sums, its cardinality $|A|$ belongs to this collection of sizes. The inequality $m(p) \le |A|$ then follows directly from the fact that the infimum of a set of natural numbers is at most any of its elements (`Nat.sInf_le`).

steps.claim: It suffices to show that $|A|$ belongs to the set of cardinalities of subsets of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with no unique sums.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of $m(p)$ (`nus_min_card p`), it is the infimum of all cardinalities $k$ for which there exists a subset of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ without unique sums of size $k$. By `Nat.sInf_le`, the infimum of a set of natural numbers is bounded above by any element of the set, reducing the goal to showing that $|A|$ is in this set.
steps.code:
unfold nus_min_card
  apply Nat.sInf_le

steps.claim: $|A| \in \{k \mid \exists A', \text{finset\_has\_no\_unique\_sums } A' \land |A'| = k\}$
steps.explanation: The subset $A$ itself witnesses membership in the set: it satisfies `finset_has_no_unique_sums` by the hypothesis $hA$, and its cardinality is $|A|$.
steps.code: exact ⟨A, hA, rfl⟩

glossary.Nat.sInf_le: For any set of natural numbers $s$ and any element $m \in s$, the infimum $\inf s$ satisfies $\inf s \le m$.
