declarations.name: tarski_query_tree_bind
declarations.informal: Sequential composition of query trees: run the tree, then feed its output point into the continuation g to obtain the tree that is actually executed.
declarations.statement:
def tarski_query_tree_bind {n k : ℕ} (g : (Fin k → Fin n) → TarskiQueryTree n k) :
    TarskiQueryTree n k → TarskiQueryTree n k
declarations.source:
/-- Sequential composition: run a query tree, then continue with the tree g applied to its output. -/
def tarski_query_tree_bind {n k : ℕ} (g : (Fin k → Fin n) → TarskiQueryTree n k) :
    TarskiQueryTree n k → TarskiQueryTree n k := fun _t => match _t with
  | .output x => g x
  | .query x k' => .query x (fun v => tarski_query_tree_bind g (k' v))

declarations.name: nus_min_card_three_eq_three
declarations.informal: The minimal cardinality of a set with no unique sums in Z/3Z is exactly 3.
declarations.statement: theorem nus_min_card_three_eq_three : nus_min_card 3 = 3
declarations.source:
/-- The minimal cardinality of a set with no unique sums in Z/3Z is exactly 3. -/
theorem nus_min_card_three_eq_three : nus_min_card 3 = 3 := by
  have h1 : 1 + Nat.clog 2 3 ≤ nus_min_card 3 := by
    apply nus_min_card_ge_one_add_clog
    decide
  have h2 : nus_min_card 3 ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod 3)).card := by
    apply nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums
    exact finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod_three
  rw [Finset.card_univ, ZMod.card 3] at h2
  have hc : Nat.clog 2 3 = 2 := rfl
  omega

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by sandwiching the minimal cardinality between matching lower and upper bounds. The lower bound $\mathrm{nus\_min\_card}(3) \ge 1 + \lceil \log_2 3 \rceil = 3$ is supplied by the general bound for odd primes. The upper bound $\mathrm{nus\_min\_card}(3) \le 3$ is witnessed by the universal set $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ itself, which is known to have no unique sums and contains 3 elements.

steps.claim: $\mathrm{nus\_min\_card}(3) \ge 1 + \lceil \log_2 3 \rceil$
steps.explanation: We invoke the general lower bound `nus_min_card_ge_one_add_clog`, which holds for any odd prime $p$. The primality of $3$ is resolved by typeclass inference, and the requirement $3 \neq 2$ is verified by computational reflection (`decide`).
steps.code:
have h1 : 1 + Nat.clog 2 3 ≤ nus_min_card 3 := by
    apply nus_min_card_ge_one_add_clog
    decide

steps.claim: $\mathrm{nus\_min\_card}(3) \le 3$
steps.explanation: By `nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums`, any subset with no unique sums bounds the minimal cardinality from above. The universal set $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ satisfies this property by `finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod_three`. Rewriting its cardinality using `Finset.card_univ` and `ZMod.card` shows $|\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}| = 3$, giving the upper bound $\mathrm{nus\_min\_card}(3) \le 3$.
steps.code:
have h2 : nus_min_card 3 ≤ (Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod 3)).card := by
    apply nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums
    exact finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod_three
  rw [Finset.card_univ, ZMod.card 3] at h2

steps.claim: The lower and upper bounds sandwich $\mathrm{nus\_min\_card}(3)$ to equal $3$.
steps.explanation: Evaluating the ceiling logarithm yields $\lceil \log_2 3 \rceil = 2$ by definitional equality (`rfl`), turning the lower bound into $1 + 2 = 3 \le \mathrm{nus\_min\_card}(3)$. Together with the upper bound $\mathrm{nus\_min\_card}(3) \le 3$, linear integer arithmetic (`omega`) closes the goal.
steps.code:
have hc : Nat.clog 2 3 = 2 := rfl
  omega

glossary.nus_min_card_ge_one_add_clog: For an odd prime $p$, the minimal cardinality of a set with no unique sums in $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is at least $1 + \lceil \log_2 p \rceil$.
glossary.nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums: If a finite subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ has no unique sums, then the minimal cardinality of such a set is at most $|A|$.
glossary.finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod_thre: The entire group $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$, viewed as a finite set, has no unique sums.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset of a finite type is the cardinality of the type itself.
glossary.ZMod.card: The cardinality of the type $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is $n$.

declarations.name: tarski_query_tree_slice_lift
declarations.informal: Slice lifting of a query tree one dimension up: replace every query y in dimension k by the query (insertNth i c y) in dimension k+1, and every returned answer v by its restriction (removeNth i v) to the other coordinates.
declarations.statement:
def tarski_query_tree_slice_lift {n k : ℕ} (i : Fin (k+1)) (c : Fin n) :
    TarskiQueryTree n k → TarskiQueryTree n (k+1)
declarations.source:
/-- Lift a dimension-k query tree to dimension k+1 by holding coordinate i at c. -/
def tarski_query_tree_slice_lift {n k : ℕ} (i : Fin (k+1)) (c : Fin n) :
    TarskiQueryTree n k → TarskiQueryTree n (k+1) := fun _t => match _t with
  | .output x => .output (Fin.insertNth i c x)
  | .query x k' => .query (Fin.insertNth i c x)
      (fun v => tarski_query_tree_slice_lift i c (k' (Fin.removeNth i v)))

declarations.name: nus_min_card_le_sq_of_midpoint_balanced
declarations.informal: If B is a midpoint-balanced subset of Z/pZ, then m(p) ≤ |B|².
declarations.statement: theorem nus_min_card_le_sq_of_midpoint_balanced {p : ℕ} (B : Finset (ZMod p)) (hB : finset_is_midpoint_balanced B) : nus_min_card p ≤ B.card ^ 2
declarations.source:
/-- If B is a midpoint-balanced subset of Z/pZ, then m(p) ≤ |B|². -/
theorem nus_min_card_le_sq_of_midpoint_balanced {p : ℕ} (B : Finset (ZMod p)) (hB : finset_is_midpoint_balanced B) : nus_min_card p ≤ B.card ^ 2 := by
  have h_nus := finset_has_no_unique_sums_sumset_of_balanced B hB
  have h_le := nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums ((B ×ˢ B).image (fun x => x.1 + x.2)) h_nus
  have h_card : ((B ×ˢ B).image (fun x => x.1 + x.2)).card ≤ B.card ^ 2 := by
    calc
      ((B ×ˢ B).image (fun x => x.1 + x.2)).card ≤ (B ×ˢ B).card := Finset.card_image_le
      _ = B.card ^ 2 := by rw [Finset.card_product, sq]
  omega

explanation.summary: To bound the minimum size m(p) of a subset with no unique sums, the proof considers the sumset B + B. Since B is midpoint-balanced, B + B has no unique sums, which immediately implies m(p) ≤ |B + B|. The size of the sumset is then bounded by |B × B| = |B|², yielding m(p) ≤ |B|².

steps.claim: The sumset B + B has no unique sums.
steps.explanation: Applying `finset_has_no_unique_sums_sumset_of_balanced` to B and the hypothesis that B is midpoint-balanced establishes that the sumset (B ×ˢ B).image (+) has no unique sums.
steps.code: have h_nus := finset_has_no_unique_sums_sumset_of_balanced B hB

steps.claim: m(p) ≤ |B + B|
steps.explanation: Because the sumset B + B has no unique sums, the minimum cardinality m(p) of such a subset in Z/pZ is bounded above by the size of B + B via `nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums`.
steps.code: have h_le := nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums ((B ×ˢ B).image (fun x => x.1 + x.2)) h_nus

steps.claim: |B + B| ≤ |B|²
steps.explanation: The cardinality of the sumset (the image of B ×ˢ B under addition) is at most |B ×ˢ B| by `Finset.card_image_le`. By `Finset.card_product` and the definition of squaring (`sq`), |B ×ˢ B| = |B| * |B| = |B|².
steps.code:
have h_card : ((B ×ˢ B).image (fun x => x.1 + x.2)).card ≤ B.card ^ 2 := by
    calc
      ((B ×ˢ B).image (fun x => x.1 + x.2)).card ≤ (B ×ˢ B).card := Finset.card_image_le
      _ = B.card ^ 2 := by rw [Finset.card_product, sq]

steps.claim: m(p) ≤ |B|²
steps.explanation: Linear arithmetic (`omega`) combines the bounds m(p) ≤ |B + B| and |B + B| ≤ |B|² by transitivity of ≤ on natural numbers.
steps.code: omega

glossary.finset_has_no_unique_sums_sumset_of_bala: If a finite subset B of an abelian group is midpoint-balanced, then its sumset B + B has no unique sums.
glossary.nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums: The minimum size m(p) of a subset of Z/pZ with no unique sums is bounded above by the size of any subset that has no unique sums.
glossary.Finset.card_image_le: The cardinality of the image of a finite set under a function is at most the cardinality of the domain.
glossary.Finset.card_product: The cardinality of the Cartesian product of two finite sets is the product of their cardinalities.
glossary.sq: The square a² of an element is equal to a * a.

declarations.name: tarski_query_tree_bind_spec
declarations.informal: Run/cost law for sequential composition: the run of a bind is the run of the continuation g at the output of the first tree, and the cost of a bind is the cost of the first tree plus the cost of the continuation at that output.
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_query_tree_bind_spec {n k : ℕ} (g : (Fin k → Fin n) → TarskiQueryTree n k)
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → Fin k → Fin n) (t : TarskiQueryTree n k) :
    TarskiQueryTree.run f (tarski_query_tree_bind g t) =
      TarskiQueryTree.run f (g (TarskiQueryTree.run f t)) ∧
    TarskiQueryTree.cost f (tarski_query_tree_bind g t) =
      TarskiQueryTree.cost f t +
        TarskiQueryTree.cost f (g (TarskiQueryTree.run f t))
declarations.source:
/-- Run and cost of a sequential composition. -/
theorem tarski_query_tree_bind_spec {n k : ℕ} (g : (Fin k → Fin n) → TarskiQueryTree n k)
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → Fin k → Fin n) (t : TarskiQueryTree n k) :
    TarskiQueryTree.run f (tarski_query_tree_bind g t) =
      TarskiQueryTree.run f (g (TarskiQueryTree.run f t)) ∧
    TarskiQueryTree.cost f (tarski_query_tree_bind g t) =
      TarskiQueryTree.cost f t +
        TarskiQueryTree.cost f (g (TarskiQueryTree.run f t)) := by
  induction t with
  | output x => exact ⟨rfl, (Nat.zero_add _).symm⟩
  | query x k' ih =>
    refine ⟨(ih (f x)).1, ?_⟩
    show TarskiQueryTree.cost f (tarski_query_tree_bind g (k' (f x))) + 1 =
      (TarskiQueryTree.cost f (k' (f x)) + 1) +
        TarskiQueryTree.cost f (g (TarskiQueryTree.run f (k' (f x))))
    rw [(ih (f x)).2]
    omega

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by structural induction on the query tree t. For a leaf node output x, sequential composition evaluates directly to g x, whose cost is 0 + cost f (g x). For a query node query x k', running the tree queries the oracle f at x and continues along the subtree k' (f x); applying the induction hypothesis to this response establishes the run identity immediately and reduces the cost identity to the linear arithmetic identity (c + d) + 1 = (c + 1) + d.

steps.claim: By structural induction on t, both identities hold for leaf nodes t = output x.
steps.explanation: We induct on the structure of the tree t. In the base case, t = output x represents a leaf with output value x. By definition of sequential composition, tarski_query_tree_bind g (output x) = g x, and by definition of running a tree, run f (output x) = x. Thus the run of the composed tree is run f (g x), which matches run f (g (run f (output x))) definitionally. For the query cost, a leaf node performs zero queries, so cost f (output x) = 0. The cost of the composed tree is cost f (g x), while the right-hand sum is 0 + cost f (g x); these are equal by Nat.zero_add.
steps.code:
induction t with
  | output x => exact ⟨rfl, (Nat.zero_add _).symm⟩

steps.claim: For query nodes t = query x k', the run identity holds by the induction hypothesis on the queried subtree.
steps.explanation: In the inductive step, the tree queries the oracle f at input x, receives the response f x, and continues along the subtree k' (f x). The induction hypothesis states that both identities hold for every subtree k' a. Specializing the induction hypothesis to the oracle's actual response a = f x, its first component establishes that run f (tarski_query_tree_bind g (k' (f x))) = run f (g (run f (k' (f x)))). Since executing a query node definitionally evaluates to running its continuation at f x, this immediately settles the run identity for the query node, leaving only the cost equation to verify.
steps.code:
| query x k' ih =>
    refine ⟨(ih (f x)).1, ?_⟩

steps.claim: For query nodes t = query x k', the cost identity also holds, completing the induction.
steps.explanation: The cost of executing a query node is defined as 1 plus the cost of running the continuation subtree on the oracle response f x. Unfolding this definition rephrases the goal into an explicit arithmetic statement: the cost of the composed subtree plus 1 equals the subtree cost plus 1 plus the continuation cost. Rewriting with the second component of the induction hypothesis at f x substitutes the cost of the composed subtree with the sum of the subtree cost and the continuation cost. The resulting equation has the form (c + d) + 1 = (c + 1) + d, where c is the subtree cost and d is the continuation cost; this is closed by linear arithmetic over ℕ (omega).
steps.code:
show TarskiQueryTree.cost f (tarski_query_tree_bind g (k' (f x))) + 1 =
      (TarskiQueryTree.cost f (k' (f x)) + 1) +
        TarskiQueryTree.cost f (g (TarskiQueryTree.run f (k' (f x))))
    rw [(ih (f x)).2]
    omega

glossary.Nat.zero_add: For any natural number n, 0 + n = n.

declarations.name: tarski_query_tree_slice_lift_spec
declarations.informal: Run/cost law for the slice lift: in dimension k+1, the lifted tree computes insertNth i c of the slice algorithm's output (run against the sliced map y ↦ f (insertNth i c y) ∘ succAbove i), and it costs exactly what the slice algorithm costs.
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_query_tree_slice_lift_spec {n k : ℕ} (i : Fin (k+1)) (c : Fin n)
    (f : (Fin (k+1) → Fin n) → Fin (k+1) → Fin n) (t : TarskiQueryTree n k) :
    TarskiQueryTree.run f (tarski_query_tree_slice_lift i c t) =
      Fin.insertNth i c (TarskiQueryTree.run (fun y j => f (Fin.insertNth i c y) (i.succAbove j)) t) ∧
    TarskiQueryTree.cost f (tarski_query_tree_slice_lift i c t) =
      TarskiQueryTree.cost (fun y j => f (Fin.insertNth i c y) (i.succAbove j)) t
declarations.source:
/-- Run and cost of a slice lift. -/
theorem tarski_query_tree_slice_lift_spec {n k : ℕ} (i : Fin (k+1)) (c : Fin n)
    (f : (Fin (k+1) → Fin n) → Fin (k+1) → Fin n) (t : TarskiQueryTree n k) :
    TarskiQueryTree.run f (tarski_query_tree_slice_lift i c t) =
      Fin.insertNth i c (TarskiQueryTree.run (fun y j => f (Fin.insertNth i c y) (i.succAbove j)) t) ∧
    TarskiQueryTree.cost f (tarski_query_tree_slice_lift i c t) =
      TarskiQueryTree.cost (fun y j => f (Fin.insertNth i c y) (i.succAbove j)) t := by
  induction t with
  | output x =>
    simp [tarski_query_tree_slice_lift, TarskiQueryTree.run, TarskiQueryTree.cost]
  | query x next ih =>
    simp only [tarski_query_tree_slice_lift, TarskiQueryTree.run, TarskiQueryTree.cost]
    have := ih (fun j => f (i.insertNth c x) (i.succAbove j))
    exact ⟨this.1, congrArg (· + 1) this.2⟩

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by structural induction on the query tree $t$. For an output leaf, both the lifted tree and the sliced execution immediately return the corresponding vector with query cost $0$. For a query node, performing the initial query evaluates the oracle at the lifted point, which matches the sliced oracle query on the original point; specializing the induction hypothesis to the oracle's response then equates both the resulting outputs and the incremented query costs.

steps.claim: The specification holds for leaf nodes $\operatorname{output}(x)$.
steps.explanation: We proceed by structural induction on the tree $t$. When $t = \operatorname{output}(x)$, no queries are made and the tree immediately returns $x$. Lifting it produces $\operatorname{output}(\operatorname{insertNth}(i, c, x))$, which returns $\operatorname{insertNth}(i, c, x)$ with cost $0$. Similarly, running the sliced oracle on the original leaf returns $x$ with cost $0$, and inserting $c$ at index $i$ gives $\operatorname{insertNth}(i, c, x)$ with cost $0$. Simplifying with the definitions of `tarski_query_tree_slice_lift`, `TarskiQueryTree.run`, and `TarskiQueryTree.cost` verifies both equalities directly.
steps.code:
induction t with
  | output x =>
    simp [tarski_query_tree_slice_lift, TarskiQueryTree.run, TarskiQueryTree.cost]

steps.claim: For a query node $\operatorname{query}(x, \operatorname{next})$, executing the initial query reduces the run and cost equalities to those of the continuation sub-tree, with each cost incremented by $1$.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definitions of `tarski_query_tree_slice_lift`, `TarskiQueryTree.run`, and `TarskiQueryTree.cost` evaluates the leading query. The lifted tree queries $f$ at $\operatorname{insertNth}(i, c, x)$, strips coordinate $i$ from the answer, and passes the remaining vector to the continuation. This matches querying the sliced oracle at $x$, advancing both sides to the continuation $\operatorname{next}(j \mapsto f(\operatorname{insertNth}(i, c, x))(i.\operatorname{succAbove}(j)))$ and adding $1$ to each cost.
steps.code:
| query x next ih =>
    simp only [tarski_query_tree_slice_lift, TarskiQueryTree.run, TarskiQueryTree.cost]

steps.claim: The induction hypothesis on the continuation sub-tree completes the query case, establishing the specification for all trees.
steps.explanation: We instantiate the induction hypothesis `ih` at the response vector $a = j \mapsto f(\operatorname{insertNth}(i, c, x))(i.\operatorname{succAbove}(j))$. This yields both the equality of output vectors (`this.1`) and the equality of query costs (`this.2`) for the continuation. Applying `congrArg (· + 1)` to the cost equality matches the incremented query counts, completing the inductive step.
steps.code:
have := ih (fun j => f (i.insertNth c x) (i.succAbove j))
    exact ⟨this.1, congrArg (· + 1) this.2⟩

glossary.congrArg: Applying a function to equal arguments yields equal results ($a_1 = a_2 \implies f(a_1) = f(a_2)$).
glossary.TarskiQueryTree.cost: Counts the total number of oracle queries made when executing a query tree against an oracle function.
glossary.TarskiQueryTree.run: Executes a query tree against an oracle function, returning the tree's final output vector.
glossary.tarski_query_tree_slice_lift: Lifts a $k$-dimensional query tree to dimension $k+1$ by inserting a fixed coordinate value $c$ at index $i$ into all queried points and output vectors.

caveats: The simplification in line 12 relies on the fact that removing the $i$-th coordinate via `Fin.removeNth i (f (Fin.insertNth i c x))` is definitionally equal to composing with `succAbove i`, namely `fun j => f (Fin.insertNth i c x) (i.succAbove j)`, allowing the instantiated induction hypothesis to match the continuation directly.

declarations.name: tarski_box_query_le_imp_query_complexity
declarations.informal: The box-local invariant implies the ambient query complexity notion, by taking the full box [0, n−1]^k (needs n ≥ 1 since Fin n has no Bot/Top for general n).
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_box_query_le_imp_query_complexity (n k q : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (h : tarski_box_query_le n k q) : tarski_query_complexity_le n k q
declarations.source:
/-- Box-local invariant on the full grid gives the ambient query-complexity bound. -/
theorem tarski_box_query_le_imp_query_complexity (n k q : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (h : tarski_box_query_le n k q) : tarski_query_complexity_le n k q := by
  haveI : NeZero n := ⟨by omega⟩
  unfold tarski_box_query_le at h
  unfold tarski_query_complexity_le
  let a : Fin k → Fin n := fun _ => ⟨0, by omega⟩
  let b : Fin k → Fin n := fun _ => ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
  have hab : a ≤ b := by
    intro i
    exact Fin.zero_le _
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := h a b hab
  refine ⟨t, ?_⟩
  intro f hf
  have hfa : a ≤ f a := fun _ => Fin.zero_le _
  have hfb : f b ≤ b := by
    intro i
    rw [Fin.le_def]
    have := (f b i).isLt
    show (f b i : ℕ) ≤ n - 1
    omega
  obtain ⟨-, -, hfix, hcost⟩ := ht f hf hfa hfb
  exact ⟨hfix, hcost⟩

explanation.summary: The proof reduces ambient query complexity to box-local query complexity by instantiating the box-local hypothesis with the full grid [a, b], where a = (0, ..., 0) and b = (n - 1, ..., n - 1). Because a is the global minimum and b is the global maximum of the grid, any monotone function f automatically satisfies the box-invariance boundary conditions a ≤ f a and f b ≤ b. The query tree guaranteed by the box-local hypothesis for this choice of box therefore finds a fixed point of any monotone function within cost q.

steps.claim: Establish that n ≠ 0 and unfold the definitions of box-local and ambient query complexity.
steps.explanation: Since 1 ≤ n, linear arithmetic (omega) gives n ≠ 0, yielding the NeZero n instance needed to treat 0 as an element of Fin n. We then unfold the definitions of tarski_box_query_le in the hypothesis and tarski_query_complexity_le in the goal to reveal their logical structure.
steps.code:
haveI : NeZero n := ⟨by omega⟩
  unfold tarski_box_query_le at h
  unfold tarski_query_complexity_le

steps.claim: Define the global minimum a and maximum b of the grid (Fin k → Fin n) and prove that a ≤ b.
steps.explanation: We define a as the constantly 0 function and b as the constantly n - 1 function, which are well-defined since 0 < n and n - 1 < n when 1 ≤ n. The inequality a ≤ b holds coordinatewise because a i = 0 ≤ b i by Fin.zero_le.
steps.code:
let a : Fin k → Fin n := fun _ => ⟨0, by omega⟩
  let b : Fin k → Fin n := fun _ => ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
  have hab : a ≤ b := by
    intro i
    exact Fin.zero_le _

steps.claim: Obtain the query tree t from the box-local hypothesis on [a, b] and propose it as the witness for ambient query complexity.
steps.explanation: Specializing the hypothesis h to the endpoints a and b with the proof that a ≤ b yields a query tree t. We supply t as the candidate tree for the existential goal in tarski_query_complexity_le.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := h a b hab
  refine ⟨t, ?_⟩

steps.claim: For any monotone function f, the lower boundary condition a ≤ f a holds.
steps.explanation: Let f be an arbitrary monotone function. Since a is constantly 0, each coordinate satisfies a i = 0 ≤ (f a) i by Fin.zero_le, so a ≤ f a.
steps.code:
intro f hf
  have hfa : a ≤ f a := fun _ => Fin.zero_le _

steps.claim: For any monotone function f, the upper boundary condition f b ≤ b holds.
steps.explanation: For each coordinate i, Fin.le_def translates the inequality in Fin n to the underlying natural numbers. By Fin.isLt, the natural number representing (f b) i is strictly less than n, which by linear arithmetic (omega) implies (f b) i ≤ n - 1 = b i.
steps.code:
have hfb : f b ≤ b := by
    intro i
    rw [Fin.le_def]
    have := (f b i).isLt
    show (f b i : ℕ) ≤ n - 1
    omega

steps.claim: The query tree t outputs a fixed point of f within query budget q.
steps.explanation: Feeding f, its monotonicity, and the boundary conditions a ≤ f a and f b ≤ b into the guarantee for t produces the result that running t on f yields a fixed point of f with query cost at most q, closing the goal.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨-, -, hfix, hcost⟩ := ht f hf hfa hfb
  exact ⟨hfix, hcost⟩

glossary.Fin.zero_le: Every element of Fin n is greater than or equal to zero.
glossary.Fin.le_def: The order on Fin n is defined by the inequality on the underlying natural numbers.
glossary.Fin.isLt: The underlying natural number of an element of Fin n is strictly less than n.

explanation.disclaimer: Written by a model (gemini-3.8-flash) from the Lean proof and the goal states Lean reported at each step. Lean verified the proof; this explanation is a reading aid and is not itself machine-checked.

declarations.name: tarski_box_query_le_small
declarations.informal: Brute force on small boxes: if every box in dimension k has at most M points, then every box query is answerable within M queries — and in particular tarski_box_query_le n k M holds, so the new definition is inhabited (non-vacuous).
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_box_query_le_small (n k M : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hM : ∀ a b : Fin k → Fin n, a ≤ b → (∏ j : Fin k, ((b j : ℕ) - (a j : ℕ) + 1)) ≤ M) :
    tarski_box_query_le n k M
declarations.source:
def tarski_box_query_le_small_tree {n k : ℕ} (x₀ : Fin k → Fin n) :
    List (Fin k → Fin n) → TarskiQueryTree n k
  | [] => .output x₀
  | x :: xs => .query x (fun fx => if fx = x then .output x else tarski_box_query_le_small_tree x₀ xs)

theorem tarski_box_query_le_small_cost_le {n k : ℕ} (x₀ : Fin k → Fin n) (L : List (Fin k → Fin n))
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → Fin k → Fin n) :
    TarskiQueryTree.cost f (tarski_box_query_le_small_tree x₀ L) ≤ L.length := by
  induction L with
  | nil =>
    simp [tarski_box_query_le_small_tree, TarskiQueryTree.cost]
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [tarski_box_query_le_small_tree, TarskiQueryTree.cost, List.length_cons]
    split_ifs with h
    · simp [TarskiQueryTree.cost]
    · omega

theorem tarski_box_query_le_small_run_mem_and_fixed {n k : ℕ} (x₀ : Fin k → Fin n) (L : List (Fin k → Fin n))
    (f : (Fin k → Fin n) → Fin k → Fin n) (h : ∃ z ∈ L, f z = z) :
    TarskiQueryTree.run f (tarski_box_query_le_small_tree x₀ L) ∈ L ∧
    f (TarskiQueryTree.run f (tarski_box_query_le_small_tree x₀ L)) =
      TarskiQueryTree.run f (tarski_box_query_le_small_tree x₀ L) := by
  induction L with
  | nil =>
    rcases h with ⟨z, hz, -⟩
    cases hz
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [tarski_box_query_le_small_tree, TarskiQueryTree.run]
    split_ifs with hfx
    · simp [TarskiQueryTree.run, hfx]
    · rcases h with ⟨z, hz, hfz⟩
      simp only [List.mem_cons] at hz
      rcases hz with rfl | hz
      · exact False.elim (hfx hfz)
      · have ⟨h1, h2⟩ := ih ⟨z, hz, hfz⟩
        exact ⟨List.mem_cons_of_mem x h1, h2⟩

/-- Boxes small enough to enumerate are solved by querying all their points. -/
theorem tarski_box_query_le_small (n k M : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (hM : ∀ a b : Fin k → Fin n, a ≤ b → (∏ j : Fin k, ((b j : ℕ) - (a j : ℕ) + 1)) ≤ M) :
    tarski_box_query_le n k M := by
  intro a b hab
  use tarski_box_query_le_small_tree a (Finset.Icc a b).toList
  intro f hf ha hb
  have h_fp := tarski_subinterval_fixed_point n k f hf a b hab ha hb
  rcases h_fp with ⟨x, hax, hxb, hfx⟩
  have hx_mem : x ∈ (Finset.Icc a b).toList := by
    rw [Finset.mem_toList, Finset.mem_Icc]
    exact ⟨hax, hxb⟩
  have h_run := tarski_box_query_le_small_run_mem_and_fixed a (Finset.Icc a b).toList f ⟨x, hx_mem, hfx⟩
  have h_mem_box : TarskiQueryTree.run f (tarski_box_query_le_small_tree a (Finset.Icc a b).toList) ∈ Finset.Icc a b := by
    rw [← Finset.mem_toList]
    exact h_run.1
  rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at h_mem_box
  refine ⟨h_mem_box.1, h_mem_box.2, h_run.2, ?_⟩
  have h_cost := tarski_box_query_le_small_cost_le a (Finset.Icc a b).toList f
  rw [Finset.length_toList] at h_cost
  have h_card_le : (Finset.Icc a b).card ≤ M := by
    rw [Pi.card_Icc]
    have h1 : ∀ j, (Finset.Icc (a j) (b j)).card = (b j : ℕ) - (a j : ℕ) + 1 := by
      intro j
      rw [Fin.card_Icc]
      have : a j ≤ b j := hab j
      omega
    simp_rw [h1]
    exact hM a b hab
  exact le_trans h_cost h_card_le

explanation.summary: The theorem proves that when every box [a, b] in (Fin n)^k has size at most M, a fixed point of any monotone map f on [a, b] can be found within at most M queries by brute-force search. A query tree is constructed that tests every element of the box in order, halting as soon as it encounters a fixed point. Tarski's fixed point theorem on subintervals guarantees that the box contains at least one fixed point, ensuring the search succeeds. Finally, the query cost is bounded by the number of points in the box, which is the product of coordinate interval lengths and is at most M by assumption.

steps.claim: The query tree for a candidate list L uses at most |L| queries.
steps.explanation: We proceed by induction on the candidate list L. For the empty list, the tree outputs the default point with zero queries. For a non-empty list x :: xs, the tree queries x; if f(x) = x, it halts immediately with cost 1 ≤ |x :: xs|; otherwise, it queries xs, incurring 1 + cost(xs) queries, which is at most 1 + |xs| = |x :: xs| by the induction hypothesis.
steps.code:
induction L with
  | nil =>
    simp [tarski_box_query_le_small_tree, TarskiQueryTree.cost]
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [tarski_box_query_le_small_tree, TarskiQueryTree.cost, List.length_cons]
    split_ifs with h
    · simp [TarskiQueryTree.cost]
    · omega

steps.claim: An empty candidate list cannot contain a fixed point.
steps.explanation: For the base case of search correctness, assuming there exists a fixed point in L = [] is impossible because the empty list has no elements.
steps.code:
induction L with
  | nil =>
    rcases h with ⟨z, hz, -⟩
    cases hz

steps.claim: If x :: xs contains a fixed point, the search tree terminates at a fixed point in x :: xs.
steps.explanation: If f(x) = x, the tree returns x, which is a fixed point in x :: xs. If f(x) ≠ x, the fixed point guaranteed to exist in x :: xs cannot be x, so it must lie in xs. By the induction hypothesis, running the search on xs finds a fixed point in xs, which also belongs to x :: xs via List.mem_cons_of_mem.
steps.code:
| cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [tarski_box_query_le_small_tree, TarskiQueryTree.run]
    split_ifs with hfx
    · simp [TarskiQueryTree.run, hfx]
    · rcases h with ⟨z, hz, hfz⟩
      simp only [List.mem_cons] at hz
      rcases hz with rfl | hz
      · exact False.elim (hfx hfz)
      · have ⟨h1, h2⟩ := ih ⟨z, hz, hfz⟩
        exact ⟨List.mem_cons_of_mem x h1, h2⟩

steps.claim: For any box [a, b], the search strategy is defined by querying all its points in list order.
steps.explanation: Given subinterval endpoints a ≤ b, we instantiate the existential query tree with the linear search tree over the list of points in [a, b] ((Finset.Icc a b).toList), with fallback point a. We then take any monotone map f satisfying a ≤ f(a) and f(b) ≤ b.
steps.code:
intro a b hab
  use tarski_box_query_le_small_tree a (Finset.Icc a b).toList
  intro f hf ha hb

steps.claim: The box [a, b] contains at least one fixed point of f.
steps.explanation: By Tarski's fixed point theorem on subintervals (tarski_subinterval_fixed_point), there is a point x such that a ≤ x ≤ b and f(x) = x. Therefore x belongs to the closed interval Finset.Icc a b and thus to its list representation.
steps.code:
have h_fp := tarski_subinterval_fixed_point n k f hf a b hab ha hb
  rcases h_fp with ⟨x, hax, hxb, hfx⟩
  have hx_mem : x ∈ (Finset.Icc a b).toList := by
    rw [Finset.mem_toList, Finset.mem_Icc]
    exact ⟨hax, hxb⟩

steps.claim: The query tree outputs a fixed point of f lying in the box [a, b].
steps.explanation: Applying the correctness lemma tarski_box_query_le_small_run_mem_and_fixed with witness x shows that the output of the query tree is in (Finset.Icc a b).toList and is a fixed point of f. Hence the output lies in Finset.Icc a b, satisfying a ≤ output ≤ b.
steps.code:
have h_run := tarski_box_query_le_small_run_mem_and_fixed a (Finset.Icc a b).toList f ⟨x, hx_mem, hfx⟩
  have h_mem_box : TarskiQueryTree.run f (tarski_box_query_le_small_tree a (Finset.Icc a b).toList) ∈ Finset.Icc a b := by
    rw [← Finset.mem_toList]
    exact h_run.1
  rw [Finset.mem_Icc] at h_mem_box
  refine ⟨h_mem_box.1, h_mem_box.2, h_run.2, ?_⟩

steps.claim: The query cost of the tree is at most M, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: By tarski_box_query_le_small_cost_le, the query cost is bounded by the length of the list, which equals the cardinality of [a, b] (Finset.length_toList). By Pi.card_Icc, the size of [a, b] in the product order is the product over coordinates of the 1D interval sizes, each of which is (b j - a j + 1) by Fin.card_Icc. By assumption hM, this product is at most M, so transitivity (le_trans) ensures the query cost is at most M.
steps.code:
have h_cost := tarski_box_query_le_small_cost_le a (Finset.Icc a b).toList f
  rw [Finset.length_toList] at h_cost
  have h_card_le : (Finset.Icc a b).card ≤ M := by
    rw [Pi.card_Icc]
    have h1 : ∀ j, (Finset.Icc (a j) (b j)).card = (b j : ℕ) - (a j : ℕ) + 1 := by
      intro j
      rw [Fin.card_Icc]
      have : a j ≤ b j := hab j
      omega
    simp_rw [h1]
    exact hM a b hab
  exact le_trans h_cost h_card_le

glossary.List.length_cons: Prepending an element to a list increases its length by one: `(a :: as).length = as.length + 1`.
glossary.List.mem_cons: An element belongs to `b :: l` if and only if it equals `b` or belongs to `l`.
glossary.False.elim: From a contradiction (`False`), any statement follows (ex falso quodlibet).
glossary.List.mem_cons_of_mem: If an element belongs to `l`, it also belongs to `y :: l`.
glossary.tarski_subinterval_fixed_point: Any monotone function on a subinterval `[a, b]` that maps `a ≤ f(a)` and `f(b) ≤ b` has a fixed point in `[a, b]`.
glossary.Finset.mem_toList: An element is in `s.toList` if and only if it belongs to the finite set `s`.
glossary.Finset.mem_Icc: An element `x` belongs to the closed interval `Finset.Icc a b` if and only if `a ≤ x ≤ b`.
glossary.tarski_box_query_le_small_run_mem_and_fi: If a candidate list `L` contains a fixed point of `f`, the linear-search query tree on `L` terminates at a fixed point in `L`.
glossary.tarski_box_query_le_small_cost_le: The query cost of the linear-search tree on candidate list `L` is at most the length of `L`.
glossary.Finset.length_toList: The length of the list of elements of a finite set equals the set's cardinality.
glossary.Pi.card_Icc: The cardinality of a box (product interval) in a product order is the product of the cardinalities of its coordinate intervals.
glossary.Fin.card_Icc: The cardinality of a closed interval `[a, b]` in `Fin n` is `b + 1 - a`.
glossary.le_trans: The inequality relation `≤` is transitive: if `a ≤ b` and `b ≤ c`, then `a ≤ c`.

caveats: The linear arithmetic tactic `omega` is used to justify the interval length arithmetic in `Fin n` and inductive step bounds.

declarations.name: finset_sum_collision_preserving
declarations.informal: A rational-valued function x on A is collision-preserving if it satisfies every additive collision: x a + x b = x c + x d whenever a + b = c + d with a, b, c, d ∈ A.
declarations.statement: def finset_sum_collision_preserving {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] (A : Finset G) (x : G → ℚ) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Rational collision-preserving weight on A: additive relations in A force the same relations among the weights. -/
def finset_sum_collision_preserving {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] (A : Finset G) (x : G → ℚ) : Prop := ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, ∀ c ∈ A, ∀ d ∈ A, a + b = c + d → x a + x b = x c + x d

declarations.name: finset_has_no_unique_sums_exists_rep_ne
declarations.informal: If A has no unique sums and a, b ∈ A, then the sum a + b has a second representation c + d with c, d ∈ A all four of c, d distinct from a and b.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_has_no_unique_sums_exists_rep_ne {G : Type*} [AddCancelCommMonoid G] [DecidableEq G]
    {A : Finset G} (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A) {a b : G} (ha : a ∈ A) (hb : b ∈ A) :
    ∃ c ∈ A, ∃ d ∈ A, a + b = c + d ∧ c ≠ a ∧ c ≠ b ∧ d ≠ a ∧ d ≠ b
declarations.source:
/-- In a NUS set every sum of two elements has a repair whose two entries avoid both summands. -/
theorem finset_has_no_unique_sums_exists_rep_ne {G : Type*} [AddCancelCommMonoid G] [DecidableEq G]
    {A : Finset G} (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A) {a b : G} (ha : a ∈ A) (hb : b ∈ A) :
    ∃ c ∈ A, ∃ d ∈ A, a + b = c + d ∧ c ≠ a ∧ c ≠ b ∧ d ≠ a ∧ d ≠ b := by
  classical
  have h2 := hA.2 a ha b hb
  unfold finset_unordered_sum_rep_count at h2
  have h1 : 1 < (A.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = a + b)).card := by
    omega
  obtain ⟨z, hz, hz0⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_ne h1 (Sym2.mk a b)
  rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hz
  induction z using Sym2.ind with
  | h u v =>
    simp only [Sym2.lift_mk] at hz
    obtain ⟨hzA, huv⟩ := hz
    rw [Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff] at hzA
    obtain ⟨hu, hv⟩ := hzA
    refine ⟨u, hu, v, hv, huv.symm, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro h

      have hv_eq : v = b := by
        rw [h] at huv
        exact add_left_cancel huv
      subst h
      subst hv_eq
      rfl
    · intro h

        rw [h, add_comm a b] at huv
        exact add_left_cancel huv

      subst hv_eq

        exact add_right_cancel huv

      subst hu_eq

    · intro h

explanation.summary: Because $A$ has no unique sums, the element $a + b$ has at least two unordered sum representations as pairs from $A$. Since $\{a, b\}$ is one representation, there must exist another representation $\{u, v\}$ distinct from $\{a, b\}$ with $u, v \in A$ and $u + v = a + b$. By cancellativity of the commutative monoid, if either $u$ or $v$ matched either $a$ or $b$, the remaining elements would also be forced to match, yielding $\{u, v\} = \{a, b\}$ and creating a contradiction. Thus, choosing $c = u$ and $d = v$ provides a representation whose entries avoid both $a$ and $b$.

steps.claim: The finset of unordered pairs from $A$ whose sum is $a + b$ has cardinality strictly greater than 1.
steps.explanation: Because $A$ has no unique sums (`finset_has_no_unique_sums`), the number of representations of $a + b$ as an unordered sum from $A$ is at least 2. Unfolding `finset_unordered_sum_rep_count` and applying linear arithmetic over $\mathbb{N}$ shows that this cardinality is strictly greater than 1.
steps.code:
classical
  have h2 := hA.2 a ha b hb
  unfold finset_unordered_sum_rep_count at h2
  have h1 : 1 < (A.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = a + b)).card := by
    omega

steps.claim: There exists an unordered pair $z \in A.\text{sym2}$ summing to $a + b$ such that $z \ne s(a, b)$.
steps.explanation: Since the finset of pairs summing to $a + b$ contains at least two elements, `Finset.exists_mem_ne` guarantees there is an element $z$ in this set distinct from the pair $s(a, b)$.
steps.code: obtain ⟨z, hz, hz0⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_ne h1 (Sym2.mk a b)

steps.claim: The pair $z$ has the form $s(u, v)$ with $u, v \in A$ and $u + v = a + b$.
steps.explanation: By induction on the quotient type `Sym2` via `Sym2.ind`, the pair $z$ can be written as $s(u, v)$. Unfolding membership in the filtered finset using `Finset.mem_filter` and evaluating the sum with `Sym2.lift_mk` gives $u + v = a + b$. By `Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff`, membership in $A.\text{sym2}$ means both $u \in A$ and $v \in A$.
steps.code:
rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hz
  induction z using Sym2.ind with
  | h u v =>
    simp only [Sym2.lift_mk] at hz
    obtain ⟨hzA, huv⟩ := hz
    rw [Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff] at hzA
    obtain ⟨hu, hv⟩ := hzA

Choosing $c = u$ and $d = v$ reduces the goal to proving $u 
e a$, $u 
e b$, $v 
e a$, and $v 
e b$.
steps.explanation: We supply $u$ and $v$ as the existential witnesses. Since $u, v \in A$ and $a + b = u + v$, the membership and sum equalities are satisfied, leaving only the four distinctness requirements to prove.
steps.code: refine ⟨u, hu, v, hv, huv.symm, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: $u \ne a$
steps.explanation: Suppose, for contradiction, that $u = a$. Substituting this into $u + v = a + b$ yields $a + v = a + b$, which by left cancellation (`add_left_cancel`) implies $v = b$. This means $s(u, v) = s(a, b)$, contradicting the fact that $z \ne s(a, b)$.
steps.code:
· intro h
      apply hz0
      have hv_eq : v = b := by
        rw [h] at huv
        exact add_left_cancel huv
      subst h
      subst hv_eq
      rfl

steps.claim: $u \ne b$
steps.explanation: Suppose, for contradiction, that $u = b$. Rewriting $a + b$ as $b + a$ using commutativity (`add_comm`), we obtain $b + v = b + a$, which implies $v = a$ by left cancellation (`add_left_cancel`). Thus $s(u, v) = s(b, a)$, which equals $s(a, b)$ by symmetry of unordered pairs (`Sym2.eq_swap`), contradicting $z \ne s(a, b)$.

· intro h

      have hv_eq : v = a := by
        rw [h, add_comm a b] at huv
        exact add_left_cancel huv
      subst h
      subst hv_eq
      exact Sym2.eq_swap

steps.claim: $v \ne a$
steps.explanation: Suppose, for contradiction, that $v = a$. Commuting the sum $a + b$ to $b + a$ (`add_comm`), the equation becomes $u + a = b + a$. By right cancellation (`add_right_cancel`), we get $u = b$. Then $s(u, v) = s(b, a) = s(a, b)$ by `Sym2.eq_swap`, contradicting $z \ne s(a, b)$.

        rw [h, add_comm a b] at huv
        exact add_right_cancel huv
      subst h
      subst hu_eq
      exact Sym2.eq_swap

steps.claim: $v \ne b$
steps.explanation: Suppose, for contradiction, that $v = b$. Substituting this into $u + v = a + b$ gives $u + b = a + b$, so right cancellation (`add_right_cancel`) forces $u = a$. Hence $s(u, v) = s(a, b)$, contradicting $z \ne s(a, b)$.

glossary.add_comm: Addition in a commutative magma satisfies $a + b = b + a$.
glossary.add_left_cancel: In an additive structure with left cancellation, $a + b = a + c$ implies $b = c$.
glossary.add_right_cancel: In an additive structure with right cancellation, $a + b = c + b$ implies $a = c$.
glossary.Finset.exists_mem_ne: In any finite set with cardinality strictly greater than 1, there exists an element distinct from any specified element.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finset if and only if it belongs to the base finset and satisfies the filtering predicate.
glossary.Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff: An unordered pair $s(a, b)$ belongs to the symmetric square of a finset $s$ if and only if both $a \in s$ and $b \in s$.
glossary.Sym2.eq_swap: The unordered pair $s(a, b)$ is equal to $s(b, a)$.
glossary.Sym2.ind: To prove a property for all elements of $\text{Sym2}(\alpha)$, it suffices to prove it for pairs of the form $s(x, y)$.
glossary.Sym2.lift_mk: Evaluating the lift of a symmetric function to $\text{Sym2}$ on an unordered pair $s(a, b)$ gives the value of the function on $(a, b)$.

caveats: The proof formalizes unordered pairs of elements from $G$ using the symmetric square quotient type `Sym2 G`, where $s(x, y)$ denotes the unordered pair $\{x, y\}$.

declarations.name: finset_has_no_unique_sums_max_layer
declarations.informal: Let A be NUS and let x be a rational collision-preserving weight on A. Then the set of elements of A maximizing x (i.e. {a ∈ A : x a = M} for a value M attained and dominating all of x on A) is again NUS.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_has_no_unique_sums_max_layer {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] [DecidableEq G]
    {A : Finset G} (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A) (x : G → ℚ)
    (hx : finset_sum_collision_preserving A x) (M : ℚ)
    (hM : ∀ a ∈ A, x a ≤ M) (hMne : ∃ a ∈ A, x a = M) :
    finset_has_no_unique_sums (A.filter (fun a => x a = M))
declarations.source:
/-- The top layer of a collision-preserving weight on a NUS set is again NUS: this is the maximum-layer argument behind Lemma 2.1 of arXiv:2610.09349. -/
theorem finset_has_no_unique_sums_max_layer {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G] [DecidableEq G]
    {A : Finset G} (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A) (x : G → ℚ)
    (hx : finset_sum_collision_preserving A x) (M : ℚ)
    (hM : ∀ a ∈ A, x a ≤ M) (hMne : ∃ a ∈ A, x a = M) :
    finset_has_no_unique_sums (A.filter (fun a => x a = M)) := by
  classical
  set L : Finset G := A.filter (fun a => x a = M) with hL
  have hmemL : ∀ a, a ∈ L ↔ a ∈ A ∧ x a = M := by
    intro a; rw [hL, Finset.mem_filter]
  have hAL : L ⊆ A := by rw [hL]; exact Finset.filter_subset _ _
  have key : ∀ p ∈ L, ∀ q ∈ L, ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, a + b = p + q → x a = M ∧ x b = M := by
    intro p hp q hq a ha b hb hab
    obtain ⟨hpA, hpM⟩ := (hmemL p).mp hp
    obtain ⟨hqA, hqM⟩ := (hmemL q).mp hq
    have hcol : x a + x b = x p + x q := hx a ha b hb p hpA q hqA hab
    have ha' : x a ≤ M := hM a ha
    have hb' : x b ≤ M := hM b hb
    constructor <;> linarith
  constructor
  · obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀A, ha₀M⟩ := hMne
    have ha₀L : a₀ ∈ L := (hmemL a₀).mpr ⟨ha₀A, ha₀M⟩
    have hrep : 2 ≤ finset_unordered_sum_rep_count A (a₀ + a₀) := hA.2 a₀ ha₀A a₀ ha₀A
    have hcard : 1 < (A.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = a₀ + a₀)).card := hrep
    obtain ⟨z, hzS, hzne⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_ne hcard (Sym2.mk a₀ a₀)
    obtain ⟨c, d, hcd⟩ := (Sym2.exists (α := G) (f := fun w => w = z)).mp ⟨z, rfl⟩
    have hzS' : Sym2.mk c d ∈ A.sym2.filter (fun w => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ w = a₀ + a₀) := by
      rw [hcd]; exact hzS
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hzS'
    obtain ⟨hzA, hzsum⟩ := hzS'
    obtain ⟨hcA, hdA⟩ := Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff.mp hzA
    have hsum : c + d = a₀ + a₀ := by
      rw [Sym2.lift_mk] at hzsum; exact hzsum
    obtain ⟨hcM, hdM⟩ := key a₀ ha₀L a₀ ha₀L c hcA d hdA hsum
    have hne : c ≠ a₀ ∨ d ≠ a₀ := by
      by_contra h
      simp only [not_or, not_not] at h
      exact hzne (by rw [← hcd, h.1, h.2])
    rcases hne with h | h
    · exact Finset.one_lt_card.mpr ⟨a₀, ha₀L, c, (hmemL c).mpr ⟨hcA, hcM⟩, Ne.symm h⟩
    · exact Finset.one_lt_card.mpr ⟨a₀, ha₀L, d, (hmemL d).mpr ⟨hdA, hdM⟩, Ne.symm h⟩
  · intro p hp q hq
    have hpA : p ∈ A := hAL hp
    have hqA : q ∈ A := hAL hq
    have hset : (A.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = p + q))
        = (L.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = p + q)) := by
      ext z
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hzA, hz⟩
        refine ⟨Finset.mem_sym2_iff.mpr ?_, hz⟩
        intro a ha
        obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := Sym2.mem_iff_exists.mp ha
        have hbA : b ∈ A := by
          have h1 : Sym2.mk a b ∈ A.sym2 := by rw [← hb]; exact hzA
          exact (Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff.mp h1).2
        have hab : a + b = p + q := by
          rw [hb, Sym2.lift_mk] at hz; exact hz
        exact (hmemL a).mpr ⟨Finset.mem_sym2_iff.mp hzA a ha,
          (key p hp q hq a (Finset.mem_sym2_iff.mp hzA a ha) b hbA hab).1⟩
      · rintro ⟨hzL, hz⟩
        exact ⟨Finset.sym2_mono hAL hzL, hz⟩
    have h1 : finset_unordered_sum_rep_count L (p + q)
        = (L.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = p + q)).card := rfl
    have h2 : finset_unordered_sum_rep_count A (p + q)
        = (A.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = p + q)).card := rfl
    rw [h1, ← hset, ← h2]
    exact hA.2 p hpA q hqA

explanation.summary: To show that the maximal layer L = {a ∈ A : x a = M} of a collision-preserving weight on a NUS set A is again NUS, the proof relies on a rigid conservation property: if two elements of A sum to the same value as two elements of L, both must have weight M and therefore also belong to L. Applying this to a duplicated element a₀ ∈ L whose sum a₀ + a₀ has a second representation in A produces a second element in L, showing |L| ≥ 2. Furthermore, the conservation property ensures that the unordered representations of any sum p + q with p, q ∈ L in L are exactly its representations in A, so every such sum inherits at least two representations from A.

steps.claim: Definition of the top layer L = {a ∈ A : x a = M}, its membership characterization, and the inclusion L ⊆ A.
steps.explanation: We work under classical logic (line 7). We define L as the subset of A where x takes its maximum value M (line 8). By definition of Finset.filter, an element a belongs to L if and only if a ∈ A and x a = M (lines 9-10). Because L is obtained by filtering A, it is a subset of A (line 11).
steps.code:
classical
  set L : Finset G := A.filter (fun a => x a = M) with hL
  have hmemL : ∀ a, a ∈ L ↔ a ∈ A ∧ x a = M := by
    intro a; rw [hL, Finset.mem_filter]
  have hAL : L ⊆ A := by rw [hL]; exact Finset.filter_subset _ _

steps.claim: Key property: any decomposition in A of a sum of two elements of L must consist entirely of elements of L.
steps.explanation: Let p, q ∈ L and a, b ∈ A with a + b = p + q. Since p, q ∈ L, we have x p = M and x q = M. Because x is collision-preserving, x a + x b = x p + x q = 2M. Since M is the maximum of x on A, both x a ≤ M and x b ≤ M hold. Linear rational arithmetic (linarith) on these bounds and the sum forces x a = M and x b = M, so both a and b belong to L.
steps.code:
have key : ∀ p ∈ L, ∀ q ∈ L, ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, a + b = p + q → x a = M ∧ x b = M := by
    intro p hp q hq a ha b hb hab
    obtain ⟨hpA, hpM⟩ := (hmemL p).mp hp
    obtain ⟨hqA, hqM⟩ := (hmemL q).mp hq
    have hcol : x a + x b = x p + x q := hx a ha b hb p hpA q hqA hab
    have ha' : x a ≤ M := hM a ha
    have hb' : x b ≤ M := hM b hb
    constructor <;> linarith

steps.claim: First NUS condition: the top layer L contains at least two elements (|L| ≥ 2).
steps.explanation: We split the NUS property into two goals: showing |L| ≥ 2 and showing that every sum has at least two representations in L (line 20). By assumption, M is attained at some a₀ ∈ A, so a₀ ∈ L (lines 21-22). Since A has no unique sums, the sum a₀ + a₀ has at least two unordered representations from A, so its representation finset has cardinality > 1 (lines 23-24). Hence there is an unordered pair z in A different from {a₀, a₀} summing to a₀ + a₀ (line 25). Writing z as an unordered pair {c, d} with c, d ∈ A, we have c + d = a₀ + a₀ (lines 26-33). By the key property, x c = M and x d = M, so c, d ∈ L (line 34). Because {c, d} ≠ {a₀, a₀}, we must have c ≠ a₀ or d ≠ a₀ (lines 35-38). Either case provides an element in L distinct from a₀, proving |L| ≥ 2 (lines 39-41).
steps.code:
constructor
  · obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀A, ha₀M⟩ := hMne
    have ha₀L : a₀ ∈ L := (hmemL a₀).mpr ⟨ha₀A, ha₀M⟩
    have hrep : 2 ≤ finset_unordered_sum_rep_count A (a₀ + a₀) := hA.2 a₀ ha₀A a₀ ha₀A
    have hcard : 1 < (A.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = a₀ + a₀)).card := hrep
    obtain ⟨z, hzS, hzne⟩ := Finset.exists_mem_ne hcard (Sym2.mk a₀ a₀)
    obtain ⟨c, d, hcd⟩ := (Sym2.exists (α := G) (f := fun w => w = z)).mp ⟨z, rfl⟩
    have hzS' : Sym2.mk c d ∈ A.sym2.filter (fun w => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ w = a₀ + a₀) := by
      rw [hcd]; exact hzS
    rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hzS'
    obtain ⟨hzA, hzsum⟩ := hzS'
    obtain ⟨hcA, hdA⟩ := Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff.mp hzA
    have hsum : c + d = a₀ + a₀ := by
      rw [Sym2.lift_mk] at hzsum; exact hzsum
    obtain ⟨hcM, hdM⟩ := key a₀ ha₀L a₀ ha₀L c hcA d hdA hsum
    have hne : c ≠ a₀ ∨ d ≠ a₀ := by
      by_contra h
      simp only [not_or, not_not] at h
      exact hzne (by rw [← hcd, h.1, h.2])
    rcases hne with h | h
    · exact Finset.one_lt_card.mpr ⟨a₀, ha₀L, c, (hmemL c).mpr ⟨hcA, hcM⟩, Ne.symm h⟩
    · exact Finset.one_lt_card.mpr ⟨a₀, ha₀L, d, (hmemL d).mpr ⟨hdA, hdM⟩, Ne.symm h⟩

steps.claim: For any p, q ∈ L, the set of unordered pairs from L summing to p + q is identical to the set of unordered pairs from A summing to p + q.
steps.explanation: Let p, q ∈ L. We show equality of the two sets of representations by extensionality (lines 42-49). For the forward inclusion, take an unordered pair z from A with sum p + q. For any element a in z, we write z = {a, b} for some b ∈ A; then a + b = p + q. Applying the key property, we obtain x a = M, so a ∈ L. Since this holds for every element of z, the pair z consists of elements of L (lines 50-60). For the reverse inclusion, any pair from L is already a pair from A because L ⊆ A, which implies L.sym2 ⊆ A.sym2 (lines 61-62).
steps.code:
· intro p hp q hq
    have hpA : p ∈ A := hAL hp
    have hqA : q ∈ A := hAL hq
    have hset : (A.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = p + q))
        = (L.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = p + q)) := by
      ext z
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
      constructor
      · rintro ⟨hzA, hz⟩
        refine ⟨Finset.mem_sym2_iff.mpr ?_, hz⟩
        intro a ha
        obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := Sym2.mem_iff_exists.mp ha
        have hbA : b ∈ A := by
          have h1 : Sym2.mk a b ∈ A.sym2 := by rw [← hb]; exact hzA
          exact (Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff.mp h1).2
        have hab : a + b = p + q := by
          rw [hb, Sym2.lift_mk] at hz; exact hz
        exact (hmemL a).mpr ⟨Finset.mem_sym2_iff.mp hzA a ha,
          (key p hp q hq a (Finset.mem_sym2_iff.mp hzA a ha) b hbA hab).1⟩
      · rintro ⟨hzL, hz⟩
        exact ⟨Finset.sym2_mono hAL hzL, hz⟩

steps.claim: Second NUS condition: every sum in L has at least two representations in L, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: By definition, the representation count of p + q in L and in A are the cardinalities of the respective sets of summing pairs (lines 63-66). Since these two sets are equal by the previous step, the representation counts are identical (line 67). Because A has no unique sums, the count in A is at least 2, and therefore the count in L is also at least 2 (line 68).
steps.code:
have h1 : finset_unordered_sum_rep_count L (p + q)
        = (L.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = p + q)).card := rfl
    have h2 : finset_unordered_sum_rep_count A (p + q)
        = (A.sym2.filter (fun z => Sym2.lift ⟨fun a b => a + b, fun a b => add_comm a b⟩ z = p + q)).card := rfl
    rw [h1, ← hset, ← h2]
    exact hA.2 p hpA q hqA

glossary.Finset.mem_filter: An element belongs to a filtered finset s.filter p if and only if it belongs to s and satisfies the predicate p.
glossary.Finset.filter_subset: Any filtered finset s.filter p is a subset of s.
glossary.Finset.exists_mem_ne: If a finite set has cardinality strictly greater than 1, then for any given element there exists an element in the set distinct from it.
glossary.Sym2.exists: There exists an element in the symmetric square satisfying a property if and only if there exist two elements whose unordered pair satisfies it.
glossary.Finset.mk_mem_sym2_iff.mp: If an unordered pair s(c, d) belongs to the symmetric square s.sym2, then both c and d belong to s.
glossary.Sym2.lift_mk: Evaluating the symmetric lift of a commutative binary operation on an unordered pair s(a, b) yields the operation applied to a and b.
glossary.not_or: The negation of a disjunction ¬(p ∨ q) is equivalent to ¬p ∧ ¬q.
glossary.not_not: Double negation elimination: ¬¬p is equivalent to p.
glossary.Finset.one_lt_card.mpr: If a finset contains two distinct elements, its cardinality is strictly greater than 1 (at least 2).
glossary.Ne.symm: Inequality is symmetric: if a ≠ b, then b ≠ a.
glossary.Finset.mem_sym2_iff.mpr: An unordered pair belongs to the symmetric square s.sym2 if every element in the pair belongs to s.
glossary.Sym2.mem_iff_exists.mp: If an element x belongs to an unordered pair z, then z = s(x, y) for some y.
glossary.Finset.mem_sym2_iff.mp: If an unordered pair belongs to s.sym2, then every element in the pair belongs to s.
glossary.Finset.sym2_mono: The symmetric square operation preserves inclusions: if s ⊆ t, then s.sym2 ⊆ t.sym2.

caveats: In Mathlib, representations of a sum as an unordered pair from a finset A are formalized as elements of the symmetric square `A.sym2` whose sum (evaluated via `Sym2.lift`) equals the target.
The definition `finset_has_no_unique_sums A` requires both `2 ≤ A.card` and that every sum of two elements of A has at least two representations as unordered pairs from A.

declarations.name: finset_sum_collision_preserving_const_of_minimal
declarations.informal: If A is NUS, no proper subset of A is NUS (A is inclusion-minimal), and x is a rational collision-preserving weight on A, then x is constant on A.
declarations.statement:
theorem finset_sum_collision_preserving_const_of_minimal {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G]
    [DecidableEq G] {A : Finset G} (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A)
    (hmin : ∀ B : Finset G, B ⊂ A → ¬ finset_has_no_unique_sums B)
    {x : G → ℚ} (hx : finset_sum_collision_preserving A x) :
    ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, x a = x b
declarations.source:
/-- Lemma 2.1 (rational half) of arXiv:2610.09349: a collision-preserving rational weight on an inclusion-minimal NUS set is constant. -/
theorem finset_sum_collision_preserving_const_of_minimal {G : Type*} [AddCommMonoid G]
    [DecidableEq G] {A : Finset G} (hA : finset_has_no_unique_sums A)
    (hmin : ∀ B : Finset G, B ⊂ A → ¬ finset_has_no_unique_sums B)
    {x : G → ℚ} (hx : finset_sum_collision_preserving A x) :
    ∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, x a = x b := by
  have hne : A.Nonempty := by
    have h := hA.1
    exact Finset.card_pos.mp (by omega)
  obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀, hmax⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image A x hne
  have hNUS : finset_has_no_unique_sums (A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀)) :=
    finset_has_no_unique_sums_max_layer hA x hx (x a₀) (fun a ha => hmax a ha) ⟨a₀, ha₀, rfl⟩
  have hsub : A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀) ⊆ A := Finset.filter_subset _ _
  have heq : A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀) = A := by
    by_contra hne'
    exact hmin _ (Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.mpr ⟨hsub, hne'⟩) hNUS
  intro a ha b hb
  have ha' : x a = x a₀ := by
    have : a ∈ A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀) := by rw [heq]; exact ha
    exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp this).2
  have hb' : x b = x a₀ := by
    have : b ∈ A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀) := by rw [heq]; exact hb
    exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp this).2
  rw [ha', hb']

explanation.summary: Since A is a nonempty finite set, the rational weight x attains its maximum at some element a₀ ∈ A. By a key structural lemma, the maximum-weight layer {a ∈ A | x a = x a₀} is itself a NUS set. Because A is inclusion-minimal among NUS sets, this layer cannot be a proper subset and must equal all of A. It follows that every element of A has weight x a₀, so x is constant on A.

steps.claim: A is nonempty.
steps.explanation: By definition of a NUS set, A has cardinality at least 2. In particular, its cardinality is strictly positive by linear arithmetic, which implies that A is nonempty by Finset.card_pos.mp.
steps.code:
have hne : A.Nonempty := by
    have h := hA.1
    exact Finset.card_pos.mp (by omega)

steps.claim: There exists an element a₀ ∈ A maximizing x on A.
steps.explanation: Because A is a nonempty finite set and the values of x lie in the linearly ordered field ℚ, Finset.exists_max_image guarantees that x attains a maximum at some a₀ ∈ A, so x a' ≤ x a₀ for all a' ∈ A.
steps.code: obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀, hmax⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image A x hne

steps.claim: The maximum-weight layer {a ∈ A | x a = x a₀} is also a NUS set.
steps.explanation: By finset_has_no_unique_sums_max_layer, since A is NUS, x is collision-preserving on A, x a ≤ x a₀ for all a ∈ A, and the upper bound x a₀ is achieved at a₀ ∈ A, the level set of elements achieving this maximum is itself a NUS set.
steps.code:
have hNUS : finset_has_no_unique_sums (A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀)) :=
    finset_has_no_unique_sums_max_layer hA x hx (x a₀) (fun a ha => hmax a ha) ⟨a₀, ha₀, rfl⟩

steps.claim: The maximum-weight layer {a ∈ A | x a = x a₀} equals all of A.
steps.explanation: The maximum-weight layer is a subset of A by Finset.filter_subset. If it were not all of A, it would be a proper subset by Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.mpr; but the minimality hypothesis hmin asserts that no proper subset of A can be NUS, which contradicts the fact that this layer is NUS. Thus the layer must be equal to A.
steps.code:
have hsub : A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀) ⊆ A := Finset.filter_subset _ _
  have heq : A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀) = A := by
    by_contra hne'
    exact hmin _ (Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.mpr ⟨hsub, hne'⟩) hNUS

steps.claim: The weight function x is constant on A: for all a, b ∈ A, x a = x b.
steps.explanation: Given any a, b ∈ A, rewriting with {c ∈ A | x c = x a₀} = A shows that both a and b belong to the maximum-weight layer. By Finset.mem_filter.mp, this means x a = x a₀ and x b = x a₀, and therefore x a = x b.
steps.code:
intro a ha b hb
  have ha' : x a = x a₀ := by
    have : a ∈ A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀) := by rw [heq]; exact ha
    exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp this).2
  have hb' : x b = x a₀ := by
    have : b ∈ A.filter (fun a => x a = x a₀) := by rw [heq]; exact hb
    exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp this).2
  rw [ha', hb']

glossary.Finset.card_pos.mp: A finite set is nonempty if and only if its cardinality is strictly positive.
glossary.Finset.exists_max_image: A real- or linearly-ordered-valued function on a nonempty finite set attains its maximum at some element of the set.
glossary.finset_has_no_unique_sums_max_layer: If A is a NUS set and x is a collision-preserving weight on A bounded by M that attains M, the maximum-weight layer {a ∈ A | x a = M} is also a NUS set.
glossary.Finset.filter_subset: Filtering a finite set by a predicate yields a subset of the original set.
glossary.Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne.mpr: A subset that is not equal to the superset is a strict (proper) subset.
glossary.Finset.mem_filter.mp: An element belongs to a filtered finite set if and only if it belongs to the set and satisfies the predicate.

declarations.name: nus_min_card_five_eq_four
declarations.informal: The minimal size of a set with no unique sums in Z/5Z is exactly 4 (witness {0,1,2,3}; no set of size ≤ 3 works).
declarations.statement: theorem nus_min_card_five_eq_four : nus_min_card 5 = 4
declarations.source:
/-- m(5) = 4: the least NUS subset of Z/5Z has four elements. -/
theorem nus_min_card_five_eq_four : nus_min_card 5 = 4 := by
  have hno : ∀ A : Finset (ZMod 5), A.card ≤ 3 → ¬ finset_has_no_unique_sums A := by decide
  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · exact nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums ({0,1,2,3} : Finset (ZMod 5)) (by decide)
  · haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 5) := ⟨by norm_num⟩
    unfold nus_min_card
    refine le_csInf ?_ ?_
    · exact ⟨(Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod 5)).card, Finset.univ, finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod (by norm_num), rfl⟩
    · rintro b ⟨A, hA, rfl⟩
      by_contra h
      exact hno A (by omega) hA

explanation.summary: The theorem proves that the minimal size of a subset with no unique sums in ℤ/5ℤ is 4 by establishing both inequalities nus_min_card 5 ≤ 4 and 4 ≤ nus_min_card 5 via antisymmetry. The upper bound is witnessed by the 4-element subset {0, 1, 2, 3}, verified computationally by `decide`. The lower bound holds because the set of NUS cardinalities is nonempty (witnessed by the whole space ℤ/5ℤ) and an exhaustive finite search (`decide`) confirms that no subset of size at most 3 has no unique sums.

steps.claim: No subset of ℤ/5ℤ of cardinality at most 3 has the no-unique-sums property.
steps.explanation: The decision procedure (`decide`) exhaustively inspects all subsets of ℤ/5ℤ of size at most 3 and verifies that none of them satisfies `finset_has_no_unique_sums`.
steps.code: have hno : ∀ A : Finset (ZMod 5), A.card ≤ 3 → ¬ finset_has_no_unique_sums A := by decide

steps.claim: To prove nus_min_card 5 = 4, it suffices to show nus_min_card 5 ≤ 4 and 4 ≤ nus_min_card 5.
steps.explanation: Equality in the natural numbers is reduced to the two inequalities nus_min_card 5 ≤ 4 and 4 ≤ nus_min_card 5 by antisymmetry of the order (`le_antisymm`).
steps.code: refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_

steps.claim: The minimal cardinality is at most 4 (nus_min_card 5 ≤ 4).
steps.explanation: The four-element subset {0, 1, 2, 3} ⊆ ℤ/5ℤ is checked by finite evaluation (`decide`) to have no unique sums. Applying `nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums` with this witness yields the upper bound.
steps.code: · exact nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums ({0,1,2,3} : Finset (ZMod 5)) (by decide)

steps.claim: To establish 4 ≤ nus_min_card 5, it suffices to show that every subset with no unique sums has cardinality at least 4.
steps.explanation: After establishing the primality of 5 and unfolding `nus_min_card 5` as the infimum of the cardinalities of NUS subsets, `le_csInf` reduces the lower bound to two checks: that the set of such cardinalities is nonempty, and that 4 bounds every element from below. Nonemptiness is witnessed by the full universe ℤ/5ℤ, which has no unique sums by `finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod` since 5 is prime and 5 ≠ 2.
steps.code:
· haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 5) := ⟨by norm_num⟩
    unfold nus_min_card
    refine le_csInf ?_ ?_
    · exact ⟨(Finset.univ : Finset (ZMod 5)).card, Finset.univ, finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod (by norm_num), rfl⟩

steps.claim: Every subset of ℤ/5ℤ with no unique sums has cardinality at least 4, completing the lower bound.
steps.explanation: Let A be an arbitrary subset with no unique sums. If |A| < 4, then |A| ≤ 3 by integer arithmetic (`omega`). But this contradicts the helper statement `hno` established on line 3, which asserts that no subset of size at most 3 has no unique sums. Therefore, |A| ≥ 4.
steps.code:
· rintro b ⟨A, hA, rfl⟩
      by_contra h
      exact hno A (by omega) hA

glossary.le_antisymm: In any partial order, if a ≤ b and b ≤ a, then a = b.
glossary.nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums: If a finite subset A of ℤ/pℤ has no unique sums, then the minimal cardinality nus_min_card p is at most |A|.
glossary.le_csInf: In a conditionally complete lattice, if a set s is nonempty and a is a lower bound for every element of s, then a ≤ sInf s.
glossary.finset_has_no_unique_sums_univ_zmod: For any prime p ≠ 2, the entire group ℤ/pℤ (as the universal Finset) has no unique sums.

caveats: The exhaustive check that no subset of ℤ/5ℤ of size at most 3 has no unique sums (line 3), as well as the verification that {0, 1, 2, 3} does have no unique sums (line 5), are discharged by Lean's computational evaluator `decide` by evaluating all possibilities.

/-- A request in online paging with deadlines. -/
structure DeadlineRequest (α : Type*) where
  page : α
  arrival : ℕ
  deadline : ℕ
  h_deadline : arrival ≤ deadline

declarations.statement: theorem nus_min_card_seven_eq_five : nus_min_card 7 = 5

/-- m(7) = 5: the least NUS subset of Z/7Z has five elements. -/
theorem nus_min_card_seven_eq_five : nus_min_card 7 = 5 := by

  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
  · exact nus_min_card_le_of_has_no_unique_sums ({0,1,2,3,4} : Finset (ZMod 7)) (by decide)
  · unfold nus_min_card
    refine le_csInf ⟨5, {0,1,2,3,4}, by decide, rfl⟩ ?_
    rintro b ⟨A, hA, rfl⟩
    by_contra h
    exact hno A (by omega) hA

For the upper bound, the explicit 5-element subset {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} is verified by computation to have no unique sums. For the lower bound, an exhaustive check confirms that every subset of size at most 4 fails the condition, so the infimum of all valid sizes must be at least 5.

declarations.name: IsFeasibleSchedule
declarations.informal: A schedule of cache configurations of size at most k is feasible for a list of deadline requests starting from initial cache C₀ if it starts at C₀, keeps cache size at most k at all times, and caches each requested page at some time between its arrival and deadline.
declarations.statement:
def IsFeasibleSchedule {α : Type*} (k : ℕ) (C₀ : Finset α)
    (sched : ℕ → Finset α) (reqs : List (DeadlineRequest α)) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Feasibility of a cache schedule for an instance of paging with deadlines. -/
def IsFeasibleSchedule {α : Type*} (k : ℕ) (C₀ : Finset α)
    (sched : ℕ → Finset α) (reqs : List (DeadlineRequest α)) : Prop :=
  sched 0 = C₀ ∧
  (∀ t, (sched t).card ≤ k) ∧
  (∀ r ∈ reqs, ∃ t, r.arrival ≤ t ∧ t ≤ r.deadline ∧ r.page ∈ sched t)
declarations.reading:
Given a type `α`, a natural number `k`, an initial finite set `C₀ : Finset α`, a schedule `sched : ℕ → Finset α`, and a list `reqs` of deadline requests (each having a page `r.page : α`, arrival time `r.arrival : ℕ`, deadline `r.deadline : ℕ`, and a proof that `r.arrival ≤ r.deadline`), `IsFeasibleSchedule k C₀ sched reqs` asserts that:

1. `sched 0 = C₀` (the schedule starts at configuration `C₀` at time 0),
2. For all `t : ℕ`, the cardinality of `sched t` is at most `k`, and
3. For every request `r` in `reqs`, there exists a time `t : ℕ` such that `r.arrival ≤ t`, `t ≤ r.deadline`, and `r.page ∈ sched t`.

declarations.name: tarski_slice_subbox_monotone_and_fixed
declarations.informal: For any monotone map f on [a, b] in dimension k+1 and any coordinate cut c with a_i <= c <= b_i, the sliced map g y j = f (insertNth i c y) (i.succAbove j) is monotone on [a', b'] (where a' = a ∘ i.succAbove, b' = b ∘ i.succAbove) and satisfies the sub-box invariants a' <= g a' and g b' <= b'. Moreover, any fixed point y of g lifts to an ambient point x = insertNth i c y in [a, b] that agrees with f(x) on all coordinates j != i.
declarations.statement:
theorem tarski_slice_subbox_monotone_and_fixed (n k : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (f : (Fin (k+1) → Fin n) → (Fin (k+1) → Fin n)) (hf : Monotone f)
    (a b : Fin (k+1) → Fin n) (ha : a ≤ f a) (hb : f b ≤ b)
    (i : Fin (k+1)) (c : Fin n) (hac : a i ≤ c) (hcb : c ≤ b i) :
    let g : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n) := fun y j => f (Fin.insertNth i c y) (i.succAbove j)
    let a' : Fin k → Fin n := a ∘ i.succAbove
    let b' : Fin k → Fin n := b ∘ i.succAbove
    Monotone g ∧ a' ≤ g a' ∧ g b' ≤ b' ∧
    ∀ y : Fin k → Fin n, a' ≤ y → y ≤ b' → g y = y →
      let x := Fin.insertNth i c y
      a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b ∧ (∀ j : Fin (k+1), j ≠ i → f x j = x j)
declarations.source:
/-- Monotonicity and sub-box bounds for the coordinate slice map, and lifting of a slice fixed point to an ambient point fixed off coordinate i. -/
theorem tarski_slice_subbox_monotone_and_fixed (n k : ℕ) [NeZero n]
    (f : (Fin (k+1) → Fin n) → (Fin (k+1) → Fin n)) (hf : Monotone f)
    (a b : Fin (k+1) → Fin n) (ha : a ≤ f a) (hb : f b ≤ b)
    (i : Fin (k+1)) (c : Fin n) (hac : a i ≤ c) (hcb : c ≤ b i) :
    let g : (Fin k → Fin n) → (Fin k → Fin n) := fun y j => f (Fin.insertNth i c y) (i.succAbove j)
    let a' : Fin k → Fin n := a ∘ i.succAbove
    let b' : Fin k → Fin n := b ∘ i.succAbove
    Monotone g ∧ a' ≤ g a' ∧ g b' ≤ b' ∧
    ∀ y : Fin k → Fin n, a' ≤ y → y ≤ b' → g y = y →
      let x := Fin.insertNth i c y
      a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b ∧ (∀ j : Fin (k+1), j ≠ i → f x j = x j) := by
  dsimp only
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro y y' hyy'
    intro j
    refine hf (Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩) (i.succAbove j)
    · rw [Fin.insertNth_apply_same]
    · intro l
      simp only [Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove]
      exact hyy' l
  · intro j
    apply le_trans (ha (i.succAbove j))
    exact hf (Fin.le_insertNth_iff.mpr ⟨hac, le_refl _⟩) (i.succAbove j)
  · intro j
    apply le_trans (hf (Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr ⟨hcb, le_refl _⟩) (i.succAbove j))
    exact hb (i.succAbove j)
  · intro y hay hyb hgy
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact Fin.le_insertNth_iff.mpr ⟨hac, hay⟩
    · exact Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr ⟨hcb, hyb⟩
    · intro j hj
      obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := Fin.exists_succAbove_eq hj
      subst hm
      simp only [Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove]
      exact congr_fun hgy m

explanation.summary: The theorem reduces to four claims about the coordinate slice map g obtained by fixing coordinate i to value c. Monotonicity of g follows from that of f because coordinate insertion preserves the product ordering. The sub-box invariants a' ≤ g a' and g b' ≤ b' follow by transitivity from the ambient box invariants on f combined with the cut bounds a i ≤ c ≤ b i. Finally, any fixed point y of g in [a', b'] lifts by coordinate insertion to an ambient point x in [a, b] which agrees with f(x) away from coordinate i because each index j ≠ i corresponds to a slice coordinate m where f(x)_j = g(y)_m = y_m = x_j.

steps.claim: The theorem reduces to four independent claims: monotonicity of g, the lower invariant a' ≤ g a', the upper invariant g b' ≤ b', and the fixed-point lifting property.
steps.explanation: We simplify the definitions of the coordinate slice map g and the projected lower and upper bounds a' and b', and split the four-part conjunction into four separate goals.
steps.code:
dsimp only
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: The coordinate slice map g is monotone.
steps.explanation: Let y ≤ y' and let j be any coordinate in Fin k. To show g y j ≤ g y' j, by monotonicity of f it suffices to show that inserting c at index i into y yields a vector bounded by the corresponding insertion into y'. At index i, both vectors evaluate to c by Fin.insertNth_apply_same. At any other coordinate, indexed by l via succAbove, Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove reduces the inequality to y l ≤ y' l, which holds by assumption. Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr combines these two coordinate checks to establish the vector inequality, completing the step.
steps.code:
· intro y y' hyy'
    intro j
    refine hf (Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr ⟨?_, ?_⟩) (i.succAbove j)
    · rw [Fin.insertNth_apply_same]
    · intro l
      simp only [Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove]
      exact hyy' l

steps.claim: The slice map satisfies the lower sub-box invariant a' ≤ g a'.
steps.explanation: For any coordinate j, the ambient lower invariant a ≤ f a implies a' j = a (i.succAbove j) ≤ f a (i.succAbove j). Using Fin.le_insertNth_iff.mpr with the hypothesis a i ≤ c (hac) and reflexivity a' ≤ a' (le_refl), we have a ≤ Fin.insertNth i c a'. Since f is monotone, f a ≤ f (Fin.insertNth i c a') = g a'. By transitivity (le_trans), a' j ≤ g a' j.
steps.code:
· intro j
    apply le_trans (ha (i.succAbove j))
    exact hf (Fin.le_insertNth_iff.mpr ⟨hac, le_refl _⟩) (i.succAbove j)

steps.claim: The slice map satisfies the upper sub-box invariant g b' ≤ b'.
steps.explanation: For any coordinate j, the hypothesis c ≤ b i (hcb) and reflexivity b' ≤ b' (le_refl) imply Fin.insertNth i c b' ≤ b by Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr. Monotonicity of f then gives g b' j = f (Fin.insertNth i c b') (i.succAbove j) ≤ f b (i.succAbove j). Combining this with the ambient upper invariant f b (i.succAbove j) ≤ b' j via transitivity (le_trans) yields g b' j ≤ b' j.
steps.code:
· intro j
    apply le_trans (hf (Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr ⟨hcb, le_refl _⟩) (i.succAbove j))
    exact hb (i.succAbove j)

steps.claim: Any fixed point y of g in [a', b'] lifts to a point x in [a, b] that agrees with f x on all coordinates j ≠ i.
steps.explanation: Given y with a' ≤ y ≤ b' and g y = y, define x = Fin.insertNth i c y. The bound a ≤ x follows from a i ≤ c and a' ≤ y via Fin.le_insertNth_iff.mpr, and x ≤ b follows from c ≤ b i and y ≤ b' via Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr, so x lies in [a, b]. For any coordinate j ≠ i, Fin.exists_succAbove_eq gives an index m with j = i.succAbove m. By Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove, x (i.succAbove m) = y m, and evaluating the fixed-point equation g y = y at m via congr_fun shows that f x j = g y m = y m = x j.
steps.code:
· intro y hay hyb hgy
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · exact Fin.le_insertNth_iff.mpr ⟨hac, hay⟩
    · exact Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr ⟨hcb, hyb⟩
    · intro j hj
      obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := Fin.exists_succAbove_eq hj
      subst hm
      simp only [Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove]
      exact congr_fun hgy m

glossary.Fin.insertNth_apply_same: Evaluating a vector with x inserted at index i at index i itself gives x.
glossary.Fin.insertNth_apply_succAbove: Evaluating a vector with x inserted at index i at any coordinate other than i (written as i.succAbove j) gives the j-th component of the original vector.
glossary.Fin.insertNth_le_iff.mpr: The vector obtained by inserting x at index i into p is coordinatewise bounded by q if x ≤ q i and p is coordinatewise bounded by q on all remaining coordinates.
glossary.Fin.le_insertNth_iff.mpr: A vector q is coordinatewise bounded by the result of inserting x at index i into p if q i ≤ x and q on all remaining coordinates is bounded by p.
glossary.le_trans: Transitivity of order: if a ≤ b and b ≤ c, then a ≤ c.
glossary.le_refl: Reflexivity of order: a ≤ a for every a.
glossary.Fin.exists_succAbove_eq: Every index j ≠ i in Fin (k + 1) can be uniquely written as i.succAbove m for some m in Fin k.
glossary.congr_fun: Equality of functions implies equality of their evaluations: if f = g, then f a = g a.

caveats: The function `Fin.succAbove i : Fin k → Fin (k + 1)` embeds dimension k into dimension k + 1 by skipping index i. Its counterpart `Fin.insertNth i c y` inserts the coordinate c at index i and populates all other indices using y.
