declarations.name: mixed_diamond_fan_ramsey_bound_all_singletons_one_fan_colour
declarations.informal: Case b = 1 with every singleton of the unique fan colour: if d ≥ j*a + j and the statement holds at (a, 0) in dimension d-j, then χ has a monochromatic diamond in one of the a diamond colours or a monochromatic F_j in the single fan colour.
declarations.statement:
theorem mixed_diamond_fan_ramsey_bound_all_singletons_one_fan_colour (j a d : ℕ) (hj : 2 ≤ j)
    (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hd : j * a + j ≤ d)
    (ih : mixed_ramsey_property j a 0 (d - j))
    (χ : Finset (Fin d) → Fin (a + 1)) (hx : ∀ x : Fin d, χ {x} = Fin.natAdd a 0) :
    (∃ col : Fin a, has_monochromatic_diamond_copy j d (Fin.castAdd 1 col) χ) ∨
      ∃ col : Fin 1, has_monochromatic_fan_copy j d (Fin.natAdd a col) χ
declarations.source:
/-- b = 1 step with the unique fan colour on every singleton: either a large fan-coloured set is already a fan, or every fan-coloured set has size < j and compressing onto a j-subset Y makes the colouring fan-free, so the (a, 0) instance at dimension d-j gives the diamond. -/
theorem mixed_diamond_fan_ramsey_bound_all_singletons_one_fan_colour (j a d : ℕ) (hj : 2 ≤ j)
    (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hd : j * a + j ≤ d)
    (ih : mixed_ramsey_property j a 0 (d - j))
    (χ : Finset (Fin d) → Fin (a + 1)) (hx : ∀ x : Fin d, χ {x} = Fin.natAdd a 0) :
    (∃ col : Fin a, has_monochromatic_diamond_copy j d (Fin.castAdd 1 col) χ) ∨
      ∃ col : Fin 1, has_monochromatic_fan_copy j d (Fin.natAdd a col) χ := by
  have hj_le_d : j ≤ d := by
    have : j * 1 + j ≤ j * a + j := by nlinarith
    omega
  by_cases h_fan : ∃ S : Finset (Fin d), j ≤ S.card ∧ χ S = Fin.natAdd a 0
  · right
    rcases h_fan with ⟨S, hS_card, hS_col⟩
    use 0
    unfold has_monochromatic_fan_copy
    refine ⟨S, hS_col, ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨T, hTS, hTcard⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hS_card
    have hT_equiv : Nonempty (Fin j ≃ T) := by
      have : Fintype.card T = j := by rw [Fintype.card_coe, hTcard]
      exact ⟨Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq this |>.symm⟩
    obtain ⟨e⟩ := hT_equiv
    let mid : Fin j → Finset (Fin d) := fun i => { (e i : Fin d) }
    refine ⟨mid, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro i
      refine ⟨?_, hx (e i : Fin d)⟩
      rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
      refine ⟨Finset.singleton_subset_iff.mpr (hTS (e i).2), ?_⟩
      intro heq
      have h1 : (mid i).card = S.card := congrArg Finset.card heq
      have h2 : (mid i).card = 1 := Finset.card_singleton _
      omega
    · intro i i' hne
      dsimp [mid]
      rw [Finset.singleton_subset_iff, Finset.mem_singleton]
      intro heq
      apply hne
      apply e.injective
      exact Subtype.ext heq
  · left
    have hd' : j + (d - j) = d := Nat.add_sub_of_le hj_le_d
    let e_iso := (Fin.castOrderIso hd').toEquiv
    let Y_emb : Fin j ↪ Fin d := (Fin.castAddEmb (d - j)).trans e_iso.toEmbedding
    let emb : Fin (d - j) ↪ Fin d := (Fin.natAddEmb j).trans e_iso.toEmbedding
    let Y : Finset (Fin d) := Finset.univ.map Y_emb
    have h_disj : ∀ x, emb x ∉ Y := by
      intro x
      rw [Finset.mem_map]
      rintro ⟨y, hy, heq⟩
      change e_iso (Fin.castAddEmb (d - j) y) = e_iso (Fin.natAddEmb j x) at heq
      have heq' := e_iso.injective heq
      have h_val := congrArg Fin.val heq'
      have h1 : (Fin.castAddEmb (d - j) y).val = y.val := rfl
      have h2 : (Fin.natAddEmb j x).val = j + x.val := rfl
      rw [h1, h2] at h_val
      have : y.val < j := y.isLt
      omega
    let U : Finset (Fin (d - j)) → Finset (Fin d) := fun B => B.map emb ∪ Y
    have hU_card : ∀ B, j ≤ (U B).card := by
      intro B
      have : Y ⊆ U B := Finset.subset_union_right
      have := Finset.card_le_card this
      have hY_card : Y.card = j := by
        rw [Finset.card_map, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
      omega
    have hU_sub : ∀ B B', U B ⊆ U B' ↔ B ⊆ B' := by
      intro B B'
      constructor
      · intro h x hx
        have h1 : emb x ∈ U B := by
          simp only [U, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_map]
          left; exact ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
        have h2 := h h1
        simp only [U, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_map] at h2
        rcases h2 with ⟨y, hy, heqy⟩ | hy
        · have : y = x := emb.injective heqy
          rwa [← this]
        · exact (h_disj x hy).elim
      · intro h
        dsimp [U]
        exact Finset.union_subset_union_left (Finset.map_subset_map.mpr h)
    have hU_ssub : ∀ B B', U B ⊂ U B' ↔ B ⊂ B' := by
      intro B B'
      rw [Finset.ssubset_def, Finset.ssubset_def, hU_sub, hU_sub]
    have h_val_lt : ∀ B, (χ (U B)).val < a := by
      intro B
      have h_ne : χ (U B) ≠ Fin.natAdd a 0 := fun h => h_fan ⟨U B, hU_card B, h⟩
      have h1 : (Fin.natAdd a (0 : Fin 1)).val = a := rfl
      have h2 : (χ (U B)).val < a + 1 := (χ (U B)).isLt
      have h3 : (χ (U B)).val ≠ a := by
        intro h
        apply h_ne
        ext
        rw [h, h1]
      omega
    let ψ : Finset (Fin (d - j)) → Fin (a + 0) := fun B => ⟨(χ (U B)).val, by
      have := h_val_lt B
      omega⟩
    rcases ih ψ with ⟨col, hcol⟩ | ⟨col, _⟩
    · use col
      unfold has_monochromatic_diamond_copy at hcol ⊢
      rcases hcol with ⟨bot, top, h_bot_top, h_col_bot, h_col_top, mid, h_mid, h_incomp⟩
      refine ⟨U bot, U top, ?_, ?_, ?_, fun i => U (mid i), ?_, ?_⟩
      · rwa [hU_ssub]
      · ext
        have : (Fin.castAdd 0 col).val = col.val := rfl
        have : (Fin.castAdd 1 col).val = col.val := rfl
        have h_psi := congrArg Fin.val h_col_bot
        dsimp [ψ] at h_psi
        omega
      · ext
        have : (Fin.castAdd 0 col).val = col.val := rfl
        have : (Fin.castAdd 1 col).val = col.val := rfl
        have h_psi := congrArg Fin.val h_col_top
        dsimp [ψ] at h_psi
        omega
      · intro i
        refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
        · rw [hU_ssub]
          exact (h_mid i).1
        · rw [hU_ssub]
          exact (h_mid i).2.1
        · dsimp only
          ext
          have : (Fin.castAdd 0 col).val = col.val := rfl
          have : (Fin.castAdd 1 col).val = col.val := rfl
          have h_psi := congrArg Fin.val (h_mid i).2.2
          dsimp [ψ] at h_psi
          omega
      · intro i i' hne
        rw [hU_sub]
        exact h_incomp i i' hne
    · exact col.elim0

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by case analysis on whether there exists a set S ⊆ Fin d of size at least j coloured with the unique fan colour a. If such a set S exists, its singletons—all coloured with the fan colour by assumption—form the middle elements of a monochromatic fan with top S. If no such set exists, every set of size at least j must receive one of the a diamond colours; by fixing a j-element subset Y and mapping B ↦ B ∪ Y, we obtain an inclusion-preserving embedding from subsets of Fin (d - j) into sets of size at least j in Fin d. Applying the induction hypothesis at (a, 0) in dimension d - j then produces a monochromatic diamond, which lifts under this embedding to dimension d.

steps.claim: j ≤ d
steps.explanation: From 1 ≤ a (hypothesis ha) and j * a + j ≤ d (hypothesis hd), linear arithmetic implies j ≤ j * 1 + j ≤ j * a + j ≤ d.
steps.code:
have hj_le_d : j ≤ d := by
    have : j * 1 + j ≤ j * a + j := by nlinarith
    omega

steps.claim: If there exists a subset S ⊆ Fin d with |S| ≥ j coloured with the unique fan colour, then there exists a monochromatic fan copy of that colour.
steps.explanation: We split into cases on whether there exists a subset S of size at least j coloured with the fan colour a (represented as Fin.natAdd a 0). If such an S exists, we extract a subset T ⊆ S of cardinality exactly j using Finset.exists_subset_card_eq and construct a bijection e : Fin j ≃ T via Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq. We choose S as the top set and the singletons {e(i)} as the j middle sets. Each singleton has colour a by the theorem hypothesis hx. Since |{e(i)}| = 1 and 2 ≤ j ≤ |S|, each singleton is strictly contained in S. Finally, distinct singletons are mutually incomparable by injectivity of e.
steps.code:
by_cases h_fan : ∃ S : Finset (Fin d), j ≤ S.card ∧ χ S = Fin.natAdd a 0
  · right
    rcases h_fan with ⟨S, hS_card, hS_col⟩
    use 0
    unfold has_monochromatic_fan_copy
    refine ⟨S, hS_col, ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨T, hTS, hTcard⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hS_card
    have hT_equiv : Nonempty (Fin j ≃ T) := by
      have : Fintype.card T = j := by rw [Fintype.card_coe, hTcard]
      exact ⟨Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq this |>.symm⟩
    obtain ⟨e⟩ := hT_equiv
    let mid : Fin j → Finset (Fin d) := fun i => { (e i : Fin d) }
    refine ⟨mid, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro i
      refine ⟨?_, hx (e i : Fin d)⟩
      rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
      refine ⟨Finset.singleton_subset_iff.mpr (hTS (e i).2), ?_⟩
      intro heq
      have h1 : (mid i).card = S.card := congrArg Finset.card heq
      have h2 : (mid i).card = 1 := Finset.card_singleton _
      omega
    · intro i i' hne
      dsimp [mid]
      rw [Finset.singleton_subset_iff, Finset.mem_singleton]
      intro heq
      apply hne
      apply e.injective
      exact Subtype.ext heq

steps.claim: In the remaining case, Fin d decomposes into a j-element subset Y and an embedding of Fin (d - j) disjoint from Y.
steps.explanation: Assuming no set of size at least j has the fan colour, we must produce a monochromatic diamond. Using j + (d - j) = d from Nat.add_sub_of_le, we identify Fin d with Fin (j + (d - j)) via Fin.castOrderIso. We define Y as the image of the first j coordinates via Fin.castAddEmb, and emb as the embedding of the remaining d - j coordinates via Fin.natAddEmb. Since elements of Y have value < j while elements in the range of emb have value ≥ j, the image of emb is disjoint from Y.
steps.code:
· left
    have hd' : j + (d - j) = d := Nat.add_sub_of_le hj_le_d
    let e_iso := (Fin.castOrderIso hd').toEquiv
    let Y_emb : Fin j ↪ Fin d := (Fin.castAddEmb (d - j)).trans e_iso.toEmbedding
    let emb : Fin (d - j) ↪ Fin d := (Fin.natAddEmb j).trans e_iso.toEmbedding
    let Y : Finset (Fin d) := Finset.univ.map Y_emb
    have h_disj : ∀ x, emb x ∉ Y := by
      intro x
      rw [Finset.mem_map]
      rintro ⟨y, hy, heq⟩
      change e_iso (Fin.castAddEmb (d - j) y) = e_iso (Fin.natAddEmb j x) at heq
      have heq' := e_iso.injective heq
      have h_val := congrArg Fin.val heq'
      have h1 : (Fin.castAddEmb (d - j) y).val = y.val := rfl
      have h2 : (Fin.natAddEmb j x).val = j + x.val := rfl
      rw [h1, h2] at h_val
      have : y.val < j := y.isLt
      omega

steps.claim: The cylinder operation U(B) = emb(B) ∪ Y satisfies |U(B)| ≥ j for all B, and reflects and preserves set inclusion and strict inclusion: U(B) ⊆ U(B') ↔ B ⊆ B' and U(B) ⊂ U(B') ↔ B ⊂ B'.
steps.explanation: For any B ⊆ Fin (d - j), Y ⊆ U(B) and |Y| = j, so |U(B)| ≥ j by monotonicity of cardinality. For inclusion, if U(B) ⊆ U(B') and x ∈ B, then emb(x) ∈ U(B) ⊆ U(B'); since emb(x) ∉ Y, emb(x) must belong to emb(B'), which implies x ∈ B' by injectivity of emb. The reverse direction is immediate from union monotonicity. Strict inclusion equivalence U(B) ⊂ U(B') ↔ B ⊂ B' then follows directly from the definition of strict subset.
steps.code:
let U : Finset (Fin (d - j)) → Finset (Fin d) := fun B => B.map emb ∪ Y
    have hU_card : ∀ B, j ≤ (U B).card := by
      intro B
      have : Y ⊆ U B := Finset.subset_union_right
      have := Finset.card_le_card this
      have hY_card : Y.card = j := by
        rw [Finset.card_map, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
      omega
    have hU_sub : ∀ B B', U B ⊆ U B' ↔ B ⊆ B' := by
      intro B B'
      constructor
      · intro h x hx
        have h1 : emb x ∈ U B := by
          simp only [U, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_map]
          left; exact ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
        have h2 := h h1
        simp only [U, Finset.mem_union, Finset.mem_map] at h2
        rcases h2 with ⟨y, hy, heqy⟩ | hy
        · have : y = x := emb.injective heqy
          rwa [← this]
        · exact (h_disj x hy).elim
      · intro h
        dsimp [U]
        exact Finset.union_subset_union_left (Finset.map_subset_map.mpr h)
    have hU_ssub : ∀ B B', U B ⊂ U B' ↔ B ⊂ B' := by
      intro B B'
      rw [Finset.ssubset_def, Finset.ssubset_def, hU_sub, hU_sub]

steps.claim: For every B ⊆ Fin (d - j), χ(U(B)) is strictly less than a, yielding an induced colouring ψ : Finset (Fin (d - j)) → Fin a that uses only diamond colours.
steps.explanation: Because every set U(B) has cardinality at least j, it cannot receive the fan colour a under χ, as no set of size at least j has that colour in this case. Since χ takes values in Fin (a + 1), the numerical value of χ(U(B)) must be strictly less than a. We can therefore restrict the target to Fin a, defining ψ(B) = χ(U(B)).
steps.code:
have h_val_lt : ∀ B, (χ (U B)).val < a := by
      intro B
      have h_ne : χ (U B) ≠ Fin.natAdd a 0 := fun h => h_fan ⟨U B, hU_card B, h⟩
      have h1 : (Fin.natAdd a (0 : Fin 1)).val = a := rfl
      have h2 : (χ (U B)).val < a + 1 := (χ (U B)).isLt
      have h3 : (χ (U B)).val ≠ a := by
        intro h
        apply h_ne
        ext
        rw [h, h1]
      omega
    let ψ : Finset (Fin (d - j)) → Fin (a + 0) := fun B => ⟨(χ (U B)).val, by
      have := h_val_lt B
      omega⟩

steps.claim: The induction hypothesis applied to ψ yields a monochromatic diamond in dimension d - j, which lifts under U to a monochromatic diamond for χ in dimension d.
steps.explanation: We apply the induction hypothesis ih to the colouring ψ on subsets of Fin (d - j). Since the parameter b is 0, there are no fan colours, so the fan alternative is impossible. Hence ψ admits a monochromatic diamond of some diamond colour col < a, given by a bottom set bot, a top set top, and j pairwise incomparable middle sets mid(i). Mapping this configuration to dimension d via U preserves the strict inclusions and incomparability, and every set retains colour col under χ. This gives the required monochromatic diamond for χ.
steps.code:
rcases ih ψ with ⟨col, hcol⟩ | ⟨col, _⟩
    · use col
      unfold has_monochromatic_diamond_copy at hcol ⊢
      rcases hcol with ⟨bot, top, h_bot_top, h_col_bot, h_col_top, mid, h_mid, h_incomp⟩
      refine ⟨U bot, U top, ?_, ?_, ?_, fun i => U (mid i), ?_, ?_⟩
      · rwa [hU_ssub]
      · ext
        have : (Fin.castAdd 0 col).val = col.val := rfl
        have : (Fin.castAdd 1 col).val = col.val := rfl
        have h_psi := congrArg Fin.val h_col_bot
        dsimp [ψ] at h_psi
        omega
      · ext
        have : (Fin.castAdd 0 col).val = col.val := rfl
        have : (Fin.castAdd 1 col).val = col.val := rfl
        have h_psi := congrArg Fin.val h_col_top
        dsimp [ψ] at h_psi
        omega
      · intro i
        refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
        · rw [hU_ssub]
          exact (h_mid i).1
        · rw [hU_ssub]
          exact (h_mid i).2.1
        · dsimp only
          ext
          have : (Fin.castAdd 0 col).val = col.val := rfl
          have : (Fin.castAdd 1 col).val = col.val := rfl
          have h_psi := congrArg Fin.val (h_mid i).2.2
          dsimp [ψ] at h_psi
          omega
      · intro i i' hne
        rw [hU_sub]
        exact h_incomp i i' hne
    · exact col.elim0

glossary.Finset.exists_subset_card_eq: Any finite set with at least n elements contains a subset of cardinality exactly n.
glossary.Fintype.card_coe: The cardinality of the subtype corresponding to a finset equals the cardinality of the finset itself.
glossary.Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq: Any finite type whose cardinality is n is equivalent to Fin n.
glossary.Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne: A finset s is a strict subset of t if and only if s ⊆ t and s ≠ t.
glossary.Finset.singleton_subset_iff: The singleton set {a} is a subset of s if and only if a ∈ s.
glossary.congrArg: Applying a function to equal arguments produces equal values: if a₁ = a₂ then f a₁ = f a₂.
glossary.Finset.card_singleton: The cardinality of any singleton finset {a} is 1.
glossary.Finset.mem_singleton: An element b belongs to the singleton {a} if and only if b = a.
glossary.Subtype.ext: Two subtype elements are equal if their underlying values are equal.
glossary.Nat.add_sub_of_le: For natural numbers with a ≤ b, a + (b - a) = b.
glossary.Fin.castOrderIso: An equality of natural numbers n = m induces an order isomorphism between Fin n and Fin m.
glossary.Fin.castAddEmb: The canonical embedding of Fin n into Fin (n + m) that preserves the underlying natural number value.
glossary.Fin.natAddEmb: The embedding of Fin m into Fin (n + m) that shifts each index by n.
glossary.Finset.mem_map: An element b belongs to the mapped finset Finset.map f s if and only if b = f a for some a ∈ s.
glossary.Finset.subset_union_right: A set s₂ is a subset of the union s₁ ∪ s₂.
glossary.Finset.card_le_card: If s ⊆ t, then |s| ≤ |t|.
glossary.Finset.card_map: An embedding preserves the cardinality of a finset: |Finset.map f s| = |s|.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset of a finite type equals the cardinality of the type.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The cardinality of Fin n is n.
glossary.Finset.mem_union: An element belongs to s ∪ t if and only if it belongs to s or to t.
glossary.Finset.union_subset_union_left: If s₁ ⊆ s₂, then s₁ ∪ t ⊆ s₂ ∪ t.
glossary.Finset.ssubset_def: A set s is a strict subset of t if and only if s ⊆ t and ¬ t ⊆ s.
glossary.Fin.natAdd: The canonical embedding of Fin m into Fin (n + m) mapping i to n + i.
glossary.Fin.castAdd: The canonical embedding of Fin n into Fin (n + m) preserving index values.

caveats: The identification of Fin d with Fin (j + (d - j)) and the definitions of Y_emb and emb are formal infrastructure to partition the coordinates into two disjoint blocks of sizes j and d - j.

In Step 6, the fan alternative of the induction hypothesis mixed_ramsey_property j a 0 (d - j) produces a colour in Fin 0, which is eliminated as impossible (col.elim0), leaving only the diamond alternative.

declarations.name: mdfrbf_compress
declarations.informal: The compression map: given a block W ⊆ Fin d, a colouring χ and an excluded colour c, send a set A of points outside W to its image together with W if A admits a nonempty subset whose image is c-coloured, and to its image alone otherwise. So T ∅ = ∅, and (T A) \ W always recovers the image of A.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def mdfrbf_compress {d k : ℕ} (W : Finset (Fin d)) (χ : Finset (Fin d) → Fin k) (c : Fin k)
    (A : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W)) : Finset (Fin d)
declarations.source:
/-- Compression map T on subsets of the complement of W, used to remove the fan colour c. -/
noncomputable def mdfrbf_compress {d k : ℕ} (W : Finset (Fin d)) (χ : Finset (Fin d) → Fin k) (c : Fin k)
    (A : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W)) : Finset (Fin d) := by
  classical
  exact if A.Nonempty ∧ ∃ B : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), B.Nonempty ∧ B ⊆ A ∧
      χ (B.map (Function.Embedding.subtype fun x => x ∈ Finset.univ \ W)) = c
    then A.map (Function.Embedding.subtype fun x => x ∈ Finset.univ \ W) ∪ W
    else A.map (Function.Embedding.subtype fun x => x ∈ Finset.univ \ W)

declarations.name: mdfrbf_compression_bound
declarations.informal: Arithmetic side condition of the compression step: if j ≥ 2, a ≥ 1, b ≥ 2 and j*a + (j-1)*b + 1 ≤ d, then j*a + (j-1)*(b-1) + 1 ≤ d - (j-1).
declarations.statement:
theorem mdfrbf_compression_bound (j a b d : ℕ) (hj : 2 ≤ j) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 2 ≤ b)
    (hd : j * a + (j - 1) * b + 1 ≤ d) :
    j * a + (j - 1) * (b - 1) + 1 ≤ d - (j - 1)
declarations.source:
/-- Arithmetic: the (a, b-1) bound at dimension d-(j-1) follows from the (a, b) bound at dimension d. -/
theorem mdfrbf_compression_bound (j a b d : ℕ) (hj : 2 ≤ j) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 2 ≤ b)
    (hd : j * a + (j - 1) * b + 1 ≤ d) :
    j * a + (j - 1) * (b - 1) + 1 ≤ d - (j - 1) := by
  have hb1 : 1 ≤ b := by omega
  have h1 : (j - 1) * (b - 1) + (j - 1) = (j - 1) * b := by
    conv_rhs => rw [show b = (b - 1) + 1 from (Nat.sub_add_cancel hb1).symm]
    rw [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one]
  omega

explanation.summary: The proof expands the term (j - 1) * b into (j - 1) * (b - 1) + (j - 1) by writing b = (b - 1) + 1 and distributing. Substituting this identity into the given inequality j * a + (j - 1) * b + 1 ≤ d reveals that adding (j - 1) to the desired left-hand side gives at most d, from which the conclusion follows by linear arithmetic.

steps.explanation: This follows immediately from the hypothesis that 2 ≤ b.
steps.code: have hb1 : 1 ≤ b := by omega

steps.explanation: Because 1 ≤ b, we can express b as (b - 1) + 1 using Nat.sub_add_cancel. Distributing the factor (j - 1) over (b - 1) + 1 using Nat.mul_add and simplifying (j - 1) * 1 with Nat.mul_one yields the desired identity.
steps.code:
have h1 : (j - 1) * (b - 1) + (j - 1) = (j - 1) * b := by
    conv_rhs => rw [show b = (b - 1) + 1 from (Nat.sub_add_cancel hb1).symm]
    rw [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_one]

steps.explanation: Using the algebraic identity just established, the hypothesis j * a + (j - 1) * b + 1 ≤ d can be rewritten as (j * a + (j - 1) * (b - 1) + 1) + (j - 1) ≤ d. Subtracting (j - 1) from both sides yields the target inequality, which is completed by linear arithmetic.
steps.code: omega

glossary.Nat.sub_add_cancel: For natural numbers m ≤ n, (n - m) + m = n.
glossary.Nat.mul_add: Multiplication distributes over addition: n * (m + k) = n * m + n * k.
glossary.Nat.mul_one: Multiplying any natural number by one gives the number itself: n * 1 = n.

declarations.name: mdfrbf_compression_card
declarations.informal: If W is a set of j-1 points of Fin d (j ≥ 2), then the complement of W has exactly d - (j-1) elements, so it can be reindexed by Fin (d - (j-1)).
declarations.statement:
theorem mdfrbf_compression_card (j d : ℕ) (hj : 2 ≤ j) (W : Finset (Fin d)) (hW : W.card = j - 1) :
    Fintype.card ↥(Finset.univ \ W) = d - (j - 1)
declarations.source:
/-- The complement of the compressed block has the cardinality used to reindex Fin (d - (j-1)). -/
theorem mdfrbf_compression_card (j d : ℕ) (hj : 2 ≤ j) (W : Finset (Fin d)) (hW : W.card = j - 1) :
    Fintype.card ↥(Finset.univ \ W) = d - (j - 1) := by
  rw [Fintype.card_coe, Finset.card_sdiff, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin,
      Finset.inter_univ, hW]

explanation.summary: The proof computes the cardinality of the complement `Finset.univ \\ W` in `Fin d` via a sequence of algebraic rewrites. It converts the subtype cardinality to a finset difference, expands the difference as `|univ| - |W ∩ univ|`, simplifies `|univ|` to `d` and `W ∩ univ` to `W`, and substitutes the given size `|W| = j - 1`.

steps.claim: The subtype corresponding to the complement `univ \\ W` has cardinality `d - (j - 1)`.
steps.explanation: We compute the cardinality directly by rewriting: the subtype cardinality `Fintype.card ↥(univ \\ W)` equals the finset cardinality `(univ \\ W).card` (`Fintype.card_coe`). The cardinality of the set difference `univ \\ W` is `univ.card - (W ∩ univ).card` (`Finset.card_sdiff`). The size of the universe of `Fin d` is `Fintype.card (Fin d) = d` (`Finset.card_univ`, `Fintype.card_fin`), and intersecting `W` with `univ` leaves `W` unchanged (`Finset.inter_univ`). Finally, substituting the hypothesis `hW` that `W.card = j - 1` yields `d - (j - 1) = d - (j - 1)`, closing the goal.
steps.code:
rw [Fintype.card_coe, Finset.card_sdiff, Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin,
      Finset.inter_univ, hW]

glossary.Fintype.card_coe: The cardinality of a finset coerced to a subtype equals the cardinality of the finset itself.
glossary.Finset.card_sdiff: The cardinality of the difference of two finsets `t \\ s` is `t.card - (s ∩ t).card`.
glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset `univ` of a finite type `α` is `Fintype.card α`.
glossary.Fintype.card_fin: The cardinality of the standard finite type `Fin n` is `n`.
glossary.Finset.inter_univ: The intersection of any finset with the universal finset is the finset itself.

declarations.name: mdfrbf_fibre_subset
declarations.informal: Pigeonhole: if f : Fin d → Fin b and b*n < d, then some fibre of f contains n+1 points; equivalently there are a colour c and a set W of n+1 points on which f is constantly c.
declarations.statement:
theorem mdfrbf_fibre_subset {d b : ℕ} (f : Fin d → Fin b) (n : ℕ) (h : b * n < d) :
    ∃ c : Fin b, ∃ W : Finset (Fin d), W.card = n + 1 ∧ ∀ w ∈ W, f w = c
declarations.source:
/-- Pigeonhole step extracting j-1 = n+1 points sharing one fan colour. -/
theorem mdfrbf_fibre_subset {d b : ℕ} (f : Fin d → Fin b) (n : ℕ) (h : b * n < d) :
    ∃ c : Fin b, ∃ W : Finset (Fin d), W.card = n + 1 ∧ ∀ w ∈ W, f w = c := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Fintype.exists_lt_card_fiber_of_mul_lt_card f (n := n) (by simpa using h)
  refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
  have hc' : n + 1 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = c)).card := hc
  obtain ⟨W, hW, hWc⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hc'
  exact ⟨W, hWc, fun w hw => by simpa using hW hw⟩

explanation.summary: By the pigeonhole principle, since $b \cdot n < d$, there is some colour $c \in \mathrm{Fin}(b)$ whose fiber under $f$ has strictly more than $n$ elements. Consequently, this fiber has cardinality at least $n + 1$. Selecting any subset $W$ of $n + 1$ elements from this fiber yields the desired set on which $f$ is identically $c$.

steps.claim: There is an element $c \in \mathrm{Fin}(b)$ whose fiber under $f$ contains strictly more than $n$ elements.
steps.explanation: The domain $\mathrm{Fin}(d)$ has cardinality $d$ and the codomain $\mathrm{Fin}(b)$ has cardinality $b$. Given the hypothesis $b \cdot n < d$, the pigeonhole principle (`Fintype.exists_lt_card_fiber_of_mul_lt_card`) implies that some fiber $\{x \mid f(x) = c\}$ contains strictly more than $n$ elements.
steps.code:
classical
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := Fintype.exists_lt_card_fiber_of_mul_lt_card f (n := n) (by simpa using h)

steps.claim: The fiber of $c$ contains a subset $W$ of cardinality $n + 1$, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: We choose $c$ as the witness colour. Because its fiber has cardinality strictly greater than $n$, the cardinality is at least $n + 1$. By `Finset.exists_subset_card_eq`, any finite set of size at least $n + 1$ contains a subset of size exactly $n + 1$, yielding a subset $W \subseteq \{x \mid f(x) = c\}$ with $|W| = n + 1$. Since every $w \in W$ belongs to the fiber of $c$, $f(w) = c$ holds for all $w \in W$.
steps.code:
refine ⟨c, ?_⟩
  have hc' : n + 1 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun x => f x = c)).card := hc
  obtain ⟨W, hW, hWc⟩ := Finset.exists_subset_card_eq hc'
  exact ⟨W, hWc, fun w hw => by simpa using hW hw⟩

glossary.Fintype.exists_lt_card_fiber_of_mul_lt_c: If a map between finite types satisfies $|\beta| \cdot n < |\alpha|$, then some element of $\beta$ has a fiber with strictly more than $n$ elements.
glossary.Finset.exists_subset_card_eq: A finite set of cardinality at least $n$ contains a subset of cardinality exactly $n$.

caveats: Line 4 invokes `classical` to provide decidability instances (such as decidable equality on `Fin b`), a formal requirement for defining fibers as finite sets and applying `Fintype.exists_lt_card_fiber_of_mul_lt_card`.

declarations.name: mdfrbf_compress_subset_iff
declarations.informal: The compression map is an order embedding: for all sets A, A' of points outside W, T A ⊆ T A' holds if and only if A ⊆ A'. Consequently T is injective, monotone, and reflects inclusions (hence strict inclusions), which is what lets an induced copy be pushed back from the compressed colouring to χ.
declarations.statement:
theorem mdfrbf_compress_subset_iff {d k : ℕ} (W : Finset (Fin d)) (χ : Finset (Fin d) → Fin k) (c : Fin k)
    (A A' : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W)) :
    mdfrbf_compress W χ c A ⊆ mdfrbf_compress W χ c A' ↔ A ⊆ A'
declarations.source:
/-- The compression map is an order embedding of the subsets of the complement of W; it yields injectivity, monotonicity and reflection of inclusions at once. -/
theorem mdfrbf_compress_subset_iff {d k : ℕ} (W : Finset (Fin d)) (χ : Finset (Fin d) → Fin k) (c : Fin k)
    (A A' : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W)) :
    mdfrbf_compress W χ c A ⊆ mdfrbf_compress W χ c A' ↔ A ⊆ A' := by
  classical
  set emb : ↥(Finset.univ \ W) ↪ Fin d := Function.Embedding.subtype fun x => x ∈ Finset.univ \ W with hemb
  have hdef : ∀ A : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), mdfrbf_compress W χ c A
      = A.map emb ∪ (if (A.Nonempty ∧ ∃ B : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), B.Nonempty ∧ B ⊆ A ∧ χ (B.map emb) = c) then W else ∅) := by
    intro A
    unfold mdfrbf_compress
    simp only [← hemb]
    by_cases h : (A.Nonempty ∧ ∃ B : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), B.Nonempty ∧ B ⊆ A ∧ χ (B.map emb) = c)
    · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h]
    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]; simp
  have hnotW : ∀ x : ↥(Finset.univ \ W), (emb x : Fin d) ∉ W := by
    intro x hx
    have hx2 : (x : Fin d) ∈ Finset.univ \ W := x.2
    rw [Finset.mem_sdiff] at hx2
    have hv : (emb x : Fin d) = (x : Fin d) := rfl
    rw [hv] at hx
    exact hx2.2 hx
  have hdisj : ∀ A : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), Disjoint (A.map emb) W := by
    intro A
    rw [Finset.disjoint_left]
    intro y hy hyW
    rw [Finset.mem_map] at hy
    obtain ⟨x, -, rfl⟩ := hy
    exact hnotW x hyW
  have hWa : ∀ A : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W),
      (if (A.Nonempty ∧ ∃ B : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), B.Nonempty ∧ B ⊆ A ∧ χ (B.map emb) = c) then W else ∅) ⊆ W := by
    intro A
    split_ifs <;> simp
  have hdiff : ∀ A : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), mdfrbf_compress W χ c A \ W = A.map emb := by
    intro A
    rw [hdef A]
    ext y
    simp only [Finset.mem_sdiff, Finset.mem_union]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨hy | hy, hyW⟩
      · exact hy
      · exact absurd (hWa A hy) hyW
    · intro hy
      exact ⟨Or.inl hy, fun h => Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hdisj A) hy h⟩
  constructor
  · intro hsub x hx
    have h1 : emb x ∈ A.map emb := by rw [Finset.mem_map]; exact ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    have h2 : emb x ∈ mdfrbf_compress W χ c A' := by
      apply hsub
      rw [hdef A]
      exact Finset.mem_union_left _ h1
    have h4 : emb x ∈ A'.map emb := by
      rw [← hdiff A', Finset.mem_sdiff]
      exact ⟨h2, hnotW x⟩
    rw [Finset.mem_map] at h4
    obtain ⟨y, hy, hyx⟩ := h4
    rw [emb.injective hyx] at hy
    exact hy
  · intro hsub
    rw [hdef A, hdef A']
    have hmap : A.map emb ⊆ A'.map emb := Finset.map_subset_map.mpr hsub
    have hHA : (A.Nonempty ∧ ∃ B : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), B.Nonempty ∧ B ⊆ A ∧ χ (B.map emb) = c) →
        (A'.Nonempty ∧ ∃ B : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), B.Nonempty ∧ B ⊆ A' ∧ χ (B.map emb) = c) := by
      rintro ⟨hne, B, hBne, hBsub, hBc⟩
      exact ⟨hne.mono hsub, B, hBne, hBsub.trans hsub, hBc⟩
    by_cases hA : (A.Nonempty ∧ ∃ B : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), B.Nonempty ∧ B ⊆ A ∧ χ (B.map emb) = c)
    · rw [if_pos hA, if_pos (hHA hA)]
      exact Finset.union_subset_union hmap (le_refl W)
    · by_cases hA' : (A'.Nonempty ∧ ∃ B : Finset ↥(Finset.univ \ W), B.Nonempty ∧ B ⊆ A' ∧ χ (B.map emb) = c)
      · rw [if_neg hA, if_pos hA']
        intro y hy
        rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hy with h | h
        · exact Finset.mem_union_left _ (hmap h)
        · exact absurd h (by simp)
      · rw [if_neg hA, if_neg hA']
        intro y hy
        rcases Finset.mem_union.mp hy with h | h
        · exact Finset.mem_union_left _ (hmap h)
        · exact absurd h (by simp)

explanation.summary: The compression map embeds a set A outside W into the ambient space and optionally adjoins W whenever A contains a monochromatic witness of color c. Because embedded points never belong to W, removing W from the compressed set uniquely recovers the embedded image of A, which immediately gives the forward implication via injectivity of the embedding. The reverse implication follows because both the embedded image and the condition for adjoining W are monotonic with respect to inclusion.

steps.claim: The compression map can be written uniformly as the union of the embedded set with a conditional term that is either W or ∅.
steps.explanation: By definition, mdfrbf_compress A is emb(A) ∪ W if A is nonempty and contains a nonempty monochromatic subset of color c, and emb(A) otherwise. Rewriting emb(A) as emb(A) ∪ ∅ in the negative case allows expressing both branches uniformly as emb(A) ∪ (if P(A) then W else ∅).

  set emb : ↥(Finset.univ \ W) ↪ Fin d := Function.Embedding.subtype fun x => x ∈ Finset.univ \ W with hemb

    · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h]
    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]; simp

steps.explanation: Every element x of the subtype Finset.univ \ W satisfies x ∉ W by definition of set difference. Consequently, emb(x) ∉ W for every point, so emb(A) and W are disjoint. Furthermore, whether the condition holds or not, the conditional set is either W or ∅, both of which are subsets of W.

steps.explanation: In the representation mdfrbf_compress A = emb(A) ∪ (if P(A) then W else ∅), the second term is contained in W while emb(A) is disjoint from W. Taking the set difference with W removes the conditional term completely and leaves emb(A) untouched, yielding (mdfrbf_compress A) \ W = emb(A).

Since emb(x) ∉ W, it belongs to (mdfrbf_compress A') \ W, which equals emb(A') by the previous identity. Because emb is an embedding (and hence injective), emb(x) ∈ emb(A') implies x ∈ A'.

glossary.Function.Embedding.subtype: The canonical embedding of a subtype into its ambient type, mapping an element to its underlying value.
glossary.if_pos: If a condition is true, an if-then-else expression reduces to its 'then' branch.
glossary.if_neg: If a condition is false, an if-then-else expression reduces to its 'else' branch.
glossary.Finset.mem_sdiff: An element belongs to a set difference s \\ t if and only if it belongs to s and not to t.
glossary.Finset.disjoint_left: Two finite sets are disjoint if and only if no element of the first set belongs to the second.
glossary.Finset.disjoint_left.mp: If two sets are disjoint, any element in the first set does not belong to the second set.
glossary.Finset.mem_map: An element b belongs to the image Finset.map f s if and only if b = f a for some a in s.
glossary.Finset.mem_union: An element belongs to s ∪ t if and only if it belongs to s or to t.
glossary.Finset.mem_union.mp: If an element belongs to s ∪ t, then it belongs to s or to t.
glossary.Or.inl: Introduces a disjunction proof from a proof of its left disjunct.
glossary.Finset.mem_union_left: If an element belongs to s, it belongs to the union s ∪ t.
glossary.Finset.map_subset_map.mpr: If s ⊆ t, then the image of s under an embedding is a subset of the image of t.
glossary.Finset.union_subset_union: If s ⊆ u and t ⊆ v, then s ∪ t ⊆ u ∪ v.
glossary.le_refl: In any preorder, every element is less than or equal to itself (here, reflexivity of subset inclusion W ⊆ W).

declarations.name: mdfrbf_diamond_transfer
declarations.informal: Push-forward of a monochromatic diamond along an order embedding of set systems: if T is injective, monotone and reflects inclusions on finsets, χ (T A) = f (ψ A) for every nonempty A, ψ ∅ ≠ col, and ψ has a monochromatic j-diamond in colour col, then χ has a monochromatic j-diamond in colour f col.
declarations.statement:
theorem mdfrbf_diamond_transfer {j K d k k' : ℕ} (f : Fin k → Fin k')
    (T : Finset (Fin K) → Finset (Fin d)) (hT : ∀ A A', T A ⊆ T A' ↔ A ⊆ A')
    (χ : Finset (Fin d) → Fin k') (ψ : Finset (Fin K) → Fin k)
    (h : ∀ A, A.Nonempty → χ (T A) = f (ψ A)) (col : Fin k) (hempty : ψ ∅ ≠ col) :
    has_monochromatic_diamond_copy j K col ψ → has_monochromatic_diamond_copy j d (f col) χ
declarations.source:
/-- Transfers a monochromatic diamond copy across an order embedding T of set systems (colour change f). -/
theorem mdfrbf_diamond_transfer {j K d k k' : ℕ} (f : Fin k → Fin k')
    (T : Finset (Fin K) → Finset (Fin d)) (hT : ∀ A A', T A ⊆ T A' ↔ A ⊆ A')
    (χ : Finset (Fin d) → Fin k') (ψ : Finset (Fin K) → Fin k)
    (h : ∀ A, A.Nonempty → χ (T A) = f (ψ A)) (col : Fin k) (hempty : ψ ∅ ≠ col) :
    has_monochromatic_diamond_copy j K col ψ → has_monochromatic_diamond_copy j d (f col) χ := by
  rintro ⟨bot, top, hbot, hbotc, htopc, mid, hmid, hincomp⟩
  have hinj : Function.Injective T := fun A A' hh =>
    Finset.Subset.antisymm ((hT A A').mp (le_of_eq hh)) ((hT A' A).mp (le_of_eq hh.symm))
  have hbotne : bot.Nonempty := by
    rw [Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
    intro h0
    rw [h0] at hbotc
    exact hempty hbotc
  have htopne : top.Nonempty := hbotne.mono hbot.1
  have hmidne : ∀ i : Fin j, (mid i).Nonempty := by
    intro i
    rw [Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
    intro h0
    have hc := (hmid i).2.2
    rw [h0] at hc
    exact hempty hc
  refine ⟨T bot, T top, ?_, ?_, ?_, fun i => T (mid i), ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
    exact ⟨(hT bot top).mpr hbot.1, fun heq => hbot.2 (le_of_eq (hinj heq).symm)⟩
  · rw [h bot hbotne, hbotc]
  · rw [h top htopne, htopc]
  · intro i
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
      exact ⟨(hT bot (mid i)).mpr (hmid i).1.1, fun heq => (hmid i).1.2 (le_of_eq (hinj heq).symm)⟩
    · rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
      exact ⟨(hT (mid i) top).mpr (hmid i).2.1.1, fun heq => (hmid i).2.1.2 (le_of_eq (hinj heq).symm)⟩
    · rw [h (mid i) (hmidne i), (hmid i).2.2]
  · intro i i' hne hincl
    exact hincomp i i' hne ((hT (mid i) (mid i')).mp hincl)

explanation.summary: To transfer a monochromatic diamond from ψ to χ along the mapping T, we push forward each set in the diamond by T. Because T reflects inclusions, it is injective and preserves both strict inclusions and incomparability. Since the empty set does not have colour col, every set in the original diamond is nonempty, allowing the transfer hypothesis χ (T A) = f (ψ A) to colour all image sets f col.

steps.claim: Assume the existence of a monochromatic j-diamond for ψ in colour col.
steps.explanation: By assumption, ψ contains a monochromatic diamond copy in colour col, giving bottom and top sets bot ⊂ top with ψ bot = col and ψ top = col, and j middle sets mid i strictly between bot and top, all with ψ (mid i) = col and pairwise incomparable.
steps.code: rintro ⟨bot, top, hbot, hbotc, htopc, mid, hmid, hincomp⟩

steps.claim: The mapping T is injective.
steps.explanation: If T A = T A', then T A ⊆ T A' and T A' ⊆ T A by le_of_eq. Since T reflects inclusions via hT, this implies A ⊆ A' and A' ⊆ A, hence A = A' by Finset.Subset.antisymm.
steps.code:
have hinj : Function.Injective T := fun A A' hh =>
    Finset.Subset.antisymm ((hT A A').mp (le_of_eq hh)) ((hT A' A).mp (le_of_eq hh.symm))

steps.claim: The sets bot, top, and every mid i are nonempty.
steps.explanation: If bot were empty, then ψ ∅ = ψ bot = col, contradicting hempty (ψ ∅ ≠ col); thus bot is nonempty by Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty. Since bot ⊂ top, top is also nonempty. Similarly, if any mid i were empty, its colour ψ (mid i) = col would contradict hempty, so every mid i is nonempty.
steps.code:
have hbotne : bot.Nonempty := by
    rw [Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
    intro h0
    rw [h0] at hbotc
    exact hempty hbotc
  have htopne : top.Nonempty := hbotne.mono hbot.1
  have hmidne : ∀ i : Fin j, (mid i).Nonempty := by
    intro i
    rw [Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
    intro h0
    have hc := (hmid i).2.2
    rw [h0] at hc
    exact hempty hc

steps.claim: The candidate diamond for χ is given by T bot, T top, and T (mid i).
steps.explanation: We provide the images under T as witnesses for the existential quantifier defining a monochromatic diamond copy for χ: bottom T bot, top T top, and middle sets i ↦ T (mid i).
steps.code: refine ⟨T bot, T top, ?_, ?_, ?_, fun i => T (mid i), ?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: T bot ⊂ T top and both sets are coloured f col under χ.
steps.explanation: Using Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne, T bot ⊂ T top requires inclusion and inequality: inclusion follows from bot ⊆ top by hT, and equality would imply bot = top by injectivity of T (via le_of_eq), contradicting bot ⊂ top. Because bot and top are nonempty, hypothesis h applies to give χ (T bot) = f (ψ bot) = f col and χ (T top) = f (ψ top) = f col.
steps.code:
· rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
    exact ⟨(hT bot top).mpr hbot.1, fun heq => hbot.2 (le_of_eq (hinj heq).symm)⟩
  · rw [h bot hbotne, hbotc]
  · rw [h top htopne, htopc]

steps.claim: Each T (mid i) strictly lies between T bot and T top, with colour f col under χ.
steps.explanation: By Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne, the order preservation and reflection hT together with the injectivity of T (via le_of_eq) ensure that bot ⊂ mid i ⊂ top pushes forward to T bot ⊂ T (mid i) ⊂ T top. Nonemptiness of mid i then lets hypothesis h evaluate χ (T (mid i)) = f (ψ (mid i)) = f col.
steps.code:
· intro i
    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
      exact ⟨(hT bot (mid i)).mpr (hmid i).1.1, fun heq => (hmid i).1.2 (le_of_eq (hinj heq).symm)⟩
    · rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
      exact ⟨(hT (mid i) top).mpr (hmid i).2.1.1, fun heq => (hmid i).2.1.2 (le_of_eq (hinj heq).symm)⟩
    · rw [h (mid i) (hmidne i), (hmid i).2.2]

steps.claim: For distinct indices i ≠ i', the image sets T (mid i) are incomparable.
steps.explanation: If T (mid i) ⊆ T (mid i'), then order reflection hT would give mid i ⊆ mid i', contradicting the incomparability of the original middle elements mid i and mid i'.
steps.code:
· intro i i' hne hincl
    exact hincomp i i' hne ((hT (mid i) (mid i')).mp hincl)

glossary.Finset.Subset.antisymm: If two finite sets are subsets of each other, they are equal.
glossary.le_of_eq: Equality implies the preorder relation (here, subset inclusion).
glossary.Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty: A finite set is nonempty if and only if it is not equal to the empty set.
glossary.Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne: A finite set is a strict subset of another if and only if it is a subset and the two sets are distinct.

declarations.name: comparison_tree_selects_rank
declarations.informal: A comparison decision tree T on n elements (T : ComparisonTree n) correctly selects the element of rank r : Fin n if for every permutation σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), applying σ to the index returned by evaluating T on σ equals r, that is, σ (comparison_tree_eval σ T) = r.
declarations.statement: def comparison_tree_selects_rank {n : ℕ} (T : ComparisonTree n) (r : Fin n) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- A comparison decision tree on n elements selects rank r if on every permutation of Fin n it returns the index whose value is r. -/
def comparison_tree_selects_rank {n : ℕ} (T : ComparisonTree n) (r : Fin n) : Prop := ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), σ (comparison_tree_eval σ T) = r
declarations.reading: Given a natural number $n$, a comparison tree $T$ on $n$ elements, and an index/rank $r \in \operatorname{Fin} n$, the declaration defines the proposition that for every permutation $\sigma$ of $\operatorname{Fin} n$, applying $\sigma$ to the index in $\operatorname{Fin} n$ returned by evaluating $T$ on the input $\sigma$ equals $r$.

theorem mdfrbf_fan_transfer {j K d k k' : ℕ} (hj : 2 ≤ j) (f : Fin k → Fin k')
    (T : Finset (Fin K) → Finset (Fin d)) (hT : ∀ A A', T A ⊆ T A' ↔ A ⊆ A')

declarations.source:
/-- Transfers a monochromatic fan copy across an order embedding T of set systems (colour change f). -/
theorem mdfrbf_fan_transfer {j K d k k' : ℕ} (hj : 2 ≤ j) (f : Fin k → Fin k')
    (T : Finset (Fin K) → Finset (Fin d)) (hT : ∀ A A', T A ⊆ T A' ↔ A ⊆ A')
    (χ : Finset (Fin d) → Fin k') (ψ : Finset (Fin K) → Fin k)
    (h : ∀ A, A.Nonempty → χ (T A) = f (ψ A)) (col : Fin k) :
    has_monochromatic_fan_copy j K col ψ → has_monochromatic_fan_copy j d (f col) χ := by
  rintro ⟨top, htopc, mid, hmid, hincomp⟩
  have hinj : Function.Injective T := fun A A' hh =>
    Finset.Subset.antisymm ((hT A A').mp (le_of_eq hh)) ((hT A' A).mp (le_of_eq hh.symm))
  have hmidne : ∀ i : Fin j, (mid i).Nonempty := by
    intro i
    rw [Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
    intro h0
    have hpos : 0 < (Finset.univ.erase i).card := by
      rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i), Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
      omega
    obtain ⟨i', hi'⟩ := Finset.card_pos.mp hpos
    rw [Finset.mem_erase] at hi'
    exact hincomp i i' hi'.1.symm (by rw [h0]; exact Finset.empty_subset _)
  have htopne : top.Nonempty :=
    Finset.Nonempty.mono (hmid ⟨0, by omega⟩).1.1 (hmidne ⟨0, by omega⟩)
  refine ⟨T top, ?_, fun i => T (mid i), ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [h top htopne, htopc]
  · intro i
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
      exact ⟨(hT (mid i) top).mpr (hmid i).1.1, fun heq => (hmid i).1.2 (le_of_eq (hinj heq).symm)⟩
    · rw [h (mid i) (hmidne i), (hmid i).2]
  · intro i i' hne hincl
    exact hincomp i i' hne ((hT (mid i) (mid i')).mp hincl)

explanation.summary: The proof transfers a monochromatic fan copy across the order embedding T by setting the new top element to T top and the new petals to T (mid i). Because the colouring hypothesis χ (T A) = f (ψ A) requires A to be nonempty, the argument first proves that each petal is nonempty (as an empty petal would be contained in any other petal, contradicting incomparability since j ≥ 2), which also implies top is nonempty. Finally, order reflection and injectivity of T ensure that strict inclusions, pairwise incomparabilities, and monochromaticity under colour f col are all preserved.

steps.claim: Let top and (mid i) witness that ψ has a monochromatic fan copy of size j in colour col.
steps.explanation: Unpack the definition of `has_monochromatic_fan_copy`: we obtain a top set with ψ top = col, and j middle sets (mid i) that are strict subsets of top, coloured col, and pairwise incomparable under inclusion.
steps.code: rintro ⟨top, htopc, mid, hmid, hincomp⟩

steps.claim: T is injective.
steps.explanation: If T A = T A', then T A ⊆ T A' and T A' ⊆ T A. Because T reflects inclusions, A ⊆ A' and A' ⊆ A, so A = A' by antisymmetry of Finset inclusion (`Finset.Subset.antisymm`).
steps.code:
have hinj : Function.Injective T := fun A A' hh =>
    Finset.Subset.antisymm ((hT A A').mp (le_of_eq hh)) ((hT A' A).mp (le_of_eq hh.symm))

steps.claim: Every middle set mid i is nonempty.
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that mid i = ∅. Since j ≥ 2, the set of indices Fin j with i removed has cardinality j - 1 > 0, so there exists another index i' ≠ i. But then mid i = ∅ ⊆ mid i', contradicting the pairwise incomparability of the middle sets.
steps.code:
have hmidne : ∀ i : Fin j, (mid i).Nonempty := by
    intro i
    rw [Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
    intro h0
    have hpos : 0 < (Finset.univ.erase i).card := by
      rw [Finset.card_erase_of_mem (Finset.mem_univ i), Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin]
      omega
    obtain ⟨i', hi'⟩ := Finset.card_pos.mp hpos
    rw [Finset.mem_erase] at hi'
    exact hincomp i i' hi'.1.symm (by rw [h0]; exact Finset.empty_subset _)

steps.claim: The top set is nonempty.
steps.explanation: Since j ≥ 2, index 0 is valid. The middle set mid 0 is nonempty and is a subset of top, so top is nonempty by monotonicity of nonemptiness (`Finset.Nonempty.mono`).
steps.code:
have htopne : top.Nonempty :=
    Finset.Nonempty.mono (hmid ⟨0, by omega⟩).1.1 (hmidne ⟨0, by omega⟩)

steps.claim: It suffices to show that T top and the family i ↦ T (mid i) satisfy the three properties of a monochromatic fan copy for χ in colour f col.
steps.explanation: We provide T top as the candidate top element and i ↦ T (mid i) as the candidate petals, generating three subgoals: the colour of T top, the strict inclusion and colour of each T (mid i), and the pairwise incomparability of the petals.
steps.code: refine ⟨T top, ?_, fun i => T (mid i), ?_, ?_⟩

steps.claim: χ (T top) = f col.
steps.explanation: Since top is nonempty, the colouring preservation hypothesis gives χ (T top) = f (ψ top). Substituting ψ top = col yields f col.
steps.code: · rw [h top htopne, htopc]

steps.claim: For every index i, T (mid i) is a strict subset of T top, and χ (T (mid i)) = f col.
steps.explanation: Strict inclusion is equivalent to inclusion and inequality (`Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne`). T (mid i) ⊆ T top holds because mid i ⊆ top and T preserves inclusions. If T (mid i) = T top, injectivity of T would force mid i = top, contradicting mid i ⊂ top. For the colour, since mid i is nonempty, χ (T (mid i)) = f (ψ (mid i)) = f col.
steps.code:
· intro i
    refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [Finset.ssubset_iff_subset_ne]
      exact ⟨(hT (mid i) top).mpr (hmid i).1.1, fun heq => (hmid i).1.2 (le_of_eq (hinj heq).symm)⟩
    · rw [h (mid i) (hmidne i), (hmid i).2]

steps.claim: For all distinct indices i ≠ i', T (mid i) is not a subset of T (mid i').
steps.explanation: If T (mid i) ⊆ T (mid i'), then because T reflects inclusions, mid i ⊆ mid i', which contradicts the incomparability of the original petals.
steps.code:
· intro i i' hne hincl
    exact hincomp i i' hne ((hT (mid i) (mid i')).mp hincl)

glossary.le_of_eq: An equality implies the corresponding non-strict inequality (here, set equality implies inclusion).
glossary.Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty: A finite set is nonempty if and only if it is not equal to the empty set.
glossary.Finset.card_erase_of_mem: Removing an element from a finite set that contains it decreases the set's cardinality by 1.

glossary.Finset.card_univ: The cardinality of the universal finset of a finite type equals the cardinality of the type.

glossary.Finset.card_pos.mp: A finite set with strictly positive cardinality is nonempty.
glossary.Finset.mem_erase: An element belongs to a finite set with another element erased if and only if it is not equal to the erased element and belongs to the original set.

theorem comparison_tree_selects_rank_one_zero :

declarations.name: comparison_selection_complexity
declarations.informal: The worst-case comparison complexity to select the element of rank r : Fin n among n elements, defined as the infimum of the depths of all comparison decision trees T : ComparisonTree n that satisfy comparison_tree_selects_rank T r.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def comparison_selection_complexity {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- Worst-case comparison complexity to select the element of 0-based rank r in Fin n. -/
noncomputable def comparison_selection_complexity {n : ℕ} (r : Fin n) : ℕ := sInf { d : ℕ | ∃ T : ComparisonTree n, comparison_tree_selects_rank T r ∧ comparison_tree_depth T = d }
declarations.reading:
The declaration defines `comparison_selection_complexity`, which takes an implicit natural number `n` and an explicit `r : Fin n`, and returns a natural number.

It is defined as the infimum (in `ℕ`, i.e., the minimum) of the set of all depths `d : ℕ` for which there exists a comparison tree `T : ComparisonTree n` such that:
1. `T` selects rank `r`: for every permutation `σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`, evaluating `T` on input `σ` produces an index whose value under `σ` is equal to `r` (i.e., `σ (comparison_tree_eval σ T) = r`).
2. The depth of `T` is equal to `d` (`comparison_tree_depth T = d`).

Here, tree evaluation recursively starts at the root: at a branch comparing indices `i` and `j`, it branches to the left subtree if `σ i < σ j` and to the right subtree otherwise; at a leaf with answer `ans`, it returns `ans`. The depth of a tree is 0 at a leaf, and 1 plus the maximum of the depths of its left and right subtrees at a branch.

Specializing this requirement to the identity permutation forces $0 = 1$ in $\mathrm{Fin}(2)$, an immediate contradiction.

We then specialize this universal assumption to the identity permutation $\sigma = \mathrm{Equiv.refl}(\mathrm{Fin}\,2)$.

  have h0 := h (Equiv.refl (Fin 2))

declarations.name: v_selection
declarations.informal: The minimum number of pairwise comparisons V_i(n) needed in the worst case by a deterministic comparison algorithm (decision tree) to find the i-th smallest element among n distinct elements, defined for 0 < i ∧ i ≤ n as the comparison selection complexity of 0-based rank i - 1 in Fin n, and 0 otherwise.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def v_selection (n : ℕ) (i : ℕ) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- The minimum worst-case comparison complexity V_i(n) to find the i-th smallest of n elements. -/
noncomputable def v_selection (n : ℕ) (i : ℕ) : ℕ := if h : 0 < i ∧ i ≤ n then comparison_selection_complexity (n := n) ⟨i - 1, by omega⟩ else 0
declarations.reading: The function `v_selection n i` defines the worst-case comparison complexity $V_i(n)$ of selecting the $i$-th smallest element out of $n$ elements. For $0 < i \le n$, it evaluates to the minimum depth of a comparison tree on $n$ elements that correctly identifies the element of rank $i - 1$ (0-indexed) for all permutations of the inputs. If $i = 0$ or $i > n$, it returns $0$.

declarations.name: mdfrbf_colour_inj
declarations.informal: There is a bijection from Fin (a + (b-1)) onto the colours of Fin (a+b) other than the fan colour Fin.natAdd a c, which fixes the a diamond colours (Fin.castAdd (b-1) col ↦ Fin.castAdd b col), sends fan colours to fan colours, and never takes the value Fin.natAdd a c.
declarations.statement:
theorem mdfrbf_colour_inj (a b : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (c : Fin b) :
    ∃ f : Fin (a + (b - 1)) → Fin (a + b),
      Function.Injective f ∧
      (∀ v : Fin (a + b), v ≠ Fin.natAdd a c → ∃ u : Fin (a + (b - 1)), f u = v) ∧
      (∀ col : Fin a, f (Fin.castAdd (b - 1) col) = Fin.castAdd b col) ∧
      (∀ u : Fin (b - 1), ∃ col' : Fin b, f (Fin.natAdd a u) = Fin.natAdd a col') ∧
      (∀ u : Fin (a + (b - 1)), f u ≠ Fin.natAdd a c)
declarations.source:
/-- Colour bijection from the a+b-1 colours surviving deletion of the fan colour c into the a+b colours, fixing the a diamond colours. -/
theorem mdfrbf_colour_inj (a b : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 2 ≤ b) (c : Fin b) :
    ∃ f : Fin (a + (b - 1)) → Fin (a + b),
      Function.Injective f ∧
      (∀ v : Fin (a + b), v ≠ Fin.natAdd a c → ∃ u : Fin (a + (b - 1)), f u = v) ∧
      (∀ col : Fin a, f (Fin.castAdd (b - 1) col) = Fin.castAdd b col) ∧
      (∀ u : Fin (b - 1), ∃ col' : Fin b, f (Fin.natAdd a u) = Fin.natAdd a col') ∧
      (∀ u : Fin (a + (b - 1)), f u ≠ Fin.natAdd a c) := by
  let g : Fin (b - 1) → Fin b := fun u =>
    if h : u.val < c.val then ⟨u.val, by omega⟩ else ⟨u.val + 1, by have := u.isLt; omega⟩
  let f : Fin (a + (b - 1)) → Fin (a + b) := fun v =>
    if h : v.val < a then ⟨v.val, by omega⟩
    else Fin.natAdd a (g ⟨v.val - a, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩)
  have g_inj : Function.Injective g := by
    intro u u' h
    apply Fin.ext
    dsimp [g] at h
    split_ifs at h with h1 h2 h1 h2
    all_goals simp only [Fin.mk.injEq] at h ⊢
    all_goals omega
  have g_ne : ∀ u : Fin (b - 1), (g u).val ≠ c.val := by
    intro u
    have g_val : (g u).val = if u.val < c.val then u.val else u.val + 1 := by
      dsimp [g]
      split_ifs <;> rfl
    rw [g_val]
    split_ifs with h
    · omega
    · omega
  have g_surj : ∀ w : Fin b, w.val ≠ c.val → ∃ u : Fin (b - 1), g u = w := by
    intro w hw
    by_cases hwlt : w.val < c.val
    · refine ⟨⟨w.val, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
      dsimp [g]
      rw [if_pos hwlt]
    · have hle : c.val < w.val := by omega
      refine ⟨⟨w.val - 1, by have := w.isLt; omega⟩, ?_⟩
      dsimp [g]
      have hnot : ¬ w.val - 1 < c.val := by omega
      rw [dif_neg hnot]
      apply Fin.ext
      simp
      omega
  have f_natAdd : ∀ u : Fin (b - 1), f (Fin.natAdd a u) = Fin.natAdd a (g u) := by
    intro u
    dsimp [f]
    rw [dif_neg (by omega)]
    congr 1
    congr 1
    apply Fin.ext
    simp
  have f_inj : Function.Injective f := by
    intro v v' h
    by_cases hv : v.val < a
    · by_cases hv' : v'.val < a
      · apply Fin.ext
        dsimp [f] at h
        rw [dif_pos hv, dif_pos hv'] at h
        have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
        simpa using hval
      · dsimp [f] at h
        rw [dif_pos hv, dif_neg hv'] at h
        have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
        rw [Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
        have hval' : v.val = a + (g ⟨v'.val - a, by have := v'.isLt; omega⟩).val := by
          simpa using hval
        omega
    · by_cases hv' : v'.val < a
      · dsimp [f] at h
        rw [dif_neg hv, dif_pos hv'] at h
        have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
        rw [Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
        have hval' : a + (g ⟨v.val - a, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩).val = v'.val := by
          simpa using hval
        omega
      · dsimp [f] at h
        rw [dif_neg hv, dif_neg hv'] at h
        have hg : g ⟨v.val - a, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩ =
            g ⟨v'.val - a, by have := v'.isLt; omega⟩ := by
          apply Fin.ext
          have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
          rw [Fin.val_natAdd, Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
          omega
        have hsub : v.val - a = v'.val - a :=
          congrArg (fun x : Fin (b - 1) => x.val) (g_inj hg)
        apply Fin.ext
        omega
  have f_cast : ∀ col : Fin a, f (Fin.castAdd (b - 1) col) = Fin.castAdd b col := by
    intro col
    dsimp [f]
    have h : col.val < a := col.isLt
    rw [dif_pos h]
    apply Fin.ext
    simpa using (Fin.val_castAdd b col).symm
  have f_fan : ∀ u : Fin (b - 1), ∃ col' : Fin b, f (Fin.natAdd a u) = Fin.natAdd a col' := by
    intro u
    exact ⟨g u, f_natAdd u⟩
  have f_ne : ∀ u : Fin (a + (b - 1)), f u ≠ Fin.natAdd a c := by
    intro u h
    by_cases hu : u.val < a
    · dsimp [f] at h
      rw [dif_pos hu] at h
      have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
      rw [Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
      have hval' : u.val = a + c.val := by
        simpa using hval
      omega
    · let u0 : Fin (b - 1) := ⟨u.val - a, by have := u.isLt; omega⟩
      have hu_eq : u = Fin.natAdd a u0 := by
        apply Fin.ext
        simp [u0]
        omega
      rw [hu_eq, f_natAdd] at h
      have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
      rw [Fin.val_natAdd, Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
      exact g_ne u0 (by omega)
  refine ⟨f, f_inj, ?_, f_cast, f_fan, f_ne⟩
  intro v hv
  by_cases hvlt : v.val < a
  · refine ⟨⟨v.val, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩, ?_⟩
    dsimp [f]
    rw [dif_pos hvlt]
  · have hvge : a ≤ v.val := by omega
    let w : Fin b := ⟨v.val - a, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩
    have hw_ne : w.val ≠ c.val := by
      intro hw
      apply hv
      apply Fin.ext
      rw [Fin.val_natAdd]
      dsimp [w] at hw
      omega
    obtain ⟨u0, hu0⟩ := g_surj w hw_ne
    refine ⟨Fin.natAdd a u0, ?_⟩
    rw [f_natAdd, hu0]
    apply Fin.ext
    rw [Fin.val_natAdd]
    dsimp [w]
    omega

explanation.summary: The theorem constructs a colour bijection f from the a + (b - 1) colours surviving the deletion of the fan colour c into the original a + b colours, fixing the a diamond colours and avoiding the deleted fan colour a + c. The construction first defines an auxiliary map g from Fin (b - 1) to Fin b that skips c (by mapping u to u when u < c and to u + 1 when u ≥ c), and then defines f to be the identity on diamond colours and a + g(v - a) on fan colours. The proof verifies that g is an injective map avoiding c with image Fin b \ {c}, from which the injectivity, range constraints, and surjectivity of f onto all colours except a + c follow directly.

steps.claim: Define the fan-colour skipping map g and the full colour map f.
steps.explanation: The fan has b - 1 colours after deleting c, which need to be mapped into the original b colours skipping c. We define g : Fin (b - 1) → Fin b by g(u) = u if u < c and g(u) = u + 1 if u ≥ c. Then we define f : Fin (a + (b - 1)) → Fin (a + b) piecewise: on the first a colours (the diamond colours), f acts as the identity; on the remaining b - 1 colours (the fan colours), f(v) = a + g(v - a).
steps.code:
let g : Fin (b - 1) → Fin b := fun u =>
    if h : u.val < c.val then ⟨u.val, by omega⟩ else ⟨u.val + 1, by have := u.isLt; omega⟩
  let f : Fin (a + (b - 1)) → Fin (a + b) := fun v =>
    if h : v.val < a then ⟨v.val, by omega⟩
    else Fin.natAdd a (g ⟨v.val - a, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩)

steps.claim: The auxiliary fan map g is injective.
steps.explanation: Suppose g(u) = g(u'). By Fin.ext, their underlying numerical values are equal. Case analysis on whether u < c and u' < c yields four cases: if both are less than c, u = u'; if both are at least c, u + 1 = u' + 1, so u = u'; and the mixed cases (u < c ≤ u' with u = u' + 1, or vice versa) are contradictions by linear arithmetic.
steps.code:
have g_inj : Function.Injective g := by
    intro u u' h
    apply Fin.ext
    dsimp [g] at h
    split_ifs at h with h1 h2 h1 h2
    all_goals simp only [Fin.mk.injEq] at h ⊢
    all_goals omega

steps.claim: The auxiliary map g never takes the value c.
steps.explanation: For any u, if u < c then g(u) = u < c, so g(u) ≠ c; if u ≥ c then g(u) = u + 1 > c, so again g(u) ≠ c.
steps.code:
have g_ne : ∀ u : Fin (b - 1), (g u).val ≠ c.val := by
    intro u
    have g_val : (g u).val = if u.val < c.val then u.val else u.val + 1 := by
      dsimp [g]
      split_ifs <;> rfl
    rw [g_val]
    split_ifs with h
    · omega
    · omega

steps.claim: The map g is surjective onto Fin b \ {c}.
steps.explanation: Given w : Fin b with w ≠ c, we construct its pre-image under g. If w < c, we choose u = w; then u < c, so g(u) = w by if_pos. If w > c, we choose u = w - 1; then u ≥ c, so g(u) = (w - 1) + 1 = w by dif_neg.
steps.code:
have g_surj : ∀ w : Fin b, w.val ≠ c.val → ∃ u : Fin (b - 1), g u = w := by
    intro w hw
    by_cases hwlt : w.val < c.val
    · refine ⟨⟨w.val, by omega⟩, ?_⟩
      dsimp [g]
      rw [if_pos hwlt]
    · have hle : c.val < w.val := by omega
      refine ⟨⟨w.val - 1, by have := w.isLt; omega⟩, ?_⟩
      dsimp [g]
      have hnot : ¬ w.val - 1 < c.val := by omega
      rw [dif_neg hnot]
      apply Fin.ext
      simp
      omega

steps.claim: On fan colours, f(a + u) = a + g(u).
steps.explanation: Since a + u ≥ a, unfolding the definition of f selects the second branch via dif_neg. The argument passed to g is (a + u) - a = u, yielding f(a + u) = a + g(u).
steps.code:
have f_natAdd : ∀ u : Fin (b - 1), f (Fin.natAdd a u) = Fin.natAdd a (g u) := by
    intro u
    dsimp [f]
    rw [dif_neg (by omega)]
    congr 1
    congr 1
    apply Fin.ext
    simp

steps.claim: The colour map f is injective.
steps.explanation: Suppose f(v) = f(v'). We branch on whether v < a and v' < a. If both are < a, both evaluate to their identity values, so v = v'. If v < a ≤ v', then v = a + g(v' - a) ≥ a, contradicting v < a. Symmetrically, v' < a ≤ v is impossible. If both are ≥ a, then a + g(v - a) = a + g(v' - a), which gives g(v - a) = g(v' - a); by the injectivity of g (g_inj), v - a = v' - a, so v = v'.
steps.code:
have f_inj : Function.Injective f := by
    intro v v' h
    by_cases hv : v.val < a
    · by_cases hv' : v'.val < a
      · apply Fin.ext
        dsimp [f] at h
        rw [dif_pos hv, dif_pos hv'] at h
        have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
        simpa using hval
      · dsimp [f] at h
        rw [dif_pos hv, dif_neg hv'] at h
        have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
        rw [Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
        have hval' : v.val = a + (g ⟨v'.val - a, by have := v'.isLt; omega⟩).val := by
          simpa using hval
        omega
    · by_cases hv' : v'.val < a
      · dsimp [f] at h
        rw [dif_neg hv, dif_pos hv'] at h
        have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
        rw [Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
        have hval' : a + (g ⟨v.val - a, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩).val = v'.val := by
          simpa using hval
        omega
      · dsimp [f] at h
        rw [dif_neg hv, dif_neg hv'] at h
        have hg : g ⟨v.val - a, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩ =
            g ⟨v'.val - a, by have := v'.isLt; omega⟩ := by
          apply Fin.ext
          have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
          rw [Fin.val_natAdd, Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
          omega
        have hsub : v.val - a = v'.val - a :=
          congrArg (fun x : Fin (b - 1) => x.val) (g_inj hg)
        apply Fin.ext
        omega

steps.claim: f fixes the diamond colours.
steps.explanation: For col : Fin a, since col < a, f takes the first branch via dif_pos, leaving col unchanged. Its value in Fin (a + b) matches Fin.castAdd b col by Fin.val_castAdd.
steps.code:
have f_cast : ∀ col : Fin a, f (Fin.castAdd (b - 1) col) = Fin.castAdd b col := by
    intro col
    dsimp [f]
    have h : col.val < a := col.isLt
    rw [dif_pos h]
    apply Fin.ext
    simpa using (Fin.val_castAdd b col).symm

steps.claim: f sends fan colours to fan colours.
steps.explanation: For u : Fin (b - 1), f(a + u) = a + g(u) by f_natAdd, so col' = g(u) : Fin b is the desired witness.
steps.code:
have f_fan : ∀ u : Fin (b - 1), ∃ col' : Fin b, f (Fin.natAdd a u) = Fin.natAdd a col' := by
    intro u
    exact ⟨g u, f_natAdd u⟩

steps.claim: f never takes the deleted fan colour a + c.
steps.explanation: Suppose f(u) = a + c. If u < a, f(u) = u < a while a + c ≥ a, a contradiction. If u ≥ a, write u = a + u0 where u0 = u - a. Then f(u) = a + g(u0) = a + c, which implies g(u0) = c, contradicting g_ne.
steps.code:
have f_ne : ∀ u : Fin (a + (b - 1)), f u ≠ Fin.natAdd a c := by
    intro u h
    by_cases hu : u.val < a
    · dsimp [f] at h
      rw [dif_pos hu] at h
      have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
      rw [Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
      have hval' : u.val = a + c.val := by
        simpa using hval
      omega
    · let u0 : Fin (b - 1) := ⟨u.val - a, by have := u.isLt; omega⟩
      have hu_eq : u = Fin.natAdd a u0 := by
        apply Fin.ext
        simp [u0]
        omega
      rw [hu_eq, f_natAdd] at h
      have hval := congrArg (fun x : Fin (a + b) => x.val) h
      rw [Fin.val_natAdd, Fin.val_natAdd] at hval
      exact g_ne u0 (by omega)

steps.claim: Package the bijection f and verify that every colour other than a + c is in the range.
steps.explanation: We instantiate the existential goal with f and the properties established above. For surjectivity onto Fin (a + b) \ {a + c}, let v ≠ a + c. If v < a, u = v gives f(u) = v. If v ≥ a, let w = v - a : Fin b. Since v ≠ a + c, w ≠ c. By the surjectivity of g (g_surj), there is u0 with g(u0) = w. Then u = a + u0 satisfies f(u) = a + g(u0) = a + w = v.
steps.code:
refine ⟨f, f_inj, ?_, f_cast, f_fan, f_ne⟩
  intro v hv
  by_cases hvlt : v.val < a
  · refine ⟨⟨v.val, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩, ?_⟩
    dsimp [f]
    rw [dif_pos hvlt]
  · have hvge : a ≤ v.val := by omega
    let w : Fin b := ⟨v.val - a, by have := v.isLt; omega⟩
    have hw_ne : w.val ≠ c.val := by
      intro hw
      apply hv
      apply Fin.ext
      rw [Fin.val_natAdd]
      dsimp [w] at hw
      omega
    obtain ⟨u0, hu0⟩ := g_surj w hw_ne
    refine ⟨Fin.natAdd a u0, ?_⟩
    rw [f_natAdd, hu0]
    apply Fin.ext
    rw [Fin.val_natAdd]
    dsimp [w]
    omega

glossary.Fin.ext: Two elements of Fin n are equal if and only if their underlying natural numbers are equal.
glossary.Fin.mk.injEq: Two elements of Fin n formed by Fin.mk are equal if and only if their numerical values are equal.
glossary.if_pos: An if-then-else expression reduces to its positive branch when the condition holds.
glossary.dif_neg: A dependent if-then-else expression reduces to its negative branch when the condition is refuted.
glossary.dif_pos: A dependent if-then-else expression reduces to its positive branch when the condition holds.
glossary.congrArg: Functions send equal inputs to equal outputs: if a = b then f(a) = f(b).
glossary.Fin.val_natAdd: The numerical value of Fin.natAdd n i equals n plus the numerical value of i.
glossary.Fin.val_castAdd: The numerical value of Fin.castAdd m i equals the numerical value of i.

caveats: While mathematically this proof simply shifts fan colour indices at or above c by 1 to skip the deleted colour, Lean formalises colours as elements of finite types Fin n. Working with dependent subtypes requires explicit boundary arithmetic via omega, case splits on dependent conditionals (dif_pos, dif_neg), and congruence/extensionality lemmas relating Fin elements to their underlying natural numbers (Fin.ext, Fin.val_natAdd, Fin.val_castAdd).

declarations.name: comparison_tree_bind
declarations.informal: Composition of comparison decision trees: run `T`, and at each leaf `a` continue with the tree `f a`. Recursion peels off the first stage and appends a continuation stage below each leaf.
declarations.statement: def comparison_tree_bind {n : ℕ} : ComparisonTree n → (Fin n → ComparisonTree n) → ComparisonTree n
declarations.source:
/-- Sequential composition of comparison trees: `comparison_tree_bind T f` runs the first stage `T` and then the continuation `f a` selected by the returned index. -/
def comparison_tree_bind {n : ℕ} : ComparisonTree n → (Fin n → ComparisonTree n) → ComparisonTree n := fun T f =>
  match T with
  | .leaf a => f a
  | .branch i j l r => .branch i j (comparison_tree_bind l f) (comparison_tree_bind r f)

declarations.name: glove_number_complete_graph_eq_iff_ge
declarations.informal: For any integer $n \ge 2$, the glove number of the complete graph $K_n$ is equal to $n - 1$ if and only if it is at least $n - 1$.
declarations.statement:
theorem glove_number_complete_graph_eq_iff_ge (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    glove_number (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) = n - 1 ↔
    n - 1 ≤ glove_number (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n))
declarations.source:
/-- For n ≥ 2, the glove number of K_n is equal to n - 1 if and only if it is at least n - 1. -/
theorem glove_number_complete_graph_eq_iff_ge (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    glove_number (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) = n - 1 ↔
    n - 1 ≤ glove_number (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) := by
  have h := glove_number_complete_graph_upper_bound n hn
  constructor
  · intro heq
    rw [heq]
  · intro hle
    exact le_antisymm h hle
declarations.reading: For every natural number $n$ such that $2 \le n$, the glove number of the complete graph on the vertex set $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ is equal to $n - 1$ if and only if $n - 1 \le \mathrm{glove\_number}(\mathrm{completeGraph}(\mathrm{Fin}(n)))$.

explanation.summary: The proof establishes that the glove number of K_n equals n - 1 if and only if it is at least n - 1 by using the known upper bound that the glove number is at most n - 1. The forward implication is trivial by reflexivity of ≤, while the reverse implication combines the hypothesis with the upper bound and applies antisymmetry.

steps.claim: The glove number of K_n is at most n - 1.
steps.explanation: By the lemma `glove_number_complete_graph_upper_bound`, the glove number of the complete graph on n vertices is bounded from above by n - 1 when n ≥ 2.
steps.code: have h := glove_number_complete_graph_upper_bound n hn

steps.claim: If the glove number of K_n is equal to n - 1, then it is at least n - 1.
steps.explanation: We split the "if and only if" into both directions. In the forward direction, assuming the glove number equals n - 1, substituting this equality into the desired inequality n - 1 ≤ glove_number(K_n) yields n - 1 ≤ n - 1, which holds by reflexivity.
steps.code:
constructor
  · intro heq
    rw [heq]

steps.claim: If the glove number of K_n is at least n - 1, then it is equal to n - 1.
steps.explanation: In the reverse direction, assuming n - 1 ≤ glove_number(K_n) and combining it with the upper bound glove_number(K_n) ≤ n - 1, the antisymmetry of ≤ (`le_antisymm`) proves the equality.
steps.code:
· intro hle
    exact le_antisymm h hle

glossary.glove_number_complete_graph_upper_bound: For any n ≥ 2, the glove number of the complete graph K_n is at most n - 1.
glossary.le_antisymm: If a ≤ b and b ≤ a in a partial order, then a = b.

caveats: In line 8, rewriting with the hypothesis `heq` replaces the glove number with `n - 1`, resulting in `n - 1 ≤ n - 1`, which Lean's `rw` tactic closes automatically by reflexivity.

declarations.name: glove_number_complete_graph_no_zero_gloves
declarations.informal: For any integer $n \ge 2$, there is no clean handshake sequence with zero gloves covering all edges of the complete graph $K_n$.
declarations.statement:
theorem glove_number_complete_graph_no_zero_gloves (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ¬ has_clean_handshake_seq (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) 0
declarations.source:
/-- For n ≥ 2, there is no clean handshake sequence for K_n using zero gloves. -/
theorem glove_number_complete_graph_no_zero_gloves (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    ¬ has_clean_handshake_seq (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) 0 := by
  rintro ⟨seq, -, hcov⟩
  have hedge : s((⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n), (⟨1, by omega⟩ : Fin n)) ∈
      (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet]
    simp only [SimpleGraph.completeGraph, SimpleGraph.top_adj, ne_eq]
    intro hne
    have := Fin.mk.inj_iff.mp hne
    omega
  obtain ⟨h, hmem, -⟩ := hcov _ hedge
  cases h with
  | single x a y => exact Fin.elim0 a.1
  | double x a b y => exact Fin.elim0 a.1
declarations.reading: For every natural number $n$ such that $2 \le n$, there does not exist a clean handshake sequence using 0 gloves (`Fin 0`) that covers all edges of the complete graph on vertices `Fin n`.

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by contradiction. If a clean handshake sequence using zero gloves could cover the complete graph K_n for n ≥ 2, it would in particular have to cover the edge between vertices 0 and 1. However, every handshake constructor (single or double) requires at least one glove from the glove set Fin 0, which is empty, so no such handshake can exist.

steps.claim: Assume for contradiction that there exists a clean handshake sequence with zero gloves covering all edges of K_n.
steps.explanation: We assume the negation of the theorem and unpack the existential hypothesis into a handshake sequence seq, its cleanliness condition (which is unused), and a coverage hypothesis hcov asserting that every edge in the complete graph K_n is covered by some handshake in seq.
steps.code: rintro ⟨seq, -, hcov⟩

steps.claim: The unordered pair {0, 1} is an edge in the complete graph K_n.
steps.explanation: Because n ≥ 2, the elements 0 and 1 are well-defined vertices in Fin n (justified by linear arithmetic). By definition, an unordered pair forms an edge of K_n if and only if the vertices are adjacent, which in a complete graph means they are distinct. Assuming for contradiction that 0 = 1 in Fin n, their underlying natural numbers would be equal, yielding 0 = 1, which omega refutes.
steps.code:
have hedge : s((⟨0, by omega⟩ : Fin n), (⟨1, by omega⟩ : Fin n)) ∈
      (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet := by
    rw [SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet]
    simp only [SimpleGraph.completeGraph, SimpleGraph.top_adj, ne_eq]
    intro hne
    have := Fin.mk.inj_iff.mp hne
    omega

steps.claim: Contradiction: covering the edge requires a handshake, but any handshake requires at least one glove and no gloves exist.
steps.explanation: Applying the covering hypothesis hcov to the edge {0, 1} yields a handshake h in seq that covers it. By the inductive definition of Handshake, h must be either a single-glove handshake or a double-glove handshake. In both cases, the constructor requires a glove identifier a.1 ∈ Fin 0. Since the type Fin 0 has no elements, Fin.elim0 closes both branches with a contradiction.
steps.code:
obtain ⟨h, hmem, -⟩ := hcov _ hedge
  cases h with
  | single x a y => exact Fin.elim0 a.1
  | double x a b y => exact Fin.elim0 a.1

glossary.Fin.elim0: An element of the empty type Fin 0 is impossible, so it can prove any goal.
glossary.Fin.mk.inj_iff.mp: If two elements of Fin n are equal, their underlying natural numbers are equal.
glossary.ne_eq: The inequality a ≠ b is definitionally the proposition ¬(a = b).
glossary.SimpleGraph.completeGraph: The complete graph on a vertex type V, in which all distinct vertices are adjacent.
glossary.SimpleGraph.mem_edgeSet: An unordered pair s(v, w) belongs to the edge set of a graph if and only if v and w are adjacent.
glossary.SimpleGraph.top_adj: In the complete graph ⊤, two vertices are adjacent if and only if they are not equal.
