declarations.name: spider_gamma_reversal
declarations.informal: For every fuel, centre status s and leg list L, the value of the spider state (s;L) equals the value of the state obtained by exchanging incoming and outgoing in the centre status and in every far end of L.
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_gamma_reversal (fuel : ℕ) (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) :
    spider_gamma fuel s L =
      spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2)))
declarations.source:
lemma spider_gamma_reversal_rho_star (h : ℕ) (phi : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_rho_star h (spider_reverse_leg_end phi) = spider_rho_star h phi := by
  cases phi <;> rfl

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_free_foldl (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) (acc : ℕ) :
    List.foldl (fun acc p => acc ^^^ spider_rho_star p.1 (spider_reverse_leg_end p.2)) acc L =
      List.foldl (fun acc p => acc ^^^ spider_rho_star p.1 p.2) acc L := by
  induction L generalizing acc with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons head tail ih =>
    rw [List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_cons, spider_gamma_reversal_rho_star]
    exact ih _

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_inj (a b : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_reverse_leg_end a = spider_reverse_leg_end b ↔ a = b := by
  constructor
  · intro h; cases a <;> cases b <;> revert h <;> decide
  · intro h; rw [h]

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne (a b : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_reverse_leg_end a ≠ spider_reverse_leg_end b ↔ a ≠ b := by
  rw [not_iff_not, spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_inj]

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne_free (x : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_reverse_leg_end x ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ↔ x ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free := by
  cases x <;> simp [spider_reverse_leg_end]

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_rho (h : ℕ) (delta phi : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_rho h (spider_reverse_leg_end delta) (spider_reverse_leg_end phi) = spider_rho h delta phi := by
  cases delta <;> cases phi <;> rfl

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_update_centre (s : CentreStatus) (delta : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_update_centre (spider_reverse_centre_status s) (spider_reverse_leg_end delta) =
      spider_reverse_centre_status (spider_update_centre s delta) := by
  cases s <;> cases delta <;> rfl

theorem spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_option_eq
    (fuel : ℕ)
    (ih : ∀ (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)),
      spider_gamma fuel s L = spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))))
    (s : CentreStatus) (rest : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd))
    (h j : ℕ) (phi delta : SpiderLegEnd) :
    (if (j == h) = true ∧ spider_reverse_leg_end phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ spider_reverse_leg_end delta ≠ spider_reverse_leg_end phi then Option.none
     else
       have d := spider_rho (h - j) (spider_reverse_leg_end delta) (spider_reverse_leg_end phi);
       if j ≥ 2 then
         have new_L := (j - 1, spider_reverse_leg_end delta) :: rest.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2));
         some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s) new_L)
       else
         have new_s := spider_update_centre (spider_reverse_centre_status s) (spider_reverse_leg_end delta);
         some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel new_s (rest.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2)))))
    =
    (if (j == h) = true ∧ phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ phi then Option.none
     else
       have d := spider_rho (h - j) delta phi;
       if j ≥ 2 then
         have new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: rest;
         some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel s new_L)
       else
         have new_s := spider_update_centre s delta;
         some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel new_s rest)) := by
  simp only [spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne_free, spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne, spider_gamma_reversal_rho]
  split_ifs with hc hj
  · rfl
  · rw [ih s ((j - 1, delta) :: rest)]
    rfl
  · rw [spider_gamma_reversal_update_centre]
    rw [ih (spider_update_centre s delta) rest]

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_two_perm (F G : SpiderLegEnd → Option ℕ)
    (h_rev : ∀ delta, G (spider_reverse_leg_end delta) = F delta) :
    ([SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap G).Perm
      ([SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap F) := by
  have h1 : [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap G =
      ([SpiderLegEnd.outward, SpiderLegEnd.inward].map spider_reverse_leg_end).filterMap G := by rfl
  rw [h1, List.filterMap_map]
  have hcomp : (G ∘ spider_reverse_leg_end) = F := by
    funext d; exact h_rev d
  rw [hcomp]
  have h2 : [SpiderLegEnd.outward, SpiderLegEnd.inward] = [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].reverse := rfl
  rw [h2, List.filterMap_reverse]
  exact List.reverse_perm _

def spider_gamma_reversal_options (fuel : ℕ) (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) : List ℕ :=
  List.flatMap
    (fun x =>
      match x with
      | ((h, phi), idx) =>
        have rest := L.eraseIdx idx;
        List.flatMap
          (fun j_zero =>
            have j := j_zero + 1;
            List.filterMap
              (fun delta =>
                if (j == h) = true ∧ phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ phi then Option.none
                else
                  have d := spider_rho (h - j) delta phi;
                  if j ≥ 2 then
                    have new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: rest;
                    some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel s new_L)
                  else
                    have new_s := spider_update_centre s delta;
                    some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel new_s rest))
              [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward])
          (List.range h))
    L.zipIdx

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm (fuel : ℕ)
    (ih : ∀ (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)),
      spider_gamma fuel s L = spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))))
    (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) :
    (spider_gamma_reversal_options fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
      (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2)))).Perm
    (spider_gamma_reversal_options fuel s L) := by
  unfold spider_gamma_reversal_options
  have hzip : (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))).zipIdx =
      L.zipIdx.map (fun ((h, phi), idx) => ((h, spider_reverse_leg_end phi), idx)) := by
    rw [List.zipIdx_map]
    rfl
  rw [hzip, List.flatMap_map]
  apply List.Perm.flatMap_left
  intro ⟨⟨h, phi⟩, idx⟩ hmem
  dsimp only
  rw [List.eraseIdx_map]
  apply List.Perm.flatMap_left
  intro j_zero hjmem
  apply spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_two_perm
  intro delta
  exact spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_option_eq fuel ih s (L.eraseIdx idx) h (j_zero + 1) phi delta

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_loop_congr {l1 l2 : List ℕ} (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ l1 ↔ x ∈ l2) (fuel : ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    nat_mex_list.loop l1 n fuel = nat_mex_list.loop l2 n fuel := by
  induction fuel generalizing n with
  | zero =>
    rw [nat_mex_list.loop.eq_def, nat_mex_list.loop.eq_def]
  | succ fuel ih =>
    rw [nat_mex_list.loop.eq_def, nat_mex_list.loop.eq_def]
    by_cases hn : n ∈ l1
    · have hn2 : n ∈ l2 := (hmem n).mp hn
      simp [hn, hn2, ih]
    · have hn2 : n ∉ l2 := fun h => hn ((hmem n).mpr h)
      simp [hn, hn2]

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of_perm {l1 l2 : List ℕ} (h : l1.Perm l2) :
    nat_mex_list l1 = nat_mex_list l2 := by
  unfold nat_mex_list
  rw [h.length_eq]
  exact spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_loop_congr (fun _ => h.mem_iff) (l2.length + 1) 0

theorem spider_gamma_reversal_step (fuel : ℕ)
    (ih : ∀ (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)),
      spider_gamma fuel s L = spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))))
    (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) :
    spider_gamma (fuel + 1) s L =
      spider_gamma (fuel + 1) (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))) := by
  cases s
  · cases L with
    | nil => rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rfl
    | cons p1 tl =>
      cases tl with
      | nil =>
        rcases p1 with ⟨h, phi⟩
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rfl
      | cons p2 rest =>
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        exact (spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of_perm
          (spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm fuel ih CentreStatus.none (p1 :: p2 :: rest))).symm
  · cases L with
    | nil => rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rfl
    | cons p1 tl =>
      cases tl with
      | nil =>
        rcases p1 with ⟨h, phi⟩
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        have := (spider_gamma_reversal_rho h SpiderLegEnd.outward phi).symm
        exact this
      | cons p2 rest =>
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        exact (spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of_perm
          (spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm fuel ih CentreStatus.incoming (p1 :: p2 :: rest))).symm
  · cases L with
    | nil => rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rfl
    | cons p1 tl =>
      cases tl with
      | nil =>
        rcases p1 with ⟨h, phi⟩
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        have := (spider_gamma_reversal_rho h SpiderLegEnd.inward phi).symm
        exact this
      | cons p2 rest =>
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        exact (spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of_perm
          (spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm fuel ih CentreStatus.outgoing (p1 :: p2 :: rest))).symm
  · rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
    dsimp [spider_reverse_centre_status]
    rw [List.foldl_map]
    exact (spider_gamma_reversal_free_foldl L 0).symm

/-- Reversing the centre status and every far end leaves the Grundy value unchanged (paper Lemma 8.3). -/
theorem spider_gamma_reversal (fuel : ℕ) (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) :
    spider_gamma fuel s L =
      spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))) := by
  induction fuel generalizing s L with
  | zero =>
    rw [spider_gamma.eq_1, spider_gamma.eq_1]
  | succ fuel ih =>
    exact spider_gamma_reversal_step fuel ih s L

explanation.summary: The theorem establishes that the Sprague-Grundy value `spider_gamma` of a spider position is invariant under simultaneously reversing the inward and outward orientations of the centre status and every leg endpoint. The proof proceeds by induction on `fuel`. Base cases with a free centre or at most one leg reduce directly to the reflectional symmetries of the elementary Grundy functions `spider_rho_star` and `spider_rho`. For general configurations, every move in the reversed position produces the same Grundy value as the corresponding move in the original position, so the lists of reachable options are permutations of each other. Because the minimal excluded value (`nat_mex_list`) is invariant under list permutations, the Grundy values of the original and reversed positions coincide.

steps.claim: `spider_rho_star` is invariant under reversing the leg end orientation.
steps.explanation: By definition, `spider_rho_star h phi` is `h % 2` when `phi = SpiderLegEnd.free` and `h` otherwise. Because `spider_reverse_leg_end` swaps `inward` and `outward` while fixing `free`, `spider_rho_star` evaluates definitionally to the same quantity in all three cases.
steps.code:
lemma spider_gamma_reversal_rho_star (h : ℕ) (phi : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_rho_star h (spider_reverse_leg_end phi) = spider_rho_star h phi := by
  cases phi <;> rfl

steps.claim: Reversing leg ends preserves the XOR sum of `spider_rho_star` folded over any leg list.
steps.explanation: By induction on the leg list `L`. The empty list is trivial. For `head :: tail`, we unfold `List.foldl_cons` on both sides and substitute `spider_gamma_reversal_rho_star` on `head`, ensuring that the accumulators match before invoking the induction hypothesis on `tail`.
steps.code:
lemma spider_gamma_reversal_free_foldl (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) (acc : ℕ) :
    List.foldl (fun acc p => acc ^^^ spider_rho_star p.1 (spider_reverse_leg_end p.2)) acc L =
      List.foldl (fun acc p => acc ^^^ spider_rho_star p.1 p.2) acc L := by
  induction L generalizing acc with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons head tail ih =>
    rw [List.foldl_cons, List.foldl_cons, spider_gamma_reversal_rho_star]
    exact ih _

steps.claim: Reversing leg ends is an injective involution that preserves distinctness and non-freeness.
steps.explanation: Injectivity (`spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_inj`) is verified by exhausting all 9 constructor pairs for `(a, b)` with `decide`. Rewriting by `not_iff_not` shows that reversal preserves distinctness (`spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne`), and case analysis with simplification proves that an orientation is not `free` if and only if its reversal is not `free` (`spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne_free`).
steps.code:
lemma spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_inj (a b : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_reverse_leg_end a = spider_reverse_leg_end b ↔ a = b := by
  constructor
  · intro h; cases a <;> cases b <;> revert h <;> decide
  · intro h; rw [h]

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne (a b : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_reverse_leg_end a ≠ spider_reverse_leg_end b ↔ a ≠ b := by
  rw [not_iff_not, spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_inj]

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne_free (x : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_reverse_leg_end x ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ↔ x ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free := by
  cases x <;> simp [spider_reverse_leg_end]

steps.claim: `spider_rho` is invariant under simultaneously reversing both leg endpoints.
steps.explanation: The value `spider_rho h delta phi` depends only on whether `phi` is `free`, and if not, whether `delta` and `phi` share the same orientation. Since `spider_reverse_leg_end` is a bijection, `delta = phi` holds if and only if their reversals are equal, so case exhaustion over all 9 pairs evaluates definitionally to the same result.
steps.code:
lemma spider_gamma_reversal_rho (h : ℕ) (delta phi : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_rho h (spider_reverse_leg_end delta) (spider_reverse_leg_end phi) = spider_rho h delta phi := by
  cases delta <;> cases phi <;> rfl

steps.claim: Updating the centre status commutes with reversing orientations.
steps.explanation: Exhaustive case analysis on the 4 centre statuses and 3 leg end orientations confirms definitionally that updating a reversed centre with a reversed leg end yields the reversal of the original updated centre.
steps.code:
lemma spider_gamma_reversal_update_centre (s : CentreStatus) (delta : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_update_centre (spider_reverse_centre_status s) (spider_reverse_leg_end delta) =
      spider_reverse_centre_status (spider_update_centre s delta) := by
  cases s <;> cases delta <;> rfl

steps.claim: Under the induction hypothesis on fuel, each transition option in the reversed position produces the same outcome as in the original position.
steps.explanation: We rewrite the move conditions and weights using `spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne_free`, `spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne`, and `spider_gamma_reversal_rho`. Splitting on the case conditions, an illegal move returns `none` on both sides. If the remaining leg length satisfies `j ≥ 2`, the move creates a new shortened leg, and the induction hypothesis `ih` applies to `(j - 1, delta) :: rest`. If `j < 2`, the leg merges into the centre, and rewriting by `spider_gamma_reversal_update_centre` allows `ih` to match the two options.
steps.code:
theorem spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_option_eq
    (fuel : ℕ)
    (ih : ∀ (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)),
      spider_gamma fuel s L = spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))))
    (s : CentreStatus) (rest : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd))
    (h j : ℕ) (phi delta : SpiderLegEnd) :
    (if (j == h) = true ∧ spider_reverse_leg_end phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ spider_reverse_leg_end delta ≠ spider_reverse_leg_end phi then Option.none
     else
       have d := spider_rho (h - j) (spider_reverse_leg_end delta) (spider_reverse_leg_end phi);
       if j ≥ 2 then
         have new_L := (j - 1, spider_reverse_leg_end delta) :: rest.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2));
         some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s) new_L)
       else
         have new_s := spider_update_centre (spider_reverse_centre_status s) (spider_reverse_leg_end delta);
         some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel new_s (rest.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2)))))
    =
    (if (j == h) = true ∧ phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ phi then Option.none
     else
       have d := spider_rho (h - j) delta phi;
       if j ≥ 2 then
         have new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: rest;
         some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel s new_L)
       else
         have new_s := spider_update_centre s delta;
         some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel new_s rest)) := by
  simp only [spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne_free, spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne, spider_gamma_reversal_rho]
  split_ifs with hc hj
  · rfl
  · rw [ih s ((j - 1, delta) :: rest)]
    rfl
  · rw [spider_gamma_reversal_update_centre]
    rw [ih (spider_update_centre s delta) rest]

steps.claim: Filter-mapping functions related by orientation reversal over `[inward, outward]` produces permuted lists.
steps.explanation: Applying `spider_reverse_leg_end` to `[inward, outward]` yields `[outward, inward]`, which is the reverse of `[inward, outward]`. Using `List.filterMap_map` and the relation `G ∘ spider_reverse_leg_end = F`, this simplifies to `([inward, outward].filterMap F).reverse`, which is a permutation of the original by `List.reverse_perm`.
steps.code:
lemma spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_two_perm (F G : SpiderLegEnd → Option ℕ)
    (h_rev : ∀ delta, G (spider_reverse_leg_end delta) = F delta) :
    ([SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap G).Perm
      ([SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap F) := by
  have h1 : [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap G =
      ([SpiderLegEnd.outward, SpiderLegEnd.inward].map spider_reverse_leg_end).filterMap G := by rfl
  rw [h1, List.filterMap_map]
  have hcomp : (G ∘ spider_reverse_leg_end) = F := by
    funext d; exact h_rev d
  rw [hcomp]
  have h2 : [SpiderLegEnd.outward, SpiderLegEnd.inward] = [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].reverse := rfl
  rw [h2, List.filterMap_reverse]
  exact List.reverse_perm _

steps.claim: The list of all move options available in the reversed state is a permutation of the options in the original state.
steps.explanation: We unfold `spider_gamma_reversal_options`. Mapping reversal over `L` commutes with indexing by `List.zipIdx_map`. Using `List.Perm.flatMap_left`, we distribute the permutation across all legs, commute leg deletion with `List.eraseIdx_map`, distribute across all cut points `j`, and finally apply `spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_two_perm` combined with `spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_option_eq` to show that the options generated for `delta ∈ [inward, outward]` are permuted.
steps.code:
def spider_gamma_reversal_options (fuel : ℕ) (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) : List ℕ :=
  List.flatMap
    (fun x =>
      match x with
      | ((h, phi), idx) =>
        have rest := L.eraseIdx idx;
        List.flatMap
          (fun j_zero =>
            have j := j_zero + 1;
            List.filterMap
              (fun delta =>
                if (j == h) = true ∧ phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ phi then Option.none
                else
                  have d := spider_rho (h - j) delta phi;
                  if j ≥ 2 then
                    have new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: rest;
                    some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel s new_L)
                  else
                    have new_s := spider_update_centre s delta;
                    some (d ^^^ spider_gamma fuel new_s rest))
              [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward])
          (List.range h))
    L.zipIdx

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm (fuel : ℕ)
    (ih : ∀ (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)),
      spider_gamma fuel s L = spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))))
    (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) :
    (spider_gamma_reversal_options fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
      (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2)))).Perm
    (spider_gamma_reversal_options fuel s L) := by
  unfold spider_gamma_reversal_options
  have hzip : (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))).zipIdx =
      L.zipIdx.map (fun ((h, phi), idx) => ((h, spider_reverse_leg_end phi), idx)) := by
    rw [List.zipIdx_map]
    rfl
  rw [hzip, List.flatMap_map]
  apply List.Perm.flatMap_left
  intro ⟨⟨h, phi⟩, idx⟩ hmem
  dsimp only
  rw [List.eraseIdx_map]
  apply List.Perm.flatMap_left
  intro j_zero hjmem
  apply spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_two_perm
  intro delta
  exact spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_option_eq fuel ih s (L.eraseIdx idx) h (j_zero + 1) phi delta

steps.claim: The minimal excluded value function `nat_mex_list` is invariant under list permutation.
steps.explanation: First, induction on fuel in `spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_loop_congr` shows that the loop evaluating the mex depends only on list membership `x ∈ l`. Since a permutation preserves both length (`h.length_eq`) and element membership (`h.mem_iff`), `nat_mex_list` computes the exact same value on `l1` and `l2`.
steps.code:
lemma spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_loop_congr {l1 l2 : List ℕ} (hmem : ∀ x, x ∈ l1 ↔ x ∈ l2) (fuel : ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    nat_mex_list.loop l1 n fuel = nat_mex_list.loop l2 n fuel := by
  induction fuel generalizing n with
  | zero =>
    rw [nat_mex_list.loop.eq_def, nat_mex_list.loop.eq_def]
  | succ fuel ih =>
    rw [nat_mex_list.loop.eq_def, nat_mex_list.loop.eq_def]
    by_cases hn : n ∈ l1
    · have hn2 : n ∈ l2 := (hmem n).mp hn
      simp [hn, hn2, ih]
    · have hn2 : n ∉ l2 := fun h => hn ((hmem n).mpr h)
      simp [hn, hn2]

lemma spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of_perm {l1 l2 : List ℕ} (h : l1.Perm l2) :
    nat_mex_list l1 = nat_mex_list l2 := by
  unfold nat_mex_list
  rw [h.length_eq]
  exact spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_loop_congr (fun _ => h.mem_iff) (l2.length + 1) 0

steps.claim: The inductive step for `spider_gamma` holds for fuel + 1.
steps.explanation: We unfold `spider_gamma` via `spider_gamma.eq_def` and case-split on `s`: when `s` is `none`, `incoming`, or `outgoing`, positions with at most one leg simplify by definition or by `spider_gamma_reversal_rho`, while positions with at least two legs match because their options are permutations (`spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm`) and mex is permutation-invariant (`spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of_perm`). When `s = free`, the value is an XOR sum over `L`, which is invariant by `List.foldl_map` and `spider_gamma_reversal_free_foldl`.
steps.code:
theorem spider_gamma_reversal_step (fuel : ℕ)
    (ih : ∀ (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)),
      spider_gamma fuel s L = spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))))
    (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) :
    spider_gamma (fuel + 1) s L =
      spider_gamma (fuel + 1) (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))) := by
  cases s
  · cases L with
    | nil => rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rfl
    | cons p1 tl =>
      cases tl with
      | nil =>
        rcases p1 with ⟨h, phi⟩
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rfl
      | cons p2 rest =>
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        exact (spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of_perm
          (spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm fuel ih CentreStatus.none (p1 :: p2 :: rest))).symm
  · cases L with
    | nil => rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rfl
    | cons p1 tl =>
      cases tl with
      | nil =>
        rcases p1 with ⟨h, phi⟩
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        have := (spider_gamma_reversal_rho h SpiderLegEnd.outward phi).symm
        exact this
      | cons p2 rest =>
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        exact (spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of_perm
          (spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm fuel ih CentreStatus.incoming (p1 :: p2 :: rest))).symm
  · cases L with
    | nil => rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rfl
    | cons p1 tl =>
      cases tl with
      | nil =>
        rcases p1 with ⟨h, phi⟩
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        have := (spider_gamma_reversal_rho h SpiderLegEnd.inward phi).symm
        exact this
      | cons p2 rest =>
        rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
        dsimp only [spider_reverse_centre_status]
        exact (spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of_perm
          (spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm fuel ih CentreStatus.outgoing (p1 :: p2 :: rest))).symm
  · rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]; rw [spider_gamma.eq_def]
    dsimp [spider_reverse_centre_status]
    rw [List.foldl_map]
    exact (spider_gamma_reversal_free_foldl L 0).symm

steps.claim: The reversal theorem `spider_gamma_reversal` holds for all fuel, centre statuses, and leg lists.
steps.explanation: By induction on `fuel`. When `fuel = 0`, both sides vanish by `spider_gamma.eq_1`. In the inductive step `fuel + 1`, we directly apply `spider_gamma_reversal_step` with the induction hypothesis `ih`.
steps.code:
/-- Reversing the centre status and every far end leaves the Grundy value unchanged (paper Lemma 8.3). -/
theorem spider_gamma_reversal (fuel : ℕ) (s : CentreStatus) (L : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)) :
    spider_gamma fuel s L =
      spider_gamma fuel (spider_reverse_centre_status s)
        (L.map (fun p => (p.1, spider_reverse_leg_end p.2))) := by
  induction fuel generalizing s L with
  | zero =>
    rw [spider_gamma.eq_1, spider_gamma.eq_1]
  | succ fuel ih =>
    exact spider_gamma_reversal_step fuel ih s L

glossary.List.foldl_map: Folding over a mapped list equals folding the composed operation over the original list.
glossary.List.filterMap_map: Applying `filterMap g` to a mapped list `List.map f l` equals `List.filterMap (g ∘ f) l`.
glossary.List.filterMap_reverse: Filter-mapping over a reversed list yields the reverse of the filter-mapped list.
glossary.List.reverse_perm: Any list is a permutation of its list reversal.
glossary.List.zipIdx_map: Zipping indices into a mapped list is equivalent to mapping the element transformation over the zipped original list.
glossary.List.flatMap_map: Flat-mapping `g` over `List.map f l` equals flat-mapping `g ∘ f` over `l`.
glossary.List.Perm.flatMap_left: If `f a` is a permutation of `g a` for each `a ∈ l`, then flat-mapping `f` over `l` is a permutation of flat-mapping `g` over `l`.
glossary.List.eraseIdx_map: Erasing the element at index `n` commutes with mapping a function over the list.
glossary.nat_mex_list.loop.eq_def: The defining recurrence of `nat_mex_list.loop`, checking membership at each candidate natural number.
glossary.not_iff_not: Two propositions are equivalent if and only if their negations are equivalent.
glossary.spider_gamma.eq_def: The defining equation of `spider_gamma`, unfolding its evaluation by cases on fuel, centre status, and leg configuration.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_free_foldl: When the centre is free, reversing leg ends preserves the XOR sum of `spider_rho_star` values.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_option_e: Assuming the reversal induction hypothesis for lower fuel, each individual move option under reversed parameters produces the exact same Grundy value as the original move.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_filterMap_two_perm: If a function on reversed leg ends agrees with another function, filtering and mapping them over `[inward, outward]` produces mutually permuted lists.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_inj: Reversing a leg end orientation is an injective operation.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne: Two leg ends are distinct if and only if their reversals are distinct.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_leg_end_ne_free: A leg end is not `free` if and only if its reversal is not `free`.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_loop_: The search loop for the minimal excluded value depends only on the elements present in the list, not their order.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_nat_mex_list_eq_of: Two lists that are permutations of each other have the same minimal excluded value (`nat_mex_list`).
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_options_perm: The list of all legal move options from the reversed state is a permutation of the options from the original state.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_rho: The atomic Grundy function `spider_rho` is invariant under reversing both endpoints simultaneously.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_rho_star: The detached leg Grundy function `spider_rho_star` is invariant under reversing the leg's end orientation.
glossary.spider_gamma_reversal_step: If `spider_gamma` is invariant under reversal at fuel `n`, it is also invariant under reversal at fuel `n + 1`.

declarations.name: nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt
declarations.informal: For a list l of naturals, nat_mex_list l is not a member of l, and every natural number below nat_mex_list l is a member of l.
declarations.statement:
theorem nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt (l : List ℕ) :
    nat_mex_list l ∉ l ∧ ∀ k, k < nat_mex_list l → k ∈ l
declarations.source:
lemma nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt_loop_spec (l : List ℕ) (fuel : ℕ) (n : ℕ) :
    (nat_mex_list.loop l n fuel ∉ l ∧ (∀ k, n ≤ k → k < nat_mex_list.loop l n fuel → k ∈ l)) ∨
    (nat_mex_list.loop l n fuel = n + fuel ∧ (∀ k, n ≤ k → k < n + fuel → k ∈ l)) := by
  induction fuel generalizing n with
  | zero =>
    right
    exact ⟨rfl, fun k h1 h2 => by omega⟩
  | succ fuel ih =>
    have hstep : nat_mex_list.loop l n (fuel + 1) = if n ∈ l then nat_mex_list.loop l (n + 1) fuel else n := rfl
    rw [hstep]
    by_cases hn : n ∈ l
    · rw [if_pos hn]
      rcases ih (n + 1) with (⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩)
      · left
        refine ⟨h1, fun k hk1 hk2 => ?_⟩
        rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hk1 with rfl | hlt
        · exact hn
        · exact h2 k hlt hk2
      · right
        refine ⟨by omega, fun k hk1 hk2 => ?_⟩
        rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hk1 with rfl | hlt
        · exact hn
        · exact h2 k hlt (by omega)
    · rw [if_neg hn]
      left
      exact ⟨hn, fun k hk1 hk2 => by omega⟩

/-- The mex of a finite list of naturals is absent from the list, and every smaller number occurs in it. -/
theorem nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt (l : List ℕ) :
    nat_mex_list l ∉ l ∧ ∀ k, k < nat_mex_list l → k ∈ l := by
  change (nat_mex_list.loop l 0 (l.length + 1) ∉ l ∧ ∀ k, k < nat_mex_list.loop l 0 (l.length + 1) → k ∈ l)
  rcases nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt_loop_spec l (l.length + 1) 0 with (⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨-, h2⟩)
  · exact ⟨h1, fun k hk => h2 k (Nat.zero_le k) hk⟩
  · have hsub : List.range (l.length + 1) ⊆ l := by
      intro x hx
      rw [List.mem_range] at hx
      exact h2 x (Nat.zero_le x) (by omega)
    have hle := List.Nodup.length_le_of_subset List.nodup_range hsub
    rw [List.length_range] at hle
    omega

explanation.summary: The theorem proves that `nat_mex_list l`—computed by a loop starting at 0 with fuel |l| + 1—is the minimum excluded value of l. An auxiliary lemma shows by induction on fuel that searching from n either finds an excluded value not in l whose predecessors down to n are all in l, or exhausts fuel reaching n + fuel with all intermediate values in l. When specialized to start 0 with fuel |l| + 1, the exhausted-fuel alternative would imply that all |l| + 1 distinct elements of `List.range (l.length + 1)` belong to l, contradicting the list length |l|. Hence only the first alternative can occur, proving that `nat_mex_list l ∉ l` and all smaller naturals belong to l.

steps.claim: When fuel is 0, the loop specification holds because the loop reaches n + 0 with no intermediate values to check.
steps.explanation: We proceed by induction on `fuel`, generalizing over n. For the base case `fuel = 0`, the loop immediately returns n, which equals n + 0. The second disjunct holds: the equality is definitional, and the condition that every k with n ≤ k < n + 0 belongs to l is vacuously satisfied because n ≤ k < n is an arithmetic contradiction.
steps.code:
induction fuel generalizing n with
  | zero =>
    right
    exact ⟨rfl, fun k h1 h2 => by omega⟩

steps.claim: For fuel + 1, we unfold one step of the loop and branch on whether n ∈ l.
steps.explanation: In the inductive step, the definition of the loop unwinds one iteration: if n ∈ l, it recurses to `loop l (n + 1) fuel`, and otherwise it terminates with n. We rewrite using this definition and perform a case split on whether n ∈ l.
steps.code:
| succ fuel ih =>
    have hstep : nat_mex_list.loop l n (fuel + 1) = if n ∈ l then nat_mex_list.loop l (n + 1) fuel else n := rfl
    rw [hstep]
    by_cases hn : n ∈ l

steps.claim: If n ∈ l and the induction hypothesis on n + 1 yields an excluded value, then the first disjunct holds for n.
steps.explanation: Since n ∈ l, rewriting with `if_pos` shows the loop proceeds to `loop l (n + 1) fuel`. In the first case of the induction hypothesis for n + 1, the loop produces a value m ∉ l such that every k with n + 1 ≤ k < m is in l. For any k with n ≤ k < m, by `eq_or_lt_of_le` either k = n (which is in l by assumption) or n < k (which implies n + 1 ≤ k < m, so k ∈ l by the induction hypothesis). Thus the first disjunct holds for n.
steps.code:
· rw [if_pos hn]
      rcases ih (n + 1) with (⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩)
      · left
        refine ⟨h1, fun k hk1 hk2 => ?_⟩
        rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hk1 with rfl | hlt
        · exact hn
        · exact h2 k hlt hk2

steps.claim: If n ∈ l and the induction hypothesis on n + 1 exhausts fuel, then the second disjunct holds for n.
steps.explanation: In the second case of the induction hypothesis for n + 1, the loop reaches (n + 1) + fuel = n + (fuel + 1) with all k in [n + 1, n + 1 + fuel) belonging to l. For any k with n ≤ k < n + (fuel + 1), either k = n (in l by assumption) or n < k (so n + 1 ≤ k < n + 1 + fuel, hence in l by the induction hypothesis), using `eq_or_lt_of_le` and linear arithmetic.
steps.code:
· right
        refine ⟨by omega, fun k hk1 hk2 => ?_⟩
        rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hk1 with rfl | hlt
        · exact hn
        · exact h2 k hlt (by omega)

steps.claim: If n ∉ l, the loop halts immediately and the first disjunct holds.
steps.explanation: Since n ∉ l, rewriting with `if_neg` shows that the loop returns n. The first disjunct holds: n ∉ l is our hypothesis, and the condition on all k with n ≤ k < n is vacuously true by linear arithmetic.
steps.code:
· rw [if_neg hn]
      left
      exact ⟨hn, fun k hk1 hk2 => by omega⟩

steps.claim: Expressing `nat_mex_list l` via the loop specification with start 0 and fuel |l| + 1, the theorem follows if an excluded value is found.
steps.explanation: By definition, `nat_mex_list l` is `loop l 0 (l.length + 1)`. Applying `nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt_loop_spec` with starting value 0 and fuel l.length + 1, the first alternative gives that the returned value is not in l and every k with 0 ≤ k < loop is in l. Since 0 ≤ k is unconditionally true for naturals (`Nat.zero_le`), every k smaller than the loop's output belongs to l, which directly establishes the theorem.
steps.code:
change (nat_mex_list.loop l 0 (l.length + 1) ∉ l ∧ ∀ k, k < nat_mex_list.loop l 0 (l.length + 1) → k ∈ l)
  rcases nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt_loop_spec l (l.length + 1) 0 with (⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨-, h2⟩)
  · exact ⟨h1, fun k hk => h2 k (Nat.zero_le k) hk⟩

steps.claim: If the loop instead exhausts its fuel, then every element of `List.range (l.length + 1)` belongs to l.
steps.explanation: Under the second alternative of the loop specification, every natural k < l.length + 1 (with 0 ≤ k by `Nat.zero_le`) must belong to l. Any element x in `List.range (l.length + 1)` satisfies x < l.length + 1 by `List.mem_range`, so x ∈ l. Thus `List.range (l.length + 1) ⊆ l`.
steps.code:
· have hsub : List.range (l.length + 1) ⊆ l := by
      intro x hx
      rw [List.mem_range] at hx
      exact h2 x (Nat.zero_le x) (by omega)

steps.claim: The inclusion `List.range (l.length + 1) ⊆ l` yields a length contradiction, ruling out the exhausted-fuel case.
steps.explanation: Because `List.range (l.length + 1)` contains no duplicate elements (`List.nodup_range`), its inclusion in l implies that its length is at most that of l (`List.Nodup.length_le_of_subset`). Since the length of `List.range (l.length + 1)` is l.length + 1 (`List.length_range`), we obtain l.length + 1 ≤ l.length, an impossible inequality that `omega` uses to complete the proof by contradiction.
steps.code:
have hle := List.Nodup.length_le_of_subset List.nodup_range hsub
    rw [List.length_range] at hle
    omega

glossary.if_pos: If condition c is true, then `if c then t else e` equals t.
glossary.eq_or_lt_of_le: If a ≤ b in a partial order, then either a = b or a < b.
glossary.if_neg: If condition c is false, then `if c then t else e` equals e.
glossary.nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt_loop_spec: For any list l, starting number n, and fuel, the loop either finds an excluded value not in l whose predecessors down to n belong to l, or reaches n + fuel with all intermediate values in l.
glossary.Nat.zero_le: Every natural number is greater than or equal to 0.
glossary.List.mem_range: A natural number m is an element of `List.range n` if and only if m < n.
glossary.List.Nodup.length_le_of_subset: If a duplicate-free list l₁ is a subset of l₂, then the length of l₁ is at most the length of l₂.
glossary.List.nodup_range: The list `List.range n` has no duplicate elements.
glossary.List.length_range: The length of `List.range n` is n.

caveats: The function `nat_mex_list` is defined using a fuel-bounded helper `loop` to satisfy Lean's termination checker; setting fuel to `l.length + 1` ensures that the loop cannot exhaust its fuel without violating the pigeonhole principle for lists.

declarations.name: nat_mex_list_eq_zero
declarations.informal: If a list of naturals does not contain 0, then its mex (minimum excluded value) is 0.
declarations.statement: theorem nat_mex_list_eq_zero (l : List ℕ) (h : 0 ∉ l) : nat_mex_list l = 0
declarations.source:
/-- The mex of a list not containing 0 is 0. -/
theorem nat_mex_list_eq_zero (l : List ℕ) (h : 0 ∉ l) : nat_mex_list l = 0 := by
  by_contra hne
  exact h ((nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt l).2 0 (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hne))

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by contradiction. If the mex of the list were non-zero, it would be strictly positive. By the defining property of the minimum excluded value, every natural number strictly less than the mex must belong to the list, which implies that 0 is in the list, contradicting the hypothesis that 0 is not in the list.

steps.claim: Assume, for contradiction, that the mex of the list is not 0.
steps.explanation: We proceed by contradiction (`by_contra hne`), assuming that `nat_mex_list l ≠ 0`.
steps.code: by_contra hne

steps.claim: A contradiction is reached, because 0 must belong to the list.
steps.explanation: Because the mex is non-zero, it is strictly positive (`Nat.pos_of_ne_zero`), which means $0 < \\operatorname{nat\\_mex\\_list} l$. By the second part of `nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt`, any natural number strictly less than the mex must be in the list $l$. Applying this to $0$ shows that $0 \\in l$, directly contradicting the hypothesis $h : 0 \\notin l$.
steps.code: exact h ((nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt l).2 0 (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hne))

glossary.Nat.pos_of_ne_zero: If a natural number is not zero, then it is strictly greater than zero.
glossary.nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt: The mex of a list of natural numbers is not in the list, and every natural number strictly less than the mex is an element of the list.

declarations.name: nat_mex_list_eq_one
declarations.informal: If a list of naturals contains 0 but not 1, then its mex is 1.
declarations.statement: theorem nat_mex_list_eq_one (l : List ℕ) (h0 : 0 ∈ l) (h1 : 1 ∉ l) : nat_mex_list l = 1
declarations.source:
/-- The mex of a list containing 0 but not 1 is 1. -/
theorem nat_mex_list_eq_one (l : List ℕ) (h0 : 0 ∈ l) (h1 : 1 ∉ l) : nat_mex_list l = 1 := by
  obtain ⟨hnot, hlt⟩ := nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt l
  have h_ne_zero : nat_mex_list l ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    apply hnot
    rw [h]
    exact h0
  have h_le_one : nat_mex_list l ≤ 1 := by
    by_contra! h2
    have : 1 ∈ l := hlt 1 h2
    exact h1 this
  omega

explanation.summary: The proof characterises the mex of l by its defining properties: it is not in l, but every strictly smaller natural number is in l. Because 0 is in l, the mex cannot be 0, and because 1 is not in l, the mex cannot be strictly greater than 1. Since the only natural number at most 1 other than 0 is 1, the mex must be 1.

steps.claim: The mex of l is not in l, and every natural number strictly less than the mex belongs to l.
steps.explanation: We unpack the defining properties of the minimum excluded natural number for l using nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt: nat_mex_list l does not belong to l (hnot), and any k < nat_mex_list l must belong to l (hlt).
steps.code: obtain ⟨hnot, hlt⟩ := nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt l

steps.claim: nat_mex_list l ≠ 0
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that the mex were 0. Then, by the non-membership property, 0 would not be in l, which contradicts the hypothesis h0 that 0 ∈ l.
steps.code:
have h_ne_zero : nat_mex_list l ≠ 0 := by
    intro h
    apply hnot
    rw [h]
    exact h0

steps.claim: nat_mex_list l ≤ 1
steps.explanation: Suppose for contradiction that nat_mex_list l > 1. Then 1 < nat_mex_list l, which by the minimality property implies that 1 ∈ l. This contradicts the assumption h1 that 1 ∉ l.
steps.code:
have h_le_one : nat_mex_list l ≤ 1 := by
    by_contra! h2
    have : 1 ∈ l := hlt 1 h2
    exact h1 this

steps.claim: nat_mex_list l = 1
steps.explanation: Since nat_mex_list l is a natural number such that nat_mex_list l ≠ 0 and nat_mex_list l ≤ 1, linear integer arithmetic determines that it must equal 1.
steps.code: omega

declarations.name: spider_gamma_root_options
declarations.informal: The option list of the root state S(1,2,z) at fuel N+1 (with z = m+1 and N ≥ 3) is the mex of 8 explicit "head" options together with the long block (List.range m).flatMap over cuts of the leg of length z.
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_gamma_root_options (N z m : ℕ) (hz : z = m + 1) (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    spider_gamma (N + 1) CentreStatus.none
        [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)] =
      nat_mex_list
        ([ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.incoming [(2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           spider_gamma N CentreStatus.outgoing [(2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           1 ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           1 ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.outgoing [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           spider_gamma N CentreStatus.none [(1, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           spider_gamma N CentreStatus.none [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           m ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           m ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.outgoing [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free)]] ++
         (List.range m).flatMap (fun i =>
           [(z - (i + 2)) ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.none [(i + 1, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
            (z - (i + 2)) ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.none [(i + 1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free)]]))
declarations.source:
/-- Normal form of the root S(1,2,z) option list at fuel N+1. -/
theorem spider_gamma_root_options (N z m : ℕ) (hz : z = m + 1) (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    spider_gamma (N + 1) CentreStatus.none
        [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)] =
      nat_mex_list
        ([ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.incoming [(2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           spider_gamma N CentreStatus.outgoing [(2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           1 ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           1 ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.outgoing [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           spider_gamma N CentreStatus.none [(1, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           spider_gamma N CentreStatus.none [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (z, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           m ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
           m ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.outgoing [(1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free)]] ++
         (List.range m).flatMap (fun i =>
           [(z - (i + 2)) ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.none [(i + 1, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free)],
            (z - (i + 2)) ^^^ spider_gamma N CentreStatus.none [(i + 1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (1, SpiderLegEnd.free), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free)]])) := by
  have _ := hN
  subst hz
  apply congr_arg nat_mex_list
  change
    List.flatMap _ [((1, SpiderLegEnd.free), 0), ((2, SpiderLegEnd.free), 1), ((m + 1, SpiderLegEnd.free), 2)] = _
  rw [List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil]
  dsimp only
  have hr1 : List.range 1 = [0] := rfl
  have hr2 : List.range 2 = [0, 1] := rfl
  rw [hr1, hr2]
  rw [List.range_succ_eq_map (n := m)]
  simp only [List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil, List.append_nil, List.flatMap_map]
  simp [spider_rho, spider_update_centre]

explanation.summary: The theorem determines the normal form of the option list for the root spider state $S(1,2,z)$ with $z = m + 1$ at fuel $N+1$ by unrolling the definition of `spider_gamma`. The outer loop flatMaps over cuts of the three legs of lengths 1, 2, and $m+1$. Evaluating the cut ranges for the first two legs explicitly and splitting the range of the third leg into a complete cut and partial cuts yields the 8 explicit initial options together with the parameterized family of cuts along the third leg.

steps.claim: Substitute $z = m + 1$ and reduce the equality of Grundy values to equality of their underlying option lists.
steps.explanation: The substitution `hz` replaces $z$ with $m + 1$. Applying congruence (`congr_arg`) with respect to `nat_mex_list` strips the outer minimum excluded value operator, reducing the theorem to showing that the list of options generated by `spider_gamma` equals the right-hand list. (The hypothesis `hN : 3 ≤ N` is recorded on line 17 but not needed for the expansion.)
steps.code:
have _ := hN
  subst hz
  apply congr_arg nat_mex_list

steps.claim: Unfold `spider_gamma` and expand the outer loop over the three legs of the spider.
steps.explanation: By definition, for fuel $N + 1$ and centre status `none`, `spider_gamma` computes options by flatMapping over the indexed legs `[((1, free), 0), ((2, free), 1), ((m + 1, free), 2)]`. Rewriting with `List.flatMap_cons` and `List.flatMap_nil` decomposes this outer loop into the concatenation of three lists of moves—one per leg—and `dsimp only` simplifies pattern matching and index deletions.
steps.code:
change
    List.flatMap _ [((1, SpiderLegEnd.free), 0), ((2, SpiderLegEnd.free), 1), ((m + 1, SpiderLegEnd.free), 2)] = _
  rw [List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil]
  dsimp only

steps.claim: Evaluate the cut position ranges for each leg, splitting the third leg's range into the full cut and partial cuts.
steps.explanation: For the leg of length 1, `List.range 1` evaluates definitionally to `[0]`. For the leg of length 2, `List.range 2` evaluates to `[0, 1]`. For the leg of length $m + 1$, `List.range_succ_eq_map` splits `List.range (m + 1)` into `0` (cutting off the entire leg) followed by `List.map Nat.succ (List.range m)` (partial cuts that leave a stub on the spider).
steps.code:
have hr1 : List.range 1 = [0] := rfl
  have hr2 : List.range 2 = [0, 1] := rfl
  rw [hr1, hr2]
  rw [List.range_succ_eq_map (n := m)]

steps.claim: Unroll the cuts for the first two legs and index partial cuts along the third leg directly over `List.range m`.
steps.explanation: Simplifying with `List.flatMap_cons` and `List.flatMap_nil` unrolls the inner loops over cut positions for the explicit lists `[0]` and `[0, 1]`, and `List.append_nil` removes trailing nil appends. Furthermore, `List.flatMap_map` absorbs `Nat.succ` into the cut function, expressing partial cuts along the third leg directly as a `flatMap` over $i \in \text{List.range } m$.
steps.code: simp only [List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil, List.append_nil, List.flatMap_map]

steps.claim: The evaluated options match the 8 explicit head options and the parameterized cuts along the third leg.
steps.explanation: Simplifying with the definitions of `spider_rho` (the Grundy value of the detached cut segment) and `spider_update_centre` (the updated centre status), along with ground arithmetic, resolves each branch: cuts of length 1 remove the leg entirely and change the centre status to incoming or outgoing, while cuts of length at least 2 retain the centre status and leave a stub of length $j - 1$. The resulting list matches the 8 leading options and the list comprehension along the third leg.
steps.code: simp [spider_rho, spider_update_centre]

glossary.congr_arg: applying a function to equal arguments yields equal results ($a_1 = a_2 \implies f(a_1) = f(a_2)$)
glossary.List.flatMap_cons: flatMapping a function over `x :: xs` equals the function applied to `x` concatenated with the flatMap over `xs`
glossary.List.flatMap_nil: flatMapping any function over the empty list produces the empty list
glossary.List.range_succ_eq_map: the list `List.range (n + 1)` is equal to `0` followed by the elementwise successors of `List.range n`
glossary.List.append_nil: appending the empty list to any list leaves it unchanged
glossary.List.flatMap_map: mapping $f$ over a list and then flatMapping $g$ is equivalent to flatMapping the composition $g \circ f$ directly

caveats: The hypothesis `hN : 3 ≤ N` is stated in the theorem and acknowledged on line 17 (`have _ := hN`), but it is not used; the algebraic equality of option lists holds formally for any fuel $N+1 \ge 1$.
Step 5 relies on the `simp` tactic to evaluate ground arithmetic, boolean conditions, and definition unfoldings (`spider_rho`, `spider_update_centre`) across all cut positions and orientations.

declarations.name: spider_mex_one_two
declarations.informal: The mex of the explicit closed-form option list of S(1,2,z) (8 head values plus the long block, after substituting all closed forms) equals (z+1) % 2, for z ≥ 1.
declarations.source:
lemma spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_zero_of_sum_odd (a b : ℕ) (h : (a + b) % 2 = 1) :
    a ^^^ b ≠ 0 := by
  intro h0
  have hx := Nat.xor_mod_two_eq (m := a) (n := b)
  rw [h0, h] at hx
  exact Nat.zero_ne_one hx

lemma spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_one_of_sum_even (a b : ℕ) (h : (a + b) % 2 = 0) :
    a ^^^ b ≠ 1 := by
  intro h1
  have hx := Nat.xor_mod_two_eq (m := a) (n := b)
  rw [h1, h] at hx
  exact absurd hx (by decide)

/-- Mex of the substituted root option list equals (z+1)%2. -/
theorem spider_mex_one_two (z : ℕ) (hz : 1 ≤ z) :
    nat_mex_list
      ([z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2),
        z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), (z-1) ^^^ 1, (z-1) ^^^ 1] ++
       (List.range (z-1)).flatMap (fun i =>
          [(z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1), (z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1)]))
      = (z+1) % 2 := by
  rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one z with h | h
  · have h0 : 0 ∈ ([z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2),
        z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), (z-1) ^^^ 1, (z-1) ^^^ 1] ++
       (List.range (z-1)).flatMap (fun i =>
          [(z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1), (z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1)]) : List ℕ) := by
      simp [h]
    have h1 : 1 ∉ ([z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2),
        z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), (z-1) ^^^ 1, (z-1) ^^^ 1] ++
       (List.range (z-1)).flatMap (fun i =>
          [(z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1), (z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1)]) : List ℕ) := by
      simp [h]
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · omega
      · intro hh
        exact spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_one_of_sum_even _ _ (by omega) hh.symm
      · intro x hx hh
        have hpar : ((x+1) ^^^ 1) % 2 = (x+2) % 2 := by rw [Nat.xor_mod_two_eq]
        exact spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_one_of_sum_even _ _ (by omega) hh.symm
    rw [nat_mex_list_eq_one _ h0 h1]
    omega
  · have h0 : 0 ∉ ([z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2),
        z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), (z-1) ^^^ 1, (z-1) ^^^ 1] ++
       (List.range (z-1)).flatMap (fun i =>
          [(z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1), (z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1)]) : List ℕ) := by
      simp [h]
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · omega
      · intro hh
        exact spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_zero_of_sum_odd _ _ (by omega) hh.symm
      · intro x hx hh
        have hpar : ((x+1) ^^^ 1) % 2 = (x+2) % 2 := by rw [Nat.xor_mod_two_eq]
        exact spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_zero_of_sum_odd _ _ (by omega) hh.symm
    rw [nat_mex_list_eq_zero _ h0]
    omega

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by case analysis on the parity of z. Since the minimum excluded value (mex) of a list of natural numbers is 1 if 0 is present and 1 is absent, and 0 if 0 is absent, it suffices to test membership of 0 and 1. When z is even, 1 ^^^ 1 = 0 appears in the list while every XOR term combines numbers of the same parity and thus cannot equal 1, making the mex 1. When z is odd, all head terms are nonzero and every XOR term combines numbers of opposite parity and thus cannot equal 0, making the mex 0.

steps.claim: If the sum a + b is odd, then the bitwise XOR a ^^^ b is nonzero.
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that a ^^^ b = 0. By Nat.xor_mod_two_eq, the parity of a ^^^ b matches the parity of a + b. Rewriting with the assumption that a + b is odd and a ^^^ b = 0 yields 0 % 2 = 1 (i.e., 0 = 1), contradicting Nat.zero_ne_one.
steps.code:
intro h0
  have hx := Nat.xor_mod_two_eq (m := a) (n := b)
  rw [h0, h] at hx
  exact Nat.zero_ne_one hx

steps.claim: If the sum a + b is even, then the bitwise XOR a ^^^ b cannot equal 1.
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that a ^^^ b = 1. By Nat.xor_mod_two_eq, the parity of a ^^^ b equals the parity of a + b. Rewriting with a ^^^ b = 1 and (a + b) % 2 = 0 yields 1 % 2 = 0, which is an immediate arithmetic contradiction.
steps.code:
intro h1
  have hx := Nat.xor_mod_two_eq (m := a) (n := b)
  rw [h1, h] at hx
  exact absurd hx (by decide)

steps.claim: The proof reduces to two cases based on whether z is even or odd.
steps.explanation: We split into the cases z % 2 = 0 and z % 2 = 1 using Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one.
steps.code: rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one z with h | h

steps.claim: When z is even, 0 is an element of the option list.
steps.explanation: When z % 2 = 0, the head entry 1 ^^^ (1 - z % 2) simplifies to 1 ^^^ 1 = 0, so 0 is present in the list.

steps.claim: When z is even, 1 is not an element of the option list.
steps.explanation: Simplifying with z % 2 = 0 reduces non-membership of 1 to three conditions: (1) z - 2 ≠ 1, which holds because z ≥ 1 and z is even implies z ≥ 2 and z ≠ 3; (2) (z - 1) ^^^ 1 ≠ 1, which follows from spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_one_of_sum_even because the operands sum to z, which is even; and (3) (z - (x + 2)) ^^^ ((x + 1) ^^^ 1) ≠ 1 for all x < z - 1, which also follows from spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_one_of_sum_even because ((x + 1) ^^^ 1) % 2 = (x + 2) % 2 by Nat.xor_mod_two_eq, making the sum of the two operands congruent modulo 2 to (z - (x + 2)) + (x + 2) = z, which is even.
steps.code:
have h1 : 1 ∉ ([z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2),
        z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), (z-1) ^^^ 1, (z-1) ^^^ 1] ++
       (List.range (z-1)).flatMap (fun i =>
          [(z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1), (z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1)]) : List ℕ) := by
      simp [h]
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · omega
      · intro hh
        exact spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_one_of_sum_even _ _ (by omega) hh.symm
      · intro x hx hh
        have hpar : ((x+1) ^^^ 1) % 2 = (x+2) % 2 := by rw [Nat.xor_mod_two_eq]
        exact spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_one_of_sum_even _ _ (by omega) hh.symm

steps.claim: When z is even, the mex of the option list is (z + 1) % 2.
steps.explanation: Since 0 is in the list and 1 is not, nat_mex_list_eq_one establishes that the mex is 1. Because z is even, (z + 1) % 2 = 1 as well.
steps.code:
rw [nat_mex_list_eq_one _ h0 h1]
    omega

steps.claim: When z is odd, 0 is not an element of the option list.
steps.explanation: Simplifying with z % 2 = 1 reduces non-membership of 0 to three conditions: (1) z ≠ 0, which holds because z ≥ 1; (2) (z - 1) ^^^ 1 ≠ 0, which holds by spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_zero_of_sum_odd because the sum of the operands is z, which is odd; and (3) (z - (x + 2)) ^^^ ((x + 1) ^^^ 1) ≠ 0 for all x < z - 1, which holds by spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_zero_of_sum_odd because ((x + 1) ^^^ 1) % 2 = (x + 2) % 2 by Nat.xor_mod_two_eq, so the sum of the operands has the same parity as z, which is odd.
steps.code:
· have h0 : 0 ∉ ([z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2), 1 ^^^ (1 - z%2),
        z - 2*(1 - z%2), z - 2*(1 - z%2), (z-1) ^^^ 1, (z-1) ^^^ 1] ++
       (List.range (z-1)).flatMap (fun i =>
          [(z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1), (z - (i+2)) ^^^ ((i+1) ^^^ 1)]) : List ℕ) := by
      simp [h]
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
      · omega
      · intro hh
        exact spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_zero_of_sum_odd _ _ (by omega) hh.symm
      · intro x hx hh
        have hpar : ((x+1) ^^^ 1) % 2 = (x+2) % 2 := by rw [Nat.xor_mod_two_eq]
        exact spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_zero_of_sum_odd _ _ (by omega) hh.symm

steps.claim: When z is odd, the mex of the option list is (z + 1) % 2.
steps.explanation: Since 0 is not in the list, nat_mex_list_eq_zero establishes that the mex is 0. Because z is odd, (z + 1) % 2 = 0 as well.
steps.code:
rw [nat_mex_list_eq_zero _ h0]
    omega

glossary.Nat.xor_mod_two_eq: The bitwise XOR of two natural numbers has the same parity (remainder modulo 2) as their sum.
glossary.Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one: Every natural number modulo 2 is equal to either 0 or 1.
glossary.spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_one_of_sum_eve: If the sum of two natural numbers is even, their bitwise XOR is not equal to 1.
glossary.spider_mex_one_two_xor_ne_zero_of_sum_od: If the sum of two natural numbers is odd, their bitwise XOR is not equal to 0.
glossary.nat_mex_list_eq_one: If a list of natural numbers contains 0 and does not contain 1, its minimum excluded value is 1.
glossary.nat_mex_list_eq_zero: If a list of natural numbers does not contain 0, its minimum excluded value is 0.

declarations.name: pell_nfa_is_trim
declarations.informal: The n-state Pell NFA pell_nfa n is trim: every state is reachable from the start state and can reach an accept state.
declarations.statement: theorem pell_nfa_is_trim (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : nfa_is_trim (pell_nfa n)
declarations.source:
/-- The letter of the `p`-th chain step: `2` from the first state, `p % 5` above. -/
def pell_nfa_is_trim_letter (p : ℕ) : Fin 5 := if p = 0 then 2 else ⟨p % 5, Nat.mod_lt p (by norm_num)⟩

/-- A single chain step: from a state of value `p` the letter `pell_nfa_is_trim_letter p` reaches any
state of value `p + 1`. -/
theorem pell_nfa_is_trim_step_succ (n p : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hp : p + 1 < n) :
    ∀ (s q : Fin n), s.val = p → q.val = p + 1 →
      q ∈ (pell_nfa n).step s (pell_nfa_is_trim_letter p) := by
  intro s q hs hq
  simp only [pell_nfa, pell_nfa_is_trim_letter, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
  rw [hs, hq]
  by_cases hp0 : p = 0
  · rw [hp0]
    refine ⟨1, by norm_num, by omega, ?_⟩
    norm_num
  · refine ⟨p, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
    simp only [if_neg hp0]
    simp

/-- From a state of value `p` one reaches any state of value `p + m` by walking the chain. -/
theorem pell_nfa_is_trim_reach_fwd (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : ∀ (m p : ℕ), p + m < n →
    ∀ (s q : Fin n), s.val = p → q.val = p + m →
      ∃ w, q ∈ (pell_nfa n).evalFrom {s} w := by
  intro m
  induction m with
  | zero =>
    intro p hp s q hs hq
    exact ⟨[], by simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff]; exact Fin.ext (by omega)⟩
  | succ m ih =>
    intro p hp s q hs hq
    have hpm : p + m < n := by omega
    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := ih p hpm s ⟨p + m, hpm⟩ hs rfl
    have hstep : q ∈ (pell_nfa n).step ⟨p + m, hpm⟩ (pell_nfa_is_trim_letter (p + m)) := by
      refine pell_nfa_is_trim_step_succ n (p + m) hn (by omega) _ q rfl ?_
      show (↑q : ℕ) = p + m + 1
      omega
    refine ⟨w ++ [pell_nfa_is_trim_letter (p + m)], ?_⟩
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_append, NFA.evalFrom_singleton, NFA.mem_stepSet]
    exact ⟨_, hw, hstep⟩

/-- The n-state Pell NFA pell_nfa n is trim for n ≥ 3. -/
theorem pell_nfa_is_trim (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : nfa_is_trim (pell_nfa n) := by
  intro q
  constructor
  · obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := pell_nfa_is_trim_reach_fwd n hn q.val 0 (by omega) ⟨0, by omega⟩ q rfl (by omega)
    exact ⟨w, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists.mpr ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩, rfl, hw⟩⟩
  · obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := pell_nfa_is_trim_reach_fwd n hn (n - 1 - q.val) q.val (by omega) q
      ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ rfl (by simp; omega)
    exact ⟨w, ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩, by show (n - 1) + 1 = n; omega, hw⟩

explanation.summary: To show that the Pell NFA with n ≥ 3 states is trim, we show that every state q is reachable from the initial state 0 and can reach the unique accept state n - 1. We establish this by constructing a directed path along the linear chain 0 → 1 → ... → n - 1. A helper lemma shows that from any state p < n - 1, a single step along the chain to p + 1 is valid under a designated input letter (letter 2 when p = 0, and p % 5 when p > 0). By induction on the distance m, any state p + m is reachable from state p by walking this chain. Setting p = 0 gives reachability from the start state to q, and setting p = q gives reachability from q to the accept state n - 1.

steps.claim: The stepping letter from state p is well-defined as an element of Fin 5: it is 2 when p = 0, and p % 5 when p > 0.
steps.explanation: When p > 0, the remainder p % 5 is strictly less than 5 by Nat.mod_lt, since 0 < 5 is verified by numerical computation (norm_num).
steps.code:
/-- The letter of the `p`-th chain step: `2` from the first state, `p % 5` above. -/
def pell_nfa_is_trim_letter (p : ℕ) : Fin 5 := if p = 0 then 2 else ⟨p % 5, Nat.mod_lt p (by norm_num)⟩

steps.claim: A single chain step from p to p + 1 reduces to finding an index i that satisfies the Pell NFA transition relation.
steps.explanation: We fix states s and q with values p and p + 1. Unfolding the definition of pell_nfa, pell_nfa_is_trim_letter, and set comprehension membership via Set.mem_ofPred_eq, and substituting the values of s and q, the goal is to find an index i such that 1 ≤ i and i + 2 ≤ n satisfying the transition formula.
steps.code:
theorem pell_nfa_is_trim_step_succ (n p : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (hp : p + 1 < n) :
    ∀ (s q : Fin n), s.val = p → q.val = p + 1 →
      q ∈ (pell_nfa n).step s (pell_nfa_is_trim_letter p) := by
  intro s q hs hq
  simp only [pell_nfa, pell_nfa_is_trim_letter, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]
  rw [hs, hq]

steps.claim: For p = 0, state 0 transitions to state 1 with letter 2.
steps.explanation: We split on whether p = 0. When p = 0, the stepping letter is 2. Choosing index i = 1, the bounds 1 ≤ 1 and 1 + 2 ≤ n hold since n ≥ 3, and numerical evaluation (norm_num) verifies the second clause with (1 + 1) % 5 = 2, transitioning from 0 = i - 1 to 1 = i.
steps.code:
by_cases hp0 : p = 0
  · rw [hp0]
    refine ⟨1, by norm_num, by omega, ?_⟩
    norm_num

steps.claim: For p > 0, state p transitions to state p + 1 with letter p % 5.
steps.explanation: When p ≠ 0, we choose index i = p. Since p ≥ 1 and p + 1 < n, we have 1 ≤ p and p + 2 ≤ n. Simplifying with if_neg hp0 reduces the letter to p % 5 = i % 5, which satisfies the first transition clause from p = i to p + 1 = i + 1.
steps.code:
· refine ⟨p, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
    simp only [if_neg hp0]
    simp

/-- From a state of value `p` one reaches any state of value `p + m` by walking the chain. -/

steps.claim: Any state q of value p + m is reachable from state s of value p; in the base case m = 0, the empty word suffices.
steps.explanation: We induct on m. In the base case m = 0, the values of q and s are both p, so q = s by Fin.ext. Running the empty word [] from {s} keeps the automaton in {s} by NFA.evalFrom_nil and Set.mem_singleton_iff, reaching q.
steps.code:
theorem pell_nfa_is_trim_reach_fwd (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : ∀ (m p : ℕ), p + m < n →
    ∀ (s q : Fin n), s.val = p → q.val = p + m →
      ∃ w, q ∈ (pell_nfa n).evalFrom {s} w := by
  intro m
  induction m with
  | zero =>
    intro p hp s q hs hq
    exact ⟨[], by simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff]; exact Fin.ext (by omega)⟩

steps.claim: In the induction step, extending a path of length m by one chain step reaches state q of value p + m + 1.
steps.explanation: By the induction hypothesis, there is a word w reaching the state with value p + m from s. By pell_nfa_is_trim_step_succ, reading pell_nfa_is_trim_letter (p + m) transitions from value p + m to state q with value p + m + 1. Appending this letter to w and rewriting via NFA.evalFrom_append, NFA.evalFrom_singleton, and NFA.mem_stepSet confirms that q is reached.
steps.code:
| succ m ih =>
    intro p hp s q hs hq
    have hpm : p + m < n := by omega
    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := ih p hpm s ⟨p + m, hpm⟩ hs rfl
    have hstep : q ∈ (pell_nfa n).step ⟨p + m, hpm⟩ (pell_nfa_is_trim_letter (p + m)) := by
      refine pell_nfa_is_trim_step_succ n (p + m) hn (by omega) _ q rfl ?_
      show (↑q : ℕ) = p + m + 1
      omega
    refine ⟨w ++ [pell_nfa_is_trim_letter (p + m)], ?_⟩
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_append, NFA.evalFrom_singleton, NFA.mem_stepSet]
    exact ⟨_, hw, hstep⟩

steps.claim: Every state q in the Pell NFA is reachable from the start state.
steps.explanation: Applying pell_nfa_is_trim_reach_fwd with start value 0 and distance q.val yields a word w reaching q from state 0. Since state 0 is the start state of pell_nfa n, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists.mpr shows that q is reachable from the NFA's start set.
steps.code:
/-- The n-state Pell NFA pell_nfa n is trim for n ≥ 3. -/
theorem pell_nfa_is_trim (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : nfa_is_trim (pell_nfa n) := by
  intro q
  constructor
  · obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := pell_nfa_is_trim_reach_fwd n hn q.val 0 (by omega) ⟨0, by omega⟩ q rfl (by omega)
    exact ⟨w, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists.mpr ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩, rfl, hw⟩⟩

steps.claim: Every state q in the Pell NFA can reach an accept state, completing the proof that the NFA is trim.
steps.explanation: The accept condition in pell_nfa n is val + 1 = n, which corresponds uniquely to state n - 1. Applying pell_nfa_is_trim_reach_fwd from q with distance n - 1 - q.val yields a word w reaching state n - 1 from q. Since (n - 1) + 1 = n, state n - 1 is an accept state, proving that pell_nfa n is trim.
steps.code:
· obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := pell_nfa_is_trim_reach_fwd n hn (n - 1 - q.val) q.val (by omega) q
      ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ rfl (by simp; omega)
    exact ⟨w, ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩, by show (n - 1) + 1 = n; omega, hw⟩

glossary.Nat.mod_lt: For any natural numbers x and y with y > 0, the remainder x % y satisfies x % y < y.
glossary.pell_nfa: The definition of the Pell NFA on n states with alphabet Fin 5, having start state 0, accept state n - 1, and transition relation defined by modular arithmetic conditions.
glossary.pell_nfa_is_trim_letter: The stepping letter for state value p, defined as 2 if p = 0, and p % 5 (in Fin 5) if p > 0.
glossary.Set.mem_ofPred_eq: Membership of an element x in a set defined by a predicate {y | p y} is definitionally equivalent to p x.
glossary.if_neg: If a proposition c is false, then the conditional expression if c then t else e evaluates to e.
glossary.NFA.evalFrom_nil: Evaluating an NFA on the empty word [] from a state set S leaves the set S unchanged.
glossary.Set.mem_singleton_iff: An element a belongs to the singleton set {b} if and only if a = b.
glossary.Fin.ext: Two elements of Fin n are equal if and only if their underlying natural number values are equal.
glossary.pell_nfa_is_trim_step_succ: In the Pell NFA with n ≥ 3 states, if p + 1 < n, then reading letter pell_nfa_is_trim_letter p transitions from any state with value p to any state with value p + 1.
glossary.NFA.evalFrom_append: Evaluating an NFA on a concatenated word x ++ y from state set S equals evaluating on y starting from the set of states reached after reading x.
glossary.NFA.evalFrom_singleton: Evaluating an NFA on a single-letter word [a] from state set S equals the one-step set transition stepSet S a.
glossary.NFA.mem_stepSet: A state s belongs to stepSet S a if and only if s is reachable in one step on letter a from some state t in S.
glossary.pell_nfa_is_trim_reach_fwd: In the Pell NFA with n ≥ 3 states, for any p and m with p + m < n, any state of value p + m is reachable by some word starting from any state of value p.
glossary.NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists.mpr: If a state is reachable on word w from the singleton {t} for some t in S, then it is reachable on word w from the set of states S.

caveats: The stepping letters are chosen differently for the first transition (p = 0, which uses letter 2) versus subsequent transitions (p > 0, which use letter p % 5) to match the two clauses in the definition of the Pell NFA transition relation. Small arithmetic verifications ensuring indices lie within the valid range [1, n-2] and satisfy the modular congruence conditions are handled by omega and norm_num.

declarations.name: pell_nfa_step_table
declarations.informal: In A_n, if q is reachable from p in one step on letter k, then one of the following holds: (i) k ≡ p (mod 5) and q = p or q = p+1; (ii) k ≡ p+1 (mod 5) and q = p or q = p+2; (iii) k ≡ p+2 (mod 5) and q = p+1 or q = p+2. In particular all transitions are nondecreasing in the state index and jump by at most 2, and the letters of residues k ≡ p+3, p+4 (mod 5) are dead at p.
declarations.statement:
theorem pell_nfa_step_table (n : ℕ) {p q : Fin n} {k : Fin 5}
    (h : q ∈ (pell_nfa n).step p k) :
    (k.val = p.val % 5 ∧ (q.val = p.val ∨ q.val = p.val + 1)) ∨
    (k.val = (p.val + 1) % 5 ∧ (q.val = p.val ∨ q.val = p.val + 2)) ∨
    (k.val = (p.val + 2) % 5 ∧ (q.val = p.val + 1 ∨ q.val = p.val + 2))
declarations.source:
/-- Local transition table of `pell_nfa n`: from state ⟨p⟩ only the three letters of residue p, p+1, p+2 (mod 5) are readable, and they act by staying or by jumping one/two places. -/
theorem pell_nfa_step_table (n : ℕ) {p q : Fin n} {k : Fin 5}
    (h : q ∈ (pell_nfa n).step p k) :
    (k.val = p.val % 5 ∧ (q.val = p.val ∨ q.val = p.val + 1)) ∨
    (k.val = (p.val + 1) % 5 ∧ (q.val = p.val ∨ q.val = p.val + 2)) ∨
    (k.val = (p.val + 2) % 5 ∧ (q.val = p.val + 1 ∨ q.val = p.val + 2)) := by
  simp only [pell_nfa] at h
  obtain ⟨i, hi1, hi2, h⟩ := h
  rcases h with h | h
  · obtain ⟨hk, hpq⟩ := h
    rcases hpq with ⟨hp1, hq⟩ | ⟨hp2, hq⟩
    · right; left
      exact ⟨by omega, by rcases hq with hq | hq <;> omega⟩
    · left
      exact ⟨by omega, by rcases hq with hq | hq <;> omega⟩
  · obtain ⟨hk, hpq⟩ := h
    rcases hpq with ⟨hp1, hq1⟩ | ⟨hp2, hq2⟩ | ⟨hp3, hq⟩
    · right; left
      exact ⟨by omega, by omega⟩
    · left
      exact ⟨by omega, by omega⟩
    · right; right
      exact ⟨by omega, by rcases hq with hq | hq <;> omega⟩

explanation.summary: The proof unfolds the definition of `pell_nfa` to extract the internal index $i$ governing the transition from $p$ to $q$ on letter $k$. It then performs a case analysis on the five possible configurations of $(p, q)$ relative to $i$ specified by the automaton. In each case, expressing $i$ in terms of $p$ immediately matches one of the three clauses in the theorem, and integer linear and modular arithmetic (`omega`) verifies the claim.

steps.claim: The transition assumption $q \in \operatorname{step}(p, k)$ unfolds into an existential witness $i$ satisfying $1 \le i \le n - 2$ and one of two main transition conditions.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of the automaton `pell_nfa` in $h$ shows that a transition from state $p$ to state $q$ on letter $k$ is parameterized by an integer index $i$ with $1 \le i$ and $i + 2 \le n$. We unpack $i$, these bounds, and the disjunctive condition on $k, p, q$.
steps.code:
simp only [pell_nfa] at h
  obtain ⟨i, hi1, hi2, h⟩ := h

steps.claim: In the case where $k \equiv i \pmod 5$, the step satisfies either clause (ii) or clause (i) of the theorem.
steps.explanation:
We split on the outer disjunction. Here $k \equiv i \pmod 5$, and there are two possible configurations for $p$:
1. $p = i - 1$ and $q \in \{i - 1, i + 1\}$: Since $1 \le i$, we have $i = p + 1$, which gives $k \equiv p + 1 \pmod 5$ and $q \in \{p, p + 2\}$. This matches clause (ii), so we choose the middle disjunct (`right; left`) and close the arithmetic with `omega`.
2. $p = i$ and $q \in \{i, i + 1\}$: Here $k \equiv p \pmod 5$ and $q \in \{p, p + 1\}$. This matches clause (i), so we choose the first disjunct (`left`) and close with `omega`.
steps.code:
rcases h with h | h
  · obtain ⟨hk, hpq⟩ := h
    rcases hpq with ⟨hp1, hq⟩ | ⟨hp2, hq⟩
    · right; left
      exact ⟨by omega, by rcases hq with hq | hq <;> omega⟩
    · left
      exact ⟨by omega, by rcases hq with hq | hq <;> omega⟩

steps.claim: In the case where $k \equiv i + 1 \pmod 5$, the step satisfies clause (ii), clause (i), or clause (iii) of the theorem.
steps.explanation:
In the second outer branch, $k \equiv i + 1 \pmod 5$. The transition definition provides three subcases:
1. $p = i$ and $q = i$: Then $k \equiv p + 1 \pmod 5$ and $q = p$, matching clause (ii) (`right; left`).
2. $p = i + 1$ and $q = i + 1$: Then $k \equiv p \pmod 5$ and $q = p$, matching clause (i) (`left`).
3. $p = i - 1$ and $q \in \{i, i + 1\}$: Since $i = p + 1$, we obtain $k \equiv p + 2 \pmod 5$ and $q \in \{p + 1, p + 2\}$, matching clause (iii) (`right; right`).
In all three cases, linear and modular arithmetic (`omega`) closes the goals.
steps.code:
· obtain ⟨hk, hpq⟩ := h
    rcases hpq with ⟨hp1, hq1⟩ | ⟨hp2, hq2⟩ | ⟨hp3, hq⟩
    · right; left
      exact ⟨by omega, by omega⟩
    · left
      exact ⟨by omega, by omega⟩
    · right; right
      exact ⟨by omega, by rcases hq with hq | hq <;> omega⟩
