declarations.name: pell_nfa_no_ida
declarations.informal: The Pell automaton A_n does not comply with IDA: there are no distinct states p, q and no word v such that p is reachable from p by v, q from p by v, and q from q by v.
declarations.statement: theorem pell_nfa_no_ida (n : ℕ) : ¬ nfa_complies_ida (pell_nfa n)
declarations.source:
lemma pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_le (n : ℕ) {v : List (Fin 5)} {p q : Fin n}
    (h : q ∈ (pell_nfa n).evalFrom {p} v) : (p : ℕ) ≤ (q : ℕ) := by
  induction v generalizing p with
  | nil =>
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at h
    subst h
    exact le_rfl
  | cons a v ih =>
    rw [NFA.evalFrom_cons, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists] at h
    rcases h with ⟨m, hm, hq⟩
    rw [NFA.stepSet, Set.mem_iUnion] at hm
    rcases hm with ⟨p', hp'⟩
    rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hp'
    rcases hp' with ⟨hp_eq, hm_step⟩
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hp_eq
    subst hp_eq
    have h1 : (p' : ℕ) ≤ (m : ℕ) := by
      have := pell_nfa_step_table n hm_step
      rcases this with ⟨-, h'⟩ | ⟨-, h'⟩ | ⟨-, h'⟩ <;> omega
    have h2 := ih hq
    omega

lemma pell_nfa_no_ida_step_self (n : ℕ) {p : Fin n} {k : Fin 5}
    (h : p ∈ (pell_nfa n).step p k) :
    (k : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) % 5 ∨ (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 := by
  have := pell_nfa_step_table n h
  rcases this with ⟨hk, -⟩ | ⟨hk, -⟩ | ⟨hk, hq⟩
  · left; exact hk
  · right; exact hk
  · rcases hq with h | h <;> omega

lemma pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_cons (n : ℕ) {a : Fin 5} {v : List (Fin 5)} {p : Fin n}
    (h : p ∈ (pell_nfa n).evalFrom {p} (a :: v)) :
    p ∈ (pell_nfa n).step p a ∧ p ∈ (pell_nfa n).evalFrom {p} v := by
  rw [NFA.evalFrom_cons, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists] at h
  rcases h with ⟨m, hm, hq⟩
  rw [NFA.stepSet, Set.mem_iUnion] at hm
  rcases hm with ⟨p', hp'⟩
  rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hp'
  rcases hp' with ⟨hp_eq, hm_step⟩
  simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hp_eq
  subst hp_eq
  have h1 : (p' : ℕ) ≤ (m : ℕ) := by
    have := pell_nfa_step_table n hm_step
    rcases this with ⟨-, h'⟩ | ⟨-, h'⟩ | ⟨-, h'⟩ <;> omega
  have h2 : (m : ℕ) ≤ (p' : ℕ) := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_le n hq
  have h_eq : m = p' := Fin.ext (by omega)
  subst h_eq
  exact ⟨hm_step, hq⟩

lemma pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_letters (n : ℕ) {v : List (Fin 5)} {p : Fin n}
    (h : p ∈ (pell_nfa n).evalFrom {p} v) :
    ∀ k ∈ v, (k : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) % 5 ∨ (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 := by
  induction v with
  | nil => intros k hk; contradiction
  | cons a v ih =>
    intros k hk
    obtain ⟨ha_step, hp_v⟩ := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_cons n h
    rcases List.mem_cons.mp hk with rfl | hk_v
    · exact pell_nfa_no_ida_step_self n ha_step
    · exact ih hp_v k hk_v

lemma pell_nfa_no_ida_step_in_range (n : ℕ) {p s t : Fin n} {k : Fin 5}
    (hs : (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) ∨ (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 1 ∨ (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2)
    (hk : (k : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) % 5 ∨ (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5)
    (h_step : t ∈ (pell_nfa n).step s k) :
    (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) ∨ (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 1 ∨ (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2 := by
  have := pell_nfa_step_table n h_step
  rcases this with ⟨hk', ht⟩ | ⟨hk', ht⟩ | ⟨hk', ht⟩ <;>
    rcases hs with hs | hs | hs <;>
    rcases hk with hk | hk <;>
    rcases ht with ht | ht <;>
    omega

lemma pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_in_range (n : ℕ) {p : Fin n} {v : List (Fin 5)}
    (hv : ∀ k ∈ v, (k : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) % 5 ∨ (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5)
    {s t : Fin n}
    (hs : (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) ∨ (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 1 ∨ (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2)
    (ht : t ∈ (pell_nfa n).evalFrom {s} v) :
    (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) ∨ (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 1 ∨ (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2 := by
  induction v generalizing s with
  | nil =>
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ht
    subst ht
    exact hs
  | cons a v ih =>
    rw [NFA.evalFrom_cons, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists] at ht
    rcases ht with ⟨m, hm, ht⟩
    rw [NFA.stepSet, Set.mem_iUnion] at hm
    rcases hm with ⟨s', hs'⟩
    rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hs'
    rcases hs' with ⟨hs_eq, hm_step⟩
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hs_eq
    subst hs_eq
    have ha : (a : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) % 5 ∨ (a : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 :=
      hv a List.mem_cons_self
    have hm_range := pell_nfa_no_ida_step_in_range n hs ha hm_step
    have hv' : ∀ k ∈ v, (k : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) % 5 ∨ (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 :=
      fun k hk => hv k (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hk)
    exact ih hv' hm_range ht

lemma pell_nfa_no_ida_step_p_plus_1_letter (n : ℕ) {p s t : Fin n} {k : Fin 5}
    (hs : (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) ∨ (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2)
    (hk : (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5)
    (h_step : t ∈ (pell_nfa n).step s k) :
    (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) ∨ (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2 := by
  have := pell_nfa_step_table n h_step
  rcases this with ⟨hk', ht⟩ | ⟨hk', ht⟩ | ⟨hk', ht⟩ <;>
    rcases hs with hs | hs <;>
    rcases ht with ht | ht <;>
    omega

lemma pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_p_plus_1_letters (n : ℕ) {p : Fin n} {v : List (Fin 5)}
    (hv : ∀ k ∈ v, (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5)
    {s t : Fin n}
    (hs : (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) ∨ (s : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2)
    (ht : t ∈ (pell_nfa n).evalFrom {s} v) :
    (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) ∨ (t : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2 := by
  induction v generalizing s with
  | nil =>
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ht
    subst ht
    exact hs
  | cons a v ih =>
    rw [NFA.evalFrom_cons, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists] at ht
    rcases ht with ⟨m, hm, ht⟩
    rw [NFA.stepSet, Set.mem_iUnion] at hm
    rcases hm with ⟨s', hs'⟩
    rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hs'
    rcases hs' with ⟨hs_eq, hm_step⟩
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hs_eq
    subst hs_eq
    have ha : (a : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 :=
      hv a List.mem_cons_self
    have hm_range := pell_nfa_no_ida_step_p_plus_1_letter n hs ha hm_step
    have hv' : ∀ k ∈ v, (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 :=
      fun k hk => hv k (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hk)
    exact ih hv' hm_range ht

/-- A_n does not comply with IDA: no single word v can carry q_p → q_p, q_p → q_q and q_q → q_q with p ≠ q, because letters that keep the state fixed at index p are dead two places to the right. -/
theorem pell_nfa_no_ida (n : ℕ) : ¬ nfa_complies_ida (pell_nfa n) := by
  intro h_ida
  rcases h_ida with ⟨p, q, hpq, v, hp_v, hqp_v, hq_v⟩
  cases v with
  | nil =>
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hqp_v
    exact hpq hqp_v.symm
  | cons a v =>
    have h_le : (p : ℕ) ≤ (q : ℕ) := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_le n hqp_v
    have h_lt : (p : ℕ) < (q : ℕ) := by
      rcases eq_or_lt_of_le h_le with heq | hlt
      · exfalso; exact hpq (Fin.ext heq)
      · exact hlt
    have hv_p := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_letters n hp_v
    have h_range := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_in_range n hv_p (Or.inl rfl) hqp_v
    have h_q_val : (q : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 1 ∨ (q : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2 := by
      rcases h_range with h1 | h2 | h3 <;> omega
    rcases h_q_val with h_plus_1 | h_plus_2
    · have hv_q := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_letters n hq_v
      have hv_all : ∀ k ∈ a :: v, (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 := by
        intro k hk
        have hk_p := hv_p k hk
        have hk_q := hv_q k hk
        omega
      have h_q_res := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_p_plus_1_letters n hv_all (Or.inl rfl) hqp_v
      omega
    · obtain ⟨hp_step, -⟩ := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_cons n hp_v
      obtain ⟨hq_step, -⟩ := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_cons n hq_v
      have h_step_p := pell_nfa_step_table n hp_step
      have h_step_q := pell_nfa_step_table n hq_step
      omega

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by contradiction: assuming an IDA pattern with distinct states p and q and word v such that p loops on v, q loops on v, and v drives p to q, path monotonicity implies p < q. Because self-loops at p restrict all letters of v to {p mod 5, (p+1) mod 5}, the state reached from p cannot exceed p + 2, limiting q to p + 1 or p + 2. If q = p + 1, self-loops at both states force all letters to be (p+1) mod 5, which preserves {p, p+2} and skips p + 1. If q = p + 2, the first letter must fix both p and p + 2, but the modulo 5 letter requirements for self-loops at indices separated by 2 are disjoint.

steps.claim: If state q is reachable from state p along word v, then p ≤ q.
steps.explanation: By induction on v. For the empty word, q = p and reflexivity applies. For a :: v, the path begins with a step p → m on letter a; the transition table pell_nfa_step_table shows that every transition leaves the state invariant or increases it by 1 or 2, so p ≤ m. The induction hypothesis gives m ≤ q, whence p ≤ q by transitivity.
steps.code:
induction v generalizing p with
  | nil =>
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at h
    subst h
    exact le_rfl
  | cons a v ih =>
    rw [NFA.evalFrom_cons, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists] at h
    rcases h with ⟨m, hm, hq⟩
    rw [NFA.stepSet, Set.mem_iUnion] at hm
    rcases hm with ⟨p', hp'⟩
    rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hp'
    rcases hp' with ⟨hp_eq, hm_step⟩
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hp_eq
    subst hp_eq
    have h1 : (p' : ℕ) ≤ (m : ℕ) := by
      have := pell_nfa_step_table n hm_step
      rcases this with ⟨-, h'⟩ | ⟨-, h'⟩ | ⟨-, h'⟩ <;> omega
    have h2 := ih hq
    omega

steps.claim: A self-loop at state p on letter k requires k ≡ p (mod 5) or k ≡ p + 1 (mod 5).
steps.explanation: From pell_nfa_step_table, a transition from p to p on letter k can only arise from the first two cases (where k = p % 5 or k = (p + 1) % 5). The third case requires the target state to be at least p + 1, which contradicts reaching p.
steps.code:
have := pell_nfa_step_table n h
  rcases this with ⟨hk, -⟩ | ⟨hk, -⟩ | ⟨hk, hq⟩
  · left; exact hk
  · right; exact hk
  · rcases hq with h | h <;> omega

steps.claim: If word a :: v loops at state p, the automaton loops at p on letter a and also loops at p on suffix v.
steps.explanation: The first letter a takes p to some state m from which v leads back to p. Since transitions never decrease states, p ≤ m, and by pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_le, m ≤ p. Hence m = p, establishing both p ∈ step p a and p ∈ evalFrom {p} v.
steps.code:
rw [NFA.evalFrom_cons, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists] at h
  rcases h with ⟨m, hm, hq⟩
  rw [NFA.stepSet, Set.mem_iUnion] at hm
  rcases hm with ⟨p', hp'⟩
  rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hp'
  rcases hp' with ⟨hp_eq, hm_step⟩
  simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hp_eq
  subst hp_eq
  have h1 : (p' : ℕ) ≤ (m : ℕ) := by
    have := pell_nfa_step_table n hm_step
    rcases this with ⟨-, h'⟩ | ⟨-, h'⟩ | ⟨-, h'⟩ <;> omega
  have h2 : (m : ℕ) ≤ (p' : ℕ) := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_le n hq
  have h_eq : m = p' := Fin.ext (by omega)
  subst h_eq
  exact ⟨hm_step, hq⟩

steps.claim: Every letter in a word looping at state p is congruent to p or p + 1 modulo 5.
steps.explanation: By induction on v. The base case is vacuously true. For a :: v, the previous lemma shows that p loops on a and on v. The letter a satisfies the congruence by pell_nfa_no_ida_step_self, and all letters in v satisfy it by the induction hypothesis.
steps.code:
induction v with
  | nil => intros k hk; contradiction
  | cons a v ih =>
    intros k hk
    obtain ⟨ha_step, hp_v⟩ := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_cons n h
    rcases List.mem_cons.mp hk with rfl | hk_v
    · exact pell_nfa_no_ida_step_self n ha_step
    · exact ih hp_v k hk_v

steps.claim: Letters fixing p preserve the three-state neighborhood {p, p+1, p+2} in one step.
steps.explanation: Assuming s ∈ {p, p+1, p+2} and k ∈ {p % 5, (p+1) % 5}, case analysis on the transitions given by pell_nfa_step_table shows that any target state t remains in {p, p+1, p+2}, with each case verified by linear arithmetic.
steps.code:
have := pell_nfa_step_table n h_step
  rcases this with ⟨hk', ht⟩ | ⟨hk', ht⟩ | ⟨hk', ht⟩ <;>
    rcases hs with hs | hs | hs <;>
    rcases hk with hk | hk <;>
    rcases ht with ht | ht <;>
    omega

steps.claim: Words consisting of letters fixing p preserve the neighborhood {p, p+1, p+2}.
steps.explanation: By induction on the word v. The empty word preserves the state. For a :: v, the first step lands in {p, p+1, p+2} by pell_nfa_no_ida_step_in_range, and the induction hypothesis applies to the rest of the path.
steps.code:
induction v generalizing s with
  | nil =>
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ht
    subst ht
    exact hs
  | cons a v ih =>
    rw [NFA.evalFrom_cons, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists] at ht
    rcases ht with ⟨m, hm, ht⟩
    rw [NFA.stepSet, Set.mem_iUnion] at hm
    rcases hm with ⟨s', hs'⟩
    rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hs'
    rcases hs' with ⟨hs_eq, hm_step⟩
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hs_eq
    subst hs_eq
    have ha : (a : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) % 5 ∨ (a : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 :=
      hv a List.mem_cons_self
    have hm_range := pell_nfa_no_ida_step_in_range n hs ha hm_step
    have hv' : ∀ k ∈ v, (k : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) % 5 ∨ (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 :=
      fun k hk => hv k (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hk)
    exact ih hv' hm_range ht

steps.claim: A step on letter (p+1) % 5 preserves the two-element set {p, p+2}.
steps.explanation: Assuming s ∈ {p, p+2} and k = (p+1) % 5, pell_nfa_step_table restricts the possible destinations. Linear arithmetic confirms that the intermediate state p + 1 cannot be reached, so t ∈ {p, p+2}.
steps.code:
have := pell_nfa_step_table n h_step
  rcases this with ⟨hk', ht⟩ | ⟨hk', ht⟩ | ⟨hk', ht⟩ <;>
    rcases hs with hs | hs <;>
    rcases ht with ht | ht <;>
    omega

steps.claim: Words consisting entirely of letter (p+1) % 5 preserve {p, p+2}.
steps.explanation: By induction on v, applying pell_nfa_no_ida_step_p_plus_1_letter on each step.
steps.code:
induction v generalizing s with
  | nil =>
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at ht
    subst ht
    exact hs
  | cons a v ih =>
    rw [NFA.evalFrom_cons, NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists] at ht
    rcases ht with ⟨m, hm, ht⟩
    rw [NFA.stepSet, Set.mem_iUnion] at hm
    rcases hm with ⟨s', hs'⟩
    rw [Set.mem_iUnion] at hs'
    rcases hs' with ⟨hs_eq, hm_step⟩
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hs_eq
    subst hs_eq
    have ha : (a : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 :=
      hv a List.mem_cons_self
    have hm_range := pell_nfa_no_ida_step_p_plus_1_letter n hs ha hm_step
    have hv' : ∀ k ∈ v, (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 :=
      fun k hk => hv k (List.mem_cons_of_mem a hk)
    exact ih hv' hm_range ht

steps.claim: Under the IDA hypothesis, the connecting word v cannot be empty.
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that IDA holds, giving distinct states p ≠ q and a word v such that p loops on v, q loops on v, and v takes p to q. If v is nil, evaluation from {p} yields {p}, forcing q = p, which contradicts p ≠ q.
steps.code:
intro h_ida
  rcases h_ida with ⟨p, q, hpq, v, hp_v, hqp_v, hq_v⟩
  cases v with
  | nil =>
    simp only [NFA.evalFrom_nil, Set.mem_singleton_iff] at hqp_v
    exact hpq hqp_v.symm

steps.claim: State q must be either p + 1 or p + 2.
steps.explanation: Because v is non-empty and takes p to q, path monotonicity (pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_le) gives p ≤ q, and since p ≠ q, p < q. Because p loops on v, every letter in v is in {p % 5, (p+1) % 5} (pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_letters), so pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_in_range confines q to {p, p+1, p+2}. Combined with p < q, q must be p + 1 or p + 2.
steps.code:
| cons a v =>
    have h_le : (p : ℕ) ≤ (q : ℕ) := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_le n hqp_v
    have h_lt : (p : ℕ) < (q : ℕ) := by
      rcases eq_or_lt_of_le h_le with heq | hlt
      · exfalso; exact hpq (Fin.ext heq)
      · exact hlt
    have hv_p := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_letters n hp_v
    have h_range := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_in_range n hv_p (Or.inl rfl) hqp_v
    have h_q_val : (q : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 1 ∨ (q : ℕ) = (p : ℕ) + 2 := by
      rcases h_range with h1 | h2 | h3 <;> omega

steps.claim: State q cannot be p + 1.
steps.explanation: If q = p + 1, then because q loops on v, every letter in v must belong to {q % 5, (q+1) % 5} = {(p+1) % 5, (p+2) % 5}. Intersecting this with the requirement from p that every letter belongs to {p % 5, (p+1) % 5} forces every letter of v to be (p+1) % 5. But then pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_p_plus_1_letters shows that any path from p stays in {p, p+2}, so it cannot reach q = p + 1.
steps.code:
rcases h_q_val with h_plus_1 | h_plus_2
    · have hv_q := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_letters n hq_v
      have hv_all : ∀ k ∈ a :: v, (k : ℕ) = ((p : ℕ) + 1) % 5 := by
        intro k hk
        have hk_p := hv_p k hk
        have hk_q := hv_q k hk
        omega
      have h_q_res := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_p_plus_1_letters n hv_all (Or.inl rfl) hqp_v
      omega

steps.claim: State q cannot be p + 2, completing the contradiction.
steps.explanation: If q = p + 2, pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_cons implies that the first letter a of v must satisfy both p ∈ step p a and q ∈ step q a. Consulting pell_nfa_step_table for both transitions yields incompatible constraints modulo 5 on a, which linear integer arithmetic (omega) refutes.
steps.code:
· obtain ⟨hp_step, -⟩ := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_cons n hp_v
      obtain ⟨hq_step, -⟩ := pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_cons n hq_v
      have h_step_p := pell_nfa_step_table n hp_step
      have h_step_q := pell_nfa_step_table n hq_step
      omega

glossary.NFA.evalFrom_nil: Evaluating an NFA from a state set on the empty word yields the state set itself.
glossary.Set.mem_singleton_iff: An element belongs to the singleton {b} if and only if it equals b.
glossary.le_rfl: Any element in a preorder satisfies a ≤ a.
glossary.NFA.evalFrom_cons: Evaluating an NFA on a :: v equals evaluating the one-step successor set on v.
glossary.NFA.mem_evalFrom_iff_exists: A state is reachable from a set S on word x iff it is reachable from some state in S on x.
glossary.NFA.stepSet: The one-step image of a state set is the union of the one-step transitions of its elements.
glossary.Set.mem_iUnion: Membership in an indexed union is equivalent to membership in at least one set of the family.
glossary.pell_nfa_step_table: Every transition p → q on letter k in the Pell NFA falls into one of three explicit cases relating k, p, and q.
glossary.pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_le: Transitions in the Pell NFA never decrease the state index: if q is reachable from p, then p ≤ q.
glossary.Fin.ext: Two elements of Fin n are equal if and only if their underlying natural numbers are equal.
glossary.pell_nfa_no_ida_step_self: A self-loop at state p on letter k requires k ≡ p (mod 5) or k ≡ p + 1 (mod 5).
glossary.pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_cons: If a word a :: v loops at state p, then the automaton loops at p on letter a and on the suffix v.
glossary.List.mem_cons.mp: An element in the list a :: l either equals a or belongs to l.
glossary.List.mem_cons_self: The head element a belongs to the list a :: l.
glossary.List.mem_cons_of_mem: An element belonging to l also belongs to y :: l.
glossary.pell_nfa_no_ida_step_in_range: If s ∈ {p, p+1, p+2} and k ∈ {p mod 5, (p+1) mod 5}, any one-step successor of s on k remains in {p, p+1, p+2}.
glossary.pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_in_range: If every letter in v is in {p mod 5, (p+1) mod 5} and s ∈ {p, p+1, p+2}, any state reachable from s on v is in {p, p+1, p+2}.
glossary.pell_nfa_no_ida_step_p_plus_1_letter: If s ∈ {p, p+2} and k = (p+1) mod 5, any one-step successor of s on k remains in {p, p+2}.
glossary.pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_p_plus_1_letter: If every letter in v is (p+1) mod 5 and s ∈ {p, p+2}, any state reachable from s on v remains in {p, p+2}.
glossary.eq_or_lt_of_le: If a ≤ b in a partial order, then a = b or a < b.
glossary.Or.inl: Proves a disjunction A ∨ B from a proof of A.
glossary.pell_nfa_no_ida_evalFrom_self_letters: Every letter in a word that loops at state p must be congruent to p or p + 1 modulo 5.

caveats: Several case analyses on automaton transitions (notably in pell_nfa_no_ida_step_in_range, pell_nfa_no_ida_step_p_plus_1_letter, and the final step of pell_nfa_no_ida) decompose into dozens of subcases where the resulting arithmetic and modular conditions are discharged by Lean's omega decision procedure.

declarations.name: nat_mex_list_append_comm
declarations.informal: For any two lists of natural numbers l1 and l2, nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2) = nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1).
declarations.statement:
theorem nat_mex_list_append_comm (l1 l2 : List ℕ) :
    nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2) = nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1)
declarations.source:
/-- The mex of the concatenation of two lists does not depend on the order of concatenation. -/
theorem nat_mex_list_append_comm (l1 l2 : List ℕ) :
    nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2) = nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1) := by
  have h1 := nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt (l1 ++ l2)
  have h2 := nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt (l2 ++ l1)
  have h_iff (k : ℕ) : k ∈ l1 ++ l2 ↔ k ∈ l2 ++ l1 := by
    simp [List.mem_append, or_comm]
  rcases lt_trichotomy (nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2)) (nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1)) with hlt | heq | hgt
  · have := h2.2 (nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2)) hlt
    rw [← h_iff] at this
    exact (h1.1 this).elim
  · exact heq
  · have := h1.2 (nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1)) hgt
    rw [h_iff] at this
    exact (h2.1 this).elim

explanation.summary: The proof shows that the minimum excluded value (mex) of a list depends only on the set of elements in the list. Since list concatenation is set-theoretically commutative, l1 ++ l2 and l2 ++ l1 contain exactly the same elements. By trichotomy, if one mex were strictly less than the other, it would have to belong to the other list by the definition of mex and therefore to its own list by element equivalence, contradicting that a mex never belongs to its list. Thus, the two mex values must be equal.

steps.claim: The minimum excluded value of l1 ++ l2 does not belong to l1 ++ l2 while every smaller natural number does, and symmetrically for l2 ++ l1.
steps.explanation: Applying nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt to l1 ++ l2 gives hypothesis h1, and applying it to l2 ++ l1 gives hypothesis h2. Together, these establish the characteristic properties of the mex for each concatenated list.
steps.code:
have h1 := nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt (l1 ++ l2)
  have h2 := nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt (l2 ++ l1)

steps.claim: For any natural number k, k ∈ l1 ++ l2 ↔ k ∈ l2 ++ l1.
steps.explanation: Membership in a concatenated list s ++ t means membership in s or in t (by List.mem_append). Since disjunction is commutative (by or_comm), k ∈ l1 ∨ k ∈ l2 is equivalent to k ∈ l2 ∨ k ∈ l1, so the two concatenations contain exactly the same elements.
steps.code:
have h_iff (k : ℕ) : k ∈ l1 ++ l2 ↔ k ∈ l2 ++ l1 := by
    simp [List.mem_append, or_comm]

steps.claim: It suffices to consider the three trichotomy cases: nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2) < nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1), equality, and nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1) < nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2).
steps.explanation: By trichotomy of the strict linear order on natural numbers (lt_trichotomy), exactly one of these three relations must hold between the two values.
steps.code: rcases lt_trichotomy (nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2)) (nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1)) with hlt | heq | hgt

steps.claim: The strict inequality nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2) < nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1) leads to a contradiction.
steps.explanation: If nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2) were strictly less than nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1), the defining property h2 would force nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2) to be an element of l2 ++ l1. By the equivalence of list membership (h_iff), it would also belong to l1 ++ l2, which directly contradicts h1 (that the mex of a list cannot be an element of that list).
steps.code:
· have := h2.2 (nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2)) hlt
    rw [← h_iff] at this
    exact (h1.1 this).elim

steps.claim: When nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2) = nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1), the theorem holds directly.
steps.explanation: The equality goal is identical to the assumption heq in this branch.
steps.code: · exact heq

steps.claim: The strict inequality nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1) < nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2) leads to a contradiction.
steps.explanation: Symmetrically, if nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1) were strictly less than nat_mex_list (l1 ++ l2), then by h1 it would belong to l1 ++ l2. Using the membership equivalence (h_iff), it would belong to l2 ++ l1, contradicting h2.
steps.code:
· have := h1.2 (nat_mex_list (l2 ++ l1)) hgt
    rw [h_iff] at this
    exact (h2.1 this).elim

glossary.nat_mex_list_not_mem_and_lt: For any list of natural numbers l, the minimum excluded value nat_mex_list l does not belong to l, and every natural number strictly less than nat_mex_list l belongs to l.
glossary.List.mem_append: An element belongs to the concatenation of two lists if and only if it belongs to the first list or to the second list.
glossary.or_comm: Logical disjunction is commutative: a ∨ b is equivalent to b ∨ a.
glossary.lt_trichotomy: For any two elements a and b in a linear order, either a < b, a = b, or b < a.

declarations.name: nfa_run_count_list
declarations.informal: The number of runs of the word w in the NFA M from state p to state q: state sequences of length |w|+1 that start at p, end at q and follow the transitions.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def nfa_run_count_list {α σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] (M : NFA α σ) (w : List α) (p q : σ) : ℕ
declarations.source:
/-- The number of runs of the word w in the NFA M from state p to state q. -/
noncomputable def nfa_run_count_list {α σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] (M : NFA α σ) (w : List α) (p q : σ) : ℕ := {r : Fin (w.length + 1) → σ |
    r 0 = p ∧ r (Fin.last w.length) = q ∧
      ∀ i : Fin w.length, r i.succ ∈ M.step (r i.castSucc) (w.get i)}.ncard

declarations.name: nat_mex_list_eq_of_all_eq_bit
declarations.informal: For any list of natural numbers whose elements all equal a single bit b ∈ {0, 1}, if the list is non-empty, its nat_mex_list is 1 - b.
declarations.statement:
theorem nat_mex_list_eq_of_all_eq_bit {l : List ℕ} (b : ℕ) (hb : b = 0 ∨ b = 1)
    (h_all : ∀ x ∈ l, x = b) (h_nonempty : l ≠ []) :
    nat_mex_list l = 1 - b
declarations.source:
/-- The mex of a non-empty list of natural numbers whose elements all equal a bit b in {0, 1} is 1 - b. -/
theorem nat_mex_list_eq_of_all_eq_bit {l : List ℕ} (b : ℕ) (hb : b = 0 ∨ b = 1)
    (h_all : ∀ x ∈ l, x = b) (h_nonempty : l ≠ []) :
    nat_mex_list l = 1 - b := by
  rcases hb with rfl | rfl
  · rw [Nat.sub_zero]
    apply nat_mex_list_eq_one
    · obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, x ∈ l := List.exists_mem_of_ne_nil l h_nonempty
      have hx0 := h_all x hx
      subst hx0
      exact hx
    · intro h1
      have h10 := h_all 1 h1
      revert h10
      decide
  · rw [Nat.sub_self]
    apply nat_mex_list_eq_zero
    intro h0
    have h01 := h_all 0 h0
    revert h01
    decide

explanation.summary: The proof proceeds by case analysis on whether the bit b is 0 or 1. If b = 0, the non-empty list contains only zeros, so it contains 0 and does not contain 1, making its minimum excluded value (mex) equal to 1 = 1 - 0. If b = 1, the list contains only ones and therefore lacks 0, making its mex equal to 0 = 1 - 1.

steps.claim: Consider separately the cases b = 0 and b = 1.
steps.explanation: The hypothesis hb provides the disjunction b = 0 ∨ b = 1, so we split into two cases.
steps.code: rcases hb with rfl | rfl

steps.claim: In the case b = 0, it suffices to prove that 0 ∈ l and 1 ∉ l.
steps.explanation: Since 1 - 0 = 1 by Nat.sub_zero, the goal simplifies to nat_mex_list l = 1. By nat_mex_list_eq_one, this equality holds if 0 is an element of l and 1 is not.
steps.code:
· rw [Nat.sub_zero]
    apply nat_mex_list_eq_one

steps.explanation: Because l is non-empty, List.exists_mem_of_ne_nil guarantees an element x ∈ l. Since every element of l equals 0, we have x = 0, and hence 0 ∈ l.
steps.code:
· obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ : ∃ x, x ∈ l := List.exists_mem_of_ne_nil l h_nonempty
      have hx0 := h_all x hx
      subst hx0
      exact hx

steps.explanation: Assuming for contradiction that 1 ∈ l, the assumption that all elements are 0 implies 1 = 0, which is false by direct evaluation.
steps.code:
· intro h1
      have h10 := h_all 1 h1
      revert h10
      decide

steps.claim: In the case b = 1, it suffices to prove that 0 ∉ l.
steps.explanation: Since 1 - 1 = 0 by Nat.sub_self, the goal becomes nat_mex_list l = 0. By nat_mex_list_eq_zero, this follows once we show that 0 is not in l.
steps.code:
· rw [Nat.sub_self]
    apply nat_mex_list_eq_zero

steps.explanation: Assuming for contradiction that 0 ∈ l, the assumption that all elements of l are 1 implies 0 = 1, which is false by direct evaluation.
steps.code:
intro h0
    have h01 := h_all 0 h0
    revert h01
    decide

glossary.Nat.sub_zero: Subtracting zero from any natural number leaves it unchanged: n - 0 = n.
glossary.nat_mex_list_eq_one: If a list of natural numbers contains 0 and does not contain 1, its minimum excluded value (mex) is 1.
glossary.List.exists_mem_of_ne_nil: Any non-empty list contains at least one element.
glossary.Nat.sub_self: Subtracting any natural number from itself yields zero: n - n = 0.
glossary.nat_mex_list_eq_zero: If a list of natural numbers does not contain 0, its minimum excluded value (mex) is 0.

declarations.name: pell_word_prefix
declarations.informal: The prefix v_j of u_n consisting of its first j two-letter blocks, v_j = c_1c_2 c_2c_3 … c_jc_(j+1), built by appending one block at a time; v_0 = [] and v_(j+1) = v_j ++ [c_(j+1), c_(j+2)].
declarations.statement: def pell_word_prefix : ℕ → List (Fin 5)
declarations.source:
/-- The prefix of pell_word n consisting of its first j two-letter blocks. -/
def pell_word_prefix : ℕ → List (Fin 5)
  | 0 => []
  | i + 1 => pell_word_prefix i ++
      [⟨(i + 1) % 5, Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)⟩, ⟨(i + 2) % 5, Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)⟩]

declarations.name: spider_gamma_swap_two
declarations.informal: The Grundy value of a two-legged spider state is invariant under swapping the two legs in the list.
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_gamma_swap_two (fuel : ℕ) (s : CentreStatus) (A B : ℕ × SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_gamma fuel s [A, B] = spider_gamma fuel s [B, A]
declarations.source:
/-- The Grundy value of a two-legged spider state is invariant under swapping the two legs in the list. -/
theorem spider_gamma_swap_two (fuel : ℕ) (s : CentreStatus) (A B : ℕ × SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_gamma fuel s [A, B] = spider_gamma fuel s [B, A] := by
  cases fuel with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ f =>
    cases s with
    | free =>
      dsimp [spider_gamma]
      rw [Nat.zero_xor, Nat.zero_xor, Nat.xor_comm]
    | _ =>
      dsimp [spider_gamma]
      simp only [List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil, List.append_nil]
      dsimp [List.eraseIdx]
      rw [nat_mex_list_append_comm]

explanation.summary: The Grundy value of a two-legged spider state is shown to be symmetric in the two legs by case analysis on the recursion fuel and the centre status. When the centre is free, the Grundy value is the XOR sum of the two legs' individual values, which is symmetric by the commutativity of bitwise XOR. When the centre is not free, the Grundy value is the mex of all moves available from either leg; swapping the legs simply swaps the two blocks of moves in the concatenated options list, leaving the overall mex unchanged.

steps.claim: The Grundy value is invariant under swapping the two legs when fuel = 0.
steps.explanation: When the recursion fuel is 0, `spider_gamma` evaluates to 0 by definition regardless of the list of legs, so both sides are definitionally equal to 0 and the goal is solved by reflexivity (`rfl`).
steps.code:
cases fuel with
  | zero => rfl

steps.claim: When fuel = f + 1 and the centre status is free, swapping the two legs does not change the Grundy value.
steps.explanation: For a free centre, `spider_gamma` computes the XOR sum of `spider_rho_star` over the leg list, initialized with 0. Simplifying both sides gives 0 ^^^ ρ*(A) ^^^ ρ*(B) on the left and 0 ^^^ ρ*(B) ^^^ ρ*(A) on the right. Removing the leading zero with `Nat.zero_xor` reduces this to ρ*(A) ^^^ ρ*(B) = ρ*(B) ^^^ ρ*(A), which holds by commutativity of XOR (`Nat.xor_comm`).
steps.code:
| succ f =>
    cases s with
    | free =>
      dsimp [spider_gamma]
      rw [Nat.zero_xor, Nat.zero_xor, Nat.xor_comm]

steps.claim: When fuel = f + 1 and the centre status is not free, swapping the two legs does not change the Grundy value.
steps.explanation: When the centre status is not free (covering `none`, `incoming`, and `outgoing`), `spider_gamma` computes the mex (`nat_mex_list`) of the combined moves available from each leg. Expanding the flat-map over the list of legs and evaluating index erasure splits the options for [A, B] into the moves on A concatenated with the moves on B, whereas for [B, A] they appear as moves on B concatenated with moves on A. Commuting the two sublists under `nat_mex_list` via `nat_mex_list_append_comm` establishes equality.
steps.code:
| _ =>
      dsimp [spider_gamma]
      simp only [List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil, List.append_nil]
      dsimp [List.eraseIdx]
      rw [nat_mex_list_append_comm]

glossary.Nat.zero_xor: Bitwise exclusive-or of zero with any natural number x yields x (0 ^^^ x = x).
glossary.Nat.xor_comm: Bitwise exclusive-or on natural numbers is commutative (x ^^^ y = y ^^^ x).
glossary.List.flatMap_cons: Flat-mapping a function over a non-empty list x :: xs equals the result of the function on x concatenated with the flat-map over the tail xs.
glossary.List.flatMap_nil: Flat-mapping any function over the empty list yields the empty list.
glossary.List.append_nil: Appending the empty list to any list leaves the list unchanged (as ++ [] = as).
glossary.nat_mex_list_append_comm: The minimum excluded value (mex) of the concatenation of two lists of natural numbers is independent of the concatenation order: mex(l1 ++ l2) = mex(l2 ++ l1).

caveats: The `fuel` parameter is an explicit recursion bound required for Lean's termination checker when defining `spider_gamma`; it has no game-theoretic meaning beyond ensuring termination.

declarations.name: spider_blocked_incoming_one_inward_options_nonempty
declarations.informal: The options list generated by [(1, inward), (r, φ)] at incoming centre is non-empty.
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_blocked_incoming_one_inward_options_nonempty (r : ℕ) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) :
    ([(1, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (r, φ)].zipIdx.flatMap (fun ⟨⟨h, phi⟩, idx⟩ =>
      let rest := [(1, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (r, φ)].eraseIdx idx
      (List.range h).flatMap (fun j_zero =>
        let j := j_zero + 1
        [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap (fun delta =>
          if j == h ∧ phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ phi then none
          else
            let d := spider_rho (h - j) delta phi
            if j ≥ 2 then
              let new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: rest
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) CentreStatus.incoming new_L)
            else
              let new_s := spider_update_centre CentreStatus.incoming delta
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) new_s rest)
        )
      )
    )) ≠ []
declarations.source:
/-- The options list generated by [(1, inward), (r, φ)] at incoming centre is non-empty. -/
theorem spider_blocked_incoming_one_inward_options_nonempty (r : ℕ) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) :
    ([(1, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (r, φ)].zipIdx.flatMap (fun ⟨⟨h, phi⟩, idx⟩ =>
      let rest := [(1, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (r, φ)].eraseIdx idx
      (List.range h).flatMap (fun j_zero =>
        let j := j_zero + 1
        [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap (fun delta =>
          if j == h ∧ phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ phi then none
          else
            let d := spider_rho (h - j) delta phi
            if j ≥ 2 then
              let new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: rest
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) CentreStatus.incoming new_L)
            else
              let new_s := spider_update_centre CentreStatus.incoming delta
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) new_s rest)
        )
      )
    )) ≠ [] := by
  simp

explanation.summary: The theorem states that the list of options generated from the configuration [(1, inward), (r, φ)] with incoming centre status is non-empty. The proof proceeds by direct simplification: evaluating the transition rules on the first leg (1, inward) with cut length j = 1 and direction inward yields a valid option, because the blocking condition requires delta ≠ phi. Since the first leg produces at least one transition, the resulting list starts with a cons cell and is therefore non-empty, which the `simp` tactic verifies by computation.

steps.claim: The list of options is non-empty.
steps.explanation: The simplifier `simp` evaluates the list operations (`flatMap`, `range`, and `filterMap`) on the concrete first element of the list, `(1, SpiderLegEnd.inward)`. For this leg of length 1, the only index in `List.range 1` is `j_zero = 0`, giving `j = 1`. Testing direction `delta = SpiderLegEnd.inward` avoids the blocking condition because `delta == phi` (both are `inward`), yielding a valid transition `some (...)`. This places a concrete element at the head of the resulting list (`_ :: _`), which definitionally cannot equal the empty list `[]`.
steps.code: simp

caveats: The entire proof is executed in a single step by `simp`, which evaluates the list operations for the first leg of length 1, finding an explicit move and constructing a non-empty list without requiring any user-guided case splits or lemmas.

declarations.name: spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_one
declarations.informal: For the configuration κ₂ = (in;{(1,outward)}), the blocked family V^φ_κ₂(1) equals 1 ^^^ 1 for both φ ≠ free.
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_one (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) :
    spider_gamma 3 CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (1, φ)] = 1 ^^^ 1
declarations.source:
/-- The base case r = 1 for the configuration κ₂ = (in;{(1,outward)}) evaluates to 1 ^^^ 1. -/
theorem spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_one (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) :
    spider_gamma 3 CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (1, φ)] = 1 ^^^ 1 := by
  rcases φ with _ | _ | _
  · exact absurd rfl hφ
  · decide
  · decide

explanation.summary: The theorem evaluates the Sprague-Grundy function `spider_gamma` for a two-legged spider graph configuration with incoming centre status and leg parameters (1, outward) and (1, φ), showing it equals the nim-sum 1 ^^^ 1. A case analysis on the leg-end status φ yields three possibilities. The case φ = free is eliminated immediately as it contradicts the hypothesis φ ≠ free, while the remaining cases φ = inward and φ = outward are closed terms verified by direct computational evaluation.

steps.claim: It suffices to verify the equality for each of the three possible values of φ: free, inward, and outward.
steps.explanation: The leg-end status type `SpiderLegEnd` is an inductive type with three constructors (`free`, `inward`, and `outward`). We split the proof into these three cases.
steps.code: rcases φ with _ | _ | _

steps.claim: The case φ = free is ruled out by contradiction.
steps.explanation: When φ is `free`, the assumption hφ asserts that `free ≠ free`. Since equality is reflexive (`rfl`), this is an immediate contradiction (`absurd`).
steps.code: · exact absurd rfl hφ

steps.claim: The identity holds when φ = inward.
steps.explanation: When φ is `inward`, both sides of the equation are closed terms with no free variables. The `decide` tactic computes the Sprague-Grundy value `spider_gamma` on the configuration (incoming; [(1, outward), (1, inward)]) and confirms that it equals the nim-sum 1 ^^^ 1 = 0.
steps.code: · decide

steps.claim: The identity holds when φ = outward.
steps.explanation: Similarly, when φ is `outward`, the configuration contains only concrete parameters. The `decide` tactic computes `spider_gamma` on (incoming; [(1, outward), (1, outward)]) and verifies that it evaluates to 1 ^^^ 1 = 0.
steps.code: · decide

glossary.absurd: From a proposition A and its negation ¬A, any conclusion B follows (principle of explosion).
glossary.rfl: Equality is reflexive: for every term a, a = a.

caveats: The `decide` tactic evaluates the recursive game-theoretic definition of `spider_gamma` (computing the list of move options and their minimal excluded value) on concrete inputs via computational reduction, taking the place of manual case analysis over all transitions.

declarations.name: picking_turn
declarations.informal: One turn of a picking-sequence mechanism: the active agent i receives the first good of its reported ranking l (best first) that is not yet allocated; the state is the partial allocation together with the set of allocated goods.
declarations.statement:
def picking_turn {N G : Type*} [DecidableEq N] [DecidableEq G] (l : List G) (i : N)
    (st : (N → Finset G) × Finset G) : (N → Finset G) × Finset G
declarations.source:
/-- One turn of a picking-sequence mechanism: the active agent `i` receives the first good of its reported ranking `l` (best first) not yet allocated. The state is the partial allocation and the set of goods already allocated. -/
def picking_turn {N G : Type*} [DecidableEq N] [DecidableEq G] (l : List G) (i : N)
    (st : (N → Finset G) × Finset G) : (N → Finset G) × Finset G :=
  match l.find? (fun g => decide (g ∉ st.2)) with
  | some g => (Function.update st.1 i (insert g (st.1 i)), insert g st.2)
  | none => st
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.23040 (On the Convergence of Iterated Round Robin), Sec. 2; also arXiv:2610.23686 Sec. 2

declarations.name: picking_sequence_outcome
declarations.informal: The allocation returned by the picking-sequence mechanism PS_π: agents act in the order seq, and at each turn the active agent takes its highest-ranked remaining good, where rank i k is the good agent i reports in position k (position 0 is its top good).
declarations.statement:
def picking_sequence_outcome {N G : Type*} [DecidableEq N] [DecidableEq G]
    {m : ℕ} (seq : List N) (rank : N → Fin m ≃ G) : N → Finset G
declarations.source:
/-- The allocation of the picking-sequence mechanism `PS_π`: agents act in the order `seq`, and at each turn the active agent takes its highest-ranked available good; `rank i k` is the good agent `i` reports in position `k` (position `0` best). -/
def picking_sequence_outcome {N G : Type*} [DecidableEq N] [DecidableEq G]
    {m : ℕ} (seq : List N) (rank : N → Fin m ≃ G) : N → Finset G :=
  (seq.foldl (fun st i => picking_turn (List.ofFn (rank i)) i st) (fun _ => ∅, ∅)).1
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.23040 (On the Convergence of Iterated Round Robin), Sec. 2; also arXiv:2610.23686 Sec. 2

declarations.name: round_robin_sequence
declarations.informal: The Round-Robin picking sequence (1, 2, ..., n, 1, 2, ...) of length m, with agents numbered 0, ..., n-1.
declarations.statement: def round_robin_sequence (n m : ℕ) [NeZero n] : List (Fin n)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.23040 (On the Convergence of Iterated Round Robin), Sec. 2; also arXiv:2610.23686 Sec. 2

declarations.name: is_picking_sequence_pne
declarations.informal: A profile of reported strict rankings is a pure Nash equilibrium of the picking-sequence mechanism if no agent can obtain a bundle of strictly higher true value by unilaterally changing its reported ranking.
declarations.source:
/-- A report profile is a pure Nash equilibrium of the picking-sequence mechanism if no agent can obtain a bundle of strictly higher true value `v` by unilaterally changing its reported strict ranking. -/
def is_picking_sequence_pne {N G : Type*} [DecidableEq N] [DecidableEq G] {m : ℕ}
    (v : SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.Valuation N G) (seq : List N)
    (rank : N → Fin m ≃ G) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : N) (r : Fin m ≃ G),
    v.val i (picking_sequence_outcome seq (Function.update rank i r) i) ≤
      v.val i (picking_sequence_outcome seq rank i)
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.23686 (Revisiting the Fairness of Pure Nash Equilibria of Round-Robin), Definition 3; arXiv:2610.23040 Definition 2.3

declarations.name: spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq
declarations.informal: For r ≥ 2, the raw options list generated by [(1, outward), (r, φ)] at fuel r + 2 with centre status incoming unfolds to the explicit list of head options plus flatMap over range (r - 2) and the final cut, under the induction hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free)
    (ih : ∀ r' < r, 1 ≤ r' → ∀ φ' ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free,
      spider_gamma (r' + 2) CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r', φ')] = r' ^^^ 1) :
    ([(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r, φ)].zipIdx.flatMap (fun ⟨⟨h, phi⟩, idx⟩ =>
      let rest := [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r, φ)].eraseIdx idx
      (List.range h).flatMap (fun j_zero =>
        let j := j_zero + 1
        [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap (fun delta =>
          if j == h ∧ phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ phi then none
          else
            let d := spider_rho (h - j) delta phi
            if j ≥ 2 then
              let new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: rest
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) CentreStatus.incoming new_L)
            else
              let new_s := spider_update_centre CentreStatus.incoming delta
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) new_s rest)
        )
      )
    )) =
    ([r, spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ 1, spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ 1] ++
     (List.range (r - 2)).flatMap (fun idx =>
       let i := idx + 1
       [spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1),
        spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1)]) ++
     [spider_rho 0 φ φ ^^^ ((r - 1) ^^^ 1)])
declarations.source:
def spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1 (r : ℕ) (φ : SpiderLegEnd)
    (j_zero : ℕ) : List ℕ :=
  let j := j_zero + 1
  [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap (fun delta =>
    if j == r ∧ φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ φ then none
    else
      let d := spider_rho (r - j) delta φ
      if j ≥ 2 then
        let new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)]
        some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) CentreStatus.incoming new_L)
      else
        let new_s := spider_update_centre CentreStatus.incoming delta
        some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) new_s [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)]))

def spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0 (r : ℕ) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) : List ℕ :=
  (List.range 1).flatMap (fun j_zero =>
    let j := j_zero + 1
    [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap (fun delta =>
      if j == 1 ∧ SpiderLegEnd.outward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ SpiderLegEnd.outward then none
      else
        let d := spider_rho (1 - j) delta SpiderLegEnd.outward
        if j ≥ 2 then
          let new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: [(r, φ)]
          some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) CentreStatus.incoming new_L)
        else
          let new_s := spider_update_centre CentreStatus.incoming delta
          some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) new_s [(r, φ)])))

lemma spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_split
    (r : ℕ) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) :
    ([(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r, φ)].zipIdx.flatMap (fun ⟨⟨h, phi⟩, idx⟩ =>
      let rest := [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r, φ)].eraseIdx idx
      (List.range h).flatMap (fun j_zero =>
        let j := j_zero + 1
        [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap (fun delta =>
          if j == h ∧ phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ phi then none
          else
            let d := spider_rho (h - j) delta phi
            if j ≥ 2 then
              let new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: rest
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) CentreStatus.incoming new_L)
            else
              let new_s := spider_update_centre CentreStatus.incoming delta
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) new_s rest)
        )
      )
    )) =
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0 r φ ++
      (List.range r).flatMap (spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1 r φ) := by
  rw [show ([(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r, φ)] : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)).zipIdx
      = [((1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), 0), ((r, φ), 1)] from by simp [List.zipIdx]]
  simp only [List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil, List.append_nil,
    List.eraseIdx_cons_zero, List.eraseIdx_cons_succ]
  rfl

lemma spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_range_succ_two (n : ℕ) :
    List.range (n+2) = 0 :: (List.map (·+1) (List.range n) ++ [n+1]) := by
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [show k + 1 + 2 = (k + 2) + 1 by ring, List.range_succ, ih]
    rw [show k + 1 + 1 = k + 2 by ring]
    rw [List.range_succ (n:=k), List.map_append]
    simp [List.cons_append, List.append_assoc]

lemma spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_range_split (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) :
    List.range r = 0 :: (List.map (·+1) (List.range (r-2)) ++ [r-1]) := by
  conv => lhs; rw [show r = (r-2)+2 by omega]
  rw [spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_range_succ_two]
  rw [show r - 2 + 1 = r - 1 by omega]

lemma spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0_head (r : ℕ) (φ : SpiderLegEnd)
    (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) :
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0 r φ = [r] := by
  have hg : spider_gamma (r + 1) CentreStatus.free [(r, φ)] = r := by
    rcases φ with _ | _ | _
    · exact absurd rfl hφ
    · simp only [spider_gamma]; simp [spider_rho_star]
    · simp only [spider_gamma]; simp [spider_rho_star]
  unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0
  simp only [List.range_one, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil, List.filterMap_cons,
    List.filterMap_nil, List.append_nil]
  simp only [spider_rho, spider_update_centre]
  rw [hg]
  simp

lemma spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_zero (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (φ : SpiderLegEnd) :
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1 r φ 0 =
      [spider_rho (r-1) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ 1,
       spider_rho (r-1) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ 1] := by
  have h1r : (1 == r) = false := by
    rw [Bool.eq_false_iff]; simp [beq_iff_eq]; omega
  have h1g : ¬ (1 ≥ 2) := by omega
  unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1
  simp only [Nat.zero_add, h1r, Bool.false_eq_true, false_and, if_false, h1g, if_false]
  simp only [List.filterMap_cons, List.filterMap_nil, spider_update_centre]
  rw [show spider_gamma (r+1) CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)] = 1 from by
      simp only [spider_gamma]; simp [spider_rho]]
  rw [show spider_gamma (r+1) CentreStatus.free [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)] = 1 from by
      simp only [spider_gamma]; simp [spider_rho_star]]

lemma spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_mid (r : ℕ) (φ : SpiderLegEnd)
    (ih : ∀ r' < r, 1 ≤ r' → ∀ φ' ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free,
      spider_gamma (r' + 2) CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r', φ')] = r' ^^^ 1)
    (idx : ℕ) (hidx : idx < r - 2) :
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1 r φ (idx+1) =
      [spider_rho (r - 1 - (idx+1)) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ ((idx+1) ^^^ 1),
       spider_rho (r - 1 - (idx+1)) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ ((idx+1) ^^^ 1)] := by
  have hmid : ∀ (j : ℕ) (δ : SpiderLegEnd), δ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free → 2 ≤ j → j ≤ r →
      spider_gamma (r+1) CentreStatus.incoming [(j-1, δ), (1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)] = (j-1) ^^^ 1 := by
    intro j δ hδ h2 hjr
    have hsum : ((([(j-1, δ), (1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)]).map Prod.fst).sum) + 1 = j + 1 := by
      simp; omega
    rw [spider_gamma_fuel_independent (r+1) CentreStatus.incoming _ (by omega)]
    rw [hsum]
    rw [spider_gamma_swap_two]
    have := ih (j-1) (by omega) (by omega) δ hδ
    rw [show (j-1)+2 = j+1 by omega] at this
    exact this
  unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1
  rw [show idx + 1 + 1 = idx + 2 by omega]
  have hjr : (idx + 2 == r) = false := by
    rw [Bool.eq_false_iff]; simp [beq_iff_eq]; omega
  have hj2 : 2 ≤ idx + 2 := by omega
  simp only [hjr, Bool.false_eq_true, false_and, if_false, hj2, if_pos]
  simp only [List.filterMap_cons, List.filterMap_nil]
  rw [show r - (idx + 2) = r - 1 - (idx + 1) by omega]
  rw [hmid (idx+2) SpiderLegEnd.inward (by decide) hj2 (by omega)]
  rw [hmid (idx+2) SpiderLegEnd.outward (by decide) hj2 (by omega)]
  simp only [show idx + 2 - 1 = idx + 1 by omega]

lemma spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_last (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free)
    (ih : ∀ r' < r, 1 ≤ r' → ∀ φ' ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free,
      spider_gamma (r' + 2) CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r', φ')] = r' ^^^ 1) :
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1 r φ (r-1) =
      [spider_rho 0 φ φ ^^^ ((r-1)^^^1)] := by
  have hg : spider_gamma (r+1) CentreStatus.incoming [(r-1,φ),(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)] =
      (r-1)^^^1 := by
    rw [spider_gamma_swap_two]
    have := ih (r-1) (by omega) (by omega) φ hφ
    rw [show (r-1)+2 = r+1 by omega] at this
    exact this
  rcases φ with _ | _ | _
  · exact absurd rfl hφ
  · unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1
    rw [show r - 1 + 1 = r by omega]
    simp only [beq_self_eq_true, true_and, List.filterMap_cons, List.filterMap_nil,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.inward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) = True from by decide,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.inward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.inward) = False from by decide,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.outward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.inward) = True from by decide,
      and_true, if_false, if_true, hr, spider_rho]
    rw [show r - r = 0 by omega, hg]
  · unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1
    rw [show r - 1 + 1 = r by omega]
    simp only [beq_self_eq_true, true_and, List.filterMap_cons, List.filterMap_nil,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.outward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) = True from by decide,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.inward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.outward) = True from by decide,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.outward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.outward) = False from by decide,
      and_true, if_false, if_true, hr, spider_rho]
    rw [show r - r = 0 by omega, hg]

lemma spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_mid_all (r : ℕ) (φ : SpiderLegEnd)
    (ih : ∀ r' < r, 1 ≤ r' → ∀ φ' ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free,
      spider_gamma (r' + 2) CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r', φ')] = r' ^^^ 1) :
    (List.map (·+1) (List.range (r-2))).flatMap
        (spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1 r φ) =
      (List.range (r - 2)).flatMap (fun idx =>
        let i := idx + 1
        [spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1),
         spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1)]) := by
  rw [List.flatMap_map]
  apply List.flatMap_congr
  intro idx hidx
  rw [List.mem_range] at hidx
  exact spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_mid r φ ih idx hidx

lemma spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_main (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free)
    (ih : ∀ r' < r, 1 ≤ r' → ∀ φ' ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free,
      spider_gamma (r' + 2) CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r', φ')] = r' ^^^ 1) :
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0 r φ ++
        (List.range r).flatMap (spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1 r φ) =
      ([r, spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ 1,
          spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ 1] ++
       (List.range (r - 2)).flatMap (fun idx =>
         let i := idx + 1
         [spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1),
          spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1)]) ++
       [spider_rho 0 φ φ ^^^ ((r - 1) ^^^ 1)]) := by
  rw [spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0_head r φ hφ,
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_range_split r hr, List.flatMap_cons,
    List.flatMap_append, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil,
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_zero r hr φ,
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_mid_all r φ ih,
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_last r hr φ hφ ih]
  simp only [List.append_nil]
  rfl

/-- For r ≥ 2, the options list generated by [(1, outward), (r, φ)] at fuel r + 2 with centre status incoming simplifies under the induction hypothesis to the explicit list of head options, intermediate cuts, and the final cut. -/
theorem spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free)
    (ih : ∀ r' < r, 1 ≤ r' → ∀ φ' ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free,
      spider_gamma (r' + 2) CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r', φ')] = r' ^^^ 1) :
    ([(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r, φ)].zipIdx.flatMap (fun ⟨⟨h, phi⟩, idx⟩ =>
      let rest := [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r, φ)].eraseIdx idx
      (List.range h).flatMap (fun j_zero =>
        let j := j_zero + 1
        [SpiderLegEnd.inward, SpiderLegEnd.outward].filterMap (fun delta =>
          if j == h ∧ phi ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free ∧ delta ≠ phi then none
          else
            let d := spider_rho (h - j) delta phi
            if j ≥ 2 then
              let new_L := (j - 1, delta) :: rest
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) CentreStatus.incoming new_L)
            else
              let new_s := spider_update_centre CentreStatus.incoming delta
              some (d ^^^ spider_gamma (r + 1) new_s rest)
        )
      )
    )) =
    ([r, spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ 1, spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ 1] ++
     (List.range (r - 2)).flatMap (fun idx =>
       let i := idx + 1
       [spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1),
        spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1)]) ++
     [spider_rho 0 φ φ ^^^ ((r - 1) ^^^ 1)]) := by
  rw [spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_split r φ]
  exact spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_main r hr φ hφ ih

explanation.summary: To compute the game options for the two-leg position [(1, outward), (r, φ)] with incoming centre status, the proof decomposes the list of available moves into cuts on leg 0 and cuts on leg 1. Cutting leg 0 leaves only leg 1 with a free centre, evaluating to the singleton option [r]. The cuts on leg 1 are partitioned into the initial cut of length 1, intermediate cuts of length 2 ≤ j < r, and the final cut of length r. For each cut with j ≥ 2, the remaining spider has two legs and incoming centre, so swapping the legs and applying the induction hypothesis computes its nim-value as (j - 1) ^^^ 1. Concatenating these pieces yields the simplified explicit list of all option nim-values.

steps.claim: The raw options list for [(1, outward), (r, φ)] splits into moves on leg 0 and moves on leg 1.
steps.explanation: The two-element list of legs has indices 0 and 1. Expanding List.zipIdx, unfolding the flatMap over this two-element list, and simplifying index erasure decomposes the options into cuts on the first leg (captured by spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0) appended to cuts on the second leg (captured by spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1 mapped over List.range r).
steps.code:
rw [show ([(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (r, φ)] : List (ℕ × SpiderLegEnd)).zipIdx
      = [((1, SpiderLegEnd.outward), 0), ((r, φ), 1)] from by simp [List.zipIdx]]
  simp only [List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil, List.append_nil,
    List.eraseIdx_cons_zero, List.eraseIdx_cons_succ]
  rfl

steps.claim: For any n, List.range (n + 2) splits into 0, the range of n shifted by +1, and n + 1.
steps.explanation: Proved by induction on n. The base case n = 0 holds definitionally. For the induction step, rewriting (k + 1) + 2 = (k + 2) + 1, applying List.range_succ and the induction hypothesis, and distributing List.map over list concatenation with List.map_append rearranges the list into head 0, shifted elements, and the last element k + 2.
steps.code:
induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [show k + 1 + 2 = (k + 2) + 1 by ring, List.range_succ, ih]
    rw [show k + 1 + 1 = k + 2 by ring]
    rw [List.range_succ (n:=k), List.map_append]
    simp [List.cons_append, List.append_assoc]

steps.claim: For r ≥ 2, List.range r decomposes into 0, intermediate elements mapped from range (r - 2) by +1, and r - 1.
steps.explanation: Rewriting r = (r - 2) + 2 via arithmetic, this follows directly from spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_range_succ_two with n = r - 2.
steps.code:
conv => lhs; rw [show r = (r-2)+2 by omega]
  rw [spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_range_succ_two]
  rw [show r - 2 + 1 = r - 1 by omega]

steps.claim: The options generated by cutting leg 0 evaluate to the singleton list [r].
steps.explanation: Leg 0 has length 1 with outward orientation, so the only cut length is j = 1. The rules filter out inward orientation, leaving only outward, which transitions the centre to free on the single remaining leg [(r, φ)]. For φ ≠ free, spider_gamma on [(r, φ)] with free centre evaluates to r. Since the cut piece has length 0, its nim-value is 0, yielding 0 ^^^ r = r.
steps.code:
have hg : spider_gamma (r + 1) CentreStatus.free [(r, φ)] = r := by
    rcases φ with _ | _ | _
    · exact absurd rfl hφ
    · simp only [spider_gamma]; simp [spider_rho_star]
    · simp only [spider_gamma]; simp [spider_rho_star]
  unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0
  simp only [List.range_one, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil, List.filterMap_cons,
    List.filterMap_nil, List.append_nil]
  simp only [spider_rho, spider_update_centre]
  rw [hg]
  simp

steps.claim: Cutting length 1 (j_zero = 0) on leg 1 produces two options, each XOR-summed with 1.
steps.explanation: When j = 1, since r ≥ 2, j ≠ r and j < 2. The cut removes leg 1 completely, leaving only the first leg [(1, outward)]. For either choice of new orientation δ ∈ {inward, outward}, the centre updates to incoming or free, and spider_gamma on [(1, outward)] evaluates to 1. The cut piece of length r - 1 contributes ρ(r - 1, δ, φ), giving the two options ρ(r - 1, inward, φ) ^^^ 1 and ρ(r - 1, outward, φ) ^^^ 1.
steps.code:
have h1r : (1 == r) = false := by
    rw [Bool.eq_false_iff]; simp [beq_iff_eq]; omega
  have h1g : ¬ (1 ≥ 2) := by omega
  unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1
  simp only [Nat.zero_add, h1r, Bool.false_eq_true, false_and, if_false, h1g, if_false]
  simp only [List.filterMap_cons, List.filterMap_nil, spider_update_centre]
  rw [show spider_gamma (r+1) CentreStatus.incoming [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)] = 1 from by
      simp only [spider_gamma]; simp [spider_rho]]
  rw [show spider_gamma (r+1) CentreStatus.free [(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)] = 1 from by
      simp only [spider_gamma]; simp [spider_rho_star]]

steps.claim: For any 2 ≤ j ≤ r and δ ≠ free, the two-leg spider [(j - 1, δ), (1, outward)] with incoming centre has nim-value (j - 1) ^^^ 1.
steps.explanation: By spider_gamma_fuel_independent, the fuel r + 1 can be replaced by the minimal fuel j + 1. Swapping the two legs using spider_gamma_swap_two transforms the state to [(1, outward), (j - 1, δ)], to which the induction hypothesis ih applies at length j - 1 < r, yielding (j - 1) ^^^ 1.
steps.code:
have hmid : ∀ (j : ℕ) (δ : SpiderLegEnd), δ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free → 2 ≤ j → j ≤ r →
      spider_gamma (r+1) CentreStatus.incoming [(j-1, δ), (1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)] = (j-1) ^^^ 1 := by
    intro j δ hδ h2 hjr
    have hsum : ((([(j-1, δ), (1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)]).map Prod.fst).sum) + 1 = j + 1 := by
      simp; omega
    rw [spider_gamma_fuel_independent (r+1) CentreStatus.incoming _ (by omega)]
    rw [hsum]
    rw [spider_gamma_swap_two]
    have := ih (j-1) (by omega) (by omega) δ hδ
    rw [show (j-1)+2 = j+1 by omega] at this
    exact this

steps.claim: For each intermediate index idx < r - 2, the cut j = idx + 2 on leg 1 yields two options XOR-summed with (idx + 1) ^^^ 1.
steps.explanation: With j = idx + 2, we have 2 ≤ j < r, so neither boundary filtering condition triggers. The cut piece has length r - j = r - 1 - (idx + 1). The remaining spider has legs [(idx + 1, δ), (1, outward)] and incoming centre, which evaluates to (idx + 1) ^^^ 1 by the previous step (hmid) for both δ = inward and δ = outward.
steps.code:
unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1
  rw [show idx + 1 + 1 = idx + 2 by omega]
  have hjr : (idx + 2 == r) = false := by
    rw [Bool.eq_false_iff]; simp [beq_iff_eq]; omega
  have hj2 : 2 ≤ idx + 2 := by omega
  simp only [hjr, Bool.false_eq_true, false_and, if_false, hj2, if_pos]
  simp only [List.filterMap_cons, List.filterMap_nil]
  rw [show r - (idx + 2) = r - 1 - (idx + 1) by omega]
  rw [hmid (idx+2) SpiderLegEnd.inward (by decide) hj2 (by omega)]
  rw [hmid (idx+2) SpiderLegEnd.outward (by decide) hj2 (by omega)]
  simp only [show idx + 2 - 1 = idx + 1 by omega]

steps.claim: After a cut of length r on leg 1, the remaining spider [(r - 1, φ), (1, outward)] with incoming centre has nim-value (r - 1) ^^^ 1.
steps.explanation: Swapping the two legs via spider_gamma_swap_two and applying the induction hypothesis ih at length r - 1 < r yields (r - 1) ^^^ 1.
steps.code:
have hg : spider_gamma (r+1) CentreStatus.incoming [(r-1,φ),(1, SpiderLegEnd.outward)] =
      (r-1)^^^1 := by
    rw [spider_gamma_swap_two]
    have := ih (r-1) (by omega) (by omega) φ hφ
    rw [show (r-1)+2 = r+1 by omega] at this
    exact this

steps.claim: The final cut j = r (j_zero = r - 1) on leg 1 yields the single option ρ(0, φ, φ) ^^^ ((r - 1) ^^^ 1).
steps.explanation: Case analysis on φ ≠ free: when j = r, any orientation δ ≠ φ is filtered out, leaving only δ = φ. Since r ≥ 2, the remaining leg has length r - 1 with orientation φ. The cut piece has length r - r = 0, contributing ρ(0, φ, φ), while the remaining spider evaluates to (r - 1) ^^^ 1 by hg.
steps.code:
rcases φ with _ | _ | _
  · exact absurd rfl hφ
  · unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1
    rw [show r - 1 + 1 = r by omega]
    simp only [beq_self_eq_true, true_and, List.filterMap_cons, List.filterMap_nil,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.inward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) = True from by decide,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.inward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.inward) = False from by decide,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.outward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.inward) = True from by decide,
      and_true, if_false, if_true, hr, spider_rho]
    rw [show r - r = 0 by omega, hg]
  · unfold spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1
    rw [show r - 1 + 1 = r by omega]
    simp only [beq_self_eq_true, true_and, List.filterMap_cons, List.filterMap_nil,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.outward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) = True from by decide,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.inward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.outward) = True from by decide,
      show (SpiderLegEnd.outward ≠ SpiderLegEnd.outward) = False from by decide,
      and_true, if_false, if_true, hr, spider_rho]
    rw [show r - r = 0 by omega, hg]

steps.claim: The flatMap of leg 1 over all shifted intermediate indices equals the flatMap over List.range (r - 2) using the intermediate cut formula.
steps.explanation: Using List.flatMap_map, the map of +1 is composed into the flatMap. Applying List.flatMap_congr with List.mem_range allows rewriting each term pointwise using spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_mid.
steps.code:
rw [List.flatMap_map]
  apply List.flatMap_congr
  intro idx hidx
  rw [List.mem_range] at hidx
  exact spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_mid r φ ih idx hidx

steps.claim: The options from leg 0 and all cuts on leg 1 concatenate to the explicit list of head options, intermediate cuts, and the final cut.
steps.explanation: Rewriting leg 0 via spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0_head yields [r]. Splitting List.range r via spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_range_split and distributing flatMap over list concatenation (List.flatMap_append, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil) substitutes the evaluations for the initial cut (leg1_zero), intermediate cuts (mid_all), and the final cut (leg1_last).
steps.code:
rw [spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg0_head r φ hφ,
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_range_split r hr, List.flatMap_cons,
    List.flatMap_append, List.flatMap_cons, List.flatMap_nil,
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_zero r hr φ,
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_mid_all r φ ih,
    spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_leg1_last r hr φ hφ ih]
  simp only [List.append_nil]
  rfl

steps.claim: The raw options list generated by [(1, outward), (r, φ)] unfolds to the explicit list of head options, intermediate cuts, and the final cut.
steps.explanation: The proof rewrites the raw options list into leg 0 and leg 1 via spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_split, and concludes by applying spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_main.
steps.code:
rw [spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_split r φ]
  exact spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_options_eq_main r hr φ hφ ih

glossary.List.zipIdx: Pairs each element of a list with its zero-based index.
glossary.List.flatMap_cons: FlatMapping a function over a non-empty list x :: xs yields f(x) appended to the flatMap of xs.
glossary.List.flatMap_nil: FlatMapping a function over the empty list yields the empty list.
glossary.List.append_nil: Appending the empty list to any list yields the original list.
glossary.List.eraseIdx_cons_zero: Erasing index 0 of a :: as leaves as.
glossary.List.eraseIdx_cons_succ: Erasing index i + 1 of a :: as leaves a :: eraseIdx i as.
glossary.List.range_succ: The range of n + 1 equals the range of n followed by [n].
glossary.List.map_append: Mapping a function over the concatenation of two lists equals the concatenation of the mapped lists.
glossary.List.cons_append: Prepending an element to the concatenation of two lists equals prepending it to the first list.
glossary.List.append_assoc: Concatenation of lists is associative: (as ++ bs) ++ cs = as ++ (bs ++ cs).
glossary.spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_opti: The range of n + 2 decomposes into 0, the range of n shifted by +1, and n + 1.
The definition of the options list generated by cuts on the first leg [(1, outward)].
glossary.List.range_one: The range of 1 is the singleton list [0].
glossary.spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_opti: The definition of the options list generated by cutting the second leg (r, φ) at cut length j_zero + 1.
glossary.Bool.eq_false_iff: A boolean value is false if and only if it is not true.
glossary.beq_iff_eq: Boolean equality a == b is true if and only if a = b.
glossary.spider_gamma_fuel_independent: The game value function γ is fuel-independent once fuel exceeds the sum of leg lengths plus 1.
glossary.spider_gamma_swap_two: The game value γ of a two-leg position is invariant under swapping the two legs.
glossary.List.flatMap_map: FlatMapping a function g over List.map f l equals flatMapping g ∘ f directly over l.
glossary.List.flatMap_congr: Two flatMaps over the same list are equal if the functions agree on every element of the list.
glossary.List.mem_range: A natural number m belongs to List.range n if and only if m < n.
glossary.spider_blocked_incoming_one_outward_opti: For idx < r - 2, the cut of length idx + 2 on leg 1 produces two options XOR-summed with (idx + 1) ^^^ 1, under the induction hypothesis.
The options generated by cutting leg 0 in state [(1, outward), (r, φ)] evaluate to [r] when φ ≠ free.
For r ≥ 2, List.range r decomposes into 0, the shifted range of r - 2, and r - 1.

declarations.name: spider_blocked_two_three_reversal
declarations.informal: For any fuel and leg length t, the spider gamma value with centre none and legs (t, outward), (2, free), (3, free) equals the gamma value with (t, inward), (2, free), (3, free).
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_blocked_two_three_reversal (fuel t : ℕ) :
    spider_gamma fuel CentreStatus.none [(t, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (3, SpiderLegEnd.free)] =
    spider_gamma fuel CentreStatus.none [(t, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (3, SpiderLegEnd.free)]
declarations.source:
/-- For the spider state with legs (t, delta), (2, free), (3, free) and centre none, outward and inward orientations of the first leg yield equal gamma values for all fuels. -/
theorem spider_blocked_two_three_reversal (fuel t : ℕ) :
    spider_gamma fuel CentreStatus.none [(t, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (3, SpiderLegEnd.free)] =
    spider_gamma fuel CentreStatus.none [(t, SpiderLegEnd.inward), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (3, SpiderLegEnd.free)] := by
  rw [spider_gamma_reversal fuel CentreStatus.none
    [(t, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (3, SpiderLegEnd.free)]]
  rfl

explanation.summary: The equality follows from the spider reversal symmetry theorem (`spider_gamma_reversal`), which asserts that the γ-value is invariant under simultaneously reversing the centre status and inverting all leg orientations. For the given state, the centre status `none` and the two free legs of lengths 2 and 3 are fixed under reversal, while the outward leg of length t reverses to an inward leg. The resulting reversed configuration is definitionally identical to the right-hand side, completing the proof.

steps.claim: The γ-value of the initial configuration equals the γ-value of its reversed configuration.
steps.explanation: We rewrite the left-hand side using `spider_gamma_reversal`, which replaces the centre status `CentreStatus.none` with its reversal `spider_reverse_centre_status CentreStatus.none`, and applies `spider_reverse_leg_end` to the orientation of each leg in the list.
steps.code:
rw [spider_gamma_reversal fuel CentreStatus.none
    [(t, SpiderLegEnd.outward), (2, SpiderLegEnd.free), (3, SpiderLegEnd.free)]]

steps.claim: The reversed configuration simplifies definitionally to the goal configuration with an inward first leg, completing the proof.
steps.explanation: By definition of the reversal operations, `spider_reverse_centre_status CentreStatus.none` evaluates to `CentreStatus.none`, `spider_reverse_leg_end SpiderLegEnd.outward` evaluates to `SpiderLegEnd.inward`, and `spider_reverse_leg_end SpiderLegEnd.free` evaluates to `SpiderLegEnd.free`. The reversed state is therefore definitionally equal to the right-hand side, so reflexivity (`rfl`) finishes the proof.
steps.code: rfl

glossary.spider_gamma_reversal: For any fuel, centre status s, and leg list L, the spider γ-value is invariant under reversing the centre status and reversing the orientation of every leg end.

declarations.name: is_item_preserving_swap_bid
declarations.informal: Bid r of agent i is obtained from b i by an item-preserving swap: a swap of the goods in positions k < l that demotes the good g = b i k, where g is allocated to i both before and after the swap.
declarations.statement:
def is_item_preserving_swap_bid {N G : Type*} [DecidableEq N] [DecidableEq G] {m : ℕ}
    (seq : List N) (b : N → Fin m ≃ G) (i : N) (r : Fin m ≃ G) : Prop
declarations.source:
/-- Agent `i`'s bid `r` is obtained from `b i` by an item-preserving swap: positions `k < l` exchanged, demoting the good `b i k`, which `i` receives both before and after the swap. -/
def is_item_preserving_swap_bid {N G : Type*} [DecidableEq N] [DecidableEq G] {m : ℕ}
    (seq : List N) (b : N → Fin m ≃ G) (i : N) (r : Fin m ≃ G) : Prop :=
  ∃ k l : Fin m, k < l ∧ r = ranking_swap (b i) k l ∧
    b i k ∈ picking_sequence_outcome seq b i ∧
    b i k ∈ picking_sequence_outcome seq (Function.update b i r) i

declarations.name: irr_step
declarations.informal: One step of iterated picking sequences restricted to admissible bids adm: some agent i that has a strictly profitable admissible manipulation changes its bid to a best response among its admissible bids, the other bids unchanged. Utilities are additive with item values v.
declarations.source:
/-- One step of the iterated picking-sequence dynamics `IPS_π` restricted to the admissible bids `adm b i`: an agent `i` with a strictly profitable admissible manipulation replaces its bid by a best response among its admissible bids; the other bids are unchanged. Utilities are additive with item values `v`. -/
def irr_step {N G : Type*} [DecidableEq N] [DecidableEq G] {m : ℕ}
    (v : N → G → ℝ) (seq : List N) (adm : (N → Fin m ≃ G) → N → (Fin m ≃ G) → Prop)
    (b b' : N → Fin m ≃ G) : Prop :=
  ∃ i : N,
    (∃ r, adm b i r ∧ ∑ g ∈ picking_sequence_outcome seq b i, v i g <
        ∑ g ∈ picking_sequence_outcome seq (Function.update b i r) i, v i g) ∧
    ∃ r, adm b i r ∧ b' = Function.update b i r ∧
      ∀ r', adm b i r' → ∑ g ∈ picking_sequence_outcome seq (Function.update b i r') i, v i g ≤
        ∑ g ∈ picking_sequence_outcome seq b' i, v i g
declarations.citation: arXiv:2610.23040 Sec. 2 (Iterated setting) and Sec. 3 (restricted manipulations)

declarations.name: ranking_swap_apply_left
declarations.informal: After swapping positions k and l, position k holds the good that was at position l.
declarations.statement:
theorem ranking_swap_apply_left {G : Type*} {m : ℕ} (r : Fin m ≃ G) (k l : Fin m) :
    ranking_swap r k l k = r l
declarations.source:
theorem ranking_swap_apply_left {G : Type*} {m : ℕ} (r : Fin m ≃ G) (k l : Fin m) :
    ranking_swap r k l k = r l := by
  simp [ranking_swap]

explanation.summary: The theorem asserts that after swapping positions k and l, position k is assigned the item originally at position l. The proof unfolds the definition of ranking_swap as the composition of the transposition swap k l with the ranking r. The simplifier then evaluates the transposition at k, which gives l, and concludes that the composite maps k to r l.

steps.claim: The swapped ranking maps position k to r l.
steps.explanation: By definition, ranking_swap r k l is the composition (Equiv.swap k l).trans r. Applying this equivalence to position k first swaps k with l (yielding l) and then applies the ranking r, resulting in r l. The simp tactic unfolds ranking_swap and evaluates this composition directly.
steps.code: simp [ranking_swap]

glossary.ranking_swap: The ranking obtained by first swapping the positions k and l, then applying r; defined as the composition (Equiv.swap k l).trans r.

caveats: The simplifier automatically unfolds `ranking_swap` into `(Equiv.swap k l).trans r` and applies the standard equivalence rules for composition (`Equiv.trans_apply`) and swapping (`Equiv.swap_apply_left`).
