      (if x = v3 then c else 0) + (if x = v4 then d else 0) := by
    intro a b c d x
    simp only [Multiset.count_add, Multiset.count_replicate,
      @eq_comm _ v1 x, @eq_comm _ v2 x, @eq_comm _ v3 x, @eq_comm _ v4 x]
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro h
    have hc := congrArg Multiset.card h
    dsimp [davenport_box_three_even_sequence] at hc
    simp only [Multiset.card_add, Multiset.card_replicate] at hc
    have : 0 < 4 * m ^ 3 - 4 * m ^ 2 + 2 * m := by
      have : 4 * m ^ 2 < 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
      omega
    omega
  · exact davenport_box_three_even_sequence_sum m hm
  · intro t ht ht0 hts
    rw [hS] at ht ⊢
    set a := t.count v1
    set b := t.count v2
    set c := t.count v3
    set d := t.count v4
    have hteq : t = Multiset.replicate a v1 + Multiset.replicate b v2 +
        Multiset.replicate c v3 + Multiset.replicate d v4 := by
      ext x
      rw [hcount]
      by_cases h1 : x = v1
      · rw [h1, if_pos rfl, if_neg h12, if_neg h13, if_neg h14]
        simp only [add_zero]
        rfl
      by_cases h2 : x = v2
      · rw [h2, if_neg h12.symm, if_pos rfl, if_neg h23, if_neg h24]
        simp only [zero_add, add_zero]
        rfl
      by_cases h3 : x = v3
      · rw [h3, if_neg h13.symm, if_neg h23.symm, if_pos rfl, if_neg h34]
        simp only [zero_add, add_zero]
        rfl
      by_cases h4 : x = v4
      · rw [h4, if_neg h14.symm, if_neg h24.symm, if_neg h34.symm, if_pos rfl]
        simp only [zero_add]
        rfl
      simp only [h1, h2, h3, h4, if_false, add_zero]
      rw [Multiset.count_eq_zero]
      intro hx
      have := Multiset.mem_of_le ht hx
      simp only [Multiset.mem_add, Multiset.mem_replicate] at this
      rcases this with (((⟨_, rfl⟩ | ⟨_, rfl⟩) | ⟨_, rfl⟩) | ⟨_, rfl⟩) <;> contradiction
    have ha : a ≤ k1 := by
      have := Multiset.count_le_of_le v1 ht
      rwa [hcount, if_pos rfl, if_neg h12, if_neg h13, if_neg h14, add_zero, add_zero, add_zero] at this
    rw [hteq] at hts
    have he0 := congrFun hts (0 : Fin 3)
    have he1 := congrFun hts (1 : Fin 3)
    have he2 := congrFun hts (2 : Fin 3)
    simp [Multiset.sum_add, Multiset.sum_replicate, hv1, hv2, hv3, hv4] at he0 he1 he2
    set A : ℤ := (a : ℤ)
    set B : ℤ := (b : ℤ)
    set C : ℤ := (c : ℤ)
    set D : ℤ := (d : ℤ)
    set K1 : ℤ := (k1 : ℤ)
    set K2 : ℤ := (k2 : ℤ)
    set K3 : ℤ := (k3 : ℤ)
    set K4 : ℤ := (k4 : ℤ)
    have hrel2 : B * K1 = A * K2 := by
      rw [hk1Z, hk2Z]
      linear_combination (2 * M ^ 2 - 2 * M + 1) * he1 + (2 * M ^ 2 - 2 * M + 1) * he2
    have hrel3 : C * K1 = A * K3 := by
      rw [hk1Z, hk3Z]
      linear_combination (2 * M ^ 2 - M) * he0 + M * he1 + (2 * M ^ 2 - 2 * M + 1) * he2
    have hrel4 : D * K1 = A * K4 := by
      rw [hk1Z, hk4Z]
      linear_combination (2 * M ^ 2 - 3 * M + 1) * he0 + (2 * M ^ 2 - M) * he1
    set c1 : ℤ := -1
    set c2 : ℤ := 4 * M ^ 2 - 6 * M + 4
    set c3 : ℤ := 0
    set c4 : ℤ := -(4 * M ^ 2 - 6 * M + 4)
    have hbez : c1 * K1 + c2 * K2 + c3 * K3 + c4 * K4 = 1 := by
      dsimp [c1, c2, c3, c4]
      rw [hk1Z, hk2Z, hk3Z, hk4Z]
      ring
    have hAK1 : A = K1 * (c1 * A + c2 * B + c3 * C + c4 * D) := by
      calc
        A = A * 1 := by ring
        _ = A * (c1 * K1 + c2 * K2 + c3 * K3 + c4 * K4) := by rw [hbez]
        _ = c1 * A * K1 + c2 * (A * K2) + c3 * (A * K3) + c4 * (A * K4) := by ring
        _ = c1 * A * K1 + c2 * (B * K1) + c3 * (C * K1) + c4 * (D * K1) := by rw [← hrel2, ← hrel3, ← hrel4]
        _ = K1 * (c1 * A + c2 * B + c3 * C + c4 * D) := by ring
    have hK1pos : 0 < K1 := by
      rw [hk1Z]
      have : 4 * M ^ 3 - 6 * M ^ 2 + 4 * M - 1 = 2 * M ^ 2 * (2 * M - 3) + 4 * M - 1 := by ring
      rw [this]
      have : 0 ≤ 2 * M - 3 := by omega
      have : 0 ≤ 2 * M ^ 2 := by nlinarith
      have : 0 ≤ 2 * M ^ 2 * (2 * M - 3) := by nlinarith
      omega
    have hK1ne : K1 ≠ 0 := by linarith
    set q : ℤ := c1 * A + c2 * B + c3 * C + c4 * D
    have hq0 : 0 ≤ q := by
      have : 0 ≤ A := Nat.cast_nonneg a
      have : 0 ≤ K1 * q := by rw [← hAK1]; exact this
      nlinarith
    have hq1 : q ≤ 1 := by
      have : A ≤ K1 := Nat.cast_le.mpr ha
      have : K1 * q ≤ K1 * 1 := by rw [← hAK1]; linarith
      nlinarith
    rcases (show q = 0 ∨ q = 1 by omega) with hq | hq
    · exfalso
      apply ht0
      have hA0 : A = 0 := by rw [hAK1, hq]; ring
      have hB0 : B = 0 := by
        have : B * K1 = 0 := by rw [hrel2, hA0, zero_mul]
        exact mul_eq_zero.mp this |>.resolve_right hK1ne
      have hC0 : C = 0 := by
        have : C * K1 = 0 := by rw [hrel3, hA0, zero_mul]
        exact mul_eq_zero.mp this |>.resolve_right hK1ne
      have hD0 : D = 0 := by
        have : D * K1 = 0 := by rw [hrel4, hA0, zero_mul]
        exact mul_eq_zero.mp this |>.resolve_right hK1ne
      have ha0 : a = 0 := Nat.cast_eq_zero.mp hA0
      have hb0 : b = 0 := Nat.cast_eq_zero.mp hB0
      have hc0 : c = 0 := Nat.cast_eq_zero.mp hC0
      have hd0 : d = 0 := Nat.cast_eq_zero.mp hD0
      rw [hteq, ha0, hb0, hc0, hd0]
      simp
    · have hA1 : A = K1 := by rw [hAK1, hq]; ring
      have hB1 : B = K2 := by
        have : B * K1 = K2 * K1 := by rw [hrel2, hA1, mul_comm]
        exact mul_right_cancel₀ hK1ne this
      have hC1 : C = K3 := by
        have : C * K1 = K3 * K1 := by rw [hrel3, hA1, mul_comm]
        exact mul_right_cancel₀ hK1ne this
      have hD1 : D = K4 := by
        have : D * K1 = K4 * K1 := by rw [hrel4, hA1, mul_comm]
        exact mul_right_cancel₀ hK1ne this
      have ha1 : a = k1 := Nat.cast_inj.mp hA1
      have hb1 : b = k2 := Nat.cast_inj.mp hB1
      have hc1 : c = k3 := Nat.cast_inj.mp hC1
      have hd1 : d = k4 := Nat.cast_inj.mp hD1
      rw [hteq, ha1, hb1, hc1, hd1]
declarations.citation: The core of the proof of Theorem 3 of arXiv:2610.16562 (even m).

explanation.summary: The proof establishes that the sequence $T(m)$ is nonempty (its cardinality is positive) and has zero sum (by a previously proven lemma). To show that any zero-sum sub-multiset $t \le T(m)$ with $t \ne 0$ must equal $T(m)$, the three coordinate equations of the vector sum $\sum t = 0$ are linearly combined to show that the multiplicities $(a, b, c, d)$ of the four vectors in $t$ are proportional to their total counts $(k_1, k_2, k_3, k_4)$ in $T(m)$. Using an explicit Bézout identity $\sum_{i=1}^4 c_i k_i = 1$, the ratio $q = a / k_1$ is shown to be an integer satisfying $0 \le q \le 1$. Finally, $q = 0$ is ruled out because $t \ne 0$, forcing $q = 1$ and therefore $t = T(m)$.

steps.claim: Definition of the four vectors and their multiplicity polynomials, cast into $\mathbb{Z}$
steps.explanation: We introduce the integer $M = (m : \mathbb{Z}) \ge 2$, define the four basis vectors $v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4 \in \mathbb{Z}^3$, and define the counts $k_1, k_2, k_3, k_4 \in \mathbb{N}$ as polynomials in $m$. To ensure that the truncated subtractions in $\mathbb{N}$ match the ordinary integer subtractions, we verify the required inequalities via non-linear arithmetic (`nlinarith`) and cast the polynomial expressions into $\mathbb{Z}$ using `Nat.cast_sub`, producing the identities `hk1Z` through `hk4Z`.
steps.code:
have _ := heven
  set M : ℤ := (m : ℤ) with hM
  have hM2 : 2 ≤ M := by rw [hM]; exact_mod_cast hm
  set v1 : Fin 3 → ℤ := ![-M, -M, -M] with hv1
  set v2 : Fin 3 → ℤ := ![-M, M - 1, M] with hv2
  set v3 : Fin 3 → ℤ := ![M, -(M - 1), M - 1] with hv3
  set v4 : Fin 3 → ℤ := ![M - 1, M, -M] with hv4
  set k1 := 4 * m ^ 3 - 6 * m ^ 2 + 4 * m - 1 with hk1
  set k2 := 4 * m ^ 3 - 4 * m ^ 2 + 2 * m with hk2
  set k3 := 4 * m ^ 3 - 2 * m ^ 2 + m with hk3
  set k4 := 4 * m ^ 3 - 4 * m ^ 2 + m with hk4
  have hk1Z : (k1 : ℤ) = 4 * M ^ 3 - 6 * M ^ 2 + 4 * M - 1 := by
    rw [hk1, hM]
    have h1 : 6 * m ^ 2 ≤ 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
    have h2 : 1 ≤ 4 * m ^ 3 - 6 * m ^ 2 + 4 * m := by
      have : 6 * m ^ 2 < 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
      omega
    rw [Nat.cast_sub h2]
    push_cast
    rw [Nat.cast_sub h1]
    push_cast
    ring
  have hk2Z : (k2 : ℤ) = 4 * M ^ 3 - 4 * M ^ 2 + 2 * M := by
    rw [hk2, hM]
    have h3 : 4 * m ^ 2 ≤ 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
    push_cast
    rw [Nat.cast_sub h3]
    push_cast
    ring
  have hk3Z : (k3 : ℤ) = 4 * M ^ 3 - 2 * M ^ 2 + M := by
    rw [hk3, hM]
    have h3 : 2 * m ^ 2 ≤ 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
    push_cast
    rw [Nat.cast_sub h3]
    push_cast
    ring
  have hk4Z : (k4 : ℤ) = 4 * M ^ 3 - 4 * M ^ 2 + M := by
    rw [hk4, hM]
    have h3 : 4 * m ^ 2 ≤ 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
    push_cast
    rw [Nat.cast_sub h3]
    push_cast
    ring

steps.claim: The sequence is a multiset sum of four pairwise distinct vectors, with an explicit counting formula
steps.explanation: We express the sequence $S = T(m)$ as the multiset sum of $k_i$ copies of $v_i$ for $i \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$. Evaluating individual components shows that $v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4$ are pairwise distinct. Consequently, for any multiset composed of copies of these four vectors, the multiplicity of any element $x$ is given by `hcount`: it is the corresponding coefficient if $x$ matches one of the $v_i$, and $0$ otherwise.
steps.code:
have hS : davenport_box_three_even_sequence m =
      Multiset.replicate k1 v1 + Multiset.replicate k2 v2 +
      Multiset.replicate k3 v3 + Multiset.replicate k4 v4 := rfl
  have h12 : v1 ≠ v2 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 1; simp [hv1, hv2] at this; omega
  have h13 : v1 ≠ v3 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 0; simp [hv1, hv3] at this; omega
  have h14 : v1 ≠ v4 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 1; simp [hv1, hv4] at this; omega
  have h23 : v2 ≠ v3 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 0; simp [hv2, hv3] at this; omega
  have h24 : v2 ≠ v4 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 2; simp [hv2, hv4] at this; omega
  have h34 : v3 ≠ v4 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 0; simp [hv3, hv4] at this; omega
  have hcount : ∀ (a b c d : ℕ) (x : Fin 3 → ℤ),
      (Multiset.replicate a v1 + Multiset.replicate b v2 +
       Multiset.replicate c v3 + Multiset.replicate d v4).count x =
      (if x = v1 then a else 0) + (if x = v2 then b else 0) +
      (if x = v3 then c else 0) + (if x = v4 then d else 0) := by
    intro a b c d x
    simp only [Multiset.count_add, Multiset.count_replicate,
      @eq_comm _ v1 x, @eq_comm _ v2 x, @eq_comm _ v3 x, @eq_comm _ v4 x]

steps.claim: $T(m)$ is nonempty and sums to zero in $\mathbb{Z}^3$
steps.explanation: We split the goal `multiset_is_minimal_zero_sum` into three parts: nonemptiness, zero sum, and subsequence minimality. Nonemptiness holds because the total cardinality is strictly positive (as $k_2 = 4m^3 - 4m^2 + 2m > 0$ for $m \ge 2$). The condition that $T(m)$ sums to zero is provided by the previously established lemma `davenport_box_three_even_sequence_sum`.
steps.code:
refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro h
    have hc := congrArg Multiset.card h
    dsimp [davenport_box_three_even_sequence] at hc
    simp only [Multiset.card_add, Multiset.card_replicate] at hc
    have : 0 < 4 * m ^ 3 - 4 * m ^ 2 + 2 * m := by
      have : 4 * m ^ 2 < 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
      omega
    omega
  · exact davenport_box_three_even_sequence_sum m hm

steps.claim: Any sub-multiset $t \le T(m)$ is supported on $\{v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4\}$ and its coordinate sum yields three linear equations
steps.explanation: Let $t \le S$ be a sub-multiset with $t \ne 0$ and $\sum t = 0$. Let $a, b, c, d \in \mathbb{N}$ be the multiplicities of $v_1, v_2, v_3, v_4$ in $t$. Since every element of $t$ must belong to $S$ and $S$ contains only these four vectors, $t = a[v_1] + b[v_2] + c[v_3] + d[v_4]$ and $a \le k_1$. Expanding the zero-sum condition $\sum t = 0$ along the three coordinate axes gives three linear equations `he0`, `he1`, `he2` in the multiplicities.
steps.code:
· intro t ht ht0 hts
    rw [hS] at ht ⊢
    set a := t.count v1
    set b := t.count v2
    set c := t.count v3
    set d := t.count v4
    have hteq : t = Multiset.replicate a v1 + Multiset.replicate b v2 +
        Multiset.replicate c v3 + Multiset.replicate d v4 := by
      ext x
      rw [hcount]
      by_cases h1 : x = v1
      · rw [h1, if_pos rfl, if_neg h12, if_neg h13, if_neg h14]
        simp only [add_zero]
        rfl
      by_cases h2 : x = v2
      · rw [h2, if_neg h12.symm, if_pos rfl, if_neg h23, if_neg h24]
        simp only [zero_add, add_zero]
        rfl
      by_cases h3 : x = v3
      · rw [h3, if_neg h13.symm, if_neg h23.symm, if_pos rfl, if_neg h34]
        simp only [zero_add, add_zero]
        rfl
      by_cases h4 : x = v4
      · rw [h4, if_neg h14.symm, if_neg h24.symm, if_neg h34.symm, if_pos rfl]
        simp only [zero_add]
        rfl
      simp only [h1, h2, h3, h4, if_false, add_zero]
      rw [Multiset.count_eq_zero]
      intro hx
      have := Multiset.mem_of_le ht hx
      simp only [Multiset.mem_add, Multiset.mem_replicate] at this
      rcases this with (((⟨_, rfl⟩ | ⟨_, rfl⟩) | ⟨_, rfl⟩) | ⟨_, rfl⟩) <;> contradiction
    have ha : a ≤ k1 := by
      have := Multiset.count_le_of_le v1 ht
      rwa [hcount, if_pos rfl, if_neg h12, if_neg h13, if_neg h14, add_zero, add_zero, add_zero] at this
    rw [hteq] at hts
    have he0 := congrFun hts (0 : Fin 3)
    have he1 := congrFun hts (1 : Fin 3)
    have he2 := congrFun hts (2 : Fin 3)
    simp [Multiset.sum_add, Multiset.sum_replicate, hv1, hv2, hv3, hv4] at he0 he1 he2

steps.claim: The sub-multiset multiplicities $(A, B, C, D)$ are proportional to $(K_1, K_2, K_3, K_4)$
steps.explanation: Letting $A, B, C, D, K_1, K_2, K_3, K_4$ denote the integer casts of the multiplicities and total counts, we use linear combinations of the three coordinate equations `he0`, `he1`, `he2` to eliminate variables. This establishes the cross-multiplication identities $B K_1 = A K_2$, $C K_1 = A K_3$, and $D K_1 = A K_4$.
steps.code:
set A : ℤ := (a : ℤ)
    set B : ℤ := (b : ℤ)
    set C : ℤ := (c : ℤ)
    set D : ℤ := (d : ℤ)
    set K1 : ℤ := (k1 : ℤ)
    set K2 : ℤ := (k2 : ℤ)
    set K3 : ℤ := (k3 : ℤ)
    set K4 : ℤ := (k4 : ℤ)
    have hrel2 : B * K1 = A * K2 := by
      rw [hk1Z, hk2Z]
      linear_combination (2 * M ^ 2 - 2 * M + 1) * he1 + (2 * M ^ 2 - 2 * M + 1) * he2
    have hrel3 : C * K1 = A * K3 := by
      rw [hk1Z, hk3Z]
      linear_combination (2 * M ^ 2 - M) * he0 + M * he1 + (2 * M ^ 2 - 2 * M + 1) * he2
    have hrel4 : D * K1 = A * K4 := by
      rw [hk1Z, hk4Z]
      linear_combination (2 * M ^ 2 - 3 * M + 1) * he0 + (2 * M ^ 2 - M) * he1

steps.claim: A Bézout identity implies $A = K_1 q$ for an integer $q \in \{0, 1\}$
steps.explanation: We define polynomial integer coefficients $c_1 = -1$, $c_2 = 4M^2 - 6M + 4$, $c_3 = 0$, $c_4 = -(4M^2 - 6M + 4)$ and verify by ring arithmetic that $\sum_{i=1}^4 c_i K_i = 1$. Multiplying this identity by $A$ and substituting the proportionality relations gives $A = K_1 \cdot q$, where $q = c_1 A + c_2 B + c_3 C + c_4 D \in \mathbb{Z}$. Because $K_1 > 0$ and $0 \le A \le K_1$, the ratio $q$ must satisfy $0 \le q \le 1$.
steps.code:
set c1 : ℤ := -1
    set c2 : ℤ := 4 * M ^ 2 - 6 * M + 4
    set c3 : ℤ := 0
    set c4 : ℤ := -(4 * M ^ 2 - 6 * M + 4)
    have hbez : c1 * K1 + c2 * K2 + c3 * K3 + c4 * K4 = 1 := by
      dsimp [c1, c2, c3, c4]
      rw [hk1Z, hk2Z, hk3Z, hk4Z]
      ring
    have hAK1 : A = K1 * (c1 * A + c2 * B + c3 * C + c4 * D) := by
      calc
        A = A * 1 := by ring
        _ = A * (c1 * K1 + c2 * K2 + c3 * K3 + c4 * K4) := by rw [hbez]
        _ = c1 * A * K1 + c2 * (A * K2) + c3 * (A * K3) + c4 * (A * K4) := by ring
        _ = c1 * A * K1 + c2 * (B * K1) + c3 * (C * K1) + c4 * (D * K1) := by rw [← hrel2, ← hrel3, ← hrel4]
        _ = K1 * (c1 * A + c2 * B + c3 * C + c4 * D) := by ring
    have hK1pos : 0 < K1 := by
      rw [hk1Z]
      have : 4 * M ^ 3 - 6 * M ^ 2 + 4 * M - 1 = 2 * M ^ 2 * (2 * M - 3) + 4 * M - 1 := by ring
      rw [this]
      have : 0 ≤ 2 * M - 3 := by omega
      have : 0 ≤ 2 * M ^ 2 := by nlinarith
      have : 0 ≤ 2 * M ^ 2 * (2 * M - 3) := by nlinarith
      omega
    have hK1ne : K1 ≠ 0 := by linarith
    set q : ℤ := c1 * A + c2 * B + c3 * C + c4 * D
    have hq0 : 0 ≤ q := by
      have : 0 ≤ A := Nat.cast_nonneg a
      have : 0 ≤ K1 * q := by rw [← hAK1]; exact this
      nlinarith
    have hq1 : q ≤ 1 := by
      have : A ≤ K1 := Nat.cast_le.mpr ha
      have : K1 * q ≤ K1 * 1 := by rw [← hAK1]; linarith
      nlinarith

steps.claim: The ratio $q$ cannot be $0$ and must be $1$, which forces $t = T(m)$
steps.explanation: Since $q \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $0 \le q \le 1$, either $q = 0$ or $q = 1$. If $q = 0$, then $A = 0$, which through the proportionality relations and $K_1 \ne 0$ forces $B = C = D = 0$; hence $a = b = c = d = 0$, giving $t = 0$, which contradicts the assumption $t \ne 0$. Thus $q = 1$, which gives $A = K_1$, and canceling $K_1$ from the proportionality relations yields $B = K_2$, $C = K_3$, and $D = K_4$. Translating back to natural numbers gives $a = k_1, b = k_2, c = k_3, d = k_4$, which proves $t = T(m)$.
steps.code:
rcases (show q = 0 ∨ q = 1 by omega) with hq | hq
    · exfalso
      apply ht0
      have hA0 : A = 0 := by rw [hAK1, hq]; ring
      have hB0 : B = 0 := by
        have : B * K1 = 0 := by rw [hrel2, hA0, zero_mul]
        exact mul_eq_zero.mp this |>.resolve_right hK1ne
      have hC0 : C = 0 := by
        have : C * K1 = 0 := by rw [hrel3, hA0, zero_mul]
        exact mul_eq_zero.mp this |>.resolve_right hK1ne
      have hD0 : D = 0 := by
        have : D * K1 = 0 := by rw [hrel4, hA0, zero_mul]
        exact mul_eq_zero.mp this |>.resolve_right hK1ne
      have ha0 : a = 0 := Nat.cast_eq_zero.mp hA0
      have hb0 : b = 0 := Nat.cast_eq_zero.mp hB0
      have hc0 : c = 0 := Nat.cast_eq_zero.mp hC0
      have hd0 : d = 0 := Nat.cast_eq_zero.mp hD0
      rw [hteq, ha0, hb0, hc0, hd0]
      simp
    · have hA1 : A = K1 := by rw [hAK1, hq]; ring
      have hB1 : B = K2 := by
        have : B * K1 = K2 * K1 := by rw [hrel2, hA1, mul_comm]
        exact mul_right_cancel₀ hK1ne this
      have hC1 : C = K3 := by
        have : C * K1 = K3 * K1 := by rw [hrel3, hA1, mul_comm]
        exact mul_right_cancel₀ hK1ne this
      have hD1 : D = K4 := by
        have : D * K1 = K4 * K1 := by rw [hrel4, hA1, mul_comm]
        exact mul_right_cancel₀ hK1ne this
      have ha1 : a = k1 := Nat.cast_inj.mp hA1
      have hb1 : b = k2 := Nat.cast_inj.mp hB1
      have hc1 : c = k3 := Nat.cast_inj.mp hC1
      have hd1 : d = k4 := Nat.cast_inj.mp hD1
      rw [hteq, ha1, hb1, hc1, hd1]

glossary.Nat.cast_sub: For natural numbers $m \le n$, the cast of their difference $(n - m)$ into an additive group with one equals the difference of their casts, $\uparrow n - \uparrow m$.
glossary.congrFun: Equal functions take equal values at the same input: if $f = g$, then $f(a) = g(a)$.
glossary.Multiset.count_add: The multiplicity of an element in a sum of multisets $s + t$ is the sum of its multiplicities in $s$ and in $t$.

declarations.name: davenport_constant_support_four_int_box_three_ge_even
declarations.informal: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2610.16562, even m: for every even m ≥ 2, the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over [[-m,m]]^3 with support of size 4 is at least 16m^3 - 16m^2 + 8m - 1.
declarations.statement:
theorem davenport_constant_support_four_int_box_three_ge_even (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (heven : Even m) :
    ((16 * m ^ 3 - 16 * m ^ 2 + 8 * m - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤
      davenport_constant_support 4 (int_box_three m)
declarations.source:
theorem davenport_constant_support_four_int_box_three_ge_even (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) (heven : Even m) :
    ((16 * m ^ 3 - 16 * m ^ 2 + 8 * m - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤
      davenport_constant_support 4 (int_box_three m) := by
  let s := davenport_box_three_even_sequence m
  have hmem : ((16 * m ^ 3 - 16 * m ^ 2 + 8 * m - 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ∈
      {n | ∃ s : Multiset (Fin 3 → ℤ), (∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ int_box_three m) ∧ multiset_is_minimal_zero_sum s ∧
        s.toFinset.card = 4 ∧ (Multiset.card s : ℕ∞) = n} := by
    refine ⟨s, ?_, davenport_box_three_even_sequence_minimal m hm heven, ?_, ?_⟩
    · intro x hx
      dsimp [davenport_box_three_even_sequence, s] at hx
      simp only [Multiset.mem_add, Multiset.mem_replicate] at hx
      have hmZ : (2 : ℤ) ≤ m := Nat.cast_le.mpr hm
      rcases hx with (((⟨_, rfl⟩ | ⟨_, rfl⟩) | ⟨_, rfl⟩) | ⟨_, rfl⟩)
      · intro i; fin_cases i <;> simp
      · intro i; fin_cases i <;> { simp; try omega }
      · intro i; fin_cases i <;> { simp; try omega }
      · intro i; fin_cases i <;> { simp; try omega }
    · set v1 : Fin 3 → ℤ := ![-(m : ℤ), -m, -m]
      set v2 : Fin 3 → ℤ := ![-(m : ℤ), m - 1, m]
      set v3 : Fin 3 → ℤ := ![(m : ℤ), -(m - 1), m - 1]
      set v4 : Fin 3 → ℤ := ![(m : ℤ) - 1, m, -m]
      have hk1 : 4 * m ^ 3 - 6 * m ^ 2 + 4 * m - 1 ≠ 0 := by
        have : 6 * m ^ 2 ≤ 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
        have : 1 < 4 * m ^ 3 - 6 * m ^ 2 + 4 * m := by
          zify [this]
          nlinarith
        omega
      have hk2 : 4 * m ^ 3 - 4 * m ^ 2 + 2 * m ≠ 0 := by
        have : 4 * m ^ 2 < 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
        omega
      have hk3 : 4 * m ^ 3 - 2 * m ^ 2 + m ≠ 0 := by
        have : 2 * m ^ 2 < 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
        omega
      have hk4 : 4 * m ^ 3 - 4 * m ^ 2 + m ≠ 0 := by
        have : 4 * m ^ 2 < 4 * m ^ 3 := by nlinarith
        omega
      have hS : s =
          Multiset.replicate (4 * m ^ 3 - 6 * m ^ 2 + 4 * m - 1) v1 +
          Multiset.replicate (4 * m ^ 3 - 4 * m ^ 2 + 2 * m) v2 +
          Multiset.replicate (4 * m ^ 3 - 2 * m ^ 2 + m) v3 +
          Multiset.replicate (4 * m ^ 3 - 4 * m ^ 2 + m) v4 := rfl
      rw [hS]
      simp only [Multiset.toFinset_add, Multiset.toFinset_replicate,
        if_neg hk1, if_neg hk2, if_neg hk3, if_neg hk4]
      have heq : ({v1} ∪ {v2} ∪ {v3} ∪ {v4} : Finset (Fin 3 → ℤ)) = {v1, v2, v3, v4} := by
        ext x
        simp
      rw [heq]
      have h12 : v1 ≠ v2 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 1; simp [v1, v2] at this; omega
      have h13 : v1 ≠ v3 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 0; simp [v1, v3] at this; omega
      have h14 : v1 ≠ v4 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 1; simp [v1, v4] at this; omega
      have h23 : v2 ≠ v3 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 0; simp [v2, v3] at this; omega
      have h24 : v2 ≠ v4 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 2; simp [v2, v4] at this; omega
      have h34 : v3 ≠ v4 := by intro h; have := congrFun h 1; simp [v3, v4] at this; omega
      have h3 : v3 ∉ ({v4} : Finset (Fin 3 → ℤ)) := by simp [h34]
      have h2 : v2 ∉ ({v3, v4} : Finset (Fin 3 → ℤ)) := by simp [h23, h24]
      have h1 : v1 ∉ ({v2, v3, v4} : Finset (Fin 3 → ℤ)) := by simp [h12, h13, h14]
      rw [Finset.card_insert_of_notMem h1,
          Finset.card_insert_of_notMem h2,
          Finset.card_insert_of_notMem h3,
          Finset.card_singleton]
    · rw [davenport_box_three_even_sequence_card m hm]
  exact le_sSup hmem

explanation.summary: The proof establishes the lower bound by exhibiting an explicit sequence s (defined as `davenport_box_three_even_sequence m`) of vectors in [[-m, m]]³. The sequence is composed of four distinct vectors with positive multiplicities that sum to 16m³ - 16m² + 8m - 1. With minimality of s supplied by a companion lemma, the proof verifies that each vector is in [[-m, m]]³, that all four multiplicities are non-zero, and that the vectors are pairwise distinct, showing that the support has size 4. Consequently, this length belongs to the set whose supremum defines the Davenport constant, yielding the desired lower bound.

Minimality of s as a zero-sum sequence is supplied by `davenport_box_three_even_sequence_minimal`, leaving three subgoals: showing all elements of s are in [[-m, m]]³, that s has support of size 4, and that the cardinality of s equals 16m³ - 16m² + 8m - 1.

declarations.name: pell_step_iff
declarations.informal: Closed form of the transitions of A_n: q is reachable from p in one step on letter k iff one of five explicit arithmetic conditions holds (letter k congruent to p, p+1 or p+2 mod 5, with the state bounds of the gadget and the two boundary cases where the top of the chain is reached).
declarations.statement:
theorem pell_step_iff (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) {p q : Fin n} {k : Fin 5} :
    q ∈ (pell_nfa n).step p k ↔
      (k.val = p.val % 5 ∧ 1 ≤ p.val ∧ p.val + 2 ≤ n ∧ (q.val = p.val ∨ q.val = p.val + 1)) ∨
      (k.val = p.val % 5 ∧ p.val + 1 = n ∧ q.val = p.val) ∨
      (k.val = (p.val + 1) % 5 ∧ p.val + 3 ≤ n ∧ (q.val = p.val ∨ q.val = p.val + 2)) ∨
      (k.val = (p.val + 1) % 5 ∧ p.val + 2 = n ∧ q.val = p.val) ∨
      (k.val = (p.val + 2) % 5 ∧ p.val + 3 ≤ n ∧ (q.val = p.val + 1 ∨ q.val = p.val + 2))
declarations.source:
/-- Explicit closed form of the transition relation of the Pell automaton. -/
theorem pell_step_iff (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) {p q : Fin n} {k : Fin 5} :
    q ∈ (pell_nfa n).step p k ↔
      (k.val = p.val % 5 ∧ 1 ≤ p.val ∧ p.val + 2 ≤ n ∧ (q.val = p.val ∨ q.val = p.val + 1)) ∨
      (k.val = p.val % 5 ∧ p.val + 1 = n ∧ q.val = p.val) ∨
      (k.val = (p.val + 1) % 5 ∧ p.val + 3 ≤ n ∧ (q.val = p.val ∨ q.val = p.val + 2)) ∨
      (k.val = (p.val + 1) % 5 ∧ p.val + 2 = n ∧ q.val = p.val) ∨
      (k.val = (p.val + 2) % 5 ∧ p.val + 3 ≤ n ∧ (q.val = p.val + 1 ∨ q.val = p.val + 2)) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    simp only [pell_nfa] at h
    obtain ⟨i, hi1, hi2, h⟩ := h
    rcases h with ⟨hk, hpq⟩ | ⟨hk, hpq⟩
    · rcases hpq with ⟨hp, hq⟩ | ⟨hp, hq⟩
      · right; right; left
        exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by rcases hq with h | h <;> omega⟩
      · left
        exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by omega, by rcases hq with h | h <;> omega⟩
    · rcases hpq with ⟨hp, hq⟩ | ⟨hp, hq⟩ | ⟨hp, hq⟩
      · by_cases hb : p.val + 2 = n
        · right; right; right; left
          exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by omega⟩
        · right; right; left
          exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by omega⟩
      · by_cases hb : p.val + 1 = n
        · right; left
          exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by omega⟩
        · left
          exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by omega, by omega⟩
      · right; right; right; right
        exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by rcases hq with h | h <;> omega⟩
  · intro h
    simp only [pell_nfa]
    rcases h with ⟨hk, hp1, hp2, hq⟩ | ⟨hk, hpn, hq⟩ | ⟨hk, hp3, hq⟩ | ⟨hk, hpn2, hq⟩ | ⟨hk, hp3', hq⟩
    · refine ⟨p.val, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
      left
      refine ⟨by omega, Or.inr ⟨by omega, ?_⟩⟩
      rcases hq with h | h <;> omega
    · refine ⟨n - 2, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
      right
      refine ⟨by omega, Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨by omega, by omega⟩)⟩
    · refine ⟨p.val + 1, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
      left
      refine ⟨by omega, Or.inl ⟨by omega, ?_⟩⟩
      rcases hq with h | h <;> omega
    · refine ⟨p.val, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
      right
      refine ⟨by omega, Or.inl ⟨by omega, by omega⟩⟩
    · refine ⟨p.val + 1, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
      right
      refine ⟨by omega, Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨by omega, ?_⟩)⟩
      rcases hq with h | h <;> omega

explanation.summary: The proof establishes the logical equivalence by demonstrating both directions separately. For the forward direction (⇒), it unfolds the definition of `pell_nfa`, extracts the existential gadget index `i`, and analyzes the resulting cases on `p`, `q`, and `k`, distinguishing the internal transitions from the top-boundary transitions where `p + 1 = n` or `p + 2 = n`. For the backward direction (⇐), it inspects each of the five disjunctive arithmetic conditions and provides an explicit gadget index witness—either `i = p`, `i = p + 1`, or `i = n - 2`—verifying in each case that the transition relation's range constraints and congruences are satisfied via linear integer arithmetic (`omega`).

steps.claim: In the forward direction, assuming `q` is reachable from `p` on letter `k` yields a gadget index `i` with `1 ≤ i ≤ n - 2`, reducing the goal to the two cases `k ≡ i mod 5` and `k ≡ i + 1 mod 5`.
steps.explanation: We split the bi-implication into forward and backward directions with `constructor`. For the forward direction, assuming `q ∈ step p k`, we unfold the definition of `pell_nfa` to extract a gadget index `i` satisfying `1 ≤ i` and `i + 2 ≤ n`, and split into cases based on whether `k.val = i % 5` or `k.val = (i + 1) % 5`.
steps.code:
constructor
  · intro h
    simp only [pell_nfa] at h
    obtain ⟨i, hi1, hi2, h⟩ := h
    rcases h with ⟨hk, hpq⟩ | ⟨hk, hpq⟩

steps.claim: When `k ≡ i mod 5`, either condition 3 holds (if `p = i - 1`) or condition 1 holds (if `p = i`).
steps.explanation: From the first branch of the automaton definition, either `p = i - 1` and `q ∈ {i - 1, i + 1}`, or `p = i` and `q ∈ {i, i + 1}`. In the first subcase, `k ≡ p + 1 mod 5`, `p + 3 ≤ n`, and `q ∈ {p, p + 2}`, which matches condition 3. In the second subcase, `k ≡ p mod 5`, `1 ≤ p`, `p + 2 ≤ n`, and `q ∈ {p, p + 1}`, which matches condition 1. Linear arithmetic (`omega`) verifies the bounds and equalities in each branch.
steps.code:
· rcases hpq with ⟨hp, hq⟩ | ⟨hp, hq⟩
      · right; right; left
        exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by rcases hq with h | h <;> omega⟩
      · left
        exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by omega, by rcases hq with h | h <;> omega⟩

steps.claim: When `k ≡ i + 1 mod 5`, depending on `p` and boundary conditions, one of the five conditions holds, completing the forward direction.
steps.explanation:
The second branch of the automaton definition gives three subcases:
- If `p = i` and `q = i`, we branch on whether `p + 2 = n`. If it is, condition 4 holds (`k ≡ p + 1 mod 5`, `p + 2 = n`, `q = p`); otherwise `p + 3 ≤ n`, which satisfies condition 3.
- If `p = i + 1` and `q = i + 1`, we branch on whether `p + 1 = n`. If it is, condition 2 holds (`k ≡ p mod 5`, `p + 1 = n`, `q = p`); otherwise `p + 2 ≤ n` and `1 ≤ p`, satisfying condition 1.
- If `p = i - 1` and `q ∈ {i, i + 1}`, then `k ≡ p + 2 mod 5`, `p + 3 ≤ n`, and `q ∈ {p + 1, p + 2}`, satisfying condition 5.
All arithmetic constraints are verified by `omega`.

      · by_cases hb : p.val + 2 = n

          exact ⟨by omega, by omega, by omega⟩
        · right; right; left

      · by_cases hb : p.val + 1 = n
        · right; left

        · left

steps.explanation: For the converse implication, we assume one of the five explicit arithmetic conditions holds and unfold `pell_nfa`. The goal is to provide a gadget index `i` with `1 ≤ i ≤ n - 2` witnessing that `q ∈ step p k`. We split the hypothesis into its five disjunctive cases.

We select the first branch of the automaton transition (`k ≡ i mod 5`) and its second sub-branch (`p = i` and `q ∈ {i, i + 1}`) using `Or.inr`. Linear arithmetic (`omega`) closes all side conditions.

      left
      refine ⟨by omega, Or.inr ⟨by omega, ?_⟩⟩
      rcases hq with h | h <;> omega

steps.explanation: Condition 2 corresponds to the top-boundary state where `p + 1 = n`, `q = p`, and `k ≡ p mod 5`. Since `3 ≤ n`, setting `i = n - 2` yields `1 ≤ i` and `i + 2 ≤ n`. Then `p = i + 1` and `k ≡ i + 1 mod 5`. We select the second branch of the automaton (`k ≡ i + 1 mod 5`) and navigate to the middle sub-branch (`p = i + 1 ∧ q = i + 1`) via `Or.inr (Or.inl ...)`, with `omega` checking the arithmetic.

      right

steps.explanation: Condition 3 specifies `p + 3 ≤ n`, `k ≡ p + 1 mod 5`, and `q ∈ {p, p + 2}`. Setting `i = p + 1` guarantees `1 ≤ i` and `i + 2 ≤ n`. Then `k ≡ i mod 5`, `p = i - 1`, and `q ∈ {i - 1, i + 1}`. We choose the first branch (`k ≡ i mod 5`) and select the first sub-branch using `Or.inl`, completed by `omega`.

      refine ⟨by omega, Or.inl ⟨by omega, ?_⟩⟩

steps.explanation: Condition 4 is the boundary case where `p + 2 = n`, `q = p`, and `k ≡ p + 1 mod 5`. Since `3 ≤ n`, `p ≥ 1`. Setting `i = p` gives `1 ≤ i ≤ n - 2`, with `k ≡ i + 1 mod 5` and `p = q = i`. We select the second branch (`k ≡ i + 1 mod 5`) and its first sub-branch via `Or.inl`, closed by `omega`.

      right

Then `k ≡ i + 1 mod 5`, `p = i - 1`, and `q ∈ {i, i + 1}`. We select the second branch (`k ≡ i + 1 mod 5`) and navigate to the third sub-branch via nested `Or.inr`, with all checks completed by `omega`.

      right

declarations.name: nfa_run_count_list_nil
declarations.informal: There is exactly one empty run from p to q if p = q and none otherwise.
declarations.statement:
open Classical in
theorem nfa_run_count_list_nil {α σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] (M : NFA α σ) (p q : σ) :
    nfa_run_count_list M [] p q = if p = q then 1 else 0
declarations.source:
open Classical in
/-- There is exactly one run of the empty word from p to q, namely when p = q. -/
theorem nfa_run_count_list_nil {α σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] (M : NFA α σ) (p q : σ) :
    nfa_run_count_list M [] p q = if p = q then 1 else 0 := by
  unfold nfa_run_count_list
  simp only [List.length_nil, Fin.last_zero, IsEmpty.forall_iff, and_true]
  split_ifs with h
  · subst h
    have : {r : Fin 1 → σ | r 0 = p ∧ r 0 = p} = {fun _ => p} := by
      ext r
      simp only [and_self, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
      constructor
      · intro hr
        ext i
        fin_cases i
        exact hr
      · rintro rfl
        rfl
    rw [this, Set.ncard_singleton]
  · have : {r : Fin 1 → σ | r 0 = p ∧ r 0 = q} = ∅ := by
      ext r
      simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
      rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      exact h (h1.symm.trans h2)
    rw [this, Set.ncard_empty]

explanation.summary: The proof unfolds the definition of run count for the empty word, where a run is a function from Fin 1 to the state space σ. Because the empty list has length 0, the step conditions hold vacuously, leaving only the boundary requirements that the initial and final state (both r(0)) equal p and q respectively. A case split on p = q then concludes: if p = q, the unique run is the constant function at p (giving cardinality 1), and if p ≠ q, the requirements r(0) = p and r(0) = q are contradictory (giving the empty set of cardinality 0).

steps.claim: The count of runs for the empty word reduces to the cardinality of the set of functions r : Fin 1 → σ satisfying r(0) = p and r(0) = q.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of `nfa_run_count_list` for the empty word w = [], the domain of a run is Fin (|w| + 1) = Fin 1, since the empty list has length 0 (`List.length_nil`). The step conditions quantify over Fin 0, which is empty, so they are vacuously satisfied (`IsEmpty.forall_iff`, `and_true`). With `Fin.last 0 = 0` (`Fin.last_zero`), the endpoint condition r(last) = q reduces to r(0) = q, leaving the condition r(0) = p ∧ r(0) = q.
steps.code:
unfold nfa_run_count_list
  simp only [List.length_nil, Fin.last_zero, IsEmpty.forall_iff, and_true]

steps.claim: It suffices to evaluate the cardinality separately for p = q and p ≠ q.
steps.explanation: We split into the two branches of the `if p = q then 1 else 0` expression: assuming p = q (where the target count is 1) and assuming p ≠ q (where the target count is 0).
steps.code: split_ifs with h

steps.claim: When p = q, the set of runs consists solely of the constant function at p, so its cardinality is 1.
steps.explanation: Substituting q = p (`subst h`), the condition on a run r becomes r(0) = p ∧ r(0) = p, which simplifies to r(0) = p (`and_self`). Since Fin 1 contains only the single element 0, any function r with r(0) = p is identical to the constant function x ↦ p. Thus the set of runs is the singleton {x ↦ p} (`Set.mem_singleton_iff`), whose cardinality is 1 (`Set.ncard_singleton`).
steps.code:
· subst h
    have : {r : Fin 1 → σ | r 0 = p ∧ r 0 = p} = {fun _ => p} := by
      ext r
      simp only [and_self, Set.mem_singleton_iff]
      constructor
      · intro hr
        ext i
        fin_cases i
        exact hr
      · rintro rfl
        rfl
    rw [this, Set.ncard_singleton]

steps.claim: When p ≠ q, the set of runs is empty, so its cardinality is 0.
steps.explanation: If there were a run r : Fin 1 → σ, it would satisfy both r(0) = p and r(0) = q, which by symmetry and transitivity would imply p = q. This contradicts the assumption p ≠ q (`Set.mem_empty_iff_false`, `iff_false`). Hence no such run exists, the set of runs is empty, and its cardinality is 0 (`Set.ncard_empty`).
steps.code:
· have : {r : Fin 1 → σ | r 0 = p ∧ r 0 = q} = ∅ := by
      ext r
      simp only [Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
      rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
      exact h (h1.symm.trans h2)
    rw [this, Set.ncard_empty]

glossary.Fin.last_zero: The last element of Fin 1 (indexed by 0) is 0.
glossary.IsEmpty.forall_iff: A universal quantification over an empty type is vacuously true.
glossary.and_true: Conjoining a proposition with True is equivalent to the proposition itself.
glossary.and_self: Conjoining a proposition with itself is equivalent to the proposition.
glossary.Set.mem_singleton_iff: An element belongs to a singleton set if and only if it equals the member of that set.
glossary.Set.ncard_singleton: The cardinality of a singleton set is 1.
glossary.iff_false: An equivalence between a proposition and False is equivalent to the negation of the proposition.
glossary.Set.mem_empty_iff_false: Belonging to the empty set is false for any element.
glossary.Set.ncard_empty: The cardinality of the empty set is 0.

caveats: Formalizing that a function from Fin 1 to σ is uniquely determined by its value at 0 requires function extensionality followed by finite case exhaustion (`fin_cases i`), whereas on paper this identification is immediate.

declarations.name: pell_word_eq_prefix
declarations.informal: The word u_n is the prefix v_(n-2) of the block-by-block sequence.
declarations.statement: theorem pell_word_eq_prefix (n : ℕ) : pell_word n = pell_word_prefix (n - 2)
declarations.source:
lemma pell_word_eq_prefix_aux (j : ℕ) :
    pell_word_prefix j = ((List.range j).map (· + 1)).flatMap (fun i =>
      [⟨i % 5, Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)⟩, ⟨(i + 1) % 5, Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)⟩]) := by
  induction j with
  | zero =>
    rfl
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [pell_word_prefix, ih]
    rw [List.range_succ, List.map_append, List.flatMap_append]
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.flatMap_singleton]

/-- pell_word n is the j-fold block prefix with j = n - 2. -/
theorem pell_word_eq_prefix (n : ℕ) : pell_word n = pell_word_prefix (n - 2) := by
  rw [pell_word, pell_word_eq_prefix_aux]

explanation.summary: The theorem establishes that the nth Pell word pell_word n coincides with the block-by-block prefix pell_word_prefix (n - 2). The proof proceeds via an auxiliary lemma showing by induction on j that pell_word_prefix j is equal to the flatMap construction over range j. The base case holds by definition, and the inductive step follows by splitting range (j + 1) into range j ++ [j] and distributing map and flatMap.

steps.claim: 5 is positive, ensuring modulo 5 arithmetic produces valid indices in Fin 5.
steps.explanation: The bound 0 < 5 is checked by direct arithmetic evaluation.
steps.code:
lemma pell_word_eq_prefix_aux (j : ℕ) :
    pell_word_prefix j = ((List.range j).map (· + 1)).flatMap (fun i =>
      [⟨i % 5, Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)⟩, ⟨(i + 1) % 5, Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)⟩]) := by

steps.claim: pell_word_prefix 0 equals the flat-mapped range of length 0.
steps.explanation: By induction on j. In the base case j = 0, both sides evaluate to the empty list by definition.
steps.code:
induction j with
  | zero =>
    rfl

steps.claim: pell_word_prefix (j + 1) expands to pell_word_prefix j ++ [(j + 1) % 5, (j + 2) % 5], matching the induction hypothesis.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the recursive definition of pell_word_prefix and rewriting with the induction hypothesis replaces the left-hand side with the flat-mapped range j followed by the two new symbols.
steps.code:
| succ j ih =>
    rw [pell_word_prefix, ih]

steps.claim: The right-hand side over range (j + 1) decomposes into the expression over range j followed by the operation on the singleton [j].
steps.explanation: We split range (j + 1) into range j ++ [j] using List.range_succ, and then distribute map and flatMap across the list concatenation.
steps.code: rw [List.range_succ, List.map_append, List.flatMap_append]

steps.claim: Evaluating map and flatMap on the singleton [j] gives the pair [(j + 1) % 5, (j + 2) % 5], completing the inductive step.
steps.explanation: Simplifying the mapping of (· + 1) over [j] yields [j + 1], and flatMap on this singleton evaluates directly to the two-element block [⟨(j + 1) % 5, _⟩, ⟨(j + 2) % 5, _⟩], matching the left-hand side.
steps.code: simp only [List.map_cons, List.map_nil, List.flatMap_singleton]

steps.claim: pell_word n = pell_word_prefix (n - 2).
steps.explanation: Unfolding pell_word n into its flatMap definition and applying the auxiliary lemma with j = n - 2 finishes the proof.
steps.code:
/-- pell_word n is the j-fold block prefix with j = n - 2. -/
theorem pell_word_eq_prefix (n : ℕ) : pell_word n = pell_word_prefix (n - 2) := by
  rw [pell_word, pell_word_eq_prefix_aux]

glossary.List.range: The list of natural numbers [0, ..., n - 1].
glossary.List.map: Applying a function to every element of a list.
glossary.List.flatMap: Mapping a function returning lists over a list and concatenating the results.
glossary.Nat.mod_lt: If y > 0, then x % y < y.
glossary.List.map_cons: map over a non-empty list applies f to the head and recurses on the tail.
glossary.List.map_nil: map over an empty list is empty.
glossary.List.flatMap_singleton: flatMap of f over a singleton list [x] is f x.
glossary.pell_word_prefix: Definition of the prefix sequence by appending blocks of length 2.
glossary.pell_word: Definition of pell_word via flatMap over range (n - 2) shifted by 1.
glossary.pell_word_eq_prefix_aux: pell_word_prefix j equals the flatMap construction over range j shifted by 1.

declarations.name: pell_word_length
declarations.informal: The word u_n = c_1c_2…c_(n-2)c_(n-1) has length 2(n-2).
declarations.statement: theorem pell_word_length (n : ℕ) : (pell_word n).length = 2 * (n - 2)
declarations.source:
/-- The word u_n has length 2(n-2). -/
theorem pell_word_length (n : ℕ) : (pell_word n).length = 2 * (n - 2) := by
  rw [pell_word_eq_prefix]
  generalize n - 2 = j
  induction j with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ j ih =>
    simp [pell_word_prefix, ih]
    omega

explanation.summary: The theorem is proved by first rewriting pell_word n as pell_word_prefix (n - 2) and generalizing n - 2 to an arbitrary natural number j. The generalized statement that pell_word_prefix j has length 2j is then established by induction on j, where the base case is the empty list and the inductive step adds two elements to the length at each step.

steps.claim: It suffices to show that (pell_word_prefix j).length = 2 * j for any natural number j.
steps.explanation: Rewriting with pell_word_eq_prefix replaces pell_word n with pell_word_prefix (n - 2). Generalizing n - 2 to an arbitrary natural number j reduces the theorem to showing that the prefix of parameter j has length 2j.
steps.code:
rw [pell_word_eq_prefix]
  generalize n - 2 = j

steps.claim: The base case holds: (pell_word_prefix 0).length = 2 * 0.
steps.explanation: We proceed by induction on j. In the base case j = 0, pell_word_prefix 0 is defined as the empty list, whose length is 0, which equals 2 * 0 by definition.
steps.code:
induction j with
  | zero => rfl

steps.claim: The inductive step holds: if pell_word_prefix j has length 2 * j, then pell_word_prefix (j + 1) has length 2 * (j + 1).
steps.explanation: By the recursive definition of pell_word_prefix, pell_word_prefix (j + 1) is formed by appending two elements to pell_word_prefix j. Simplifying with this definition and the induction hypothesis gives length 2 * j + 2, and linear arithmetic (omega) verifies that 2 * j + 2 = 2 * (j + 1).
steps.code:
| succ j ih =>
    simp [pell_word_prefix, ih]
    omega

glossary.pell_word_eq_prefix: for any natural number n, the Pell word pell_word n equals pell_word_prefix (n - 2)
glossary.pell_word_prefix: the recursive prefix function mapping 0 to the empty list and each successor i + 1 to pell_word_prefix i concatenated with two elements

declarations.name: pell_word_get
declarations.informal: The j-th letter of u_n is c_(j/2+1) if j is even and c_(j/2+2) if j is odd.
declarations.statement:
theorem pell_word_get (n j : ℕ) (hj : j < (pell_word n).length) :
    ((pell_word n).get ⟨j, hj⟩).val = (j / 2 + 1 + j % 2) % 5
declarations.source:
lemma pell_word_get_list_two_zero {α : Type} (a b : α) (i : ℕ) (hi : i = 0) (h : i < [a, b].length) :
    [a, b][i]'h = a := by
  subst hi
  rfl

lemma pell_word_get_list_two_one {α : Type} (a b : α) (i : ℕ) (hi : i = 1) (h : i < [a, b].length) :
    [a, b][i]'h = b := by
  subst hi
  rfl

lemma pell_word_get_prefix_length (j : ℕ) : (pell_word_prefix j).length = 2 * j := by
  induction j with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ j ih =>
    simp [pell_word_prefix, ih]
    omega

lemma pell_word_get_prefix_get (j i : ℕ) (hi : i < (pell_word_prefix j).length) :
    ((pell_word_prefix j)[i]'hi).val = (i / 2 + 1 + i % 2) % 5 := by
  induction j generalizing i with
  | zero =>
    rw [pell_word_get_prefix_length] at hi
    omega
  | succ j ih =>
    have hj_len : (pell_word_prefix j).length = 2 * j := pell_word_get_prefix_length j
    dsimp only [pell_word_prefix] at hi ⊢
    by_cases h : i < (pell_word_prefix j).length
    · rw [List.getElem_append_left h]
      exact ih i h
    · rw [List.getElem_append_right (by omega)]
      have hi2 : i < 2 * j + 2 := by
        revert hi
        simp only [List.length_append, List.length_cons, List.length_nil, hj_len]
        omega
      have : i = 2 * j ∨ i = 2 * j + 1 := by omega
      rcases this with rfl | rfl
      · rw [pell_word_get_list_two_zero _ _ _ (by omega)]
        have h1 : (2 * j) / 2 = j := by omega
        have h2 : (2 * j) % 2 = 0 := by omega
        rw [h1, h2]
      · rw [pell_word_get_list_two_one _ _ _ (by omega)]
        have h1 : (2 * j + 1) / 2 = j := by omega
        have h2 : (2 * j + 1) % 2 = 1 := by omega
        rw [h1, h2]

/-- The j-th letter of u_n is c_(j/2+1) for j even and c_(j/2+2) for j odd, i.e. of residue (j/2+1+j%2) mod 5. -/
theorem pell_word_get (n j : ℕ) (hj : j < (pell_word n).length) :
    ((pell_word n).get ⟨j, hj⟩).val = (j / 2 + 1 + j % 2) % 5 := by
  have hp : pell_word n = pell_word_prefix (n - 2) := pell_word_eq_prefix n
  revert hj
  rw [hp]
  intro hj
  rw [List.get_eq_getElem]
  exact pell_word_get_prefix_get (n - 2) j hj

explanation.summary: The character formula for the Pell word is established by proving it first for the recursive prefix construction `pell_word_prefix j` by induction on `j`. At each step, two characters with residues `(j + 1) mod 5` and `(j + 2) mod 5` are appended at indices `2j` and `2j + 1`, which precisely match the formula `(i / 2 + 1 + i % 2) mod 5` for both even and odd indices. The main theorem then follows immediately because `pell_word n` is definitionally equal to `pell_word_prefix (n - 2)`.

steps.claim: The element at index 0 of a two-element list [a, b] is a.
steps.explanation: Substituting the hypothesis that the index is 0 reduces the lookup to `[a, b][0]`, which evaluates to `a` definitionally.
steps.code:
subst hi
  rfl

steps.claim: The element at index 1 of a two-element list [a, b] is b.
steps.explanation: Substituting the hypothesis that the index is 1 reduces the lookup to `[a, b][1]`, which evaluates to `b` definitionally.
steps.code:
subst hi
  rfl

steps.claim: For every natural number j, the length of `pell_word_prefix j` is 2 * j.
steps.explanation: We argue by induction on `j`. The base case `j = 0` holds definitionally since `pell_word_prefix 0` is empty. In the inductive step, `pell_word_prefix (j + 1)` appends a two-element block to `pell_word_prefix j`; simplifying with the induction hypothesis gives length `2 * j + 2`, which linear arithmetic simplifies to `2 * (j + 1)`.
steps.code:
induction j with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ j ih =>
    simp [pell_word_prefix, ih]
    omega

steps.claim: In the base case j = 0, no valid index into `pell_word_prefix 0` exists.
steps.explanation: We proceed by induction on `j`, generalizing the index `i`. For `j = 0`, rewriting the bound `i < (pell_word_prefix 0).length` using `pell_word_get_prefix_length` yields `i < 2 * 0 = 0`, an immediate contradiction by linear arithmetic.
steps.code:
induction j generalizing i with
  | zero =>
    rw [pell_word_get_prefix_length] at hi
    omega

steps.claim: For indices i < (pell_word_prefix j).length, the character at index i in `pell_word_prefix (j + 1)` is determined by the induction hypothesis.
steps.explanation: In the induction step, `pell_word_prefix (j + 1)` unfolds to `pell_word_prefix j` concatenated with the two-element block `[⟨(j + 1) % 5, _⟩, ⟨(j + 2) % 5, _⟩]`. We branch on whether `i < (pell_word_prefix j).length`. When this holds, `List.getElem_append_left` shows that indexing into the concatenation retrieves the `i`-th element of `pell_word_prefix j`, to which the induction hypothesis applies directly.
steps.code:
have hj_len : (pell_word_prefix j).length = 2 * j := pell_word_get_prefix_length j
    dsimp only [pell_word_prefix] at hi ⊢
    by_cases h : i < (pell_word_prefix j).length
    · rw [List.getElem_append_left h]
      exact ih i h

steps.claim: For indices i ≥ (pell_word_prefix j).length, the lookup shifts into the appended block and i is restricted to 2 * j or 2 * j + 1.
steps.explanation: When `i ≥ (pell_word_prefix j).length`, `List.getElem_append_right` shifts the index to `i - (pell_word_prefix j).length` within the appended two-element list. Simplifying the full list length using `List.length_append`, `List.length_cons`, `List.length_nil`, and the known prefix length `2 * j` proves `i < 2 * j + 2`. Together with `i ≥ 2 * j`, linear arithmetic leaves only two possibilities: `i = 2 * j` or `i = 2 * j + 1`.
steps.code:
· rw [List.getElem_append_right (by omega)]
      have hi2 : i < 2 * j + 2 := by
        revert hi
        simp only [List.length_append, List.length_cons, List.length_nil, hj_len]
        omega
      have : i = 2 * j ∨ i = 2 * j + 1 := by omega
      rcases this with rfl | rfl

steps.claim: When i = 2 * j, the character value in `pell_word_prefix (j + 1)` is (i / 2 + 1 + i % 2) % 5.
steps.explanation: At `i = 2 * j`, the shifted index in the appended block is `2 * j - 2 * j = 0`. By `pell_word_get_list_two_zero`, this lookup yields the first appended element `⟨(j + 1) % 5, _⟩`. Since `(2 * j) / 2 = j` and `(2 * j) % 2 = 0`, the target formula evaluates to `(j + 1 + 0) % 5 = (j + 1) % 5`, matching the character's value.
steps.code:
· rw [pell_word_get_list_two_zero _ _ _ (by omega)]
        have h1 : (2 * j) / 2 = j := by omega
        have h2 : (2 * j) % 2 = 0 := by omega
        rw [h1, h2]

steps.claim: When i = 2 * j + 1, the character value in `pell_word_prefix (j + 1)` is (i / 2 + 1 + i % 2) % 5.
steps.explanation: At `i = 2 * j + 1`, the shifted index in the appended block is `(2 * j + 1) - 2 * j = 1`. By `pell_word_get_list_two_one`, this lookup yields the second appended element `⟨(j + 2) % 5, _⟩`. Since `(2 * j + 1) / 2 = j` and `(2 * j + 1) % 2 = 1`, the formula evaluates to `(j + 1 + 1) % 5 = (j + 2) % 5`, matching the character's value.
steps.code:
· rw [pell_word_get_list_two_one _ _ _ (by omega)]
        have h1 : (2 * j + 1) / 2 = j := by omega
        have h2 : (2 * j + 1) % 2 = 1 := by omega
        rw [h1, h2]

steps.claim: The j-th letter of `pell_word n` has value (j / 2 + 1 + j % 2) % 5.
steps.explanation: Using `pell_word_eq_prefix`, we rewrite `pell_word n` into `pell_word_prefix (n - 2)`. After rewriting `List.get` to `List.getElem` via `List.get_eq_getElem`, the result follows directly from the prefix evaluation lemma `pell_word_get_prefix_get`.
steps.code:
have hp : pell_word n = pell_word_prefix (n - 2) := pell_word_eq_prefix n
  revert hj
  rw [hp]
  intro hj
  rw [List.get_eq_getElem]
  exact pell_word_get_prefix_get (n - 2) j hj

glossary.pell_word_get_list_two_zero: In a two-element list `[a, b]`, the element at index 0 is `a`.
glossary.pell_word_get_list_two_one: In a two-element list `[a, b]`, the element at index 1 is `b`.
glossary.pell_word_get_prefix_length: For any natural number `j`, the length of the prefix word `pell_word_prefix j` is `2 * j`.
glossary.List.getElem_append_left: Accessing an element at index `i` in a concatenated list `as ++ bs`, where `i < as.length`, yields `as[i]`.
glossary.List.getElem_append_right: Accessing an element at index `i` in a concatenated list `as ++ bs`, where `i ≥ as.length`, yields `bs[i - as.length]`.
glossary.List.length_append: The length of the concatenation of two lists `as ++ bs` is the sum of their lengths, `as.length + bs.length`.
glossary.List.length_cons: Prepending an element to a list increases its length by 1.
glossary.pell_word_eq_prefix: The `n`-th Pell word `pell_word n` is equal to `pell_word_prefix (n - 2)`.
glossary.List.get_eq_getElem: Retrieving an element via `List.get` with a bounded index `Fin l.length` is equal to array indexing `l[i]`.
glossary.pell_word_get_prefix_get: The value of the `i`-th character of `pell_word_prefix j` is `(i / 2 + 1 + i % 2) % 5`.

caveats: The character formula `(j / 2 + 1 + j % 2) % 5` unifies both cases: when `j` is even (`j % 2 = 0`), it yields `(j / 2 + 1) % 5`, and when `j` is odd (`j % 2 = 1`), it yields `(j / 2 + 2) % 5`.
The full word `pell_word n` is identified with the prefix `pell_word_prefix (n - 2)`, which reduces character lookups in the infinite family to the inductive prefix construction.

declarations.name: pell_run_encard_eq_count
declarations.informal: The set of accepting runs of u_n in A_n has encard equal to the number of runs from q_1 to q_n.
declarations.statement:
open Classical in
theorem pell_run_encard_eq_count (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    Set.encard {r : Fin ((pell_word n).length + 1) → Fin n |
        r 0 ∈ (pell_nfa n).start ∧
        r (Fin.last (pell_word n).length) ∈ (pell_nfa n).accept ∧
        ∀ i : Fin (pell_word n).length,
          r i.succ ∈ (pell_nfa n).step (r i.castSucc) ((pell_word n).get i)}
      = (nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word n) ⟨0, by omega⟩ ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ : ℕ∞)
declarations.source:
open Classical in
/-- The set of accepting runs of u_n in A_n has the same cardinality as the run count from q_1 to q_n. -/
theorem pell_run_encard_eq_count (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    Set.encard {r : Fin ((pell_word n).length + 1) → Fin n |
        r 0 ∈ (pell_nfa n).start ∧
        r (Fin.last (pell_word n).length) ∈ (pell_nfa n).accept ∧
        ∀ i : Fin (pell_word n).length,
          r i.succ ∈ (pell_nfa n).step (r i.castSucc) ((pell_word n).get i)}
      = (nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word n) ⟨0, by omega⟩ ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ : ℕ∞) := by
  have hset : {r : Fin ((pell_word n).length + 1) → Fin n |
        r 0 ∈ (pell_nfa n).start ∧
        r (Fin.last (pell_word n).length) ∈ (pell_nfa n).accept ∧
        ∀ i : Fin (pell_word n).length,
          r i.succ ∈ (pell_nfa n).step (r i.castSucc) ((pell_word n).get i)}
      = {r : Fin ((pell_word n).length + 1) → Fin n |
        r 0 = ⟨0, by omega⟩ ∧
        r (Fin.last (pell_word n).length) = ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ ∧
        ∀ i : Fin (pell_word n).length,
          r i.succ ∈ (pell_nfa n).step (r i.castSucc) ((pell_word n).get i)} := by
    ext r
    simp only [pell_nfa, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, h3⟩
      · rw [Fin.ext_iff]; exact h1
      · rw [Fin.ext_iff]; simp only [Fin.val_mk]; omega
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, h3⟩
      · rw [h1]
      · rw [h2]; simp only [Fin.val_mk]; omega
  rw [hset]
  rw [Set.encard_eq_coe_toFinset_card]
  unfold nfa_run_count_list
  rw [Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card']

explanation.summary: The theorem shows that the extended cardinality of accepting runs of the Pell word in the Pell automaton equals the run count from state 0 to state n - 1. The proof first characterizes the set of accepting runs as the set of runs starting at state 0 and ending at state n - 1, since the automaton's start and accept sets are singletons containing 0 and n - 1, respectively. Finally, rewriting along this set equality and unfolding the definition of the run count expresses both sides as the cardinality of the underlying finite set of runs in ℕ∞.

steps.claim: The initial state 0 and target state n - 1 are well-defined elements of Fin n.
steps.explanation: The theorem statement uses the states ⟨0, ·⟩ and ⟨n - 1, ·⟩ in Fin n. Under the assumption 3 ≤ n, linear arithmetic (`omega`) verifies 0 < n and n - 1 < n, ensuring both state expressions are well-typed.
steps.code: = (nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word n) ⟨0, by omega⟩ ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ : ℕ∞) := by

steps.claim: The set of accepting runs of pell_word n in pell_nfa n is identical to the set of runs from state 0 to state n - 1.
steps.explanation: We establish the auxiliary equality `hset` by set extensionality (`ext r`). Unfolding the definition of `pell_nfa`, a run is accepting if its initial state has value 0 and its final state has value satisfying `q.val + 1 = n`. Since states belong to `Fin n`, equality of elements is equivalent to equality of their values via `Fin.ext_iff`. For any accepting run, the initial state must be ⟨0, ·⟩ and, since `q.val + 1 = n`, the final state must be ⟨n - 1, ·⟩ by linear arithmetic. Conversely, any run starting at ⟨0, ·⟩ and ending at ⟨n - 1, ·⟩ satisfies the start condition (0 = 0) and the accept condition ((n - 1) + 1 = n). The step conditions are identical on both sides.
steps.code:
have hset : {r : Fin ((pell_word n).length + 1) → Fin n |
        r 0 ∈ (pell_nfa n).start ∧
        r (Fin.last (pell_word n).length) ∈ (pell_nfa n).accept ∧
        ∀ i : Fin (pell_word n).length,
          r i.succ ∈ (pell_nfa n).step (r i.castSucc) ((pell_word n).get i)}
      = {r : Fin ((pell_word n).length + 1) → Fin n |
        r 0 = ⟨0, by omega⟩ ∧
        r (Fin.last (pell_word n).length) = ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩ ∧
        ∀ i : Fin (pell_word n).length,
          r i.succ ∈ (pell_nfa n).step (r i.castSucc) ((pell_word n).get i)} := by
    ext r
    simp only [pell_nfa, Set.mem_setOf_eq]
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, h3⟩
      · rw [Fin.ext_iff]; exact h1
      · rw [Fin.ext_iff]; simp only [Fin.val_mk]; omega
    · rintro ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩
      refine ⟨?_, ?_, h3⟩
      · rw [h1]
      · rw [h2]; simp only [Fin.val_mk]; omega

steps.claim: The extended cardinality of the set of accepting runs equals the run count from state 0 to state n - 1 in ℕ∞.
steps.explanation: Rewriting with the set equality `hset`, the accepting runs are replaced by runs from 0 to n - 1. By `Set.encard_eq_coe_toFinset_card`, the extended cardinality of this finite set of runs is represented as the coercion of its finset cardinality. Unfolding `nfa_run_count_list`, the right-hand side is defined as the natural cardinality (`ncard`) of the same set of runs, which by `Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card'` also equals the coercion of its finset cardinality. Both sides are identical, concluding the proof.
steps.code:
rw [hset]
  rw [Set.encard_eq_coe_toFinset_card]
  unfold nfa_run_count_list
  rw [Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card']

glossary.pell_nfa: The non-deterministic finite automaton for the Pell language on states `Fin n`, with start states satisfying `p.val = 0` and accept states satisfying `q.val + 1 = n`.
glossary.Set.mem_setOf_eq: An element `x` belongs to the set `{y | p y}` if and only if the predicate `p x` holds.
glossary.Fin.ext_iff: Two elements of `Fin n` are equal if and only if their underlying natural values are equal.
glossary.Fin.val_mk: For `m < n`, the value of the `Fin n` element `⟨m, h⟩` as a natural number is `m`.
glossary.Set.encard_eq_coe_toFinset_card: For a finite set `s`, its extended cardinality in `ℕ∞` equals the coercion of the cardinality of its associated `Finset`.
glossary.nfa_run_count_list: The number of runs of automaton `M` on word `w` from state `p` to state `q`, defined as the cardinality (`ncard`) of the set of valid runs.
glossary.Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card': For a finite set `s`, its natural number cardinality `ncard` equals the cardinality of its associated `Finset`.

caveats: In Lean, states are typed as elements of `Fin n` (natural numbers strictly less than `n`), which requires explicit proofs that `0 < n` and `n - 1 < n` to construct the states `⟨0, ·⟩` and `⟨n - 1, ·⟩`.

Lean distinguishes between extended cardinality `encard` (taking values in `ℕ∞ = WithTop ℕ`) and finite cardinality `ncard` (in `ℕ`). The equality between them is reconciled by converting both to the cardinality of the underlying finite set (`toFinset.card`).

declarations.name: spider_rho_zero_same
declarations.informal: For any non-free spider leg end φ, spider_rho 0 φ φ = 0.
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_rho_zero_same (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) :
    spider_rho 0 φ φ = 0
declarations.source:
/-- For any non-free spider leg end φ, spider_rho 0 φ φ equals 0. -/
theorem spider_rho_zero_same (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) :
    spider_rho 0 φ φ = 0 := by
  cases φ with
  | free => exact absurd rfl hφ
  | inward => simp [spider_rho]
  | outward => simp [spider_rho]

explanation.summary: The proof argues by case analysis on the spider leg end φ. The case where φ is free is ruled out by the hypothesis that φ ≠ free, and the remaining cases φ = inward and φ = outward follow directly by simplifying the definition of spider_rho at height 0.

steps.claim: The case φ = free cannot occur.
steps.explanation: We consider the possible constructors for the spider leg end φ. If φ is free, reflexivity gives φ = free, which directly contradicts the hypothesis hφ that φ ≠ free.
steps.code:
cases φ with
  | free => exact absurd rfl hφ

steps.claim: When φ = inward, spider_rho 0 inward inward = 0.
steps.explanation: Simplifying with the definition of spider_rho: when phi and delta are both inward and the height is 0, the function evaluates to 0 % 2, which is 0.
steps.code: | inward => simp [spider_rho]

steps.claim: When φ = outward, spider_rho 0 outward outward = 0.
steps.explanation: Similarly, when phi and delta are both outward and the height is 0, the definition of spider_rho evaluates to 0 % 2, which is 0.
steps.code: | outward => simp [spider_rho]

glossary.absurd: from a proposition a and its negation ¬a, any goal b follows
glossary.rfl: equality is reflexive: any term equals itself
glossary.spider_rho: the spider_rho function, computing the leg state based on height and ends

declarations.name: spider_rho_pair_values
declarations.informal: For every h ≥ 1 and φ ≠ free, the pair of rho values (spider_rho h inward φ, spider_rho h outward φ) is either (0, 1) or (1, 0).
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_rho_pair_values (h : ℕ) (hh : 1 ≤ h) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) :
    (spider_rho h SpiderLegEnd.inward φ = 0 ∧ spider_rho h SpiderLegEnd.outward φ = 1) ∨
    (spider_rho h SpiderLegEnd.inward φ = 1 ∧ spider_rho h SpiderLegEnd.outward φ = 0)
declarations.source:
/-- For any leg length h ≥ 1 and non-free spider leg end φ, one of spider_rho h inward φ and spider_rho h outward φ equals 0 and the other equals 1. -/
theorem spider_rho_pair_values (h : ℕ) (hh : 1 ≤ h) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) :
    (spider_rho h SpiderLegEnd.inward φ = 0 ∧ spider_rho h SpiderLegEnd.outward φ = 1) ∨
    (spider_rho h SpiderLegEnd.inward φ = 1 ∧ spider_rho h SpiderLegEnd.outward φ = 0) := by
  cases φ with
  | free => contradiction
  | inward =>
    simp [spider_rho]
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one h with h0 | h1
    · left
      have : 2 ≤ h := by omega
      simp [h0, this]
    · right
      simp [h1]
  | outward =>
    simp [spider_rho]
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one h with h0 | h1
    · right
      have : 2 ≤ h := by omega
      simp [h0, this]
    · left
      simp [h1]

explanation.summary: The proof argues by case analysis on the spider leg end φ. The case φ = free is ruled out by assumption. For the remaining cases φ = inward and φ = outward, evaluating the definition of spider_rho reduces the claim to the parity of h: because h ≥ 1, even h implies h ≥ 2, making the pair of values (0, 1) or (1, 0) according to which direction matches the leg end.

steps.claim: The case φ = free is ruled out by the hypothesis that φ ≠ free.
steps.explanation: We perform case analysis on the spider leg end φ. The constructor φ = free directly contradicts the hypothesis hφ : φ ≠ free, so contradiction finishes this case.
steps.code:
cases φ with
  | free => contradiction

steps.claim: When φ = inward, the pair of rho values is (0, 1) if h is even and (1, 0) if h is odd, satisfying the theorem.
steps.explanation: Unfolding the definition of spider_rho, the inward value is h % 2, while the outward value evaluates to 1 if 2 ≤ h and h % 2 = 0, and 0 otherwise. By Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one, either h % 2 = 0 or h % 2 = 1. If h is even, the assumption 1 ≤ h implies 2 ≤ h by linear arithmetic (omega), so the pair is (0, 1). If h is odd, the outward condition fails and the inward value is 1, so the pair is (1, 0).
steps.code:
| inward =>
    simp [spider_rho]
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one h with h0 | h1
    · left
      have : 2 ≤ h := by omega
      simp [h0, this]
    · right
      simp [h1]

steps.claim: When φ = outward, the pair of rho values is (1, 0) if h is even and (0, 1) if h is odd, satisfying the theorem.
steps.explanation: Similarly, unfolding spider_rho shows that the inward value evaluates the conditional (yielding 1 if 2 ≤ h and h % 2 = 0, and 0 otherwise) while the outward value is h % 2. By Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one, if h is even then 2 ≤ h (via omega), producing the pair (1, 0); if h is odd, we obtain (0, 1).
steps.code:
| outward =>
    simp [spider_rho]
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one h with h0 | h1
    · right
      have : 2 ≤ h := by omega
      simp [h0, this]
    · left
      simp [h1]

declarations.name: spider_mex_incoming_one_outward_not_mem
declarations.informal: The value r ^^^ 1 is not a member of the explicit options list for (in;{(1,outward),(r,φ)}) when r ≥ 2 and φ ≠ free.
declarations.statement:
theorem spider_mex_incoming_one_outward_not_mem (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) :
    r ^^^ 1 ∉
      ([r, spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ 1, spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ 1] ++
       (List.range (r - 2)).flatMap (fun idx =>
         let i := idx + 1
         [spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1),
          spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1)]) ++
       [spider_rho 0 φ φ ^^^ ((r - 1) ^^^ 1)])
declarations.source:
/-- The candidate mex value r ^^^ 1 is not an element of the options list for the configuration κ₂ = (in;{(1,outward),(r,φ)}). -/
theorem spider_mex_incoming_one_outward_not_mem (r : ℕ) (hr : 2 ≤ r) (φ : SpiderLegEnd) (hφ : φ ≠ SpiderLegEnd.free) :
    r ^^^ 1 ∉
      ([r, spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ 1, spider_rho (r - 1) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ 1] ++
       (List.range (r - 2)).flatMap (fun idx =>
         let i := idx + 1
         [spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.inward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1),
          spider_rho (r - 1 - i) SpiderLegEnd.outward φ ^^^ (i ^^^ 1)]) ++
       [spider_rho 0 φ φ ^^^ ((r - 1) ^^^ 1)]) := by
  simp only [List.mem_append, not_or]
  refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · intro h
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at h
    have hh : 1 ≤ r - 1 := by omega
    rcases spider_rho_pair_values (r - 1) hh φ hφ with ⟨h_in, h_out⟩ | ⟨h_in, h_out⟩
    · rw [h_in, h_out] at h
      rcases h with h1 | h2 | h3
      · rcases Nat.even_or_odd r with he | ho
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_even he] at h1; omega
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_odd ho] at h1; omega
      · have : r = 0 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h2
        omega
      · have : r = 1 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h3
        omega
    · rw [h_in, h_out] at h
      rcases h with h1 | h2 | h3
      · rcases Nat.even_or_odd r with he | ho
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_even he] at h1; omega
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_odd ho] at h1; omega
      · have : r = 1 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h2
        omega
      · have : r = 0 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h3
        omega
  · intro h
    rw [List.mem_flatMap] at h
    rcases h with ⟨idx, hidx, hmem⟩
    rw [List.mem_range] at hidx
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hmem
    let i := idx + 1
    have hi : i ≤ r - 2 := by omega
    have hh : 1 ≤ r - 1 - i := by omega
    rcases spider_rho_pair_values (r - 1 - i) hh φ hφ with ⟨h_in, h_out⟩ | ⟨h_in, h_out⟩
    · rw [h_in, h_out, zero_xor, xor_comm 1 (i ^^^ 1), xor_cancel_right] at hmem
      rcases hmem with h1 | h2
      · have : r = i := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h1
        omega
      · rcases Nat.even_or_odd r with he | ho
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_even he] at h2; omega
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_odd ho] at h2; omega
    · rw [h_in, h_out, zero_xor, xor_comm 1 (i ^^^ 1), xor_cancel_right] at hmem
      rcases hmem with h1 | h2
      · rcases Nat.even_or_odd r with he | ho
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_even he] at h1; omega
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_odd ho] at h1; omega
      · have : r = i := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h2
        omega
  · intro h
    simp only [List.mem_singleton] at h
    rw [spider_rho_zero_same φ hφ, zero_xor] at h
    have : r = r - 1 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h
    omega

explanation.summary: The proof establishes that the candidate mex value r ^^^ 1 does not belong to the options list of the spider configuration by partitioning the concatenated options list into three parts: an initial 3-element list, an intermediate list flat-mapped over indices i ∈ {1, ..., r - 2}, and a terminal singleton list. For each part, assuming membership yields an equality involving the spider invariant ρ, which is evaluated using the known values of ρ on positive leg lengths (where it takes values in {0, 1}) and on zero length (where it evaluates to 0). In every case, either the injectivity of bitwise XOR with 1 forces r to equal 0, 1, or i ≤ r - 2, or parity-based evaluation of r ^^^ 1 as r ± 1 leads to an immediate arithmetic impossibility, contradicting r ≥ 2.

steps.claim: It suffices to show that r ^^^ 1 does not belong to any of the three concatenated sublists comprising the options list.
steps.explanation: The options list is constructed by concatenating three parts: an initial three-element list, an intermediate family of lists flat-mapped over indices in List.range (r - 2), and a terminal singleton list. Rewriting membership across list concatenation via List.mem_append and distributing negation over disjunction with not_or transforms the goal into proving non-membership in each part separately. The refine tactic splits this into three independent subgoals.
steps.code:
simp only [List.mem_append, not_or]
  refine ⟨⟨?_, ?_⟩, ?_⟩

steps.claim: r ^^^ 1 is not an element of the initial three-element list [r, spider_rho (r - 1) inward φ ^^^ 1, spider_rho (r - 1) outward φ ^^^ 1].
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that r ^^^ 1 is in this list. Unfolding list membership with List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, and or_false gives three possibilities: r ^^^ 1 = r, or r ^^^ 1 is one of the two ρ-values XORed with 1. Since r ≥ 2, we have 1 ≤ r - 1, so spider_rho_pair_values shows that the pair of inward and outward values of ρ at r - 1 is either (0, 1) or (1, 0). In either case: (1) if r ^^^ 1 = r, case analysis on the parity of r (Nat.even_or_odd) implies r + 1 = r when r is even (Nat.xor_one_of_even) or r - 1 = r when r is odd (Nat.xor_one_of_odd), both impossible; (2) if r ^^^ 1 = 0 ^^^ 1, the injectivity of (· ^^^ 1) from xor_left_involutive implies r = 0, contradicting r ≥ 2; (3) if r ^^^ 1 = 1 ^^^ 1, injectivity implies r = 1, again contradicting r ≥ 2.
steps.code:
· intro h
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at h
    have hh : 1 ≤ r - 1 := by omega
    rcases spider_rho_pair_values (r - 1) hh φ hφ with ⟨h_in, h_out⟩ | ⟨h_in, h_out⟩
    · rw [h_in, h_out] at h
      rcases h with h1 | h2 | h3
      · rcases Nat.even_or_odd r with he | ho
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_even he] at h1; omega
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_odd ho] at h1; omega
      · have : r = 0 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h2
        omega
      · have : r = 1 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h3
        omega
    · rw [h_in, h_out] at h
      rcases h with h1 | h2 | h3
      · rcases Nat.even_or_odd r with he | ho
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_even he] at h1; omega
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_odd ho] at h1; omega
      · have : r = 1 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h2
        omega
      · have : r = 0 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h3
        omega

steps.claim: r ^^^ 1 is not an element of the intermediate list obtained by flat-mapping over idx ∈ List.range (r - 2).
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that r ^^^ 1 is in the flat-mapped list (List.mem_flatMap). Then there is an index idx < r - 2 (List.mem_range) such that r ^^^ 1 is in the two-element list for i = idx + 1. Since idx < r - 2, we have i ≤ r - 2 and 1 ≤ r - 1 - i. By spider_rho_pair_values, the inward and outward values of ρ at r - 1 - i are {0, 1}. Simplifying with zero_xor, xor_comm, and xor_cancel_right reveals the two list elements to be i ^^^ 1 and i. If r ^^^ 1 = i ^^^ 1, injectivity of XOR (xor_left_involutive) implies r = i, which contradicts i ≤ r - 2 < r. If r ^^^ 1 = i, case analysis on the parity of r (Nat.even_or_odd) gives r + 1 = i (Nat.xor_one_of_even) or r - 1 = i (Nat.xor_one_of_odd), both of which contradict i ≤ r - 2.
steps.code:
· intro h
    rw [List.mem_flatMap] at h
    rcases h with ⟨idx, hidx, hmem⟩
    rw [List.mem_range] at hidx
    simp only [List.mem_cons, List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hmem
    let i := idx + 1
    have hi : i ≤ r - 2 := by omega
    have hh : 1 ≤ r - 1 - i := by omega
    rcases spider_rho_pair_values (r - 1 - i) hh φ hφ with ⟨h_in, h_out⟩ | ⟨h_in, h_out⟩
    · rw [h_in, h_out, zero_xor, xor_comm 1 (i ^^^ 1), xor_cancel_right] at hmem
      rcases hmem with h1 | h2
      · have : r = i := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h1
        omega
      · rcases Nat.even_or_odd r with he | ho
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_even he] at h2; omega
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_odd ho] at h2; omega
    · rw [h_in, h_out, zero_xor, xor_comm 1 (i ^^^ 1), xor_cancel_right] at hmem
      rcases hmem with h1 | h2
      · rcases Nat.even_or_odd r with he | ho
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_even he] at h1; omega
        · rw [Nat.xor_one_of_odd ho] at h1; omega
      · have : r = i := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h2
        omega

steps.claim: r ^^^ 1 is not an element of the singleton list [spider_rho 0 φ φ ^^^ ((r - 1) ^^^ 1)].
steps.explanation: Assume for contradiction that r ^^^ 1 is in the singleton list (List.mem_singleton). Because φ ≠ free, spider_rho_zero_same gives ρ(0, φ, φ) = 0, so the list element simplifies via zero_xor to (r - 1) ^^^ 1. The equation r ^^^ 1 = (r - 1) ^^^ 1 implies r = r - 1 by injectivity of XOR (xor_left_involutive). Linear arithmetic (omega) derives a contradiction from r = r - 1, completing the proof.
steps.code:
· intro h
    simp only [List.mem_singleton] at h
    rw [spider_rho_zero_same φ hφ, zero_xor] at h
    have : r = r - 1 := (xor_left_involutive 1).injective h
    omega

glossary.List.mem_cons: An element belongs to a prepended list b :: l if and only if it equals b or belongs to l.
glossary.List.not_mem_nil: No element belongs to the empty list.
glossary.or_false: A proposition disjoined with False is equivalent to the proposition itself: (p ∨ False) ↔ p.

glossary.Nat.xor_one_of_odd: For an odd natural number n, n ^^^ 1 = n - 1.
