    (w : Fin n → Fin (2 * n + 1) → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i g, 0 ≤ w i g)
    (rank : Fin n → Fin (2 * n + 1) ≃ Fin (2 * n + 1))
    (h : is_picking_sequence_pne
      (SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation ⟨w⟩)
      (round_robin_sequence n (2 * n + 1)) rank)
    (i : Fin n) (hi : i ≠ 0) :
    ∃ g ∈ picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence n (2 * n + 1)) rank 0,
      (SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation ⟨w⟩).val i
          (picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence n (2 * n + 1)) rank 0 \ {g}) ≤
        (SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation ⟨w⟩).val i
          (picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence n (2 * n + 1)) rank i)
open.citation: The remaining case of the conjecture round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one (thread RT-3); exact for n = 3 by exp 1515, sampled for n = 4..6 by exp 1598.

open.name: round_robin_three_agents_high_count_two_thirds_ef1
open.informal: In a three-agent Round-Robin pure Nash equilibrium with nonnegative additive valuations, if the envied agent j is picked at least three times in the picking sequence, then every other agent i satisfies 2/3-EF1 towards j: some good g of j's bundle can be removed so that i's value for the rest is at most 3/2 times i's value for her own bundle.
open.statement:
theorem round_robin_three_agents_high_count_two_thirds_ef1
    (m : ℕ) (w : Fin 3 → Fin m → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i g, 0 ≤ w i g)
    (rank : Fin 3 → Fin m ≃ Fin m)
    (h : is_picking_sequence_pne
      (SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation ⟨w⟩)
      (round_robin_sequence 3 m) rank)
    (i j : Fin 3) (hij : i ≠ j)
    (hj : 3 ≤ (round_robin_sequence 3 m).count j)
    (hne : (picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 m) rank j).Nonempty) :
    ∃ g ∈ picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 m) rank j,
      (2 / 3) *
          (∑ x ∈ (picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 m) rank j) \ {g}, w i x)
        ≤ ∑ x ∈ picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 m) rank i, w i x

open.name: round_robin_three_agents_not_guaranteed_above_two_thirds
open.informal: For every α > 2/3 there is a three-agent Round-Robin instance with nonnegative additive valuations that admits a pure Nash equilibrium whose outcome is not α-EF1.
open.statement:
theorem round_robin_three_agents_not_guaranteed_above_two_thirds :
    ∀ α : ℝ, 2 / 3 < α → ¬ is_guaranteed_round_robin_ef1_factor 3 α

open.name: round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1
open.informal: With three agents and seven goods, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin (nonnegative additive valuations) is EF1; so the eight-good counterexample of arXiv:2610.23686 Proposition 1 is the smallest possible.
open.statement:
theorem round_robin_three_agents_seven_goods_pne_ef1
    (w : Fin 3 → Fin 7 → ℝ) (hw : ∀ i g, 0 ≤ w i g) (rank : Fin 3 → Fin 7 ≃ Fin 7)
    (h : is_picking_sequence_pne
      (SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation ⟨w⟩)
      (round_robin_sequence 3 7) rank) :
    SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.IsEF1
      (SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.AdditiveValuation.toValuation ⟨w⟩)
      (picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 7) rank)
open.citation: Smallest open case of round_robin_pne_ef1_of_card_le_two_mul_add_one; arXiv:2610.23686 Proposition 1 has eight goods.

open.name: round_robin_three_agents_two_thirds_guaranteed
open.informal: For three agents, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin with nonnegative additive valuations induces a (2/3)-EF1 allocation; equivalently 2/3 is a guaranteed EF1 factor.
open.statement:
theorem round_robin_three_agents_two_thirds_guaranteed :
    is_guaranteed_round_robin_ef1_factor 3 (2 / 3)

open.name: rr4_agent_zero_bundle_of_first_pick
open.informal: For the Round-Robin sequence [0,1,2,0] on 3 agents and 4 goods, changing only agent 0's report to a new report r that has the same first-ranked good as its current report (r 0 = (b 0) 0) leaves agent 0's bundle unchanged, because agent 0's bundle is determined entirely by its first pick and the (unchanged) reports of agents 1 and 2.
open.statement:
theorem rr4_agent_zero_bundle_of_first_pick (b : Fin 3 → Fin 4 ≃ Fin 4)
    (r : Fin 4 ≃ Fin 4) (h : r 0 = (b 0) 0) :
    picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) (Function.update b 0 r) 0
      = picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b 0

open.name: rr4_irr_step_agent_zero
open.informal: For the Round-Robin sequence [0,1,2,0] on 3 agents and 4 goods, any irr_step under item-preserving swap bids is carried out by agent 0: the resulting profile is obtained by replacing only agent 0's report by an item-preserving swap r, and agent 0 strictly increases its additive value.
open.statement:
theorem rr4_irr_step_agent_zero (v : Fin 3 → Fin 4 → ℝ)
    (b b' : Fin 3 → Fin 4 ≃ Fin 4)
    (h : irr_step v (round_robin_sequence 3 4)
      (is_item_preserving_swap_bid (round_robin_sequence 3 4)) b b') :
    ∃ r : Fin 4 ≃ Fin 4, b' = Function.update b 0 r ∧
      is_item_preserving_swap_bid (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b 0 r ∧
      ∑ g ∈ picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b 0, v 0 g
        < ∑ g ∈ picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b' 0, v 0 g

open.name: rr4_no_two_consecutive_steps_from_truthful
open.informal: For the Round-Robin sequence [0,1,2,0] on 3 agents and 4 goods, from a profile b whose agent 0 first-picks its true top good ((b 0) 0 = (pref 0) 0) there are no two consecutive irr_step steps under item-preserving swap bids: no b' then b'' can both be reached.
open.statement:
theorem rr4_no_two_consecutive_steps_from_truthful
    (pref : Fin 3 → Fin 4 ≃ Fin 4) (v : Fin 3 → Fin 4 → ℝ)
    (hcons : ∀ (i : Fin 3) (k l : Fin 4), k < l → v i (pref i l) < v i (pref i k))
    (b b' b'' : Fin 3 → Fin 4 ≃ Fin 4) (hb : (b 0) 0 = (pref 0) 0)
    (h1 : irr_step v (round_robin_sequence 3 4)
      (is_item_preserving_swap_bid (round_robin_sequence 3 4)) b b')
    (h2 : irr_step v (round_robin_sequence 3 4)
      (is_item_preserving_swap_bid (round_robin_sequence 3 4)) b' b'') :
    False

open.name: rr4_round_robin_outcome_structure
open.informal: For the Round-Robin sequence [0,1,2,0] on 3 agents and 4 goods, for ANY report profile b, agent 0's bundle has exactly 2 goods, agents 1 and 2 have exactly 1 each, and agent 0's first-ranked good (b 0) 0 lies in agent 0's own bundle.
open.statement:
theorem rr4_round_robin_outcome_structure (b : Fin 3 → Fin 4 ≃ Fin 4) :
    (picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b 0).card = 2 ∧
    (picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b 1).card = 1 ∧
    (picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b 2).card = 1 ∧
    (b 0) 0 ∈ picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b 0

open.name: rr4_side_agent_item_preserving_bundle_eq
open.informal: For the Round-Robin sequence [0,1,2,0] on 3 agents and 4 goods, an item-preserving swap bid by a side agent i (i = 1 or 2) leaves that agent's bundle unchanged, because such an agent always ends up with exactly one good and the item-preserving swap must keep the demoted good in the bundle both before and after.
open.statement:
theorem rr4_side_agent_item_preserving_bundle_eq (b : Fin 3 → Fin 4 ≃ Fin 4)
    (i : Fin 3) (hi : i ≠ 0) (r : Fin 4 ≃ Fin 4)
    (hr : is_item_preserving_swap_bid (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b i r) :
    picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) (Function.update b i r) i
      = picking_sequence_outcome (round_robin_sequence 3 4) b i

open.name: condorcet_dimension_le_three
open.informal: Open problem: every election with at least one voter has a Condorcet winning set of at most three candidates, i.e. the Condorcet dimension of every election is at most 3.
open.statement:
theorem condorcet_dimension_le_three :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (P : Fin n → Equiv.Perm (Fin m)), 0 < n →
      ∃ S : Finset (Fin m), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ is_condorcet_winning_set P S
open.citation: open question from Condorcet winning sets (Social Choice and Welfare 44(3):493-517, 2015); dimension 3 is attained, and the best upper bound is 5 (arXiv:2506.22133); arXiv:2604.19851 finds no election of dimension above 3 by computer search

open.name: ejr_committee_monotone_chain_exists
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2007.01795, open problems, Q2): every approval profile with at least one voter admits an ordering c_1, ..., c_m of all candidates such that for every k ≤ m the prefix {c_1, ..., c_k} satisfies EJR for committee size k; equivalently, some resolute committee-monotonic approval-based committee rule satisfies EJR.
open.statement:
theorem ejr_committee_monotone_chain_exists :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Finset (Fin m)), 0 < n →
      ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin m), ∀ k, k ≤ m →
        is_ejr_committee A k (Finset.univ.filter fun c => (σ c : ℕ) < k)
open.citation: open question of arXiv:2007.01795 (Multi-Winner Voting with Approval Preferences) (committee monotonicity and proportionality); sequential Phragmén is committee monotonic but only satisfies PJR, and the known EJR rules are not committee monotonic; a positive answer is known for party-list profiles (arXiv:1911.08365)

open.name: crystal_components_unique
open.informal: Crystals have unique components (arXiv:1601.03081, open): if n is a crystal with components a, b and also with components c, d, then {a, b} = {c, d}.

open.name: davenport_constant_int_box_two_eq
open.informal: Conjecture: for every m ≥ 2, D(⟦−m, m⟧²) = 4m² − q(m), and every minimal zero-sum sequence over ⟦−m, m⟧² of that maximal length is the image of S(m) under one of the eight symmetries of the square.
open.statement:
theorem davenport_constant_int_box_two_eq (m : ℕ) (hm : 2 ≤ m) :
    davenport_constant (↑(int_box_two m) : Set (ℤ × ℤ)) =
        ((4 * m ^ 2 - nat_least_prime_not_dvd m : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ∧
      ∀ s : Multiset (ℤ × ℤ), (∀ x ∈ s, x ∈ int_box_two m) → multiset_is_minimal_zero_sum s →
        (Multiset.card s : ℕ∞) = davenport_constant (↑(int_box_two m) : Set (ℤ × ℤ)) →
        ∃ e₁ e₂ : ℤˣ, ∃ sw : Bool,
          s = (davenport_box_extremal_sequence m).map (int_square_symmetry e₁ e₂ sw)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.16562 (The Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes), Conjecture 1; the paper proves the lower bound (Corollary 2) and the exact value among sequences with support of size 3 (Theorem 1).

open.name: op_153_eventually_subexp_bound_positive_quadratic
open.informal: For a degree-2 intersective integer polynomial g that is strictly positive on all positive integers, there are constants c, C > 0 and a threshold N₀ such that for every N ≥ N₀, every subset A ⊆ {1, ..., N} whose distinct elements never differ by a value g(n) with n a positive integer has cardinality at most C·N·exp(−c√(log N · log log N)).
open.statement:
theorem op_153_eventually_subexp_bound_positive_quadratic (g : Polynomial ℤ)
    (hdeg : g.degree = 2) (hint : is_intersective g)
    (hpos : ∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → 0 < g.eval (n : ℤ)) :
    ∃ c > 0, ∃ C > 0, ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N →
      ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, a ≠ b → ¬ ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (a : ℤ) - b = g.eval (n : ℤ)) →
      (A.card : ℝ) ≤ C * (N : ℝ) * Real.exp (-c * Real.sqrt (Real.log (N : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (N : ℝ))))

open.name: op_153_subexp_bound_intersective_quadratic
open.informal: Let $h \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be an intersective polynomial of degree 2. Do there exist constants $c > 0$ and $C > 0$ depending only on $h$ such that for all integers $N \ge 3$, every subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ whose distinct elements have difference not equal to $h(n)$ for any positive integer $n$ satisfies $|A| \le C N \exp(-c \sqrt{\log N \log \log N})$?
open.statement:
theorem op_153_subexp_bound_intersective_quadratic :
    ∀ (h : Polynomial ℤ), h.degree = 2 → is_intersective h →
    ∃ c > 0, ∃ C > 0, ∀ N : ℕ, 3 ≤ N → ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
    (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ b ∈ A, a ≠ b → ¬ ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (a : ℤ) - b = h.eval (n : ℤ)) →
    (A.card : ℝ) ≤ C * (N : ℝ) * Real.exp (-c * Real.sqrt (Real.log (N : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (N : ℝ))))
open.citation: arXiv:2610.07765 Sec. 1, after line 248 -- A new bound for the Furstenberg--Sárközy theorem using the van der Corput property

open.name: postage_stamp_number_neg_two_eq_of_mod_four_eq_two
open.informal: If h ≥ 2 and h ≡ 2 (mod 4), then n♭_h(2) = n_h(2) = (h² + 6h)/4.
open.statement:
theorem postage_stamp_number_neg_two_eq_of_mod_four_eq_two (h : ℕ) (hh : 2 ≤ h) (h4 : h % 4 = 2) :
    postage_stamp_number_neg h 2 = (h ^ 2 + 6 * h) / 4 ∧ postage_stamp_number h 2 = (h ^ 2 + 6 * h) / 4
open.citation: arXiv:2610.19470 (Positivity and negativity for h-bases for n), Theorem 3.3 (with the value of n_h(2) from Theorem 1.1).

open.name: postage_stamp_number_neg_two_eq_of_mod_four_eq_zero
open.informal: If h ≥ 8 and h ≡ 0 (mod 4), then n♭_h(2) = n_h(2) = (h² + 6h)/4.
open.statement:
theorem postage_stamp_number_neg_two_eq_of_mod_four_eq_zero (h : ℕ) (hh : 8 ≤ h) (h4 : h % 4 = 0) :
    postage_stamp_number_neg h 2 = (h ^ 2 + 6 * h) / 4 ∧ postage_stamp_number h 2 = (h ^ 2 + 6 * h) / 4
open.citation: arXiv:2610.19470 (Positivity and negativity for h-bases for n), Theorem 3.4 (with the value of n_h(2) from Theorem 1.1).

open.name: postage_stamp_number_three_lt_neg
open.informal: For four-element sets (k = 3) and every h ≥ 8, sets containing a negative integer do strictly better than nonnegative ones: n♭_h(3) > n_h(3). This reverses the three-element case, where n♭_h(2) ≤ n_h(2) for every h.
open.statement:
theorem postage_stamp_number_three_lt_neg (h : ℕ) (hh : 8 ≤ h) :
    postage_stamp_number h 3 < postage_stamp_number_neg h 3

open.name: postage_stamp_number_two_eq
open.informal: The classical postage stamp number for three stamps: n_h(2) = ⌊(h² + 6h + 1)/4⌋ for every h ≥ 1.
open.statement:
theorem postage_stamp_number_two_eq (h : ℕ) (hh : 1 ≤ h) :
    postage_stamp_number h 2 = (h ^ 2 + 6 * h + 1) / 4
open.citation: arXiv:2610.19470 (Positivity and negativity for h-bases for n), Theorem 1.1 (classical; cited there).

open.name: weakly_consecutive_one_at_end
open.informal: Conjecture 5.2 of arXiv:2401.09497 (open): every weakly consecutive sequence of length k begins or ends with the term 1, that is, the position holding the value 1 is the first or the last.
open.statement:
theorem weakly_consecutive_one_at_end {k : ℕ} (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin k))
    (hσ : is_weakly_consecutive σ) (i : Fin k) (hi : (σ i : ℕ) = 0) :
    (i : ℕ) = 0 ∨ (i : ℕ) + 1 = k

open.name: matroid_symmetry_gap_integral_lt_eight_seventeenths
open.informal: Sharper form of the open question of arXiv:2610.07387: there is a strongly symmetric instance — non-negative submodular f on a finite ground set, matroid M, group G of permutations with f invariant and independence determined by the symmetrized indicator vector — such that the symmetrized fractional optimum sup_{x∈P(M)} F(x̄) is strictly less than 8/17 times the best *integral* value max{f(S) : S independent in M}. This is stronger than the parent statement, whose denominator is the best fractional value sup_{x∈P(M)} F(x).
open.statement:
theorem matroid_symmetry_gap_integral_lt_eight_seventeenths :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (M : Matroid (Fin m)) (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m))),
      (∀ S, 0 ≤ f S) ∧ is_submodular f ∧ is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f G ∧
      sSup ((fun x => multilinear_extension f (perm_group_symmetrize G x)) '' matroid_polytope M) <
        8 / 17 * sSup (f '' {S : Finset (Fin m) | M.Indep ↑S})

open.name: matroid_symmetry_gap_lt_eight_seventeenths
open.informal: Open question (arXiv:2610.07387, after Corollary 3.4 and Appendix A): there is a strongly symmetric instance of non-negative submodular maximization over a matroid — a non-negative submodular f on a finite ground set, a matroid M and a permutation group G such that f is G-invariant and independence depends only on the G-symmetrized indicator vector — whose symmetry gap max_{x∈P(M)} F(x̄) / max_{x∈P(M)} F(x) is strictly below 8/17 (F the multilinear extension, P(M) the matroid polytope).
open.statement:
theorem matroid_symmetry_gap_lt_eight_seventeenths :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (M : Matroid (Fin m)) (f : Finset (Fin m) → ℝ) (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm (Fin m))),
      (∀ S, 0 ≤ f S) ∧ is_submodular f ∧ is_strongly_symmetric_instance M f G ∧
      sSup ((fun x => multilinear_extension f (perm_group_symmetrize G x)) '' matroid_polytope M) <
        8 / 17 * sSup (multilinear_extension f '' matroid_polytope M)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.07387 (Stronger Hardness for Submodular Maximization Subject to a Matroid Constraint): its gadgets attain symmetry gap 8/17, giving the 8/17 inapproximability bound (Theorem 1.1), and Appendix A shows 8/17 is optimal within the paper's three-parameter family; whether any matroid instance has a smaller gap is left open.

open.name: linear_flattening_testable_even_step
open.informal: For every even integer k ≥ 4, if the secant variety σ_{2k-2}((ℂᵏ)⊗³) is testable by the linear flattening method, then σ_{2(k+2)-2}((ℂ^{k+2})⊗³) is also testable.
open.statement:
theorem linear_flattening_testable_even_step (k : ℕ) (hk : 4 ≤ k) (heven : Even k) :
    linear_flattening_testable k (2 * k - 2) →
    linear_flattening_testable (k + 2) (2 * (k + 2) - 2)

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_int_le_22
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 8): there is a bilinear algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication with integer coefficients that uses 22 products, i.e. a list of 22 triads over the integers whose evaluation equals A * B for all integer 3x3 matrices A and B. By the paper, such an algorithm is the same as a recursive (block) algorithm with integer constants and 22 multiplications; the paper proves at least 22 are needed and 23 suffice, so the question is whether the rank is exactly 22.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_int_le_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_le ℤ 22
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 8 (a 22-product integer algorithm for 3x3 matrix multiplication), stated as posed

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_z_ge_22
open.informal: The tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over the integers is at least 22; that is, every valid decomposition of 3x3 matrix multiplication over ℤ has length at least 22.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_z_ge_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge ℤ 22
open.citation: arXiv:2610.01639, Theorem 1 and Sec. 8 (Lower Bound of 22 for 3x3 Matrix Multiplication over the Integers)

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_ge_22
open.informal: Every bilinear algorithm (valid triad decomposition) for 3x3 matrix multiplication over the two-element field uses at least 22 products. This is the main lower bound of arXiv:2610.01639 (row 0 of its table), proved there by a large computer-assisted Lean development.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_ge_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_ge (ZMod 2) 22
open.citation: arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 3 and Sec. 7, Table 1, row 0: the paper's main lower bound of 22 over the two-element field

open.name: matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_le_22
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 7, Table 1, row 0, interval [22, 23]): the tensor rank of 3x3 matrix multiplication over the two-element field is 22, i.e. there are 22 triads over ZMod 2 whose evaluation equals A * B for all 3x3 matrices A, B over ZMod 2. The paper proves the rank is at least 22 and at most 23.
open.statement: theorem matrix3_tensor_rank_zmod2_le_22 : matrix3_tensor_rank_le (ZMod 2) 22
open.citation: the open problem of arXiv:2610.01639, Sec. 7, Table 1, row 0 (rank over the two-element field in [22, 23]), stated as posed

open.name: op100_linear_flattening_potency_gt_even
open.informal: For every even natural number n ≥ 4, there exists a linear flattening on (ℂⁿ)⊗³ with potency strictly greater than 2n - 2, so the secant variety σ_{2n-2}((ℂⁿ)⊗³) is testable by the linear flattening method.
open.statement:
theorem op100_linear_flattening_potency_gt_even (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n) (heven : Even n) :
    linear_flattening_testable n (2 * n - 2)

open.name: tarski_box_query_le_five_log_sq
open.informal: The residual open content of the target, in box form: five-dimensional Tarski search has O(log² n) query complexity on every box, uniformly in the box.
open.statement:
theorem tarski_box_query_le_five_log_sq :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → ∃ q : ℕ,
      tarski_box_query_le n 5 q ∧ (q : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.logb 2 n ^ 2

open.name: tarski_query_complexity_five_le_log_sq
open.informal: Open question (arXiv:2610.07055, the case k = 5 of the gap left by its Theorems 2 and 3): Tarski(n, 5) = O(log² n), i.e. there is a constant C such that for every n ≥ 2 some deterministic query algorithm finds a fixed point of every monotone map [n]^5 → [n]^5 (componentwise order) with at most C·(log₂ n)² queries.
open.statement:
theorem tarski_query_complexity_five_le_log_sq :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n →
      ∃ q : ℕ, tarski_query_complexity_le n 5 q ∧ (q : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.logb 2 n ^ 2
open.citation: arXiv:2610.07055 (Tarski Fixed Points in Quasi-FPT Queries): Theorem 2 gives Tarski(n, 5) = O((log n)^3) and Theorem 3 (with the earlier two-dimensional bound) gives Ω((log n)^2); O(log² n) is known for k = 3 and k = 4. This is the k = 5 instance of the question how the exponent of log n grows with k. The list entry's general form (exponent c·⌈log₂ k⌉ with c < 1 for all k ≥ 3) is already refuted at k = 3 by the known Ω(log² n) lower bound, so only the k = 5 question is stated.

open.name: op_98_empty_repairs_reduction
open.informal: If there is c < 5/2 with weight(O) ≤ c·weight(A) for every packing O, then the target holds: take R = ∅, which is a compatible repair family vacuously, and apply_repairs A ∅ = A.
open.statement:
theorem op_98_empty_repairs_reduction
    (h : ∃ c : ℚ, c < 5 / 2 ∧ ∀ (α : Type) [DecidableEq α] (inst : WeightedSetPackingInstance α 4)
      (A : Finset (Finset α)), is_square_locally_optimal inst 4 A → ∀ O, is_packing inst O →
      packing_weight inst O ≤ c * packing_weight inst A) :
    ∃ c : ℚ, c < 5 / 2 ∧ ∀ (α : Type) [DecidableEq α] (inst : WeightedSetPackingInstance α 4)
      (A : Finset (Finset α)), is_square_locally_optimal inst 4 A → ∃ R : Finset (Finset (Finset α)),
      (∀ X ∈ R, is_repair inst A X) ∧ is_compatible_repair_family R ∧ ∀ O, is_packing inst O →
      packing_weight inst O ≤ c * packing_weight inst (apply_repairs A R)

open.name: op_98_objective_switching_weighted_four_set_packing
open.informal: Open Problem OP-98 (arXiv:2610.10036, Sec. 5): there exists a rational approximation ratio c < 5/2 such that for every type α with decidable equality, every weighted 4-set packing instance inst, and every packing A that is square locally optimal with respect to 4-exchanges, there exists a compatible repair family R of repairs for A such that every valid packing O in inst satisfies packing_weight inst O ≤ c * packing_weight inst (apply_repairs A R).
open.statement: theorem op_98_objective_switching_weighted_four_set_packing : ∃ c : ℚ, c < 5 / 2 ∧ ∀ (α : Type) [DecidableEq α] (inst : WeightedSetPackingInstance α 4) (A : Finset (Finset α)), is_square_locally_optimal inst 4 A → ∃ R : Finset (Finset (Finset α)), (∀ X ∈ R, is_repair inst A X) ∧ is_compatible_repair_family R ∧ ∀ O, is_packing inst O → packing_weight inst O ≤ c * packing_weight inst (apply_repairs A R)

open.name: op_98_repairs_free_bound
open.informal: There is a rational c < 5/2 such that for every weighted 4-set packing instance and every square locally optimal packing A, every packing O satisfies weight(O) ≤ c·weight(A).
open.statement:
theorem op_98_repairs_free_bound :
    ∃ c : ℚ, c < 5 / 2 ∧ ∀ (α : Type) [DecidableEq α] (inst : WeightedSetPackingInstance α 4)
      (A : Finset (Finset α)), is_square_locally_optimal inst 4 A → ∀ O, is_packing inst O →
      packing_weight inst O ≤ c * packing_weight inst A

open.name: nfa_max_ambiguity_asymptotic_upper_bound
open.informal: Sharp asymptotic upper bound: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large n, the maximum degree of ambiguity M(n) of trim finitely ambiguous n-state NFAs is at most (1 + √2 + ε)^n.
open.statement:
theorem nfa_max_ambiguity_asymptotic_upper_bound :
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
      ENNReal.toReal (nfa_max_ambiguity n) ≤ (1 + Real.sqrt 2 + ε) ^ n

open.name: nfa_max_ambiguity_limit_of_eventual_bounds
open.informal: Reduction of the asymptotic base constant to two one-sided bounds: if M(n) dominates twice the (n-2)-nd Pell number eventually, and if for every ε > 0 one has M(n) ≤ (1+√2+ε)^n eventually, then M(n)^(1/n) → 1+√2.
open.statement:
theorem nfa_max_ambiguity_limit_of_eventual_bounds
    (hlower : ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
      (2 * (pell_number (n - 2) : ℝ)) ≤ ENNReal.toReal (nfa_max_ambiguity n))
    (hupper : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
      ENNReal.toReal (nfa_max_ambiguity n) ≤ (1 + Real.sqrt 2 + ε) ^ n) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (ENNReal.toReal (nfa_max_ambiguity n)) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (1 + Real.sqrt 2))

open.name: nfa_max_ambiguity_pell_lower_bound
open.informal: Pell lower bound for the maximum ambiguity: for all sufficiently large n, twice the (n-2)-nd Pell number is at most the maximum degree of ambiguity M(n) of trim finitely ambiguous n-state NFAs.
open.statement:
theorem nfa_max_ambiguity_pell_lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop,
      (2 * (pell_number (n - 2) : ℝ)) ≤ ENNReal.toReal (nfa_max_ambiguity n)

open.name: op_359_symmetric_two_counter_reachability_semilinear
open.informal: For every symmetric 2-counter machine M with a finite state type Q and any pair of states q, q' in Q, the reachability relation two_counter_machine_reach_rel M q q' is a semilinear subset of (ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ).
open.statement: theorem op_359_symmetric_two_counter_reachability_semilinear {Q : Type*} [Finite Q] (M : TwoCounterMachine Q) (hM : two_counter_machine_is_symmetric M) (q q' : Q) : IsSemilinearSet (two_counter_machine_reach_rel M q q')

open.name: op_360_single_counter_update_strictly_less_expressive
open.informal: There exists a symmetric 2-counter machine M over a finite state type Q and states q, q' in Q whose reachability relation two_counter_machine_reach_rel M q q' cannot be realized as the reachability relation two_counter_machine_reach_rel M' q0 q1 between any states q0, q1 of any finite-state symmetric 2-counter machine M' with single-counter updates.
open.statement:
theorem op_360_single_counter_update_strictly_less_expressive :
    ∃ (Q : Type) (_ : Finite Q) (M : TwoCounterMachine Q) (_ : two_counter_machine_is_symmetric M) (q q' : Q),
      ∀ (Q' : Type) (_ : Finite Q') (M' : TwoCounterMachine Q') (_ : two_counter_machine_is_symmetric M')
        (_ : two_counter_machine_is_single_counter_update M') (q0 q1 : Q'),
        two_counter_machine_reach_rel M' q0 q1 ≠ two_counter_machine_reach_rel M q q'

open.name: optimal_asymptotic_base_constant_finitely_ambiguous_nfa
open.informal: The asymptotic base constant c = lim_{n → ∞} M(n)^{1/n} for the maximum degree of ambiguity M(n) of trim finitely ambiguous n-state NFAs equals 1 + Real.sqrt 2.
open.statement:
theorem optimal_asymptotic_base_constant_finitely_ambiguous_nfa :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (ENNReal.toReal (nfa_max_ambiguity n)) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (n : ℝ)))
      Filter.atTop (nhds (1 + Real.sqrt 2))

open.name: pell_nfa_degree_lower_bound
open.informal: The degree of ambiguity of the n-state Pell NFA pell_nfa n in ℕ∞ is at least 2 * pell_number (n - 2).
open.statement: theorem pell_nfa_degree_lower_bound (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) : (2 * pell_number (n - 2) : ℕ∞) ≤ nfa_degree_of_ambiguity (pell_nfa n)

open.name: pell_nfa_run_count_lower_bound
open.informal: In the n-state automaton A_n, the word u_n = c_1c_2c_2c_3…c_(n-2)c_(n-1) has at least 2·P(n-2) accepting runs from the initial state q_1 to the final state q_n.
open.statement:
theorem pell_nfa_run_count_lower_bound (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    ((2 * pell_number (n - 2) : ℕ) : ℕ∞) ≤
      Set.encard {r : Fin ((pell_word n).length + 1) → Fin n |
        r 0 ∈ (pell_nfa n).start ∧
        r (Fin.last (pell_word n).length) ∈ (pell_nfa n).accept ∧
        ∀ i : Fin (pell_word n).length,
          r i.succ ∈ (pell_nfa n).step (r i.castSucc) ((pell_word n).get i)}

open.name: pell_prefix_block_step
open.informal: Appending one two-letter block to a prefix whose run counts vanish off q_i, q_(i+1) with x runs at q_i and y at q_(i+1) gives a vector vanishing off q_(i+1), q_(i+2) with x+y runs at q_(i+1) and 2x+y at q_(i+2).
open.statement:
open Classical in
theorem pell_prefix_block_step (n i : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (h1 : 1 ≤ i) (hi : i + 1 ≤ n - 2)
    (hzero : ∀ s : Fin n, s.val ≠ i → s.val ≠ i + 1 → s.val ≠ i + 2 →
      nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix i) ⟨0, by omega⟩ s = 0)
    (hx : nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix i) ⟨0, by omega⟩
      ⟨i, by omega⟩ = pell_number (i + 1) - pell_number i)
    (hy : nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix i) ⟨0, by omega⟩
      ⟨i + 1, by omega⟩ = 2 * pell_number i) :
    (∀ s : Fin n, s.val ≠ i + 1 → s.val ≠ i + 2 → s.val ≠ i + 3 →
      nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix (i + 1)) ⟨0, by omega⟩ s = 0)
    ∧ nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix (i + 1)) ⟨0, by omega⟩
        ⟨i + 1, by omega⟩ = pell_number (i + 2) - pell_number (i + 1)
    ∧ nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix (i + 1)) ⟨0, by omega⟩
        ⟨i + 2, by omega⟩ = 2 * pell_number (i + 1)

open.name: pell_prefix_count_vector
open.informal: After i two-letter blocks the number of runs from q_1 vanishes off q_i, q_(i+1), q_(i+2), equals P(i+1)-P(i) at q_i and 2P(i) at q_(i+1).
open.statement:
open Classical in
theorem pell_prefix_count_vector (n i : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (h1 : 1 ≤ i) (hi : i ≤ n - 2) :
    (∀ s : Fin n, s.val ≠ i → s.val ≠ i + 1 → s.val ≠ i + 2 →
      nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix i) ⟨0, by omega⟩ s = 0)
    ∧ nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix i) ⟨0, by omega⟩
        ⟨i, by omega⟩ = pell_number (i + 1) - pell_number i
    ∧ nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix i) ⟨0, by omega⟩
        ⟨i + 1, by omega⟩ = 2 * pell_number i

open.name: pell_prefix_two_letter_vector
open.informal: From the one-letter vector (x at q_i, y at q_(i+1), x+y at q_(i+2)), appending c_(i+2) yields the block-step conclusion: vanish off q_(i+1),q_(i+2),q_(i+3); P(i+2)-P(i+1) at q_(i+1); 2P(i+1) at q_(i+2).
open.statement:
open Classical in
theorem pell_prefix_two_letter_vector (n i : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (h1 : 1 ≤ i) (hi : i + 1 ≤ n - 2)
    (hV1 : ∀ s : Fin n,
      nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix i ++ [⟨(i + 1) % 5, by omega⟩])
        ⟨0, by omega⟩ s
      = (if s.val = i then (pell_number (i + 1) - pell_number i) else 0)
        + (if s.val = i + 1 then (2 * pell_number i) else 0)
        + (if s.val = i + 2 then ((pell_number (i + 1) - pell_number i) + 2 * pell_number i) else 0)) :
    (∀ s : Fin n, s.val ≠ i + 1 → s.val ≠ i + 2 → s.val ≠ i + 3 →
      nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix (i + 1)) ⟨0, by omega⟩ s = 0)
    ∧ nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix (i + 1)) ⟨0, by omega⟩
        ⟨i + 1, by omega⟩ = pell_number (i + 2) - pell_number (i + 1)
    ∧ nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word_prefix (i + 1)) ⟨0, by omega⟩
        ⟨i + 2, by omega⟩ = 2 * pell_number (i + 1)

open.name: pell_runs_exact_count
open.informal: The word u_n has exactly 2·P(n-2) runs from q_1 to q_n in A_n.
open.statement:
open Classical in
theorem pell_runs_exact_count (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) :
    nfa_run_count_list (pell_nfa n) (pell_word n) ⟨0, by omega⟩ ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
      = 2 * pell_number (n - 2)

open.name: single_counter_symmetric_cannot_match_diag_reach
open.informal: No finite-state symmetric 2-counter machine with single-counter updates can have reachability relation equal to that of the diagonal machine between false and true.
open.statement:
theorem single_counter_symmetric_cannot_match_diag_reach :
    ∀ (Q' : Type) (_ : Finite Q') (M' : TwoCounterMachine Q') (_ : two_counter_machine_is_symmetric M')
      (_ : two_counter_machine_is_single_counter_update M') (q0 q1 : Q'),
      two_counter_machine_reach_rel M' q0 q1 ≠
        two_counter_machine_reach_rel (⟨{(false, TwoCounterInstr.update 1 1, true)}⟩ : TwoCounterMachine Bool) false true

open.name: symmetric_two_counter_boundary_reachability_semilinear
open.informal: For every symmetric 2-counter machine M with finite state type Q and states q, q', the reachability relation restricted to source and target boundary configurations (where at least one counter is zero) is semilinear.
open.statement: theorem symmetric_two_counter_boundary_reachability_semilinear {Q : Type*} [Finite Q] (M : TwoCounterMachine Q) (hM : two_counter_machine_is_symmetric M) (q q' : Q) : IsSemilinearSet { p : (ℕ × ℕ) × (ℕ × ℕ) | (p.1.1 = 0 ∨ p.1.2 = 0) ∧ (p.2.1 = 0 ∨ p.2.2 = 0) ∧ Relation.ReflTransGen (two_counter_machine_step M) (q, p.1) (q', p.2) }

open.name: brgc_necklace_order_consecutive_adjacent_of_prime
open.informal: For every prime n, consecutive necklaces of D_n (the nonconstant binary necklaces of length n ordered by the binary reflected Gray code rank of their first occurrence) are adjacent in the necklace graph Q_n: some representatives differ in exactly one bit.
open.statement:
theorem brgc_necklace_order_consecutive_adjacent_of_prime :
    ∀ n : ℕ, n.Prime → ∀ t t' : ℕ, brgc_necklace_first_rank n t →
      brgc_necklace_first_rank n t' → t < t' →
      (∀ s, t < s → s < t' → ¬ brgc_necklace_first_rank n s) →
      bitword_necklace_adjacent n (brgc_word t) (brgc_word t')
open.citation: arXiv:2610.24758 (Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces), Conjecture 1 (prime case of a conjecture from 2007), Sec. 1. The paper verifies it for all primes n <= 47 by computation and proves it implies optimal single-track Gray codes; it fails for composite n such as 6 and 9.

open.name: brgc_necklace_order_consecutive_aperiodic_adjacent
open.informal: For every n, if two consecutive necklaces of D_n (the nonconstant binary necklaces of length n ordered by the BRGC rank of their first occurrence) are both aperiodic, then they are adjacent in the necklace graph Q_n. For prime n every nonconstant necklace is aperiodic, so this contains the prime case conjectured in arXiv:2610.24758.
open.statement:
theorem brgc_necklace_order_consecutive_aperiodic_adjacent :
    ∀ n t t' : ℕ, brgc_necklace_first_rank n t → brgc_necklace_first_rank n t' → t < t' →
      (∀ s, t < s → s < t' → ¬ brgc_necklace_first_rank n s) →
      bitword_is_aperiodic n (brgc_word t) → bitword_is_aperiodic n (brgc_word t') →
      bitword_necklace_adjacent n (brgc_word t) (brgc_word t')
open.citation: arXiv:2610.24758 (Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces), Conjecture 1 and the remark after it: the paper states the adjacency conjecture for prime n only, and notes it fails for composite odd n (n = 9, 15, 21) 'as the exceptions in their conjecture allow'; it does not describe the exceptions.

open.name: card_edgeSet_completeGraph
open.informal: The edge set of $K_n$ is the set of unordered non-diagonal pairs, so $K_n$ has $\binom{n}{2}$ edges; in particular $K_5$ has 10.
open.statement:
theorem card_edgeSet_completeGraph (n : ℕ) :
    (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet.ncard = n.choose 2

open.name: clean_handshake_seq_edges_card_lt_choose_two
open.informal: A clean handshake sequence over $k$ gloves starting from the empty contamination map covers strictly fewer than $\binom{k+2}{2}$ distinct edges.

open.name: five_diamond_poset_ramsey_number_le
open.informal: For every natural number k with 1 ≤ k, the k-color poset Ramsey number of the 5-diamond DiamondPoset 5 is at most 5 * k.
open.statement: theorem five_diamond_poset_ramsey_number_le (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : poset_ramsey_number (DiamondPoset 5) k ≤ 5 * k
open.citation: arXiv:2610.20545, The k-color poset Ramsey number of the diamond is 2k, Theorem 2

open.name: five_diamond_ramsey_property_at_four_mul
open.informal: For k ≥ 2, every k-colouring of the subsets of Fin (4k) contains a monochromatic induced copy of the 5-diamond.
open.statement:
theorem five_diamond_ramsey_property_at_four_mul (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) :
    poset_ramsey_property (DiamondPoset 5) k (4 * k)

open.name: galvin_bipartite_multigraph_list_edge_colouring
open.informal: Galvin's theorem in matroid-free form (list edge colouring of bipartite multigraphs): view the finite set α as the edge set of the bipartite multigraph whose left and right endpoints of e are the labels f e and g e. If every fibre of f and every fibre of g has at most k elements (so the maximum degree is at most k), then for every list assignment L with |L e| ≥ k there is a choice c e ∈ L e such that each colour class meets every fibre of f and every fibre of g in at most one element, i.e. is a matching. This is Galvin's theorem χ'_ℓ = Δ for bipartite multigraphs (1995); it is a strictly weaker statement than the target (two unit-capacity partition matroids are strongly base orderable), k = 1 is trivial and k = 2 is proved here.
open.statement:
theorem galvin_bipartite_multigraph_list_edge_colouring {α : Type*} [Finite α] (f g : α → ℕ) (k : ℕ)
    (hf : ∀ γ : ℕ, {e | f e = γ}.ncard ≤ k) (hg : ∀ γ : ℕ, {e | g e = γ}.ncard ≤ k)
    (L : α → Finset ℕ) (hL : ∀ e : α, k ≤ (L e).card) :
    ∃ c : α → ℕ, (∀ e : α, c e ∈ L e) ∧
      ∀ γ : ℕ, (∀ e₁ e₂ : α, c e₁ = γ → c e₂ = γ → f e₁ = f e₂ → e₁ = e₂) ∧
        ∀ e₁ e₂ : α, c e₁ = γ → c e₂ = γ → g e₁ = g e₂ → e₁ = e₂

open.name: glove_number_complete_graph_choose_two_le_sq
open.informal: For $n \ge 2$, the number of edges $\binom{n}{2}$ of $K_n$ is at most the square of its glove number: $\mathrm{gl}(K_n) \ge \sqrt{n(n-1)/2}$.
open.statement:
theorem glove_number_complete_graph_choose_two_le_sq (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    n.choose 2 ≤ glove_number (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) ^ 2

open.name: glove_number_k4
open.informal: The glove number of the complete graph $K_4$ is equal to 3.
open.statement: theorem glove_number_k4 : glove_number (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 4)) = 3

open.name: glove_number_k4_no_one_glove
open.informal: There is no clean handshake sequence with exactly one glove that covers all six edges of $K_4$: with one glove all covered edges coincide, and $K_4$ has two distinct edges.
open.statement:
theorem glove_number_k4_no_one_glove :
    ¬ has_clean_handshake_seq (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 4)) 1

open.name: glove_number_k4_no_two_gloves
open.informal: There is no clean handshake sequence with exactly two gloves covering all six edges of $K_4$, i.e. two gloves are not enough for $K_4$.
open.statement:
theorem glove_number_k4_no_two_gloves :
    ¬ has_clean_handshake_seq (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 4)) 2

open.name: glove_number_k4_no_zero_gloves
open.informal: There is no clean handshake sequence with zero gloves covering all edges of $K_4$: the glove type `Fin 0` is empty, so there is no handshake at all, hence the sequence is empty and covers no edge, while $K_4$ has the edge $\{0,1\}$.
open.statement:
theorem glove_number_k4_no_zero_gloves :
    ¬ has_clean_handshake_seq (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 4)) 0

open.name: glove_number_k4_two_gloves_all_sides_touched
open.informal: If a clean two-glove sequence covers all six edges of $K_4$, then each of the four glove sides is directly touched by some vertex. Reason: a pair of sides has fixed touchers and hence can serve for at most one edge, while the six edges of $K_4$ need six distinct pairs of touched sides, and there are exactly $\binom{4}{2} = 6$ pairs of sides.
open.statement:
theorem glove_number_k4_two_gloves_all_sides_touched
    (seq : List (Handshake (Fin 4) (Fin 2)))
    (hclean : CleanHandshakeSeq seq (fun _ => (∅ : Set (Fin 4))))
    (hcover : ∀ e ∈ (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 4)).edgeSet, ∃ h ∈ seq, handshake_edge h = e) :
    ∀ s : Fin 2 × Bool, (seq_touchers seq s).Nonempty

open.name: glove_number_k4_two_gloves_touchers_eq_singleton
open.informal: If a clean two-glove sequence covers all edges of $K_4$, there is a bijection $u$ from the four glove sides to the four vertices with the property that the set of vertices directly touching a side $s$ anywhere in the sequence is exactly $\{u(s)\}$.
open.statement:
theorem glove_number_k4_two_gloves_touchers_eq_singleton
    (seq : List (Handshake (Fin 4) (Fin 2)))
    (hclean : CleanHandshakeSeq seq (fun _ => (∅ : Set (Fin 4))))
    (hcover : ∀ e ∈ (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 4)).edgeSet, ∃ h ∈ seq, handshake_edge h = e) :
    ∃ u : (Fin 2 × Bool) → Fin 4, Function.Injective u ∧ ∀ s, seq_touchers seq s = {u s}

open.name: glove_number_k5_no_small_gloves
open.informal: For every $k \le 3$ there is no clean handshake sequence with $k$ gloves covering every edge of $K_5$: $k$ gloves cover at most $k^2 \le 9$ edges, while $K_5$ has 10.
open.statement:
theorem glove_number_k5_no_small_gloves :
    ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ 3 → ¬ has_clean_handshake_seq (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 5)) k

open.name: glove_number_k5_no_three_gloves
open.informal: There is no clean handshake sequence with at most three gloves covering every edge of $K_5$: with $k$ gloves at most $k^2$ edges are covered, but $K_5$ has 10 edges and $3^2 = 9 < 10$.
open.statement:
theorem glove_number_k5_no_three_gloves :
    ¬ has_clean_handshake_seq (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin 5)) 3

open.name: greedy_distinct_diff_seq_one_two_surjective
open.informal: The greedy sequence with distinct consecutive differences started at 1, 2 takes every positive integer as a value.
open.statement:
theorem greedy_distinct_diff_seq_one_two_surjective :
    ∀ v, 0 < v → ∃ n, greedy_distinct_diff_seq 1 2 n = v
open.citation: 'Permutations of the positive integers with restrictions on the sequence of differences' (Pacific J. Math. 71, 1977), main theorem, as cited in arXiv:2610.15860 (A note on the Slater–Vélez permutation); the special case a₁ = 1, a₂ = 2 of OP-203.

open.name: greedy_distinct_diff_seq_surjective
open.informal: Conjecture: for any distinct positive integers a₁, a₂, the greedy sequence with distinct consecutive differences started at a₁, a₂ takes every positive integer as a value (it is a permutation of the positive integers).
open.statement:
theorem greedy_distinct_diff_seq_surjective (a₁ a₂ : ℕ) (h₁ : 0 < a₁) (h₂ : 0 < a₂)
    (h : a₁ ≠ a₂) : ∀ v, 0 < v → ∃ n, greedy_distinct_diff_seq a₁ a₂ n = v
open.citation: arXiv:2610.15860 (A note on the Slater–Vélez permutation): the 1977 paper it cites proves this for a₁ = 1, a₂ = 2; the question for arbitrary starting terms is raised after Theorem 1. A computation of the first 3000 terms for every start with a₁, a₂ ≤ 12 found every integer up to at least 1660 among them.

open.name: handshake_seq_edge_eq_of_sides_eq
open.informal: Two handshakes of the same clean sequence that directly touch the same pair of glove sides cover the same edge, because each glove side is directly touched by at most one vertex.
open.statement:
theorem handshake_seq_edge_eq_of_sides_eq {V Γ : Type*} [DecidableEq Γ]
    (seq : List (Handshake V Γ)) (t : Γ × Bool → Set V) (hc : CleanHandshakeSeq seq t)
    {h₁ h₂ : Handshake V Γ} (hm₁ : h₁ ∈ seq) (hm₂ : h₂ ∈ seq)
    (hl : handshake_left_side h₁ = handshake_left_side h₂)
    (hr : handshake_right_side h₁ = handshake_right_side h₂) :
    handshake_edge h₁ = handshake_edge h₂

open.name: handshake_seq_edge_eq_of_sym2_sides_eq
open.informal: Two handshakes of the same clean sequence that touch the same unordered pair of sides in $\mathrm{Sym}^2(\Gamma \times \mathrm{Bool})$ cover the same edge, since each side has at most one toucher along the sequence.
open.statement:
theorem handshake_seq_edge_eq_of_sym2_sides_eq {V Γ : Type*} [DecidableEq Γ]
    (seq : List (Handshake V Γ)) (t : Γ × Bool → Set V) (hc : CleanHandshakeSeq seq t)
    {h₁ h₂ : Handshake V Γ} (hm₁ : h₁ ∈ seq) (hm₂ : h₂ ∈ seq)
    (hsides : (s(handshake_left_side h₁, handshake_right_side h₁) : Sym2 (Γ × Bool)) =
              s(handshake_left_side h₂, handshake_right_side h₂)) :
    handshake_edge h₁ = handshake_edge h₂

open.name: handshake_seq_edges_card_le_sq
open.informal: A clean handshake sequence using $k$ gloves covers at most $k^2$ distinct edges: at most $k$ edges come from single-gloved handshakes, and for each of the $\binom{k}{2}$ pairs of gloves at most $2$ further edges come from double-gloved handshakes between them (besides the two edges already counted for those gloves), giving $k + 2\binom{k}{2} = k^2$.
open.statement:
theorem handshake_seq_edges_card_le_sq {V Γ : Type*} [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq Γ] [Fintype Γ]
    (seq : List (Handshake V Γ)) (hc : CleanHandshakeSeq seq (fun _ => (∅ : Set V))) :
    (seq.map handshake_edge).toFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card Γ ^ 2

open.name: handshake_seq_one_glove_edges_eq
open.informal: If `seq` is a clean handshake sequence over the one-element glove type `Fin 1` starting from the empty contamination map, then all handshakes in `seq` cover one and the same edge of `V`; in particular such a sequence covers at most one edge, whatever `V` is.
open.statement:
theorem handshake_seq_one_glove_edges_eq {V : Type*} (seq : List (Handshake V (Fin 1)))
    (h : CleanHandshakeSeq seq (fun _ => (∅ : Set V))) :
    ∃ e : Sym2 V, ∀ g ∈ seq, handshake_edge g = e

open.name: handshake_seq_single_edges_card_le
open.informal: In a clean sequence over $k$ gloves starting from the empty contamination map, all single-gloved handshakes together cover at most $k$ distinct edges: a single handshake on glove $g$ touches both sides of $g$, and each side is touched by at most one vertex, so every single handshake on $g$ covers the same edge.
open.statement:
theorem handshake_seq_single_edges_card_le {V Γ : Type*} [DecidableEq V] [DecidableEq Γ] [Fintype Γ]
    (seq : List (Handshake V Γ)) (hc : CleanHandshakeSeq seq (fun _ => (∅ : Set V))) :
    (seq.filterMap (fun h => match h with
      | .single _ _ _ => some (handshake_edge h)
      | .double _ _ _ _ => none)).toFinset.card ≤ Fintype.card Γ

open.name: handshake_sides_ne_of_clean
open.informal: In any clean handshake sequence, the left and right glove sides of each handshake are distinct (single handshakes use opposite sides of the same glove; double handshakes use sides of distinct gloves).
open.statement:
theorem handshake_sides_ne_of_clean {V Γ : Type*} [DecidableEq Γ]
    (seq : List (Handshake V Γ)) (t : Γ × Bool → Set V) (hc : CleanHandshakeSeq seq t)
    {h : Handshake V Γ} (hm : h ∈ seq) :
    handshake_left_side h ≠ handshake_right_side h

open.name: handshake_touchers_subset_seq_touchers
open.informal: If a handshake $h$ is in the sequence `seq`, the vertices directly touching side $s$ during $h$ are contained in the sequence touchers of $s$.
open.statement:
theorem handshake_touchers_subset_seq_touchers {V Γ : Type*} [DecidableEq Γ]
    (seq : List (Handshake V Γ)) (h : Handshake V Γ) (s : Γ × Bool)
    (hm : h ∈ seq) : handshake_touchers h s ⊆ seq_touchers seq s

open.name: latin_square_exists_principal_isotope_avoiding
open.informal: If L and L' are any Latin squares of the same order n > 1, there are permutations π, ρ of {1, ..., n} with L'(π(i), ρ(j)) ≠ L(i, j) for all i, j: some principal isotope of L' avoids L.
open.statement:
theorem latin_square_exists_principal_isotope_avoiding (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n)
    (L L' : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n) (hL : latin_square_is L) (hL' : latin_square_is L') :
    ∃ π ρ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∀ i j, L' (π i) (ρ j) ≠ L i j
open.citation: arXiv:2610.20008 (Avoiding a partial Latin square with an isotope of a given Latin square), Conjecture 4: the paper proves it for all sufficiently large n (Theorem 1, applied to the conjugates with symbols and columns exchanged), notes it holds when L' is a principal isotope of L and for n ≤ 3, and checked n ≤ 7 by computer.

open.name: matroid_common_list_chromatic_le_add_const
open.informal: Open question (arXiv:2610.07318, Question 3.1): there is an absolute constant C such that χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) ≤ χ(M₁, M₂) + C for every pair of loopless matroids on a common finite ground set. (The paper also asks whether C = 1 works; its Theorem 1.1, matroid_common_list_colorable_two_not_of_colorable_two here, shows C = 0 does not.)
open.statement:
theorem matroid_common_list_chromatic_le_add_const :
    ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (α : Type) [Finite α] (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α), M₁.Loopless → M₂.Loopless →
      M₁.E = M₂.E →
      matroid_common_list_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ ≤ matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ + C
open.citation: arXiv:2610.07318 (A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids), Question 3.1. Known: χ_ℓ ≤ 2χ for every pair (Combinatorica 45, 2025, Article 46), and the paper's Theorem 1.1 gives a pair with χ = 2, χ_ℓ = 3.

open.name: matroid_common_list_colorable_succ_of_common_colorable
open.informal: One-step list-lifting (the C = 1 case): if two loopless matroids on a common finite ground set have a common coloring with k colors, then they are (k+1)-list-colorable. This is a matroid analogue of Galvin's theorem for the general (non-strongly-base-orderable) pair case, and is exactly the C = 1 form of Question 3.1 (arXiv:2610.07318), strictly stronger than the parent's existence-of-some-C statement.
open.statement:
theorem matroid_common_list_colorable_succ_of_common_colorable {α : Type*} (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α) [Finite α] (h₁ : M₁.Loopless) (h₂ : M₂.Loopless) (hE : M₁.E = M₂.E) (k : ℕ) (h : matroid_common_colorable M₁ M₂ k) :
    matroid_common_list_colorable M₁ M₂ (k + 1)

open.name: matroid_sbo_common_list_chromatic_eq
open.informal: Open question (arXiv:2610.07318, Question 3.2): for any two loopless strongly base-orderable matroids M₁, M₂ on a common finite ground set, the common list chromatic number equals the common chromatic number, χ_ℓ(M₁, M₂) = χ(M₁, M₂).
open.statement:
theorem matroid_sbo_common_list_chromatic_eq :
    ∀ (α : Type) [Finite α] (M₁ M₂ : Matroid α), M₁.Loopless → M₂.Loopless → M₁.E = M₂.E →
      matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₁ → matroid_strongly_base_orderable M₂ →
      matroid_common_list_chromatic_number M₁ M₂ = matroid_common_chromatic_number M₁ M₂
open.citation: arXiv:2610.07318 (A note on the list chromatic number of two matroids), Question 3.2. The paper shows χ_ℓ = χ can fail for general pairs (Theorem 1.1) and proves the strongly base-orderable case when two colors suffice (Corollary 2.3); equality was known for two transversal matroids. The case χ ≥ 3 is open.

open.name: matroid_sbo_reduction_partition_classes_of_colourable
open.informal: Generalised partition-matroid reduction for strongly base-orderable matroids (Proposition 2.2 of arXiv:2610.07318 with 2 replaced by k): let M be a finite strongly base-orderable matroid whose ground set is the union of k independent sets (equivalently M is k-colourable). Then M has a reduction to a unit-capacity partition matroid with classes of size at most k: there is a class map f : α → ℕ whose fibres meet E in at most k elements and such that every T ⊆ E containing no two distinct elements with the same f-value is independent in M. The case k = 2 is proved here (matroid_sbo_reduction_pairs_of_two_indep, involution form, used for matroid_sbo_common_list_chromatic_eq_of_le_two); the case k ≥ 3 is a conjecture and is the crux of Question 3.2.
open.statement:
theorem matroid_sbo_reduction_partition_classes_of_colourable {α : Type*} (M : Matroid α) [M.Finite]
    (hM : matroid_strongly_base_orderable M) (k : ℕ) (hc : matroid_common_colorable M M k) :
    ∃ f : α → ℕ, (∀ γ : ℕ, {e | e ∈ M.E ∧ f e = γ}.ncard ≤ k) ∧
      ∀ T ⊆ M.E, (∀ e₁ ∈ T, ∀ e₂ ∈ T, f e₁ = f e₂ → e₁ = e₂) → M.Indep T

open.name: mondrian_liminf_min_defect_seven_eq
open.informal: Conjecture: for Mondrian partitions of the n×n square into seven pairwise noncongruent integer rectangles, liminf_{n→∞} M₇(n) = 280, i.e. no sequence of seven-rectangle partitions has defect eventually below 280.
open.statement:
theorem mondrian_liminf_min_defect_seven_eq :
    Filter.liminf (fun n => mondrian_min_defect_seven n) Filter.atTop = 280
open.citation: arXiv:2610.19193 (A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem), Conjecture 1; list entry OP-282. The upper bound ≤ 280 is Theorem 1.1 (mondrian_liminf_min_defect_seven_le).

open.name: mondrian_no_perfect_partition
open.informal: No square has a perfect Mondrian partition: there is no partition of an n×n square into at least two pairwise noncongruent integer rectangles all of the same area.
open.statement:
theorem mondrian_no_perfect_partition (n : ℕ) :
    ¬ ∃ P, mondrian_is_partition n P ∧ mondrian_defect P = 0
open.citation: arXiv:2610.19193 (A Bounded-Defect Construction for the Mondrian Art Problem), Sec. 1 (the zero-defect question, conjectured negative since the problem's proposal); list entry OP-280.

open.name: nus_min_card_ge_c_log_sq
open.informal: Open question: there is an absolute constant c > 0 such that m(p) ≥ c (log p)² for all sufficiently large primes p.
open.statement:
theorem nus_min_card_ge_c_log_sq :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∃ p₀ : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p₀ ≤ p → p.Prime →
      c * Real.log p ^ 2 ≤ (nus_min_card p : ℝ)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.09349 (A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums), Question 5.1. The paper proves m(p) ≥ 2^{-80} (log p / log log p)² for p ≥ 64 (Theorem 1.1) and m(p) ≤ (log p)²/(2 (log 3)²) + O((log p)²/log log p) (Theorem 1.2); an affirmative answer would give m(p) = Θ((log p)²).

open.name: nus_min_card_ge_near_quadratic
open.informal: There is an absolute constant C > 0 (explicitly C = 2⁻⁸⁰) with m(p) ≥ C (log p / log log p)² for every prime p ≥ 64. Published theorem of Hou–Yang; not yet formalized anywhere.
open.statement:
theorem nus_min_card_ge_near_quadratic :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∃ p₀ : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p₀ ≤ p → p.Prime →
      C * (Real.log p / Real.log (Real.log p)) ^ 2 ≤ (nus_min_card p : ℝ)

open.name: op_258_forces_step
open.informal: Let a : ℕ+ → ℝ be positive, antitone, with Σ a i > 1, and let k ≥ 3. If a forces a monochromatic K_k, then a forces a monochromatic K_{k+1}.
open.statement:
theorem op_258_forces_step (a : ℕ+ → ℝ) (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < a i) (hanti : Antitone a)
    (hsum : 1 < ∑' i : ℕ+, ENNReal.ofReal (a i)) :
    ∀ k : ℕ, 3 ≤ k → op_258_forces a k → op_258_forces a (k + 1)

open.name: op_258_triangle_forcing_implies_decay_ramsey
open.informal: For every sequence a : ℕ+ → ℝ, if a is positive, antitone, and has sum strictly greater than 1 in ℝ≥0∞, and if a forces a monochromatic triangle K_3 on sufficiently large complete graphs under a-bounded edge colourings, then for every integer k ≥ 3, a forces a monochromatic clique K_k.
open.statement:
theorem op_258_triangle_forcing_implies_decay_ramsey :
    ∀ (a : ℕ+ → ℝ),
      ((∀ i, 0 < a i) ∧ Antitone a ∧ 1 < ∑' i : ℕ+, ENNReal.ofReal (a i)) →
      (∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ c : (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet → ℕ+,
        (∀ i : ℕ+, ((Finset.univ : Finset (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet).filter (fun e => c e = i)).card ≤ a i * (n.choose 2 : ℝ)) →
        ∃ (s : Finset (Fin n)) (i : ℕ+), s.card = 3 ∧
          ∀ ⦃u v : Fin n⦄, u ∈ s → v ∈ s → (h : u ≠ v) →
            c ⟨s(u, v), by simp [SimpleGraph.completeGraph_eq_top, h]⟩ = i) →
      ∀ k ≥ 3,
        ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ c : (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet → ℕ+,
          (∀ i : ℕ+, ((Finset.univ : Finset (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)).edgeSet).filter (fun e => c e = i)).card ≤ a i * (n.choose 2 : ℝ)) →
          ∃ (s : Finset (Fin n)) (i : ℕ+), s.card = k ∧
            ∀ ⦃u v : Fin n⦄, u ∈ s → v ∈ s → (h : u ≠ v) →
              c ⟨s(u, v), by simp [SimpleGraph.completeGraph_eq_top, h]⟩ = i

open.name: op_270_five_diamond_poset_ramsey_number
open.informal: For every natural number k with 2 ≤ k, the k-color poset Ramsey number of the 5-diamond DiamondPoset 5 is equal to 4 * k.
open.statement: theorem op_270_five_diamond_poset_ramsey_number (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) : poset_ramsey_number (DiamondPoset 5) k = 4 * k
open.citation: arXiv:2610.20545, The k-color poset Ramsey number of the diamond is 2k, Section 1

open.name: optimal_single_track_gray_code_of_gray_necklace_path
open.informal: Let n >= 7 be prime. If the list of non-constant binary necklaces of length n, ordered by the rank of their first occurrences in the binary reflected Gray code, forms a Gray path in the necklace graph, then the necklace graph has a Hamilton cycle, and an optimal single-track Gray code of length n and period 2^n - 2 exists.
open.statement:
theorem optimal_single_track_gray_code_of_gray_necklace_path
    (n : ℕ) (hn : n.Prime) (hge : 7 ≤ n)
    (hpath : gray_ordered_necklaces_is_gray_path n) :
    necklace_graph_has_hamilton_cycle n ∧
      ∃ w : ℕ → ℕ, is_single_track_gray_code n (2 ^ n - 2) w
open.citation: arXiv:2610.24758 Theorem A -- Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces

open.name: optimal_single_track_gray_code_of_necklace_hamilton_cycle
open.informal: For any prime n at least 3, if the necklace graph has a Hamilton cycle of length (2^n - 2) / n visiting every non-constant necklace, then there exists an optimal single-track Gray code of length n and period 2^n - 2.
open.statement:
theorem optimal_single_track_gray_code_of_necklace_hamilton_cycle
    (n : ℕ) (hn : n.Prime) (hge : 3 ≤ n)
    (hcycle : necklace_graph_has_hamilton_cycle n) :
    ∃ w : ℕ → ℕ, is_single_track_gray_code n (2 ^ n - 2) w
open.citation: arXiv:2610.24758 Lemma 1 -- Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces

open.name: perm_offset_avoiding_count_neg_one_one_eq_menage_add_two_of_even
open.informal: For even n >= 4 the number of permutations avoiding the offsets {-1, 1} mod n equals the menage number U(n) plus 2.
open.statement:
theorem perm_offset_avoiding_count_neg_one_one_eq_menage_add_two_of_even (n : ℕ) (hn : 4 ≤ n)
    (he : Even n) :
    perm_offset_avoiding_count n {-1, 1} = perm_offset_avoiding_count n {-1, 0} + 2
open.citation: arXiv:2610.23958 (Unranking S-avoiding permutations with two forbidden offsets), Theorem 6.3

open.name: poset_height_one_reconstructible
open.informal: Open problem (arXiv:2610.12690, Sec. 9, from an open problem in a monograph on ordered sets): every finite ordered set of height one with at least four elements is reconstructible from its deck: if P and Q are finite ordered sets of height one, |P| ≥ 4, and P, Q have the same deck of one-element-deleted suborders, then P ≅ Q.
open.statement:
theorem poset_height_one_reconstructible :
    ∀ (P Q : Type) [Fintype P] [Fintype Q] [PartialOrder P] [PartialOrder Q],
      4 ≤ Fintype.card P → poset_height_one P → poset_height_one Q →
      poset_hypomorphic P Q → Nonempty (P ≃o Q)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.12690 (Reconstruction of Finite Posets of Width Three), Sec. 9 (Conclusions): the paper settles width at most three and leaves the height-one case of the open problem open.

open.name: poset_nonempty_order_iso_of_card_order_hom_eq_of_connected
open.informal: Let X and Y be finite posets (possibly empty). If for every finite nonempty connected poset Z the number of order-preserving maps Z → X equals the number of order-preserving maps Z → Y, then X and Y are order-isomorphic. (A poset is connected when its comparability graph is.)
open.statement:
theorem poset_nonempty_order_iso_of_card_order_hom_eq_of_connected {X Y : Type}
    [Fintype X] [PartialOrder X] [Fintype Y] [PartialOrder Y]
    (h : ∀ (Z : Type) [Fintype Z] [Nonempty Z] [PartialOrder Z],
      (SimpleGraph.fromRel fun a b : Z => a ≤ b).Connected →
        Nat.card (Z →o X) = Nat.card (Z →o Y)) :
    Nonempty (X ≃o Y)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.20802 (Two short proofs of the A^A theorem), Lemma 2.4.

open.name: prime_two_pow_sub_two_div_mul
open.informal: For any prime n ≥ 3, n divides 2^n - 2 by Fermat's Little Theorem, so ((2^n - 2) / n) * n = 2^n - 2.
open.statement:
theorem prime_two_pow_sub_two_div_mul (n : ℕ) (hn : n.Prime) (hge : 3 ≤ n) :
    ((2 ^ n - 2) / n) * n = 2 ^ n - 2

open.name: segment_crossing_symm
open.informal: The segment crossing relation between two segments in ℝ² is symmetric.
open.statement:
theorem segment_crossing_symm (e₁ e₂ : Sym2 (ℝ × ℝ)) :
    segment_crossing e₁ e₂ ↔ segment_crossing e₂ e₁

open.name: segments_block_points_of_card_le_one
open.informal: Any finite point set in ℝ² of cardinality at most 1 is vacuously blocked by any finite family of segments L under the triangle-free crossing property.
open.statement:
theorem segments_block_points_of_card_le_one (L : Finset (Sym2 (ℝ × ℝ))) {P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ)}
    (hP : P.card ≤ 1) : segments_block_points L P

open.name: segments_block_points_subset
open.informal: If a segment family L blocks a point set Q under the triangle-free crossing property, then L also blocks any subset P ⊆ Q.

open.name: seq_contam_mono_append
open.informal: Contamination is monotone along a clean sequence: if a vertex's germs are on a glove side after the prefix $l_1$, they are still there after the prefix $l_1$ followed by $l_2$.
open.statement:
theorem seq_contam_mono_append {V Γ : Type*} [DecidableEq Γ]
    (l₁ l₂ : List (Handshake V Γ)) (t : Γ × Bool → Set V) (s : Γ × Bool) :
    seq_contam l₁ t s ⊆ seq_contam (l₁ ++ l₂) t s

open.name: simple_graph_cycle_power_seven_cover_four_tight_dvd
open.informal: A tight cover of C_n^7 (n ≥ 22) by 4 equivalence subgraphs (every distance-7, 6, 4 pair covered exactly once, every class spanned by a distance-7 pair) exists only when 8 divides n.
open.statement:
theorem simple_graph_cycle_power_seven_cover_four_tight_dvd (n : ℕ) [NeZero n] (hn : 22 ≤ n)
    (c : Fin 4 → ZMod n → ZMod n)
    (hc : ∀ s u v, u ≠ v → c s u = c s v → (simple_graph_cycle_power n 7).Adj u v)
    (hcov : ∀ u v, (simple_graph_cycle_power n 7).Adj u v → ∃ s, c s u = c s v)
    (h7 : ∀ i, ∃! s, c s i = c s (i + 7)) (h6 : ∀ i, ∃! s, c s i = c s (i + 6))
    (h4 : ∀ i, ∃! s, c s i = c s (i + 4))
    (hspan : ∀ s i, ∃ d : ℕ, d ≤ 7 ∧ c s (i - d) = c s (i - d + 7) ∧ c s (i - d) = c s i) :
    8 ∣ n
open.citation: the structural step of the k = 7 case of OP-205 (arXiv:2610.15635), research thread RT-1, case k = 7 (k + 1 = 8); the analogue of simple_graph_cycle_power_three_cover_three_tight_dvd (4 | n for k = 3)

open.name: simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number_cycle_power_dvd
open.informal: For k ≥ 1 and q ≥ 2, the k-th power of the cycle on q(k + 1) vertices has equivalence covering number exactly 1 + ⌈log₂(k + 1)⌉.
open.statement:
theorem simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number_cycle_power_dvd (k q : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hq : 2 ≤ q) :
    simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number (simple_graph_cycle_power (q * (k + 1)) k) =
      1 + Nat.clog 2 (k + 1)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.15635 (Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs), Theorem 2.6.

open.name: simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number_cycle_power_ge
open.informal: For k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2k + 2, eq(C_n^k) ≥ 1 + ⌈log₂(k + 1)⌉.
open.statement:
theorem simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number_cycle_power_ge (n k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k)
    (hn : 2 * k + 2 ≤ n) :
    1 + Nat.clog 2 (k + 1) ≤
      simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number (simple_graph_cycle_power n k)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.15635 (Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs), Lemma 2.2 (the lower bound of Theorem 1.2).

open.name: simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number_cycle_power_two_pow_even_not_dvd
open.informal: Let k + 1 = 2^m with m ≥ 1, and let n ≥ max{2k + 2, k²(k + 2)} be even with k + 1 not dividing n. Then eq(C_n^k) = 2 + ⌈log₂(k + 1)⌉ = m + 2 (the larger of the two values the paper leaves open).
open.statement:
theorem simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number_cycle_power_two_pow_even_not_dvd
    (k m n : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hkm : k + 1 = 2 ^ m)
    (hn : max (2 * k + 2) (k ^ 2 * (k + 2)) ≤ n) (hev : Even n) (hnd : ¬ (k + 1) ∣ n) :
    simple_graph_equivalence_covering_number (simple_graph_cycle_power n k) = m + 2
open.citation: arXiv:2610.15635 (Covering powers of cycles with equivalence subgraphs), the case left open by Theorems 1.3 and 1.4: the paper determines eq(C_n^k) for n ≥ max{2k+2, k²(k+2)} when k+1 is not a power of two, when (k+1) | n, and when k+1 is a power of two and n is odd (value 2 + ⌈log₂(k+1)⌉ by a parity argument with maximal isotropic subspaces in characteristic 2), and for n ≥ (k+1)·max{41, 5⌈log₂(k+1)⌉} only narrows it to two values. A SAT search (experiment 708) finds eq(C_n^3) = 4 for every n in 9..30 not divisible by 4 and for n = 46, 50, 54, and 3 when 4 | n, so the statement takes the larger value.

open.name: simple_graph_not_has_equivalence_cover_cycle_power_seven_of_not_dvd
open.informal: For n ≥ 22 not divisible by 8, C_n^7 cannot be covered by 4 equivalence subgraphs; this is the lower bound eq(C_n^7) ≥ 5 = m + 2 of the open case k = 7 (m = 3) of OP-205.
open.statement:
theorem simple_graph_not_has_equivalence_cover_cycle_power_seven_of_not_dvd (n : ℕ) (hn : 22 ≤ n)
    (h8 : ¬ 8 ∣ n) : ¬ simple_graph_has_equivalence_cover (simple_graph_cycle_power n 7) 4
open.citation: the lower-bound half of the k = 7 case of OP-205 (arXiv:2610.15635), research thread RT-1, case k = 7 (k + 1 = 8); SAT finds no 4-cover for 17 ≤ n ≤ 39 unless 8 | n (exp 721)

open.name: triangle_free_blocking_ge_vertex_cover
open.informal: For every finite family of line segments L in ℝ² whose crossing graph is triangle-free, the blocking number of L under the triangle-free crossing property is at least the minimum vertex cover size of G(L).
open.statement:
theorem triangle_free_blocking_ge_vertex_cover
    (L : Finset (Sym2 (ℝ × ℝ)))
    (h_tf : (segment_crossing_graph L).CliqueFree 3) :
    ∃ P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), segments_block_points L P ∧
      (segment_crossing_graph L).vertexCoverNum ≤ P.card

open.name: triangle_free_blocking_ge_vertex_cover_of_le_one
open.informal: For every finite family of line segments L whose crossing graph has vertex cover number at most 1, there exists a point set P blocked by L with cardinality at least the vertex cover number.
open.statement:
theorem triangle_free_blocking_ge_vertex_cover_of_le_one
    (L : Finset (Sym2 (ℝ × ℝ)))
    (h_vc : (segment_crossing_graph L).vertexCoverNum ≤ 1) :
    ∃ P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), segments_block_points L P ∧
      (segment_crossing_graph L).vertexCoverNum ≤ P.card

open.name: triangle_free_blocking_ge_vertex_cover_of_le_two
open.informal: For every finite family of line segments L whose crossing graph is triangle-free and has vertex cover number at most 2, there exists a point set P blocked by L with cardinality at least the vertex cover number.
open.statement:
theorem triangle_free_blocking_ge_vertex_cover_of_le_two
    (L : Finset (Sym2 (ℝ × ℝ)))
    (h_tf : (segment_crossing_graph L).CliqueFree 3)
    (h_vc : (segment_crossing_graph L).vertexCoverNum ≤ 2) :
    ∃ P : Finset (ℝ × ℝ), segments_block_points L P ∧
      (segment_crossing_graph L).vertexCoverNum ≤ P.card

open.name: zero_sum_w_eq_question
open.informal: Does w_r(n) = 2r(n−1) + 1 hold for every r ≥ 1 and n > 1?
open.statement:
theorem zero_sum_w_eq_question :
    ∀ r n : ℕ, 1 ≤ r → 1 < n → zero_sum_w r n = ((2 * r * (n - 1) + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.19965 (Proofs and disproofs of some conjectures on zero-sum problems), Question 3.1; list entry OP-259. Known for r = 1 (Sun), n = 2 (Theorem 1.2 (i)) and r = 2, n = 2^k3^ℓp (Theorem 1.2 (iii)); the lower bound is Lemma 3.1.

open.name: zero_sum_w_two
open.informal: For every r ≥ 1, w_r(2) = 2r + 1.
open.statement: theorem zero_sum_w_two (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r) : zero_sum_w r 2 = ((2 * r + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.19965 (Proofs and disproofs of some conjectures on zero-sum problems), Theorem 1.2 (i). The case n = 2 of Question 3.1 (list entry OP-259).

open.name: chain_graph_k_independence_number_eq_upper_k_star_forming_number
open.informal: Conjecture: for every finite chain graph G and every k ≥ 3, β_k(G) = SF_k(G).
open.statement:
theorem chain_graph_k_independence_number_eq_upper_k_star_forming_number {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (A : Set V) (hG : simple_graph_is_chain_graph G A) (k : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) :
    simple_graph_k_independence_number G k = simple_graph_upper_k_star_forming_number G k
open.citation: arXiv:2610.03785 (Upper k-star-forming sets, k-independence, and upper domination), Conjecture 6.4 (the paper proves the case k = 2, Theorem 6.2, and the complete bipartite case, Theorem 3.2). An exhaustive search over all chain graphs with at most 12 vertices and k = 3, 4, 5 found no counterexample.

open.name: cycle_eleven_compl_strongly_chromatic_choosable
open.informal: The case ℓ = 6 of Conjecture 9 of arXiv:2610.14241: the odd antihole complement(C_11) is strongly 6-chromatic-choosable: χ = 6, and every assignment of lists of size 5 that are not all identical admits a proper list colouring.
open.statement:
theorem cycle_eleven_compl_strongly_chromatic_choosable :
    IsStronglyChromaticChoosable (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 11)ᶜ 6
open.citation: arXiv:2610.14241 (Restricting odd antiholes in critical graphs via list coloring), Conjecture 9 (open for ℓ ≥ 5; the paper notes that ℓ = 5 is the first case with new consequences: with its Theorem 10 it gives Conjecture 3 whenever k = Δ - 1, in particular for (k, Δ) = (7, 8), the first open case). Theorem 8 proves the case where all lists lie in a common ℓ-set

open.name: cycle_nine_compl_strongly_chromatic_choosable
open.informal: The case ℓ = 5 of Conjecture 9 of arXiv:2610.14241: the odd antihole complement(C_9) is strongly 5-chromatic-choosable: χ = 5, and every assignment of lists of size 4 that are not all identical admits a proper list colouring.
open.statement:
theorem cycle_nine_compl_strongly_chromatic_choosable :
    IsStronglyChromaticChoosable (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 9)ᶜ 5
open.citation: arXiv:2610.14241 (Restricting odd antiholes in critical graphs via list coloring), Conjecture 9 (open for ℓ ≥ 5; the paper notes that ℓ = 5 is the first case with new consequences: with its Theorem 10 it gives Conjecture 3 whenever k = Δ - 1, in particular for (k, Δ) = (7, 8), the first open case). Theorem 8 proves the case where all lists lie in a common ℓ-set

open.name: diam_le_three_of_forall_power_well_covered
open.informal: If G is a finite simple connected graph such that G^d is well-covered for all d ≥ 1, then diam(G) ≤ 3.
open.statement:
theorem diam_le_three_of_forall_power_well_covered :
    ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.Connected →
      (∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)) → G.diam ≤ 3
open.citation: First part of OP-160 (arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Question 3.9). Exhaustive search: no counterexample on at most 7 vertices.

open.name: digraph_exists_bipartition_both_cuts_ge_ceil_div_six
open.informal: Let G be a finite loopless digraph with m edges and minimum outdegree at least 2. Then there is a vertex bipartition V = A ⊔ B with e(A, B) ≥ ⌈m/6⌉ and e(B, A) ≥ ⌈m/6⌉.
open.statement:
theorem digraph_exists_bipartition_both_cuts_ge_ceil_div_six {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : Digraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hloop : ∀ v, ¬ G.Adj v v)
    (hdeg : ∀ v, 2 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (G.Adj v)).card) :
    ∃ A : Finset V, ⌈(digraph_edge_count G : ℚ) / 6⌉₊ ≤ digraph_cut_count G A Aᶜ ∧
      ⌈(digraph_edge_count G : ℚ) / 6⌉₊ ≤ digraph_cut_count G Aᶜ A
open.citation: arXiv:2610.21381 (Optimally large cuts in both directions), Theorem 1.4 (the case d = 2 of Conjecture 6.1, for all m). Digraphs are Mathlib `Digraph`s (at most one arc per ordered pair) with loops excluded by hypothesis.

open.name: digraph_exists_bipartition_both_cuts_ge_min_outdegree_bound
open.informal: Conjecture: for every integer d ≥ 2, every finite loopless digraph with m edges and minimum outdegree at least d has a vertex bipartition V = A ⊔ B with both e(A, B) and e(B, A) at least ⌈(d − 1)m / (2(2d − 1))⌉.
open.statement:
theorem digraph_exists_bipartition_both_cuts_ge_min_outdegree_bound {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [DecidableEq V] (G : Digraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (d : ℕ) (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    (hloop : ∀ v, ¬ G.Adj v v)
    (hdeg : ∀ v, d ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (G.Adj v)).card) :
    ∃ A : Finset V,
      ⌈((d - 1 : ℚ) * digraph_edge_count G) / (2 * (2 * d - 1))⌉₊ ≤ digraph_cut_count G A Aᶜ ∧
      ⌈((d - 1 : ℚ) * digraph_edge_count G) / (2 * (2 * d - 1))⌉₊ ≤ digraph_cut_count G Aᶜ A
open.citation: arXiv:2610.21381 (Optimally large cuts in both directions), Conjecture 6.1 (proved there for d = 2 for all m, Theorem 1.4, and for every d when m is large, Theorem 1.1, with a stronger additive term).

open.name: edge_connectivity_ge_half_scale_mul_min_degree_mul_lly_lower_bound
open.informal: For every d ≥ 3 and every finite connected graph G of diameter at least d: κ'(G) ≥ (d/2) · δ(G) · κ_LLY^(d)(G).
open.statement:
theorem edge_connectivity_ge_half_scale_mul_min_degree_mul_lly_lower_bound :
    ∀ d : ℕ, 3 ≤ d → ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
      [DecidableRel G.Adj], G.Connected → d ≤ G.diam →
      ((d : ℝ) / 2) * (G.minDegree : ℝ) * graph_lly_curvature_lower_bound G d ≤
        (graph_edge_connectivity G : ℝ)
open.citation: Open-problem entry OP-164, asked after arXiv:2610.10559 (Edge-Connectivity versus Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature), Theorem 1.2 (which is the case d = 3). Stated for finite graphs. Exact computation finds no counterexample among K_m□P_k, K_m□C_k, Q_4, P_4□P_4, C_4□P_4 (n ≤ 16); equality holds in several of them at d = diam (e.g. K_2□P_k, Q_4).

open.name: edge_connectivity_ge_three_halves_min_degree_mul_lly_lower_bound_three
open.informal: Every finite connected graph of diameter at least 3 has κ'(G) ≥ (3/2) · δ(G) · κ_LLY^(3)(G).
open.statement:
theorem edge_connectivity_ge_three_halves_min_degree_mul_lly_lower_bound_three
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : G.Connected) (hd : 3 ≤ G.diam) :
    (3 / 2 : ℝ) * (G.minDegree : ℝ) * graph_lly_curvature_lower_bound G 3 ≤
      (graph_edge_connectivity G : ℝ)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.10559 (Edge-Connectivity versus Lin--Lu--Yau Curvature), Theorem 1.2 (for finite graphs). The case d = 3 of OP-164.

open.name: exists_dist_three_cut_potential_witness
open.informal: Sharp cut certificate: in the regime |E(X,Xᶜ)| < δ(G) there are vertices x, y with d(x,y) = 3 and a 1-Lipschitz potential f with f(x) − f(y) = 3 whose neighbourhood averages satisfy 3 − A_x + A_y ≤ 2|E(X,Xᶜ)|/δ(G).
open.statement:
theorem exists_dist_three_cut_potential_witness
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : G.Connected) (hd : 3 ≤ G.diam) (X : Finset V)
    (hX1 : X.Nonempty) (hX2 : (Xᶜ : Finset V).Nonempty)
    (hk : (G.edgeFinset.filter (fun e => ∃ u ∈ X, ∃ v ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V), e = s(u, v))).card
      < G.minDegree) :
    ∃ (x y : V) (f : V → ℝ), G.dist x y = 3 ∧
      (∀ a b : V, f a - f b ≤ (G.dist a b : ℝ)) ∧
      f x - f y = 3 ∧
      (3 - (∑ a ∈ G.neighborFinset x, f a) / (G.degree x : ℝ)
        + (∑ b ∈ G.neighborFinset y, f b) / (G.degree y : ℝ))
        ≤ 2 * ((G.edgeFinset.filter (fun e => ∃ u ∈ X, ∃ v ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V), e = s(u, v))).card : ℝ) /
            (G.minDegree : ℝ)

open.name: exists_dist_three_lly_curvature_le_cut
open.informal: For any finite connected graph G with diameter at least 3 and any non-trivial vertex cut (X, X^c), κ_LLY^(3)(G) ≤ 2 |E(X, X^c)| / (3 δ(G)).
open.statement:
theorem exists_dist_three_lly_curvature_le_cut
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : G.Connected) (hd : 3 ≤ G.diam) (X : Finset V)
    (hX1 : X.Nonempty) (hX2 : (Xᶜ : Finset V).Nonempty) :
    graph_lly_curvature_lower_bound G 3 ≤
      (2 * ((G.edgeFinset.filter (fun e => ∃ u ∈ X, ∃ v ∈ (Xᶜ : Finset V), e = s(u, v))).card : ℝ)) /
        (3 * (G.minDegree : ℝ))

open.name: exists_nonempty_regular_eight_triangle_distinct
open.informal: There exists a finite simple 8-regular triangle-distinct graph with at least one vertex: a graph on {0,…,n−1}, n ≥ 1, in which every vertex has degree 8 and the triangle-degrees are pairwise distinct.
open.statement:
theorem exists_nonempty_regular_eight_triangle_distinct :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ ∃ G : SimpleGraph (Fin n), ∃ _ : DecidableRel G.Adj,
      G.IsRegularOfDegree 8 ∧ simple_graph_is_triangle_distinct G
open.citation: Open-problem entry OP-123 after arXiv:2610.08478 (Regular K_3-Irregular Graphs of Every Regularity at Least Nine), Sec. 1: regular triangle-distinct graphs exist for every regularity r ≥ 9 (Theorem 1.1), and by earlier work cited there not for r ≤ 7; regularity 8 was narrowed to six possible orders and is open. Replaces exists_regular_eight_triangle_distinct, which omitted n ≥ 1 and is vacuously true at n = 0.

open.name: forall_power_well_covered_diam_le_three_and_twin_free_bounded
open.informal: Let G be a finite simple connected graph with G^d well-covered for every d ≥ 1. Then diam(G) ≤ 3; moreover, there are only finitely many such graphs (up to isomorphism) of diameter exactly 3 without true twins (adjacent u, v with N[u] = N[v]) — stated as a uniform bound M on their number of vertices.
open.statement:
theorem forall_power_well_covered_diam_le_three_and_twin_free_bounded :
    (∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.Connected →
      (∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)) → G.diam ≤ 3) ∧
    ∃ M : ℕ, ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), G.Connected →
      (∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → simple_graph_is_well_covered (simple_graph_power G d)) → G.diam = 3 →
      (∀ u v : V, G.Adj u v → insert u (G.neighborSet u) ≠ insert v (G.neighborSet v)) →
      Fintype.card V ≤ M
open.citation: Open-problem entry OP-160: arXiv:2610.09300 (On graphs whose powers are well-covered), Question 3.9 (the paper knows no example of diameter ≥ 4; every well-covered graph of diameter 2 qualifies). Finitely many isomorphism classes of finite graphs is equivalent to a bound on the order.

open.name: kayak_paddle_leap_group_of_odd_cycles
open.informal: If both cycles of the kayak paddle graph KP(k, m, l) have odd length, its leap group is the symmetric or the alternating group on its N = k + m + l − 1 vertices.
open.statement:
theorem kayak_paddle_leap_group_of_odd_cycles (k m l : ℕ) (hk : 3 ≤ k) (hm : 3 ≤ m) (hl : 1 ≤ l)
    (hko : Odd k) (hmo : Odd m) :
    simple_graph_leap_group (simple_graph_kayak_paddle k m l) = ⊤ ∨
      simple_graph_leap_group (simple_graph_kayak_paddle k m l) = alternatingGroup _
open.citation: arXiv:2610.18463 (The group generated by a graph's derangements), Question 2.20 (and the sentence before it: 'We believe that many, if not all, kayak paddle graphs have leap group equal to either S_n or A_n'); list entry OP-301 (the other half of the classification; the paper proves the case k = m = 3, l = 2n − 5 with leap group S_{2n}, Lemma 2.19).

open.name: mixed_cage_order_one_eq
open.informal: For all z ≥ 1 and g ≥ 3, the minimum order of a mixed graph that is 1-regular in edges and z-regular in arcs with girth g is n(1, z, g) = N(z, g), where N(z, g) = z(g − 1) + 2 if z is even and (z + 1)(g − 1) if z is odd.
open.statement:
theorem mixed_cage_order_one_eq (z g : ℕ) (hz : 1 ≤ z) (hg : 3 ≤ g) :
    mixed_cage_order 1 z g = if Even z then z * (g - 1) + 2 else (z + 1) * (g - 1)
open.citation: arXiv:2610.14110 (New mixed cages, bounds and computational results), Conjecture 2: the paper proves n(1,z,g) ≤ N(z,g) (Theorem 4.2), n(r,z,3) = r + 2z + 1 (Theorem 5.1, so g = 3 holds), and matches N(z,g) computationally for small z and g.

open.name: mixed_cage_order_one_le
open.informal: For z ≥ 1 and g ≥ 3, n(1, z, g) ≤ N(z, g), where N(z, g) = z(g − 1) + 2 for even z and (z + 1)(g − 1) for odd z: the circulant M(z, g) on 2m = N(z, g) vertices with arcs of jumps 1..⌈z/2⌉ and m+1..m+⌊z/2⌋ and the antipodal edges is a (1, z, g)-mixed graph.
open.statement:
theorem mixed_cage_order_one_le (z g : ℕ) (hz : 1 ≤ z) (hg : 3 ≤ g) :
