That is, does every sequence over $(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})^r$ of length $(k + r)q - r$ contain a zero-sum subsequence of length $kq$?
literature.source_title: Generalized Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv Constants for finite abelian groups of rank three
literature.rationale: While settled for rank r = 1, 2, and now r = 3 (by the paper under review), the conjecture remains open for all ranks r ≥ 4.

literature.title: Critical Multiplier for the Generalized Erdős–Ginzburg–Ziv Constant
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group with exponent $\exp(G) = n$, and let $\mathsf{D}(G)$ be the Davenport constant of $G$. Let $\ell(G)$ be the smallest integer $t$ such that $s_{kn}(G) = kn + \mathsf{D}(G) - 1$ holds for every integer $k \ge t$. Is it true that $\ell(G) = \lceil \mathsf{D}(G) / n \rceil$ for every finite abelian group $G$?
literature.source_title: Generalized Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv Constants for finite abelian groups of rank three
literature.rationale: It is known that D(G)/n ≤ ℓ(G) ≤ |G|/n. Determining whether the lower ceiling bound always holds is a major open problem in zero-sum theory cited in the paper.

literature.title: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for Subadditivity of Mutual f-Information
literature.statement: Let f : [0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R} \cup \{+\infty\} be a convex function satisfying f(1) = 0. For finite discrete random variables X, Y, define the mutual f-information by \widetilde{I}_f(X; Y) = D_f(p_{XY} \| p_X p_Y) = \sum_{x, y} p_X(x) p_Y(y) f(p_{XY}(x,y) / (p_X(x) p_Y(y))). Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on f such that for all finite discrete random variables X, Y, Z satisfying p_{XYZ} = p_X p_{Y|X} p_{Z|X} (the Markov chain condition Y \to X \to Z), the subadditivity inequality \widetilde{I}_f(X; YZ) \le \widetilde{I}_f(X; Y) + \widetilde{I}_f(X; Z) holds.
literature.source_title: On the Subadditivity of Mutual f-Information
literature.rationale: The paper establishes a sufficient differential condition on g(x) = x^2 f''(x) and provides several new parametric families of subadditive generators, but notes that a complete necessary and sufficient characterization of all functions f yielding subadditive mutual f-information remains open.

literature.title: Subadditivity of Mutual f-Information for Power Divergences
literature.statement: For \beta \in (0, 1), let f_\beta: [0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R} be the power divergence generator f_\beta(x) = \frac{x^\beta - \beta x + (\beta - 1)}{\beta(\beta - 1)}. For any finite discrete random variables X, Y, Z satisfying the Markov chain relation Y \to X \to Z (i.e., p_{XYZ}(x,y,z) = p_X(x) p_{Y|X}(y|x) p_{Z|X}(z|x)), does the subadditivity inequality \widetilde{I}_{f_\beta}(X; YZ) \le \widetilde{I}_{f_\beta}(X; Y) + \widetilde{I}_{f_\beta}(X; Z) hold for all such distributions, or does there exist a finite alphabet counterexample? In particular, does subadditivity hold for the Hellinger case \beta = 1/2?
literature.source_title: On the Subadditivity of Mutual f-Information
literature.rationale: The paper establishes that f(x) = x log x, f(x) = (x-1) log x, and new families such as f(x) = x log x + (2/3)(\sqrt{x}-1)^2 yield subadditive mutual f-information, but does not address whether the standard Hellinger / Tsallis / power divergences f_\beta(x) = (x^\beta - \beta x + \beta - 1)/(\beta(\beta - 1)) for \beta \in (0, 1) satisfy subadditivity under conditionally independent observations. For \beta = 1/2 (the Hellinger affinity / Bhattacharyya distance), g(x) = x^2 f''(x) = (1/4) \sqrt{x}, which does not satisfy the condition of Theorem 1 since g''(x) < 0 but the differential inequality (3) does not hold without the affine log term.

literature.title: Complete cycle permutations for every $n$
literature.statement: For an integer $n \ge 1$, arrange a permutation $\sigma(1), \ldots, \sigma(n)$ of $\{1, \ldots, n\}$ cyclically around the $n$-cycle. An arc is a nonempty contiguous segment of the cycle (the whole cycle included); its sum is the sum of its labels. Call $\sigma$ complete if every integer $k \in \{1, \ldots, n(n+1)/2\}$ is the sum of some arc. Is there a complete permutation for every $n \ge 1$?
literature.rationale: OP-121 asked whether some n >= 8 admits a complete permutation; it is settled in Lean (n = 8; also n = 9 and n = 10). The paper shows the increasing order fails for n = 6 and every n >= 8, while there are n(n-1)+1 arcs for only n(n+1)/2 targets. A computer search (10-09) found complete placements for every n <= 19 and for n = 21 (exhaustively for n <= 10). The Lean conjecture exists_cycle_labeling_complete was retired on 10-17 as out of reach: no general construction is known. A uniform construction, or a family of n with none, would answer it.

literature.title: Exact edge-connectivity threshold $c(n)$ for positive Lin-Lu-Yau curvature, general $n$
literature.statement: For each integer $n \ge 3$, let $c(n)$ be the smallest integer $k$ such that every connected simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with edge-connectivity $\kappa'(G) \ge k$ has $\kappa_{LLY}(x, y) > 0$ on every edge $xy$. The paper gives $c(n) \le \lceil 2n/3 - 1 \rceil$ for all $n$, with equality when $2n/3$ is an even integer $\ge 6$; but $c(3) = 0$ and $c(5) = 2$ lie below that bound. Determine $c(n)$ for the remaining $n$. In particular, is $c(n) = \lceil 2n/3 - 1 \rceil$ for all sufficiently large $n$?
literature.rationale: OP-165 asked whether c(n) = ceil(2n/3 - 1) for all n >= 3; Lean refutes it (c(3) = 0, and c(5) = 2 against 3). Theorem 1.3 (edge-connectivity >= 2n/3 - 1 suffices) is proved in Lean; Theorem 1.4 shows sharpness only when 2n/3 is an even integer >= 6. So the exact threshold is known only on that arithmetic progression, and small n behave differently. The next steps are c(4), c(6), c(7), c(8) by finite search, then lower-bound constructions for n not covered by Theorem 1.4.

literature.title: The Lonely Runner Conjecture
literature.statement: Let $n \ge 1$ be an integer, and let $V \subset \mathbb{N}$ be a set of $n$ distinct positive integers. Is it true that $\mathrm{ML}(V) = \max_{t \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}} \min_{v \in V} \|v t\| \ge \frac{1}{n+1}$, where $\|x\| = \mathrm{dist}(x, \mathbb{Z})$ denotes the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer?
literature.source_title: Near optimal gap in the Lonely Runner Conjecture

literature.title: Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture
literature.statement: Let $D = (V, E)$ be a finite loopless directed graph with no source (every vertex has in-degree at least 1). A subset $Q \subseteq V$ is an independent set if there is no directed arc between any pair of distinct vertices in $Q$. A subset $Q$ is a quasi-kernel of $D$ if $Q$ is independent and every vertex in $V$ is reachable from $Q$ by a directed path of length at most 2. Does every such source-free digraph $D$ contain a quasi-kernel $Q$ such that $|Q| \le |V|/2$?
literature.source_title: Small and large quasi-kernels: a weighted transfer theorem

literature.title: Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture
literature.statement: Let $D = (V, E)$ be a finite loopless directed graph. For any subset $Q \subseteq V$, let $N_D^+[Q] = Q \cup \{v \in V \setminus Q : \exists u \in Q, (u, v) \in E\}$ denote the closed out-neighbourhood of $Q$. Does every digraph $D$ admit a quasi-kernel $Q$ (an independent set reaching every vertex in at most two steps) such that $|N_D^+[Q]| \ge |V|/2$?
literature.source_title: Small and large quasi-kernels: a weighted transfer theorem

literature.title: Convergence of iterated Round Robin under adjacent swaps for two agents
literature.statement: Let there be n = 2 agents and m >= 5 items allocated using the Round Robin sequence pi = (1, 2, 1, 2, ...). Each agent has an additive utility function consistent with a strict linear order over the items. In iterated Round Robin starting from truthful preferences, at each step an agent who can strictly improve their utility by exchanging two adjacent items in their reported ranking performs a best-response adjacent swap. Does this iterated Round Robin dynamic always converge to a pure Nash equilibrium under adjacent swaps for all m >= 5, or can it enter a cycle?
literature.source_title: On the Convergence of Iterated Round Robin
literature.rationale: The paper proves that iterated Round Robin under adjacent swaps converges to a pure Nash equilibrium for n = 2 and m = 4, but may cycle for n = 3 and m = 5; it conjectures that for n = 2, convergence holds for all m.

literature.title: Polynomial bound on convergence of iterated Round Robin under item-preserving swaps
literature.statement: Let n >= 3 be a fixed number of agents, and let m items be allocated via the Round Robin sequence pi = (1, 2, ..., n, 1, 2, ...). Agents have additive valuations consistent with strict linear preference rankings over items. In iterated Round Robin starting from truthful preferences, at each step an agent performs a strictly profitable item-preserving swap (exchanging two items in their reported ranking such that an item initially allocated to the agent is demoted yet remains allocated to that agent after the swap). Is the maximum number of manipulations in any such execution bounded by a polynomial in m, or can it be superpolynomial in m?
literature.source_title: On the Convergence of Iterated Round Robin
literature.rationale: Theorem 3.13 proves that iterated Round Robin under item-preserving swaps converges to a pure Nash equilibrium for any n >= 2 and m items within m! - 1 steps. For n = 2, Theorem 3.12 proves convergence in at most m(m-1)/2 steps via a potential function based on Kendall tau distance. The authors note that the Kendall tau argument does not extend to n >= 3 (the sum of pairwise Kendall tau distances can increase), leaving a large gap between the O(m^2) bound for two agents and the O(m!) bound for three or more agents.

literature.title: Sharp Hole Budget Bound for Second-Order Augmented Zarankiewicz Numbers
literature.statement: For all integers m, n >= 2, is the second-order augmented Zarankiewicz number bounded by the second-order Zarankiewicz number and the hole deficit according to z_{2A}(m,n) <= z_2(m,n) + floor(H_limited(m,n) / 3), where H_limited(m,n) = mn + z(m,n) - 2*z_2(m,n) is the number of unoccupied cells in a limited extremal configuration on the m x n grid?
literature.source_title: Overtake and the recursive-line equality for second-order Zarankiewicz numbers
literature.rationale: The paper proves that z_{2A} <= z_2 + floor((H_limited - 1)/2) and that every unit move costs 3 holes, conjecturing this sharper bound for all m,n >= 2.

literature.title: Overtake Threshold for Second-Order Zarankiewicz Numbers
literature.statement: For integers m, n with min(m,n) >= 3, does an overtake (the strict inequality z_{2A}(m,n) > z_2(m,n) between the second-order augmented Zarankiewicz number and the second-order Zarankiewicz number) occur if and only if H_limited(m,n) >= 5?
literature.source_title: Overtake and the recursive-line equality for second-order Zarankiewicz numbers

literature.title: Recursive-Line Equality for Second-Order Zarankiewicz Numbers at the Four Unsettled Orders
literature.statement: Does the recursive-line equality z_2(m,n) = z_RL(m,n) hold at the four open orders (m,n) in {(12,4), (14,4), (11,5), (8,7)} in the range n <= 7, yielding the exact values z_2(12,4) = 32, z_2(14,4) = z_RL(14,4), z_2(11,5) = 37, and z_2(8,7) = 38?
literature.source_title: Overtake and the recursive-line equality for second-order Zarankiewicz numbers

literature.title: Tight universal EF1 approximation factor for Round-Robin pure Nash equilibria
literature.statement: Let alpha_RR be the supremum of all constants alpha in [0, 1] such that for every instance with n agents and m indivisible goods with nonnegative additive valuations, every pure Nash equilibrium of the Round-Robin mechanism induces an alpha-EF1 allocation with respect to the agents' true valuations. What is the exact value of alpha_RR, which is currently known only to satisfy 1/2 <= alpha_RR <= 2/3?
literature.source_title: Revisiting the Fairness of Pure Nash Equilibria of Round-Robin
literature.rationale: The paper proves every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin is 1/2-EF1 (Theorem 1) and provides a family of equilibria showing no factor strictly greater than 2/3 is guaranteed (Theorem 2). The exact value of alpha_RR in [1/2, 2/3] remains unknown.

literature.title: Equivalence of EF1 guarantees for Round-Robin and recursively balanced sequences
literature.statement: Let alpha_RR be the largest universal EF1 approximation factor guaranteed at every pure Nash equilibrium of every Round-Robin instance with additive valuations, and let alpha_RB be the corresponding factor for all fixed recursively balanced picking sequence mechanisms. Does allowing the agent picking order to vary across rounds strictly decrease the worst-case EF1 guarantee, i.e., is alpha_RB < alpha_RR, or is alpha_RB = alpha_RR?
literature.source_title: Revisiting the Fairness of Pure Nash Equilibria of Round-Robin
literature.rationale: The lower bound of 1/2 applies to all recursively balanced picking sequences, while the upper-bound construction of 2/3 uses standard Round-Robin where the order of agents is identical in every round. Whether varying the order between rounds can strictly degrade the worst-case EF1 factor is open.

literature.title: Best guaranteed EF1 factor for Round-Robin pure Nash equilibria with three agents
literature.statement: For fair division with indivisible goods and additive valuations allocated via the Round-Robin mechanism with n = 3 agents, what is the supremum alpha_RR(3) of factors alpha in [0, 1] such that every pure Nash equilibrium induces an alpha-EF1 allocation? In particular, is alpha_RR(3) equal to 15/16 (the bound from the 8-good counterexample), or does it decrease towards 2/3 as the number of goods grows?
literature.source_title: Revisiting the Fairness of Pure Nash Equilibria of Round-Robin
literature.rationale: For two agents, every pure Nash equilibrium of Round-Robin is 1-EF1. For three agents, Proposition 1 shows that 1-EF1 fails and yields an upper bound of 15/16 with 8 goods. It is open whether 15/16 is the tight worst-case factor for three agents or whether the guarantee decreases as the number of rounds grows.

literature.title: Closing the gap between 3/2 and O(log n) metric distortion for deterministic ordinal MST
literature.statement: Let V be a finite set of n vertices and d a pseudometric on V. An ordinal profile π consistent with d specifies, for each v ∈ V, a strict ranking of V \ {v} where u appears before w whenever d(v, u) < d(v, w). A deterministic ordinal algorithm takes π and outputs a spanning tree T of the complete graph on V. Its distortion is sup_{d consistent with π} cost_d(T) / cost_d(MST_d). Does there exist a deterministic ordinal algorithm with distortion o(log n) (or O(1)) on all finite metric spaces, or does every deterministic ordinal algorithm have distortion ω(1) or Ω(log n)?
literature.source_title: On the Metric Distortion of the Minimum Spanning Tree Problem
literature.rationale: The paper establishes an upper bound of 2 ceil(log_2 n) on the metric distortion of deterministic ordinal algorithms for minimum spanning trees, and a lower bound of 3/2 - ε. Closing this exponential gap between O(log n) and 3/2 is the central open problem left by the paper.

literature.title: Minimality of g-adic Asymptotic Bases for Partitions with g at Most h
literature.statement: Let $g, h$ be integers with $2 \leq g \leq h$. For any nonempty subset $W \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, define $A_g(W) = \{\sum_{f \in F} a_f g^f : F \subseteq W \text{ finite nonempty}, 1 \leq a_f \leq g - 1\}$. Given a partition $\mathbb{N} = W_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup W_h$ into $h$ infinite pairwise disjoint sets, let $A = \bigcup_{i=1}^h A_g(W_i)$. Under the product probability measure on partitions $\mathbb{N} \to \{1, \dots, h\}$ where each natural number is assigned independently and uniformly at random to one of the $h$ parts with probability $1/h$, is $A$ almost surely a minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$?
literature.source_title: Minimal asymptotic \(g\)-adic bases from arbitrary partitions
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.1 settles Problem 2 affirmatively for all infinite partitions when g > h. The question remains open when 2 ≤ g ≤ h, where counterexamples exist for specific partitions and the almost-sure behavior is unknown.

literature.title: Existence of Minimal Mixed Orthogonal Arrays of Strength Two with Six Factors for Nine Parameter Sets
literature.statement: Let a mixed orthogonal array $\text{MOA}(N; s_1 s_2 \dots s_k, t)$ be an $N \times k$ array with entries in column $i$ from $\{0, 1, \dots, s_i - 1\}$ such that in every $N \times t$ subarray, every possible $t$-tuple of symbols occurs equally often as a row (with frequency $N / \prod_{j \in J} s_j$ for each column index subset $J$ of size $t$). For a 6-tuple of factor levels $(a,b,c,d,e,f)$ with each entry $> 1$, let $M = \operatorname{lcm}\{\alpha\beta : \{\alpha,\beta\} \subset \{a,b,c,d,e,f\}\}$. Let $\mathcal{P}$ denote the set of nine 6-tuples of factor levels: $(10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10)$ with $M = 100$; $(10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 5)$ with $M = 100$; $(10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 2)$ with $M = 100$; $(10, 10, 10, 10, 5, 5)$ with $M = 100$; $(10, 10, 10, 10, 2, 5)$ with $M = 100$; $(22, 22, 22, 22, 22, 22)$ with $M = 484$; $(22, 22, 22, 22, 22, 11)$ with $M = 484$; $(22, 22, 22, 22, 22, 2)$ with $M = 484$; and $(22, 22, 22, 22, 11, 11)$ with $M = 484$. For each $abcdef \in \mathcal{P}$, does there exist an $\text{MOA}(M; a b c d e f, 2)$?
literature.source_title: On the existence of mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors

literature.title: Existence Spectrum of Minimal Mixed Orthogonal Arrays of Strength Two with Seven Factors
literature.statement: Let a mixed orthogonal array $\text{MOA}(N; s_1 s_2 \dots s_7, 2)$ be an $N \times 7$ array where each column $i$ has symbols from $\{0, \dots, s_i - 1\}$ such that in every pair of distinct columns $i, j$, each pair of symbols occurs equally often as a row (namely $N / (s_i s_j)$ times). For integers $a,b,c,d,e,f,g > 1$, define the minimal necessary run size $M^* = \operatorname{lcm}\{\alpha\beta : \{\alpha,\beta\} \subset \{a,b,c,d,e,f,g\}\}$. For which 7-tuples $(a,b,c,d,e,f,g)$ does there exist an $\text{MOA}(M^*; abcdefg, 2)$?
literature.source_title: On the existence of mixed orthogonal arrays of strength two with six factors

literature.title: Exact Communication Complexity of OR in Multiparty Private Simultaneous Messages
literature.statement: What is the asymptotic communication complexity of the n-party OR function OR_n(x_1, ..., x_n) = ⋁_{i=1}^n x_i (where each party holds one input bit x_i) in a perfectly correct, support-private (or perfectly private) Private Simultaneous Messages protocol? Specifically, is C(OR_n) = Θ(n log n), or does there exist a protocol with communication complexity o(n log n)?
literature.source_title: On the Complexity of Symmetric Boolean Functions in Multiparty Private Simultaneous Messages

literature.title: Decidability of Reachability for Symmetric d-Counter Machines with d >= 3
literature.statement: Let d ≥ 3 be an integer. A d-counter machine M = (Q, T) consists of a finite state set Q and transitions T ⊆ Q × I × Q, where instructions I are counter updates update(w) with w ∈ ℤ^d and zero-tests zero-test(i) for i ∈ {1, ..., d}. The machine is symmetric if its update transitions are invariant under the action of the full symmetric group S_d on coordinates (with no symmetry restriction on zero-tests). Is the configuration-to-configuration reachability problem decidable for symmetric d-counter machines?
literature.source_title: Symmetric two-counter machines
literature.rationale: The paper proves decidability for symmetric 2-counter machines (Theorem 1) and undecidability for cyclic permutation groups of order d >= 3 (Theorem 2), but leaves open whether symmetry under the full symmetric group S_d makes reachability decidable for d >= 3.

literature.title: Semilinearity of Reachability Relations in Symmetric Two-Counter Machines
literature.statement: Let M = (Q, T) be a symmetric 2-counter machine. For each pair of states q, q' ∈ Q, let R_{q, q'} ⊆ ℕ^2 × ℕ^2 denote the set of pairs of counter vectors (u, v) such that configuration (q', v) is reachable from configuration (q, u) in M. Is R_{q, q'} a semilinear subset of ℕ^4 (that is, a finite union of linear sets, or equivalently, definable in Presburger arithmetic)?
literature.source_title: Symmetric two-counter machines
literature.rationale: Effective semilinearity of reachability sets is known for 2-VASS and symmetric 2-VASS, and the paper proves effective semilinearity of certain 1-dimensional boundary reachability slices, but leaves open whether the full 4-dimensional reachability relation is semilinear.

literature.title: Expressiveness and Complexity of Single-Counter Update Symmetric Counter Machines
literature.statement: Consider the syntactic fragment of symmetric d-counter machines (for d ≥ 2) in which all update transitions (q, update(w), q') are single-counter, meaning that w has at most one non-zero coordinate, while zero-test transitions remain unrestricted. Is this single-counter fragment strictly less expressive than unrestricted symmetric d-counter machines in terms of reachability relations, and what is the computational complexity of its reachability problem?
literature.source_title: Symmetric two-counter machines
literature.rationale: The paper shows that if both zero-tests and updates are restricted to single counters / symmetric, the model degenerates to 1-VASS, but the expressive power and complexity when only update instructions are restricted to single-counter modifications remains open.

literature.title: Competitive ratio of Greedy for online triangle-free-crossing matching
literature.statement: Let P ⊂ ℝ² be a finite set of points in general position. A set of straight-line segments L with endpoints in P is triangle-free-crossing if no three segments in L pairwise cross (their relative interiors do not pairwise intersect). A triangle-free family L of ℓ segments blocks an unmatched point set Q ⊂ ℝ² (in general position with L) if for every pair of distinct points u, v ∈ Q, the segment uv pairwise crosses two segments of L that cross each other, so that L ∪ {uv} is not triangle-free. Let β_△(ℓ) be the maximum cardinality of a point set blocked by a triangle-free family of ℓ segments. Is it true that for every positive integer ℓ, β_△(ℓ) ≤ ℓ? Equivalently, does the deterministic Greedy algorithm for online triangle-free-crossing geometric matching have asymptotic competitive ratio at least 2/3?
literature.source_title: Online geometric matching and segments block points

literature.title: Deterministic online algorithm beating two-thirds competitive ratio for k-crossing matching
literature.statement: In the online geometric k-crossing matching problem, an adversary presents a sequence of n points in ℝ² in general position one by one. Upon the arrival of each point v, an online algorithm must either irrevocably match v to an existing unmatched point u or leave v unmatched, subject to the constraint that in the resulting geometric matching L, each straight-line segment crosses the relative interior of at most k other matched segments. For every fixed integer k ≥ 1, does there exist a deterministic online algorithm that achieves an asymptotic competitive ratio strictly greater than 2/3?
literature.source_title: Online geometric matching and segments block points

literature.title: Lower bound on triangle-free blocking number by vertex cover number
literature.statement: Let L be a finite family of ℓ straight-line segments in ℝ² in general position whose crossing graph G(L) (with edges between segments whose relative interiors intersect) is triangle-free. Let τ(G(L)) denote the minimum vertex cover size of G(L), and let τ(ℓ) = max { τ(G(L)) : |L| = ℓ, G(L) is triangle-free }. Let β_△(L) be the maximum cardinality of a point set P ⊂ ℝ² blocked by L under the triangle-free crossing property (meaning for every pair of distinct points u, v ∈ P, adding segment uv creates a triangle in the crossing graph), and let β_△(ℓ) = max_{|L|=ℓ} β_△(L). Is it true that for every positive integer ℓ, β_△(ℓ) ≥ τ(ℓ)? Furthermore, does β_△(L) ≥ τ(G(L)) hold for every triangle-free family of segments L?
literature.source_title: Online geometric matching and segments block points

literature.title: Optimal randomized competitive ratio for online noncrossing geometric matching
literature.statement: In the online noncrossing geometric matching problem, points in ℝ² in general position arrive one by one, and an algorithm must irrevocably match arriving points with noncrossing straight-line segments. What is the supremum of competitive ratios ρ achievable by randomized online algorithms against an oblivious adversary? (The best known bounds establish that ρ lies in [0.67034, 6/7].)
literature.source_title: Online geometric matching and segments block points

literature.title: Simonovits-Sos Conjecture on 3-AP-Intersecting Families
literature.statement: Let $n \ge 3$ be an integer. A non-constant 3-term arithmetic progression (3-AP) in $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is a set of the form $\{a, a+d, a+2d\}$ with $a, d \ge 1$ and $a+2d \le n$. A family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is 3-AP-intersecting if for every pair of sets $F_1, F_2 \in \mathcal{F}$, the intersection $F_1 \cap F_2$ contains at least one non-constant 3-AP. Does every 3-AP-intersecting family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ satisfy $|\mathcal{F}| \le 2^{n-3}$ (or equivalently, does the maximum uniform density satisfy $m_3 = 1/8$)?
literature.source_title: Families that intersect in an arithmetic progression

literature.title: Generalized Simonovits-Sos Conjecture on k-AP-Intersecting Families
literature.statement: For integers $k \ge 3$ and $n \ge k$, a $k$-term arithmetic progression ($k$-AP) in $\{1, \dots, n\}$ is a set $Q(a,d) = \{a, a+d, \dots, a+(k-1)d\}$ with $a, d \ge 1$ and $a+(k-1)d \le n$. A family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is $k$-AP-intersecting if $F_1 \cap F_2$ contains a $k$-AP for all $F_1, F_2 \in \mathcal{F}$. Let $m_{k,n} = \max \{|\mathcal{F}| / 2^n : \mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^{[n]} \text{ is } k\text{-AP-intersecting}\}$ and $m_k = \lim_{n \to \infty} m_{k,n}$. Is $m_k = 2^{-k}$ for all $k \ge 3$?
literature.source_title: Families that intersect in an arithmetic progression

literature.title: Multiplicative Merino-Welsh conjecture for general graphs
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a finite connected loopless bridgeless graph. Let $\tau(G)$ denote the number of spanning trees of $G$, $\alpha(G)$ the number of acyclic orientations of $G$, and $\alpha^*(G)$ the number of totally cyclic orientations of $G$. Is it true that $\alpha(G)\alpha^*(G) \ge \tau(G)^2$, and in particular $\max\{\alpha(G), \alpha^*(G)\} \ge \tau(G)$?
literature.source_title: The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality for chordal graphs
literature.rationale: The original Merino-Welsh conjecture and its multiplicative strengthening remain open for general connected bridgeless graphs, as explicitly discussed in the paper's introduction.

literature.title: Orientation and spanning tree bounds for unions with non-clique intersection
literature.statement: Let $H$ and $J$ be connected simple graphs intersecting in a subgraph $S = H \cap J$ that is not necessarily a clique, with $p = |V(S)|$. Can upper bounds on the spanning tree count $\tau(H \cup J)$ analogous to $\tau(H \cup J)/\tau(H) \le \tau(K_p \cup J)/\tau(K_p)$, and corresponding lower bounds on acyclic and totally cyclic orientation counts of $H \cup J$, be established for non-clique intersections $S$?
literature.source_title: The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality for chordal graphs

literature.title: Worst-case approximation ratio of the better of separate selling and bundling
literature.statement: For an additive buyer with $m$ independent items distributed according to a product distribution $D = \prod_{j=1}^m F_j$ on $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^m$ with finite monopoly revenues, let $\mathrm{REV}(D)$ denote the optimal truthful, individually rational auction revenue, $\mathrm{SREV}(D) = \sum_{j=1}^m \sup_{p \ge 0} p \Pr[V_j \ge p]$ denote the revenue from selling items separately, and $\mathrm{BREV}(D) = \sup_{p \ge 0} p \Pr[\sum_{j=1}^m V_j \ge p]$ denote the revenue from selling the grand bundle at a single price. What is the exact worst-case approximation ratio $\sup_D \frac{\mathrm{REV}(D)}{\max\{\mathrm{SREV}(D), \mathrm{BREV}(D)\}}$, currently known to lie in the interval $[2.11, 1 + \pi^2/6] \approx [2.11, 2.645]$?
literature.source_title: Improved Approximation and Tight Competition for Simple Auctions
literature.rationale: The paper narrows the worst-case approximation ratio C = sup_D REV(D) / max{SREV(D), BREV(D)} to the interval [2.11, 1 + π^2/6] ≈ [2.11, 2.645], leaving the exact tight constant open.

literature.title: Existence of a balanced 6-coloring of K_36
literature.statement: Does the complete graph $K_{36}$ admit a balanced 6-coloring? That is, does there exist a 6-coloring of the edges of $K_{36}$, $c : E(K_{36}) \to \{1, \dots, 6\}$, such that every subset of 7 vertices spans at least one edge of each of the 6 colors (equivalently, such that $E(K_{36})$ can be partitioned into 6 graphs each having independence number at most 6)?
literature.source_title: Erd\H{o}s-Gy\'arf\'as Balanced Five-Colorings
literature.rationale: For prime powers $r$, an affine plane of order $r$ yields a balanced $r$-coloring of $K_{r^2}$. Because 6 is not a prime power, no affine plane of order 6 exists (Tarry 1901; Bruck-Ryser theorem). It is therefore unknown whether $K_{36}$ admits any balanced 6-coloring at all, or whether non-affine balanced colorings can reach $r^2$ when affine planes fail.

literature.title: Erdos-Gyarfas balanced coloring conjecture for r at least 6
literature.statement: For every integer $r \ge 6$, does there exist no balanced $r$-coloring of the complete graph $K_{r^2 + 1}$? That is, is it true that for every $r \ge 6$, every edge coloring $c : E(K_{r^2 + 1}) \to \{1, \dots, r\}$ contains a subset of $r+1$ vertices that misses at least one color?
literature.source_title: Erd\H{o}s-Gy\'arf\'as Balanced Five-Colorings
literature.rationale: The conjecture was posed by Erdős and Gyárfás in 1999 and proved for $r = 3$ and $r = 4$. This paper proves the $r = 5$ case ($K_{26}$ has no balanced 5-coloring). All cases $r \ge 6$ remain open.

literature.title: Boundedness of finite Heesch numbers in the Euclidean plane
literature.statement: Does there exist an upper bound M in ℕ such that every planar shape T in ℝ² (a compact set equal to the closure of its interior) with a finite Heesch number satisfies H(T) ≤ M? Equivalently, are finite Heesch numbers in the Euclidean plane bounded above, or do there exist planar figures with arbitrarily large finite Heesch numbers?
literature.source_title: The Heesch number in $\mathbb{E}^3$ is unbounded
literature.rationale: Heesch's problem in dimension 2 is the seminal problem left open; this paper resolves the question in all dimensions d >= 3 by establishing that Heesch numbers are unbounded there.

literature.title: Decidability of the planar monotile tiling problem
literature.statement: Is the tiling problem for a single prototile in the Euclidean plane algorithmically decidable? That is, does there exist an algorithm that, given any planar polygon with rational coordinates, decides whether congruent copies of the polygon can tile the Euclidean plane without gaps or overlaps?
literature.source_title: The Heesch number in $\mathbb{E}^3$ is unbounded
literature.rationale: The paper highlights the connection between bounds on Heesch numbers and the algorithmic decidability of tiling for a single prototile.

literature.title: Antisymmetric Z_5-flows in fixed orientations of 8-edge-connected graphs
literature.statement: Let G = (V, E) be a finite multigraph with edge-connectivity at least 8. For every orientation of the edges of G, does there exist an antisymmetric circulation over the additive group Z/5Z, meaning a function f : E -> Z/5Z with non-zero net divergence zero at every vertex such that for every edge e in E, f(e) does not equal 0 and f(e) does not equal -f(e) (equivalently, f(e) in {1, 2} under standard identification of Z/5Z)?
literature.source_title: Graphic additive bases and graph flows
literature.rationale: The paper proves that 10-edge-connected graphs admit an antisymmetric Z_5-flow in every orientation (improving the earlier bound of 12), leaving open whether 8-edge-connectivity suffices as conjectured in the literature.

literature.title: Edge-connectivity threshold for modulo-7 orientations and strong Z_7-connectivity
literature.statement: Is the minimum edge-connectivity guaranteeing that every graph has a modulo-7 orientation (an orientation where every vertex outdegree is congruent to indegree modulo 7) equal to 13 or 14? Equivalently, does every 13-edge-connected graph admit a modulo-7 orientation?
literature.source_title: Graphic additive bases and graph flows
literature.rationale: For k = 3 (modulus 7), 12-edge-connected counterexamples are known and the paper proves sufficiency of (4k+2) = 14-edge-connectivity. It remains open whether the sharp threshold is 13 or 14.

literature.title: Size Ramsey numbers of star forests with at least three components
literature.statement: Let $s, t \ge 3$ be integers, and let $n_1 \ge \cdots \ge n_s \ge 1$ and $m_1 \ge \cdots \ge m_t \ge 1$ be non-increasing sequences of positive integers. Is the size Ramsey number of the disjoint union of stars $\bigsqcup_{i=1}^s K_{1, n_i}$ versus $\bigsqcup_{j=1}^t K_{1, m_j}$ equal to $\sum_{k=2}^{s+t} \ell_k$, where $\ell_k = \max_{i+j=k} \{n_i + m_j - 1\}$?
literature.source_title: Size Ramsey numbers of star forests with two components on one side
literature.rationale: This settles the remaining open case of the star forest conjecture (Erdős Problem #561) posed by Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp in 1978. The paper resolves all cases where one forest has at most two components; the case where both have at least three components is the remaining hurdle.

literature.title: Asymptotic multi-label radio number of paths
literature.statement: For any integers $k \ge 1$ and $m \ge 1$, does there exist an integer $n_0$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$, the $(m,k)$-radio number of the path graph $P_n$ of order $n$ satisfies $\lambda_k^m(P_n) = \lceil (k+1)^2 / 2 \rceil m - 1$?
literature.source_title: On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs
literature.rationale: Proved for k=1, k=2, and upper bound proved for k=3. Conjectured for all k and m for sufficiently large paths.

literature.title: Asymptotic upper bound on multi-label radio number of cycles
literature.statement: For any integers $k \ge 1$ and $m \ge 1$, does there exist an integer $n_0$ such that for every $n \ge n_0$, the $(m,k)$-radio number of the cycle graph $C_n$ of order $n$ satisfies $\lambda_k^m(C_n) \le \lceil (k+1)^2 / 2 \rceil m$?
literature.source_title: On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs
literature.rationale: Proved for k=1 and for k=2 when 2 <= m <= 4 or n is a multiple of 5. Conjectured for all k and m for sufficiently large cycles.

literature.title: Optimal polynomial-time approximation threshold for symmetric bimatrix games
literature.statement: Let ε_sym* be the infimum of all ε ∈ (0, 1) such that there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that, given any symmetric bimatrix game (A, Aᵀ) with payoff matrix A ∈ [0, 1]^{n × n}, computes a mixed strategy p ∈ Δ_n satisfying Reg(p) = max_{i ∈ [n]} e_iᵀ A p - pᵀ A p ≤ ε. What is the value of ε_sym*? Specifically, does ε_sym* = 0 (admitting a PTAS), or is ε_sym* strictly positive, and does it match 1 - 1/√2?
literature.source_title: Breaking the 1/3 Barrier for Approximate Nash Equilibria in Symmetric Bimatrix Games
literature.rationale: The paper achieves a limiting factor 1 - 1/√2 ≈ 0.29289 for symmetric bimatrix games, breaking the 1/3 barrier, but leaves open what the best possible polynomial-time approximation guarantee is and whether there is a matching PPAD-hardness threshold.

literature.title: VNP-Completeness of the Vandermonde Permanent
literature.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ be an integer. The Vandermonde permanent in $n$ variables $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is defined by
$$\operatorname{VPer}_n(x_1, \ldots, x_n) \coloneqq \operatorname{Per}\left((x_i^j)_{i,j \in [n]}\right) = \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\sigma(i)},$$
which equals the monomial symmetric polynomial $m_{(n, n-1, \ldots, 1)}(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ of degree $\binom{n+1}{2}$. Is the polynomial family $(\operatorname{VPer}_n)_{n \ge 1}$ $\mathsf{VNP}$-complete under $c$-reductions (or under $p$-projections)? In particular, does computing $\operatorname{VPer}_n$ require arithmetic circuits of superpolynomial size over $\mathbb{C}$, assuming $\mathsf{VP} \ne \mathsf{VNP}$?
literature.source_title: When Are Monomial Symmetric Polynomials Hard?
literature.location: Sec. 5, Removal of variable count restriction
literature.rationale: All hardness results in the paper require the number of variables to be at least the degree because they rely on the algebraic independence of power sum symmetric polynomials. The Vandermonde permanent is the canonical test case with few variables (n) but large degree (n(n+1)/2) where this independence fails.

literature.title: Complexity of Monomial Symmetric Polynomials with Subpolynomially Many Distinct Parts
literature.statement: Let $\bm{\lambda}_n$ be a sequence of integer partitions with $D(\bm{\lambda}_n)$ distinct parts and degree $d(\bm{\lambda}_n)$, and let $v_n \ge d(\bm{\lambda}_n)$ be a sequence of variable counts such that $(m_{\bm{\lambda}_n}(x_1, \ldots, x_{v_n}))_{n \ge 1}$ forms a $p$-family of polynomials over $\mathbb{C}$. Suppose that $D(\bm{\lambda}_n) = \omega(1)$ as $n \to \infty$, but $D(\bm{\lambda}_n) \le n^{o(1)}$ (for example, $D(\bm{\lambda}_n) = \Theta(\log^c n)$ for some constant $c \ge 1$). What is the algebraic circuit complexity of the family $(m_{\bm{\lambda}_n})_{n \ge 1}$? Specifically, can every such family be computed by polynomial-size arithmetic circuits (i.e., is it in $\mathsf{VP}$), or are there such families that are $\mathsf{VNP}$-complete under $c$-reductions, or does parameterization by $D(\bm{\lambda})$ yield a separation under parameterized algebraic complexity assumptions such as $\mathsf{VFPT} \ne \mathsf{VW}[1]$?
literature.source_title: When Are Monomial Symmetric Polynomials Hard?
literature.location: Sec. 5, Fine-grained complexity in the middle regime
literature.rationale: The paper establishes polynomial-size circuits for O(1) distinct parts and VNP-completeness for n^Ω(1) distinct parts (when n >= deg), leaving open the intermediate subpolynomial regime such as polylogarithmic growth.

literature.title: Optimality of the Product Construction for Intersection-Union Families
literature.statement: Let $n, p, q$ be positive integers with $p, q \ge 2$ and $n \ge p + q$. A family $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is $p$-intersecting if $|F \cap F'| \ge p$ for all $F, F' \in \mathcal{F}$, and $q$-union if $|F \cup F'| \le n - q$ for all $F, F' \in \mathcal{F}$. Let $w(n,p,q) = \max \{|\mathcal{F}|/2^n : \mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^{[n]} \text{ is } p\text{-intersecting and } q\text{-union}\}$. For $t \ge 1$ and $m \ge t$, let $w(m,t) = \max \{|\mathcal{A}|/2^m : \mathcal{A} \subseteq 2^{[m]} \text{ is } t\text{-intersecting}\}$. Does the product construction always maximize the uniform measure of a $(p,q)$-family, that is, does $w(n,p,q) = \max_{n_1 + n_2 = n} w(n_1,p) w(n_2,q)$ hold for all $p, q \ge 2$ and all $n \ge p + q$?
literature.source_title: Proving the optimality of the product construction for the intersection--union problem
literature.rationale: The paper proves the conjecture for all n ≥ 2^15 (p+q-2)^3. Prior work established it for n ≤ p+q + (1/2)(p+q)^{1/3} and for p=1 or q=1. This leaves open the intermediate range p+q < n < 2^15 (p+q-2)^3 for all p, q ≥ 2.

literature.title: Value of the Growth Exponent gamma_3 for S_3-Free Poset Dimension
literature.statement: Let $f(3, n)$ denote the maximum dimension of an $n$-element poset containing no standard example $S_3$ of order 3 as an induced subposet (where $S_3$ consists of minimal elements $a_1, a_2, a_3$ and maximal elements $b_1, b_2, b_3$ such that $a_i \le b_j$ if and only if $i \ne j$). Define the polynomial growth exponent $\gamma_3 = \inf\{\gamma \in [0, 1] : f(3, n) = \mathcal{O}(n^\gamma)\}$. What is the exact value of $\gamma_3$? In particular, is $\gamma_3 = 1/3$, $\gamma_3 = 2/3$, or strictly between $1/3$ and $2/3$?
literature.source_title: On dimension of posets excluding a standard example

literature.title: Adjacency of consecutive binary necklaces under binary reflected Gray order for primes
literature.statement: Let $n > 47$ be an odd prime. Let $D_n$ be the list of all $(2^n-2)/n$ non-constant binary necklaces of length $n$ (equivalence classes of words in $\{0, 1\}^n$ under cyclic shift), ordered by the rank of their first occurrence in the binary reflected Gray code (BRGC) $g(t) = t \oplus \lfloor t/2 \rfloor$ for $t \in \{0, \dots, 2^n-1\}$, where the first occurrence of a necklace is its representative with smallest rank. Are any two consecutive necklaces in $D_n$ adjacent in the necklace graph $Q_n$ (that is, do there exist representatives differing in exactly one bit)?
literature.source_title: Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces

literature.title: Hamiltonicity of middle weight bands in binary necklace graphs
literature.statement: Let $n = 2m+1 \ge 5$ be an odd integer, and let $1 \le \ell \le m$ be an integer. Consider the necklace graph on $\{0, 1\}^n / \mathbb{Z}_n$, where vertices are binary necklaces of length $n$, and two necklaces are adjacent if they have representatives at Hamming distance 1. Is the induced subgraph on the set of necklaces whose Hamming weight (the number of ones in any representative) lies in the interval $[m+1-\ell, m+\ell]$ Hamiltonian?
literature.source_title: Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces

literature.title: Extension of rotation-invariant symmetric chain decompositions to Hamilton cycles in necklace graphs
literature.statement: For every prime $n$, consider the rotation-invariant symmetric chain decomposition of the Boolean lattice $\{0,1\}^n$ into saturated chains invariant under cyclic shifts (which induces a decomposition of the non-constant necklace graph $Q_n$ into paths). Do these paths extend to a Hamilton cycle of $Q_n$ by joining chain bottoms to bottoms and tops to tops?
literature.source_title: Optimal single-track Gray codes from Gray-ordered necklaces

literature.title: Equivalence of strong sl_2-actions and symmetric chain decompositions for ranked posets
literature.statement: Let $P$ be a finite ranked poset with rank function $\omega : P \to \mathbb{Z}$ satisfying $\omega(a) = \omega(b) + 2$ whenever $a \gtrdot b$, with ranks symmetric about 0 (so the minimal rank is $-n$ and the maximal rank is $n$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$). Is it true that $P$ admits a strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-action (linear operators $E, F, H$ on $\mathbb{C}P$ satisfying $[E, F] = H$, $[H, E] = 2E$, $[H, F] = -2F$, with $H x = \omega(x) x$, $E$ supported only on upward cover relations $y \gtrdot x$, and $F$ supported only on downward cover relations $y \lessdot x$) if and only if $P$ admits a symmetric chain decomposition (a partition of $P$ into disjoint saturated chains each starting at rank $-k$ and ending at rank $k$ for some $k$)?
literature.source_title: Strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Actions and Symmetric Chain Decompositions

literature.title: Existence of fractional symmetric chain decompositions for Young lattices and Boolean quotients
literature.statement: For all positive integers $m, n \ge 1$, does the Young lattice $L(m, n)$ (the poset of integer partitions whose Young diagrams fit inside an $m \times n$ bounding box, ordered by inclusion) admit a fractional symmetric chain decomposition? More generally, for any integer $n \ge 1$ and any subgroup $G \subseteq S_n$ acting on the Boolean lattice $\{0, 1\}^n$ by coordinate permutation, does the quotient poset $\{0, 1\}^n / G$ (with orbits ordered by existence of an order relation between representatives) always admit a fractional symmetric chain decomposition?
literature.source_title: Strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Actions and Symmetric Chain Decompositions

literature.title: Bounded denominators of rational fractional symmetric chain decompositions
literature.statement: Let $P$ be a finite ranked poset that admits a fractional symmetric chain decomposition. Is there an upper bound on the minimum positive integer $D$ such that $P$ admits a fractional symmetric chain decomposition with all chain weights in $\frac{1}{D}\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, depending only on the number of ranks of $P$ (or the cardinality of $P$)? In particular, for posets with at most $r$ ranks, does there always exist a rational fractional SCD with denominator bounded by a function of $r$?
literature.source_title: Strong $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Actions and Symmetric Chain Decompositions

literature.title: Spectrality of 16-element translational tiles in F_2^8
literature.statement: Let $E$ be a subset of the eight-dimensional binary vector space $\mathbb{F}_2^8$ with $|E| = 16$. Suppose there exists a subset $T \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^8$ such that $E \oplus T = \mathbb{F}_2^8$ (that is, every element of $\mathbb{F}_2^8$ is uniquely expressible as $e + t$ with $e \in E$ and $t \in T$). Is $E$ necessarily spectral, meaning that there exists a spectrum $B \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^8$ of size 16 such that for all distinct $b, b' \in B$, $\sum_{e \in E} (-1)^{(b + b') \cdot e} = 0$?
literature.source_title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_2^7$

literature.title: Polynomial-time ranking and unranking of S-avoiding permutations for three or more offsets
literature.statement: Let n be a positive integer, and let S ⊂ ℤ be a finite subset with |S| ≥ 3. A permutation π of {1, ..., n} is S-avoiding if π(i) - i - s ≢ 0 (mod n) for every i ∈ {1, ..., n} and every s ∈ S. The lexicographic ranking problem asks for the position of a given S-avoiding permutation in the lexicographic order of all S-avoiding permutations of {1, ..., n}, and the unranking problem asks for the permutation at a given index. Does there exist an algorithm that performs lexicographic ranking and unranking of S-avoiding permutations of {1, ..., n} in time polynomial in n for every fixed finite set S ⊂ ℤ with |S| ≥ 3, or in particular for S = {-1, 0, 1}?
literature.source_title: Unranking $S$-avoiding permutations with two forbidden offsets
literature.rationale: Kagey (Discrete Appl. Math. 355, 2024) posed Open Question 40 asking for polynomial-time ranking and unranking algorithms for S-avoiding permutations. Theorem 5.3 settles the question for all sets S with |S| ≤ 2 by showing the forbidden board graph is 2-regular. The paper explicitly remarks that for |S| ≥ 3, the graph has degree 2(|S|-1) ≥ 4, so prefix deletion can leave components of unbounded treewidth, leaving the complexity open.

literature.title: Gao-Zhuang Conjecture on the Gao Constant of Finite Groups
literature.statement: Let $G$ be a finite group. Is it true that $\mathsf{E}(G) = |G| + \mathsf{d}(G)$, where $\mathsf{E}(G)$ is the Gao constant of $G$ and $\mathsf{d}(G)$ is the small Davenport constant of $G$?
literature.source_title: The Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv theorem for finite groups
literature.rationale: This conjecture (Conjecture 1.3 in the paper) posits that the Gao constant equals |G| + d(G) for every finite group. The paper verifies several bounds and corollaries consistent with it, but the general equality remains open.

literature.title: Nearly doubly regular property of arborescence-maximizing regular tournaments of order 4k + 1
literature.statement: Let $k \ge 1$ be an integer and let $n = 4k + 1$. A tournament $T$ on $n$ vertices is regular if every vertex has outdegree $2k$. For two distinct vertices $i \neq j$, let $c_{ij} = |N_T^+(i) \cap N_T^+(j)|$ denote the number of common outneighbors of $i$ and $j$. The tournament $T$ is called nearly doubly regular if $c_{ij} \in \{k-1, k\}$ for all pairs of distinct vertices $i \neq j$. Is it true that every regular tournament of order $4k+1$ that maximizes the total number of arborescences $\tau(T)$ among all regular tournaments of order $4k+1$ is nearly doubly regular?
literature.source_title: Extremal arborescences in graph orientations
literature.rationale: At order $n \equiv 3 \pmod 4$, arborescence maximizers among regular tournaments are known to be doubly regular tournaments. At order $n = 4k+1$, doubly regular tournaments cannot exist due to non-integrality of common outneighbor counts, and nearly doubly regular (NDR) tournaments are the nearest-integer analogue. The conjecture is verified computationally for orders 5, 9, 13, and 17.

literature.title: Sufficiency of a single chore disposal for MMS allocations
literature.statement: Let $N = \{1, \dots, n\}$ be a set of $n \ge 4$ agents and let $M$ be a finite set of indivisible chores. Each agent $i \in N$ has a nonnegative additive cost function $c_i : 2^M \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ with maximin share benchmark $\mu_i = \min_{X \in \Pi_n(M)} \max_{j \in [n]} c_i(X_j)$. Does there always exist a partial allocation $(X_1, \dots, X_n)$ of $M$ (with pairwise disjoint bundles $X_i \subseteq M$) leaving at most one chore unallocated (that is, $|M \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^n X_i| \le 1$) such that $c_i(X_i) \le \mu_i$ for all $i \in N$?
literature.source_title: MMS Allocation for Chores with Item Disposals

literature.title: Asymptotic Fraction of Planar Points Avoiding Both Minimum and Maximum Distances
literature.statement: Let X ⊂ ℝ² be a finite set of n points with |X| = n ≥ 2, and let a₁ and a_s denote the minimum and maximum pairwise Euclidean distances among distinct points of X, respectively. Let g(X, {a₁, a_s}) denote the maximum size of a subset Y ⊆ X such that no two points in Y are at distance a₁ or a_s, and let g(n, {a₁, a_s}) = min_{|X|=n} g(X, {a₁, a_s}). Theorem 9 establishes that (8n - 20)/47 ≤ g(n, {a₁, a_s}) ≤ 5n/16. What is the value of the asymptotic ratio lim_{n → ∞} g(n, {a₁, a_s}) / n? In particular, does lim_{n → ∞} g(n, {a₁, a_s}) / n = 5/16?
literature.source_title: Avoiding Distances
literature.rationale: Theorem 9 establishes (8n - 20)/47 ≤ g(n, {a₁, a_s}) ≤ 5n/16. Conjecture 19 conjectures that the upper bound 5n/16 - O(1) is the true value. Closing this gap is the central open problem highlighted in the paper and screening note.

literature.title: Independence Ratio of Planar Unit Distance Graphs with Minimum Degree at Least Three
literature.statement: Let X ⊂ ℝ² be a finite set of n points in the plane whose unit distance graph G(X, {1}) (the graph with vertex set X and edges between pairs of points at Euclidean distance 1) has minimum degree at least 3. Does there exist an absolute constant c < 1 (independent of n and X) such that the independence number α(G(X, {1})) ≤ c n for every such point set X?
literature.source_title: Avoiding Distances
literature.rationale: When the minimum degree is 2, the authors give an explicit construction achieving independence ratio 1 - Θ(n^{-1/2}), showing min degree 2 is insufficient. They conjecture that minimum degree at least 3 is sufficient to bound the independence ratio strictly below 1.

literature.title: Asymptotic Dependence of Distance Avoidance Fraction on Number of Forbidden Distances
literature.statement: For positive integers n and k, let g(n, k) denote the minimum over all n-point sets X ⊂ ℝ² and all k-element distance subsets D ⊆ {dist(u, v) : u, v ∈ X, u ≠ v} of the maximum cardinality of a subset Y ⊆ X avoiding every distance in D. What is the asymptotic behavior of c_k = lim_{n → ∞} g(n, k) / n as k → ∞? Specifically, does there exist a constant C > 0 such that c_k ≥ k^{-C} for all k, or does c_k decrease exponentially in k?
literature.source_title: Avoiding Distances
literature.rationale: Theorem 8 proves that (0.2293)^k n ≤ g(n, k) ≤ O(n / (k sqrt(log k))), leaving an exponential gap between the upper and lower bounds as functions of k.

literature.title: Boiling Point of Partizan Arc Kayles with Bounded Degree
literature.statement: In the combinatorial game Partizan Arc Kayles (played on an edge-colored graph where Left removes a blue edge and both incident vertices, and Right removes a red edge and both incident vertices), does there exist a universal upper bound on the temperature of positions whose underlying graph has maximum degree at most 4, or where each vertex is incident to at most 2 blue edges and at most 2 red edges?
literature.source_title: PArcK trees can get as hot as you want

literature.title: Boiling Point of Grid-Embeddable Partizan Arc Kayles
literature.statement: Consider the family of Partizan Arc Kayles positions whose underlying graph is a finite subgraph of the 2-dimensional Cartesian grid ℤ × ℤ, with each edge arbitrarily colored blue or red (relaxing the Domineering restriction that vertical edges are blue and horizontal edges are red). Is the temperature of every such position bounded by a universal constant, or can the temperature be arbitrarily large?
literature.source_title: PArcK trees can get as hot as you want

literature.title: Unbounded Temperature of Partizan Arc Kayles in Graphs of Large Girth
literature.statement: For every fixed integer g ≥ 3, does there exist a sequence of finite edge-colored graphs G_k with girth at least g such that the temperatures of G_k in Partizan Arc Kayles satisfy temp(G_k) → ∞ as k → ∞?
literature.source_title: PArcK trees can get as hot as you want

literature.title: Existence of empty monochromatic pentagons in bichromatic planar point sets
literature.statement: Does every sufficiently large 2-colored planar point set in general position contain a monochromatic empty simple pentagon (not necessarily convex)? Equivalently, is $\lambda_5^\star(2) = 0$, where $\lambda_r^\star(c)$ denotes the minimum integer $s \ge 0$ such that every sufficiently large $c$-colored planar point set in general position contains a monochromatic simple $r$-gon with at most $s$ interior points?
literature.source_title: Almost Empty Monochromatic Polygons in Planar Point Sets
literature.rationale: The paper shows that every sufficiently large 2-colored point set in general position contains a monochromatic pentagon with at most 1 interior point (lambda_5^*(2) <= 1), while known results establish that monochromatic empty convex pentagons can be avoided in arbitrarily large 2-colored sets. Whether allowing non-convex simple pentagons yields an empty monochromatic pentagon remains open.

literature.title: Existence of empty monochromatic hexagons in bichromatic planar point sets
literature.statement: Does every sufficiently large 2-colored planar point set in general position contain a monochromatic empty simple hexagon (not necessarily convex)? That is, is $\lambda_6^\star(2) = 0$?
literature.source_title: Almost Empty Monochromatic Polygons in Planar Point Sets
literature.rationale: The paper proves lambda_6^*(2) <= 1, improving the general bound of floor((6-2)/2) = 2. It also proves that sufficiently large 2-colored Horton sets always contain monochromatic empty r-gons for all r >= 3, removing the usual source of counterexamples. However, determining whether lambda_6^*(2) = 0 holds for all point sets remains open.

literature.title: Asymptotic leading coefficient of minimum interior points in multicolored polygons
literature.statement: For each fixed integer $r \ge 3$, what is the asymptotic growth rate of $\lambda_r^\star(c)$ as the number of colors $c \to \infty$? In particular, does the limit $\lim_{c \to \infty} \lambda_r^\star(c) / c$ exist, and does it equal $(r - 2)/2$, $r - 2$, or a value strictly between the two bounds?
literature.source_title: Almost Empty Monochromatic Polygons in Planar Point Sets
literature.rationale: For fixed r >= 3 and c colors, the paper proves that (r - 2) * floor((c - 1) / 2) <= lambda_r^*(c) <= (r - 2)(c - 2) + floor((r - 2)*delta_c), where delta_c in (0, 1/2]. The leading coefficients of c are (r - 2)/2 and r - 2 respectively, leaving a factor of 2 gap for all r >= 3 (including r = 3).

literature.title: Tightness of lower bound on metric distortion for rank score veto cores
literature.statement: Let C be a set of m ≥ 3 candidates and let s = (s_1, ..., s_m) ∈ ℚ^m be a non-increasing scoring vector with s_1 = 1 and s_j ≥ 0 for all j. For any preference profile of n voters with strict rankings over C, let q^s(c) = (∑_{j=1}^m N_{c,j} s_j) / (n ||s||_1), where N_{c,j} is the number of voters ranking candidate c in position j. Let the (p^unif, q^s)-veto core be the set of candidates admitting a fractional perfect matching in their domination graph with voter weights 1/n and candidate weights q^s(c). Is the worst-case metric distortion of the (p^unif, q^s)-veto core across all preference profiles and all consistent pseudometrics always equal to 1 + 2(||s||_1 - s_m) whenever s_m > 0?
literature.source_title: Regularizing the Veto Core
literature.rationale: The paper proves that the worst-case distortion of the (p^unif, q^s)-veto core lies in [1 + 2(||s||_1 - s_m), 1 + 2||s||_1]. When s_m = 0, the bounds coincide; when s_m > 0, the authors conjecture the lower bound is the exact worst-case distortion.

literature.title: Extension of small minimum degree subgraph bounds to odd target degrees
literature.statement: Let $s \ge 3$ be an odd integer. Is it true that there exists a constant $C = C(s) > 0$ such that every finite simple graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree $d \ge s$ contains a subgraph with minimum degree at least $s$ on at most $O_s(\max\{ n d^{-s/(s-2)} (\log n)^C, \log n \})$ vertices? Equivalently, does the minimum order $u(n, d, s)$ of a subgraph of minimum degree at least $s$ guaranteed in every $n$ -vertex graph of average degree at least $d$ satisfy $u(n, d, s) \le O_s(n d^{-s/(s-2)} (\log n)^C)$ for odd $s$?
literature.source_title: Small subgraphs of large minimum degree
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.1 resolves the problem of finding small subgraphs of minimum degree s for even s >= 4 up to polylogarithmic factors, leaving the odd case open.

literature.title: Bounded-order regular subgraphs from average degree above the Turán exponent for odd degrees
literature.statement: Let $s \ge 5$ be an odd integer and let $\varepsilon > 0$. Do there exist constants $t = t(s, \varepsilon)$ and $n_0 = n_0(s, \varepsilon)$ such that every finite simple graph on $n \ge n_0$ vertices with average degree at least $n^{1 - 2/s + \varepsilon}$ contains an $s$-regular subgraph on at most $t$ vertices?
literature.source_title: Small subgraphs of large minimum degree
literature.rationale: Theorem 1.2 finds a bounded-order subgraph of minimum degree at least s, but does not guarantee that the subgraph is s-regular. This was previously known for even s and for s = 3.

literature.title: Erdős-Rado Sunflower Conjecture for Bounded Set Sizes
literature.statement: Let $k \ge 3$ be an integer. Does there exist a real constant $c_k > 1$ such that for every positive integer $r$, every family $\mathcal{F}$ of sets of size at most $r$ that does not contain a $k$-sunflower (that is, $k$ distinct sets whose pairwise intersections are all identical) satisfies $|\mathcal{F}| \le c_k^r$?
literature.source_title: Proof of the Erd\H{o}s-Szemer\'edi sunflower conjecture
literature.rationale: The Erdős-Rado sunflower conjecture is the premier open problem in the area; while the paper proves the Erdős-Szemerédi conjecture, it notes that the Erdős-Rado conjecture remains wide open, with the current record at $O(k \log r)^r$.
